docs.title: Wonder Kingdom Wiki
docs.text: Wonder Kingdom is a MapleStory-like open-world platformer RPG built with GameLib. This wiki covers its world, its story and everything you can find, fight and make in it.

docs.title: Where things come from
docs.text:
• Lore is written here. This wiki is the source of truth for the story, the history and the people of Wonder Kingdom.
  • Game data (items, skills, jobs, monsters, bosses, NPCs, quests, maps, professions) is generated from the game's content files in GameLib, which is the source of truth for how the game plays. Those pages are rebuilt by tools/generate.py, so fix game data in GameLib, not here.

docs.title: The Blightstone
docs.text:
A golem of mossy stone and rotten wood squats over the spring at the head of Shimmerwater, souring the lake. Watch for the slam: where it lands, the ground turns bitter. Potions work at the Lakehead; scrolls do not.

docs.title: The Bootbreaker
docs.text:
A shore crab the size of a fishing boat moults in the Pinch, the Old Cut's deepest lock, and its young are the bootcrabs. Watch the floor for its claw slams; when the tide floods the lock, keep your feet. Potions work in the Pinch Lock; scrolls do not.

Boss The Bootbreaker Arena The Pinch Lock

docs.title: The Deep Lantern
docs.text:
A squid as long as a ship has found the way in under the headland to the sea-hole in the Holm Wood, and rises there at night among its lights. Fight it from the ledges round the rim; when its ink falls, read where it is from its lights. Potions work in the Lantern Deep; scrolls do not.

Saltgull Feather 48 A long grey flight feather from a savage gull of the ledges. Sawbill Bill 52 A sawbill's flat bill, set with teeth that catch and pull. Scroll Paper 5 A stiff sheet pressed from branches and fibre, ready for a scrollcrafter's ink. Scrub Wolf Pelt 18 A rough brown pelt off a scrub wolf of the Chalk Downs. A tanner will take it. Sea Newt Hide 40 A slick, mottled hide that stays wet long after the newt is gone. Seep Toad Spawn 20 A cold, wobbling clump from the seeps of the foothills. Shade Hook 86 A hook of salt mist gone hard, left by a hookshade. It looks like a sucker's hook. Shade Lash 78 A coil of shadow left where a whipshade faded. It is cold and smells of the sea. Shimmer Gel 35 A drop of slime that holds the lake's light. Shingle Crab Claw 12 A claw from a crab of the Strand's shingle. Shore Crab Claw 34 A heavy claw from a Shore Crab, barnacled at the hinge. Slater Plate 44 One pale, curved plate of a Sea Slater's back. It smells of tar. Slime Bubble 14 A wobbly bubble a slime left behind. Snapjaw Tooth 34 A long tooth from a snapjaw of the Old Cut. It does not look like a fish's. Snapping Lizard Tail 23 A sharp-ridged tail. These lizards snap at anything that moves. Sound Driftwood 22 The one piece of a Driftstump that has not rotted: grey, dense and sound. Spilt Ink 42 Ink that will not stay in its bottle. Spitter Gland 58 The gland a spitting sawbill shoots its jet of water from. Spore Puff Sac 50 The sac a Spore Puff floats on, empty now but still dusty. Brewers say the dust settles a cough. Spring-Glow 106 A cupped handful of glowing spring water that will not spill. Sprite Moss 43 Soft green moss that sprites carry about with them. Stirge Wing 22 A leathery wing from the old drains. Stolen Trinket 25 A thimble, a button, a bent spoon: something shiny a Hoarder Shroom was carrying off. Whose it was, nobody can say. Stormcrest Plume 1,800 A storm-grey plume from Stormcrest's crest. It crackles when it is brushed. Strand Fox Tail 30 A thick grey-red brush from a Strand Fox. Greer pays well for them. Surgeon Eye Tail 75 A tail as stiff as a walking stick. Swollen Wood 62 Grey, spongy wood, heavy with water it should not hold. The Ripsaw's Saw 900 The Ripsaw's saw, scarred end to end, longer than a boathook. Tegan says a sailmaker could make something of a tooth that size. Torn Crown Branch 80 A branch from the Hollow Oak's crown. Dead wood, so the forest can spare it. Torn Page 35 A page torn from an old book, the writing long gone. Trampled Turnip 18 A turnip from a far farm, rooted up and trodden flat. Wilbur would know whose field it came from. Tree Branch 2 A dry branch. Good for a fire, or for a crafter. Tunnel Bat Wing 28 A torn wing from a bat that nests in claw-cut tunnels. Tunnel Bat Wing 45 A dark wing from the Deep Roads, colder than a lampbat's. Unbound Page 64 A page from the Unbound, blank and still faintly warm. Undercut Croco Hide 44 A croco's thick hide, scarred from the undercut banks. Undertow Scale 6,000 A grey scale as big as a hand, from the great fish that lay in the Scour. Wallcreeper Cap 60 A cap that grew flat against the stones of Stonecap Keep, rough on one side from the wall. War Mask Shard 72 A painted shard of an old carved war mask. The paint is older than Midbarium. Weedy Bristle 20 Stiff boar bristle tangled with dried wrack. Caddoc swears by it for springs. Wild Boar Tooth 41 A curved yellow tusk. Herders hang them over the pens to warn the boars off. Wild Spore 18 A plump spore from a wild patch on the Humming Trail. Spore gatherers prize it; so do bakers and brewers. Wildcat Claw 20 A hooked claw from a bluff wildcat. They leap on carts from the ledges of Baysight Hill. Wisp Light 82 A small, cold light that will not go out. Wrack Boar Tusk 24 A boar's tusk, green with the weed it roots through on the shore. Wrackstone 62 Stone and weed grown into one lump, from a Wrackgolem's shoulder. Wreck Salvage 80 Old iron and seasoned timber out of the Saltgrace. Salvagers and shipwrights pay for it. Zombie Mushroom Cap 16 A grey, sagging cap. It smells of the grave and of mushrooms.

docs.title: Quest Items
docs.text: Item Price Description Agna's Sea-Glass 0 A piece of sea-glass, green as a wave, saved from the nets for Ronan. Aurel's Lesson Notes 0 A page of lesson notes in a very careful hand, slightly chewed. Bad News 0 A cracked amber lantern pane from Scrap's tin of lost things, found in a gutter under the outer towers. Scrap named it. Mind the edges. Ballad of the Singing Bank 0 Fulke's ballad, written out for Cecily: the true verses in black, the good ones in red. Bite Herb 0 Narrow leaves from the wet bottoms of the Outworks' ditches, dragged into a ditch rat's nest. It smells of pepper when crushed. Patch cleans bites with it. Brisa's Letter 0 A letter in Brisa's quick hand, to her parents near Kaldemor. You were told not to read it. Broken Keel Timber 0 A broken length of keel timber washed into the cliff foot below the Holm Wood, scored with round marks, each ringed with fine scratches. Calder's Drawing 0 A deep-water boat drawn on the back of a tally sheet, with the hatches open. Carved War Mask Shard 0 A piece of old carved wood, painted red and black, with part of a shouting mouth. It came off one of the War Camp Ruins' masks. Celandine's Plant 0 A sprig of the plant Celandine wanted. Nobody says its name. Chip of Warm Stone 0 A chip of dark stone from the Warm Quarry under Low Grad. It stays warm in the hand, long after it should have cooled. Climber's Sign 0 A strange, scraped stone a Disturbance-touched climber carried in its jaws. Clock Gear 0 A brass gear of the clock tower's works, carried off by a mushroom. Ewan will want it back. Copied Pages 0 Forty pages of the Open Table's oldest record book, copied fair in Dimity's small square hand and octopus ink. Ozzie Lantry hears first. Copied Tide Marks 0 The new tide marks, copied fair for Halvard's ledger. Corrie's Notebooks 0 Four filled notebooks, wrapped in three layers of oilcloth and tied with a careful knot. Not to be opened. Council Letters 0 The Grove Council's letters, sealed and sorted by Ilwen. Crate of Lantern Panes 0 A straw-packed crate of Tinsel's new amber panes for the outer lanterns. Keep it level. Dougal's Measure 0 A knotted cord: the width of the tracks on the lowest steps, against Dougal's boot. Downs Boar Hide 0 A thick hide from a boar of the downs, tough enough for a sole. Simkin wants ten. Drake Venom Gland 0 A small, cold gland from under a Frost Drake's jaw, wrapped in cloth. Lessa wants five, and clean boots. Eilidh's Tide Slate 0 A child's slate covered in chalked tides, one line an evening. Fresh Cable 0 A coil of tarred lowland cable, tight-laid, for Vosk's far canyon bridge. Gate Oyster 0 A big oyster off the old stones of the Sea Locks. Nerissa says they are the best on the coast. Glimmer Dew 0 Morning dew a slime soaked up on the Glimmer Path, squeezed out clean. Gloomfur Sample 0 A tuft of grey fur in a twist of paper, labelled. Great Grey Feather 0 A feather as long as an arm, with a quill like a pipe stem, picked out of a millstone ram's fleece. No hawk wore this. Grimhorn's Hide 0 The great hide of Grimhorn, thick as a door and grey with ash. Thrun has waited a long time for it. Guard's Trial Seal 0 A maple leaf stamped with the Royal Guard's seal. Captain Rhys counts them at the end of the Swordsman's trial. Gunna's Lantern 0 An ordinary quay lantern of Gunna's making. It burns steady in any wind. Gwenna's Old Map 0 A worn map of the Sounding Caves in Gwenna's hand, with a lecture folded inside. Hamish's Drawing 0 The second lift, down the cliff to the far cove, drawn on the back of a cargo list. Hamish's best one. Harra's Cheese Wheel 0 A whole three-month wheel of Tolmach goat cheese, wrapped in cloth. Harra says the price is the price. Hatch's Notes 0 A damp, chewed notebook in a blunt hand, left behind at Hatch's old camp. Most of the pages are about one boar. Hesper's List 0 Pages torn from the back of a seed book: years of hurt travellers, in Hesper's blunt hand. Honey Cake for Caelum 0 Tansy's warmest honey cake, wrapped in a cloth. It works on Liri every time. Imre's Book of Dates 0 Imre's worn yellow book: star names in two hands, and on the last pages a list of dates, each one a still, cold night when the low stars shimmered. Ironbark Limb 0 A dead limb from the Hollow Oak, iron-hard and straight. Isaura's Sealed Letter 0 A letter sealed with green wax. It is not to be opened. Juniper's Notebook 0 A season's notes, chewed at the corners, smelling of ape. Kestrel's Report 0 A folded page in a hurried hand, with a small brown stain Kestrel insists is mud. Knights' Court Notice 0 By order of the Knights' Court: travellers on the World Tree Road keep to daylight hours. Clement's copy, to post at the wayside well. Lake Reed 0 A green reed from the edge of Shimmerwater. The sprites carry it about. Ledge Pearl 0 A big pale pearl from the oyster bed on the ledge at the reef's edge, where Nerissa stopped diving. Ligator Tooth 0 A ligator's tooth from the reed beds, for Aldith to lay against the gripped bargehand's bruise. Lupin Claw Sample 0 A claw from a sharpened Lupin, wrapped and labelled. Mayor's Letter 0 A sealed letter from Mayor Tobin. Meadow Herb 0 A bunch of yarrow, plantain and feverfew pulled from a verge adder's nest in the Gate Meadows. No spots on the stems. Patch will want it. Mended Net 0 A cove net Agna mended, to be taken back to the boats. Morven's Verse 0 The end of the gap verse, as Calder heard his grandmother sing it, written out by Cormac. Mott's Pack Strap 0 A worn leather strap with a tin buckle, the kind a pedlar's pack hangs from. Molly will know it. Odda's Spring Letter 0 A thick letter sealed with Brenna wax, addressed to an old friend in Fairy Forest. Ondine's Book of Lanterns 0 Nineteen years of lantern brightnesses, one line every autumn. Ondine's Brightest Lantern 0 The brightest lantern Ondine has ever made, for the western path. Pedlar's Tinware 0 A tin cup, a pan or a brass-handled ladle from Mott's pack, carried up the walls by a Hoarder Shroom. Mott will want it back. Perch's List 0 Every route the pigeons refused, with the date and the hour, tied in a blue ribbon. One corner shows where the cat sat on it. Perch's Message 0 A message rolled small for a pigeon's leg, bound for the east. Three birds have refused to carry it over the downs. Rafe's Balrog Puppet 0 A cat-sized wooden Balrog with red-glass eyes and a hinged mouth, gnawed at one heel. Still frightening. Reed Root 0 A thick root torn up by the ligators of the reed beds. Hawise thinks it will dye. Root Soil 0 Dark soil from beside one of the great roots. Colder than it should be. Root-Water 0 Water from a root's hollow, thin and cold. Scored Plank 0 A deck plank off the Bright Morrow, scored across by sawbill teeth in the night run. Scratched Stone 0 A stone from the high landings, scored by four deep parallel cuts. Seasoned River Timber 0 Oak that has lain in the river for years under the Undercut's banks. Bennet swears by it. Shed Newt Claw 0 A claw shed on the rocks, four hooked points on a wide foot. Dougal will want to measure it. Silent Root 0 A pale, knotted root that smells of earth and cloves, packed into a barkback's moss in the Silent Cutting. Patch says it pulls a fever down. Skerries Shell 0 A weed-wrapped shell taken from the deeply touched of the Skerries, which guard them like eggs. Sound Pine Timber 0 A straight length of salt-hardened pine, cut from a Saltdead Stump: good for a keel. Sound Stave 0 A straight limb of sound twisted wood, cut from under a swollen stump's grey swelling. Zirra wants ten. Spice Crate 0 A small crate of Marisol's pepper, nibbled at the corners by bootcrabs. Spore Puff Wisp 0 A grey wisp of spore cloud caught in a jar. It hangs in one place and will not drift. Nell will want to see it. Starling's Dates 0 Two years of flicker nights in Starling's small, careful hand, with notes in the margins in even smaller letters. Strip of Torn Net 0 A strip of Cobb's net, rolled up in Wenna's basket. A long straight rent runs through it, the edges pulled, not cut. Stubborn Fern Root 0 A tough little fern root torn up from the worst soil on the road. Sulking Lantern 0 A quay lantern of Gunna's making, still lit. Its flicker has gone a little sullen. Carry it level. Surgeon Eye Sample 0 A sealed vial with a Surgeon Eye's cells in it, labelled twice. Tamsin's Pine Tar 0 A sealed crock of Tamsin's best pine tar, the batch old Fergus taught her. It is not an apology. Tide Line Shell 0 A pale shell from the Long Sands' tide line. Bree says they are the prettiest on the island. Tinsel's Newest Lens 0 A lens clear all the way through, the first Tinsel has ever made without a bubble. For Starling's telescope. Torn Leaf Fragment 0 A scrap of a very old leaf, mostly faded. A leaf number survives in one corner. Tuft of Speckled Wool 0 A tuft of speckled lamb's wool caught on a Windflower Cap. Winnie will know whose it is. Urgent Message 0 A message from the gate for Perch's loft, knotted with Kite's runner's knot. It has to go out with a bird before dusk. Warden's Message 0 A note in Reynold's square hand for the shepherds of the downs: their wool stall is held till Friday. Warden's Tide Mark 0 An iron tide mark with the wardens' notch, for driving into the rock at the waterline. Whole Sawbill Bill 0 A sawbill's bill without a tooth broken. Maren wants it for her shelf. Wild Comb 0 A broken piece of comb from a wild bee's nest in the chalk. Gilbert wants to see it. Ysmay's Advice 0 Twelve points of advice for the First Warden, numbered. Only advice. Ysmay's Note 0 A folded note in a sharp hand, about a pilot who swung wide in the gap. It is very good. Zirra's Message 0 A folded message from Zirra to the Old One. It stays folded.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text:
Wonder Kingdom is a bright, prosperous and genuinely united kingdom on the island of Veligor. Its people come from different cultures and keep different traditions, yet they share a real sense of belonging and respect for one another. Their towns are lively, their markets are full, and their differences are celebrated rather than feared.

It was not always so. Before the kingdom, Veligor was split between four peoples who had fought each other for generations. Only the coming of the Balrog, an ancient being too strong for any one of them, drove them to stand together. They beat it, sealed it beneath the roots of the great World Tree, and founded Wonder Kingdom on the cooperation that won that war.

Fifty years ago, an expedition into the World Tree opened a rift deep beneath its roots and damaged the seal. The Balrog has not escaped, but its influence has been seeping out ever since. Wild creatures have grown aggressive, and the wilderness between the towns has filled with monsters.

The kingdom is still whole and happy. The land around it is turning hostile. That contrast is the heart of the world.

Core premise

Wonder Kingdom is a genuinely happy and united civilization, born from the cooperation of four formerly divided peoples. Generations later, an ancient threat imprisoned beneath the World Tree is slowly returning, and a new generation must protect the peaceful world its ancestors created.

docs.title: The Age of Disturbance
docs.text: The fifty years since the expedition are known as the Age of Disturbance. Through the damaged seal, the Balrog's influence has been creeping out of its prison and across Veligor, and its effects grow harder to ignore every year. Above all, the island's wilderness has become far more dangerous.

docs.title: Wild Creatures Turn Aggressive
docs.text:
Creatures that once kept away from travelers, or simply went about their lives, began attacking anyone who wandered into their territory. Monsters became common in the forests, plains, mountains and caves.

It is not the same everywhere. Some places have seen only small changes, while others have become home to truly dangerous creatures. The towns themselves are still peaceful, but every road between them has grown riskier.

docs.title: The Nature of Monsters
docs.text:
The monsters roaming Veligor are tied to the weakening seal. The spread of the Balrog's influence is why such a peaceful land is now full of hostile creatures.

That does not mean the Balrog commands every one of them. Some are ordinary animals whose nature it has twisted. Others are magical beings changed by a changing land.

docs.title: The Disturbance-touched
docs.text: Some creatures carry the Disturbance far more strongly than others. They are bigger and fiercer than the rest of their kind, harder to kill, and often strange: some shrug off blows behind a shimmering shield, some heal as fast as they are wounded, some burn or freeze or sting with a power no ordinary beast has. The longer a hunter stays in one place, the more of them seem to appear. People across the kingdom call them Disturbance-touched, and the very worst of them, rarer still, are said to be deeply touched.

docs.title: Life Under the Disturbance
docs.text:
The growing danger in the wilds has made travel, exploration, farming and any work outside the towns harder. Yet Wonder Kingdom carries on. Its towns are still prosperous and welcoming, and its people work together against the threat.

The kingdom has not fallen into fear, hostility or division. The monsters are simply a new challenge, met by a civilization that was already united.

Design notes

"The Age of Disturbance" is a provisional name. Exactly how the Balrog's influence creates or changes monsters is not settled, including whether entirely new creatures can appear. In the game, the Disturbance-touched are the Elite and Epic monsters.

docs.title: The Balrog
docs.text:
The Balrog is the greatest threat Wonder Kingdom has ever faced. It is an ancient being of immense power and destruction, which once nearly destroyed every people on Veligor, and which now lies imprisoned beneath the World Tree, held by a seal that is slowly failing.

To most people today, it is a legend: a monster from history books and bedtime stories. To the guardians of Cavelor, it is the reason their city exists.

docs.title: What It Is
docs.text:
No one alive has seen the Balrog, and the old accounts disagree about almost everything. They agree on a few things:

  • It is enormous, larger than any creature on Veligor, and it moved through the land like a storm.
  • It burned. Settlements it passed were left as ash, and the ground where it stood stayed scorched for years.
  • It could not be killed. The four peoples' greatest warriors wounded it again and again, and every wound closed.
  • Its influence spreads. Even before it reached a place, the creatures there grew wild and vicious, as if something in them had answered it.

Beyond that, every people tells it differently. Savage songs describe a horned giant wreathed in flame. Magician records describe it as something less like an animal and more like a wound in the world, a hunger given shape. Commons tales call it simply "the Burning". Aristocrat chronicles, which care about numbers, record the armies and towns it destroyed, and say little about what it was.

docs.title: Where It Came From
docs.text:
The oldest question about the Balrog has never been answered. The four peoples each have a story:

  • The Savages say it came out of the deep earth, woken from a sleep older than the island by the noise of their endless wars.
  • The Magicians believe it came from somewhere else entirely, through a tear in the world, drawn by the World Tree's magic the way moths are drawn to a lantern.
  • The Commons say it was always there, under the island, and that the island's warmth and fertility are what is left over from its fire.
  • The Aristocrats recorded only that it appeared in the far wilds and moved toward the center of Veligor, toward the World Tree, from the very first day.

No one knows which, if any, is true. Cavelor's scholars say that each story might hold a piece of the truth.

docs.title: The First Burning
docs.text:
The Balrog first appeared in the wilds at the edge of Veligor, while the Age of Division still raged. Its first victims were frontier villages of both alliances. Each side blamed the other at first, and wasted precious time accusing each other of some terrible new weapon.

By the time they understood, it was moving inland. Armies sent against it were scattered. Strongholds that had held for generations against human enemies burned in a night. Refugees from all four peoples fled toward the center of the island, and the Balrog followed, always moving toward the World Tree.

docs.title: The Alliance
docs.text:
With the Balrog closing on the heart of the island, the four peoples finally met under truce. It was the first time in generations that their leaders had sat at one table. The talks were bitter and nearly failed more than once, but the refugee camps filling the plains made the choice for them. They united.

Each people gave what it did best. The Savages sent their strongest warriors. The Magicians brought their knowledge of ancient magic. The Commons supplied, armed and fed the united army. The Aristocrats organized it and commanded it as one.

docs.title: The Last Stand at the Tree
docs.text:
The final battle was fought at the foot of the World Tree. The united army could not kill the Balrog, but it could hold it and wear it down, and that was the plan: while the warriors fought, the Magicians worked a seal powerful enough to bind it forever.

The battle lasted for days. The Savage front line held the Balrog in place, at terrible cost. When the creature finally weakened enough, the Magicians drove it down into the earth beneath the Tree and closed the seal over it, binding it deep within the roots.

The war was over. The four peoples who had fought together founded Wonder Kingdom, and a company of warriors stayed below to guard the seal. Their descendants are the people of Cavelor.

docs.title: The Seal
docs.text:
The seal is a binding of powerful magic, made by the Magicians and strengthened by the combined efforts of the whole alliance. It holds the Balrog in a prison deep below the World Tree, beneath Cavelor and the oldest roots.

For the whole history of the kingdom, it held. Then, fifty years ago, the Great World Tree Expedition accidentally opened a rift in the deep passages near the prison and damaged it. The seal did not break, but it began to weaken, and it has been weakening ever since.

docs.title: The Balrog Today
docs.text:
Through the damaged seal, the Balrog's influence has been seeping out across Veligor. This is the cause of the Age of Disturbance: creatures grown aggressive, monsters filling the wilds, and danger on every road between the towns. It is exactly what the old accounts described happening before the Balrog arrived, and that is what worries Cavelor's guardians most.

What the Balrog wants, whether it is aware of the world above, and what will happen if the seal fails completely, nobody knows.

Design notes

The Balrog's true nature, intentions and fate are deliberately undecided (principle 16). The four peoples' stories about its origin are legends inside the world, not established fact. New with this page: the first appearance in the far wilds, the First Burning, the truce talks, the Last Stand at the Tree with the Savage front line holding the Balrog while the Magicians worked the seal, and the Balrog always moving toward the World Tree.

docs.title: The Great World Tree Expedition
docs.text: Fifty years ago, Wonder Kingdom sent an expedition into the World Tree. The Tree had been a landmark for centuries, but most of its interior had never been explored, and the journey became one of the greatest feats of exploration in the kingdom's history.

docs.title: The Upper Chambers
docs.text:
The explorers first climbed up through the Tree's vast inner passages. They found astonishing magical places: strange plants, extraordinary creatures and natural structures of dizzying complexity.

There they met the Children of the Tree, a magical people who had lived cut off from the rest of the world. After the expedition, the Children gradually moved to Fairy Forest and became part of the wider kingdom.

docs.title: The Discovery of Cavelor
docs.text:
Having explored the heights, the expedition turned downward, into the depths beneath the Tree. There they found Cavelor.

They learned that the descendants of ancient guardians had lived in the hidden city for generations, keeping the memory of the Balrog alive and guarding its prison. The legendary war against the Balrog, it turned out, had left behind a living order sworn to stop its return.

docs.title: The Accident
docs.text:
Exploring the passages deeper still, the explorers accidentally opened a rift, and the rift damaged the magic that held the Balrog.

The seal did not break. It began, very slowly, to weaken. At first, almost nobody on the surface realized what had happened. But over the following decades, the failing seal began to reach the world above, and the Age of Disturbance began.

docs.title: The Age of Division
docs.text: Long before Wonder Kingdom, four peoples shared Veligor, and each had its own idea of how life ought to be lived.

docs.title: The Savages
docs.text: The Savages held the rugged wilds and the mountains. They prized strength, endurance and independence, honored their ancestors, and lived close to the land. Their communities were built around survival and cooperation, and respect went to whoever showed courage and perseverance. They fought off every outside authority that tried to rule their territory or press strange customs on them.

docs.title: The Magicians
docs.text: The Magicians gave their lives to understanding the supernatural forces of Veligor, above all the World Tree, the old places where magic ran deep, and the bond between magic and nature. They valued knowledge, magical skill and preservation, and they stood against anyone who tried to exploit or seize the places they held sacred.

docs.title: The Commons
docs.text: The Commons were the farmers, merchants, craftsmen and settlers who kept ordinary life running. They built villages, farms, workshops and trade routes, and they valued cooperation, practical skill, honest work and prosperity. What they wanted most was safety and stability across the island.

docs.title: The Aristocrats
docs.text: The Aristocrats raised fortified settlements, wrote laws and built the first real institutions of government. They believed that order, administration and strong central leadership were the way to a stable and prosperous Veligor.

docs.title: The Ancient Conflict
docs.text:
For generations the island was split into two loose alliances: the Savages and the Magicians on one side, the Commons and the Aristocrats on the other.

They fought over land, over who had the right to rule, over whose traditions should prevail, and over access to the island's most important natural and magical places. The quarrels hardened into long wars. Each side had real strengths, but neither could win a lasting peace, and Veligor never became one civilization.

It took a far greater threat to end it.

docs.title: The Balrog War
docs.text:
The ancient conflict was cut short by the arrival of the Balrog, a being of immense power and destruction.

It threatened every people on the island at once. Settlements burned, armies were broken, and even the mightiest warriors and magicians could barely stand against it. For the first time, all four peoples faced an enemy none of them could beat alone, and next to that danger their old grievances suddenly seemed very small.

So they united, and each gave what it did best:

  • The Savages sent their strongest warriors, whose courage and strength carried the fight to the Balrog itself.
  • The Magicians brought their knowledge of ancient magic, which in the end made it possible to imprison the creature.
  • The Commons gathered supplies, forged equipment and kept the united armies fed and moving.
  • The Aristocrats supplied military organization and leadership, and coordinated the four forces as one.

Together they defeated the Balrog. But they could not destroy it. Instead, the alliance wove a great magical seal and bound the creature deep within the roots of the World Tree at the heart of Veligor.

That victory ended the Age of Division.

docs.title: The Founding of Wonder Kingdom
docs.text:
After the Balrog was sealed away, the leaders of the four peoples met to make the peace last. They signed a treaty that formally ended their old wars and joined them into a single realm: Wonder Kingdom.

The founding treaty declared that every people of Veligor could live together in peace, whatever their ancestry, culture, station or magical gifts. The kingdom was built on the same cooperation that had won the war.

Over the generations that followed, the four peoples grew a shared identity without giving up their own. Their cultures kept living and changing inside the new kingdom. Towns traded, friendships crossed the old lines, and knowledge passed freely from one community to the next. The old hostilities faded until nobody thought of their neighbors as ancestral enemies anymore. The unity the treaty had promised simply became the way people lived.

docs.title: The Meaning of Unity
docs.text:
Wonder Kingdom is not held together by fear, force or a fragile political bargain. Its unity is real.

Its people understand and value one another across their differences. Each town keeps its own customs and way of life, and those differences are a source of pride rather than friction. Everyone is proud of the shared history and of the civilization their ancestors built. The old wars are remembered as history, but they no longer shape how communities treat each other.

That holds for every settlement on Veligor, including Urbanograd, whose unconventional culture is accepted across the kingdom.

docs.title: Wonder Kingdom Today
docs.text:
Fifty years have passed since the Great World Tree Expedition, and Wonder Kingdom is still peaceful, prosperous and wonderfully diverse.

  • Selsior flourishes as the bustling capital.
  • Kaldemor keeps its cheerful country traditions and its love of craft.
  • Midbarium holds fast to its resilient highland ways.
  • Fairy Forest remains the heart of magic and harmony with nature.
  • Urbanograd, now a century old, still goes its own colorful way.
  • Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour thrive as independent ports with very different characters.
  • Cavelor keeps its ancient watch beneath the World Tree.

docs.title: Everyday Life
docs.text:
For all the danger beyond their walls, the people of Wonder Kingdom live ordinary, happy lives. They trade, farm, craft, learn, play, explore and celebrate. Travel, trade, friendship and shared culture tie the island's communities together, and people are proud to call the kingdom home.

Their happiness is real. It is not a pretty face hiding a broken society.

docs.title: The Dangerous Wilderness
docs.text:
Outside the towns, it is another story. Monsters roam much of Veligor's wilderness, and forests, mountains, plains, caves and ancient ruins have all grown more dangerous. Travelers and adventurers must face aggressive creatures and treacherous ground.

Peaceful towns and a dangerous wild: that contrast is the defining feature of the world.

docs.title: The Forgotten Threat
docs.text:
To most people, the Balrog is a legend, a figure out of history books. It was defeated and locked away so long ago that hardly anyone thinks of it as a danger today.

The people of Cavelor know better. They remember the first war and understand the seal, and they know that its slow failure is a serious threat.

And deep beneath the World Tree, the Balrog's influence keeps spreading.

docs.title: Worldbuilding Principles
docs.text:
These principles guide all future lore. New pages and stories should stay true to them.

  1. Wonder Kingdom is genuinely united. Its communities are not secretly hostile toward one another.
  2. The four original peoples were once divided. Their conflict ended through cooperation against the Balrog and the founding treaty that followed.
  3. Cultural differences still matter. Unity did not erase the traditions or identities of Veligor's communities.
  4. Urbanograd was founded 100 years ago, in the west of Veligor. Its people are rebels in a cultural sense, not political insurgents.
  5. Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour are independent towns. Their resemblance to other towns is cultural and atmospheric, not a sign that anyone governs them.
  6. Bain Harbour lies on the east coast of Veligor and Goa Harbour on the west. They have different identities without being rivals.
  7. Selsior is the City of Everything. It is a joyful, bustling, cosmopolitan metropolis with classic medieval fantasy architecture.
  8. Kaldemor is the Town of Joyful Craftsmanship. It is a cheerful, prosperous, pastoral community inspired by Henesys.
  9. Midbarium is a rugged, rural highland town of four families. Each family chooses its chieftain, and together they choose the Old One who leads them all. It stands for strength, resilience, independence and ancestral tradition, and its dry, desert-like highlands draw on highland, canyon and steppe cultures, not Middle Eastern ones.
  10. Fairy Forest is a magical woodland town. It is the Magicians' historic home and the new home of the Children of the Tree.
  11. Cavelor was founded by ancient guardians. Its people still carry the duty of watching over the Balrog's prison.
  12. The Great World Tree Expedition took place 50 years ago. It found the Children of the Tree and Cavelor, and accidentally damaged the Balrog's seal.
  13. The weakening seal makes the wilderness ever more dangerous. This is the core explanation for the aggressive monsters across Veligor.
  14. The kingdom stays peaceful despite the monsters. The danger is in the land and the wilds, not between its peoples.
  15. The player belongs to Wonder Kingdom from the start. The player character was born and raised here.
  16. The Balrog is the overarching ancient threat. Its true nature, intentions and fate are not yet fully decided.
  17. The world is mostly bright, colorful, prosperous and adventurous. Dark places and dangerous creatures exist, but they do not define everyday life in the kingdom.
  18. Not every story is about the Balrog. The world has ordinary lives, personal adventures, local traditions and mysteries of its own.
  19. Veligor is the starting point, not necessarily the whole world. Other islands and kingdoms may come later.
  20. Undecided details stay undecided. New lore should be clear about what is established and what is only a proposal, rather than quietly adding new canon. On these pages, open questions are kept in Design notes boxes.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: When What happened The ancient era The four peoples build their own civilizations across Veligor. The Age of Division The Savages and Magicians fight the Commons and Aristocrats for generations. The Balrog War The Balrog appears in the far wilds and burns its way toward the World Tree. The four peoples unite and make their last stand at the foot of the Tree. The Founding The Balrog is defeated and sealed beneath the World Tree. The founding treaty creates Wonder Kingdom, and guardians stay below to found Cavelor. The Age of Unity The kingdom prospers, its towns grow, and the old divisions fade away. 100 years ago The Walkers leave Selsior and settle the ruins of Old Grad, founding Urbanograd. The Open Charter recognizes it as a town of the kingdom. 50 years ago The Great World Tree Expedition finds the Children of the Tree and Cavelor. 50 years ago The expedition accidentally opens a rift that damages the Balrog's seal. The following decades The Age of Disturbance: the Balrog's influence spreads, and the wilderness grows ever more dangerous. Today Wonder Kingdom is united and prosperous, monsters roam much of the wilderness, and the Balrog's prison keeps weakening.

docs.title: Veligor
docs.text:
Veligor is a large island and the home of Wonder Kingdom. Its land is wonderfully varied: fertile plains, high mountains, enchanted forests, long coastlines, quiet farmland, ancient ruins, deep caverns and wide stretches of wilderness.

At its center rises the enormous World Tree, visible from much of the island and one of its best-known landmarks.

Roads, footpaths and trade routes link the island's towns. The wilds between them have grown dangerous, but the towns themselves are as lively, busy and prosperous as ever, and each has a character all its own.

docs.title: The Lay of the Land
docs.text:
The World Tree stands at the very center of the island, with Cavelor hidden deep beneath its roots. Selsior lies on the central plain a day's ride south of it, joined to it by the World Tree Road, and the royal roads run out from the capital to every town.

Where Town The center of the island The World Tree, with Cavelor beneath it The central plain, south of the Tree Selsior, the capital The northwest mountains Midbarium The northeast woods Fairy Forest The west Urbanograd The west coast Goa Harbour The southeast countryside, inland Kaldemor The east coast Bain Harbour

Besides the royal roads, older roads join the towns to each other: Stonefang Pass between Midbarium and Urbanograd, the Northern Woodland Trail from Midbarium to Fairy Forest, the Eastern Forest Road from Fairy Forest down to Kaldemor, and the Western Merchant Road between Goa Harbour and Urbanograd. The Verdant Coast Road runs from Kaldemor through its farmland and orchards down to Bain Harbour, green the whole way to the sea, and the Southern Coastal Road follows the island's south shore from Goa Harbour round to Bain Harbour without passing the capital.

docs.title: Towns
docs.text:
Town Known as Character Selsior The City of Everything The bustling, joyful capital Kaldemor The Town of Joyful Craftsmanship A cheerful pastoral town of makers and farmers Midbarium The Highland Settlement A rural highland town of four families, led by the Old One Fairy Forest The Magical Woodland A forest settlement with Magician roots Urbanograd The Town of Societal Rebels A century-old home of free spirits Bain Harbour The Coastal Town A lively, prosperous port Goa Harbour The Wilderness Harbour A rustic port on the far coast Cavelor The Underground City of Guardians The hidden city beneath the World Tree

Beyond Veligor

Veligor is where the story begins, not necessarily the whole world. Other islands and kingdoms may appear later.

docs.title: The World Tree
docs.text: At the very center of Veligor stands the World Tree, one of the island's great landmarks in every sense: geographic, historical and magical. It is no ordinary tree. Its size is staggering, and inside it lie vast worlds of their own, reaching both up into its crown and down into the earth.

docs.title: The Upper World Tree
docs.text:
High in the Tree lie great chambers, ancient branches, strange magical plants and whole ecosystems found nowhere else, home to wondrous magical creatures.

This was the home of the Children of the Tree. The people of the surface knew almost nothing of them until the expedition fifty years ago. Since then, many of the Children have moved to Fairy Forest.

docs.title: The Lower World Tree
docs.text:
Below the ground, the Tree's roots run deep, carving passages through ancient caverns and buried places. The hidden city of Cavelor lies down here.

Deeper still is the Balrog's prison.

docs.title: The Ancient Seal
docs.text:
When the four united peoples defeated the Balrog, they bound it beneath the World Tree with a seal made from powerful magic and the combined strength of the whole alliance. For generations it held.

So the World Tree has two faces. It is a source of natural beauty, magical wonder and extraordinary life, and in its deepest roots it holds the greatest ancient danger Wonder Kingdom has ever known.

docs.title: Alwyn
docs.text:
Shipwright

Town Bain Harbour Where Shipyard Role Craftsman Age Adult In the game Alwyn

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Cheerful, steady and good with his hands, he whistles while he works and never loses his temper. He finds his father's stubbornness exhausting and admires it anyway.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text: Alwyn is forty-one, and he has been working in the Bain Harbour shipyard since he was old enough to carry a bucket of pitch without spilling it. He is the son of Dunstan, the master shipwright, and everyone on the waterfront knows that the yard will be his one day. Most of them would say it already half is. These days Alwyn does the heavy work: he steams the planks, swings the adze, hauls the timbers into place and climbs the staging in the rain when his father's knees will no longer allow it. He whistles the whole time, and in all his years at the yard nobody has ever heard him lose his temper.

docs.title: The yard and the old man
docs.text:
Alwyn grew up in sawdust. His mother, Senara, painted the names on his father's hulls in curling gold letters, and when she died nine years ago Alwyn took over the brush, because nobody else in the yard had a steady enough hand. He still paints every name the way she taught him, and he has never told Dunstan that he practised for a month in secret before the first one.

He finds his father exhausting. Dunstan is gruff, stubborn and certain, and he talks to the ships as if they were old friends who might take offence. Alwyn has spent years trying to change the old man's mind about one thing in particular: the hulls. Since the deep water turned strange, the water past the headland has grown rougher, and the captains come home with stories of things that bump and scrape beneath them. Alwyn would like to build deeper keels, thicker planking and stronger ribs for the ships that work the deep water. Dunstan says the old designs were good enough for Old Bain, and that is usually the end of the conversation. Alwyn admires that stubbornness even as it drives him to distraction; he knows it is the same stubbornness that has kept every hull his father built afloat.

He gets on well with Peregrine, his father's apprentice, though he has learned to listen to Peregrine's ideas the way a fisherman sorts a catch, keeping one in ten. His oldest friend is Tegan the sailmaker, who has known him since they were both children underfoot in the yard. Tegan is making the sails for this summer's race boat in secret, and she will not tell even Alwyn what she is doing, which she clearly enjoys.

docs.title: Home
docs.text: Alwyn is married to Bryony, the baker of Merchant Street, and their house smells of bread and tar in equal measure. Bryony is up long before the sun and Alwyn is home long after it sets, so they meet in the middle of the day over salt rolls on the shipyard steps. They have two children. Poppy, who is eleven, delivers her mother's bread along Merchant Street and draws the ships in the bay; Alwyn keeps every drawing she gives him pinned up in the yard's tool shed. Kit, who is nine, is never anywhere but the shipyard if he can help it, and Alwyn has given up trying to get the sawdust out of his hair.

docs.title: What he wants and fears
docs.text: Alwyn wants to build a ship that can face whatever is down there and bring its crew home. He fears that one day a ship from his father's yard will not come back, and that he will have known how to make it stronger.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: A quest could help Alwyn gather the heavier timber he would need for a deep-water hull, without his father noticing. Or someone might find a way to show Dunstan, with proof he cannot argue with, what the deep water is doing to the old hulls.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Dunstan: father
  • Bryony: wife
  • Kit: son
  • Poppy: daughter
  • Tegan: friend

docs.title: Ambrose
docs.text:
Chartmaker

Town Bain Harbour Where Merchant Street Role Scholar Age Adult Sells Sea charts, tide tables and coastal maps In the game Ambrose

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Quiet, patient and fond of tiny handwriting. He apologises to his ink when he spills it.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text: Ambrose is fifty, quiet and patient, and fond of tiny handwriting. He is the chartmaker of Bain Harbour, and every captain in the harbour sails by charts he has drawn. His shop on Merchant Street is narrow, dim and full of paper, and it smells of ink and lamp oil. When he spills his ink, which is rarely, he apologises to it.

docs.title: The chartmaker's trade
docs.text:
Ambrose was born on Merchant Street, the son of a bookbinder long since dead, and he was apprenticed at fifteen to old Hedley, the harbour's chartmaker before him. Hedley was short-sighted, short-tempered and the finest draughtsman Ambrose has ever known. He taught Ambrose to listen to captains more carefully than they speak, because a captain who says "a bit north of the rock" may mean three different things. When Hedley died twenty-five years ago, Ambrose took the shop, the drawers, and the responsibility.

He draws sea charts, tide tables and coastal maps for every ship that leaves the harbour, and he updates them from the reports the captains bring him. He has never been a sailor himself. He gets seasick in a rowing boat on a calm day. But he knows the coast of Veligor better than most people who have sailed it, because every captain in Bain Harbour has described it to him, inch by inch, for twenty-five years.

docs.title: Quenna and Jowan
docs.text:
Ambrose met Quenna when she came into the shop as a young sailor, loudly demanding a chart of a stretch of coast that, he patiently explained, nobody had charted yet. She came back the next season with the soundings herself. They were married twenty-one years ago, and they are about as different as two people can be: she is brisk and loud and decides everything before the tide turns, and he takes a week over a single headland. He thinks she is the bravest person alive. She says he is the only person in the harbour she cannot rush.

Their son, Jowan, joined the Harbour Watch last spring. He has his mother's need to act and his father's handwriting, and Ambrose worries quietly that the first will one day carry him somewhere the second cannot follow.

docs.title: The locked drawer
docs.text:
Since the deep water turned strange, captains have been bringing Ambrose a new kind of mark: a place where something was seen in the water. A shape under the keel. A pale light far out. A net torn clean through. At first he added them to the ordinary charts, until he realised that frightened sailors were steering around them and missing the channels. So he started a separate chart, and he keeps it locked in a drawer in his workroom.

Very few people know about it. Quenna does, and each summer she takes the worst of its marks to the race and shares them with Goa Harbour's First Warden. Some of the captains know, because they bring the marks. Ambrose does not know what the marks mean, and he refuses to guess on paper. He has noticed only that there are more of them each year, and that they seem to be creeping closer to the headland.

docs.title: Poppy
docs.text: Poppy, the baker's daughter, has watched him through his shop window for years. One morning he invited her in, and now she comes every morning after her bread round. She has the steadiest hand and the sharpest eye he has seen since Hedley, and he has started teaching her properly. He has not shown her the locked drawer. He suspects she knows it is there.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: A quest could carry a sighting to Ambrose, check one of the marks on the locked chart in person, or help him chart a stretch of coast that changed after a storm.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Quenna: wife
  • Jowan: son
  • Poppy: admirer

docs.title: Barnaby
docs.text:
Bosun of the Bright Morrow

Town Bain Harbour Where Docks Role Worker Age Adult In the game Barnaby

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Big, booming and soft-hearted, with a story for every scar. No one is sure how many of his stories are true.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text: Barnaby is the bosun of the Bright Morrow, and he is the biggest man on the Bain Harbour docks and very nearly the loudest. He is forty-six, big, booming and soft-hearted, with a laugh that rattles the rigging and a story for every scar. He has a great many scars. No one is sure how many of the stories are true, including, on some evenings, Barnaby.

docs.title: A story for every scar
docs.text:
Barnaby has been at sea since he was a boy, and he has been bosun of the Bright Morrow for nine years, since the day Captain Seraphine bought her. As bosun he looks after the ship's rigging, sails, anchors and boats, and the crew who work them, and he does it with enormous care and a great deal of noise. He can splice a line faster than anyone in the harbour and sings while he does it, badly. The crew love him. They also know that if they leave a rope uncoiled on his deck, the whole Waterfront will hear about it.

The scar across his left hand, he says, came from a swordfish that leapt over the bow and tried to steal his dinner. The one on his chin came from a fight with three smugglers in a sea cave, or from a gull, depending on who is listening. The long one on his forearm is from a parted line in a storm, and that one is true, because Seraphine was there; she says he caught the line before it took a sailor's head off, and Barnaby, for once, does not tell that story at all.

His most devoted listener is Finch, the dock errand runner, who sits on the bollards beside the Bright Morrow whenever she is in harbour and hears every story twice. Barnaby gives him the best ones. He has never had a son, and he would not say that is what Finch is to him, but he keeps a twist of barley sugar in his coat pocket for the boy on every voyage, and it has never once come home uneaten.

docs.title: The eyes
docs.text:
Last autumn, on a moonlit night far out in deep water, Barnaby was alone on deck with the watch asleep at the wheel, and he looked over the side. A pair of eyes as large as cartwheels looked back up at him from under the Bright Morrow's hull. They did not blink. Then they sank away into the dark, slowly, as if whatever owned them was in no hurry at all.

Barnaby told the story on the Waterfront the next day, and the Waterfront laughed, because it was Barnaby, and because the eyes were as large as cartwheels. He laughed along. He has told it many times since, and it is the only one of his stories that has never grown in the telling. Two people have never laughed at it. One is Finch, who believes every word. The other is Captain Seraphine, who listened to it once in silence and then went to her cabin and shut the door. Barnaby has thought about that a great deal.

He has not slept on deck since. He used to sling a hammock under the stars on every warm night of every voyage. Now he sleeps below, in the forecastle with the crew, and when the others tease him about it he tells them his back is getting old. It is not his back.

docs.title: What he wants and fears
docs.text: Barnaby wants someone to believe him who is not ten years old. He fears that if he ever looks over the side again on a moonlit night, the eyes will be closer.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: A quest could stand the night watch on the Bright Morrow and look over the side for him, sort the true stories from the tall ones, or find out what Seraphine knows that made her shut her cabin door.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Seraphine: captain
  • Finch: devoted listener

docs.title: Barnacle
docs.text:
Harbour Cat

Town Bain Harbour Where Fish Market Role Animal Age Adult In the game Barnacle

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Lazy, greedy and dignified. She sleeps in the sun on the fish market steps and accepts tribute from all who pass.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text: Barnacle is the harbour cat of Bain Harbour. She is a large, well-fed tabby with a white chest, one torn ear and the bearing of a duchess, and she belongs to nobody and to everybody. She is lazy, greedy and dignified. She sleeps in the sun on the fish market steps and accepts tribute from all who pass, and she has never once said thank you.

docs.title: How she came
docs.text:
Nobody knows exactly where Barnacle came from. The most common story is that about seven years ago a scrawny striped kitten walked down the gangplank of a coasting ship that had just tied up, crossed the quay without looking left or right, climbed the fish market steps and lay down in the sun as if she had booked the place. The ship sailed on the next tide without her, and nobody aboard seemed to miss her.

Hesketh, the oyster seller, says he named her, on account of the way she stuck to the steps. Gwennol, the fishmonger at the next stall, says loudly that she named her and that Hesketh has never had an idea of his own in thirty years. The two of them have argued about it ever since, which is to say about as often as they argue about everything else. Barnacle answers to neither of them, and to anyone holding a fish.

docs.title: Her day
docs.text:
Barnacle's day runs on a strict schedule of her own design. At dawn she is at the Fish Market as the boats come in, sitting very straight and very still beside whichever stall is gutting first. Hesketh feeds her better than he feeds himself: the best of the scraps, an oyster now and then, and once, famously, half of his own dinner. She eats it with an air of doing him a favour. Bree, the fishmonger's daughter, slips her fish when nobody is looking, which Barnacle permits.

By mid-morning she has moved to the warmest step, beside Wenna the net-mender, who gives her fish heads and calls her the only creature in the market with any sense. Barnacle sleeps there through the middle of the day, belly to the sun, while the whole market steps around her. Jowan of the Harbour Watch salutes her when he passes. She does not return it.

In the evening she visits the back door of the Salt and Bread, where the kitchen sometimes has something for her and sometimes does not, and at night she goes to work. She hunts rats in the harbour warehouses, and old Hobart the warehouseman leaves a side door open a crack for her. He says she is the only member of staff who never miscounts.

docs.title: The water's edge
docs.text:
For most of her life Barnacle hunted along the tideline too. She would pick her way over the slipway at low tide after crabs and small fish left by the water, and sit at the very end of the quay watching the boats come in, with her tail hanging over the edge.

Then, a little over a year ago, she stopped. One morning on the slipway she froze, stared at the water, flattened her ears and went back up the steps at a run, and she has not been closer to the sea than the top step since. She will not walk the quay. She will not go down to the slipway even when the tide leaves fish flapping on it. If a bucket of seawater is set down near her, she moves.

The fishmongers have noticed. They say she has not gone near the water's edge since whatever she saw that morning, and that she is smarter than all of them. Bree finds it suspicious and has said so to everyone. Some of the older fishermen have quietly started to watch where Barnacle will and will not sit, the way their grandparents watched the gulls.

docs.title: What she wants
docs.text: Barnacle wants sun, fish and a lap at a time of her own choosing. She fears nothing on land, including dogs, dockworkers and Captain Seraphine. What she fears in the water, she cannot say.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: A quest could follow Barnacle on her night rounds through the warehouses, find out what she saw on the slipway the morning she stopped going down, or settle once and for all whether Hesketh or Gwennol gave her her name.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: • Hesketh: feeder

docs.title: Bree
docs.text:
Fishmonger's Daughter

Town Bain Harbour Where Fish Market Role Child Age Child In the game Bree

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Bossy, bright and absolutely fearless around anything with claws. She names every crab she catches.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text: Bree is ten years old and already runs a business. She is the daughter of Gwennol the fishmonger and Cobb the fisherman, the younger sister of Lowen and the granddaughter of Wenna the net-mender, and she helps at her mother's stall in the Fish Market most days. She is bossy, bright and absolutely fearless around anything with claws.

docs.title: The crab shell trade
docs.text:
Bree catches crabs in the rock pools under the harbour wall at low tide. She names every one of them, and she remembers the names. The big ones go to her mother's stall. The empty shells, scrubbed and dried in the sun, she sells to the other harbour children, who use them as boats, helmets, money and treasure. She charges a copper for a small shell and two for a large one, and she keeps her accounts on a slate under the stall. Ottilie, the clerk of the Harbour Hall, once saw the slate and said it was neater than half the ledgers she receives, and Bree has never forgotten it.

She has a long-running and entirely one-sided rivalry with Hesketh, the oyster seller at the next stall, who argues with her mother every single day. Bree has decided that if her mother is going to argue with him, she will too. Hesketh complains about her constantly and saves her the prettiest oyster shells.

She also feeds Barnacle, the harbour cat, scraps of fish when nobody is looking, which is how she learned that Barnacle will not go anywhere near the water's edge any more. Bree finds this suspicious and has said so to everyone.

docs.title: The family
docs.text:
Her mother has the loudest voice in the Fish Market and Bree intends to have the second loudest. Her father is quiet and lets her mother do the talking, and Bree loves him for being the one person who listens to every word she says. Lately he has been quieter than usual. She knows his nets came up torn twice this year, because her grandmother says so to anyone who will listen, and she knows that whatever did it was not, according to her grandmother, any fish Wenna ever knew.

Her brother Lowen has just signed on to his first trading voyage, and the house has been loud about it. Bree is on Lowen's side, mostly because she wants to go to sea herself and thinks it sets a good example.

docs.title: The race
docs.text: More than anything in the world, Bree wants to sail in the summer race around Veligor. She knows exactly how many times Bain Harbour has beaten Goa Harbour since the Harbour Master took the helm, and she can recite the winning margins. She has told Quenna, twice, to her face, that she is small enough to fit anywhere on a boat and light enough not to slow it down. Quenna laughed both times, which Bree has decided means "not yet" rather than "no".

docs.title: What she wants and fears
docs.text: Bree wants to be the youngest sailor ever to crew the race boat. She is not afraid of the sea, but she is afraid of something happening to her father or brother out on it, and she would never say so.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: A quest could start in the rock pools, where Bree has found a crab that is not like any crab she has ever named, or with Bree stowing away aboard a boat on the morning of the race.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Gwennol: mother
  • Cobb: father
  • Lowen: brother
  • Wenna: grandmother

docs.title: Brisa
docs.text:
Harbour Watchwoman

Town Bain Harbour Where Waterfront Role Guard Age Young In the game Brisa

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Sharp, fast and impatient, with a quick tongue and quicker feet. She can outrun anyone on the waterfront and likes to prove it.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text: Brisa is a watchwoman of the Harbour Watch, and she is the fastest runner on the Bain Harbour waterfront. She is nineteen, sharp, fast and impatient, with a quick tongue and quicker feet, and she likes to prove both. If a pickpocket runs on the docks, Brisa catches him. If someone says she cannot, she catches him faster.

docs.title: Why she joined
docs.text:
Brisa grew up on the Waterfront, the daughter of a fish-gutter and a carter, and spent her childhood running. She ran errands, ran races, ran away from the Fish Market whenever there was work to do there. Three years ago her parents moved inland to a cousin's farm near Kaldemor, where the work was steadier and the roads were said to be quieter. Brisa was sixteen. She refused to go, found a room above a sailmaker's loft, and stayed. Her parents write at harvest. She writes back at midwinter, briefly.

She joined the Harbour Watch last spring, not because she wanted to keep the peace, which she finds a little dull, but because it was the best way to see everything that happens in town. The Watch walks every pier and every alley, and it hears every story first, or at least second, after Finch the errand runner, who hears everything first and whom Brisa respects for it. Finch is also the only person on the waterfront who comes close to outrunning her. Twice since the night watch on the outer pier began, she has caught him trying to slip out along it in the dark, marched him back to the dock office, and threatened to tell Garrow the foreman. She has not told Garrow. She remembers what it was like to want to see everything.

docs.title: Jowan
docs.text:
Jowan joined the Watch at about the same time, and he is her friendly rival in all things. He is earnest, careful and far too proud of his coat; she is quick, careless and has never once worn hers buttoned properly. They compete over who reaches a disturbance first, who makes the catch, and whose report Halloran reads to the end. Brisa always arrives first. Jowan always writes more. She has never told him that his reports are better than hers, and she never will, but she has started reading them when he is not looking.

Halloran, their captain, settles most trouble with a hand on the shoulder and a mug of something hot, which Brisa thinks is far too slow and works far too well. She admires him and argues with him in roughly equal measure. Lately he has been standing a watch on the outer pier at night and will not say why, and it is driving her to distraction.

docs.title: The list
docs.text: Since she joined, Brisa has kept a list of the strange things the sailors report: a light under the water, a hull scraped in water too deep for rocks, a net cut clean through, a seal that would not come near the rocks. She writes them in a sewn notebook she keeps inside her coat, with the date and the name of whoever told her, and there are more than sixty entries now. She does not know what they mean. She thinks someone important ought to read it one day, and she would very much like to be standing there when they do. She has no idea that Delphine at the Salt and Bread has been keeping a ledger of her own, or that Halloran has never thought to ask for hers.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: A quest could take Brisa's list to someone who can make sense of it, race her along the waterfront for a wager, or help her find out, at last, what Halloran is watching for on the outer pier.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Halloran: commander
  • Jowan: friendly rival

docs.text:
Baker of Merchant Street

Town Bain Harbour Where Merchant Street Sells Bread, salt rolls and sailors' hard biscuits In the game Bryony
