  • Adventurers, mostly, more every month. And Helewise from the Knights' Court, who buys from both of us and tells each what the other charged. A bandit. I like her.
  • Go on. Come back when something has hit you.

docs.title: Vosk
docs.text:
Master of Bridges

Town Midbarium Where Midbarium Story Vosk in the lore Services Run: The Night Watch, Quests

Don't lean on that rail. It'll hold. I just don't like leaning.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Over, under, and pull. Never trust a knot you didn't tie."
  • "My mother's awl. Reground three times and still the best."
  • "Thrun's drum stand. Checked it this morning. Sound."
  • "Anything that sways, I watch."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Fresh Cable (completes)
  • The Split Drum (completes)
  • New Lashings (gives)
  • The Night Watch (gives)
Dialogue
  • Don't lean on that rail. I tied it, so it will hold, but I don't like leaning. Anything that sways makes me suspicious, Player, and a good deal sways around here.
  • Those stakes went into the far end of the bridge, and the lashings are doubled now. I don't send the young ones out alone any more. Not until I know what's chewing my ropes.
  • Cliff gnawers. Nests under the anchor ledge, teeth like chisels, and they come up in the dark. I knew it was something. Now I know what, and I can tie against it.
  • Thrun and I fitted the new hide, two old fools arguing over every lashing. The stand held. I built that stand when we were both young, you know. It has held every feast since.
  • Well? Say it, then.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: What's wrong on the far bridge?
    • Choice: Let's keep the night watch on the Far Anchor.
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • Vosk, master of bridges. Three generations of Kragvar learned to splice a cable from me, and Brakka is the fourth, though she'd sooner carve stairs. I trust a knot once I've tied it myself.
  • Twice this season I found ropes on the far canyon bridge gnawed half through in the night, always on the side away from town. I spliced them and doubled the lashings. I don't know what does it, and I haven't said so in council.
  • The far canyon bridge carries herders, hunters and masons out to the far slopes. Now it carries them safe, and I sleep. Mostly. I still walk it at dawn.
  • Night on the Far Anchor, then. Keep the gnawers off the anchors till the light comes, and Brakka and I will hold the ropes. Don't let them reach the knots.
  • Test the plank before you trust it.

docs.title: Kor
docs.text:
Sea Warden

Town Goa Harbour Where Goa Harbour Story Kor in the lore Services Quests

Player! The tide likes me today. Probably likes you too.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Three tunes. I know three tunes."
  • "Slack? Slack's for people who like waiting."
  • "Corrie, pen down, we're going!"
  • "Jory! Which stroke was it, off the headland?"

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Word with Iska (gives)
  • Before Slack (gives)
Dialogue
  • Noticed. She said noticed. I've been rowing round the inlet ever since. My arms have opinions.
  • My beach! I put in there yesterday. Only to look. Not before slack. Well.
  • There's my crab-catcher. What's the word?
  • What do you need? Quick, there's a ship at the turn and I want her.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: Tell me about the gap.
    • Choice: Anything worrying you?
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • Kor, sea warden. Full warden since last spring, and I take more ships through than anyone in the house. Ask Halvard, he counts.
  • Quay boy. Rowed the pilot boats from fifteen, eight years under Nessa. She argued with me about every tide. I won about two.
  • My first ship alone? A wool trader, a grey morning, a wind that couldn't make up its mind. I brought her through clean and came up the quay steps like I'd built the gap myself.
  • Nessa said I'd been lucky. I said the tide likes me. She said the tide likes nobody, and then she bought me the first round at the Gap Inn. That's Nessa. Both halves.
  • The gap's a living thing. Fast at the run, flat at slack, and in between it does what it likes. The trick is to like the same thing. Corrie says that's not a trick, it's a guess. Very rude, for an apprentice.
  • Me? No. Well. Sometimes I wonder whether the tide likes me, or whether it just hasn't made up its mind yet. Don't tell Nessa I said that. She'd be pleased.
  • Off you go! Keep the oar in the water!

docs.title: Nessa
docs.text:
Sea Warden

Town Goa Harbour Where The Wardens' House Story Nessa in the lore Services Quests

Player! Come to argue? Good. Sit down.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Too few young pilots. I'll say it till the table's sick of me."
  • "First round's mine. It's always mine."
  • "Slack in an hour. Who wants an oar?"
  • "Kor! If you go before slack again, I'll hear of it."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• One at a Time (gives)
  • Out at Slack (gives)
  • Under the Saltface (gives)
Dialogue
  • My oarsman! Not a word at the table. I want to see their faces when I tell them.
  • Two little pilots, one at a time. Arlo rows as if he's angry with the water. Good. So did I.
  • There's my best argument. Sit.
  • Well? Argue with me, or ask me something.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: The young pilots?
    • Choice: What worries you?
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • Sea warden, twenty years. Cove girl. Varro took me on at ten, and I argued with every lesson he gave me.
  • Seven years back they spoke two names for First Warden, Iska's and mine. I stood up and spoke for her. Why? I wanted my evenings free. Next question.
  • Want to know the first thing Varro ever taught me? Where to stand. I told him I knew where to stand. He let me stand there.
  • The boom came across and put me in the water. He fished me out, put me where he'd said, and never mentioned it again. Neither did I, till now. Don't you mention it either.
  • The old wardens are retiring and the seas get rougher every year. There aren't enough apprentices in the boats to fill the gap. Ha. Fill the gap. I've used that one at the table. Nobody laughed there either.
  • I put it to the table. They argued. I argued back. Nobody has said no yet, which at that table is very nearly yes.
  • That the gap gets harder to read, and one rough season we'll be a pilot short on the wrong day. I don't fear losing an argument. I fear winning one too late.
  • Go on. And if anyone asks, you lost the argument.

docs.title: Varro
docs.text:
Eldest of the Sea Wardens

Town Goa Harbour Where The Wardens' House Story Varro in the lore Services Quests

Aye. You're up early. Or late.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Wind's backing. Dirty turn tonight."
  • "Nobody waits for slack any more."
  • "My knees know the weather before anyone."
  • "Hm. No. Closer."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Where the Eddy Turned (gives)
  • The Lee Rocks (gives)
  • Three Mornings (gives)
Dialogue
  • You've been out to the Jaw with an old man and brought him home. Sit. Not there. That end.
  • The lee's clear, Kor says. He sat there an hour this morning waiting on a slack. First time in his life.
  • The boy came back. Stood a yard to my left. I said nothing. He said nothing. Good morning, that was.
  • You again. Good.
  • Ask it, then. Before the turn.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: Tell me about the pilots.
    • Choice: What troubles you?
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • Varro. Warden fifty-six years. Never lost a ship in the gap. Luck.
  • Knees stopped me five years back. A pilot who can't brace in a cross-sea is no use to anyone, and I said so first. They still bring me the hard questions. I still answer them.
  • That oilskin by my door? Maili's. My wife. She fished the coves, and she handled a boat better than half the wardens. I told her so once. She held it over me thirty years.
  • Fever took her, fourteen years back. I keep the oilskin where I see it going out. That's all. That's enough talking.
  • Iska is the best of them. Don't tell her. Nessa argued every lesson and then did exactly what I said. Still does.
  • Kor goes before slack. One day the tide will tell him what it thinks of that. Corrie writes it all down. She'll be the best of the lot, if Kor doesn't drown her first.
  • The water. Nothing I could put in a book. Or I'm getting old. Ysmay says I've been old for twenty years. She may be right.
  • You saw it with me, out under the Jaw. I had been telling myself it was my eyes. I'd rather have been right about my eyes.
  • Aye.

docs.title: Wat
docs.text:
Errand Boy

Town Selsior Where Royal Plaza Story Wat in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Errand for the warden! Coming through!"
  • "Your purse is badly tied, mister. Just saying."
  • "Gate to palace steps without one named street. Bet you can't."
  • "Kenric's humming again. Means the steel's being difficult."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Better Hand Than Mine (gives)
  • A Message Past the Gate (gives)
Dialogue
  • Warden says he never thought it was me. Not for a minute. I'm still watching purses, Player. Watching.
  • Wat. I run errands for Reynold, the warden. Messages, measures, and telling stallholders they're about to have a very bad afternoon.
  • Every alley, every gap in every fence, every courtyard with two doors. Kitchens let you run straight through if you shout 'Errand for the warden!' loud enough.
  • Two summers ago I tried for his purse. He caught my wrist without even looking round.
  • Then he asked how fast I could get a message to the far end of the market, and timed me. I've run for him ever since. Haven't let him down once.
  • See you! Probably before you see me.
  • Your purse is tied wrong, Player. Here, like that. ... What? I'm honest now. Mostly. What do you want?
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: You know the city well?
    • Choice: Why does the warden trust you?
    • Choice: Goodbye.

docs.title: Wenna
docs.text:
Net-Mender

Town Bain Harbour Where Bain Harbour Story Wenna in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Every knot in this net is mine."
  • "That woman sells her fish too cheap. Don't tell her I said she sells good fish."
  • "Nobody sits on that step. Leave it be."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Strip of Net (gives)
  • Twine for the Saltlark (gives)
Dialogue
  • If you are going to stand there, hold this end. What do you want?
    • Choice: How long have you mended nets here?
    • Choice: Whose step is that, the empty one?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • All my life. My mother mended on this step, and I sat beside her from the time I was five and could not keep my fingers still.
  • My Davey fished the Puffin. I mended his last net and gave it to our Cobb. Now I mend Cobb's.
  • Kenver's. Ysolde's husband. He died mending beside me, sixteen years ago. I held his hand and sent a boy running for Clemence.
  • Nobody sits there. The cat sits there. The cat is allowed.
  • Go on, then.

docs.title: Wilbur
docs.text:
Farmer

Town Kaldemor Where The Last Stile Story Wilbur in the lore Services Quests

Morning, Player! The pumpkins say hello.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Grow, my beauty. Grow."
  • "No snail touches this year's pumpkin."
  • "Pumpkins, turnips, beans. Best soil east of the square."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Trail Too Broad (gives)
Dialogue
  • Biggest farm east of the square, and every row of it hard won. What can I do for you, Player?
    • Choice: What do you grow?
    • Choice: What happened to your prize pumpkin?
    • Choice: How is Digby doing?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Pumpkins, turnips and beans, and most of it goes to Old Marta's stall. She has bought from me for twenty years and still squeezes every turnip.
  • My family has farmed this ground for four generations. I talk to the pumpkins. They grow better for it, whatever Hattie says.
  • Snails. The week before last year's fair. They ate a hole in it big enough for Tam to put his head through, and he did.
  • This year's champion sleeps under a net inside a ring of crushed shell. Some nights I sit up with a lantern. I take the snails personally, Player.
  • Best farmhand I ever had, and now he means to be a warrior. I gave him my blessing and a good pair of boots. He still comes back at harvest, bless him.
  • Off you go, Player. Step around the beans.

docs.title: Wilf
docs.text:
Spore Gatherer

Town Kaldemor Where The Last Stile Story Wilf in the lore Services Quests

Hmph. Player. You are standing on a good patch of damp.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Smells like rain. Good."
  • "Brown caps, orange caps, and the pale ones."
  • "Too bold by half, those Shrooms."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Shiny Things (gives)
  • Shiny Things, Found (gives)
  • Spores for Two (gives)
  • Too Bold (gives)
Dialogue
  • Spores and caps, if you want them. Mushrooms are the only thing in this town I do not grumble about. What is it?
    • Choice: What do you gather?
    • Choice: How was your trip?
    • Choice: Do you need a hand?
    • Choice: Are the Shrooms quieter now?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • The Bluecaps are, now the Mother is down. The Shrooms are not. They still go past me with their spoons and thimbles, Player, all the same way, past the far side of the woods. They are still going somewhere.
  • Mushroom spores, mostly, for Rosa's bread and Bram's potions. I grow a few caps behind my cottage too: brown, orange, and a pale one I have no name for.
  • Rosa pays on the nail. Bram argues about every bag. Twenty years I have sold to both, and carried their news back and forth for my sins.
  • A month away with my sister, south past the hills. She was poorly. She is better now.
  • Came home at the start of summer and the woods had gone strange. The Shrooms followed me in threes and fours and would not scatter. One knocked my basket clean off my arm.
  • Maybe. The woods are too bold for me to gather alone these days, and I do not say that lightly. Come back when you are handier with a weapon, Player.
  • Go on, then. Mind the caps.

docs.title: Wilmot
docs.text:
Ropemaker

Town Bain Harbour Where Bain Harbour Story Wilmot in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "humming an old sea song"
  • "There's a knot for everything. Everything."
  • "Turn the wheel steady, lad. Steady."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Child for the Wheel (gives)
  • The Last Verse (gives)
Dialogue
  • Fifty years on this rope walk. What can an old ropemaker do for you?
    • Choice: How is rope made?
    • Choice: Do you have an apprentice?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • You spin the yarn, you twist the yarn into strands, you lay the strands into rope, walking backwards the whole length of the shed. A child turns the wheel for a copper.
  • Old Penrose made me spin yarn for a whole year before he let me lay a strand. Best year of my life, and I hated it.
  • Had one. Tamar. Morwenna's husband, Ossie's father. Came to me at fourteen, best hands I ever saw. Lung fever took him seven years ago.
  • Nobody young wants to walk backwards in a shed all day any more. I don't blame them. I worry, though.
  • Fair winds, Player.

docs.title: Winifred
docs.text:
Storyteller of the Old Quarter

Town Selsior Where Old Quarter Story Winifred in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Come back at lamplighting, dearie. That's when the stories start."
  • "On Monday it came out of the ground. On Thursday, the sky. Who's to say?"
  • "Four peoples, four tales, and I've kept every one of them."
  • "Hush, Simkin. I got it wrong on purpose."
  • "Some stories climb the roofs before the sun is up."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Story for the Lane (gives)
  • The Fifth Tale (gives)
Dialogue
  • Winifred, seventy-four and born in this very lane. I married the cobbler next door forty-nine years ago, and we've argued happily ever since.
  • Half the children of the old quarters grew up on my doorstep. My grandson Hodge grew up a little higher than that.
  • As a girl I sewed for the envoys' households, and every one of the four peoples told it differently. In the Savage halls it was a horned giant wreathed in flame. The others told it their own ways.
  • But they all agree on the ending: the four peoples beat it once, together, and the kingdom they made is still here. That's the part I always tell twice.
  • The one I'm telling, dearie, for as long as I'm telling it. The children argue all the way home, and that's the whole point.
  • Off you go. Come back at lamplighting, and I'll tell it differently.
  • Well now, a new face on my step. Sit down, Player, the stool won't bite. What would you like to hear?
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: Tell me about the Balrog.
    • Choice: Which version is true?
    • Choice: Another evening.
  • Come at lamplighting, dearie. Tonight the meadow stays green at the end of the story.

docs.title: Winnie
docs.text:
Weaver

Town Kaldemor Where Kaldemor Story Winnie in the lore Services Quests

Player! Come in, sit by the loom. Did you hear about... oh, I will tell you in a minute.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Clack, clack, clack."
  • "Over, under, over, under."
  • "I have a scrap of that one somewhere!"

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Quietly, for Dottie (gives)
Dialogue
  • Wool, cloth and blankets, and a good chat while the shuttle runs. What can I do for you, Player?
    • Choice: What do you weave?
    • Choice: What are all those scraps?
    • Choice: How is Dottie?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Cloth and blankets, mostly, from the wool off Dottie's sheep. And I spin the yarn for Wren's caps, hers first every autumn.
  • Wren and I have been friends thirty years, ever since she came in to complain about a skein. Best complaint I ever had.
  • I keep a finger-long scrap of every cloth I have ever made, pinned up in my back room. Hob and Mabel's wedding blanket, Nell's cradle cloth, the mayor's first fair-day cloak. I might even have one of yours, Player.
  • She has been bringing me less wool lately, and she has the look of somebody keeping a worry in her pocket. I will not pry. Not much, anyway.
  • Off you go, Player. Come back and tell me everything.

docs.title: Wren
docs.text:
Orin's Wife

Town Kaldemor Where Kaldemor Story Wren in the lore

Hello, dear. Orin tells the same stories, but I never tire of them.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Orin, you are shouting again."
  • "I knit caps for every child in Kaldemor. Some even wear them."
  • "The park is nicest in the afternoon."

docs.title: Wulfric
docs.text:
Vault Warden

Town Selsior Where The Royal Vault Story Wulfric in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Oh. Hello. Mind your head on the arch."
  • "A sword is a promise. A promise ought to be kept bright."
  • "Past the old records room. Twice, now."
  • "Thank you? No, no. It was nothing. Really."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Present, Unlabelled (gives)
  • Digging Behind the Vault (gives)
  • The Quarry Village (gives)
Dialogue
  • She has not labelled it. She keeps it on her desk and touches it when she counts. ...Thank you, Player.
  • Oh. Hello. Sorry, I am big, I know. I am Wulfric. I watch the vault doors.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: What is it like down here?
    • Choice: Is everything quiet?
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • I grew up in a quarry village upstream. Joined the Guard at eighteen, and stood at the palace gates for eight years.
  • Then Aldous came up and looked at me. Counted me twice, I think. I have been down here twelve years now.
  • Quiet. Cool. Old. I like it. I know every corridor by the sound of my boots, and I can hear a door left ajar three rooms away.
  • My wife Jocelyn keeps the ledgers. I carry them up the stairs. I always have. That is how we... well. That is how.
  • Twelve years, and I have never drawn my sword down here. I oil it every week anyway. But Jocelyn's box keeps her awake, so I walk past that room twice now. Just in case.
  • Mind the step. And thank you for... no, nothing. Goodbye.

docs.title: Wynne
docs.text:
Copyist of the Old Records

Town Fairy Forest Where The Old Records Story Wynne in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Leaf forty-one. Forty-two. Forty-..."
  • "Fresh paper, steady hand."
  • "..."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• The Gap in the Numbering (gives)
  • Whom to Tell (gives)
Dialogue
  • Player. Sit with me while I finish this leaf? It goes faster with company.
  • Player. I was hoping you'd come by.
  • The oldest records, the ones too fragile to handle. I copy them onto fresh paper so the originals can rest in the dark.
  • You notice things, copying. The numbering. The stitching. Whether a hand was in a hurry.
  • No. I mean. I'm not sure yet, and I don't say things until I'm sure.
  • Ask me again another day.
  • She's stern because the records need her to be. She's not stern with me.
  • Most days.
  • Wynne lays down her pen, very carefully, before she speaks.
    • Choice: What do you copy?
    • Choice: Is something wrong?
    • Choice: Your grandmother?
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • Goodbye, Player.

docs.title: Wystan
docs.text:
Stablemaster

Town Selsior Where Knights' Court Story Wystan in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Wrong boots. Out of my stable."
  • "Easy, girl. Easy. Nothing out here but old Wystan."
  • "A horse knows a liar. I'll take her word over yours."
  • "Don't salute near the horses. Spooks them."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• The Horse That Came Back Alone (gives)
  • Where the Horse Sweats (gives)
Dialogue
  • What. You're standing in my light, in my stable, in those boots. Wystan. Stablemaster. Make it quick.
    • Choice: Tell me about the stables.
    • Choice: The horses seem uneasy.
    • Choice: Who is the young rider?
    • Choice: I'll go.
  • Fifty-eight years in this straw, forty of them stablemaster. Three captains. I know every horse here by name, temper and the sound of its feet. Can't say that for the captains.
  • They come back from the roads jumpy. Wild-eyed. Good steady animals kicking their stalls at night over nothing.
  • It's not the feed, the water or the shoes. I checked. It's something they smell out there, past the Greenwood. I'd give a good deal to know what.
  • Downs Edge, where the road passes the downs. Boar musk, and something under it. You found the place. Now I only need to know the something. Hmph.
  • My grandson, Aylwin. Rides the road patrol under Edric. Good hands with a horse. I taught him that much. Don't tell him I said good.
  • Mind the muck on your way out. Mind it better than you did coming in.

docs.title: Yarrek
docs.text:
Goat Herder

Town Midbarium Where Midbarium Story Yarrek in the lore Services Quests

Shh. Slowly. They startle.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Easy, Pebble. Easy."
  • "Counted twice. All here."
  • "Old Tuft used to eat from my hand."
  • "A goat knows its name. It just doesn't always answer."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• The Wild Goats (gives)
  • Three Goats' Tracks (gives)
Dialogue
  • Shh. That's Pebble, and Ash, and Old Tuft, in the far pen. They slipped away one night last month and came back up from the valley two days later. Now they bite. They won't eat from my hand.
  • So they ran from trees that walked. No wonder their eyes went wild. Kesh wanted to come all the way down; I'm glad you sent him home from the trailhead.
  • Old Tuft ate from my hand this morning. Only a little. The rimwort soothed their bites, and the quiet did the rest. They're coming back to themselves, Player.
  • Talk softly. What is it?
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: Tell me about the herd.
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • Yarrek. I lead the family's goats between the high pastures and the camps, and I walk at the back of the herd. My father taught me the herd, and my mother taught me to sing to it.
  • I know every goat by name. I count them twice each evening now, since the three came back. Harra says I talk to them more than to her. The goats listen better.
  • Walk slow near the pens.

docs.title: Ysolde
docs.text:
Keeper of the Light

Town Bain Harbour Where Bain Harbour Story Ysolde in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Forty years. Never missed a night."
  • "Seraphine comes in too fast. Corwin comes in on the minute."
  • "A hundred and seventeen stairs. My knees count every one."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• In Ink, Not in the Margin (gives)
  • Keeping the Light (gives)
Dialogue
  • I keep the light. I count the ships. I have opinions about every captain in this harbour. Which would you like?
    • Choice: What do you think of the captains?
    • Choice: How long have you kept the light?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Annis sails as if the sea were listening. Corwin is a clock with a hull on it, and I mean that kindly. Seraphine comes in under too much sail and blows me a kiss when I scold her.
  • I watched Quenna learn to sail as a deck girl from the top of that tower. Fell in twice before she was thirteen.
  • Forty years, since I was thirty. My father, old Peder, kept it before me.
  • My Kenver died on the fish market steps sixteen years ago. I lit the lamp that night as usual. Somebody had to.
  • Fair winds, Player.

docs.title: Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway
docs.text:
Young Adventurer

Town Urbanograd Where Urbanograd Story Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway in the lore Services Quests

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "One day they will sing about me at the Night Market."
  • "Footwork, guard. Footwork, guard. Footwork..."
  • "My arm says rain tomorrow."
  • "Dare me. Go on. Dare me."
  • "Torvi! Again! I was not ready!"

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• What Bravery Costs (gives)
  • When to Run (gives)
Dialogue
  • Zip! Zip Calloway. Nobody calls me Zinnia except when I am in trouble, which is often, so you might hear it. I am going to be famous. I have a head start: I already broke an arm.
  • Not wasted! I wrote it on my wall. And the bill part, too, smaller, underneath. I argue with it every morning. It wins.
  • I brought the lamp back! In one piece! Margo checked it three ways and then hugged it. Then me. In that order.
  • You. Did. It. Without me. I am furious. I am also so happy I could fall off a bank. Tell me again. The size of it. The noise.
  • Second day, Player! That is what we train on now. You walk away, and you come back when it is yours. Torvi says I am getting it. Torvi said it twice.
  • What do you want to know? Ask me anything. Ask me about the arm.
    • Choice: Tell me about your arm.
    • Choice: What is Torvi teaching you?
    • Choice: Margo's spark lamp?
    • Choice: Nothing. Goodbye.
  • Last spring, a caravan to Kaldemor, two days out. A monster burst out of the brush. Huge. Bigger than a wagon. Bigger than two wagons. Eyes like lanterns. Tusks like, like scythes!
  • And I charged it. Alone. Across a raging river and up a cliff, and I nearly had it, and then the cliff gave way. Arm in two places. Tick has three versions in his book. This one is the best. Do not ask Torvi.
  • Something big came out of the brush, and I ran at it with a borrowed sword, and it was gone, and I fell off a bank onto a rock. That is it. Version four. It is shorter. Tick likes it best. I am starting to as well.
  • Torvi carried me back to the wagons over one shoulder while I was still shouting about tusks. Then laughed at me. Then, back here, I followed Torvi round the Gate Walk until Torvi gave in.
  • Every morning, the open ground inside the gate. Footwork, guard, when to stand. And when to run. That one I hate. My feet only know forwards.
  • Margo built a lamp that throws sparks to scare monsters off the roads! Bolt tested it on a broom, a barrel and himself. I volunteered before she finished asking. I promised to bring it back. I will. Probably. Definitely.
  • It works! On ordinary boar, anyway. Sparks, bang, and off they go squealing. I brought it back, like I promised. Margo says I am her favourite tester. Bolt says that is not fair.
  • Bye! If anyone dares you to do anything, send them to me.

docs.title: Zirra
docs.text:
Bowyer

Town Midbarium Where Zirra's Workshop Story Zirra in the lore Services Quests

Hold your weapon up. No, as you'd hold it at a charge. Hm.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Nobody's rope is as good as mine. Except Vosk's. Maybe."
  • "Twisted wood makes the truest bows. Don't ask me why."
  • "My brother, the Old One. Ha."
  • "You hold that like a soup ladle."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• A Message for the Old One (gives)
  • New Staves (gives)
  • Twisted Wood (gives)
Dialogue
  • Hold your weapon up. No, as you'd hold it at a charge. Hm. I've seen worse. I've seen better on twelve-year-olds. What do you want?
  • Gnarlwood. Twisted half a century in the wind and still sound to the heart. I'll get a stave out of this that outlives both of us. Don't look so pleased with yourself.
  • You gave it to him. And what did my brother say? No, don't tell me. I'll know from his face at the next council. He never could hide anything from me.
  • Sound staves from the edge of the Dry Hills. I only complained the whole way because you walked too slowly. My wood stock hasn't been this good in years. Go on, hold a bow. You've earned the lecture.
  • Well? I have work on the bench.
    • Choice: Show me your weapons.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: What is the Old One like?
    • Choice: Goodbye.
  • Uskari-made, every piece. My bows wait for hands that can use them; these are for hunters who like to get close.
  • Zirra, bowyer of the rim. Every bow on patrol came off my bench. My best staves came from twisted trees low in the canyon valleys, and those valleys are red on Skarra's map now. My wood stock has never been lower.
  • The Old One is my little brother. I raised him from six and taught him his first bow, and he held it backwards. I'll tease him till one of us dies. Anyone else says a word against him, I'll put an arrow through their hat.
  • Practise. Then practise again.

docs.title: Professions
docs.text:
Gathering professions take materials from nodes in the fields; making professions turn them into items.

Professions go up to level 99. Ranks: Novice (1), Apprentice (20), Journeyman (40), Expert (60), Master (80).

docs.title: EXP by level gap
docs.text:
Gathering a node or making a recipe well below your profession level gives less EXP:

Your level above the node or recipe EXP 0-4 100% 5-9 60% 10-19 25% 20 or more 5%

docs.title: Selsior
docs.text: Quest Kind Level From Summary The Swordsman's Trial Story 30 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Warrior of level 30 into the Swordsman's way. Prove it on the Selsior Downs: defeat 30 of the Downs Boars of the Thyme Banks or the Chalk Hive Bees of the Chalk Hives and bring back 5 trial seals. The Swordmaster's Trial Story 70 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Swordsman of level 70 into the Swordmaster's way. Prove it with a long hunt in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 200 of its monsters. The Grand Swordmaster's Trial Story 120 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Swordmaster of level 120 to the top of the sword's road. Prove it once more in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 400 of its monsters. The Sword Saint's Trial Story 160 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Grand Swordmaster of level 160 beyond the Guard's ranks, to the Sword Saint. Prove your edge in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 600 of its monsters. Bounty: The Hedge Lanes Repeatable 5 Edric Lieutenant Edric posts a standing bounty on the Hedge Lanes outside the Tree Gate: defeat 30 of its slimes, pigs or orange mushrooms. Selsior pays it every time. One More Round Side 5 Pim Pim wants a sparring partner after drill. He thinks watching someone fight for real would help more: clear 25 monsters of the Hedge Lanes while he takes notes. Oil for the Gate Lamps Side 6 Baldwin Baldwin needs more oil for the extra lamps he keeps burning near the city gate. Fetch his order from Gilbert the candlemaker, then see the lamps at the gate. Biscuit Follows His Nose Side 6 Biscuit Biscuit has caught a smell and wants you to come with him: out to the wayside well on the Hedge Lanes, where the slimes have been at somebody's dropped lunch. Clear 20 slimes so he can investigate. Word for Clement Side 6 Gideon Gideon heard Clement rehearse to the pigeons and thinks it was splendid. He is far too proud to climb down and say so. Tell Clement for him. As Far as a Courier Rides Side 6 Peterkin Peterkin wants to know how far a royal courier gets before the first bell. Run to the far end of the Hedge Lanes for him, chasing off pigs on the way. Apothecary First Side 7 Brann Brann sends hurt travellers to an apothecary first, and the apothecary is short of slime bubbles for her salve. Bring Brann 12, then fetch the week's count of hurt travellers from Swithin. Heavier Than a Broom Side 7 Hodge Hodge wants to know how a real fight goes, not a drill. Clear the pigs on the Hedge Lanes and tell Mab how it went, so she can tell it with cartwheels. Polish for the Dais Side 7 Hugh Hugh polishes the Great Bell's dais every morning, and his polish is running out. The old Warden swore by a polish thickened with slime bubbles. Bring him some. Past the Light Side 8 Baldwin Baldwin wants to know what moves in the dark just past the last lamp outside the Tree Gate. Walk out to the end of the Hedge Lanes and clear what you find. Post the Notice Side 8 Clement Clement must cry the Knights' Court's notice to travellers: keep to daylight hours on the World Tree Road. He would like it posted at the wayside well on the Hedge Lanes as well, and the Orange Mushrooms there are no help. The Third Cut, Slowly Side 8 Tobe Tobe asks to see the third cut done on something that moves. Defeat 30 orange mushrooms on the Hedge Lanes while he watches your feet, then tell Pim what he learned. The Fifth Tale Side 8 Winifred A traveller on Winifred's step told a fifth version of the Balrog's coming, one she has never heard, and said he had it from someone by the wayside well on the Hedge Lanes. She wants to know if the well is real. A Still Evening Side 9 Hugh Hugh asks something he has never asked anyone: wait with Baldwin until the dais lamps are lit, then stand by the Great Bell and listen. Bounty: The Waystone Meadows Repeatable 10 Edric Edric's standing bounty on the Waystone Meadows: defeat 30 of its ribbon pigs, green mushrooms or horny mushrooms. Selsior pays it every time. A Bell He Does Not Know Side 10 Gideon From his perch Gideon knows every bell in Selsior, but lately a new one clanks from the north. He thinks it is the shepherd's hut on the Waystone Meadows. Find out, and see why it rings. The Great Waystone Side 10 Mab Mab heard that from the top of the great waystone on the Waystone Meadows you can see the palace. She is not allowed past the gate. You are. Too Early for Patrol Side 10 Pim Pim volunteered for a meadow patrol nobody wanted, and Bertrand said no. Clear 30 monsters on the Waystone Meadows in his place, then tell Bertrand the road is clean. What I Saw From the Ridge Side 11 Hodge From the highest ridge of the old quarters Hodge has seen, every dawn, flocks of birds lift off the Waystone Meadows all at once, as if something startled them. Go and look, then tell Wat, who will know a shortcut back. Ribbons for Dusk Side 11 Mirabel Mirabel wants ribbons for her ankles that flutter when she turns. The Ribbon Pigs of the Waystone Meadows wear the best ones. A Courier's Knot Side 11 Peterkin Real couriers tie their bundles in a courier's knot. Bring Peterkin ribbons from the Ribbon Pigs, then show Osbert the knot. Not in the Book Side 12 Brann A traveller came through Brann's gate without appearing in Swithin's book. Hollis heard from a carter that a man like him was seen at the great waystone. Ask Hollis, go to the waystone and clear 30 monsters on the Waystone Meadows. Tell Hodge Side 12 Mab Mab wants her friend Hodge to know someone stood on top of the great waystone. Hodge runs the rooftops of the old quarters and thinks nothing is higher. Clear the Stretch Side 12 Perrin Perrin rides the World Tree Road to the Tree's foot, and the Ribbon Pigs of the Waystone Meadows keep scattering his horse. Clear 25 of them, then ride on to the Rootlands. A Story for the Lane Side 12 Winifred The children of the lane now ask whether the Balrog is coming back. Winifred wants a happy ending she can stand behind: a meadow that was safe for her as a girl, walked and made safe again. Ask the Old Man Side 13 Clement Clement wants to know what the plaza sounded like the day the crowd cheered the Great Bell, and he has never quite dared ask Gideon straight out. Ask for him. The Far Side of the Bell Side 13 Mirabel Mirabel wants a second pair of ears: stand on the far side of the Great Bell at dusk, when the wind is kind, then ask Fulke whether he heard anything over his own lute. A Seventh Account Side 13 Tobe Mariota heard of a seventh account of the Sword Saint on a bookseller's cart, overturned at the Waystone Meadows. Ask Mariota where, then clear 30 monsters from around the waystones so Tobe's book can be fetched. Down the Ladder Side 14 Gideon Once a month Gideon climbs down to sit with Aldous at the Royal Vault when it closes. His knees are complaining. Tell Aldous he is coming, so the old keeper keeps the bench warm. The End of the Road Side 14 Hollis Hollis can't leave his post, and he has always wanted to know what is at the far end of a road. Walk the World Tree Road to the Rootlands, where it ends at the Tree's foot, and clear 30 of the monsters there. Mushrooms for the Pie Side 14 Maud For the first time in years Maud's dawn list has something no stall has: the mushroom pickers will not go out to the Waystone Meadows. Clear the Horny Mushrooms so they will. Where No One Watches Side 15 Avice Avice wants to train where no recruit can watch. Go with her to the Rootlands and defeat 30 of its monsters, keeping pace with her. Bounty: The Rootlands Repeatable 15 Edric Edric's standing bounty on the Rootlands at the World Tree's foot: defeat 30 of its stumps, dark stumps or axe stumps. Selsior pays it every time. A Cutting from the Roots Side 15 Godwin Godwin wants something green from the World Tree's own ground for his kingdom border. Look over the Tree's outermost root in the Rootlands, then thin out the Dark Stumps there. A Theory for Margery Side 15 Maud Maud has a new theory about what Dame Orsa did for the crown. Tell Margery, her oldest friend. Then ask Dame Orsa straight out, since Maud never has. Wood for New Clubs Side 16 Lambert Lambert's juggling clubs are cracked. For the queen's festival he wants new ones turned from Dark Stump bark, which is light and hard as horn. A Stick That Holds Side 17 Avice Avice's walking stick from the highlands finally broke. Bring her 10 pieces of hard dark stump bark from the Rootlands to bind a new one, then tell Pim she is not going soft. Stern, Then Smiling Side 17 Hollis A traveller Hollis welcomed claimed he had come straight in off the Royal Road, but there was black bark dust on his boots. Bring 10 dark stump bark to compare, then tell Brann. A Word from Rafe Side 18 Lambert Lambert does not know how a street juggler gets invited to perform for the queen. His old teacher Rafe might. Ask him on Theatre Row. The Downs I Grew Up On Side 20 Bartholomew Bartholomew grew up a shepherd's son on the downs beyond the capital. He hears the bees there have turned mean, and he would like someone to go and see. Short a Rider Story 20 Edric Edric's road patrol is a rider short. Ride out with Aylwin to Downs Edge, where the downs meet the World Tree Road, and clear 20 wild bees off the road verge. Then report to Aylwin. The Pushed-Up Grating Story 20 Ida The grating in Steps Lane was found pushed up from below. Ida takes her father's old map of the drains and asks you to go down: see the Old Drains for yourself and clear the rats. Courier's Stride Side 20 Perrin Perrin, the Royal Courier, will teach his burst of speed to anyone who can run his old test: the palace steps, the great gate and back to him in the plaza. The Long Way Side 20 Perrin Perrin wants the Dark Stumps on the Rootlands thinned so he can ride the short way to the Tree. Then tell his cousin Tilda he took it. A Message Past the Gate Side 20 Wat Wat has a message from the warden for the shepherds' sheepfold on Downs Edge, and his shortcuts stop at the city gate. Carry it, and clear the bees around the fold. Why the Bees Are Mean Side 21 Alaric Nobody can tell Alaric why the bees have gone mean. Bring him wild bee stingers for his jars, and show them to Godwin first. What the Patrols Meet Side 21 Aveline Reports are paper; the queen wants eyes. Ride out to Downs Edge, deal with the wild bees at the road's verge, and tell Leofric what you saw. Rats in the Lower Stacks Side 21 Benedict Rats have come up into the great library's lower stacks from the old drains. Benedict wants them gone before they find the Aristocrat chronicles. A Ballad on the Ridge Side 21 Cecily Fulke taught Cecily a downs shepherds' ballad and says it should be sung where it was made. She is too shy to go. She asks the player to clear the way and listen to the wind. Rosemary for the Roast Side 21 Cuthbert Midbarium's slow mutton wants fresh rosemary, and the market's is all twigs. Gather rosemary on the Downs for Cuthbert. The Extra Brace Side 21 Dickon Stirges have started coming up through the gratings at night and roosting under Dickon's skywalks. Clear them from the drains below, and let Ida know: she walks the lanes under those walks. Pins That Do Not Bend Side 21 Edith Edith's market pins bend in heavy cloth. The stingers of the wild bees on the downs, she says, make finer pins than any smith. A Song from the Downs Side 21 Fulke A shepherd at the gate sang Fulke a song about a white bank on the downs where the bees sing all day. Is it a real place? Find the singing bank on Downs Edge. Chalk on the Board Side 21 Hamon A story on Hamon's road board says the dew pond at Downs Edge is overrun. Before he leaves it up, he wants it checked: go to the dew pond and clear 30 monsters on Downs Edge. Three Days Too Long Side 21 Joan A lodger's name has stayed on Joan's slate three days past his return. She asks you to walk out to Downs Edge, find his camp and clear the bees off the verge. The Cost of Guards Side 21 Reynold Prices from the far towns are up, and Reynold has checked: it is not greed but the cost of guards on the roads. The wool and honey carts from the downs pass Downs Edge. Clear it. A Dark Ridge Side 21 Theobald Theobald wants a ridge on the downs with no city lamps, for his students and his glass. The bees will have to go first. The Wall Under the Stage Side 21 Tibb The mice have fled the Gilded Stage's under-stage for the flies. Lettice asked which cellar wall is nearest the old drains. Tibb wants it looked at from the other side. Where the Horse Sweats Story 21 Wystan Wystan wants to know what the patrol horses smell out there. Ride the road past Downs Edge and note where a horse starts to sweat, then hunt 25 downs boars on the Thyme Banks, where the smell leads. Boars on the Downs Side 22 Aylwin The boars on the Thyme Banks are the same breed as the pack Aylwin faced on the road to Kaldemor, and they are getting closer to the road. Defeat 30 of them and bring back 5 tusks for his grandfather. A Name Without a Mark Side 22 Bertrand A name on Bertrand's list has stopped appearing in the patrol reports: a former recruit posted to the old watch post on the Thyme Banks. Ask Helewise where his boots were sent, go to the post, and clear 30 downs boars around it. Bites for the Book Side 22 Edwina Edwina has stitched too many rat bites this season. She wants the drains below the lanes thinned, and the tails brought back so she can measure the bites against them. The Gnawed Ledgers Side 22 Jocelyn Something has gnawed a ledger in the vault's lowest records room. Deal with the rats of the Old Drains and bring Jocelyn their tails to count. Real Tusks for the Warrior Side 22 Lavinia Lavinia wants real boar tusks on the Savage warrior's costume in the Balrog War play. The gallery can tell painted wood from the real thing. Hold the Lantern Story 22 Lettice Lettice needs someone to hold the lantern at the mouth of a deep tunnel while she goes in, and to deal with the rats that come out at it. Nip won't go first. Scratching in the Cellars Side 22 Osbert Rats are coming up from the old drains into the palace cellars. Deal with them in the Old Drains, then tell Cuthbert his stores are safe. The Empty Box Side 22 Rafe Rafe's Balrog puppet is gone from its box. Teeth marks on the lid. The rats of the drains have been coming up into the Row's cellars. Rosemary for the Magician Side 22 Rosamund Rosamund wants a crown of real rosemary from the downs for the play's Magician. For remembrance. And because silk flowers look like silk flowers. Leather Off the Downs Side 22 Simkin The carters have stopped bringing good hide into the city, and Simkin's bench is short of leather. He wants ten boar hides from the downs. My Father's Fold Side 23 Bartholomew Bartholomew's father built a sheepfold on the Thyme Banks. Boars have come up onto the downs and root up the folds. See whether his still stands. The Shepherds' Hut Side 23 Crispin Crispin wants to know what it is like to sit where shepherds tell stories at night, with the boars outside. For the play. Probably. Boars on the Patrol Road Side 23 Elinor The boars of the Thyme Banks have been charging the road patrol's horses. Thin them out, then find Aylwin of the road patrol and see that he is whole. Comb for the Shepherds Story 23 Gilbert Gilbert sent a frame of comb to the shepherds' hives on the downs and asked how their bees fare. The hives stand empty: the bees have gone wild into the chalk. Bring him pieces of their wild comb. Wings for a Bat Side 23 Marigold Marigold means to prove she deserves a part by arriving at rehearsal as the most terrifying bat ever seen on a stage. She is forbidden to go into the drains. You are not. How the Line Held Side 23 Percival Percival wants to know how it feels to stand against a charge, for the play's Savage warrior. He would go himself, but there is a matinee. A Line Under a Name Side 23 Swithin A wool buyer Swithin wrote going out to the downs a year ago never came back through the gate. Find the milestone at Downs Edge she would have passed, clear 30 wild bees there, and tell Brann what you found. A Wing on the Sill Side 24 Agnes Agnes found a leathery wing on a windowsill in the long gallery. Peterkin says the old drains are full of stirges. Find out whether he is right. A Rumour for Mother Side 24 Alaric Alaric heard in the kitchens that boars are digging up the sheepfolds on the Downs. See the high fold on the Thyme Banks for yourself, chase off the boars, and tell the queen. The Wrong Cover Side 24 Aubrey Aubrey's page came out of a chest of old Guard drill books. He wants the rest of the book, and old paper in this city ends up in the Academy or down the drains. Go down to the Cisterns, clear 30 of what lives there and search an old shelf. A Question of Riding Side 24 Aveline The princess comes to breakfast with blistered hands. The queen asks you to put one question to Osbert and one to Elinor, gently, and bring back what they say. A Verse for Fulke Side 24 Cecily Cecily has written a new verse to the shepherds' ballad, about the wind on the ridge. She wants her teacher Fulke to hear it first, but she cannot bring herself to sing it at him unasked. Cut From Below Side 24 Dickon One of Dickon's oldest skywalks has a post that was cut through in the night, from below, where it stands over a drain grating. Go down beneath it and clear what's there. Pegs for the Lute Side 24 Fulke Fulke's old lute keeps slipping out of tune. He wants new pegs carved from Downs Boar tusk, which never swells in the damp. The Unsigned Story Side 24 Hamon Someone chalked a story on Hamon's board that nobody admits to: 'Thyme Banks, past the white stone: the bees fly at night.' Find the white stone, clear 30 wild bees on the Thyme Banks, and ask Merrick whether it was his. The Slate Behind the Bar Side 24 Joan Joan wants the boar herds on the Thyme Banks thinned before her next lodgers go out, and asks you to tell Roland it is done: he worries as much as she does. Mice in the Flies Side 24 Lettice Tibb says the theatre's mice have fled the under-stage for the flies, as high as they can get. Lettice wants the stirges under that end of the old quarters cleared, and to know which cellar wall is nearest the drains. The Honey Cart Side 24 Reynold The honey cart from the downs is stuck behind boars rooting up the Thyme Banks road. Clear them, then have Wat tell the stalls the honey is coming. The Cart-Sized Boar Side 24 Roland Roland's old story of a boar the size of a cart happened on the downs. He wants to know if the place is still there, and if the boars there still grow that big: bring him a tusk or five. A Basket for Lettice Side 24 Tibb Tibb has caught one more mouse, from the very top of the flies, for Lettice's count. He would like it delivered with a message he has not quite worked out. Tibb's Bounty: Under the Row Repeatable 24 Tibb Tibb pays from his own pocket for every drain monster kept away from the Gilded Stage's cellar. Repeatable. The Horse That Came Back Alone Side 24 Wystan A patrol horse came back to the stables at night with an empty saddle. Its rider walked home safe, but the horse will not go near the road. Find where it bolted on the Thyme Banks and clear 30 downs boars there. A Note for the Palace Side 25 Aylwin Aylwin cannot leave the patrol, and a note about a new foal in the Guard stables needs to reach the palace. Carry it to Princess Elinor, then clear 25 wild bees off the road verge at Downs Edge so he can come home on time. A Binding Described Side 25 Benedict Benedict can describe his lost chronicle's binding to the last stitch. He asks his old pupil Petronella and his sister Ermengarde to keep watch for it. More Porridge Side 25 Bertrand The biggest intake ever needs more oats than Helewise's budget allows. Bring 12 downs boar tusks from the Thyme Banks, which the market buys well, then take the news to Helewise. Boar for the Feast Side 25 Cuthbert An envoys' feast in a week and the boar carts have not come. Hunt boars on the Thyme Banks for the carters, then tell Agnes the feast is on. Haggling by Proxy Side 25 Edith Edith cannot get to the market this week. She sends the player to haggle with Isabeau, then to tell her sister Sybil what was got. Notes on the Backs of Pages Side 25 Edwina Edwina has kept notes on strange wounds on the backs of pages in her fourth book, and suspects Aldith keeps the same. She wants proof from the cisterns before she shows her oldest friend. Blank on the Map Story 25 Gervase The downs are blank on Gervase's monster map. Are they quiet, or only unwatched? Walk to the Chalk Hives and mark them. Stingers for the Hives Side 25 Gilbert Gilbert wants to compare the stingers of the wild bees on the downs with those of his own hives, to see whether they are the same bees at heart. Damp in the Oldest Room Side 25 Jocelyn The oldest records room is damp, and the vault sits over the cisterns of the first city. Clear the clogged channels of the Cisterns, then tell Wulfric. A Key Missing Side 25 Osbert For the first time in thirty-four years a key is missing from Osbert's ring: the old cistern key, by the cellar drain. Clear the black rats of the Cisterns and search the silt. The Fox's Letter Side 25 Rafe Rafe has written something he cannot say aloud to his old pupil Lambert. He has written it in the voice of the fox. Boots Never Collected Side 25 Simkin A pair of boots left at Simkin's bench months ago was never collected, the soles white with chalk and pocked with stings. He wants to know where they walked, and whether Gytha knows whose they are. The Cistern Sluice Story 25 Tancred Below the Old Drains lie the cisterns of the first city, flooded and silted. Tancred still has the sluice keys: go down to the Cisterns and turn the sluice wheel to drain them. Jasper's Lens Side 25 Theobald Jasper the curio dealer has saved Theobald a lens. Fetch it, and try it from the highest point on the downs. A Better Hand Than Mine Side 25 Wat Badly tied purses all over the market are being emptied by someone very good, possibly better than Wat ever was. Wat wants the warden to hear it from him first, and his brother Kenric too. The Fifth Act Is Missing Side 26 Crispin A draft of Crispin's fifth act has gone missing from his desk. Marigold is the obvious suspect. For once, she may not be the right one. A Partner Who Won't Hold Back Side 26 Elinor A hooded recruit at the Knights' Court wants a sparring partner who will not hold back. Ask Rowena, and show her what you can do against a Disturbance-touched boar. A Ballad for Cecily Side 26 Fulke Fulke has written the ballad of the singing bank down for his pupil Cecily: the true verses first, then the good ones. Carry it to her at the Gilded Stage. A Stain She Cannot Place Side 26 Gytha Gytha has found a stain on the linen of houses near the gratings that she cannot scrub out or name. She wants samples of whatever lives in the cisterns to compare. An Ending by Friday Side 26 Lavinia Lavinia needs to know when the fifth act is coming, and she needs Tibb to carry the answer back to her slowly enough that she can bear it. A Word with Papa Side 26 Marigold Marigold wants someone to ask her father, once more, about a child's part in the Balrog War play, and then to tell her mother she was very well behaved about it. The Dew Pond Side 26 Roland Roland's best summer was spent camped by a dew pond on the downs. He wants to know if it is still there, the bees around it cleared, and Joan told that he asked, though he would never tell her himself. A Note from Percival Side 26 Rosamund A note in Percival's hand says Rosamund is too old for the Magician. Rosamund wants to know if he really wrote it before she starts their worst quarrel yet. The Margin Guess Side 26 Swithin Last month Swithin wrote in a margin that a stranger with a fine spear was 'hunting a great boar, and will come back hurt'. He did. The boar is still on the Thyme Banks. Defeat it, an Elite downs boar, and 30 more of its herd. Tell the Boy Side 27 Aubrey Aubrey has a message for Captain Rhys he will not deliver himself. Defeat 30 tunnel bats in the drains first, wrist practice, he says, then tell Rhys. The Crown's Bounty Repeatable 27 Aveline The Chalk Hives sit too near the road. The crown pays a bounty for every forty Chalk Hive Bees cleared, as often as you like. A Question for Thomasin Side 27 Bartholomew Bartholomew wants stingers from the Chalk Hives, and a question carried, not a letter, to his protegee Thomasin. The Great Hive Story 27 Godwin Godwin has been stung four times since spring. Follow the Chalk Hive bees to where they all fly: the great hive at the Hive Hollow's mouth. An Empty Slate Side 27 Joan For one evening Joan wants every name off her slate. Thurstan is the last one out, at the Chalk Hives: clear the bees around him and tell him to come home for supper. Three Sealed Notes Side 27 Osbert Osbert has three sealed notes for Agnes, Peterkin and Cuthbert, in that order. Carry them, do not hurry, and do not read them. What She Would Need Side 27 Percival For the first time in ten years, Percival wants to ask Rosamund what she would need from him to make the Last Stand work. He cannot ask her himself. Wat Is Late Side 27 Reynold Wat has not come back from an errand, and Reynold is worried. Find Wat, then help with what kept him: Chalk Hive bees swarming the sheepfold road. Bats in the Chimneys Side 28 Agnes Something flutters in the upper hall chimney at night. Hunt the tunnel bats under the old quarters, then tell Osbert, since he only half believes Agnes. Bats Under the Walks Side 28 Dickon Tunnel bats from the buried street have found their way up under the old quarters' skywalks. Dickon wants the roost below cleared before he starts his long walk's first post. Queen of the Downs Story 28 Edric Godwin found the great hive in a hollow of the chalk. Ask Edric to take you to the Hive Hollow and defeat Queen Amberwing. A Swarm on the Great Bell Side 28 Gilbert One of Gilbert's swarms has left the roof and settled on the Great Bell in the Royal Plaza. Thin the angry hives at the Chalk Hives that keep calling them out, look at the swarm, and tell Baldwin, who lights the plaza lamps, to keep his flame away from it. Where He Goes at Dawn Side 28 Gytha The old broom handle is missing from the corner of Gytha's yard, and Hodge comes home at breakfast with roof moss on his knees. She asks you to ask her parents what they know, then clear the drains below the lanes he runs. The Buried Street Story 28 Ida Below the cisterns, fresh claw-cut tunnels break through old walls into a buried street of the first city. Ida wants it walked and the rat packs there cleared. Where Nip Won't Go Side 28 Lettice Nip stopped dead at the edge of the buried street and would not go on. Lettice wants the black rat packs there cleared and Ida told exactly where the dog stopped. What a Swarm Looks Like Side 29 Crispin Crispin's Last Stand scene needs to feel like holding a line against something that keeps coming. He wants it described by someone who has done it. Then he wants Thomasin's opinion. Again. Lemon Balm Dye Side 29 Edith Edith wants to dye the Magician's robe a pale green no merchant sells, from lemon balm off the downs. A Calm Garden Side 29 Godwin Old Gerold planted lemon balm round the hives to keep the bees kind. Gather lemon balm on the Downs and thin the wild bees of the Thyme Banks. The Delver Story 30 Ida Wulfric heard the digging behind the Royal Vault's deepest corridor, and the burrow is there. Defeat the Delver, the thing in the drains, then report to Captain Rhys. A Relic for the Stage Side 30 Lavinia Lavinia wants a real wonder on her stage, no questions asked: a piece of the amber comb from the great hive's queen. Gloves for the Practical Side 30 Morwen Morwen's young mages burn their fingers in practical lessons. Ligator hide from the Reed Beds makes gloves that do not scorch. A Night Without Lanterns Story 30 Tristan Tristan asks someone steady to watch the Long Reach with him through a night, without a lantern. Clear the ligators from the Reed Beds and reach his hide. Digging Behind the Vault Story 30 Wulfric On still nights Wulfric hears scraping behind the vault's deepest corridor. Follow the claw-cut tunnels of the Buried Street to the wall nearest the vault. Teeth for Comparing Story 31 Aldith The gripped bargehand's bruise still troubles Aldith. She wants ligator teeth from the Reed Beds to lay against her drawing of it. Field Practice Side 31 Everard Everard owes Morwen a day of field practice. He would much rather someone else did the field and he did the practice of telling her about it. Ink for the Palace Books Side 31 Petronella The ink barge is held up below the Long Reach by 'lizards'. Clear the Reed Beds for the bargemen and ask Benedict for a bottle of his ink in the meantime. Low Water Finds Side 31 Robin The ligators of the Reed Beds churn the mud, and the mud gives things up. Robin wants the reed beds cleared so he can hunt at low water there, and his best find shown to Jasper. Placed, Not Swung Side 31 Rowena Rowena wants to see whether you place a blade or swing it. Defeat 40 reed ligators on the Reed Beds, where a swung sword sticks in the mud. A Question for His Sister Story 32 Ansel Ansel has a bite in his ledger that closed from too many sides. Carry his question to his sister Aldith on the Riverside and bring back what she says. A Hide for the Chronicles Side 32 Ermengarde The Aristocrat chronicles need new spines, and calf will not do this time. Ligator hide is tougher than anything Ermengarde can buy. Mint at the Water's Edge Side 33 Aldith The mint bed at the bottom of Aldith's garden is wilting at the water's edge. She wants the ligators off the reed beds where the river comes from, and fern fibre from the Long Reach to mulch the roots. Reed-Root Dye Side 33 Hawise Hawise thinks the thick roots the ligators tear up in the Reed Beds might dye a colour she has never made. Bring her twelve. An Envoy Overdue Side 33 Melisende An envoy is nine days late, coming by the river because the road was worse. Clear the crabs from the Long Reach towpath and ask Petronella when the last letter was written. A Thread by a Certain Date Side 33 Sybil Sybil needs river fern fibre for a royal garment, ready by a date she will not name. Gather it on the Long Reach and take it to her sister Edith to spin. Torn Nets Story 34 Agatha Agatha's nets come up torn. The lorangs and clangs of the Long Reach Banks cut the small tears with their claws; hunt them, and see if that explains the rest. A Present for Mum Side 34 Robin Robin wants to give his mother something for her nets: the banks cleared of the claws that cut them, so she can fish deeper again. He asks you to tell her it was his idea. Books for Constance Side 35 Morwen Morwen has set some books aside for her former student Constance, who now takes to the road. Tell her, without making it sound warm. A Witness for the History Side 35 Petronella Petronella's secret history needs a witness, not a letter. See the old towpath bend on the Long Reach Banks, deal with the crabs, and tell Melisende what you saw. The Narrow Moment Side 35 Rowena Rowena wants claws from the Long Reach's lorangs: a lorang's claw opens like a lock, and she means to show her pupils how narrow the right moment is. Bring 10, then tell Captain Rhys his class has a new lesson. A Colour Nobody Has Seen Side 36 Hawise For Isabeau's festival of colours Hawise wants to try fern fibre from the Long Reach, mordanted with crushed lorang claw. Then Isabeau must see the cloth. A Barge That Must Sail Story 36 Lucan Lucan has a barge of grain that must sail tonight, whatever the river is doing, and not enough hands. Ride with it past the Long Reach Banks and clear what climbs aboard. Guards for the River Side 37 Agatha Silas asked, half joking, whether the river needs guards too. Agatha has stopped laughing. Clear the lorangs off the banks, then tell Silas she said yes. A Point for Mariota Side 37 Everard Mariota bet Everard he could not name the lorang's weak side. He knows it. He would rather she thought someone else did. Claw Glue Side 38 Ermengarde Ermengarde boils lorang claws into the strongest glue in the Quarter. Then her brother Benedict must be told the new spines are on their way. Oak for the Wheel Side 38 Hereward Hereward needs the clangs off the Long Reach Banks so oak timbers can be floated down past them, and their claws for the wheel's iron straps, as the old millwrights did. The Quarrel over Carts Side 38 Melisende Two envoys have quarrelled all week over who pays the guards on the river carts. Clear the Long Reach Banks, then take the news to the queen for her one sentence. Grandad's Nods Side 38 Robin Robin knows every one of Osmund's nods but one: the nod he gave the badge. Robin wants the clangs cleared off the far bank where Osmund ties up, and asks you to ask his grandfather what else that nod meant. Seasoned Timber Story 40 Bennet Bennet needs seasoned oak for the fast barge's keel: timber that has lain for years in the river under the Undercut's banks, where the crocos lie on it. Stone From the Landing Side 40 Lucan The builders want stone from the quarry landing, and Lucan's crews won't go past the Reach without someone at the bow. Meet the barge at the stone wharf, clear the banks on the way, and tell Bennet the barge came home dry. A Place He Must Try Side 41 Morwen Morwen means to take her class onto the Long Reach Banks, where a mage must try. Clear the banks, then tell Everard he is coming. Something in the Race Side 42 Hereward Something in the mill race at night was strong enough to stop the wheel for the space of a breath. Hereward wants the crocos of the Undercut thinned, and Hawise told: he will not have her working the bank at night. Across After Dark Story 43 Osmund For the first time anyone can remember, Osmund asks someone to cross with him after dark. Clear the crocos from the Undercut, then stand above the Heron Pool where the deep water runs. The Vat That Changed Side 44 Hawise One of Hawise's vats turned overnight to a colour she did not put in it and nobody on the bank can name. She wants the crocos that came up the bank that night driven back, and Hereward told before he hears it from someone else. Boots That Wear Through Side 44 Sybil A certain pair of riding boots wears through in a month. Bring Sybil hide from the Undercut's crocos for soles that will last. The Boy and the Deep Side 45 Osmund Osmund fears the day Robin decides he is old enough to find out what is in the deep channel. He asks you to put down one of the great crocos of the Undercut, and to tell Robin what you saw. The Truth for Lucan Story 46 Tristan Tristan has kept what he saw on the Long Reach from Lucan. After Osmund's crossing, he knows it is time. Stand beside him while he tells Lucan, then help keep the Undercut clear for the barges. The Fast Barge Story 48 Bennet The fast barge is finished. Bennet needs someone brave enough to run it hard on the Long Reach, over the deepest pool, with Tristan watching from the bank. Ride it to the Heron Pool. Longjaw Story 48 Tristan The great croc Longjaw followed Bennet's fast barge into the Heron Pool. Defeat it. Bennet's talk takes you to the pool. Watch, Don't Kill Story 50 Constance Constance needs the rubble golems on the Spoil Heaps observed, not killed: walk out to three vantage points and watch how they move. Count Them for Me Side 50 Mariota Mariota wants a count from the Spoil Heaps, for a date she can set beside Theobald's night book of the same weeks. A New Hearth Side 51 Kenric The hearth lining of Selene's forge has cracked, and Kenric wants it relined before he forges his first sword. Quarry rubble from the Spoil Heaps holds the heat best. The Quiet Stretch Side 51 Leofric Not one report from the quarry road in six weeks, and that worries Leofric more than any red mark. Walk it from the Quarry Landing to the Spoil Heaps. Stone, Not Stories Side 51 Thomasin Thomasin must lecture to the quarrymen's families, who want to know whether the golems are new. She wants real stone on the table, not a story. A Bounty Alone Story 51 Thurstan Thurstan took a bounty on a Disturbance-touched golem on the Terraced Cuts, and for once Constance refused to come: she wants them watched, not killed. Help him finish it. Straps Through the Landing Side 52 Helewise Helewise's order of leather and shield straps came upriver to the Quarry Landing and sits there. Go to the landing and bring back 20 quarry rubble from the Spoil Heaps, which Vessa will take off the strap price. Grit for the Furnace Side 52 Prudence Prudence's furnace lining cracked in the last experiment. Golem rubble is the only grit that holds that heat. The Quarry Village Story 53 Wulfric Wulfric's home village is in the quarries upstream, and the stone there has started to stand up. Clear the golems around the Spoil Heaps so the people still there can sleep. A Stone Run Side 54 Merrick Merrick is hiring guards at twice his rate for a stone run up to the quarries, and won't say what he's carrying. Clear the road: 30 monsters on the Spoil Heaps and 30 on the Terraced Cuts. The Rival at the Gate Side 54 Thurstan Someone has been taking the quarry bounties off the gate board before Thurstan gets there. He wants to beat them to the Spoil Heaps, and asks Roland to judge who did more. An Impossible Dot Story 55 Gervase A report puts golems on the Terraced Cuts, far ahead of the line on Gervase's map. It should be impossible. Confirm it. Whetstones for the Yard Side 55 Helewise The practice yard is wearing through whetstones. Bring Helewise 25 quarry stone from the Terraced Cuts, then tell Bertrand the new whetstones are coming. The Mason's Mark Story 56 Thomasin The oldest face of the Terraced Cuts carries an Aristocrat mason's mark. Thomasin wants it copied exactly, as a rubbing, not described. A Present, Unlabelled Side 56 Wulfric Wulfric wants to give Jocelyn something too good to label: a ledger-weight cut from the fine grey stone of the Terraced Cuts. The Adventurer's Notes Story 57 Mariota An adventurer at the Crooked Lantern keeps notes on every monster she fights. Mariota wants them very badly. Broker a meeting. The Empty Wagon Side 57 Merrick One of Merrick's wagons came back from the terraces with its driver and oxen safe and its cargo gone. Find the wagon bed on the Terraced Cuts, clear 40 quarry golems around it, then tell Edric. A Weak Side for Tobe Side 59 Mariota Tobe asked his sister whether golems have a weak side. Mariota would rather he heard it from someone who has fought them. A Rubbing for Bartholomew Side 59 Thomasin Thomasin wants the golems kept off the old faces while the quarrymen look for more marks, and her rubbing shown to her mentor Bartholomew. A Golem Core Story 60 Ansel Guards from the quarry road come to Ansel bruised as if a wall fell on them. He needs a specimen: the core stones of the Cut Golems of the Deep Cut. Powdered Golem Stone Story 60 Prudence Prudence needs a reagent found only where monsters have moved in: powdered golem stone, for the potion that heals in a moment. Ore for a First Sword Story 62 Kenric Selene has judged Kenric ready. His first sword wants iron from the old seam in the Deep Cut, where the quarries' oldest workings are. Gather it. The Waves Story 63 Constance Constance wants her notebooks' dates laid against Gervase's monster map, with Mariota reading the pattern: do the changes come in waves, and do the quarries wake at each one? The Jar That Glows Side 64 Prudence One jar of Prudence's powdered golem stone has started to glow on its own. She wants darker stone to compare, and her rival Mirel to see it. Survey the Quarry Road Story 65 Leofric The waves are real, and Leofric wants the quarry road surveyed again by someone who can defend themselves. Walk the Deep Cut and clear the road through it. The First Sword Side 66 Kenric Kenric's first sword is finished, balanced for a short arm. He wants it tried against something hard before Selene puts her mark beside his: an Elite golem of the Deep Cut. Then tell Wat. Two Maps Agree Side 66 Leofric Leofric wants his last marks fresh before he compares maps with his old colleague Gervase. Thin the Cut Golems of the Deep Cut, then take his copy to Gervase. Hold the Deep Cut Story 67 Constance The wave has come. The Deep Cut's golems are waking all at once. Hold it with Constance while the quarries stand up. Old Cairn Story 68 Edric Something as tall as a house has risen out of the First Cut's face. Ask Edric to take you to the First Cut and defeat Old Cairn, the Ancient of the Quarries. The Face Is Moving Story 68 Edric The quarrymen say the face of the First Cut is moving. Edric wants eyes on it: go to the First Cut's mouth at the far end of the Deep Cut.

docs.title: Kaldemor
docs.text: Quest Kind Level From Summary Welcome Home Story 1 Lia Lia says the mayor wants to meet you. Go and see Tobin. Settling In Story 1 Tobin Tobin wants you to see the Market and meet Bram, the potion seller. Snail Trouble Story 2 Tobin Snails are eating the town's gardens. Thin them out in the meadow, then see Ranger Hale at the park gate. Shells for the Mayor Story 2 Hale Mayor Tobin collects snail shells for the new fence. Bring him 15 Green Snail Shells. Strength of a Warrior Story 3 Tobin Tobin says a warrior is measured by more than errands. Reach level 5 and use Power Strike five times. He will teach you Warrior's Resolve. Rosa's Recipe Side 3 Rosa Rosa the baker needs 10 Mushroom Spores and 5 Blue Snail Shells for her famous mushroom bread. A Loaf for Bram Side 3 Rosa Rosa trusts you with something personal: carry her word to Bram, the potion seller in the Market. The Clock Stopped Story 4 Ewan The clock tower in the park has stopped. Old Ewan thinks a Shroom took its gear: hunt 20 Shrooms, then bring the gear back. Hale's Bounty Repeatable 3 Hale Ranger Hale pays a bounty for thinning out the meadow: defeat 30 of the field's monsters. He will pay it again, any time. A Smith's First Bar Side 3 Gareth Gareth the smith will show you the forge's first lesson: strike 4 copper ore from the veins in the fields, then smelt it into a copper ingot (open the Professions window and make it). A Pot for Rosa Side 4 Rosa Rosa the baker will teach you the kitchen's first lesson: pick 3 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then toss a herb salad from them (open the Professions window and make it). A Steady Brew Side 5 Bram Bram the potion seller will show you how a potion is brewed: pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then brew 2 red potions from them (open the Professions window and make them). A Head for Heights Side 3 Garrick Garrick the climber will teach Rope Up to anyone who can reach the top of Kaldemor Hills. A Sharper Sword Side 3 Gareth Gareth the smith gives you a Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT. Use it on a one-handed sword: drag the scroll from the Use tab onto the sword, worn (equipment window) or carried (Equip tab). A sword is on sale in his shop. Kaldemor's Pest Watch Repeatable 7 Tobin Mayor Tobin pays the town's bounty on the hills: defeat 40 of Kaldemor Hills' monsters. Every round raises Kaldemor's regard for you, and he will pay it again, any time. Rosa's Standing Order Repeatable 5 Rosa Rosa's mushroom bread sells out every morning. She buys 10 Mushroom Spores whenever you bring them, and likes you better each time. The Stretch at Dusk Side 8 Pell Pell will not drive the cab past the Crossing after dark any more. Clear the Crossing so the evening run can go again: defeat 40 of its monsters. Notices for the Lanes Side 9 Rufus Rufus's notices are not reaching the farms along the Cider Lanes, because folk have stopped walking in to hear them. Carry them out to the farm gate above the lanes and clear 30 orchard pigs. Down the Road Side 10 Mildred Mildred has a bundle of Tobin's letters for the capital, and the mail no longer goes as surely as it did. Walk the royal road to the Greenwood's far end, where it climbs toward Selsior, and clear 30 of the Greenwood's monsters on the way. The Cart That Never Came Side 10 Tobin A harvest cart left Kaldemor for Bain Harbour along the Verdant Coast Road and never arrived. Walk the road and look for it in the Greenmarsh, then tell Percy, who built it, what you found. The Snail King Story 12 Hale Ranger Hale has heard something huge in a hollow beyond the woods. Walk to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge past the hills, and tell him what you find. A Trail Too Broad Story 20 Wilbur Something has cut a trail across Wilbur's far field, far too broad for any snail. Follow it down the farm track to the Last Stile, where the hedges end and the woods begin, then defeat 30 Hedge Boars in the Boarwood. What the Ledger Says Story 21 Mildred Mildred's ledger shows the far farms by the woods losing more this year than in any five years before. Ask Elsie why her cows will not graze the far pasture, then defeat 40 Rooting Piglets and Hedge Boars in the Boarwood. The Wager Story 23 Percy Percy and Gareth have a wager on what has been gouging the wheels on the Royal Road. Bring Percy 15 Curved Tusks from the Boarwood's boars, and let Gareth look at one first. The Woodcutter's Sign Story 24 Orin Forty years ago Orin cut his sign into a great old oak in the woods, the finest tree he left standing. Find it in the deep Boarwood and come back to tell him whether it still stands. Thinning the Herd Story 26 Hale Hale's bounty now reaches past the woods. Defeat 60 Tuskers in the deep Boarwood and one Disturbance-touched monster, so the herd stops pushing up toward the farms. Stilebrook Farm Story 28 Hale The herd's wallow is the yard of Stilebrook Farm, an old farm in the deep Boarwood that has stood empty since long before anyone alive. Hale wants to know what keeps the herd there. Reach the farm's old gate. Hale's Boarwood Bounty Repeatable 28 Hale Ranger Hale pays a bounty for keeping the Boarwood's herd back from the farms: defeat 40 boars in the Boarwood. He will pay it again, any time. Too Bold Story 30 Wilf Wilf the spore gatherer will not go back into the Deepwood alone: the Hoarder Shrooms on the Humming Trail have grown too bold. Gather 15 Wild Spores from the patches there and defeat 40 Hoarder Shrooms. Shiny Things Story 32 Wilf The Hoarder Shrooms are carrying shiny things away through the Deepwood. Wilf wants to see what they take: collect 10 Stolen Trinkets from Hoarder Shrooms. Quietly, for Dottie Story 34 Winnie Winnie knows Dottie's lamb Button is missing, though Dottie has told no one. Follow the large, round, damp tracks from the bramble at the woods' edge into Windflower Glade, defeat 40 Windflower Caps and find a tuft of speckled wool. Dottie must not learn Winnie sent you. Roots from Below Story 36 Clem Something strips the roots of Clem's orchard trees nearest the woods, deep underground and only at night. Sit up with him in the orchard, then collect 20 Pale Threads from Bluecaps in the Bluecap Groves. The Late Pedlar Story 38 Molly A travelling pedlar who stops at the Sleepy Snail every summer is three weeks late, and Molly fears the Deepwood. Search the Bluecap Groves for him: defeat 60 Bluecaps and find any sign of him. Bites That Will Not Close Story 40 Bess Bess has a page in her count book for bad bites from the woods that will not close. She wants to try a poultice of Bluecap spores: collect 20 Bluecap Spore Sacs, then take them to Bram so the two can brew it side by side. The Woodcutters' Hut Story 44 Molly Past the Bluecap Groves stands the old woodcutters' hut in Breezy Hollow, and Molly thinks Mott could have taken shelter there. Reach the hut, defeat 50 Paleveil Caps around it so whoever is inside can walk out, then talk to Mott. Home Again Story 45 Dottie Button is home. Dottie wants to tell her grandmother everything at last, and asks you to come with her. Then Rufus's cat and Molly's pedlar need telling too. Houses That Will Not Listen Story 46 Bertie Since spring the mushroom houses nearest the woods have leaned away from the trees, and Bertie cannot hear them. Bring him a Paleveil cap from Breezy Hollow. Where the King Came From Story 47 Garrick Garrick saw a line of broken treetops leading toward Mano's hollow from somewhere far past the hills. He wants to see where it begins. Climb with him to the top of Breezy Hollow and look out. The Bluecap Mother Story 48 Hale The Bluecaps, the pale threads, the leaning houses: Hale thinks they all come from one place in the Deepwood. Reach the mouth of the Bluecap Hollow, at the foot of Breezy Hollow, and come back. Spores for Two Repeatable 30 Wilf Wilf supplies Rosa and Bram both, and they both want more. Bring him 20 Wild Spores from the patches of the Deepwood. He will take more, any time. Follow Her Home Story 50 Hale Ranger Hale has noticed Meg ranging past the far end of the Deepwood. He asks you to follow her quietly, past Breezy Hollow to the old road beyond, and make sure she comes home. A Dare Story 50 Meg Meg caught you following her. She makes it a dare: stand in the clearing on the Keep Road with her watching, and defeat 60 Capguards. The Cloud That Didn't Move Story 52 Nell Nell has shown you a page of her tally book: a grey cloud over the woods that did not move.
