Past the Point Side 20 Sorcha Sorcha beaches the Sea Thrift on the Strandwood shore to gut her catch, and the Wrack Boars have taken it over. Defeat 50 of them. Boots for the Road Side 20 Teague The hill road eats Teague's boots. Bring him 15 Ligator Skins from Dusk Ford for a new pair before his summer trip. Merrin's Tally Side 21 Merrin Merrin keeps a tally of who has felled the most, and the edge-wood is slow. She has decided a Driftstump counts: bring down 45 of them. The Tide Slate Side 22 Eilidh Eilidh writes the cove's tides on her slate, but she wants to know how far the water goes out on the black rocks of the Strandwood. Go and see, and clear 40 Driftstumps there. A Touched Boar Side 22 Esk A Disturbance-touched Wrack Boar has been goring the timber crews' ponies at the Strandwood Edge. Esk will split the pay: bring down the Elite and 30 of its herd. The Edge Line Side 22 Haldor Haldor's crews cut only at the forest edge now. Stand at the last stump to see where the line is, then clear 50 monsters from Strandwood Edge. A Brush for the Rope Side 22 Hamish Hamish's oiling brush has gone bald. Bring him 15 Weedy Bristles from the Wrack Boars and 10 pieces of Sound Driftwood from the Driftstumps of the Strandwood. The Log Stack Side 22 Jory A timber ship is waiting on a load of logs stacked at the Strandwood Edge, and Wrack Boars are rooting under the stack. Clear 50 of them so Jory can get the logs rafted round. The Gap at Dawn Side 22 Mhairi Mhairi's first verse is the gap at dawn, but she plays too late to ever see one. Look at the gap from the head of the Long Stair, then ask Bethoc what she remembers of the race send-offs. Something to Chalk Side 23 Kenna Kenna wants something on Bethoc's sighting board with her name beside it. Bring down 50 Wrack Boars and bring her 15 tusks to pick from. Whose Reading Side 24 Arlo Arlo and Eilidh read last night's tide differently and argued about it. Ask Eilidh what she saw, look at the water from the cove rocks, and tell Arlo who was right. Three Nights Running Side 24 Bethoc Three nights running, three different hands chalked the same thing on Bethoc's board: a fox bigger than the rest, out on the Strandwood. Defeat a Disturbance-touched Strand Fox. A Late Basket Side 24 Brigid Brigid is late with Elspeth's herb basket. Clear 40 Wrack Boars from Strandwood Edge, and tell Elspeth the basket will be late. A Board for the Boat Side 24 Corrie Corrie writes her notes on the back of her hand because there is nothing to write on in a pilot boat. Thin out 40 Driftstumps and bring her 10 Sound Driftwood for a board. Shells and Sea-Glass Side 24 Ronan Ronan wants a Wrack Boar tusk for his box, and the sea-glass his grandmother Agna has been saving for him. Bring him 10 tusks and the sea-glass. A Crew of Her Own Side 25 Merrin Merrin wants a crew to lead. Clear 50 Wrack Boars round her cutting, then ask Haldor about it, straight. Thread for Stitches Side 26 Elspeth The hunters keep bringing Elspeth fox bites. Bring her 20 Fox Sinew for stitching, and tell Torva to come and have her arm seen to. Saving for a Bow Side 26 Fionn Fionn is saving for a bow and needs fox sinew for its string. Go out to the last stump on the Forest Shore, defeat 50 Strand Foxes on the Strandwood Rocks and bring him 12 Fox Sinews. Not a word to Hamish. Knock Twice Side 26 Osric Osric keeps the old woodsmen's sayings. Put down 40 Driftstumps near the crews, then knock twice on the last stump on the Forest Shore. Brodie's Favour Side 26 Sorcha Two winters ago Sorcha let Brodie have a season's catch on credit, and he has never repaid it. Ask him about the favour, then bring Sorcha what he needs. Sound Grain Side 26 Tamsin Tamsin blames the Gap Runner's losses on her timber. Bring her 20 Sound Driftwood from the Driftstumps of the Strandwood so she can read the grain. The Blue Flame Side 26 Tarran Tarran thinks the salt in dried weed once made his lantern burn blue. Bring him 20 Weedy Bristles from the Wrack Boars so he can try again. Brave Company Side 26 Teague Teague wants company that has stood in the rocks at dusk and not run. Defeat 60 Strand Foxes, then carry his question to Esk on the Inlet Quay once more. Mhairi's Song Side 28 Cormac Cormac is hurt that his old pupil Mhairi has not asked him for a verse of her race song. Ask her, lightly, how it goes, and bring him 15 Fox Sinews for a set of old camp fiddle strings. Agna's Knots Side 28 Eilidh Eilidh wants to tie a knot her grandmother will call better than "not bad". Look at Kestra's knots on the highest bridge, ask Agna what makes them good, and bring Eilidh 20 Fox Sinews for line. Paid in Sinew Side 28 Esk Esk owes Gwenna, who will not take her coin. Bring Esk 20 Fox Sinew, which Gwenna uses to whip her rope ends. A Collar for Ma Side 28 Jory Jory's mother writes that the inland winters are cold, which means her back hurts. Bring Jory 20 Strand Fox Tails to trade with Greer for a fur collar. Clean Prints Side 28 Kenna Someone small follows the hunters to the last stump. Kenna wants the foxes thinned near the edge, and the prints in the mud there kept clear. Rules This Time Side 29 Merrin Merrin will race Kenna again, with rules this time. Carry the challenge to Kenna, then clear 60 monsters off Strandwood Rocks. Torn Nets Side 30 Agna Agna wants to lay Shore Crab claws beside her torn nets and see which tears are crab work. Bring her 20 Shore Crab Claws from the Undercliff. The Run from Above Side 30 Corrie Corrie wants to draw the whole run of the gap from the Saltface, but the cliff is thick with Shore Crabs. Clear 40 of them from the Saltface. Wood the Sea Gave Back Side 30 Gunna Gunna wants sound driftwood, the part of a Driftstump the sea has not rotted, from the Strandwood, past where the crews cut. Bring her 25 pieces. Word for Tamsin Side 30 Haldor Haldor will not send a crew into the deep forest for Tamsin's keel. Bring him 25 Sound Driftwood to send her instead, and tell Tamsin why. The Second Lift Side 30 Hamish Hamish dreams of a second lift down to the far cove. Bring him 15 Fox Sinews for his counterweight lashings, and take his drawing of the second lift to Gorm. Before Slack Side 30 Kor Kor went through the gap before slack and had to put in on the Undercliff, where the Shore Crabs went for his boat. Clear 50 of them from the Undercliff. One at a Time Side 30 Nessa Nessa takes quay children out in the pilot boats at slack, one at a time, and wants an honest second opinion. Ask Kor which child he would put on an oar, then see that child. Grandmother's Window Side 32 Arlo Arlo has written six complaints about the pilots of his own. Take his list up to his grandmother Ysmay at the top of the Cliff Stairs, and see how many she says aye to. The Sulking Lantern Side 32 Dunmor One of the quay lanterns has started to sulk. Carry it, level, to Gunna at the back of the Lantern Market. The Children Side 32 Sorcha Ronan has been wandering along the cliff foot at low tide. Clear 60 monsters on the Undercliff for Sorcha, then go and see Eilidh on the cove rocks. A Sharp Note Side 32 Ysmay Ysmay has written a sharp note about a pilot who swung wide in the gap. Take it to Varro on the Inlet Quay, then tell Arlo what Varro said. One Short Side 33 Dougal Dougal's count of boats has come up one short: a cove skiff slipped its knot and the ebb took it to the Undercliff. Go down there and clear 40 monsters so it can be towed home. The Far Cove Stair Side 34 Gorm Gorm is behind on the far cove stair. Clear 60 Shore Crabs off the Saltface below it, then ask Hamish to haul Gorm's cut stone up in his lift. The Saltface Verse Side 34 Mhairi Mhairi wants a verse for the boat going out under the Saltface, with the cliff's own noise in it. Clear 60 monsters on the Saltface, then ask Cormac how the old songs sang the cliff. The Deep-Water Boat Side 36 Calder Calder wants Tamsin's opinion of his latest drawing of the boat he means to build. Take it to her at the quay yard, then bring him what she says it needs. Four Books Side 36 Corrie Corrie's loft leaks, and she wants her four filled notebooks kept dry. Take them to Esk for her sea-chest. The Lamp in the Window Side 36 Elspeth Elspeth's lamp burns every night, for Osric. Bring her 25 Sea Newt Hides for clean lamp oil, and look in on Osric on the way. A Word with Iska Side 36 Kor Kor wants a seat in the race crew and will not ask for it. He would like someone to put in a word with Iska. Moira's Wager Side 36 Moira Moira wants to prove to Torva that she can hunt. Defeat 60 Sea Newts, race her from the foot of the stairs to the head of the Long Stair, then carry her case to Torva on the Forest Shore. The Market Lantern Side 36 Tarran Tarran has hung his brightest lantern over the Lantern Market square. Go and look at it for him, then bring him 20 Shore Crab Claws to toughen the next one's glass. Under the Saltface Side 38 Nessa Nessa rows her young pilots along under the Saltface, and the Sea Newts lie out on the rocks there watching. Clear 60 of them from the Saltface. Edges for the Anvil Side 38 Ulric The Anvil blunts Ulric's chisels faster than he can sharpen them. Bring him 20 Newt Hides for a strop, and take his word to Gorm about his mallet grip. Crab for the Warden Side 40 Dunmor Iska is out on a bad tide and will forget to eat, unless there is crab. Bring Dunmor 20 Shore Crab Claws, and tell Iska at the Wardens' House that there is crab on. The Black Marks Side 40 Osric Osric wants a black line marked along the forest edge that no cutter goes past. Bring him 25 Slater Plates for the tar, and tell Haldor what the marks are for. A Pot for Haldor Side 40 Tamsin Tamsin and Haldor have had their argument about the deep forest again. Take Haldor a crock of her best pine tar. It is not an apology. It is tar. Nets for the Boats Side 42 Agna Saltgulls come in off the Wrack Ledges and tear Agna's nets on the drying racks. Take a mended net to Sorcha, then defeat 50 Saltgulls. The Last Flights Side 44 Gorm The far cove stair's last flights run down past the Wrack Ledges. Thin the Saltgulls there and the Sea Newts on the Saltface, then take Gorm's word to Kestra about a handrope. Quills and Advice Side 44 Ysmay Ysmay wants Saltgull quills for Arlo, who wears his pens to stubs writing down what she says. Bring her 20 Saltgull Feathers, and take her written advice to Iska at the Wardens' House. The Old Mark Side 45 Iska The Sea Slaters have eaten the tar off the old leading mark in the Saltface. Clear 60 of them from the Wrack Ledges so a crew can tar it fresh. Out at Slack Side 46 Nessa Nessa wants you in a pilot boat with her at slack water. Clear 50 Saltgulls from the Wrack Ledges first, then meet her at the lowest quay steps. Gunna's Question Side 48 Gunna Gunna wants you to ask Dunmor and then Tarran how they know a lantern is failing, and to bring her 20 Saltgull Feathers for her finest brushes. The Hardest Step Side 48 Ulric Ulric is cutting the last of the Anvil, where the far cove stair runs closest to the water. Keep the Wrack Ledges below him quiet through his long day's work: defeat 80 monsters there. The Count Side 50 Halvard Halvard has counted every ship Varro ever took through the gap, and cannot decide whether to tell him. Ask Iska, then go back to Halvard. Three Mornings Side 50 Varro Arlo has not come to the quay at dawn for three mornings. Varro wants to know why, without asking. Find Arlo, then go back to Varro. A Hard Quill Side 52 Ailsa Ailsa writes the Tide Book with gull quills, and only the Saltgulls of the Wrack Ledges grow feathers hard enough. Bring her 30 Saltgull Feathers. The Lee Rocks Side 56 Varro Jaw Crabs have taken the lee rocks under the Forest Jaw, where pilot boats lie out of the run. Varro wants 60 of them cleared. A Fair Copy Side 58 Halvard Halvard's ledger lacks the tides for the last month. Copy them from the Tide Book at Ailsa's desk, then bring the copy to Halvard. Ballast Side 58 Tamsin The Gap Runner sits wrong in the water, and Tamsin wants to trim her with Wrackstone. Clear 40 Wrackgolems on the Skerries and bring her 15 Wrackstone.

docs.title: A Dare
docs.text:
Meg caught you following her. She makes it a dare: stand in the clearing on the Keep Road with her watching, and defeat 60 Capguards.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Meg Level 50 After Follow Her Home Leads to The Cloud That Didn't Move

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Capguard in the clearings (Capguard) in The Keep Road

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60,000 EXP
  • 4,000 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Right. Here is how it goes. The clearing in front of the keep, the first stretch of the Keep Road: there are mushrooms in rows along the old wall there. Capguards, I call them, because they stand like sentries. Nobody posted them. They just stand there.
  • I dare you to stand in that clearing and knock down 60 Capguards while I watch. If the ground shakes, you do not run. Neither do I. Deal?
  • Deal! I will be up on the wall with my count book. Do not make me look bad, I told the whole Park I found you.
  • Scared? That is fine. I was too, a bit. The dare stays open.
  • Sixty Capguards in the clearing on the The Keep Road, Player. I am counting. I am always counting.
  • Sixty! Well, fifty-eight, and two I am rounding up for you. And did you feel it? Halfway through, under your feet. That long low shudder. That is what I felt in the spring.
  • You did not run. I did not run either, this time. That is the best thing anyone has done for me all year, and if you tell anyone I said so, I will say you fell in the fountain.
  • Here, take these, I bought too many. Whatever is shaking the ground is inside that keep. We are going to find out what. Both of us.

docs.title: A Draught for the Dust
docs.text:
The dust of Stonecap Keep is giving the hunters who come back from it a cough. Bram wants 25 Spore Puff sacs to work out a draught for it, and will teach you the recipe.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Bram Level 60 After Old Wall Iron Leads to The Old Wall's Marks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Spore Puff Sac (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 80,000 EXP
  • 5,000 mesos
  • Spore Draught x10
  • Recipe: Spore Draught (Alchemy)
  • +35 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player! Sit down a moment and listen to this: four hunters this week, back from that old keep past the woods, and every one of them coughing like a cart with a bad wheel.
  • It is the spores. Those floating puffs on the walls burst, and the dust gets into everything. My sister says it is a tea matter. My sister is wrong. It is a draught matter. A brew is only a pot with a better reason, and here is a reason.
  • Bring me 25 Spore Puff Sacs from the Spore Puffs. The sac is what holds the dust together, and what holds dust together can draw it out. I will work out the brew and teach it to you.
  • Lovely. Do not breathe in near them when they burst. I know, I know. Easier said.
  • Then I will keep selling cough drops and listening to Bess say I told you so.
  • Twenty-five Spore Puff Sacs, Player, from the Spore Puffs at the Keep.
  • Twenty-five! Right. Two sacs, two lemon balm, one mandarin for the taste, and you stir it the wrong way round. Do not ask me why the wrong way. It works. I tried it the right way twice this morning.
  • There. A Spore Draught. It clears the dust, it takes a slow off your legs, and it puts a good deal back in you besides. Bess tasted it and said nothing at all, which means it is very good.
  • The recipe is yours now, and here are a few I made while you watched. Take them up the walls with you.

docs.title: A Head for Heights
docs.text:
Garrick the climber will teach Rope Up to anyone who can reach the top of Kaldemor Hills.

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Garrick Level 3 After Settling In

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the top of the hills in Kaldemor Hills

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • Skill: Rope Up
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • You climbed my ladder to get up here, so you have the hands for it. I have a trick that spares you the climb: Rope Up, a leap that throws you onto the rope or ledge above.
  • But I teach only those who have seen the world from above. Climb to the very top of Kaldemor Hills, west of the town, then come back to me.
  • The hills are west of the town square. It is a long climb, and the grass up there is soft if you slip.
  • Heights are not for everyone. The offer stands.
  • The top of Kaldemor Hills is west of the town, Player. Climb up, look around, then come back.
  • Ha! You have the look of someone who has seen the clouds up close. Right: bend your knees, look up, and let go.
  • That is Rope Up. Open the skills window with K, find it on the Beginner tab and drag it onto a key; Page Down is its key until you move it. It throws you up to the nearest rope or ledge above, so mind the ceilings.

docs.title: A Loaf for Bram
docs.text:
Rosa trusts you with something personal: carry her word to Bram, the potion seller in the Market.

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Rosa Level 3 After Rosa's Recipe Condition Friend standing with Rosa

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Bram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 200 EXP
  • Orange Potion x5
  • +150 standing with Rosa
  • +15 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player, you are a friend now, so I may ask you something I would ask no customer. Bram and I quarrelled over a loaf, years ago, and I never mended it.
  • Would you go to Bram, in the Market, and tell him the oven is warm for him? That is all. He will understand.
  • Thank you, dear. Take the portal east of the square, his stall is at the far end of the Market.
  • Of course. It has waited years, it can wait a little more.
  • Bram is at the far end of the Market, Player. Tell him the oven is warm.
  • Rosa said that? The oven is warm, for me? Well, well. Tell her I will come by for a loaf, and that I was the stubborn one.
  • He said he will come? Oh, Player. I could hug you, and I will, as soon as I take this tray out.
  • Here, a few Orange Potions for your trouble. You have given me more than that.

docs.title: A Pot for Rosa
docs.text:
Rosa the baker will teach you the kitchen's first lesson: pick 3 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then toss a herb salad from them (open the Professions window and make it).

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Rosa Level 4 After Rosa's Recipe Leads to A Steady Brew

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 3 Marjoram Flower
  2. Make 1 Herb Salad

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • 150 mesos
  • Recipe: Roast Pork (Cooking)
  • +50 standing with Rosa
  • +10 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • You have been such a help with the spores, Player, that I would like to hand you more than money. A baker is only half a cook! Pick 3 marjoram flowers from the little patches in the fields (press the gather key beside one), then toss a herb salad from them in your Professions window. Do that and I will teach you my roast pork.
  • Marjoram grows where the grass is thick: the east and west fields have plenty. It comes back by itself, so pick without a worry.
  • The pot will keep warm. Come back when you feel hungry for it.
  • Three marjoram flowers from the patches, then a herb salad. Press the gather key beside a patch.
  • A salad made with your own hands! Nothing in the shop tastes like it.
  • Here is your pay, and my roast pork: its recipe is yours now. A pig's head, a little firewood and a sprig of rosemary, and not a minute more on the fire.

docs.title: A Sharper Sword
docs.text:
Gareth the smith gives you a Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT. Use it on a one-handed sword: drag the scroll from the Use tab onto the sword, worn (equipment window) or carried (Equip tab). A sword is on sale in his shop.

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Gareth Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Use Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT 60%

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60 EXP
  • Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT 60% x1
Dialogue
  • A good smith never stops at the first blow, Player. A blade can be sharpened with a scroll: it adds to its attack, and each scroll takes one of the sword's upgrade slots for good. I will give you one for a one-handed sword. Use it on yours, and I will give you a second to keep. If you have no sword, there is one on my shelf.
  • Here is the scroll. Drag it from your Use tab onto the sword, worn or in your bag. Careful: the sword only has so many slots.
  • Another day, then. The scroll will keep.
  • Drag the scroll from your Use tab onto a one-handed sword. If you have none, I sell a plain Sword.
  • There, it bites deeper now. Keep this second scroll for the next sword, and here is something for your trouble.

docs.title: A Smith's First Bar
docs.text:
Gareth the smith will show you the forge's first lesson: strike 4 copper ore from the veins in the fields, then smelt it into a copper ingot (open the Professions window and make it).

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Gareth Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 4 Copper Ore
  2. Make 1 Copper Ingot

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 120 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Recipe: Bronze Axe (Smithing)
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Bring me a bar, Player, and I will teach you more than a shopkeeper ever could. The fields are full of copper veins: stand by one and press the gather key, a few blows and it gives. Strike 4 copper ore, then smelt a copper ingot from it in your Professions window. Do that and I will teach you the bronze axe.
  • Good. The veins glitter in the east and west fields. They fill again after a while, so there is always more.
  • The forge will keep. Come back when your arms itch for it.
  • Four copper ore from the veins, then an ingot from the ore. Press the gather key by a vein.
  • A fine first bar! Copper is soft, but every smith starts there.
  • Here is your pay, and the bronze axe: its recipe is yours now. Bronze takes a little more skill, but you have the hands for it.

docs.title: A Steady Brew
docs.text:
Bram the potion seller will show you how a potion is brewed: pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then brew 2 red potions from them (open the Professions window and make them).

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Bram Level 5 After A Pot for Rosa

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 4 Marjoram Flower
  2. Make 2 Red Potion

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 180 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Recipe: Orange Potion (Alchemy)
  • +15 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Rosa tells me you cook, Player. A brew is only a pot with a better reason. Pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields and brew 2 red potions in your Professions window: two flowers and a mushroom spore make one. Do that and I will teach you the orange potion.
  • Marjoram patches dot the east and west fields. Mushroom spores drop from the Shrooms. Do not drink the first batch, mind.
  • No hurry. The cauldron is not going anywhere.
  • Four marjoram flowers, then two red potions: each takes two flowers and a mushroom spore.
  • Two potions, and they do heal. You have the hands for it, Player.
  • Here is your pay, and the orange potion's recipe. It wants lavender, which grows a little deeper in the fields, and the caps of orange mushrooms.

docs.title: A Trail Too Broad
docs.text:
Something has cut a trail across Wilbur's far field, far too broad for any snail. Follow it down the farm track to the Last Stile, where the hedges end and the woods begin, then defeat 30 Hedge Boars in the Boarwood.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Wilbur Level 20 Leads to What the Ledger Says

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Last Stile
  2. Defeat 30 Hedge Boar

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,000 EXP
  • 2,000 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player! You have a minute? I need a pair of eyes that are not mine. This morning I found a trail across my far field. Turnips rooted up, beans flattened, the hedge pushed through. It is wider than my cart.
  • I have seen snails come in lines all spring, but no snail made that. It runs off down the farm track toward the Last Stile, where the hedges stop and the woods start. Will you follow it and find out what is walking through my turnips?
  • Good. The farm track leaves Kaldemor Woods and runs south to the stile. Follow the mud. Whatever it is, it is not shy about leaving a mess.
  • All right. I will go on sitting up with my lantern, then. Not that a lantern ever stopped anything.
  • Follow the trail to The Last Stile, Player, and into the woods past it. Whatever came through my field came from there.
  • Boars? Wild boars, out of the old woods, all the way up to my field? Thirty of them, you say, and still more in there.
  • Well. That explains the trail. Boars do not walk round a hedge when they can walk through it. Four generations of my family have farmed that ground, and not one of them ever saw a boar this side of the stile.
  • Take these, and my thanks. I will tell Hale, and this time I will make him say something back.

docs.title: Guards for the River
docs.text:
Silas asked, half joking, whether the river needs guards too. Agatha has stopped laughing. Clear the lorangs off the banks, then tell Silas she said yes.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Agatha Level 37 After Torn Nets

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Bank Lorang in The Long Reach Banks
  2. Talk to Silas

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,780 EXP
  • 740 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Agatha
Dialogue
  • My husband Silas hires guards for the harbour carts now, and over supper he asked whether the river needs guards too. I told him not to be daft.
  • I've been thinking about it ever since. Clear 40 Bank Lorangs on the The Long Reach Banks, then go to his stall in the Crown Market and tell him I said: yes. He'll know what it means.
  • And tell him his prices are still a disgrace.
  • Then I'll tell him myself. Loudly. In front of customers.
  • Forty lorangs, then tell Silas at the Crown Market.
  • Silas came down to the bank at noon, shouting about a guard boat. A whole boat! Ha. He'll name it after a fish.
  • Thank you, Player. You've a fisher's patience. Here, and an eel, if you want one. No? Your loss.
  • She said yes? Ha! The river needs guards! I told her! I told her over the mackerel!
  • Tell her I'll have a guard boat on the water by next week. And tell her my prices are fair, and she knows it.

docs.title: Torn Nets
docs.text:
Agatha's nets come up torn. The lorangs and clangs of the Long Reach Banks cut the small tears with their claws; hunt them, and see if that explains the rest.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Agatha Level 34 After A Question for His Sister Leads to A Barge That Must Sail, Guards for the River

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Bank Lorang in The Long Reach Banks
  • Defeat 30 Bank Clang in The Long Reach Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 16,840 EXP
  • 680 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Agatha
Dialogue
  • Look at this. Father's nets, and I mend them every night, and every morning they come up like this. Small cuts, a hundred of them, and then the big rents.
  • The small ones are claws, I'd bet my boat. Bank Lorangs and Bank Clangs on the The Long Reach Banks have grown big as buckets. Clear 30 of each and let's see if the nets come up whole.
  • Upriver, past the reed beds. Mind your fingers. Ha!
  • Fair enough. I'll mend again tonight. I always do.
  • Thirty lorangs and thirty clangs on the Long Reach Banks.
  • Fewer little cuts, that's sure. You did that, and thank you. But look here.
  • (She holds up a net with a rent through four rows at once, the edges ragged.) No crab did this. Something bigger. I'm keeping to the shallows, and I'm not telling Father. Here, for your work.

docs.title: Nets for the Boats
docs.text:
Saltgulls come in off the Wrack Ledges and tear Agna's nets on the drying racks. Take a mended net to Sorcha, then defeat 50 Saltgulls.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Agna Level 42 After Torn Nets

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Sorcha
  2. Defeat 50 Saltgull

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 23,200 EXP
  • 1,700 mesos
  • Highland Jumper x1
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Agna
Dialogue
  • Now here's a tear I understand. The big gulls come in off the Wrack Ledges, the savage ones, and rip my drying nets open for the fish scraps in them.
  • Take this Mended Net down to my Sorcha first, she'll want it for the morning. She always wants it for the morning. Then go and thin those gulls where they roost: 50 Saltgulls on The Wrack Ledges.
  • Mind your eyes with those gulls. They go for the eyes.
  • Then I'll mend and mend again. I've done it fifty years.
  • The net to Sorcha, then 50 Saltgulls on The Wrack Ledges. Off you go.
  • Fifty gulls! The racks will be quiet a while. Gulls remember. Better than people do.
  • Here. Morag knitted me this jumper, and it's three sizes too big, because Morag thinks everyone is thin. You're out on the cliffs in the wind. Take it, and don't tear it the first day. I'll know.
  • My mother's net! Look at that, you can't even see where it was torn. She's a wonder, she is, and if you tell her I said so I'll deny it.
  • Tell her it'll be in the water by dawn. Inshore. Tell her that too, she'll want to know.

docs.title: Agna's Notch
docs.text:
Agna cut a notch in the cove rocks as a girl, at the highest spring tide anyone remembered. Her knees will not take her out to it now.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Agna Level 54 After The Greystrand Leads to Marks Where the Boats Cannot Go

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at Agna's notch on the cove rocks in Goa Harbour
  2. Talk to Eilidh

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 19,500 EXP
  • 2,150 mesos
  • Eilidh's Tide Slate x1
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Agna
Dialogue
  • I cut a notch on the cove rocks when I was ten. My father's gutting knife. The highest spring tide anyone then remembered.
  • I have not walked out there in years. Go and look at it for me. Tell me where the water is.
  • Find Agna's notch on the cove rocks (press Up there).
  • Mind the weed. It is slippery, and I am too old to fish you out.
  • Suit yourself. It has been there sixty years.
  • The notch, on the cove rocks. Go on.
  • Twice. Over my notch, twice this spring. And the child wrote it down on a slate.
  • ...Not bad. The slate, I mean. Not bad at all. Take it to the Wardens' House. Ailsa will want it more than I do.
  • You found my slate! I hide it in the crack, there. Every evening I write the tide.
  • It went over Grandma's notch twice. Twice! I did not tell anyone because I did not know who to tell. Will you take it to her?

docs.title: Torn Nets
docs.text:
Agna wants to lay Shore Crab claws beside her torn nets and see which tears are crab work. Bring her 20 Shore Crab Claws from the Undercliff.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Agna Level 30 Leads to Nets for the Boats

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Shore Crab Claw (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,700 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Salted Fish x5
  • +25 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Agna
Dialogue
  • You. Yes, you. You go down to the cliff foot, don't you, where the crabs are?
  • Half the inshore nets come back cut. I know a crab's work when I see it, but I want to lay the claws beside the tears and be sure.
  • Bring me 20 Shore Crab Claws from the Shore Crabs on The Undercliff. Whole ones, mind.
  • Twenty. Whole ones, not smashed. A smashed claw tells me nothing.
  • Then I'll guess. I'm usually right. I'd rather be sure.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 claws. Whole ones.
  • Give them here.
  • This one's crab work. And this. And this, see how the mesh is nipped, not bitten through.
  • And these long ones, from the boats that went past the point. No. Not crabs. I knew it, and now I know I knew it. Here, for your trouble. And not a word of this to Eilidh.

docs.title: Agnes a wing on the sill
A Wing on the Sill
docs.text:
Agnes found a leathery wing on a windowsill in the long gallery. Peterkin says the old drains are full of stirges. Find out whether he is right.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Agnes Level 24 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to Bats in the Chimneys

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Drain Stirge in The Old Drains
  2. Bring 5 Stirge Wing (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,400 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Agnes
Dialogue
  • I found something on a windowsill in the long gallery this morning. A wing. Leathery. Not a bird's, and the window was shut.
  • Peterkin says the drains under the old quarters are full of stirges these days. I would very much like him to be wrong.
  • Go down into the The Old Drains and deal with 30 Drain Stirges, and bring me 5 Stirge Wings so I can see if they match.
  • Thank you! Not a word to anyone. Well. Half a word.
  • Then I shall keep the window shut and my mouth shut. One of those, anyway.
  • Thirty Drain Stirges in the The Old Drains, and five wings.
  • Same wing. Exactly the same. Oh, I do not like that.
  • Well, there are thirty fewer now. I will keep this to myself. Mostly. Half, anyway.

docs.title: Bats in the Chimneys
docs.text:
Something flutters in the upper hall chimney at night. Hunt the tunnel bats under the old quarters, then tell Osbert, since he only half believes Agnes.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Agnes Level 28 After A Wing on the Sill

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Tunnel Bat
  2. Talk to Osbert

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,300 EXP
  • 560 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Agnes
Dialogue
  • There is a flutter in the upper hall chimney at night. I have not told Osbert. He will want to know why I am up at night.
  • Hunt 30 Tunnel Bats in the deep tunnels under the old quarters, then tell Osbert about the chimney. Please. It is better from you; he only half believes me.
  • Thank you! And if he asks why I was up, you have no idea. Which is true.
  • Then I will sleep with a broom. Not that I sleep.
  • Thirty Tunnel Bats, then Osbert.
  • He said that? That is practically a blessing. Thank you, Player. I might even tell him the other half one day.
  • A flutter in the upper hall chimney. And Agnes heard it at night.
  • Tell her I shall have the flue netted. And tell her the hours a maid keeps are her own business, as long as the fires are laid. She will understand.

docs.title: Old Verses
docs.text:
Ahvi is troubled by an old verse about beasts growing wild. Ask Odda and Thrun what verses they remember from the oldest part of the long songs.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Ahvi Level 45 Leads to The Beast Verse

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Odda
  • Talk to Thrun

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,400 EXP
  • 900 mesos
  • Rimwort Tonic x10
  • Goat's Milk x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ahvi
Dialogue
  • There is a verse in the oldest part of the long songs, among the chieftains of the Age of Division. A short one, seldom sung. A season before the Burning, it says, when the plateau beasts grew wild: goats that bit, cats that hunted people, birds that would not settle.
  • I have sung it alone every night this summer, and every night I hear Yarrek's goats in it, and the gnawers on the bridge. I do not trust my own ears any more. Would you ask Odda and Thrun what they remember of it? Odda has heard me ask. You she may answer.
  • Ask them what they remember, not what they think. Memory first. Thinking is for afterwards.
  • Then I sing it alone again tonight. Perhaps the hundredth time will tell me.
  • Ask Odda and Thrun what they remember of the beast verse.
  • So. Odda remembers old Hadda singing it, once, at a winter feast, and the hall going quiet. Thrun remembers its beat, slow and uneven, and remembers it under his hands this summer without meaning to.
  • That is not an answer. It is two people who heard what I heard. That is worth more to me than an answer. Thank you, Player. Whether I sing it at the gathering is still mine to decide.
  • Ahvi sent you about the verse. Of course. I have been asked, and I have not answered, and Ahvi is too kind to ask a third time.
  • I remember old Hadda singing it once, at a winter feast when I was a girl. The hall went quiet and the children stopped fidgeting. I never heard it sung in the hall again. Tell Ahvi that. Only that, for now.
  • The beast verse! Slow, uneven, a beat that limps. I have drummed it maybe twice in my life. Here, listen: dum, dum... dum. Like something that does not trust the ground.
  • Funny thing. This summer I caught my hands playing it on the table at supper, and I had not thought of it in years. Odda gave me a look. Tell Ahvi my hands remember it, even if I would rather they did not.

docs.title: The Beast Verse
docs.text:
Ahvi wants to know whether her old verse about beasts grown wild is true. Hunt 60 Bone Hounds in the War Camp Ruins and tell her what you saw.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Ahvi Level 62 After Old Verses

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Bone Hound in The War Camp Ruins

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 80,500 EXP
  • 1,240 mesos
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ahvi
Dialogue
  • The verse I have sung alone all summer says that in a season before the Burning, the beasts of the plateau grew wild: goats that bit, cats that hunted people, birds that would not settle. I have always sung it as a story. I need to know whether it is true.
  • Odda and Thrun gave me the verses they remember, and none of them gainsays it. But a song-keeper does not sing what she has only heard. In the ruins of the old camp, they say, there are hounds of dust and bone that hunt anything that moves.
  • Go to The War Camp Ruins and face them: 60 Bone Hounds. Then come and tell me whether the beasts are growing wild again, or whether I am an old woman frightened of a song.
  • Watch how they hunt. Not only how many. How.
  • Then I will go on singing it to myself. That is not knowing, but it is not nothing.
  • Sixty Bone Hounds in The War Camp Ruins, and watch how they hunt.
  • In packs? Circling, and coming at you from the side you were not watching, like the cats in the verse? And nothing driving them but a hunger that is not hunger?
  • Then the verse is true. Not true as a story is true; true as a tally is true. It happened once, in a season before the Burning, and it is happening now.
  • I still do not know what it means, and I will not sing more than the verse says. But I will not doubt it again. Thank you, Player. Take these; Lessa insists.

docs.title: The Plant from Near the Edge
docs.text:
Celandine wants a plant that grows only near the Forest Edge. Ailo would rather she did not have to go.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Ailo Level 23 After Sitting Up with Ailo

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 3 Celandine's Plant (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,877 EXP
  • 506 mesos
  • +60 standing with Ailo
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +100 standing with Celandine
  • +60 standing with Merrow
Dialogue
  • ...Celandine wants a plant from near the Edge.
  • Merrow worries when she talks about going. Fetch it, so she needn't. The firefly slimes trample it. Sometimes they carry a sprig away.
  • Bring 3 sprigs of Celandine's Plant from the firefly slimes on the first Shimmerwater path.
  • ...Thank you.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • ...Three sprigs.
  • ...Good.
  • Ailo gives the sprigs to Celandine without a word. Merrow, watching from his wall, looks enormously relieved.

docs.title: Sitting Up with Ailo
docs.text:
Sit up one night in the Herb Gardens with Ailo and watch the seedling beds.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Ailo Level 20 After The Night Diggers Leads to Past the Last Lantern, The Plant from Near the Edge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the seedling beds in Fairy Forest

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,775 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • +100 standing with Ailo
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • ...It's dark now.
  • Sit by the beds. Be very still. Lanterns make them run.
  • Keep watch by the seedling beds at the bottom of the gardens (examine them).
  • ...Shh.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • ...The beds. By Merrow's wall.
  • You saw them. Small slimes, young ones, wet from the lake. They dig into the warm beds, then run from the light toward the outer paths.
  • ...I'll replant in the morning. Tell Seren. The trail goes out past the lanterns.

docs.title: A Hard Quill
docs.text:
Ailsa writes the Tide Book with gull quills, and only the Saltgulls of the Wrack Ledges grow feathers hard enough. Bring her 30 Saltgull Feathers.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Ailsa Level 52

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Saltgull Feather (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 29,000 EXP
  • 2,080 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Tonic x5
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Ailsa
Dialogue
  • You are standing on my light, Player. There. Thank you. Can you tell a good quill from a bad one? No. Nobody can, any more.
  • I write the book with gull quills, as Keeper Innes did. The harbour gulls give soft feathers that split in a week. The Saltgulls of the Wrack Ledges give long, hard ones that last a moon. Innes swore by them, and at very little else.
  • Bring me 30 Saltgull Feathers. Flight feathers, from the ledges. I shall know if you bring me harbour gulls.
  • The Wrack Ledges are below the Saltface, above the waves. Halvard says the gulls there are savage. Halvard says that about the quay gulls too.
  • Then I shall write with a split quill and blame you in the margin.
  • (how many you carry) of 30 Saltgull Feathers. I can count, Player. I count tides for a living.
  • Let me see. Long. Hard. Barely bloodied. These will do.
  • Forty-six years at this desk. I have cut a great many quills. Halvard knows the number, I expect. Do not ask him, he will tell you.
  • Take these for the walk. And thank you. The book is kinder to a good quill.

docs.title: Not All of It
docs.text:
The next day's slack comes on its hour. Ailsa has written something in the margin.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Ailsa Level 68 After The Undertow

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Brigid
  • Talk to Cormac

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 64,500 EXP
  • 2,700 mesos
  • Sounding Charm x1
  • +60 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Ailsa
Dialogue
  • The slack came on its hour this morning. On the minute. And the run is back in the middle of the gap.
  • The spring highs are still a hand's breadth higher. I have written it in the margin: not all of it. Go and tell those who should hear it from you.
  • Tell Brigid and Cormac what has changed.
  • Then come back and let me thank you properly.
  • As you like.
  • Brigid, and Cormac.
  • Not all of it. But the hour is back. The first wardens would have taken that.
  • Wear this. Lachlan found a dozen in the caves and gave me one. He says they ring when the sea is close. Nonsense, but a pleasant one.
  • The slack is on its hour? Then the low beds will drain again, a little.
  • I am moving the healthiest roots up to the high rocks anyway. Elspeth helps me now. It is easier, with her.
  • The whole verse! I sang it at the Gap Inn last night, start to finish, for the first time in my life.
  • Mhairi played under it. I cried, of course. Everyone pretended not to see. Bless them.

docs.title: Marks Where the Boats Cannot Go
docs.text:
Eilidh's slate, Agna's notch and the dead pines agree with Ailsa's pages. She wants tide marks driven where the wardens' boats cannot go.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Ailsa Level 58 After Agna's Notch Leads to The Hour the Water Forgets

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Deliver 1 Eilidh's Tide Slate
  2. Look at the Jaw's waterline in The Forest Jaw
  3. Look at the west skerry in The Skerries
  4. Look at the east skerry in The Skerries
  5. Look at the middle skerry in The Skerries
  6. Defeat 50 Wrackgolem in The Skerries
  7. Defeat 50 Grey Bull in The Skerries

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 48,500 EXP
  • 2,300 mesos
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Ailsa
Dialogue
  • A child's slate. A notch cut sixty years ago. Dead pines. And my pages. They all say the same thing, and I did not want them to.
  • I need marks where the boats cannot go: on the Jaw at the waterline, and out on the skerries. Drive these in at slack water. The reefs are not empty, I am told.
  • Give Ailsa Eilidh's slate, drive tide marks on The Forest Jaw and on three of the skerries (press Up at each), and clear 50 Wrackgolem and 50 Grey Bull on The Skerries.
  • Slack water. Not a minute after.
  • Then the marks wait. They are good at waiting.
  • The Jaw, then the skerries.
  • Your marks agree with my pages. Exactly. I had hoped one of us was wrong.
  • The oldest pages might hold the answer. They are in the first camp's Magician hand, and I can only half read it. Half is not enough.

docs.title: A Rumour for Mother
docs.text:
Alaric heard in the kitchens that boars are digging up the sheepfolds on the Downs. See the high fold on the Thyme Banks for yourself, chase off the boars, and tell the queen.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Alaric Level 24 After Why the Bees Are Mean

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the high fold in The Thyme Banks
  2. Defeat 25 Downs Boar
  3. Talk to Aveline

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,400 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Alaric
Dialogue
  • I heard in the kitchens that boars are digging up the sheepfolds on the Downs. Nobody else has heard it yet. I checked.
  • Mother acts on my rumours. Sometimes. Only the good ones, so I need proof.
  • Go to the high fold on the The Thyme Banks and see if it is dug up, and chase off 25 Downs Boars. Then tell Mother. You can say it was my rumour.
  • Remember everything. Every hoofprint!
  • Then I will have to tell her without proof. She will ask why. Everyone always asks why. Except me. No, I do too.
  • The high fold on the The Thyme Banks, the boars, then Mother.
  • She said thank you! And wash. She always says wash. That is two of my rumours she has acted on this month!
  • Alaric's rumour? About the sheepfolds?
  • Dug up, and the boars thick round it. I will send word to the patrol tonight. Tell him his mother says thank you, and that he is to wash before supper.

docs.title: Alaric why the bees are mean
Why the Bees Are Mean
docs.text:
Nobody can tell Alaric why the bees have gone mean. Bring him wild bee stingers for his jars, and show them to Godwin first.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Alaric Level 21 Leads to A Rumour for Mother

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Bee Stinger (taken)
  2. Talk to Godwin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,700 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Alaric
Dialogue
  • Why have the bees gone mean? Godwin does not know. Mother does not know. Nobody knows, and I hate that.
  • Bring me 10 Bee Stingers from the Wild Bees at Downs Edge, for my jars. And show them to Godwin first; he will want to see.
  • Do not get stung! Or do, and tell me what it feels like.
  • Why not? ...All right. Why not later, then?
  • Ten stingers, then Godwin. He is always in the rose walk.
  • He has no proverb? Then it really is a mystery! I shall label the jar 'Why'. With a question mark.
  • Stingers from the Downs. The same as ours. Only angrier, in the hand that used them.
  • Tell the boy I have no proverb for it yet. Tell him I am working on one.

docs.title: What Came Out at the Carts
docs.text:
Something came out of the dark at the carts on Alder's road to the forest. He will not talk about it. He wants to know.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Alder Level 17 Leads to The Smell of the Sea

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 50 Glimmerwings (Glimmerwing, Crowned Glimmerwing)
  • Talk to Kestrel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,184 EXP
  • 374 mesos
  • +150 standing with Alder
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Kestrel
Dialogue
  • ...All right. The carts. On the way here, at night, in the Bloomwood. Something came out of the dark. Lots of somethings. Glowing. Stinging.
  • I want to know what they were. Kestrel clears that road. Ask her. And... maybe see them for yourself. So I know they can be beaten.
  • Defeat 50 glimmerwings in the Bloomwood, then ask Kestrel what attacked Alder's carts.
  • Thanks. Really.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The Bloomwood, then Kestrel.
  • Glimmerwings. A swarm. And you cleared fifty of them? And Kestrel says they're nothing to her?
  • ...Huh. I feel better. Like it was something, not just the dark.
  • The carts from Goa? Glimmerwings. A swarm, drawn by the cart lanterns.
  • Tell the boy they're a nuisance, not a nightmare. And tell him I said he was brave to keep walking.

docs.title: The Smell of the Sea
docs.text:
Alder misses the sea. The nearest thing to it in the forest is the lake at Shimmerwater.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Alder Level 29 After What Came Out at the Carts, Past the Last Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 8 Lake Dew (taken)
  • Defeat 40 Creature of Shimmerwaters (Firefly Slime, Shimmer Slime, Water Sprite, Forest Sprite)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,693 EXP
  • 638 mesos
  • +150 standing with Alder
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • The forest has no sea. I've checked. Twice. But you've been to the lake? Does it smell of anything?
  • Bring me some of its water. I want to sit on my bed and pretend.
  • Bring Alder 8 Lake Dew from Shimmerwater, and clear 40 creatures from its paths.
  • Big water. Even pretend big water.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Lake water for Alder.
  • It doesn't smell of the sea. It smells of leaves.
  • ...It's nice, though. Leaves. I think I like leaves. Don't tell anyone at home.

docs.title: Aldith mint at the waters edge
Mint at the Water's Edge
docs.text:
The mint bed at the bottom of Aldith's garden is wilting at the water's edge. She wants the ligators off the reed beds where the river comes from, and fern fibre from the Long Reach to mulch the roots.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Aldith Level 33 After Teeth for Comparing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Reed Ligator in The Reed Beds
  • Gather 8 Fern Fibre

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,780 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Aldith
Dialogue
  • Something's wrong with my mint, dear. Seventy years it's drunk this river, and now the plants at the water's edge are wilting. Only those. The ones up the bank are fine.
  • The ligators churn the reed beds upstream and send the silt down. Thin them: 40 Reed Ligators in the The Reed Beds. And gather 8 Fern Fibre on the Long Reach. I'll mulch the roots, the way Mother did.
  • Morning's best for the ferns. Never in the rain.
  • I'll water them by hand, then. Mint likes a fuss.
  • Forty ligators in the Reed Beds, and eight fern fibres.
  • (She tucks the fern round the mint and pats the soil.) There. They've perked up already. Or I'm imagining it. Either way, it's done me good.
  • Thank you, dear. If I ever find someone patient enough for this garden, I'll tell them about you. Here.

docs.title: Teeth for Comparing
docs.text:
The gripped bargehand's bruise still troubles Aldith. She wants ligator teeth from the Reed Beds to lay against her drawing of it.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Aldith Level 31 After A Night Without Lanterns Leads to A Question for His Sister, Mint at the Water's Edge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 8 Ligator Tooth (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,440 EXP
  • 620 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Aldith
Dialogue
  • Come in, dear. You've been up the Reach with Tristan, haven't you? Then you've seen the ligators. I've a drawing here: a bruise on a bargehand's leg, shaped like a grip.
  • Bring me 8 Ligator Tooths from the Reed Ligators in the The Reed Beds. I want to lay them against the drawing. Have some river mint first. No? Have some anyway.
  • Mind the bites. And come straight here if you get one. River mint, dear.
  • Off you go, then. Mint's here when you want it.
  • Eight ligator teeth, dear. You have (how many you carry).
  • (She lays the teeth along the drawing, one by one, then sits back.) Too small. Much too small. Whatever gripped that lad, it wasn't these.
  • I'll write that down. I write everything down now. Here, for your trouble, and a sprig of mint.

docs.title: Alwyn kit on the lock gate
Kit on the Lock Gate
docs.text:
Kit has gone up the Old Cut to see a sea creature, and the tide has filled the lock behind him. Find him on the lock gate at the Timber Ponds, clear the crabs and bring him home.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Alwyn Completed with Kit Level 26 After Stings in the Casebook Leads to The Bootbreaker, The Shell in the Pinch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the lock gate in The Timber Ponds
  2. Defeat 30 Ironback Crab in The Timber Ponds

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,002 EXP
  • 780 mesos
  • +60 standing with Alwyn
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
  • Unlocks boss.bootbreaker
Dialogue
  • Player! Have you seen Kit? He's not in the yard, he's not at Maren's, and Bryony says he went off before breakfast to 'see a sea creature'.
  • Finch says he saw him going up the Old Cut. Up the Cut! The tide's been in since then. If he's on a lock gate when the lock fills...
  • Find him, Player. He'll be on a lock gate at the Timber Ponds, if I know my boy. Clear the crabs round him, 30 if that's what it takes, and walk him home to the yard.
  • Bring him back. I'll deal with the telling-off. Bryony will deal with the rest.
  • Another time, then.
  • Find Kit on the lock gate at the Timber Ponds and clear thirty ironback crabs. Then bring him home to the yard.
  • I wasn't scared. The crabs were scared. I was being BRAVE.
  • And listen, listen. Up past the Timber Ponds, in the Pinch, there's a shell moving in the water. An enormous one. Bigger than Grandad's workbench. It MOVED.
  • Tell Keziah! She'll know what to do. And don't tell Mum I was on the gate. Tell her I was near the gate.

docs.title: Proof for Dunstan
docs.text:
Alwyn wants his father to see what the sawbills do to a hull. Carry a sawbill bill and the scored plank from the night run to Dunstan's workbench.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Alwyn Completed with Dunstan Level 44 After The Night Run Leads to The Ripsaw, Heavier Timber

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Deliver 1 Sawbill Bill
  • Deliver 1 Scored Plank

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 28,403 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • +60 standing with Alwyn
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Seraphine gave you a plank off the Morrow's deck? Let me see. Look at those grooves. That's a sawbill going across the deck at night, and that's a deck plank, the same thickness as half the hulls in this harbour.
  • Dad says the old designs were good enough for Old Bain. Old Bain never met a sawbill. I've told him. He won't hear it from me.
  • Take a Sawbill Bill and the Scored Plank to his workbench in the yard. Put them down and say nothing. That's how you talk to my father.
  • Say nothing. Trust me.
  • Another time, then.
  • Take a sawbill bill and the scored plank to Dunstan's workbench.
  • ...
  • Hmph. Leave them there.
  • Alwyn. Get the heavy oak out of the far stack. The thick stuff. No reason. Don't look at me like that.

docs.title: Seasoned Timber
docs.text:
Alwyn wants old seasoned oak and iron out of the Saltgrace for the deep-water hull he has been drawing, and Kenwyn says she is safe to salvage now.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Alwyn Level 25 After The Holdfast

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Wreck Salvage (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,677 EXP
  • 550 mesos
  • +40 standing with Alwyn
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Kenwyn says the Saltgrace is quiet now. Do you know what's in her? Oak a hundred years seasoned. Iron from before the harbour had a forge. You can't buy that.
  • I've been drawing a hull for the deep water, thicker in the bow, ribs closer. Father calls it a waste of good timber. With her oak it wouldn't be.
  • Bring me 15 Wreck Salvage from the wreck. Her creatures carry it off, and the Holdfast had a store of it.
  • Old oak, old iron. Don't let Father see you bring it in.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fifteen Wreck Salvage from the Saltgrace. You've got (how many you carry).
  • Look at the grain. A hundred years at least. And this iron, hand-forged. There's nothing like it in the yard.
  • Father picked up a piece while you were here. Turned it over. Said nothing at all, which is the most he's said about my hull since spring.

docs.title: Practice Without Watching
docs.text:
Amaryl wants Siora to practise somewhere nobody watches. Siora must not realise Amaryl arranged it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Amaryl Level 20 After A Stubborn Seedling Leads to The Hazel That Answered

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Siora
  • Reach the quiet corner of the glade in Children's Glade

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,908 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • +120 standing with Amaryl
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +100 standing with Siora
Dialogue
  • Siora's gift is real. It's slow to wake because she's frightened of failing in front of people. So: no people.
  • There's a quiet corner of the Children's Glade. Suggest it. As your own idea. If she knows I sent you, it's ruined.
  • Suggest to Siora that she practise in the quiet corner of the glade, and go with her.
  • Your idea. Not mine.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Siora, then the glade.
  • She made a light. A small one. It stayed lit for a whole breath.
  • ...My idea? No, no. Yours. Entirely yours.
  • A quiet place? Where nobody watches? Is there one?
  • ...The corner of the glade? That's... that's a good idea. Will you come? Just at first?

docs.title: A Stubborn Seedling
docs.text:
Amaryl needs a stubborn seedling for her lessons: one that will not grow easily, so her students learn to coax.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Amaryl Level 15 Leads to Practice Without Watching

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 4 Stubborn Fern Root (taken)
  • Defeat 40 Road monsters (Slime, Bubbling, Glimmerwing, Crowned Glimmerwing)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 821 EXP
  • 330 mesos
  • +100 standing with Amaryl
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Easy seedlings teach nothing. I want stubborn ones. The ferns along the roads grow in the worst soil in the forest.
  • Bring me fern root and clear the roads where they grow, so my students can come and see them.
  • Bring 4 Stubborn Fern Roots: the bubblings trample them up along the roads. Clear 40 monsters there.
  • Don't pull them gently. They'll know.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Ferns and the roads.
  • Good. Ugly, stubborn and alive. Perfect.
  • My students will hate them. Then they'll love them. That's teaching.

docs.title: Checking the Marks
docs.text:
Ambrose's newest marks lie under the headland. From the Holm Wood's Old Fellings and the Rim, where the pale light comes up through the trees, they can be checked.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Ambrose Level 63 After What Seraphine Saw Leads to The Ledge She Was Reaching For, The New Marks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the light through the Old Fellings in The Old Fellings
  2. Look at the light at the Rim in The Rim
  3. Defeat 80 Glimshade

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 82,418 EXP
  • 1,890 mesos
  • +60 standing with Ambrose
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The newest marks lie under the headland. No ship can check them. But the wood above can.
  • At night a pale light comes up through the trees in the Holm Wood. The woodcutters stopped going in last year. Check my marks for me: look at the light through the Old Fellings and the light at the Rim, and tell me where it's strongest. The shades walk where the light falls. Clear 80 of the glimshades that carry it.
  • Poppy will want to draw them as you tell me. She's been here every morning since the drawer opened.
  • Strongest where? That's what the chart needs.
  • Another time, then.
  • Look at the light through the Old Fellings and at the Rim, and clear eighty glimshades.
  • Strongest at the Rim. Over the sea-hole. Poppy, the new mark goes there. Very small, like I showed you.
  • There's a sea-hole in the wood's heart, joined to the Drop under the headland. That's where it rises. Not out past the headland any more. Here. Under us.

docs.title: The Locked Chart
docs.text:
Ambrose keeps a separate chart in a locked drawer, of every mark the captains have brought him. He will open it, with the Harbour Master's leave and with Jowan there.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Ambrose Level 57 After The Blue Logbook Leads to Where the Keel Was Brushed

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Quenna
  2. Talk to Jowan

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 61,217 EXP
  • 1,710 mesos
  • +60 standing with Ambrose
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Halloran has been to see me. And Ysolde, which she has never done in twenty years. I know what they want.
  • The drawer. The captains have brought me marks for years, places where something was seen in the water. I started a separate chart when the sailors began steering round the marks on the ordinary ones. I've locked it away. I refused to guess what it meant.
  • I'll open it. But I want Quenna's leave first; it concerns the harbour. And I want Jowan there. He's walked past that drawer since he was small. He should see.
  • My son's on the docks. My wife's in the hall. Ask her first.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask the Harbour Master's leave, then fetch Jowan from the docks, for Ambrose.
  • There. Every mark the captains brought me, by year. See how they creep? Each summer a little closer to the headland.
  • And the newest lie under it. Under the headland itself, where no ship sails.
  • Jowan has gone very quiet. So has his mother. I'm sorry, Player. I should have unlocked this a long time ago.
  • Ambrose wants my leave to open his drawer? He's had it for three years. He never asked.
  • Tell him yes. And tell him I'm coming down to look, council or no council.
  • Dad's opening the drawer? The locked one? I've never looked. I promised myself I wouldn't. The key keeps moving.
  • I'm coming. Right now. Tell Captain Halloran I'm off the docks for an hour. He'll understand.

docs.title: A Golem Core
docs.text:
Guards from the quarry road come to Ansel bruised as if a wall fell on them. He needs a specimen: the core stones of the Cut Golems of the Deep Cut.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Ansel Level 60 After The Adventurer's Notes, A Question for His Sister Leads to Powdered Golem Stone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 5 Golem Core Stone (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 70,000 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Elixir x10
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Ansel
Dialogue
  • The guards from the quarry road come to me bruised from the inside, as if a wall had fallen on them. I can draw a claw. I cannot draw a wall.
  • A physician who understands a wound can treat it. I need a specimen, whole and fresh, from the The Deep Cut.
  • Bring me 5 Golem Core Stones from the Cut Golems. I shall weigh them, draw them and, I confess, knock on them.
  • Mind your head. And your ribs. And come to me after, whatever happens.
  • Of course. Come back to me when you are stronger; I will still be here, and so, I fear, will they.
  • Five cores from the Cut Golems of the The Deep Cut. Whole ones, if you can manage it.
  • Heavy. Warm, still? No... it is my hands that are cold.
  • Whether these stones slept all along or something woke them, I cannot say, and I will not pretend to. But now I can draw what strikes my guards. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Ansel a question for his sister
A Question for His Sister
docs.text:
Ansel has a bite in his ledger that closed from too many sides. Carry his question to his sister Aldith on the Riverside and bring back what she says.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Ansel Level 32 After Teeth for Comparing Leads to Torn Nets, A Golem Core

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Aldith
  2. Talk to Ansel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,400 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Ansel
Dialogue
  • My sister sends me teeth. Aldith, sending me evidence! In forty years she has sent me nothing but opinions.
  • Here is the thing. I have a bite in my ledger that closed from too many sides, drawn to scale. She has a bargehand's bruise.
  • Carry her my question, Player: not a recipe, a question. Has she drawn the bruise? Bring me back what she says.
  • She will call me a superstition with a ledger. Let her. Ask her anyway.
  • Another time. The river has kept its secrets this long.
  • My sister's cottage is on the Riverside. Ask her my question, and come back to me.
  • Thank you, Player. I came here with a ledger and went away with a question, and a sister to share it with. That is more than I had this morning.
  • From Ansel? A question? Not a lecture? Well, I never.
  • Tell him yes, I drew it. Here, the bruise, to scale, as he likes. It is not a ligator's. And tell him to eat something.
  • Her drawing. Let me lay it beside... yes. Here, and here.
  • The same shape. Twice. One on a guard's arm on the royal road, one on a bargehand's on the river.

docs.title: Grandmother's Window
docs.text:
Arlo has written six complaints about the pilots of his own. Take his list up to his grandmother Ysmay at the top of the Cliff Stairs, and see how many she says aye to.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Arlo Level 32 After Whose Reading

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ysmay

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,500 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • Salted Fish x5
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Arlo
Dialogue
  • I write down Grandmother's complaints about the pilots. She watches the gap from her window and she knows everything they do wrong. Then I check them with someone who knows. They usually agree.
  • But now I've written some of my own. Six, from the quay. I want to know if she'd say aye to any of them.
  • Would you take my list up to Ysmay, at the top of the Cliff Stairs? I can't go. Father wants me on the quay to hand him wicks till the lanterns are lit.
  • Her house is the narrow one near the top, with the window that sees the whole inlet. Knock loud. She says she can't hear. She can.
  • Fine. I'll keep them. Six complaints is a lot to keep.
  • My list, up to Grandmother at the top of the Cliff Stairs.
  • Arlo's list? Give it here. 'Kor whistles in the gap.' Aye. 'Corrie looks back at the ship too often.' Aye, she'll learn. 'Nessa argues with her crew.' Nessa argues with the sea, child, that's not a fault. Four out of six. Tell him his grandmother says four, and tell him four is more than his mother got at nine.
  • Four? She said four?
  • Four ayes. And Mother got fewer at nine? Grandmother said so? She said so!
  • I'm going to write that down. Here, this is for you, I saved it. Don't tell anyone I write complaints. They'll all want to read them.

docs.title: Whose Reading
docs.text:
Arlo and Eilidh read last night's tide differently and argued about it. Ask Eilidh what she saw, look at the water from the cove rocks, and tell Arlo who was right.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Arlo Level 24 Leads to Grandmother's Window

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Eilidh
  2. Reach the cove rocks in Goa Harbour

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,500 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Fish Cake x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Arlo
Dialogue
  • You read water, don't you? Adventurers have to. Then you can say who's right.
  • Last night on the cove rocks, Eilidh said the tide was still making when the light went. I said it had turned. We argued till her mother shouted. Then we argued quieter.
  • Go and ask Eilidh what she saw. Then go out to the cove rocks and look at the water yourself, and come back and tell me I'm right. Or tell me the truth. Tell me the truth.
  • Eilidh's in the coves. She'll say she's right. She always says she's right. Sometimes she is.
  • Fine. I'll ask Varro. No I won't. He'll only say closer.
  • Ask Eilidh first, then look at the water from the cove rocks. Then tell me.
  • Arlo sent you? Of course he did. It was still making. The weed on the black rock was still lifting when the light went, I watched it. He was looking at the foam, and foam lies. Go and look, then. You'll see.
  • Well? Who's right?
  • The water was standing? Not making, and not turned? That's not an answer.
  • ...That's slack. We were both looking at slack and calling it different things. That's worse than one of us being wrong.
  • Don't tell Eilidh I said that. I'll tell her. Tomorrow. Maybe. Here, this is for you.

docs.title: The Day the Expedition Came Home
docs.text:
Aspen wants to tell someone the story of the day the Great Expedition came home. All of it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Aspen Level 12

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Sefa
  • Defeat 30 Road monsters (Slime, Bubbling, Glimmerwing, Crowned Glimmerwing)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 428 EXP
  • 264 mesos
  • +120 standing with Aspen
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Sit! I'll tell you the whole of it. The day the expedition came home, fifty years ago. Half the forest ran to the Edge.
  • ...Sefa says I tell it wrong. Sefa says there's a better ending. Go and ask Sefa. And bring me back word of the roads, the way the carters used to.
  • Hear Sefa's side of the story from Sefa, and clear 30 monsters off the roads for news.
  • Then come back and tell me Sefa's wrong.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Sefa, and the roads.
  • Sefa's ending? Hmph. ...It is a better ending. Don't tell Sefa.
  • And the roads are clear? In my day... well. In my day they were clear without anyone clearing them.
  • Aspen's story? He always stops when the expedition comes home. That's not the end.
  • The end is the next morning, when the forest went back to work, and everyone was a little kinder. That's the end. Tell him.

docs.title: Old Friends
docs.text:
Aspen has noticed Oriel working late in the old homes. He has decided not to tell anyone, which is a first.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Aspen Level 54 After The Homes That Will Not Wake

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Oriel
  • Defeat 80 Creature of the Gloamings (Gloaming Wisp, Thorny Bramble, Forest Howlet, Night Howlet, Forest Glimmerfox, Night Glimmerfox, Blue Spring Sprite, Deep Spring Sprite)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 35,844 EXP
  • 1,188 mesos
  • +150 standing with Aspen
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +80 standing with Oriel
Dialogue
  • Oriel's working late. Every night. I've noticed. Everyone thinks I notice nothing but bridges.
  • I'm not going to tell anyone. I've decided. But I'd like him to know his old friend's with him. You tell him. And take my old walking route out west for me, it's too far for these knees now.
  • Tell Oriel that Aspen knows and won't tell, and walk Aspen's old route out west (80 creatures in the Gloaming).
  • He'll grumble. That means thank you.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Oriel, and the old route.
  • He grumbled? Good. That means thank you.
  • Fifty years we've known each other. I can keep one secret for him. One.
  • Aspen knows? And he's told nobody? Aspen?
  • Oriel is silent a while. Then he grumbles something about old fools. It sounds a great deal like thank you.

docs.title: Tell the Boy
docs.text:
Aubrey has a message for Captain Rhys he will not deliver himself. Defeat 30 tunnel bats in the drains first, wrist practice, he says, then tell Rhys.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Aubrey Level 27 After The Wrong Cover

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Tunnel Bat
  2. Talk to Rhys

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,000 EXP
  • 540 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60% x1
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Aubrey
Dialogue
  • Bats. Fast, small, never where you swing. Best wrist practice there is. I learned on them, when the drains were drier.
  • 30 Tunnel Bats in the drains. Then go and tell the boy, Rhys, that he still drops his left shoulder on the third bout. He'll know which bout.
  • Wrist straight. Zzz.
  • Mm. The boy can drop his shoulder another year.
  • Thirty tunnel bats, then the boy.
  • He said what? 'Tell him I know, and that I'm working on it.' Ha. Twenty-two years, and he still answers like a recruit.
  • Good. Off you go. Wake me if anyone holds a sword properly.
  • Aubrey says I drop my left shoulder on the third bout. ...He's right. He's been right for twenty-two years. Tell him I know, and that I'm working on it.

docs.title: The Wrong Cover
docs.text:
Aubrey's page came out of a chest of old Guard drill books. He wants the rest of the book, and old paper in this city ends up in the Academy or down the drains. Go down to the Cisterns, clear 30 of what lives there and search an old shelf.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Aubrey Level 24 Leads to Tell the Boy

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Cisterns
  2. Defeat 30 monsters in The Cisterns
  3. Look at a rotted shelf of old books in The Cisterns

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,000 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Aubrey
Dialogue
  • Mm. You again. Your wrist's better. Sit. Don't tell the boy what I'm about to say.
  • My page came from somewhere, folded in a cover where it didn't belong. In this city, old paper ends in two places: the Academy, or the drains. I've done the Academy.
  • Go down to the The Cisterns. Clear 30 of what lives there, and look at the old shelves the drain-menders talk about. If there's a page in my hand's age, bring me word of it.
  • Mind the damp. Paper doesn't, but you should.
  • Mm. Then I'll go back to sleep.
  • The Cisterns, thirty of what's down there, and the old shelf.
  • Pulp. Nothing but pulp and a binding with no name. ...Well. It was worth a look.
  • The rest of that book is somewhere, or nowhere. I'm old enough to live with both.

docs.title: The Lost Lesson Notes
docs.text:
Aurel has lost his lesson notes. Again. Before the bell. Again.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Aurel Level 14

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 4 Aurel's Lesson Notes (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 671 EXP
  • 308 mesos
  • +100 standing with Aurel
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • My notes! The whole lesson! Word for word! The wind took them out of the window and halfway to the Bloomwood.
  • The glimmerwings like paper. They pick it up. Please, before the bell.
  • Bring back 4 pages of Aurel's Lesson Notes from the glimmerwings of the Bloomwood.
  • The bell! Hurry!
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • (how many you carry) of 4 pages.
  • My notes! Oh. Oh no. I won't need them. The lesson's over. I taught it without them.
  • ...I taught it without them. It went well. Sorrel's going to be insufferable.

docs.title: A Question of Riding
docs.text:
The princess comes to breakfast with blistered hands. The queen asks you to put one question to Osbert and one to Elinor, gently, and bring back what they say.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Aveline Level 24 After What the Patrols Meet Leads to The Crown's Bounty

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Osbert
  2. Talk to Elinor

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,400 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Aveline
Dialogue
  • May I ask you something that is not a matter of state? It concerns my daughter.
  • Elinor comes to breakfast with blistered hands and a look of great innocence. I am very hard to fool, Player, and I am not fooled.
  • Ask Osbert whether anyone leaves the palace before dawn. Then ask Elinor where she goes. Gently. I will not have her spied on; I only want to hear what each of them says.
  • Gently, mind. She is very much her mother's daughter.
  • No, you are right. It is a family matter. Forget I asked. I will not.
  • Osbert first, then Elinor. Gently.
  • Every bolt in its place by breakfast. And the horses are very well.
  • Thank you, Player. I will not ask anyone else. I would rather she tells me herself, when she is ready, and I would rather be ready when she does.
  • Before dawn? The palace has a great many doors, Player, and I am a great many years old.
  • Tell Her Majesty the household is in good order. Every bolt is where it should be by breakfast.
  • Where do I go? Riding! Early. Everyone knows that.
  • Did Mother send you? ...Tell her the horses are very well. And I am very well. And there is nothing to worry about.

docs.title: The Crown's Bounty
docs.text:
The Chalk Hives sit too near the road. The crown pays a bounty for every forty Chalk Hive Bees cleared, as often as you like.

Town Selsior Category Repeatable Given by Aveline Level 27 After A Question of Riding

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Chalk Hive Bee in The Chalk Hives

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,800 EXP
  • 540 mesos
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +50 standing with Aveline
Dialogue
  • The The Chalk Hives sit too near the road for my liking, and the patrols cannot be everywhere at once.
  • The crown pays a bounty for every 40 Chalk Hive Bees cleared from the The Chalk Hives. As often as you like, Player.
  • The crown keeps its accounts. Osbert sees to that.
  • Whenever you are ready. The bounty stands.
  • Forty Chalk Hive Bees from the The Chalk Hives.
  • Forty more. The road is a little safer tonight. The crown thanks you, again, and means it every time.

docs.title: What the Patrols Meet
docs.text:
Reports are paper; the queen wants eyes. Ride out to Downs Edge, deal with the wild bees at the road's verge, and tell Leofric what you saw.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Aveline Level 21 Leads to A Question of Riding

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Wild Bee in Downs Edge
  2. Talk to Leofric

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,300 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Aveline
Dialogue
  • Every week a report from the roads, and every week the marks spread on my husband's map. Reports are paper, Player. I want eyes.
