  • Ride out to Downs Edge, where the road passes the Downs. Deal with 30 Wild Bees there, then tell Leofric what you saw. He will want it for his map.
  • Thank you. Come back and tell me too; I listen to the end.
  • Then another day. The roads will still be there, more's the pity.
  • Downs Edge first, then my husband, by his map beside my study.
  • Drawn. Thank you, Player. I listen to everyone to the end, and today you were the one worth hearing.
  • Bees at the road's verge? Thirty of them. Mm. And the date: today.
  • There. A new red mark, a little nearer the Tree Gate than the last. Tell her it is drawn.

docs.title: A Stick That Holds
docs.text:
Avice's walking stick from the highlands finally broke. Bring her 10 pieces of hard dark stump bark from the Rootlands to bind a new one, then tell Pim she is not going soft.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Avice Level 17 After Where No One Watches

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Dark Stump Bark (taken)
  2. Talk to Pim

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,500 EXP
  • 340 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Avice
Dialogue
  • My stick broke. Cut it myself in the highlands. Walked every day to Selsior on it.
  • Ten pieces of Dark Stump Bark. Hard, black ones, from the The Rootlands. I'll bind a new one. Then tell Pim I'm not going soft. He'll say I am.
  • Hard bark. Not the crumbly kind.
  • Then I'll walk without one.
  • Ten dark stump bark. Then Pim.
  • Good bark. Holds. ...Thank you.
  • Avice said WHAT? That she's not going soft? I never said she was! I said she smiled once. On Tuesday. Possibly at a horse.

docs.title: Where No One Watches
docs.text:
Avice wants to train where no recruit can watch. Go with her to the Rootlands and defeat 30 of its monsters, keeping pace with her.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Avice Level 15 Leads to A Stick That Holds

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 monsters in The Rootlands

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,000 EXP
  • 300 mesos
  • Orange Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Avice
Dialogue
  • You. Spar with me. Not here. Too many eyes.
  • The The Rootlands. Thirty of whatever's there. Keep up.
  • Good. Don't talk on the way.
  • Fine. I'll go alone.
  • Thirty. Rootlands. You're slow.
  • Not bad. ...Better than not bad. Don't tell Pim.

docs.title: Aylwin a note for the palace
A Note for the Palace
docs.text:
Aylwin cannot leave the patrol, and a note about a new foal in the Guard stables needs to reach the palace. Carry it to Princess Elinor, then clear 25 wild bees off the road verge at Downs Edge so he can come home on time.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Aylwin Level 25 After Boars on the Downs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Elinor
  2. Defeat 25 Wild Bee in Downs Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,000 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Aylwin
Dialogue
  • Could you... carry a note to the palace? It's only about the horses! The grey mare foaled last night. The princess has always come to see the foals. Since she was small. That's all.
  • I can't take it myself. Patrol. And if I went I'd... it's only about the horses.
  • Take this to Elinor, please. Then, if it's not too much, clear 25 Wild Bees off the verge at Downs Edge, so the patrol's home before the gates close.
  • Thank you! It's only about the horses. Did I say that?
  • No, of course. It's only a note. About horses.
  • The note to the palace, then the bees at Downs Edge.
  • She read it? She said that? ...Sorry. I'm not blushing. It's the sun. On the downs. Earlier.
  • Thank you, Player. Really. I'll... put that one somewhere safe.
  • A note? From the stables? ...The grey mare foaled! Tell him, tell the stables, I'll come down to see it. Tell him to call it Hat. He'll understand.

docs.title: Boars on the Downs
docs.text:
The boars on the Thyme Banks are the same breed as the pack Aylwin faced on the road to Kaldemor, and they are getting closer to the road. Defeat 30 of them and bring back 5 tusks for his grandfather.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Aylwin Level 22 After Short a Rider Leads to A Note for the Palace

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks
  • Bring 5 Boar Tusk (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Aylwin
Dialogue
  • The boars on the downs, Player. Same bristles, same eyes as the pack on the road to Kaldemor. The one that ate my hat. Really, it ate it.
  • Would you thin them out on the The Thyme Banks? 30 Downs Boars. And bring 5 tusks. My grandfather will want to look at them. He looks at everything that comes off the road.
  • Thank you! Mind your hat. I mean it.
  • That's all right. The patrol will get to them. Eventually.
  • Thirty boars on the Thyme Banks, and five tusks for my grandfather.
  • Five tusks. Grandfather will grumble over them for an hour, then tell me nothing. That's how I know he's worried.
  • Thank you, Player. The road's a little safer. That's the whole job, really.

docs.title: Baldwin oil for the gate lamps
Oil for the Gate Lamps
docs.text:
Baldwin needs more oil for the extra lamps he keeps burning near the city gate. Fetch his order from Gilbert the candlemaker, then see the lamps at the gate.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Baldwin Level 6 Leads to Past the Light

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Gilbert
  2. Reach Selsior Gate

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 50 EXP
  • 120 mesos
  • Red Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Baldwin
Dialogue
  • Evening, Player. My oil is low, and the lamps by the gate want more of it than they used to. More lamps, you see. Nobody asked me to light them. I light them anyway.
  • Go to Gilbert in the old quarters and tell him Baldwin's order is the same as last week. Then walk down to the Selsior Gate and see the lamps there.
  • Thank you. Gilbert hums while he measures. Let him finish the tune.
  • No hurry. The lamps have never minded waiting.
  • Gilbert first, then the gate.
  • You saw them? A little thread of light inside the gate. For travellers who come in late, that is all.
  • Here. It is not much. Lamplighters are not rich, but we are seldom in the dark.
  • Baldwin's order, same as last week? Here it is, all measured. ... Do not tell him what I charged. He thinks oil has always cost this. Let him think it.

docs.title: Past the Light
docs.text:
Baldwin wants to know what moves in the dark just past the last lamp outside the Tree Gate. Walk out to the end of the Hedge Lanes and clear what you find.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Baldwin Level 8 After Oil for the Gate Lamps

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the last lamp in The Hedge Lanes
  • Defeat 30 Orange Mushroom past the lights (Orange Mushroom) in The Hedge Lanes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 230 EXP
  • 160 mesos
  • Red Potion x8
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Baldwin
Dialogue
  • Fifty years I have watched the dark, Player. Lately the dark past the gates is not as empty as it was. Past the Tree Gate too, on the The Hedge Lanes.
  • I set one lamp at the near end of the lanes. Just in case. I should like someone to walk past it and see what is out there, just past the light.
  • Walk to the last lamp on the The Hedge Lanes, then deal with 30 Orange Mushrooms that wander there after dark.
  • Mind your step. Stay where the lamps are, until you cannot.
  • Quite right. The dark is not going anywhere.
  • The last lamp on the The Hedge Lanes, and what wanders past it.
  • Mushrooms, then. Only mushrooms. ... Good. That is good.
  • I shall set another lamp there tomorrow all the same. Just in case. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: The Swordfish Scar
docs.text:
Barnaby swears the scar on his hand is from a swordfish. Nobody believes him. A sawbill's bill would be proof enough for the Salt and Bread.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Barnaby Level 34

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 3 Sawbill Bill (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,106 EXP
  • 748 mesos
  • +40 standing with Barnaby
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • They laugh at my hand! 'Swordfish,' I say. 'Gull,' they say. A gull! I ask you.
  • Bring me 3 Sawbill Bills. I'll lay them on the bar at the Salt and Bread next to my hand and let them laugh then.
  • Big ones! The bigger the better!
  • Another time, then.
  • Three sawbill bills for Barnaby. You have (how many you carry).
  • HA! Look at them! Lay one by my hand. See? See the spacing? That's a bill, that is!
  • Well. A sawbill, not a swordfish. Close enough. A fish with a sword on its face. I'm telling it that way from now on.

docs.title: What Seraphine Saw
docs.text:
Barnaby wants Seraphine to see the scored keel timber. She has refused to describe what she saw in the deep water to anyone.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Barnaby Completed with Seraphine Level 61 After Where the Keel Was Brushed Leads to Checking the Marks, A Blank Chart

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Broken Keel Timber

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 74,882 EXP
  • 1,830 mesos
  • +60 standing with Barnaby
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You've got a keel with the marks on it? Annis sent you to ME? Ha! Finally!
  • Seraphine saw something out there. She's never said what. She heard my eyes story once and shut herself in her cabin. Take that timber to her, and let me come with you. I'll stand at the door. I won't say a word. I'll say a few words.
  • I'll stand at the door. Quiet as a mouse. A big mouse.
  • Another time, then.
  • Take the broken keel timber to Seraphine, with Barnaby at the door.
  • ...Sit down. Both of you. Barnaby, shut the door.
  • Last spring, the night run, deep water. A shoal of lights came up under the Morrow, pale ones, all round her. And in the middle of them something as long as my ship turned over, slow, and looked at me. Eyes as big as cartwheels.
  • Barnaby. You were right. I'm sorry I never said.

docs.title: A Question for Thomasin
docs.text:
Bartholomew wants stingers from the Chalk Hives, and a question carried, not a letter, to his protegee Thomasin.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Bartholomew Level 27 After My Father's Fold

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Chalk Hive Stinger (taken)
  2. Talk to Thomasin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,080 EXP
  • 540 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Bartholomew
Dialogue
  • I do not send letters. Letters get answered. I send questions, which get thought about.
  • Bring me some stingers from The Chalk Hives, so I can put one beside the old drawings in the library. Then carry a question to Thomasin for me.
  • Collect 10 Chalk Hive Stingers, then ask Thomasin: has any account of the war ever told of beasts turning before?
  • Word for word, mind. She hates a question that has been tidied up.
  • It will keep. The good ones always do.
  • Ten stingers from The Chalk Hives, and my question to Thomasin. Word for word.
  • Ten! Look at the length of that one. And what did she say?
  • "Nobody knows, yet." Ha. That is my girl. "Yet" is the most hopeful word in the Academy, Player. Thank you.
  • The Master sent you with a question, not a letter? Of course he did. Go on.
  • Has any account told of beasts turning before? Tell him: nobody knows, yet. And tell him I am looking, which he knew before he asked.

docs.title: My Father's Fold
docs.text:
Bartholomew's father built a sheepfold on the Thyme Banks. Boars have come up onto the downs and root up the folds. See whether his still stands.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Bartholomew Level 23 After The Downs I Grew Up On Leads to A Question for Thomasin

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the old sheepfold in The Thyme Banks
  2. Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,460 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Bartholomew
Dialogue
  • My father built a fold on The Thyme Banks. Dry stone, waist high, a gate that never shut properly. I learned my sums counting through it.
  • The shepherds say boars have come up from the woods and root the folds apart. I would like to know if his still stands. Sentimental of me. I know.
  • Look at the old sheepfold on The Thyme Banks, and drive off 30 Downs Boars while you are there.
  • Past Downs Edge, where the thyme grows thickest. Look for a gate that does not shut.
  • Quite right, quite right. Boars are no joke. Neither are old men, but we pretend.
  • The fold on The Thyme Banks, Player, and the boars around it.
  • Still standing? Half of it. Well, that is more than half of me some mornings.
  • Thank you, Player. Now: why did the boars leave the woods? Not tonight. But it is the next question.

docs.title: Bartholomew the downs i grew up on
The Downs I Grew Up On
docs.text:
Bartholomew grew up a shepherd's son on the downs beyond the capital. He hears the bees there have turned mean, and he would like someone to go and see.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Bartholomew Level 20 Leads to My Father's Fold

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach Downs Edge
  • Defeat 25 Wild Bee in Downs Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,100 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Bartholomew
Dialogue
  • Did you know I was a shepherd's boy? The open downs, beyond the city. Thyme, clover, sheep who argued less than my students.
  • Now the patrol says the wild bees on Downs Edge sting anything that walks the road. Bees, Player. Bees were the friendliest thing up there.
  • Walk out to Downs Edge for an old man and thin out 25 Wild Bees. Then come and tell me what the place looks like now.
  • Go along the royal road past the gate. You will smell the thyme before you see the downs.
  • Another time, then. The downs have waited sixty years for me; they will wait for you.
  • Downs Edge, Player. Mind the bees. Well, no: do the opposite of minding them.
  • Still green? Still wide? Good. And the bees sting the road now. I see.
  • Here, for your trouble. Now, the real question: why would a bee change its temper? Think about it on the way home.

docs.title: Bastian Gives His Time
docs.text:
Bastian has talked over Rivet twice at the Open Table and is mortified. He means to give up his own time at the next gathering so Rivet can speak about the second lift, but Rivet must not know. Make sure Rivet comes.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Bastian 'Bellows' Krell Level 35 After Measure the Gap

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Rivet

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,610 EXP
  • 2,100 mesos
  • +70 standing with Bastian 'Bellows' Krell
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player. Come here. Closer. No, closer, I am trying to be quiet, it does not come naturally. I have done a bad thing, twice, and I did not even notice I was doing it.
  • Rivet has waited two whole gatherings to speak about a second rooftop lift, by the Old Barracks. Both times I stood up first about my bridge, and both times I went on until the candles did. Dimity showed me the pages. Rivet's name is at the top of the list, and then there is me, for nine pages.
  • So at the next gathering, when Rook calls my name, I am going to stand up, say 'I give my time to Rivet', and sit down. Sit down! Me! Mags says she will believe it when she sees it, and she is bringing a stool to see it from.
  • But Rivet must not know. If I promise and fail, that is worse than never promising. Just go to Rivet on Workshops Row and make sure Rivet comes to the next gathering, with the drawings. Not a word about me. Can you be that quiet? I cannot.
  • Good! Quietly! Rivet is by the lift at the end of the Row, the big one with the crates going up. Say whatever you like, except the true thing.
  • Ah. Then I shall have to persuade Rivet myself, and I will shout, and I will give the whole thing away in the first breath. Come back if you can, Player.
  • Has Rivet promised to come? With the drawings? And you have not told? Good, good, quietly, quietly.
  • The next gathering? Why would I go? I have been twice. Both times I sat with my drawings on my knee while Bastian built a bridge out of words, and both times the candles went out first.
  • Margo says I should shout. I do not shout, I build. The second lift would save every porter on that stair by the Old Barracks a hundred climbs a day. My mother hauled crates up stairs like that for twenty years. It is not a bridge over a market. It works.
  • Fine. Because you asked, and because you have the look of someone who knows something. I will come, with the drawings. Third time. If Bastian starts on his bridge, I am leaving by the window.
  • Rivet is coming? With the drawings? And you said nothing? Player, you are the quietest person I have ever liked. I could shout. I will not. Look at me not shouting.
  • I have practised. 'I give my time to Rivet.' Five words. I have never said five words at the Table in twenty years. Mags timed me this morning. I said it in four breaths and then added a speech about the beauty of brevity, so we are still working on it.
  • Come to the gathering, Player. Sit near the front. If you see me begin to stand up for longer than five words, cough.

docs.title: Measure the Gap
docs.text:
Bastian 'Bellows' Krell wants numbers for his covered bridge over Lantern Square. Ask Vane, the rooftop bridge-builder, how wide the gap is and how much timber the bridge would need.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Bastian 'Bellows' Krell Level 23 Leads to Bastian Gives His Time

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Vane

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,050 EXP
  • 1,380 mesos
  • +50 standing with Bastian 'Bellows' Krell
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player! You have the face of somebody who wants the Night Market dry in the rain! Everybody does! A covered bridge over Lantern Square, roof and all, and nobody's pepper bun ever soggy again!
  • I have drawings. I have costings. I have a speech about the dignity of a dry bun that made Mags cry, she says from the onions. What I do not have is a number from somebody who actually builds bridges, and the Table keeps asking for one, rudely.
  • Go up to the Rooftops and ask Vane, who has built every plank bridge in this city. How wide is the gap over the square, and how much timber would my bridge need? I would go myself, but Vane jumps on planks to test them, and I am a large plank.
  • Splendid! Vane is usually somewhere high, jumping on something. Ask nicely. Ask loudly too; it is windy up there.
  • No? Ha! Then I shall estimate! I am an excellent estimator! I estimate the Table will not like it.
  • Vane, Player, on the Rooftops! The gap, the timber, the number! I have left a space in my speech the exact size of it.
  • Bastian's bridge. I know. I have measured that gap three times this month, quietly, just in case. From the Fiddler's Crossing to the far gutter it is wider than the Great Hall is long, and a roof doubles the load.
  • Timber? More than reaches this city in a year, with the carts the way they are. I have told him that. He heard 'more timber', and then he heard 'what a magnificent bridge that would be'.
  • Tell him the number anyway. And tell him the Wobbler was called impossible too, and it does not even wobble. I would not want him to give up. Just to wait.
  • More than a year of timber? A YEAR? Then the bridge is impossible! I withdraw it! I withdraw it with dignity, and a short speech!
  • Wait. The Wobbler was impossible too, Vane said? Then I un-withdraw it! A bridge built in two halves, a year apart! No, three thirds! The Table will need a vote on the fractions!
  • Inkpot will put that down as my fourth change of mind this week. Worth it. Thank you, Player: a real number at last. I shall shout it beautifully.

docs.title: Follow the Tracks
docs.text:
This time Bekk goes with leave, and with you. Follow the raider's tracks over the Hot Rocks (three places) and clear 80 Iron Boars from the way.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Bekk Level 46 After Find Bekk Leads to Grimhorn

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the tracks on the long flat in The Hot Rocks
  2. Look at the tracks on the high rock in The Hot Rocks
  3. Look at the tracks toward the mesa in The Hot Rocks
  4. Defeat 80 Iron Boar in The Hot Rocks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 62,000 EXP
  • 920 mesos
  • Trail Watch Boots x1
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Bekk
Dialogue
  • Mother says I may follow the tracks now, if you are with me and I do what you say. She said it in front of the whole rim. I have never been so embarrassed or so happy.
  • The tracks cross The Hot Rocks in three places I could not reach last time. Read them with me. And the Iron Boars will come at us the whole way: 80 of them, if it is like before. I have arrows this time. Lots of arrows.
  • You lead. I will stay behind you. Mostly.
  • I will wait. Properly, this time. I promised.
  • Three places on The Hot Rocks where the tracks cross, and eighty Iron Boars.
  • Did you see it? Up by the ash. Huge, grey with dust, and horns, great horns, one of them broken off short. It went up onto The Ash Mesa like it owned it.
  • A great horned beast. I said so a month ago and nobody listened. I do not feel as happy about being right as I thought I would. Mother will want to hear. And Thrun.

docs.title: Grimhorn
docs.text:
The raider is Grimhorn, a great horned beast on the Ash Mesa. Bekk waits at the edge; the fight is yours alone. Defeat it and bring Grimhorn's Hide to Thrun.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Bekk Completed with Thrun Level 48 After Follow the Tracks Leads to The New Hide

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Clear Grimhorn
  • Bring 1 Grimhorn's Hide (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,500 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • Highland Salve x15
  • Bonesetter's Draught x5
  • +60 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Bekk
Dialogue
  • The rim calls it Grimhorn now. Somebody said it once and it stuck. It is on The Ash Mesa, and it will come down for the herds again the moment the nights get long.
  • My father tracked a beast like that alone, out on these slopes. I will not. I will be at the edge of the mesa with every arrow I own, and I will not set foot on it, because you will be faster without me and mother made me swear. Tell me when you are ready and I will take you up.
  • And Player: if it falls, bring its hide down to Thrun. Not to me. Thrun has been waiting longer than I have.
  • Tell me when you are ready, and I take you up to the mesa. Watch its feet. It paws the ground before it charges.
  • Then we both wait. I am getting better at it.
  • Defeat Grimhorn on The Ash Mesa, then take Grimhorn's Hide to Thrun in the Great Hall. Tell me when you want to go up.
  • What is this? Is that... that is a great horned beast's hide. That is a whole hide, and thick as a door! Player, I said I would not ask anyone. I did not ask. You did it anyway.
  • Bekk brought the horn down too, the chipped one. Skarra came up to the hall and turned it over in her hands for a long while. Then she put it down and went home, and said nothing at all. I did not ask her.
  • Come back to me soon. A hide is not a drumhead until Vosk and I have fitted it, and I want you there when it speaks.

docs.title: Far Slopes Bounty
docs.text:
Bekk pays a Trail Watch bounty for 80 monsters of the Far Slopes, gnawers, boars and hogs alike. He will pay it again, any time.

Town Midbarium Category Repeatable Given by Bekk Level 31 After The First Report

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 80 Far Slopes monsters (Cliff Gnawer, Wild Boar, Scarred Boar, Flint Hog, Iron Boar)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,000 EXP
  • 620 mesos
  • +20 standing with Midbarium

The first time you complete it instead: 26,000 EXP, 1,000 mesos, Highland Salve x10, +15 standing with Midbarium, +30 standing with Bekk

Dialogue
  • The Trail Watch pays a bounty for the far slopes, and I get to hand it out, which makes me feel very important. 80 monsters out there: Cliff Gnawers, boars, hogs, anything that would bite a herder. Bring me another eighty any time and I pay again.
  • Across the far bridge and keep going. Count as you go. I would, but I lose count when I am excited.
  • Another time. The slopes are not going anywhere. Unfortunately.
  • Eighty monsters of the Far Slopes, Player. Gnawers, boars, hogs, they all count.
  • Eighty! Mother will put that on the map as one less dot. Well, eighty less dots. You know what I mean.
  • Here is the bounty, from the Trail Watch. Come back when the slopes fill up again. They always do.

docs.title: Far Slopes Elites
docs.text:
Now and then a beast of the Far Slopes is touched by the Disturbance and grows fiercer. Bekk pays well for each such Elite brought down.

Town Midbarium Category Repeatable Given by Bekk Level 32 After The First Report

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Elite Elite of the Far Slopes (Cliff Gnawer, Wild Boar, Scarred Boar, Flint Hog, Iron Boar)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,000 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • Highland Salve x3
  • +20 standing with Midbarium

The first time you complete it instead: 9,000 EXP, 1,200 mesos, Highland Salve x10, Elixir x3, +15 standing with Midbarium, +30 standing with Bekk

Dialogue
  • Some of the beasts out there are worse than the rest: bigger, angrier, and they shrug off arrows. The Trail Watch calls them Elites and pays extra for each one. Bring one down on the far slopes and the bounty is yours, as often as you like.
  • They show up when you have been hunting a while. Keep at it on the slopes and one will find you.
  • Fair. They are not friendly.
  • One Elite of the Far Slopes, Player. Keep hunting out there; they come to the busy hunters.
  • You got one? Mother will want to know which kind and where. I want to know how big.
  • The Elite bounty, with the Watch's thanks. Come back for another whenever you like.

docs.title: The Raider
docs.text:
Bekk wants to track the herd raider, and his mother has forbidden him to go alone. You agreed to go with him at first light, but at dawn he was gone. Tell Skarra.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Bekk Completed with Skarra Level 42 After Wide Tracks Leads to Find Bekk

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,300 EXP
  • 840 mesos
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Bekk
Dialogue
  • You measured the tracks for my mother. Three hands across, right? I knew it. I have been saying for a month that it is something big, and nobody listens to the youngest scout on the rim.
  • She says I may not go after it alone. Fine. I will not go alone. I will go with you. Sleep by the rim fire tonight, and we leave at first light, before the children wake and want to come too.
  • First light. I will wake you. I am always up first.
  • Then I wait. I am good at waiting. Ask anyone. No, do not ask anyone.
  • Bekk's bedroll by the rim fire is empty and cold, and his bow and rope are gone from the peg. Skarra needs to know.
  • You are alone. Where is my son? He said he would go with you, and you came back without him.
  • He left before light. His rope is gone, and his good bow. He knew you would make him wait for the morning, so he did not wait. I forbade him to go alone and he found the one way to obey me and still go.

docs.title: A Binding Described
docs.text:
Benedict can describe his lost chronicle's binding to the last stitch. He asks his old pupil Petronella and his sister Ermengarde to keep watch for it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Benedict Level 25 After Rats in the Lower Stacks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Petronella
  2. Talk to Ermengarde

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,690 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Benedict
Dialogue
  • Brown calf, blind-tooled, five raised bands, a stain shaped like a ladle on the back board. I could draw it with my eyes shut.
  • The missing volume of the Aristocrat chronicles. Eighteen years. I search every shelf every year, and it is never there.
  • Describe it to Petronella at the palace, who sees every book that passes through the scribes, then to my sister Ermengarde, who sees every spine that breaks.
  • Exactly as I said it, please. The ladle matters.
  • No, no, of course. It has waited eighteen years.
  • Petronella first, then Ermengarde. Brown calf, five bands, the ladle.
  • Neither of them has seen it. No. I did not really think so.
  • But two more pairs of eyes are watching now. That is something. Thank you, Player.
  • Brown calf, five bands and a ladle-shaped stain? Nothing like it has crossed my desk. Tell Master Benedict I will look, and that I still hold my pen the way he taught me.
  • The ladle again. I'd know that binding if I saw it, dear, he's described it to me every winter. Tell him I'm watching. Tell him books go where they are... no. Don't tell him that.

docs.title: Benedict rats in the lower stacks
Rats in the Lower Stacks
docs.text:
Rats have come up into the great library's lower stacks from the old drains. Benedict wants them gone before they find the Aristocrat chronicles.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Benedict Level 21 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to A Binding Described

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Drain Rat in The Old Drains

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,920 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Benedict
Dialogue
  • (Whispering, very fast.) Rats. In the lower stacks. Gnawed straight through a Commons almanac, two hundred years old.
  • They come up from the old drains, the rat catcher says. Up, Player. Rats do not usually come up into libraries; there is nothing to eat but paper.
  • Go down into The Old Drains and see off 30 Drain Rats, before they find the chronicles.
  • Thank you. Thank you. Quietly, if you can. No, never mind, down there you may be as loud as you like.
  • Oh dear. Then I shall sit up with a lamp and a broom.
  • The Old Drains, Player. Thirty of them. I heard one again last night.
  • Quiet. Real quiet, the old kind. Thank you, Player.
  • Here. And if you ever want a book found, you come to me first. Nearly any book.

docs.title: Seasoned Timber
docs.text:
Bennet needs seasoned oak for the fast barge's keel: timber that has lain for years in the river under the Undercut's banks, where the crocos lie on it.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Bennet Level 40 After A Barge That Must Sail Leads to Across After Dark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Seasoned River Timber (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,080 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Bennet
Dialogue
  • (He knocks twice on the half-built hull.) Hear that? Good. Now hear this. (He knocks on a new plank.) Green. Green wood twists, and a fast barge can't twist.
  • Up past the quarry landing, the The Undercut has oak that's lain in the river for years. Seasoned like nothing in a yard. The Undercut Crocos lie on it. Bring me 10 Seasoned River Timber.
  • Let it drain on the bank before you carry it. Patience. Glue doesn't set any faster for shouting.
  • Fair enough. The barge has waited a winter. It can wait a week.
  • Ten pieces of seasoned timber. You have (how many you carry).
  • (Knock, knock.) Twenty years in the river, that. Maybe thirty. Sound as a bell.
  • That's the keel. Deeper than I first drew it, too. Don't ask me why I changed it. Here, and thank you.

docs.title: The Fast Barge
docs.text:
The fast barge is finished. Bennet needs someone brave enough to run it hard on the Long Reach, over the deepest pool, with Tristan watching from the bank. Ride it to the Heron Pool.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Bennet Level 48 After The Truth for Lucan Leads to Longjaw

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach above the Heron Pool in The Undercut

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,460 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +35 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Bennet
  • Unlocks boss.longjaw
Dialogue
  • She's done. Longest, narrowest barge on the river, and the keel's seasoned oak. Now she needs a first run, hard, on the Long Reach. And the bargehands won't. And Lucan won't stand on her. Loudly.
  • Tristan says the run should go over the deepest pool, the Heron Pool, flat out, and he'll be on the bank. Will you ride her? Meet us on the The Undercut, above the pool.
  • Hold on to the rail. And the other rail. Both rails.
  • Can't say I blame you. I wouldn't ride her either, and I built her.
  • Ride the fast barge to the Undercut, above the Heron Pool.
  • She ran. Lord, she ran. And it came after her. A croc as long as the barge itself, out of the deep, right behind us into the Heron Pool.
  • Tristan's calling it Longjaw. It's in the pool now. When you're ready to finish it, ask me. I'll take you there. She's fast enough. Just.

docs.title: Bertrand a name without a mark
A Name Without a Mark
docs.text:
A name on Bertrand's list has stopped appearing in the patrol reports: a former recruit posted to the old watch post on the Thyme Banks. Ask Helewise where his boots were sent, go to the post, and clear 30 downs boars around it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Bertrand Level 22 Leads to More Porridge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Helewise
  2. Reach the old watch post in The Thyme Banks
  3. Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,500 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Bertrand
Dialogue
  • You! Come here! ...No, you're not in trouble. Sit. This is a quiet one, and I'm bad at quiet.
  • A name on my list. Good lad, slow feet, big heart. Posted out to the downs. He was in every report for two years. Now he isn't in any. Not among the hurt. Just gone.
  • My wife Helewise sends boots to every post. Ask her where his went. Then go to the old watch post on the The Thyme Banks, and clear the 30 Downs Boars around it.
  • Go on, then! And come back with good news, that's an ORDER!
  • Fine. FINE. I'll go myself, with my knees.
  • Helewise, then the watch post on the Thyme Banks, then thirty boars.
  • His initials, fresh-cut in the post, with this week's date? HA! Slow feet and a big heart and he's still standing!
  • The reports go round a different way now, that's all. No mark in the margin. Not for him. Thank you, Player.
  • His boots? Sent to the Thyme Banks post, the spring before last, and a second pair this winter that somebody signed for. Tell Bertrand somebody is still wearing out boots up there.

docs.title: More Porridge
docs.text:
The biggest intake ever needs more oats than Helewise's budget allows. Bring 12 downs boar tusks from the Thyme Banks, which the market buys well, then take the news to Helewise.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Bertrand Level 25 After A Name Without a Mark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 12 Boar Tusk (taken)
  2. Talk to Helewise

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,800 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Bertrand
Dialogue
  • A year and enough porridge, I always say! Well, I've got the year. I'm short the porridge.
  • My wife says the budget's the budget. But boar tusk sells in the Crown Market, and oats are cheap!
  • Bring me 12 Boar Tusks from the The Thyme Banks! Then tell Helewise the oats are paid for, before she finds out from someone else!
  • MARCH!
  • Then my recruits drill hungry! ...No. Not on my yard. Ask me again.
  • Twelve boar tusks, then Helewise! The recruits are counting on you! I'm counting on you! LOUDLY!
  • Twelve tusks and a wife who's only a little cross! A good day!
  • Porridge for the whole intake. I'll make guards of every one of them. You watch.
  • He sold tusks for oats? Without asking me? ...Fine. It's a good price. Tell him I'll put it in the ledger as housekeeping.

docs.title: The Board: the Forest Jaw
docs.text:
The fishing boats see things on the Forest Jaw. Bethoc's board says so.

Town Goa Harbour Category Repeatable Given by Bethoc Level 54 After The Greystrand

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Creature on the Forest Jaws in The Forest Jaw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,800 EXP
  • 2,000 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +20 standing with Bethoc

The first time you complete it instead: 19,500 EXP, 4,000 mesos, +30 standing with Goa Harbour, +100 standing with Bethoc

Dialogue
  • The boats coming in past the Jaw have started chalking their own sightings. I cannot read half of them.
  • The house pays for every sixty.
  • Clear 60 creatures from The Forest Jaw.
  • I will chalk it up.
  • The board will still be there.
  • Sixty, on the Forest Jaw.
  • Wiped off. The boats will be pleased. Here.

docs.title: The Board: the Saltface
docs.text:
The climbers on the Saltface are on Bethoc's board most mornings now.

Town Goa Harbour Category Repeatable Given by Bethoc Level 34 After Lanterns to the Landings

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Climber on the Saltfaces in The Saltface

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,300 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • +25 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +20 standing with Bethoc

The first time you complete it instead: 6,600 EXP, 2,000 mesos, +25 standing with Goa Harbour, +100 standing with Bethoc

Dialogue
  • Climbers on the Saltface, three nights running. I have had to start a second plank.
  • The house pays for every fifty.
  • Clear 50 climbers from The Saltface.
  • I will chalk it up.
  • The board will still be there.
  • Fifty, on the Saltface.
  • Wiped off. For now. Here.

docs.title: The Board: the Strandwood
docs.text:
Bethoc's sighting board always has the Strandwood on it. The Gap Inn pays for every forty.

Town Goa Harbour Category Repeatable Given by Bethoc Level 22

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Strandwood creatures in Strandwood Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 920 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +20 standing with Bethoc

The first time you complete it instead: 1,850 EXP, 1,200 mesos, +20 standing with Goa Harbour, +100 standing with Bethoc

Dialogue
  • The board says the Strandwood again. It always says the Strandwood.
  • The house pays for every forty off the board. Nobody has ever asked where the money comes from.
  • Clear 40 creatures from Strandwood Edge.
  • I will chalk it up.
  • The board will still be there.
  • Forty, on the Strandwood Edge.
  • Wiped off the board. Here is the house's thanks, and the board will fill up again by morning.

docs.title: Three Nights Running
docs.text:
Three nights running, three different hands chalked the same thing on Bethoc's board: a fox bigger than the rest, out on the Strandwood. Defeat a Disturbance-touched Strand Fox.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Bethoc Level 24

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Elite Strand Fox

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,950 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x3
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Bethoc
Dialogue
  • Look at this, Player. Three nights running, three different hands, the same thing chalked on my board. A fox bigger than the rest, out on the Strandwood rocks. "Shining," one of them wrote.
  • Bigger than Torva's usual, the hunters say, and it shrugs off a blow like it's nothing. Disturbance-touched, they call that.
  • I'd like to wipe it off myself. Find a Disturbance-touched Strand Fox, an Elite, and put it down. Stay out there long enough and one turns up, the hunters say. One always does.
  • Out on Strandwood Rocks. I'd rather wipe a fox off that board than anything else I can think of.
  • It'll be there tomorrow. They always are.
  • Still on my board, that fox. An Elite Strand Fox, out on the Strandwood.
  • Gone? Truly?
  • Then out it comes. There. Three nights running, and wiped in one. A bowl of stew on the house, and two more for the road.

docs.title: Biscuit Follows His Nose
docs.text:
Biscuit has caught a smell and wants you to come with him: out to the wayside well on the Hedge Lanes, where the slimes have been at somebody's dropped lunch. Clear 20 slimes so he can investigate.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Biscuit Level 6

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the wayside well in The Hedge Lanes
  • Defeat 20 Slime in The Hedge Lanes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 100 EXP
  • 60 mesos
  • Red Potion x3
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Biscuit
Dialogue
  • Biscuit sniffs the air, sniffs your boots, then trots three steps toward the street and looks back at you. Then three more. Then back again.
  • He wants you to follow. Somewhere out past the Tree Gate, by the smell of him, toward the wayside well on the The Hedge Lanes. Something there is very, very interesting.
  • Biscuit wags his whole back end and sets off at a trot.
  • Biscuit sits down, sighs, and waits. He has all day.
  • Biscuit looks at you, then at the road, then at you. Twenty slimes by the wayside well are between him and whatever it is.
  • At the well Biscuit noses out a dropped half-loaf the slimes had been sitting on, slightly damp, entirely perfect.
  • He eats it at once, then leans against your leg for a long, grateful while. Woof.

docs.title: Bites That Will Not Close
docs.text:
Bess has a page in her count book for bad bites from the woods that will not close. She wants to try a poultice of Bluecap spores: collect 20 Bluecap Spore Sacs, then take them to Bram so the two can brew it side by side.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Bess Level 40 After The Late Pedlar Leads to The Woodcutters' Hut

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Deliver 20 Bluecap Spore Sac
  2. Talk to Bram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 32,000 EXP
  • 6,000 mesos
  • Bluecap Poultice x5
  • Recipe: Bluecap Poultice (Alchemy)
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Sit, Player. Show me your arms. Good, nothing new. You would be surprised how many come in this summer with a bite from the woods that swells by the hour and will not close. Comfrey does nothing. A red potion does nothing.
  • I keep a page for them in my count book. It is a long page now. I showed it to Bram, and for once in his life he did not argue with me.
  • Mother Sedge used to say what the woods poison, the woods can draw. The Bluecaps carry spore sacs under their gills. Bring me 20 Bluecap Spore Sacs, and then take them over to Bram: we will brew it together.
  • Twenty, mind, not nineteen. And do not squeeze them. They burst.
  • Then do not get bitten.
  • 20 Bluecap Spore Sacs from the Bluecaps, Player. Then go to Bram's stall: he is expecting you, though he will pretend he is not.
  • Bess sent you? With the sacs? Good. Put them there. No, there, by the mortar. She is coming over. We have it worked out: her poultice, my tincture to bind it. We argued about the order for an hour.
  • She was right, as it happens. Do not tell her I said so. Go and tell her it is brewing.
  • He said I was right, did he not? I can see it on your face. Well. The first batch is cooling, and the bite on a carter's leg has gone down by half since this morning.
  • Here is how to make it yourself, and a few to start you off. Wild spores, lavender and the sacs. It draws the swelling out and clears a poisoning, which is more than I can say for most things.

docs.title: Testing Springs
docs.text:
Bolt set a row of test spring-traps along the outer ditch to see how springs hold up in the damp. The ditch rats keep setting them off and making off with the bait. Clear 40 of them so the test counts.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Bolt Level 29 After The Secret Drawings

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Ditch Rat

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,000 EXP
  • 2,320 mesos
  • +60 standing with Bolt
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Margo wants to know if her springs rust in the damp. So I set twelve little test traps down in the Outworks, in the wet cellars, all wound to the same mark. I'm meant to check them after a week and measure how much they've lost.
  • But the ditch rats keep tripping them! Snap, and off they go with the cheese, and the spring's unwound, and the whole week's wasted. I've reset them four times. I said sorry to every one.
  • Could you clear out the rats, Player? 40 Ditch Rats should do it. Then the springs can just sit there and get rusty in peace. Which is what I want. For science.
  • Thank you! The traps are painted yellow. Please don't step on them. I mean, you can, they won't hurt much. Sorry.
  • That's all right. I'll reset them a fifth time. And apologise a fifth time.
  • 40 Ditch Rats in the Outworks' wet cellars. Mind the yellow traps.
  • A whole week and not one tripped! I went down and measured. Margo's springs lost a little. Not much. But the trap I made with a little counterweight on the arm, the one I didn't tell anybody about, lost nothing at all.
  • I've written it all down. In the notebook. Under my mat. Thank you, Player. Sorry. No. Just thank you.

docs.title: The Secret Drawings
docs.text:
Bolt has one question about counterweights that only Rivet can answer, and cannot bear to ask it himself. Ask Rivet for him, without saying why.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Bolt Level 23 Leads to Testing Springs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Rivet

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,050 EXP
  • 1,380 mesos
  • +50 standing with Bolt
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Can I ask you something? It's a small thing. It's a stupid thing. It's for a, um, a drawing. Not a real drawing. A thinking drawing. Under my... somewhere.
  • When Rivet changed the counterweight line on the lift after the jam last winter, how much heavier is the weight than the empty platform? Just that. One number. I can't ask. If I ask, Rivet will ask why, and if Margo hears I asked Rivet...
  • Would you ask Rivet? Just the one question. And please, please don't say it's for me. Say it's for you. Say you're interested in weights. People are interested in weights. Sometimes.
  • Thank you! Rivet's usually at the lift, at the end of the Row, by the old granary. Sorry. Thank you.
  • No, that's fair. It's a stupid question anyway. Sorry. Forget I said anything. Please actually forget.
  • Rivet, at the lift. One question: how much heavier is the counterweight than the empty platform. Not for me. For you. Sorry.
  • The counterweight? Heavier by about a half-crate of glass. That way an empty platform sinks slow on its own, and a loaded one only needs two porters on the winch instead of four. Simple. Simple always wins.
  • Why do you want to know? ...Interested in weights. Right. Nobody's interested in weights. (Rivet squints down the Row toward Margo's scorched door, then shrugs.) Fine. Whoever's asking, tell them they can come and look at it any time.
  • Half a crate of glass heavier! Of course! So it sinks slow on its own! That's... that's exactly the part I was missing. If you put a spring under it instead of a fourth porter... no, with a fourth... no...
  • Sorry. Thank you. Rivet said whoever's asking can come and look? Oh no. Oh, that's wonderful. Oh no. Please don't tell anyone I'm smiling.

docs.title: Brakka a stair of her own
A Stair of Her Own
docs.text:
Brakka dreams of carving the first new stairway down the cliff in a hundred years. Bring her 25 Dark Bark for her trial wedges, and look at the bare cliff on the Long Ridge where the stair's rock comes out of the mountain.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Brakka Level 22

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 25 Dark Bark (taken)
  • Look at the bare cliff in The Long Ridge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,300 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • Blue Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Brakka
Dialogue
  • Do not step on that! That is my stairway. Well, a sketch of it. The real one will go down the cliff to the valley floor, along the sounder rock to the south, landings cut right into the face. The first new way down since Durra's Stair, a hundred years ago.
  • Vosk says sketches are cheap. He is right. So I want to prove the rock. The seam my stair would follow runs right through the mountain, and up on the The Long Ridge the wind has stripped it bare. I can test it there without anyone telling me to mend a wall instead.
  • Bring me 25 Dark Bark for trial wedges, it splits clean. And look at the bare cliff on The Long Ridge for me: look it over closely and tell me if the seam runs straight.
  • You are the best! Do not tell my father. Do not tell Vosk. Actually, do not tell anyone.
  • Fine. I will carve it in my head again. I have done that a hundred times already.
  • Twenty-five Dark Bark, you have (how many you carry). And the bare cliff on The Long Ridge.
  • Straight, and grey-red the whole way down? No cracks across it? Then it holds. I knew it held!
  • Look, the wedges go here, and here, and the first landing here. Oh, I am going to need a much bigger stone to draw on.
  • Potions, with my thanks. When I cut the first step, you can walk down it first. Well, second. I am walking down it first.

docs.title: The Old Walls
docs.text:
Brakka wants to know how the first Kragvar cut stone. Inspect three old walls in the War Camp Ruins and hunt 100 War Masks or Bone Hounds.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Brakka Level 58 After New Staves Leads to Follow the Springs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the old gate wall in The War Camp Ruins
  2. Look at the broken tower wall in The War Camp Ruins
  3. Look at the high wall in The War Camp Ruins
  4. Defeat 100 War Mask or Bone Hounds (War Mask, Bone Hound)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 146,000 EXP
  • 1,160 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Brakka
Dialogue
  • Is it true there's a Savage war camp out past the Weathered Rocks with its walls still up? Real walls, cut in the Age of Division? I need to see how they cut.
  • My stairway needs gates and landings, places where it can be held. Durra's Stair was cut a hundred years ago and nobody has cut a new route since. The old walls were built to be held. They'll show me how.
  • Go to The War Camp Ruins and look closely at three walls: the gate, the broken tower and the highest one. And the things that prowl there, masks and hounds, thin them out, 100 of them, so the watch can come and go.
  • Look at the joints first. Then the tool marks. Then tell me everything, slowly. I'll want to draw it.
  • Vosk would say the same. Mend before you carve. Fine, but I'll still be here.
  • Three walls in The War Camp Ruins: the gate, the broken tower, the high wall. And a hundred of the masks or hounds.
  • Dry-laid? No mortar at all, and still standing? And the stones cut to lean into each other, so the weight holds them shut. Of course. Of course!
  • That's how a gate on a cliff stays up: you cut it so the mountain is pushing it closed. Vosk will say I should have known that. Vosk is right, which is the annoying part.
  • Take these, you'll need them more than I will. And tell me about the tool marks again. Slowly. I'm drawing.

docs.title: Apothecary First
docs.text:
Brann sends hurt travellers to an apothecary first, and the apothecary is short of slime bubbles for her salve. Bring Brann 12, then fetch the week's count of hurt travellers from Swithin.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Brann Level 7 Leads to Not in the Book

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 12 Slime Bubble (taken)
  2. Talk to Swithin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • 140 mesos
  • Red Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Brann
Dialogue
  • Hurt travellers go to the apothecary first, questions after. That's the rule at my gate. Trouble is, she's short of salve.
  • Bring me 12 Slime Bubbles from the The Hedge Lanes for her salve. Then go to Swithin and fetch me this week's count of the hurt. He keeps it in his book.
  • Good. Keep to the road.
  • Then the salve runs short. Don't make me say it twice.
  • Twelve slime bubbles, then Swithin's count.
  • Twelve bubbles for the salve, and Swithin's count. ...More crosses than last week.
  • Goes to the Knights' Court today. Thank you, Player. You've earned your welcome twice.
  • The week's count? Here. Nine crosses. Nine. Tell Brann I underlined it, so he cannot pretend he did not see.

docs.title: Not in the Book
docs.text:
A traveller came through Brann's gate without appearing in Swithin's book. Hollis heard from a carter that a man like him was seen at the great waystone. Ask Hollis, go to the waystone and clear 30 monsters on the Waystone Meadows.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Brann Level 12 After Apothecary First

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Hollis
  2. Reach the great waystone in The Waystone Meadows
  3. Defeat 30 monsters in The Waystone Meadows

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 700 EXP
  • 240 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Brann
Dialogue
  • A man came through my gate yesterday. I saw him. Swithin didn't write him. Swithin writes everyone. Twenty years, he's never missed one.
  • Either Swithin's getting old, and he isn't, or that man didn't want to be written.
  • Hollis talks to the carters. Ask him what he heard. Then go to the great waystone on the The Waystone Meadows and clear the 30 monsters around it. A man walking alone leaves a trail where the road's quiet.
  • Keep to the road. And mind the Guard. That's us.
  • Then I'll wait. I'm good at waiting. It's my job.
  • Hollis first, then the great waystone, then thirty on the meadows.
  • Footprints round the waystone and none going on. And nothing in Swithin's book.
  • Whoever he was, he knows how to walk past a gate. I don't like it. It goes to the Court today, and I'll watch the faces closer.
  • The man with the grey pack? A carter saw someone like him up at the great waystone, sitting on it like he owned the meadows. Stern face. I'd have welcomed him anyway. That's my trouble, isn't it?

docs.title: Brass and Tin
docs.text:
Mott the pedlar has heard where his stolen wares went. Recover 15 pieces of Pedlar's Tinware from the Hoarder Shrooms of Stonecap Keep.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Mott Level 57 After Shiny Things, Found Leads to Old Wall Iron

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 15 Pedlar's Tinware

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 70,000 EXP
  • 6,000 mesos
  • White Potion x25
  • +35 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Ah, my rescuer! Sit down, sit down. Wilf came by with a sack of buttons and said a thing that made me sit up: the Shrooms carry everything shiny up the walls of that old keep. Everything shiny, Player. That would include a pedlar's tinware.
  • Cups, pans, a brass-handled ladle I was very proud of. They had the lot off my pack in the woods. I have been selling ribbons all summer and telling people the tin is coming. It is not coming. It is up a wall.
  • Bring me back 15 pieces of Pedlar's Tinware from the Hoarder Shrooms at the Keep. Fifteen and I have a stall again. I will knock a little off anything you buy from me ever after. A little.
  • Wonderful. You will know my tin: every cup has an M scratched on the bottom. I scratched them myself on a long wet evening.
  • Of course. Ribbons are lighter to carry anyway. That is what I keep telling myself.
  • Fifteen pieces of Pedlar's Tinware, Player. Every cup has an M on the bottom.
  • The ladle! Oh, the ladle. A little bent, but a ladle is a ladle. And the M cups, and the pans. Do you mind if I just put them all on the table and look at them for a bit?
  • Brass and tin, back on the table. I shall polish them tonight and the Sleepy Snail will hear me humming, and nobody will complain because I shall buy the first round.
  • Here, take these, I came by them honestly. Next summer, when I stop in again, there will be a cup with your name scratched on the bottom instead of an M.

docs.title: A Crab With No Name
docs.text:
Bree has caught a crab in her rock pools she cannot name: the shell is too hard and the wrong colour. She wants to know where it came from.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Bree Level 21 After The Prettiest Shells Leads to Back and Bigger

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 12 Bootcrab Shell (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,202 EXP
  • 630 mesos
  • +60 standing with Bree
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Look. LOOK. I caught it in the pools under the harbour wall this morning. I have named every crab in the bay, Player, and I can't name this one.
  • The shell's too hard. Hesketh's oyster knife wouldn't go in. And it's the wrong colour, like an old boot. Crabs aren't that colour. Not ours.
  • Somebody said there are crabs like it up the Old Cut, past Baysight Hill. Bring me 12 Bootcrab Shells from the First Locks and I'll find one that matches.
  • Bring them all. Even the ugly ones. Especially the ugly ones.
  • Another time, then.
  • Twelve shells from the First Locks, on the Old Cut. You've got (how many you carry).
  • This one. And this one. They MATCH. Same boot colour, same horrible hardness. So my crab came down the Cut from the locks.
  • I'm calling them bootcrabs. Because of the colour. And because they'd break your boot. Go and tell Keziah, she cleared crabs below the headland her first week. She'll want to know.

docs.title: The Prettiest Shells
docs.text:
Bree has heard the Long Sands' tide line has the prettiest shells on the island. The grey toms there are in the way.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Bree Level 18 Leads to A Crab With No Name

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 12 Tide Line Shell (taken)
  • Defeat 20 Grey Tom

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,400 EXP
  • 396 mesos
  • +40 standing with Bree
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Business is GOOD. So good I'm running out of shells. And everyone knows the prettiest ones are on the Long Sands, west past Marram Cove.
  • But there are grey toms on the beach and they're grumpy. Grumpier than Hesketh. One sat on my last shell and would NOT move.
  • Bring me 12 Tide Line Shells from the tide line, and move 20 Grey Toms out of the way. One copper small, two large. You get a discount.
  • Don't scratch them! Scratched shells are half price.
  • Another time, then.
  • Twelve tide line shells, and twenty grey toms. You've got (how many you carry) shells.
  • Ooh. Ooh! This one's pink inside. That's two coppers. No, three. Special price.
  • Here's your share. And you can have one shell free. Not the pink one.

docs.title: A Late Basket
docs.text:
Brigid is late with Elspeth's herb basket. Clear 40 Wrack Boars from Strandwood Edge, and tell Elspeth the basket will be late.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Brigid Level 24

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Wrack Boar
  • Talk to Elspeth

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x3
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Brigid
Dialogue
  • Oh. Hello. I'm sorry, I didn't hear you. The tide's turning, and I'm late with Elspeth's basket again.
  • I walk further for my baskets now, and it takes longer. And the boars come out of the trees onto the near rocks and root through the weed, and I have to wait for them to go.
  • Could you clear 40 Wrack Boars from Strandwood Edge? And tell Elspeth the basket will be late, so she doesn't worry. Please don't tell her I'm walking far. She'll only be kind about it.
  • Thank you. I'll be on the rocks. You'll see my basket before you see me.
  • That's all right. I'll wait for them to go. They always go, in the end.
  • Forty Wrack Boars, on Strandwood Edge. And a word to Elspeth, if you would. Only that the basket is late.
  • Late again? She works too hard, that girl. Tell her to come home before the light goes, basket or no basket. And tell her there's soup.
  • She said there's soup? She always says there's soup.
  • Here, take these. I made them myself, with Elspeth watching. They're not as good as hers. Not yet.

docs.title: The Greystrand
docs.text:
Brigid wants to show you the Greystrand beyond the Forest Jaw, and then she has something to tell Elspeth.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Brigid Level 50 After The Gapclaw Leads to Agna's Notch, The Board: the Forest Jaw

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 60 Saltdead Stump in The Greystrand
  2. Bring 15 Salt-Killed Bark (taken)
  3. Talk to Elspeth

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 31,000 EXP
  • 2,000 mesos
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Brigid
Dialogue
  • Beyond the Jaw there is a strand where the pines stand dead in the weed. Salt-killed. The wrack line is higher there. Higher than it ought to be.
  • Bring me bark from the dead pines. And then... then come with me while I tell Elspeth something. I have not told her. I should have.
  • Clear 60 Saltdead Stump on The Greystrand, bring 15 Salt-Killed Bark, then go with Brigid to tell Elspeth.
  • The dead stumps walk. Be careful of them.
  • That is all right. I have waited this long.
  • Bark from the drowned pines, and then Elspeth.
  • She was kind. I knew she would be. I do not know why I waited.
  • The beds are dying because the high water covers them now. I can move what is left to higher rocks. That is something.
  • Brigid, child, you are shaking. Sit. What is it?
  • ...Five of the eleven. And you walked to the far rocks alone every day to make up the baskets. Oh, Brigid.
  • No. I am not cross. We will move the good roots to the high beds and we will see. Thank you, Player, for walking with her.

docs.title: The Far Rocks
docs.text:
Brigid gathers sea-herbs on the far rocks at low tide, and the Strandwood's creatures come down to the water there now. She has found something.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Brigid Level 26 After A Better Trigger Leads to The Cub

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 60 monsters in Strandwood Rocks
  • Look at where the swept trail leaves the rocks in Strandwood Rocks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,500 EXP
  • 1,050 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Brigid
Dialogue
  • I walk out to the far rocks at low tide. For the baskets. I go further than I used to.
  • There is a trail there. Swept. Like a broom went over the sand. It goes from the rocks into the trees. I did not follow it.
  • Clear 60 creatures from Strandwood Rocks, so Brigid can gather, and find where the swept trail leaves the rocks (press Up there).
  • Thank you. I will be quick. I am always quick.
  • That is all right. I will go another day.
  • The far rocks are at the end of the Strandwood, past the weed.
  • You found it. It goes right into the trees, under the big fallen pine.
  • Caddoc should know. I am glad it was you who looked, and not me.

docs.title: Brindle a count for the slate
A Count for the Slate
docs.text:
Brindle keeps a weekly slate of sightings by the gate, and Stonefang Pass has gone uncounted since the carters stopped reporting. Hunt 20 seep toads and 20 dark stumps along the pass and bring Brindle a count.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Brindle Level 18

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 20 Seep Toad
  • Defeat 20 Dark Stump

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,240 EXP
  • 1,440 mesos
  • +40 standing with Brindle
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • See the slate? Every week, every sighting the Watch hears of, chalked by the road it came from. Walkers' Road, full. Outworks, full. Stonefang Pass: three marks and a question. That question annoys me.
  • The wool carters used to tell us what they saw on the way down. Now they come in late, tired and in no mood to be counted. So the pass goes blank, and a blank on a slate is not the same as nothing on a road.
  • Walk the pass for me. Hunt 20 Seep Toads in the foothills and 20 Dark Stumps on the Descent, and keep your eyes open for anything I should chalk.
  • Good. Northeast from the meadows. Count what you fight and what you only see. Check twice.
  • The question mark stays, then. It has been there long enough to feel at home.
  • Twenty Seep Toads, twenty Dark Stumps, Stonefang Pass. The slate is waiting, and it is not patient.
  • Toads in the boardwalk bogs, thicker than last year. Stumps standing in the switchbacks, closer to the road than the carters said. Right. Chalk.
  • There. No question mark. The numbers go one way, same as every road, but at least now I know which way. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: A Way In
docs.text:
If a tunnel runs under Old Grad's walls, it is a way into the city that no gate guards. Brindle will not act on it alone: take it to Rook, the Caller of the Open Table.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Brindle Completed with Rook Level 20 After The Wanderer's Story Leads to The Table Argues

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 870 EXP
  • +50 standing with Brindle
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Here is the trouble. The Walkers found an iron door under the Great Hall, behind the kitchens, locked, and they never opened it. A hundred years. If that tunnel comes out anywhere, it comes out behind that door.
  • I could take the Watch down there with crowbars tomorrow. I am not going to. The door is under the Great Hall, and the Great Hall is everyone's. That is the whole point of this city: nobody opens a door for everybody without asking everybody.
  • Take it to Rook at the Great Hall. Tell Rook what Tick wrote and what I think: there is a way into the city no gate guards, and it is behind a door we have never opened. The Table should decide.
  • Good. Rook will listen all the way through and then ask one question you did not think of. Have an answer ready, or say you do not have one. Rook prefers the second.
  • Then I will go myself, after my watch. It will be late, and Rook will be tired, and I will say it badly.
  • Take the wanderer's story to Rook at the Great Hall. A way in under the walls, behind the iron door.
  • Brindle sent you, and Tick's notebook sent Brindle. That is the right order for this city: the youngest pencil in town finds the thing, and the Watch carries it to the Table. I like that more than I can say at the Table.
  • A way in that no gate guards. Under a door we have left shut for a hundred years because the Walkers left it shut. I have one question, and it is not for you: whose door is it, now? The Table will have to answer that.
  • I will call the Table. It will argue all night, I expect. Bastian has already cleared his throat and I have not even told him yet. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: The Watch's Slate: the Outworks
docs.text:
Brindle's slate pays for the Outworks too: defeat 50 lampbats, gloomeyes or ditch rats in the ruined defences under the walls. Every round raises Urbanograd's regard for you, and Brindle will pay it again, any time.

Town Urbanograd Category Repeatable Given by Brindle Level 20

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Outworks monsters (Lampbat, Gloomeye, Ditch Rat)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,830 EXP
  • 2,000 mesos
  • +40 standing with Brindle
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The Outworks are right under our walls, and that is the trouble. Every lampbat out there is one the outer lanterns have to live with. 50 monsters of the Outworks, lampbats, gloomeyes or ditch rats, and the Watch pays. Every fifty, every time.
  • Good. The side path off the Gate Meadows, down into the ditch. Take a lantern. Take two, if you ask Dagny.
  • Another night, then. There is always another night out there.
  • Fifty from the Outworks: lampbats, gloomeyes and ditch rats all count.
  • Fifty. Lux will see the difference before I do: fewer lanterns to mend in the morning.
  • The Watch pays, and the Table hears your name again. Go and get some sleep; one of us should.

docs.title: The Watch's Slate: the Road
docs.text:
The Gate Watch pays a standing bounty from Brindle's slate: defeat 40 of the Walkers' Road's monsters, stack rats, pool octopi, verge adders or young gloomeyes. Every round raises Urbanograd's regard for you, and Brindle will pay it again, any time.

Town Urbanograd Category Repeatable Given by Brindle Level 14

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Road monsters (Stack Rat, Pool Octopus, Verge Adder, Young Gloomeye)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,540 EXP
  • 1,120 mesos
  • +40 standing with Brindle
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The Watch has a purse, not a big one, and it pays for marks off the slate. 40 monsters of the Walkers' Road, between the Halfway Stone and the gate: rats, octopi, adders, the little gloomeyes. Bring me forty and I pay; bring me another forty and I pay again.
  • Good. Out the gate and east. Your tracker keeps the count; I keep the chalk.
  • Fair enough. The road will still be there. So, unfortunately, will they.
  • Forty from the Walkers' Road, Player. Rats, octopi, adders and young gloomeyes all count.
  • Forty. Let me rub a few marks off the slate. There. Doesn't that look better.
  • Here is the Watch's purse, the part of it that is yours. The Table hears who keeps the road. Come back when it fills up again; it will.

docs.title: The Deep Roads
docs.text:
Below the Floodwells, long sally tunnels run out under the hills. Somewhere along them is the tunnel mouth the wanderer came in by. Brindle wants it found: hunt 40 tunnel bats in the Deep Roads and reach the tunnel mouth.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Brindle Level 24 After The Floodwells Leads to The Iron Grate

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Tunnel Bat
  2. Reach the tunnel mouth in Low Grad: the Deep Roads

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,530 EXP
  • 3,360 mesos
  • +60 standing with Brindle
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Leland says you crossed the Floodwells, and that past them the tunnels run out long and narrow under the hills. Sally roads. That is the wanderer's tunnel, or one of its cousins.
  • I need to know where it comes out. Not roughly. Exactly. Because wherever it comes out, the Watch has a second gate to keep, and this one is a hole in a hillside that nobody has looked at in a hundred years.
  • Go down through Low Grad into the Low Grad: the Deep Roads. Clear 40 Tunnel Bats out of the way, and walk the tunnels to the tunnel mouth. Then come back and tell me what it looks like from inside.
  • Good. Leland will let you through. Take a lantern for the tunnels; the bats will go for it, so take a second one for when they do.
  • Understood. The hole has been there a hundred years. One more night will not change it. I will just not sleep, as usual.
  • 40 Tunnel Bats in the Low Grad: the Deep Roads, and the tunnel mouth at the end of them.
  • A square-cut mouth in a hillside, half grown over with bramble, looking down on the road a morning's walk east of the gate. You could walk past it every day and never see it. People have.
  • I am not posting a guard out there; I do not have one to spare. I am going to shut it. Ferro can forge a grate. A proper one, iron, set in the stone, with a gate the Watch holds the key to.
  • Go and see Ferro on Workshops Row. Ferro will grumble and then make something better than I asked for. That is how it goes. Thank you, Player. Two doors now. I will check them both twice.

docs.title: The Gloamwing
docs.text:
Go into the flooded vault under the Fallen Tower and defeat the Gloamwing, the Disturbance-touched bat that leads the lampbats against the outer lanterns. Brindle will open the way.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Brindle Level 28 After Under the Fallen Tower

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Gloamwing

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,750 EXP
  • 840 mesos
  • +80 standing with Brindle
  • +50 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • This is the part I like least about the job. Not the danger: the asking. I am the one who says go, and then I stand here with a lantern and wait.
  • Go into the The Fallen Tower and put an end to the Gloamwing. Ask me for the way in when you are ready, and not before.
  • Right. Talk to me when you want to go in. Lux says it hates noise. Make plenty.
  • Good. I mean that. Better a day late than a lantern short.
  • The Gloamwing, under the The Fallen Tower. Ask me for the way in when you are ready.
  • Lux came down from the towers this morning and said four words to me: every lantern still lit. Then went to sleep on a bench in the square. I have never seen Lux sleep in daylight.
  • There will be lampbats in the Outworks for years, and gloomeyes, and whatever else comes. But the thing that led them is gone, and the outer wall stays lit. You did that.
  • I am telling the Table tonight, and I am going to tell it plainly, which I am told is my only speaking style. Thank you, Player. Go and get some sleep. I mean it this time.

docs.title: The Night Watch
docs.text:
Brindle asks you to stand the night watch at the gate beside Dagny, then go down into the Outworks at dusk and hunt the gloomeyes whose eyes she sees in the dark.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Brindle Level 20 Leads to Morning Prints

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe
  2. Defeat 20 Gloomeye

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,440 EXP
  • 2,000 mesos
  • +50 standing with Brindle
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Two things are wrong out there, and I cannot tell yet whether they are one thing. Dagny sees eyes in the dark beyond the road, more every week. And Lux finds lanterns smashed on the outer wall in the mornings, never two nights running.
  • I would like someone who can fight to stand the watch with Dagny tonight and see what she sees. Then go down into the Outworks at dusk, where the eyes come from, and find out what they belong to.
  • Stand the watch beside Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe at the gate. Then hunt 20 Gloomeyes in the Outworks and come and tell me whether those are the things breaking Lux's lanterns.
  • Good. Dagny is at the gate from sundown. She talks a lot on watch. Let her; it is how she does it.
  • Understood. The watch will be stood either way. It always is.
  • Watch with Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe at the gate first, then 20 Gloomeyes in the Outworks, off the side path from the Gate Meadows.
  • Oh! Brindle sent you? Good. Good. Stand there, on the left, where the light is. No, a little more. There. Now look out past the road. Low down. Wait for it.
  • There. Two. And there, two more, further out, by the old walls. They are in the Outworks, I think, where the ditches are. I call out to them. I say, I can see you. They never answer. Rude.
  • Will you go down there? Into the ditches? At dusk is when they come up. I would go myself, but if I leave the gate, the gate is just a hole in a wall. Come back and tell me what they are.
  • Lizards with big shining eyes, low in the brush, and they watch the lanterns but do not go near them. Hm. And the frames Lux finds are bent from above, glass thrown wide. A lizard does not do that.
  • So: two different things. The eyes are the eyes, and something else breaks the lanterns. That is worse news and better news at the same time. At least now I know what I do not know.
  • Thank you, Player. Go and see Dagny in the morning. She will want to know you came back in one piece. So did I, for the record.

docs.title: Under the Fallen Tower
docs.text:
The lampbats roost under the Fallen Tower, and something leads them. Talk with Lux about what lives in the flooded vault, then come back to Brindle to plan the way in.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Brindle Level 28 After The Rhythm Outside Leads to The Gloamwing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Lux

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,330 EXP
  • 1,680 mesos
  • +60 standing with Brindle
  • +30 standing with Urbanograd
  • Unlocks boss.gloamwing
Dialogue
  • Drum's beat scatters them. I heard. Drum says it proves nothing; the lanterns survived the night, so I say it proves enough. But a swarm does not choose every second night by itself. Something leads it.
  • Lux has watched the roost under the Fallen Tower longer than anyone. Lux will have seen something, even if Lux has not said it yet. Lux is like that: notices everything, says it later.
  • Go and talk to Lux in Lantern Square. Find out what is down in that vault. Then come back here and we will decide how you get in.
  • Good. Lux climbs the towers at dusk; catch Lux before, or wait at the bottom. Do not shout up. Lux hates that.
  • When you are ready. Whatever it is has waited this long.
  • Talk to Lux in Lantern Square about the roost under the Fallen Tower, then come back to me.
  • Brindle sent you. I thought so. Sit; the lanterns can wait a moment. I went down to the vault under the Fallen Tower three nights ago, as far as the water. The lampbats were hanging in the dark like wet washing. Hundreds.
  • And then one of the shadows on the ceiling unfolded. It was as wide as a market awning. It did not come for me. It went out, up through the broken roof, and the whole swarm went after it. Toward the wall. Toward my lanterns.
  • Every second night it goes out. On the other nights it sleeps. That is why the lanterns are never smashed twice running. Tell Brindle. And tell Brindle it hates noise; when I dropped my lamp-hook it screamed. I did not wait to hear it twice.
  • A bat the size of an awning that leads the swarm and hates noise. Every second night. Well. That is a lot more than a question mark.
  • I am calling it the Gloamwing, for the slate; things go better with a name. The way in is the flooded cellar under the Fallen Tower, where the roof fell open. You will not be fighting it alone: half the swarm will be in there with it.
  • When you are ready, tell me, and I will show you the way into the Fallen Tower. Take potions. Take more than that. Check twice.

docs.title: Tea and a Little News
docs.text:
Briony wants a pot of tea and a carefully chosen piece of news carried to her sister.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Briony Level 11 Leads to A Quarrel Before It Reaches the Council

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Thessaly
  • Bring 5 Bubbling's Huge Bubble (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 332 EXP
  • 242 mesos
  • +120 standing with Briony
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Thessaly's had a dreadful week in the Council. She needs tea and good news, in that order.
  • The good news is that I've found a bubble big enough for her to see her own reflection in. She'll pretend she isn't amused. Bring me five and carry the tea.
  • Bring 5 Bubbling's Huge Bubbles from the bubblings on the roads, and carry Briony's tea to Thessaly.
  • Tell her it's from me. She'll know anyway.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Bubbles, then my sister.
  • She laughed? She laughed! Not out loud, but her eyes did.
  • Here, a cup for you. Sit. Tell me exactly how her eyes did it.
  • Tea. From Briony. And... a bubble with my face in it.
  • Thessaly looks at it for a long moment. Her mouth stays precisely straight. Her eyes do not.

docs.title: A Quarrel Before It Reaches the Council
