docs.text:
Two families of the Lantern Paths are quarrelling over a shared branch-bridge. Briony wants it settled over tea, not in the chamber.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Briony Level 38 After Tea and a Little News, The Swarming Shore

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Linnet
  • Talk to Ondine
  • Defeat 60 Creature of the High Shore or the Oaks (Evil Eye, Curse Eye, Cold Eye, Sharpened Lupin, Gloomfur Lupin, Surgeon Eye)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,651 EXP
  • 836 mesos
  • +150 standing with Briony
  • +20 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +40 standing with Linnet
  • +40 standing with Ondine
Dialogue
  • The lantern-makers want a lantern on the shared bridge. The treewrights say it'll scorch the branch. They've both written to the Council. I intercepted the letters.
  • Talk to Linnet and Ondine. And bring back ironbark-hard proof that the oak's deadfall makes a good bracket: clear the oak so they can see for themselves.
  • Talk to Linnet and Ondine, and clear 60 creatures from the High Shore or the Hollow Oak.
  • Over tea. Always over tea.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Linnet, Ondine, and the oak.
  • An ironbark bracket. The lantern hangs off the branch, not on it. Both families are delighted.
  • And not a word of it reached the chamber. My sister will never know. She'll know.
  • The bridge? A lantern on that branch will scorch it. Unless it hangs off a bracket. Ironbark would do.
  • I'd agree to that. Tell Ondine.
  • An ironbark bracket? Hm. The light would fall better, too.
  • Fine. Tell Briony fine. And tell her I know she intercepted my letter.

docs.title: Entry Sixty-Five
docs.text:
Brisa wants entry sixty-five in her list to be something she saw herself. The Crossways' whipshades will do.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Brisa Level 57 After Faster Than Finch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 70 Whipshade in The Crossways

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 42,087 EXP
  • 1,254 mesos
  • +40 standing with Brisa
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Sixty-four entries, every one somebody else's. Sixty-five's going to be mine. I want to see the shades myself.
  • I can't leave the waterfront. You go. The Crossways in the Holm Wood. Clear 70 of those whipshades and tell me exactly what they're like. I'll write it like I saw it.
  • Exactly what they're like. Every detail.
  • Another time, then.
  • Seventy whipshades at the Crossways, for Brisa's list.
  • Tall, hooded, made of shadow and salt mist, a pale light where a face should be, a lash like a squid's arm. Got it. Entry sixty-five.
  • Nearly as good as seeing it myself. Nearly.

docs.title: Faster Than Finch
docs.text:
Brisa hears Finch has been asking about the Sea Locks. She wants to know what is there before he goes looking.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Brisa Level 37 After A Letter to Marram Cove Leads to Entry Sixty-Five

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the Sea Locks' far upper ledge in The Sea Locks
  2. Defeat 25 Spitting Sawbill

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,692 EXP
  • 814 mesos
  • +40 standing with Brisa
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Finch has been asking sailors what's at the Sea Locks. That means he's going. That means I'll be chasing him down the Cut in the dark.
  • Go there first. See what's on the Sea Locks' far upper ledge, and thin out 25 Spitting Sawbills. If it's safe, I'll take him myself. If it's not, I'll sit on him.
  • Run, don't walk.
  • Another time, then.
  • Look at the Sea Locks' far upper ledge and clear twenty-five spitting sawbills.
  • Spitting sawbills on every ledge. Right. I'm sitting on him.
  • I'll write it down. Entry sixty-four. Thanks. You're nearly as fast as me.

docs.title: A Letter to Marram Cove
docs.text:
Brisa's midwinter letter to her parents travels inland by way of Marram Cove. She asks you to carry it there, and the road is full of dune cats.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Brisa Level 16 Leads to Faster Than Finch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach Marram Cove
  2. Defeat 20 Dune Cat

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 992 EXP
  • 352 mesos
  • +40 standing with Brisa
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You going west along the coast? Take this. It's a letter. Don't read it.
  • My mum and dad moved to a cousin's farm near Kaldemor. The post goes from Marram Cove, the fishing hamlet past the Dune Reach. I'd run it myself but I'm on watch. Sort of.
  • Take it to Marram Cove, and knock some sense into the 20 Dune Cats on the way, would you? They chase the post rider.
  • Run, don't walk. I always do.
  • Another time, then.
  • Marram Cove, past the Dune Reach. And twenty dune cats, for the post rider.
  • You took your time. No, that was quick. I'm just used to being faster.
  • Thanks. Here. Write that down somewhere: you did a Watch errand and nobody got shouted at.

docs.title: A Better Trigger
docs.text:
Caddoc means to build a trigger the old fox cannot learn, from the Strandwood's own creatures.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Caddoc Level 24 After The Night Trap Leads to The Far Rocks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 15 Fox Sinew (taken)
  • Bring 15 Weedy Bristle (taken)
  • Bring 10 Sound Driftwood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,550 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Caddoc
Dialogue
  • Right. It reads my traps. So I will make one it has not read.
  • Fox sinew for the line, it knows the smell of its own. Boar bristle for the spring. Sound driftwood for the frame, nothing rotten.
  • Bring 15 Fox Sinew, 15 Weedy Bristle and 10 Sound Driftwood from the Strandwood.
  • Do not bring me rotten wood. I will know.
  • Then I will sit here and think about that fox. I do that anyway.
  • Sinew, bristle, driftwood. Sound driftwood.
  • That will do. That will very nearly do.
  • It cannot learn a trap it has never smelled. That is what I keep telling myself.

docs.title: The Cub
docs.text:
The new trap caught something: a cub. The old fox is still out there, and Torva and Kenna mean to go after it.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Caddoc Level 28 After The Far Rocks Leads to Old Brushtail

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Torva
  • Talk to Kenna

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,750 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Caddoc
  • Unlocks boss.old_brushtail
Dialogue
  • It worked. It worked and it caught a cub. A little grey thing, all teeth and sulk. I let it go.
  • The old one is still out there. Torva says she knows where its earth is, under the fallen pine where Brigid's trail went. Talk to her. And Kenna, Gap Inn help us.
  • Talk to Torva and Kenna on the Forest Shore.
  • Go on. I am going to sit here and be pleased with my trap.
  • It will wait. It has waited all season.
  • Torva and Kenna, on the Forest Shore.
  • So you are going under the pine. Good. Bring me back a tail and I will never set a cage trap again. I will, but I will think about not doing it.
  • The swept trail ends at the root-hollow under the fallen pine. That is its earth. Brushtail, Caddoc calls it now.
  • I will take you there when you are ready. Kenna is coming whether I like it or not.
  • Torva says it is the size of a calf! Something that size and nobody has ever brought one down.
  • If we do, they will talk about it at the Gap Inn for a year. I am ready now. Are you?

docs.title: The Night Trap
docs.text:
Something has been springing Caddoc's biggest cage trap every night without being caught. He wants someone to sit up beside it with him.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Caddoc Level 22 After Bethoc's Board Leads to A Better Trigger

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Caddoc's Night Trap

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,750 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x3
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Caddoc
Dialogue
  • Three times I have rebuilt that trigger. Three times. Bait gone, door dropped, nothing inside. No hair. No blood. The ground swept smooth.
  • Tonight I am sitting up beside it. You are sitting up with me. Things come out of the trees at night and I would like to see the dawn.
  • Sit up through the night beside Caddoc's cage trap on the Strandwood Rocks. Talk to him when you are ready to go out.
  • Bring something warm. And do not fall asleep. I mean it.
  • Fine. I will sit up alone and freeze.
  • When you are ready, say so, and we will go out to the trap.
  • You saw it. Tell me you saw it.
  • A fox. A fox as big as a calf, grey all round the muzzle. It lifted the door with its teeth. It took the bait. And then it swept its own tracks away with its tail. With its tail.
  • I always thought cleverness was the one thing they did not have. Twenty-six years I have thought that.
  • ...Give me a moment.

docs.title: Pelts from the Woods
docs.text:
Caddoc needs proper skins for his traps' hinges, and the Seaward Woods and Dusk Ford have them.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Caddoc Level 17

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 15 Ligator Skin (taken)
  • Bring 10 Lupin's Banana (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,100 EXP
  • 680 mesos
  • +10 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +100 standing with Caddoc
Dialogue
  • My hinges keep cracking. Fox gnaws them, or the damp gets in. Ligator skin does not crack. Do not ask me how I know.
  • And I need bananas. For bait. Do not ask about that either.
  • Bring me 15 Ligator Skin from Dusk Ford and 10 Lupin's Banana from Seaward Woods.
  • And do not let the Ligators near your boots.
  • Fine. My hinges will crack, and I will complain about it.
  • Still waiting on those skins. The hinges are still cracking.
  • Hm. Not bad skins. Not good either. They will do.

docs.title: Three Kinds, Sharpened
docs.text:
Caelum needs fresh evidence to set beside Hesper's list: samples from three kinds of sharpened creature on the Hollow Oak.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Caelum Level 42 After The Back of the Seed Book Leads to Before Dark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 8 Lupin Claw Sample (taken)
  • Bring 8 Gloomfur Sample (taken)
  • Bring 8 Surgeon Eye Sample (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 24,747 EXP
  • 1,260 mesos
  • +60 standing with Caelum
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • With Hesper's list I can see where. What I can't see is how. I need the creatures themselves. Pieces of them. Fresh.
  • Three kinds: the sharpened Lupins of the boughs, the grey ones higher up, and the Surgeon Eyes near the crown. Eight samples each. Labelled. Please label them.
  • Bring 8 Lupin Claw Samples, 8 Gloomfur Samples and 8 Surgeon Eye Samples from the Hollow Oak.
  • Labelled! Did I say labelled?
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Samples: (how many you carry), (how many you carry) and (how many you carry) of 8 each.
  • Beautiful. Horrible. Beautiful.
  • Give me a day with these and the list. Maybe two. Maybe a week.

docs.title: The Deep-Water Boat
docs.text:
Calder wants Tamsin's opinion of his latest drawing of the boat he means to build. Take it to her at the quay yard, then bring him what she says it needs.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Calder Level 36

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Tamsin
  2. Bring 20 Sea Newt Hide (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,800 EXP
  • 1,400 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x3
  • +25 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Calder
Dialogue
  • Player. I've drawn her again. The boat. Better this time, I think, but I always think that.
  • Would you take this Calder's Drawing to Tamsin at the quay yard? She'll tell you what's wrong with it. She always does, and she's always right. I'd go myself, but she'd tell me to my face, and I'd rather hear it from you.
  • She'll be at the yard on the Inlet Quay, swearing at the Gap Runner. Wait till she stops.
  • No hurry. She's seen a hundred of my drawings. She'll be there for the next.
  • Did Tamsin have a look? If she wants something, bring it here. She usually wants something. You have (how many you carry) Sea Newt Hide.
  • Hatch covers. Of course. I drew the hatches open because I like to look down into her. Daft.
  • "The best one yet." She'll have told you not to tell me that. Thank you, Player. Here. It isn't much, but the hide is worth more to me than you'd think.
  • Calder's boat. Again. Give it here.
  • Keel's right. Mast's too far forward, he always does that. And look at this, open hatches. In deep water she'll ship a sea over the bow and every locker fills.
  • Tell him hatch covers, tight ones, under oiled hide. The Sea Newts on the Saltface have a hide that stays wet and never rots. 20 Sea Newt Hide would cover her. And tell him it's the best one yet. Don't tell him I said so.

docs.title: Timber for the Boat
docs.text:
Calder will sing Morven's ending of the gap verse once he has keel timber from the Greystrand's drowned pines.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Calder Level 58 After The Hour the Water Forgets Leads to The Verse and the Page

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Sound Pine Timber (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 48,500 EXP
  • 2,300 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Calder
Dialogue
  • Ten lengths of the salt-hardened pine, cut from the stumps that walk the Greystrand. Then sit down, and I will sing it.
  • Bring Calder 10 lengths of Sound Pine Timber, cut from the Saltdead Stump of The Greystrand.
  • Straight ones. A keel does not forgive.
  • Then the verse keeps.
  • Ten lengths of sound pine. Straight.
  • These are good. Better than good. Sit down, then. I will sing it once, quietly.
  • ...the run that leaned against the wood, the slack that came too late, they sounded out the Jaw's dark foot and found a sleeper there. They drove it out to the deep. And the water remembered its hour.
  • That is all of it. Tell Cormac. Tell him it was hers. And do not tell him I cried.

docs.title: A Spring Basket
docs.text:
An old friend among the Brenna of Midbarium visits Calyra each spring. Calyra wants a basket ready, and the roads made safer for the visit.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Calyra Level 40 After The Swarming Shore

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 80 Creature of the High Shore or the Oaks (Evil Eye, Curse Eye, Cold Eye, Sharpened Lupin, Gloomfur Lupin, Surgeon Eye)
  • Talk to Halcy

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,725 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • +150 standing with Calyra
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Halcy
Dialogue
  • Every spring an old friend comes down the Northern Woodland Trail from Midbarium. One of the Brenna. We drink tea and say very little. It's the best week of my year.
  • The northern paths are worse this year. And I'd like a basket of glade flowers waiting. Halcy will know which.
  • Make the paths safer (80 creatures on the High Shore or the Hollow Oak) and ask Halcy for a spring basket.
  • Thank you. Short words, remember.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The paths, then Halcy.
  • Halcy chose bluebells and grey fern. The Brenna colours. Of course Halcy knew.
  • It will be a good spring.
  • A spring basket for Calyra's friend? Bluebells and grey fern. Those are the Brenna's colours.
  • Halcy weaves it while you watch, quick and sure. 'Tell her it's from the glade.'

docs.title: Rest for the Scholars
docs.text:
The Eldest wants her seal scholars to rest, and knows they will not listen to her.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Calyra Level 26 After The Night Diggers

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Caelum
  • Talk to Isaura
  • Bring 6 Lavender Flower (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,127 EXP
  • 572 mesos
  • Dew Tea x5
  • +120 standing with Calyra
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • My scholars sleep too little and find too little. I've told them to rest. They nod and keep reading.
  • Perhaps they will listen to someone who is not the Eldest. And Hesper swears by a lavender pillow.
  • Persuade Caelum and Isaura to rest, and bring 6 Lavender Flower for their pillows.
  • Short words. They respond to short words.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Caelum, Isaura, and lavender.
  • Caelum slept four hours. Isaura closed a book before midnight. Both are records.
  • Thank you. Lavender. I'll remember that.
  • Sleep? Now? But theory... Lavender? ...Fine. Four hours. Not five. Four.
  • He is asleep in three minutes.
  • The Eldest sent you. Of course she did.
  • Isaura closes the book. 'One night,' she says. 'Tell her one night.'

docs.title: Captain annis salt over the stern
Salt Over the Stern
docs.text:
Annis throws a pinch of salt over the stern every time she casts off. The salt barrel is low, and the best salt crusts on the Sea Locks' old stones, where the spitting sawbills nest.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Annis Level 36

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Spitting Sawbill in The Sea Locks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,782 EXP
  • 792 mesos
  • +40 standing with Annis
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The salt barrel's low, and I won't cast off without a pinch over the stern. The best salt crusts on the old stones of the Sea Locks, where the tide dries.
  • The spitting sawbills nest on those stones now. Clear 40 of them from the Sea Locks so my deck boy can scrape the salt.
  • Left boot first, when you go. Never on deck.
  • Another time, then.
  • Forty spitting sawbills on the Sea Locks, so Annis's deck boy can scrape the salt.
  • A full barrel. Good salt. The Saltlark will cast off right.
  • Corwin can laugh. Forty-four years and not a hand lost. You tell me which of us is wasting salt.

docs.title: Captain annis where the keel was brushed
Where the Keel Was Brushed
docs.text:
Annis gave Ambrose the mark the morning after something brushed the Saltlark's keel, bow to stern, on a still night in deep water. From the Cliff Edge you can see that water.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Annis Level 59 After The Locked Chart Leads to What Seraphine Saw, At the Wheel

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 60 Hookshade in The Cliff Edge
  2. Bring 1 Broken Keel Timber

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 67,821 EXP
  • 1,770 mesos
  • +60 standing with Annis
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • That mark on Ambrose's chart, the one just off the shelf. That's mine. The Saltlark's. Morwenna had the wheel. Something brushed the keel from bow to stern, slow, on a still night. Every soul aboard felt it.
  • I turned for home and gave Ambrose the mark next morning. Morwenna's not told her mother or her boy. I've not pressed her.
  • From the Cliff Edge in the Holm Wood you look straight down on that water. Things wash into the cliff foot there. Clear 60 of those shades from the Cliff Edge and look for a Broken Keel Timber. If anything came off a hull, it ends up there.
  • Left boot first. Never on deck.
  • Another time, then.
  • Clear sixty hookshades from the Cliff Edge, and find a broken length of keel timber.
  • A length of keel. Scored. And look: round marks, each ringed with fine scratches, the same as Halloran's pilings.
  • Something took hold of a ship and let go. Morwenna will want to see this. And Seraphine. Barnaby's been telling the Salt and Bread about eyes for a year; take it to him first, he's earned it.

docs.title: Captain corwin a harpoon at the bow
A Harpoon at the Bow
docs.text:
Corwin pays Tristram to stand the Heron's bow, and grumbles at every council about the cost. He wants Tristram's opinion of the Cut before the Heron tries it.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Corwin Level 45 After Waste Not

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Tristram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,872 EXP
  • 990 mesos
  • +40 standing with Corwin
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • If the Heron comes in by the Old Cut one day, I want my harpooner's opinion before my navigator's. Caspian has bearings. Tristram has eyes.
  • Ask Tristram what he thinks of the Cut, now the Ripsaw's shoals are thinning. He'll say three words. They'll be the right ones.
  • Three words. Write them down.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Tristram on the docks what he thinks of the Old Cut.
  • 'Not yet. Soon.' Three words. Two, really.
  • He's right. He usually is. Here's for your trouble, and none of it wasted.
  • The Cut?
  • Not yet. Soon.

docs.title: Waste Not
docs.text:
Corwin hates waste. Sawbill scales fetch a fair price for buttons and inlay, and the Salt Reach is thick with them.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Corwin Level 32 Leads to A Harpoon at the Bow

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Sawbill Scale (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,613 EXP
  • 704 mesos
  • +40 standing with Corwin
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The sawbills have cost this harbour nets, sails and a great deal of my money in harpooners. I mean to have something back from them.
  • Their scales take a polish. Cordelia will buy them for buttons. Bring me 25 Sawbill Scales. Waste is a habit. So is thrift.
  • Count them twice.
  • Another time, then.
  • Twenty-five sawbill scales for Corwin. You have (how many you carry).
  • Twenty-five. Cordelia will pay a silver a dozen.
  • Your share. The first money a sawbill ever paid me. I'll mention it at council.

docs.title: A Blank Chart
docs.text:
Seraphine keeps a blank chart sheet in her cabin for waters past Ambrose's charts. Now she wants Ambrose to have what she saw.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Seraphine Level 63 After What Seraphine Saw

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ambrose

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 56,662 EXP
  • 1,386 mesos
  • +40 standing with Seraphine
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • I keep a blank chart in my cabin for water past Ambrose's lines. It's still blank. I never wrote down what I saw.
  • Take it to Ambrose. Tell him: last spring, the night run, two leagues past the headland, a shoal of lights. Let him put it where it goes.
  • Two leagues past the headland. He'll know.
  • Another time, then.
  • Take Seraphine's blank chart and her mark to Ambrose.
  • He drew it in? On my sheet? And gave it back?
  • Then the sheet's not blank any more. I'll hang it in the cabin. Next to my dares. I've stopped taking those.
  • Seraphine's mark? Two leagues past the headland, last spring. Yes. It fits. It fits the creep exactly.
  • I'll draw it on her own sheet and give it back. A captain should have her own chart.

docs.title: The Night Run
docs.text:
The Bright Morrow sails a night run past the headland, and Keziah cannot face it. Sail it in her place, and keep the leaping sawbills off the deck.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Seraphine Level 41 After The Sea End Leads to Proof for Dunstan

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Keziah
  2. Clear The Bright Morrow's Night Run

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 23,042 EXP
  • 1,230 mesos
  • Scored Plank x1
  • +60 standing with Seraphine
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The Morrow has a night run, past the headland and back before dawn. Fast cargo, good money, and lately the sawbills come over the rail in the dark.
  • Keziah's sailed every run with me since spring. But she came to me this morning and asked to sit this one out. First time. She wouldn't say why. I didn't ask.
  • Talk to Keziah, then come back and tell me you'll sail in her place. Then sail the night run: talk to me again when you're ready to climb aboard.
  • Mind the third plank. It squeaks.
  • Another time, then.
  • Talk to Keziah, then sail the Bright Morrow's night run (talk to Seraphine to board).
  • Not a sawbill on the mainsail, and Barnaby says you fought like a bosun. He'll be telling it at the Salt and Bread for a week, bigger every time.
  • And here. A plank off the deck, scored by their teeth. Alwyn will want to see it. Thank you for sailing in Keziah's place. Whatever her reason is, it's hers.
  • Seraphine sent you? Good. I mean... yes. I can't do the night run. I have a... prior engagement.
  • Don't ask. Please. And don't tell her I said please. Just sail it. You'll be fine. I've never once been fine and I always came back.

docs.title: Bearings on the Cut
docs.text:
Caspian wants exact bearings for the Old Cut's sea half, in case the Heron ever comes in that way.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Caspian Level 34 Leads to The Race Navigator

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the Salt Reach's high bank in The Salt Reach
  • Look at the Sea Locks' upper gate in The Sea Locks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,106 EXP
  • 748 mesos
  • +40 standing with Caspian
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Uncle Corwin says if the Cut stays open the Heron might come in that way one day. Naturally I want the bearings ready before anyone asks.
  • Take a sighting from the Salt Reach's high bank and from the Sea Locks' upper gate. Note where the headland lies. I'd go myself, but... the light's better for you.
  • The light's better for you. That's all.
  • Another time, then.
  • Take sightings from the Salt Reach's high bank and the Sea Locks' upper gate.
  • Two sightings. Lovely. With those and the stars I can put the Cut on a chart to a ship's length.
  • I'll give them to Ambrose. He'll think I did it myself. You don't mind. Do you?

docs.title: The Race Navigator
docs.text:
Caspian wants to navigate the race boat this summer. He has not dared ask the Harbour Master, and he asks you to sound her out.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Caspian Level 42 After Bearings on the Cut

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Quenna

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 17,013 EXP
  • 924 mesos
  • +40 standing with Caspian
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The race crew. Quenna picks it herself. I'm the obvious navigator. Everyone agrees. I've told everyone.
  • I just haven't told Quenna. Would you... find out what she thinks? Without saying I asked. Casually.
  • Casually. Very casually.
  • Another time, then.
  • Find out from the Harbour Master what she thinks of Caspian as the race navigator.
  • She said what? 'If he can steer by the stars in a squall'? In a squall.
  • ...I can. Probably. Thank you. I think.
  • Caspian sent you. Don't deny it, I can see him from the window pretending to coil a rope.
  • He's the best young navigator in the harbour. Tell him I'll think about it if he can steer by the stars in a squall. Then watch his face.

docs.title: Cecily a ballad on the ridge
A Ballad on the Ridge
docs.text:
Fulke taught Cecily a downs shepherds' ballad and says it should be sung where it was made. She is too shy to go. She asks the player to clear the way and listen to the wind.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Cecily Level 21 Leads to A Verse for Fulke

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 25 Wild Bee in Downs Edge
  2. Reach the windy ridge in Downs Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,220 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Cecily
Dialogue
  • Fulke taught me a shepherds' song from the downs. He says a song should be sung where it was made, once at least.
  • I can't go out there. The bees, and... sorry. I mean, could you go and see? Just see what it sounds like up there.
  • Clear 25 Wild Bees on Downs Edge, then stand on the windy ridge and listen. Tell me what the wind sounds like.
  • Thank you. Sorry. Thank you.
  • Oh, of course. Sorry for asking.
  • Downs Edge, the bees, then the windy ridge. Listen, please.
  • Loud and wide and nothing to stop it? Like the shingle at home, when the wind is up.
  • Then I'll sing it loud. Nobody will hear me properly. That's how I like to start. Thank you.

docs.title: A Verse for Fulke
docs.text:
Cecily has written a new verse to the shepherds' ballad, about the wind on the ridge. She wants her teacher Fulke to hear it first, but she cannot bring herself to sing it at him unasked.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Cecily Level 24 After A Ballad on the Ridge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Fulke

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,370 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Cecily
Dialogue
  • I wrote a verse. To the ballad. About the wind on the ridge, the way you told it.
  • I want Fulke to hear it first. But I can't just... sing at him. Not unasked.
  • Take the verse to Fulke in the plaza. Ask him if it's true enough to sing. Sorry. Thank you.
  • If he laughs, don't tell me. If he doesn't, tell me twice.
  • Oh. Of course. It probably isn't good anyway.
  • Fulke, in the plaza. The verse. Please.
  • He said it was true? And good? Both? He never says both.
  • I'll sing it tonight between the acts. Loud. Thank you, Player. Sorry. No. Just thank you.
  • A verse from Cecily? Let me see. Hm. Hm.
  • Tell her it is true, and it is good, and that is the rarest pair in a ballad. Tell her to sing it loud and not to look at her shoes.

docs.title: Stings in the Casebook
docs.text:
Clemence has written down two stings that match no jellyfish she knows. The glass jellies in the Old Cut's basins might be the answer.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Clemence Level 24 After Back and Bigger Leads to Kit on the Lock Gate, The Long Scrape

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Glass Jelly Stinger (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,742 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • Sting Salve x5
  • +60 standing with Clemence
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Keziah tells me there are jellies in the Old Cut's basins now. Glassy ones. Floating over the water like soap bubbles.
  • I keep a book of wounds I can't explain. Two of them are stings, and they match no jellyfish I've ever treated. I'd like to know if they match these.
  • Bring me 20 Glass Jelly Stingers from the Timber Ponds. Carefully. I'll make a salve from them, and you'll have the first jars.
  • Gloves, dear. Thick ones.
  • Another time, then.
  • Twenty glass jelly stingers. You've got (how many you carry).
  • Let me see. The barb, the little ring of hooks... Yes. That's the sting in my book. Both of them.
  • So now I know what stung them, and soon I'll have a salve for it. Take these. And don't tell anyone about the book, would you? Not yet.

docs.title: The Long Scrape
docs.text:
One page of Clemence's casebook is a dockworker's long, straight, shallow scrape on the calf. She wants to compare it with a sawbill's bill.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Clemence Level 36 After Stings in the Casebook Leads to Welts in the Casebook

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 8 Sawbill Bill (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,782 EXP
  • 792 mesos
  • +40 standing with Clemence
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • My casebook has a dockworker with a long straight scrape down his calf. Shallow. Clean. He said something brushed him from the water at the end of the pier.
  • Maren tells me the sawbills have teeth set in a line. I'd like to measure that line against my drawing. Bring me 8 Sawbill Bills, dear. I'll want a few for comparison.
  • Gloves again. Always gloves.
  • Another time, then.
  • Eight sawbill bills for Clemence. You have (how many you carry).
  • The spacing of the teeth, the length of the bill... yes. That's the scrape. Exactly.
  • Another page explained. I wish they all were. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Welts in the Casebook
docs.text:
Clemence wants to compare the round welts in her casebook with the hooks of salt mist the shades leave behind.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Clemence Level 60 After The Long Scrape

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Shade Hook (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 49,014 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • +40 standing with Clemence
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The round welts in my book. Halloran's pilings. And now Brisa says the hookshades leave hooks of salt mist behind when they fade.
  • I'd like to know if they're the same shape. Bring me 15 Shade Hooks, dear. Gloves, as always.
  • Thick gloves. They're cold.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fifteen shade hooks for Clemence. You have (how many you carry).
  • The same ring of tiny hooks. The shades are its shadow, then. Made in its shape.
  • Another page explained. Two left. I may yet close this book.

docs.title: Ask the Old Man
docs.text:
Clement wants to know what the plaza sounded like the day the crowd cheered the Great Bell, and he has never quite dared ask Gideon straight out. Ask for him.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Clement Level 13 After Post the Notice

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Gideon

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 380 EXP
  • 260 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Clement
Dialogue
  • Player, may I ask you something foolish? One day I should like to cry a proclamation the whole plaza cheers. Gideon says they cheered like thunder the day the Great Bell rang.
  • I have climbed his ladder every week for sixteen years, and I have never once asked him what it was like. It seems... too large a question to bring with a pie.
  • Would you climb up and ask Gideon for me? What did the plaza sound like, that day? I should like to know what I am aiming for.
  • Thank you. Do not tell him it was my question. ... He will know. Tell him anyway.
  • No, no, quite right. I shall ask him myself. One of these Thursdays.
  • Gideon's perch, above the plaza. Mind the ladder.
  • Every voice stopped at once, and then every voice started at once? ... That is it. That is what I am aiming for.
  • Thank you, Player. I shall write it on the back of every proclamation, where only I can see it.
  • Clement wants to know? Ha! The boy could have asked. ... Every voice in the square stopped at once, Player. Then the Bell. Then every voice started again at once, and it went straight into my chest.
  • Tell him that. And tell him he will hear it himself one day, on those steps, and he will not faint. Probably.

docs.title: Post the Notice
docs.text:
Clement must cry the Knights' Court's notice to travellers: keep to daylight hours on the World Tree Road. He would like it posted at the wayside well on the Hedge Lanes as well, and the Orange Mushrooms there are no help.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Clement Level 8 After Word for Clement Leads to Ask the Old Man

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the wayside well in The Hedge Lanes
  • Defeat 25 Orange Mushroom

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 200 EXP
  • 160 mesos
  • Red Potion x8
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Clement
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player. A notice from the Knights' Court: travellers on the World Tree Road keep to daylight hours. I cry it from the steps, but the people who need it most are already out on the road.
  • There is a wayside well on the The Hedge Lanes, where every carter stops. If the notice were nailed there... But the Orange Mushrooms crowd round it, and I am a herald, not a... well. Not a you.
  • Take this Knights' Court Notice and post it at the wayside well on the The Hedge Lanes: press Up beside it. And thin out 25 Orange Mushrooms while you are there.
  • Thank you. Oh, and if anyone reads it aloud, do tell me how it sounded.
  • Of course. I shall just... cry it louder. Somehow.
  • The wayside well on the The Hedge Lanes, and the mushrooms around it.
  • Posted! And the carters stopping to read it? Wonderful. Wonderful. I rehearsed that notice to the pigeons for two days.
  • Here, for your trouble. A notice is only words until someone carries it where it is needed.

docs.title: The Drying Racks
docs.text:
The coast families dry their catch on racks along the Dune Reach, and the dune cats raid them. Cobb asks for help.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Cobb Level 16

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 35 Dune Cat in The Dune Reach

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 992 EXP
  • 352 mesos
  • +40 standing with Cobb
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • My cousins dry fish on racks out on the Dune Reach. Along the south shore.
  • Dune cats get at them. Every night. Whole racks, gone. My cousins don't say much either. That's the family.
  • Clear 35 Dune Cats off the Dune Reach. I'd go myself. Gwennol says I'm needed here.
  • Thank you.
  • Another time, then.
  • Thirty-five dune cats. The Dune Reach, west along the shore.
  • My cousin sent word. The racks are full this week.
  • ...Thank you. Gwennol says to say it properly. Thank you very much.

docs.title: The Ripsaw
docs.text:
The sawbills follow one great fish, and Tristram has seen it lying up under the broken sea gates. Cobb asks you to put it down.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Cobb Level 47 After Proof for Dunstan

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Tristram
  2. Clear The Ripsaw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,536 EXP
  • 1,410 mesos
  • Elixir x4
  • +60 standing with Cobb
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The shoals follow one fish. A big one. Tristram's seen it, from the headland, lying up under the broken sea gates where the tide runs hardest.
  • He calls it the Ripsaw. Longer than my boat. Its saw scarred end to end. While it lives the shoals keep coming in through the Cut.
  • Talk to Tristram on the docks. Then go down to the Gullet and put the Ripsaw down. The last lock post under the gates lets you climb down.
  • Breathe before you go down. Nerissa's rule.
  • Another time, then.
  • Talk to Tristram on the docks, then defeat the Ripsaw in the Gullet Gates.
  • The Ripsaw. Gone.
  • The shoals will scatter without it. My nets will come up whole. I'll take Lowen's little sister out past the middle of the bay next week. First time in a year.
  • The Ripsaw. Under the sea gates, in the Gullet. I've watched it from the headland three mornings. It doesn't move much. It doesn't need to.
  • Watch its charge. It goes the whole length of the channel. And when the tide turns, so does it.

docs.title: What Tears the Nets
docs.text:
Cobb has not been past the middle of the bay since his nets came up torn. He meets you on the Sea Locks and sets a net across the Cut to see what comes.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Cobb Level 37 After The Shelf of Beach Finds Leads to The Sea End

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at Cobb's net across the Cut in The Sea Locks
  2. Defeat 60 monsters in The Sea Locks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 17,006 EXP
  • 1,110 mesos
  • +60 standing with Cobb
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • My mother says it was sawbills. Maren has a card on her shelf now.
  • I want to see it. Myself. I'll set a net across the Cut at the Sea Locks. Whatever tore mine will come to it.
  • Meet me at the net on the Sea Locks. Then keep them off it. Sixty, maybe. I'll hold the line.
  • I'll be there before you.
  • Another time, then.
  • Check Cobb's net across the Cut on the Sea Locks, then clear sixty of what comes to it.
  • Saw them. Saw the teeth go into the mesh. Saw them pull.
  • ...I can sleep now. Knowing is better. Thank you. Gwennol says to say it properly. Thank you very much.

docs.title: Good Hides
docs.text:
Good hides reach the city less and less, and Cobble hoards the best for the rooftop runners. The downs howlers on the Beacon Downs grow thick, tough pelts: bring Cobble 20 Howler Pelts.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Cobble Level 58 After The Awl by the Door

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Downs Howler Pelt (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 77,800 EXP
  • 5,800 mesos
  • +70 standing with Cobble
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Hide merchant came in last week. Twice the price, half the thickness. I sent him off. Then I sat and counted what I've got in the back. Enough for six pairs. Six. Runners go through a pair a year.
  • Henrike used wolf for winter uppers. Thick, takes a stitch, sheds rain. Howlers up on the downs these days, big shaggy horned brutes. Good hide on those. Bad tempers.
  • 20 Downs Howler Pelts, from the Downs Howlers on the Beacon Downs. Whole. No arrow holes in the good part. You know which the good part is? The back. Always the back.
  • The back, mind. I'll know.
  • Hm. Then six pairs it is, and Kite runs barefoot after. Kite would, too.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Downs Howler Pelts. Downs howlers. The back's the good part.
  • (Cobble spreads a pelt across the bench, presses a thumb into it, folds it, sniffs it.) Hm. Hm. That'll do. That'll more than do.
  • Twenty runners' winters in that pile. I'll make you a pair one day, Player. Not today. When I've decided what sort of feet you've got.

docs.title: Cobble the awl by the door
The Awl by the Door
docs.text:
Cobble left a scrap of hide and an awl by the shop door to see what Edgar would do with them. Both are gone. Cobble will not ask Edgar; you can.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Cobble Level 25 Leads to Good Hides

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Edgar Penhallow

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,340 EXP
  • 1,500 mesos
  • +60 standing with Cobble
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • That Selsior boy. Edgar. Sweeps my step every morning whether I like it or not. Asked me three times to take him on. I said no once out loud and twice with my face.
  • So I left a scrap of hide and my second-best awl by the door. Wanted to see what he'd do. Pocket them, leave them, cut himself. This morning, both gone. Step swept. Not a word.
  • I'm not asking him. I'd never hear the end of it. You ask. Find out what Edgar Penhallow did with my hide and my awl. Don't say I want to know.
  • He'll be somewhere on the Row with a notebook, drawing something that isn't his business. Go.
  • Hm. Then I'll wonder. I'm good at wondering. Had seventy-six years' practice.
  • The hide and the awl. What the Selsior boy did with them. Don't say I asked.
  • The awl? Oh dear. Was it not meant for me? I am so sorry. It was lying right by the step, point up. Someone might have trodden on it. So I took the scrap of hide that was beside it, please forgive me, and cut a little sheath for it, and stitched it round.
  • Saddle stitch, eight to the inch, waxed thread; that is how we were taught at the guild hall. Then I put it back exactly where it was, in the sheath, a little further from the step. Is Cobble angry? Please say Cobble is not angry.
  • Oh. You will not say who asked. Of course. I understand entirely. (He looks down the Row toward the shop with no sign, and goes a little pink.)
  • A sheath. For my awl. Out of a scrap. (Cobble picks up the awl from beside the door, turns the little sheath over in his fingers, and counts the stitches under his breath.) Eight to the inch. Straight. Waxed.
  • Hm. Wrong sort of hands. Probably. (He does not put the awl down.) Go on. Shut the door behind you. No. Leave it open. The boy'll be along to sweep.

docs.title: Hold the Deep Cut
docs.text:
The wave has come. The Deep Cut's golems are waking all at once. Hold it with Constance while the quarries stand up.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Constance Level 67 After Survey the Quarry Road Leads to The Face Is Moving

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 80 Deep Cut golems in The Deep Cut

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 92,750 EXP
  • 1,340 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Constance
Dialogue
  • It's started. Earlier than I wanted, exactly when I guessed. The whole The Deep Cut is standing up.
  • Thurstan's already there, which is both good and terrifying. Hold the Deep Cut with us: 80 golems. I'll plan. He'll charge. You keep us both alive.
  • Go. I'll be right behind you. Taking notes.
  • I understand. I'd rather you came. But I understand.
  • Eighty golems in the Deep Cut.
  • We held. All three of us, and not one name on Joan's slate for the wrong reason.
  • This season's notebook is finished, Player. I think I'll send it to someone who can do something with it. Thank you. I don't say that often. Ask Thurstan.

docs.title: The Waves
docs.text:
Constance wants her notebooks' dates laid against Gervase's monster map, with Mariota reading the pattern: do the changes come in waves, and do the quarries wake at each one?

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Constance Level 63 After Ore for a First Sword Leads to Survey the Quarry Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Mariota
  2. Talk to Gervase
  3. Talk to Constance

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 77,240 EXP
  • 1,260 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +35 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Constance
Dialogue
  • Three years of notebooks, Player, and a feeling I can't prove. I'm done with feelings. I want proof.
  • Take my dates to Mariota, then go to Gervase and lay them against his monster map. Then come back and tell me what you saw. I'll be here, pretending to be calm.
  • Mariota first. She'll make you wait while she reads. Let her.
  • Then I'll go on keeping notes. Somebody has to.
  • Mariota, then Gervase, then back to me.
  • So. The notebooks and the map agree. It comes in waves, and the quarries woke at every one.
  • (She closes the notebook very gently.) Why, nobody knows. When, I can guess. The next one is due. Thank you, Player. We'll need you at the quarries.
  • Constance's dates. Oh, these are lovely. Give me a moment. Give me an hour.
  • There. Clusters. Long quiet, then a rush, then quiet. Take this to Gervase and have him lay it on his map.
  • Dates? Against my map? Hand them over.
  • (He lays them out, dot by dot, and goes very still.) Every rush on her list, a new cluster of dots at the quarries. Every one. Tell her that.
  • Well? No, don't soften it. Tell it plainly. I'll write it down.

docs.title: Watch, Don't Kill
docs.text:
Constance needs the rubble golems on the Spoil Heaps observed, not killed: walk out to three vantage points and watch how they move.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Constance Level 50 Leads to A Bounty Alone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the first vantage point in The Spoil Heaps
  • Reach the second vantage point in The Spoil Heaps
  • Reach the third vantage point in The Spoil Heaps

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 38,900 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Constance
Dialogue
  • For once I need a monster observed, not killed. Thurstan finds this concept very difficult.
  • The stone at the quarries has started to stand up. Walk the The Spoil Heaps and stand at three vantage points I've marked. Watch the Rubble Golems: how they wake, which way they turn, how long they stand. Fight if you must. I'd rather you didn't.
  • Take your time at each point. Patience is the whole of the method.
  • Understood. Watching is harder than it sounds.
  • Three vantage points on the Spoil Heaps. Watch the golems.
  • They woke in a row, one after another, like a line of lamps being lit? (She writes very fast.) Not one at a time. In a row.
  • That's the first useful thing anyone's told me about them. Thank you, Player. This one goes on a fresh page.

docs.title: Corisande's Key
docs.text:
Corisande keeps the key to the old wing, as her mother and grandmother did. Nobody has ever asked her to open it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Corisande Level 23 After Faelan's First Lantern Leads to The Rootbound Wing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Sorrel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,184 EXP
  • 690 mesos
  • +200 standing with Corisande
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
  • Unlocks boss.the_unbound
Dialogue
  • You want to go into the old wing? Truly? Nobody has ever asked me that. Not once. Not my mother either, nor hers.
  • I'll open it. Oh, I'll open it gladly. But the door's behind the Grove School, and Sorrel ought to know someone's going in. It's his school.
  • Tell Sorrel you're going into the old wing. Then come back and I'll open the door.
  • Oh, I'm so pleased. I've polished the key.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Sorrel first, dear. It's his school.
  • Sorrel said 'listen first'? That sounds like Sorrel.
  • Here we are, then. It turns. It actually turns. The door's at the end of the old branch of the Lantern Paths, and the inner door at the wing's heart will answer to the key now too.
  • ...The old wing.
  • ...Listen first. Inside. Before anything else. Then go.

docs.title: Mhairi's Song
docs.text:
Cormac is hurt that his old pupil Mhairi has not asked him for a verse of her race song. Ask her, lightly, how it goes, and bring him 15 Fox Sinews for a set of old camp fiddle strings.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Cormac Level 28

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Mhairi
  2. Bring 15 Fox Sinew (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,600 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x2
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Cormac
Dialogue
  • Sit, sit. I have a sorrow, and a sorrow wants an audience.
  • Mhairi, my Mhairi, the best thing I ever did, is writing a song about the race. A verse for the gap, a verse for Iska, for Tamsin, for that great lump Jory. And has she asked her old teacher for a single line? She has not.
  • Go and ask her, lightly, as if it were your own idea, how the song goes. And bring me 15 Fox Sinew from the Strand Foxes. The old camp fiddles were strung with sinew, and I mean to have a set made for her. A gift. Not a bribe. A gift.
  • Lightly, mind! As if you had only just thought of it.
  • No, no, quite right. Leave an old man to his sorrow. It suits him.
  • Did you ask her? Lightly? And the sinew, fifteen. You have (how many you carry).
  • "He'll hear it when it's finished." She said that? Exactly that?
  • Is that a slight? It sounds like a slight. Or a promise. Oh, I don't know, Player. I've sung other people's hearts for sixty years, and I can't read the one I taught.
  • The strings will be ready by the send-off. I'll give them to her and say nothing about verses. Nothing at all. Here, take this, and don't let me cry on it.
  • Cormac sent you, didn't he? Don't make that face. He always sends someone.
  • Tell him it isn't finished. Tell him he'll hear it when it's finished, and not a note before. Tell him exactly that.

docs.title: The Hour the Water Forgets
docs.text:
Cormac has only ever sung the first line of the gap verse. Morven had the ending, and Calder heard it.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Cormac Level 58 After Marks Where the Boats Cannot Go Leads to Timber for the Boat

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Calder

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 24,000 EXP
  • 2,300 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Cormac
Dialogue
  • The hour the water forgets. That is all I have ever sung of it, my friend. The old pilot who taught it to me was frightened, and told me to keep it.
  • Morven had another ending. I would swear it. And Calder sat at her knee. Go to him. He will sing for you when he will not for me.
  • Ask Calder for Morven's ending of the gap verse.
  • Gently, now. It is his grandmother's song.
  • Ah. Another winter, then.
  • Calder, at the coves.
  • He wants keel timber first? Of course he does. He has drawn that boat on every net-shed wall in the coves.
  • Get him his timber, and listen well when he sings.
  • Morven's verse? Cormac has been at me about that for years. And now he sends you. Clever old man.
  • I will sing it. But I want something first. The drowned pines on the Greystrand went hard in the salt, straight as you like. Good keel timber, for a boat I have drawn too many times.

docs.title: The Verse and the Page
docs.text:
The verse is a Savage song. Ailsa's oldest page is Magician writing. With one, she might read the other.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Cormac Completed with Ailsa Level 60 After Timber for the Boat Leads to Where the Eddy Turned

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Morven's Verse

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 44,500 EXP
  • 2,400 mesos
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Ailsa
Dialogue
  • He sang it. He sang it for you. Say it again. Slowly.
  • There. I have written it down. I have not written a song down in fifty years. The verse is Savage, from the hunters' side of the first camp. Ailsa's oldest pages are the Magicians' hand. One camp, two tongues.
  • Take Morven's verse to Ailsa at the Wardens' House.
  • Go, my friend, before I lose my nerve and sing it at the Gap Inn instead.
  • Then I will keep it a while longer.
  • To Ailsa, at the Wardens' House.
  • Give it here. Wait. Wait. This word, here, and this mark on the page: they are the same word.
  • Before the kingdom the slack came late a whole season, and the run pressed the forest cliff. The first wardens sounded the Jaw's foot and found it hollow, and something great in the hollow. They drove it out to sea, and the water kept its hour again.
  • It is back. That is what my pages have been saying. Varro will have felt it. He has not asked me, which is how I know.

docs.title: Corrie a board for the boat
A Board for the Boat
docs.text:
Corrie writes her notes on the back of her hand because there is nothing to write on in a pilot boat. Thin out 40 Driftstumps and bring her 10 Sound Driftwood for a board.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Corrie Level 24 Leads to The Run from Above

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Driftstump
  • Bring 10 Sound Driftwood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • Fish Cake x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Corrie
Dialogue
  • Oh. Player. Sorry, my hand. It's ink. It's always ink.
  • I write my notes on the back of my hand in the pilot boat, because there's nothing else to write on, and by evening I'm blue to the wrist. Kor calls me the squid. I'd like a board. A small one, that floats, that I can lash to the thwart.
  • It has to be Sound Driftwood. It's dense, and it doesn't rot, and the Driftstumps in the Strandwood are made of it. Mostly.
  • Could you thin out 40 Driftstumps and bring me 10 Sound Driftwood? I'll need spares. I'll drop the first one. I always drop the first one.
  • The Strandwood track leaves the Saltwood Road. The stumps walk about by the timber crews' cutting. I've written it down for you. Oh. On my hand. Never mind.
  • That's all right. I've still got the other hand.
  • Forty Driftstumps, and 10 Sound Driftwood. You have (how many you carry) so far. I'm keeping count.
  • Ten! And all sound. I can plane one smooth tonight and write on it tomorrow.
  • Thank you, Player. I'll still write on my hand, probably. But then I'll copy it onto the board, and then into the book, and I'll have it three times. Here.

docs.title: Four Books
docs.text:
Corrie's loft leaks, and she wants her four filled notebooks kept dry. Take them to Esk for her sea-chest.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Corrie Completed with Esk Level 36 After The Run from Above

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Corrie's Notebooks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,000 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x5
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Corrie
Dialogue
  • I've filled four books now. Four. Every tide since I got a tiller, every ship, every one of Kor's mistakes on its own page. I've never lost one.
  • But the loft leaks over my bed when the wind's in the west, and I lie awake thinking about the books, not the roof. Esk keeps her sea-chest dry as a bone. She's the only person I know who's more careful than me.
  • Would you take my books to Esk and ask her to keep them in her chest? Don't open them. Not because there's anything in them. Just, don't.
  • Esk will be on the Inlet Quay, by the net stores. She'll know they're mine. Nobody else wraps things in three layers of oilcloth.
  • Oh. No. Of course. I'll put them under the bed. The other side of the bed.
  • My books to Esk, for her sea-chest. Please don't open them.
  • Corrie's books. Three layers of oilcloth, and a knot I taught her.
  • Tell her yes. They'll sit at the bottom of my chest, under everything I own, and nobody will open them. Not even me.
  • She'll want to hear it twice, so tell her twice. Here. She'd want you paid, and so would I.

docs.title: The Run from Above
docs.text:
Corrie wants to draw the whole run of the gap from the Saltface, but the cliff is thick with Shore Crabs. Clear 40 of them from the Saltface.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Corrie Level 30 After A Board for the Boat Leads to Four Books

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Shore Crab in The Saltface

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,700 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Corrie
Dialogue
  • Kor reads the gap from the water. Varro reads it from the end of the quay. I can't do either yet, not properly. I can only write down what I see, a bit at a time.
  • From the Saltface you can see the whole run at once, from the inlet to the open sea. I want to draw it. All of it, on one page. But the Shore Crabs are thick on the cliff, and I'm not much good with a knife.
  • Would you go down onto the Saltface and clear 40 Shore Crabs? Then I'll go down and draw the run while it's quiet. I'll be quick. I'm never quick. I'll try.
  • Down the steep way from the Gullwalk. Thank you. I'll get my board.
  • No, it's fine. I'll draw it from the quay. It'll be a smaller picture.
  • Forty Shore Crabs on the Saltface. Then I can draw.
  • It's quiet down there? Really? Then I'm going this afternoon, before the wind gets up.
  • When the page is done I'll show you. It'll have the run, and the slack, and the eddies, every one I can see. And a little mark where you stood, if you like. Here, for your trouble.

docs.title: Boggles on the Road
docs.text:
Corwell's caravans come up later every month, and the Dust Boggles on the Canyon Road are part of why. Hunt 40 of them.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Corwell Level 14 Leads to Traders from the Woods

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Dust Boggle in The Canyon Road

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,350 EXP
  • 280 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Corwell
Dialogue
  • Sit, sit, Player, there is always a chair at my counter. Have you noticed the caravans? They used to come up on the first of the month, regular as rain in the lowlands. Now it is the tenth, the fifteenth, or never.
  • The drivers all say the same thing: the The Canyon Road is crawling with Dust Boggles. Little dusty things, all teeth and temper, and they spook the mules at every bend.
  • Would you go down and thin them out for me? 40 Dust Boggles on The Canyon Road, and I will make it worth the walk.
  • Bless you. The The Canyon Road is past the The South Path, out of the south gate and down. Mind the rope bridge over the dry wash, it bounces.
  • No harm in it. The boggles will still be there, sadly, and so will my chair.
  • Forty Dust Boggles on The Canyon Road, Player. Down the The South Path and keep going.
  • Forty! I can hear the mules singing already. Well, braying. It is the same thing to a trader.
  • Here, take these potions and a little coin. If the next caravan is on time, I shall tell the drivers whom to thank.

docs.title: Fresh Cable
docs.text:
Corwell has a coil of fresh lowland cable for Vosk. Carry it to him, and clear 50 Wild Boars from around the anchor stakes at the Far Anchor before the next gnawing.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Corwell Completed with Vosk Level 34 After The Night Watch Leads to Grey and Bitter

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Deliver 1 Fresh Cable
  • Defeat 50 Wild Boar in The Far Anchor

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 17,000 EXP
  • 680 mesos
  • Highland Salve x10
  • Travel Ration x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Corwell
Dialogue
  • Ah, the bridge hero. Sit, sit, no? Pity, it is a very good chair. Vosk ordered cable from the lowlands in spring, and it came up with the last caravan, late as everything is these days.
  • He will not trust it until he has tied it himself, of course. Would you take the coil to Vosk? And while you are out that way: the Wild Boars at The Far Anchor root around the anchor stakes and loosen them. Clear 50 of them and Vosk will have firm ground to work on.
  • Here is the coil. Heavier than it looks, like most good things. Mind it does not touch the fire.
  • Then it sits in my storeroom and Vosk glares at me across the square. I am used to that, too.
  • The Fresh Cable goes to Vosk in the Kragvar Quarter, and fifty Wild Boars at The Far Anchor.
  • Lowland cable. Hm. Hemp, tarred, tight lay. Corwell did not cheat me, which will annoy him to hear.
  • And you cleared the boars from the stakes. Good. I will splice this in at the far anchor myself, and I will tie the knots, and I will sleep a little better. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Traders from the Woods
docs.text:
The Fairy Forest traders come up the Northern Woodland Trail, and the Snapping Lizards of the Young Woods have been snapping at them. Hunt 40.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Corwell Level 18 After Boggles on the Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Snapping Lizard in The Young Woods

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,550 EXP
  • 360 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Corwell
Dialogue
  • My lowland caravan came in on time last month, Player, and I know whose doing that was. Now I have the other road on my mind.
  • The Fairy Forest traders walk the old trail along the North Ridge and out through the woods. Lovely folk, they pay in honey and lamp-glass. But they write that the Snapping Lizards in the The Young Woods go for their ankles.
  • Would you hold the trail for them? 40 Snapping Lizards in The Young Woods. That is the last stretch before their lanterns.
  • Out of the north gate, over the The North Ridge, through the The Edgewood, and you are there. Take a snack, it is a long way for a short visit.
  • Another time, then. I will tell them to wear thick boots.
  • Forty Snapping Lizards in The Young Woods, Player. It is the far end of the Northern Woodland Trail.
  • All forty? Then the honey will come up the trail this season, and I will not have to explain to Harra why my tea is bitter.
  • Potions and coin, with my thanks. A trading post is only as good as its roads, and you have kept two of them open.

docs.title: Crispin the fifth act is missing
The Fifth Act Is Missing
docs.text:
A draft of Crispin's fifth act has gone missing from his desk. Marigold is the obvious suspect. For once, she may not be the right one.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Crispin Level 26 After The Shepherds' Hut Leads to What a Swarm Looks Like

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Marigold
  2. Talk to Rosamund

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Crispin
Dialogue
  • It's gone. The draft. The fifth act, or one of them, the third one, from my desk. I had it. I had it this morning.
  • And Marigold looked at me over breakfast. You know the look.
  • Ask Marigold about it. Then, if she says what I think she'll say, ask my wife Rosamund.
  • Gently with Marigold. She'll make a scene. A good one, but a scene.
  • Then I'll write it again. From memory. Badly.
  • Marigold first, then Rosamund. Gently.
  • Rosamund had it? She was reading it aloud. To the mirror. Of course she was.
  • Well, it's found. And Marigold didn't take it. I'll have to apologise. She'll want a part for it.
  • I did not take it. For once in my life, I did not take it.
  • Ask Mama. She reads everything aloud, in the dressing room, to the mirror. And tell Papa I expect an apology. In writing.
  • The third ending? Oh, I have it here. I was reading it aloud. It needs a beat before the last line.
  • Take it back to him. And tell him the third ending is better than he thinks, and the fifth is better still.

docs.title: The Shepherds' Hut
docs.text:
Crispin wants to know what it is like to sit where shepherds tell stories at night, with the boars outside. For the play. Probably.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Crispin Level 23 Leads to The Fifth Act Is Missing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks
  • Look at the shepherds' hut in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,460 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Crispin
Dialogue
  • The first act opens with shepherds. Telling a story by a fire. About the... well. About it.
  • I have never sat in a shepherds' hut. I have sat in a great many wings. It is not the same.
  • Drive off 30 Downs Boars on The Thyme Banks, then sit in the shepherds' hut and tell me how it feels. The dark, the sounds, the...
  • Notice the small things. The small things are where lines come from.
  • No, quite right. I'll imagine it. I'm good at imagining. It's endings I'm bad at.
  • The Thyme Banks. The boars, then the hut. The small things.
  • The wind through the door. Something snuffling outside. Nobody inside, and a cold fire.
  • No, wait. That's it. That's the first line. Here, take this, I need both hands.

docs.title: Crispin what a swarm looks like
What a Swarm Looks Like
docs.text:
Crispin's Last Stand scene needs to feel like holding a line against something that keeps coming. He wants it described by someone who has done it. Then he wants Thomasin's opinion. Again.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Crispin Level 29 After The Fifth Act Is Missing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Chalk Hive Bee in The Chalk Hives
  2. Talk to Thomasin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,880 EXP
  • 580 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Crispin
Dialogue
  • The Last Stand. The front line held for days at the Tree. Days! How does it feel when it keeps coming?
  • I can't ask anyone who was there. I can ask you to stand in front of a swarm on The Chalk Hives.
  • Hold your ground against 40 Chalk Hive Bees on The Chalk Hives. Then tell Thomasin what it was like, and ask if the accounts say it felt like that.
  • She'll say nobody knows. Ask her anyway. I'm used to it.
  • Fair. It's a lot to ask. Most things in this play are.
  • Forty of the swarm on The Chalk Hives, then Thomasin.
  • She said "nobody knows what they felt; we only know they stayed"? They stayed.
  • That's the scene. Not the fighting. The staying. No, wait, write this down. No, I'll write it down. Thank you.
  • Crispin sent you to ask how the Last Stand felt. Of course he did.
  • Tell him nobody knows what they felt. We only know they stayed. Every account agrees on that, and they agree on very little.

docs.title: Boar for the Feast
docs.text:
An envoys' feast in a week and the boar carts have not come. Hunt boars on the Thyme Banks for the carters, then tell Agnes the feast is on.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Cuthbert Level 25 After Rosemary for the Roast

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks
  2. Talk to Agnes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,100 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Cuthbert
Dialogue
  • An envoys' feast in a week, and the boar carts have not come in! Boar on the Downs, they say, rooting up the folds! Fat ones!
  • Hunt 30 Downs Boars on the The Thyme Banks; the carters will follow behind you. Then go up and tell my girl Agnes the feast is on. She lays the tables in the upper hall.
  • Ha! Go on! I will have the spit turning before you are back!
  • Then it is turnips for the envoys. TURNIPS!
  • Thirty Downs Boars, then Agnes. The spit is waiting!
  • She said not to send biscuits? Then take these biscuits. HA! Thank you, Player. One day it will be every town on one table.
  • The feast is on? Oh, good. Father has been shouting at an empty spit for three days.
  • Tell him I will have the hall ready. And tell him not to send biscuits up with you. I know he will.

docs.title: Rosemary for the Roast
docs.text:
Midbarium's slow mutton wants fresh rosemary, and the market's is all twigs. Gather rosemary on the Downs for Cuthbert.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Cuthbert Level 21 Leads to Boar for the Feast

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Gather 15 Rosemary Flower

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,000 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Cuthbert
Dialogue
  • Midbarium's slow mutton wants rosemary, fresh, and the market's is all twigs! TWIGS! Do you hear me, basket? TWIGS!
  • Gather me 15 Rosemary Flowers from the Downs. Fresh, mind! I can smell a stale one from here!
  • Off you go! The mutton is not getting any younger! Well, it is not getting older either. Go!
  • Then the envoys get twigs, and I get the blame!
  • Fifteen Rosemary Flowers, fresh, from the Downs!
  • AH! Smell that! That is mutton, that is! Sit down, I will feed you. No arguments!

docs.title: Eyes by the Stackyards
docs.text:
Dagny sees pairs of eyes in the dark beyond the road every night now, low in the stackyards below the gate. Hunt 30 young gloomeyes in the Gate Meadows and find out if those are the eyes.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe Level 16

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Young Gloomeye in Gate Meadows

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,070 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • +40 standing with Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Can I tell you something and you will not laugh? Every night there are eyes out there. Pairs of them, low down, by the beam piles in the stackyards. They catch the lamplight and they hold still. I count them. I tell Brindle. The number goes up.
  • I cannot leave the gate to look, not at night, and in the day I am asleep, mostly, or pretending to be. I want to know what they belong to. In daylight. Please.
  • There are Young Gloomeyes in the Gate Meadows, the little pale lizards. Would you hunt 30 of them in the stackyards and tell me if those are my eyes?
  • Oh, thank you. Straight out of the gate; the stackyards are right there, sheds and scaffolds and stone piles. Look under things. That is where they sit.
  • No, that is fine. I will just keep counting. Counting is good. It is something to say to them.
  • Thirty Young Gloomeyes in the Gate Meadows. Look at their eyes, will you? Are they the same eyes?
  • Big round eyes that shine and hold still. Yes. Yes, that is them, I think. Some of them. The low ones by the beam piles.
  • But you said they were small. The ones I see further out, past the road, near the old walls, those sit higher. And they are wider apart. So that is half an answer. Half is better than none.
  • I am going to tell Brindle the small ones have a name now. It is easier to talk to something with a name. Thank you, Player. Really.

docs.title: Morning Prints
docs.text:
Every morning there are prints in the dust by the road below the gate. Dagny wants a proper count of the gloomeyes that make them: hunt 40 in the Outworks and report to Brindle's slate.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe Completed with Brindle Level 21 After The Night Watch Leads to The Smashers

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Gloomeye

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,150 EXP
  • 1,680 mesos
  • +50 standing with Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • You came back! I knew you would. I mean, I hoped. I said it out loud to the dark, which is the same thing. Listen: every morning, when the sun comes up, there are prints in the dust by the road. Little splayed feet and a tail drag.
  • Gloomeye prints, now that I know what gloomeyes are. And there are more of them every morning, coming closer to the gate. Brindle wants numbers for the slate. Real numbers, not my numbers, which are mostly me being frightened.
  • Would you go back into the Outworks, hunt 40 Gloomeyes, and give Brindle a proper count? Then the slate is right, and the Table has to listen.
  • Thank you! Count the prints too, if you see any. And when you are done, go straight to Brindle; I will be asleep. Probably. Trying.
  • That is all right. I will count the prints myself. From the gate. With both lamps.
  • Forty Gloomeyes in the Outworks, then tell Brindle. The slate is by the gate, the big one with all the chalk.
  • Forty, and Dagny's prints match the size of them. Good. That is a count I can stand up at the Table and say out loud without anyone asking if I was dreaming.
  • She sent you, I take it. She stood out there two years with only her own voice for company, and never once asked me for help with it. Somebody should notice that sort of thing. I have. I am working out how to say so.
  • There, chalked. Gloomeyes, forty, by the gate road. Thank you, Player. Now the lanterns: Lux will want you, I expect.

docs.title: The Eyes That Do Not Blink
docs.text:
Some of the gloomeyes in the Outworks are Disturbance-touched: bigger, bolder, eyes that never blink. Dagny wants them gone before they come up to the gate. Defeat 2 Elite gloomeyes. She will ask again, any time.

Town Urbanograd Category Repeatable Given by Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe Level 22

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 2 Elite Gloomeye

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,680 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • +40 standing with Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Most of the eyes out there blink. Some of them do not. Those ones are bigger, and they come closer, and when I talk at them they just keep looking. Hunt 2 of the Disturbance-touched Gloomeyes in the Outworks for me? I ask every time I see them. I see them a lot.
  • Thank you. They are the ones that glow wrong. You will know. Take a lamp. Take one of mine, actually. No, I need both. Take your own.
  • That is all right. I will talk at them some more. Maybe they will get bored.
  • Two of the touched Gloomeyes. The ones that do not blink.
  • Both? Both. Good. Tonight there will be two pairs fewer looking at me. I will notice. I count them.
  • Brindle will put it on the slate, and the Table will hear. Come back when they come back, Player. They always do.

docs.title: Bread for the Bar
docs.text:
Bryony's bread comes to the Salt and Bread every morning. This morning it did not, and Delphine has a room full of sailors.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Delphine Level 33 Leads to The Ledger of Tales

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Bryony

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,337 EXP
  • 726 mesos
  • +40 standing with Delphine
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • No bread this morning. Bryony's never late. I have a room full of sailors and soup with nothing to dip in it.
  • Run up to Bryony on Merchant Street and see what's happened? If it's trouble, tell her not to worry about us.
  • Run. Sailors without bread are worse than sailors without ale.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Bryony on Merchant Street about the inn's bread.
  • Kit took the cart to the Old Cut to 'see a crab'? With the bread on it?
  • Well, the bread's here now, a little sandy. Thank you. Two columns in my book: you're in the second one.
  • Oh no, the inn! Kit took the cart this morning. With the bread on it. He said he wanted to see the crabs on the Cut.
  • Alwyn's fetching him now. Tell Delphine the loaves are coming, and I'm sorry. And there's an extra one for her, for the trouble.

docs.title: The Ledger of Tales
docs.text:
Delphine has thought for years of showing her ledger of sea tales to Ambrose. Now that the drawer is open, she asks you to take it.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Delphine Level 58 After Bread for the Bar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ambrose

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 44,318 EXP
  • 1,276 mesos
  • +40 standing with Delphine
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Thirty years of the strangest tales told at my tables. Teller, ship, date, place. I've thought of showing it to Ambrose a hundred times.
  • His drawer's open now. Take it to him. Every place in it is a place he can put on that chart.
  • Don't spill anything on it. The bar does enough of that.
  • Another time, then.
  • Take Delphine's ledger of sea tales to Ambrose.
  • He's putting them on the chart? All of them? My grandmother's tales too?
  • Then the book did its job. Here. A kindness for the second column.
  • Delphine's ledger? Oh, my. Places, dates, ships. Thirty years of marks I never had.
  • Tell her each one goes on the chart, very small, with her name beside it. She deserves that much.

docs.title: A Serious Role
docs.text:
Dex has played the grandee for fifteen years and wants a serious role, just once, but whenever he says so everybody laughs. Tell Dina Finch he means it.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Dex Level 26 Leads to Lark's Song

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Dina Finch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,500 EXP
  • 1,560 mesos
  • +50 standing with Dex
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player! You know who I am, of course. The grandee! Fifteen years of falling off carts. Children throw sausages at me in the street. Lovingly.
  • But in here (Dex thumps his chest) lives a tragedian. A betrayed general. A father at a deathbed. I say 'I want a serious role' and the whole troupe laughs, and then I bow, because I cannot help it.
  • Go to Dina Finch. Tell her I am serious about being serious. If I tell her myself she laughs, and then I laugh, and then it is a comedy again.
  • Use a grave voice. Like this: 'Dina. He is serious.' No, lower. Lower. Perfect.
  • Ha! You see? Even you think it is funny. Everybody is a critic.
  • Tell Dina Finch that Dex is serious, Player. In the grave voice.
  • Serious. (Dina does not laugh.) Do you know that he comes in at dawn and recites tragedies to the empty theatre? Every morning. He thinks nobody hears.
  • I hear. My office is above the stage. Tell him: one morning soon, I will sit in the back row on purpose. One speech, his choice. And if he bows at the end, I walk out.
  • She has heard me? Every morning? The general's speech? The deathbed? (Dex sits down on the edge of the stage, very quietly for a man his size.)
  • One speech. Dina in the back row. And no bow. No bow! That will be the hardest part of the whole thing. Thank you, Player. Truly. That was me being serious. Did you notice?

docs.title: Lark's Song
docs.text:
On her day each year, Dex and Sprout sing one of Lark's songs on the Rooftops, and this year Dex lost the middle verse. Piper writes everything down; ask about the swallow song.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Dex Level 40 After A Serious Role

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Piper

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,350 EXP
  • 2,400 mesos
  • +60 standing with Dex
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Sprout's mother was Lark. She sang in the chorus, the best voice we ever had. A fever took her when Sprout was barely one.
