  • Every year on her day, Sprout and I go up on the Rooftops, watch the lanterns come on, and sing one of her songs. This year I lost the middle verse. I stood there booming the first verse like a fool, and then nothing. Sprout sang the rest. He knew it.
  • I do not want to lose it again. Piper writes everything down. Ask Piper whether any of the old chorus sheets have Lark's songs on them. The one about the swallow under the bridge.
  • Do not tell Sprout. He would be kind about it, and I could not stand that.
  • No, no. I will ask Piper myself. Tomorrow. Or the day after.
  • Ask Piper about Lark's swallow song, Player.
  • Lark's swallow song? Oh, I know it. It is not on any sheet. Hambone hums it when he polishes the wheels, the old way, and I wrote it down years ago because I loved the turn in the middle verse.
  • Here, I will write it out clean, middle verse and all. Tell Dex I did not change a note. I wanted to. There is a place where it begs to go up instead of down. But I did not. It is hers.
  • This is it. This is the middle verse. Yes. Yes, that is how it goes. (Dex reads it twice, without booming at all.)
  • Piper did not change a note? Piper changes every note of everything. Then I owe Piper a song. And you, Player, I owe a whole evening of not booming. Starting now. Very quietly. Thank you.

docs.title: Bats Under the Walks
docs.text:
Tunnel bats from the buried street have found their way up under the old quarters' skywalks. Dickon wants the roost below cleared before he starts his long walk's first post.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Dickon Level 28 After Cut From Below, The Buried Street

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Tunnel Bat in The Buried Street

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,800 EXP
  • 560 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Dickon
Dialogue
  • Good news! I'm sinking the first post for the long walk. Ha! Don't tell Lavinia. Bad news: there's a roost of Tunnel Bats right under where it goes.
  • They come up from that buried street Ida found. Clear 40 of them down on the The Buried Street and I'll get my post in before anybody says no.
  • Off you go! Keep your eyes up. Even down there.
  • Then the post waits. I hate waiting. I'm terrible at it.
  • Forty tunnel bats on the Buried Street.
  • Post's in! Straight as a mast. You can see it from Theatre Row if you squint and want to.
  • One post down, a long walk to go. Thank you, Player. When it opens, you walk it first. Well, second. Ida walks it first.

docs.title: Cut From Below
docs.text:
One of Dickon's oldest skywalks has a post that was cut through in the night, from below, where it stands over a drain grating. Go down beneath it and clear what's there.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Dickon Level 24 After The Extra Brace Leads to Bats Under the Walks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach beneath the cut post in The Old Drains
  • Defeat 30 Drain Rat in The Old Drains

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,370 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Dickon
Dialogue
  • Not whistling today, Player. Godric's old walk over the dye lane: one of its posts stands over a grating, and somebody, or something, cut it half through. From underneath.
  • Get under it. The spot's in the The Old Drains, at the far end past the chalk marks. Clear 30 Drain Rats round about. I'll prop the walk while you're down.
  • I'll be up top with a jack and a lot of language. Go!
  • Then I'll close the walk and put up a sign. Hate putting up signs.
  • The spot beneath the cut post in the Old Drains, then thirty rats.
  • Gnawed. Not sawn. Gnawed, by teeth bigger than any rat's I want to meet. Well. I'll sleeve that post in iron.
  • Thank you, Player. The walk's open again, and I'm whistling. Listen. Here, for your trouble.

docs.title: The Extra Brace
docs.text:
Stirges have started coming up through the gratings at night and roosting under Dickon's skywalks. Clear them from the drains below, and let Ida know: she walks the lanes under those walks.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Dickon Level 21 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to Cut From Below

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Drain Stirge in The Old Drains
  2. Talk to Ida

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,410 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Dickon
Dialogue
  • Hoy, Player! Got a minute? Bats. Or not bats. Drain Stirges, Ida calls them. They come up the gratings at night and hang under my walks. Ugly little things.
  • Pop down into the The Old Drains and clear 30 of them. Then tell Ida. She walks right under those walks, and I'd sleep better. Well. I'd whistle better.
  • The grating in Steps Lane. Tancred will show you down. Ha, mind your head!
  • No bother! I'll just add another brace. I always add another brace.
  • Thirty stirges in the Old Drains, then a word to Ida.
  • Ida says you came up out of the grating looking like a chimney sweep. Ha! Thank you, Player.
  • I still put the extra brace on, mind. Can't help myself. Here.
  • Dickon sent you down after the stirges? (She almost smiles.) He worries in timber. Every brace on those walks is a worry.
  • Tell him the lanes are quieter tonight. Tell him at dusk. He likes to hear it at dusk.

docs.title: Octopus Ink
docs.text:
Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash is copying the Table's oldest record book before it crumbles, and the city's ink is too thin to last. Bring her pool octopus tentacles from the Halfway Stone for a darker, longer-lived ink.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash Level 20 Leads to The Oldest Volume

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Octopus Tentacle (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,580 EXP
  • 2,220 mesos
  • +50 standing with Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Do not touch that, it is older than the Charter's case and twice as touchy. That is the Table's oldest record book. Scavenged paper, old ledgers turned upside down, ink gone brown as tea. Every time I open it, a little more of it stays on my fingers.
  • I am copying it, a page or two after every session. But the ink we buy now is thin stuff, and I will not copy a hundred-year-old heckle in ink that fades in twenty. The pool octopi out at the Halfway Stone make a black that would outlast the walls.
  • Bring me 25 Octopus Tentacles from the Pool Octopuses on the Walkers' Road. I will do the unpleasant part. I will also write down that you did the other unpleasant part.
  • Out of the gate, east on the Walkers' Road to the The Halfway Stone. The octopi sit in the drainage pools. Mind the ones that squirt; I am told it does not wash out, which is rather the point.
  • Noted. With the date. I note everything; do not take it personally.
  • You have (how many you carry) of 25 Octopus Tentacles. Meanwhile I am copying page nine with the last of the good ink, very small.
  • Twenty-five. Smelly, perfect. Give me a night with these and a pot on Mags's back stove, and she will give me a lecture I will also write down.
  • The first thing I copy in the new ink will be the oldest joke in the book. It is about a goat. It is not a good joke. It is ours, though, and now it will last.

docs.title: The Oldest Volume
docs.text:
Dimity has finished a first bundle of fair copies from the Table's oldest record book. She and Ozzie Lantry agreed to tell each other first about anything old; carry the copied pages to Ozzie's corner of the Great Hall.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash Completed with Ozzie Lantry Level 24 After Octopus Ink

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Copied Pages

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,190 EXP
  • 1,440 mesos
  • +60 standing with Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash
  • +30 standing with Ozzie Lantry
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Forty pages. Forty pages of the oldest volume, copied fair in your octopus ink, and the black has not so much as blinked. I have not been this pleased since Bastian changed his mind three times in one sentence.
  • Ozzie and I have an agreement: anything old, the other hears first. He will want these before I have finished blotting them, and if I take them myself he will talk until the session starts and I will miss the opening heckle.
  • Carry the Copied Pages to Ozzie Lantry, in his corner of the hall. The corner with the boxes. All the corners have boxes; his is the one where the boxes have boxes.
  • Flat, please, not rolled. And if he asks whether there is anything about the first winter, tell him gently: no. The book starts after it, the same as every other.
  • Then they wait in my drawer, and Ozzie will find out, and he will be hurt in a very long and rambling way. Come back if you change your mind.
  • Ozzie, Player. Behind the boxes. If you cannot see him, say 'spectacles' loudly; he will answer to find out where they are.
  • From Dimity? The oldest volume, copied? Oh. Oh, look at the hand on this, square as a paving stone. Where are my, no, these are distance ones. Here. Yes.
  • Look, the spring after the first winter: a vote on whether the goat may attend the Table. Carried. I had a copy from somebody's diary, but the diary said 'defeated'. Now I shall have to find out who was lying, and that will take me a very happy month.
  • Nothing of the winter itself, no. I knew there would not be. Thank Dimity for me, Player, and tell her the goat won.

docs.title: The Cart Must Roll
docs.text:
Dina knows about the cracked wheel Hambone has been hiding since spring. Tell Hambone, gently, that the cart must roll on Walkout Day, and find out what he means to do.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Dina Finch Level 36 After The Funniest Year, Seasoned Wood

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Hambone

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,920 EXP
  • 2,160 mesos
  • +60 standing with Dina Finch
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Hambone thinks I do not know about the wheel. The left rear, bound in wire since spring. Hambone is the worst liar in the Old Barracks, and the Old Barracks is full of actors.
  • He has his seasoned wood now, thanks to you. Good. But wood in a shed is not a wheel on a cart, and Walkout Day does not wait for anybody's feelings.
  • Go and tell Hambone from me: the cart must roll. The whole way round the square, with Rue on it and Dex falling off it, three times. Ask him what he means to do. Gently. He cries at the second act every year.
  • Gently, Player. I said gently. I am never gentle with him myself, so somebody has to be.
  • Fine. I will tell him myself, and we will both shout, and Thimble will come out with a mouthful of pins and shout at us both.
  • Tell Hambone, gently: the cart must roll. Then come back and tell me what he said.
  • Dina knows? Of course she knows. I told her it was nothing. I told her it was a squeak. She said a squeak does not need wire. (Hambone polishes the wheel without looking at it.)
  • Tell her the new spokes are cut. I will fit them. But the rim, the old rim... Fenwick fitted that rim, and Fenwick had it from... I will think of something. Tell her it will roll. It will roll.
  • 'It will roll.' He said that, did he? In that voice. The one that wobbles.
  • Then it will roll. Hambone has never once let that cart down, whatever he tells himself. Thank you, Player. That is my last note for today. Possibly.

docs.title: The Funniest Year
docs.text:
Dina Finch is sure this year's play will be the funniest in a decade. The words of Juna's play never change, so ask Dex and Rue what they would do to make it funnier.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Dina Finch Level 24 Leads to The Cart Must Roll

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Dex
  2. Talk to Rue

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,370 EXP
  • 2,880 mesos
  • +40 standing with Dina Finch
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • You! Yes, you. Stand there. No, there, in the light. Hm. Good posture. Bad timing, I can tell already. Never mind.
  • This year, Player, the play will be the funniest in a decade. I said that last year. I said it the year before. This year I mean it more.
  • The words of Juna's play never change, so the funny has to come from the people. Go and ask Dex and Rue what they would do to make it funnier, and bring me their answers before they think too hard about it.
  • Dex will say something enormous. Rue will say something small and right. Bring me both.
  • Coward. Lovely coward. Off you go.
  • Dex and Rue, Player. What would make it funnier. Quickly, before they rehearse an answer.
  • Funnier? The grandee falls off the cart in the fourth scene. What if he fell off TWICE? Off the cart, back on, and off the other side!
  • No, no, hear me out: three times. The crowd counts with him. ONE. TWO. Tell Dina three. She will say two. We will agree on three.
  • Funnier? (Rue thinks for a long time.) When the guild hauls Juna's cart away, in the first act... what if she just keeps performing? To nobody. To the empty space where the cart was.
  • Not for long. Just a breath. Then the crowd brings it back. I think that is funny. And a bit sad. Is that allowed?
  • Three falls. Of course three. He will do four on the night and I will pretend to be furious.
  • And Rue... performing to the empty space where the cart was. (For once, Dina is quiet.) That is it. That is the whole play in one breath. That girl.
  • Funniest in a decade, Player. Mark my words. I have said them before, but this time write them down.

docs.title: Kragvar Stone
docs.text:
The masons wear out their hammers on the hard Kragvar stone. Bring Dorrek 30 Flint Hooves to make new hammer heads.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Dorrek Level 40 After Wedges for the Scaffold Leads to The Old North Stair

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Flint Hoof (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 29,000 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • Far Slope Shield x1
  • Travel Ration x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Dorrek
Dialogue
  • You did good work with the wedges. Here is harder work. The stone we cut on this mountain is hard, and it eats hammers. Iron from the lowlands comes late or not at all.
  • The Flint Hogs on the Ironback Flats have hooves like struck flint. My grandfather's masons fitted them to hafts and swore by them. Bring me 30 Flint Hoofs and every mason in the quarter gets a hammer.
  • Thirty. Not twenty-nine. I count.
  • Then the masons share hammers and argue. They argue anyway.
  • Thirty Flint Hoofs from the Flint Hogs. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Thirty. I counted. Good, hard hooves, these.
  • Take this shield. Hide over Kragvar-cut timber; it will turn a boar. The Kragvar pay what they owe, Player, and not a copper less.

docs.title: The Old North Stair
docs.text:
Dorrek wants the patch on the old north stair checked, where his uncle Baruk fell. Inspect it on the North Ridge.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Dorrek Level 55 After Kragvar Stone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the patch on the old north stair in The North Ridge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,500 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • Travel Ration x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Dorrek
Dialogue
  • The old north stair runs up the cliff out on The North Ridge. Eleven years ago a rockfall took it, and my uncle Baruk with it. I dug for him all night while my father kept the fire.
  • We patched the stair afterwards. Patched it, not rebuilt it, because nobody had the heart to cut there. I've climbed every scaffold in this town since, and I've never once gone back up that stair to look.
  • Go and look at the patch for me: the joints, the wedges, whether the rock above it has moved. Tell me straight. You're the one I'd trust to tell me straight.
  • It's on the west side of The North Ridge, on the climb above the trail. You'll see where the stone changes colour.
  • Aye. Some other day. It's waited eleven years.
  • The patch on the old north stair, on The North Ridge. Look at the joints and the rock above.
  • It holds? The wedges tight, no new cracks above? Then it was good work, though the men who did it were weeping while they cut.
  • My daughter wants to cut a new stairway further south, on sounder rock. I keep a copy of her sketch in my coat. Don't tell her.
  • Maybe I'll let her cut it. Maybe I'll climb the old one again first. Here, for your trouble. And thank you.

docs.title: Wedges for the Scaffold
docs.text:
Dorrek climbs the highest scaffold himself before any mason goes up, and he wants it wedged tight. Bring him 30 Ridge Bark for wedges.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Dorrek Level 24 Leads to Kragvar Stone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Ridge Bark (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,300 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Dorrek
Dialogue
  • You. You look like you can carry. Good. See that scaffold? The tallest one, on the west wall. Nobody goes up it until I have been up it, and I have been up it, and it shifts.
  • It wants wedges between the poles and the stone. Ridge bark makes the best: tough, it swells a little when the night is cold and holds tighter for it.
  • Bring me 30 Ridge Bark. The Ridge Stumps on the The South Path and the The North Ridge carry it.
  • Good. Do not dawdle. My masons are standing about, and a mason standing about starts to talk.
  • Then I carve the wedges out of my own patience, and I have less of that than bark.
  • Thirty Ridge Bark. You have (how many you carry).
  • That is good bark. Thick. You took it from the big ones. I will cut the wedges myself, then I will go up first, and then my masons.
  • Here. Salve and potions. You carried, and you did not complain. That is most of what being Kragvar is.

docs.title: One Short
docs.text:
Dougal's count of boats has come up one short: a cove skiff slipped its knot and the ebb took it to the Undercliff. Go down there and clear 40 monsters so it can be towed home.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Dougal Level 33

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Undercliff
  2. Defeat 40 monsters in The Undercliff

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,600 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • Steamed Crab x5
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Dougal
Dialogue
  • Twelve. Eleven. Twelve, eleven. No, I've counted six times, Player. One short.
  • Old Ewart told me: count everything, every night, because one night the count will be wrong. Thirty years, and tonight it's wrong. The little skiff off the third ring, a cove lad's. He tied her with a knot I wouldn't hang a sock on.
  • The ebb will have taken her along the cliff foot. If she's anywhere, she's on the Undercliff, up on the boulders. And the Undercliff's no place to go poking about alone these days.
  • Go down to the Undercliff and clear 40 monsters off the beach, so the lad can row round and tow her home. Then come and tell me. I'll be here. I'm always here.
  • The steep way down off the Gullwalk, then the cliff foot. Low water's best. Why did the skiff go to the Undercliff? Because it was feeling a bit rocky. ...I'll work on that one.
  • Fair enough. I'll count her missing. It's still a count.
  • The Undercliff, forty monsters, then back to me. The skiff's still one short till you do.
  • The beach is clear? Good. The lad's rowing round for her at the turn, and I've told him what I think of his knot.
  • Twelve. Twelve, twelve. You don't know how good that sounds, Player.
  • Take these. And if you ever hear me say one short again, run the other way. Twice in thirty years would be too many.

docs.title: The Wake
docs.text:
Dougal has watched the lowest quay steps for thirty years. Something has been leaving tracks there.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Dougal Level 40 After The Unlit Stretches Leads to Below the Anvil

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the lowest quay steps in Goa Harbour
  2. Defeat 40 Shore Crab in The Undercliff
  3. Defeat 40 Sea Newt in The Undercliff
  4. Bring 1 Shed Newt Claw (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 16,000 EXP
  • 1,600 mesos
  • Dougal's Measure x1
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Dougal
Dialogue
  • Old Ewart told me: count everything, every night, because one night the count will be wrong. Well. It is wrong.
  • Sit the night with me on the lowest steps. No sword. Just watch. Then, if you see what I think you will see, follow it.
  • Watch from the lowest quay steps (press Up there), then follow the wake to The Undercliff, clear 40 Shore Crab and 40 Sea Newt where they come ashore, and bring back a shed claw.
  • Bring a flask. The steps are cold.
  • Ah well. More tea for me.
  • Steps, then the Undercliff. And a claw, if you find one.
  • Long and grey, it was. Came up out of the water, tasted the air, and slipped back. You saw it too. I am not mad, then. That is a comfort and it is not.
  • And this claw. I put my boot beside it. Wider than my boot, see? I have knotted the width into a cord. Ruan will want it, when he is ready to hear it.

docs.title: Down the Road
docs.text:
Mildred has a bundle of Tobin's letters for the capital, and the mail no longer goes as surely as it did. Walk the royal road to the Greenwood's far end, where it climbs toward Selsior, and clear 30 of the Greenwood's monsters on the way.

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Mildred Level 10

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Monster in the Greenwoods in The Greenwood
  • Reach the road toward Selsior in The Greenwood

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,300 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • The mail does not go as surely as it did, Player. Two carriers turned back at the Greenwood last month. I have the mayor's letters for the capital here, all of them tied and sealed. Would you see them down the road? Clear the Greenwood as you go, 30 of whatever is in it, and carry them to where the road climbs toward Selsior.
  • Thank you. The royal road leaves the Hills' west end: Kaldemor Woods, then the Crossing, then the Greenwood. At the far end of the Greenwood the road climbs over the rise. The capital's carriers meet ours there.
  • Then they will wait in my box another week. They are used to it.
  • The Greenwood's far end, Player, where the road climbs toward Selsior. And thirty of its monsters, so the carriers can walk it again.
  • Handed over at the rise? Good. I will write it in the book: the mayor's letters, carried by Player, every one of them on time.
  • The town thanks you, and so does my ledger. It hates a gap.

docs.title: A Washtub
docs.text:
Drum wants something bigger and louder to beat on. Hambone, at the Old Barracks Yard, has an old washtub from the theatre.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Drum Level 21

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Hambone

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 800 EXP
  • 1,260 mesos
  • +50 standing with Drum
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • (Drum hits the washtub. It goes thup. Drum frowns at it.) Too small. Need bigger. Louder.
  • Hambone. Theatre yard. Old washtub, from a play. Ask?
  • (Two beats on the pan. Thank you, in Drum.) Old Barracks Yard.
  • (A shrug. Thup.)
  • Hambone. The washtub. (Thup.)
  • The washtub? The big one from the laundry scene in the old farce? Bellamy Stroud put it on the cart forty years back and nobody ever took it off again. It has been a rain barrel since, mostly.
  • Drum can have it, gladly, so long as it comes back for Walkout Day if the troupe asks. Tell Drum to hit it gently the first time. That tub has had a long life and the bottom is all memories.
  • (Drum turns the great tub over, taps it once, then hits it hard. BOOM. Across the square three people jump and one starts dancing. Drum smiles.)
  • Good tub. (BOOM.) Thank you.

docs.title: The Rhythm Outside
docs.text:
For the first time, Drum plays the monster-rhythm outside the gate, on the Outworks' edge. Hunt the lampbats in the outer ditch while it plays, and see whether they scatter.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Drum Level 26 After Bite Herbs Leads to Under the Fallen Tower

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Lampbat in The Outworks: Outer Ditch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,000 EXP
  • 3,120 mesos
  • +70 standing with Drum
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • (Drum stops playing. The whole square notices.) Lux got new glass. Patch cleaned the bites. The lampbats will come again.
  • Loud nights, the outer lanterns last. Maybe. Proves nothing. (A long breath.) Tonight I play outside. On the wall above the ditch. First time.
  • You go down. Into the The Outworks: Outer Ditch. Hunt 60 Lampbats while I play. Watch them. Tell me what they do.
  • (Drum stacks the buckets, the pans and the big tub onto a handcart.) Brindle says the wall is mine till dawn. Go.
  • (Drum sits back down. Tok.) Another night.
  • (From up on the wall, between beats:) 60 Lampbats. In the ditch. Watch them.
  • They scattered? When the tub came in? (Drum is quiet a long moment.) I couldn't see. Too dark down there. Too busy playing.
  • One night. One ditch. Maybe the wind. Maybe you. Proves nothing.
  • (Then, very quietly, Drum writes something down on the tally sheet and underlines it twice.) Tomorrow night too. Louder.

docs.title: Crab for the Warden
docs.text:
Iska is out on a bad tide and will forget to eat, unless there is crab. Bring Dunmor 20 Shore Crab Claws, and tell Iska at the Wardens' House that there is crab on.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Dunmor Level 40 After The Sulking Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 20 Shore Crab Claw (taken)
  2. Talk to Iska

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 13,400 EXP
  • 1,600 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x5
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Dunmor
Dialogue
  • Iska's taking a ship through on the late tide tonight. A bad one. I'll light the end of the quay first and stand by it, same as always.
  • And when she comes in, she'll go straight up to the Wardens' House to see it written down, and she'll forget to eat. Unless there's crab. She never forgets crab.
  • Bring me 20 Shore Crab Claws, and then go up to the Wardens' House and tell Iska there's crab on. She'll say she's busy. Tell her anyway.
  • The Shore Crabs are on the Saltface and down on the Undercliff. I'll have the pot on when you're back.
  • That's all right. There's always fish. She forgets fish.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Shore Crab Claws. Then a word to Iska at the Wardens' House: crab.
  • Crab? He sent you all the way up here to say crab. ...Tell him I'm coming down when the ship's written in. Tell him I said that, and he'll know it means an hour, and he'll wait anyway. He always waits.
  • She said she's coming? Then she'll be an hour. Pot's on.
  • Thank you, Player. Twelve years, and it's still the best part of my day, her coming in off the water. Take these. And come down for a claw yourself, if you like. There's always enough.

docs.title: The Sulking Lantern
docs.text:
One of the quay lanterns has started to sulk. Carry it, level, to Gunna at the back of the Lantern Market.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Dunmor Completed with Gunna Level 32 Leads to Crab for the Warden

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Sulking Lantern

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,500 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Dunmor
Dialogue
  • Evening, Player. See the third lantern from the market stair? Watch it a moment. There. It's sulking.
  • It's not going out, not for a week. But it's started to think about it. Gunna likes to have them before they've made up their minds.
  • I'd take it up myself, but if I leave the quay before the last one's lit, the gulls sit on the dark ones, and then Dougal tells his joke.
  • Would you carry it up to Gunna, at the back of the Lantern Market? Carry it level. They don't like to be tipped.
  • Level, mind. And don't ask her how it works. She'll only ask you why you want to know.
  • No hurry. It'll sulk a while longer. They always do.
  • The sulking lantern to Gunna, at the back of the Lantern Market. Level, mind.
  • Dunmor's? He always brings them before anyone else has seen a thing. How do you suppose he knows?
  • No, don't tell me. Tell him I'll have it back to him in a few days, and that it was right to sulk.
  • Here, from him. He asks me to see his carriers paid. Did you think he'd forget? Does he ever?

docs.title: Heavier Timber
docs.text:
Dunstan wants the heavy oak out of the far stack, and the sawbills nesting in the Sea Locks' timber are in the way.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Dunstan Level 46 After Logs in the Ponds, Proof for Dunstan

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 70 monsters in The Sea Locks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 22,277 EXP
  • 1,012 mesos
  • +40 standing with Dunstan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The heavy oak. Far stack, Sea Locks end of the Cut. Where my father stored his thick timber.
  • Sawbills nesting in it. Clear 70 of whatever's on the Sea Locks. No reason. Ships need oak. That's all.
  • Hmph. No reason.
  • Another time, then.
  • Seventy of anything on the Sea Locks, for Dunstan's heavy oak.
  • The lads have the oak out. Thick. Good.
  • ...Thicker planking never hurt a hull. Don't tell Alwyn I said that.

docs.title: Logs in the Ponds
docs.text:
Dunstan's seasoning timber floats in the Old Cut's timber ponds, and nobody can get to it for the crabs and jellies.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Dunstan Level 23 Leads to Heavier Timber

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 monsters in The Timber Ponds

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,877 EXP
  • 506 mesos
  • +40 standing with Dunstan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You. The Timber Ponds, up the Old Cut. My oak's in there. Seasoning. Forty years I've floated timber in those ponds.
  • My lads won't go up there now for the crabs and the jellies. Alwyn says it's dangerous. Alwyn's right, which is annoying.
  • Clear 50 of whatever's in the Timber Ponds so my lads can pole the logs out. Don't scratch the oak.
  • Hmph. Don't scratch the oak.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fifty of anything in the Timber Ponds, so the lads can get the logs out.
  • My lads poled out six logs this morning. Good oak. Seasoned right.
  • ...You did well. Don't let it go to your head.

docs.title: A Letter Home
docs.text:
Edgar is writing his report home to the guild, and it must be exact about the rooftop boot. He needs one detail of the sole from Cobble.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Edgar Penhallow Level 31 After The Fifth Notebook

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Cobble

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,520 EXP
  • 1,860 mesos
  • +70 standing with Edgar Penhallow
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The carter leaves for Selsior at the end of the week, and I owe my family and the guild hall a letter. A proper report. Boots, mostly. I have written a great deal about boots.
  • But there is one thing I have not got right. The rooftop sole is stitched round, not nailed, but how thick is the inner layer before the welt? I measured four pairs and got four answers. Master Cobble would know. I cannot ask him a fourth time for anything.
  • Would you ask Cobble for me, please? How thick the inner sole is, on a rooftop boot. It is for the guild. It must be exact.
  • Thank you. I shall start the letter while you are gone. 'Dear Mother, dear Father, the boots here are remarkable...'
  • Of course. I shall write 'approximately'. The guild hates 'approximately'.
  • Master Cobble, at the shop with no sign: how thick is the inner sole of a rooftop boot?
  • Inner sole? Depends on the runner. Heavy runner, two hide-widths. Light one like Kite, one and a half, so the foot feels the slate. That's why his four pairs came out different. They're different people's boots.
  • Writing home, is he? (Cobble is quiet a moment.) End of summer, he's going back. Hm. (Another moment.) Step'll get dirty again. Go on.
  • It depends on the runner. Of course. Of course it does! In Selsior every boot is the same so that the guild can inspect it. Here every boot is the person's. That is the report, really, isn't it? That is all of it.
  • (Edgar writes two pages about soles, welts and hide-widths, signs them, seals them. Then, from the back of notebook five, he slides out a second sheet, folded very small, written over and crossed out and written again. He reads it. He folds it smaller and puts it back.)
  • Thank you, Player. The boots letter goes with the carter. The other one is not ready. It may not be ready for some time.

docs.title: The Fifth Notebook
docs.text:
Edgar has started a fifth notebook and does not yet know what it is about. He would like one rule of work from each of the two makers he admires most on the Row: Rivet and Cobble.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Edgar Penhallow Level 22 Leads to A Letter Home

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Rivet
  2. Talk to Cobble

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,840 EXP
  • 2,640 mesos
  • +50 standing with Edgar Penhallow
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • May I trouble you? I started a fifth notebook last week, and it has a title and nothing else. The title is 'How They Decide'. In Selsior the guild decides what you make and how. Here nobody does. And yet things get made. Beautifully.
  • I should like one rule from each of the two makers I admire most on the Row. The rule they work by. But if I ask Rivet, Rivet will laugh, and if I ask Master Cobble, he will grunt. Twice.
  • Would you ask them for me, please? Rivet, at the lift, and Cobble, at the shop with no sign. One rule each. I will write them on the first two pages.
  • Thank you so very much. Please do not let Master Cobble know the notebook is about him. Partly about him. A little.
  • Of course. Forgive me for asking. The first two pages will wait; they are very patient pages.
  • One rule from Rivet, at the lift, and one from Master Cobble, at the shop with no sign. Thank you ever so much.
  • A rule? For Edgar's book? (Rivet snorts, but does not say no.) Fine. Simple always wins. Build what works. If it sparkles too, lucky you. If it only sparkles, take it apart.
  • And tell Edgar to stop saying please to the winch. The porters are starting to do it too.
  • A rule. For what? (He looks at you a long time.) For the Selsior boy. Hm. Fine. A boot should outlive its owner. If it won't, don't make it.
  • That's the rule. There's only the one. Everything else is just doing it. Tell him that last part too. He'll need it more.
  • 'Simple always wins.' And: 'A boot should outlive its owner.' And: 'Everything else is just doing it.' Oh, that is three. He gave me two. Master Cobble gave me two!
  • Page one, page two, and page three. Now notebook five knows what it is about. Thank you, Player. Please excuse me: I must go and write very carefully for some time.

docs.title: Haggling by Proxy
docs.text:
Edith cannot get to the market this week. She sends the player to haggle with Isabeau, then to tell her sister Sybil what was got.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Edith Level 25 After Pins That Do Not Bend Leads to Lemon Balm Dye

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Isabeau
  2. Talk to Sybil

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,690 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Edith
Dialogue
  • I can't get down to the market this week, and Isabeau will think I've given up. I never give up.
  • Go and haggle for me. Then go up to the palace and tell my sister Sybil what you got. She'll want to gloat or console, either suits her.
  • Haggle with Isabeau at the Crown Market for a bolt of red wool, then tell Sybil at the palace the price.
  • Offer half. She'll laugh. That's where it starts.
  • Then I'll go next week and lose properly, in person.
  • Isabeau for the wool, then Sybil. Offer half.
  • Two-thirds? You got two-thirds out of Isabeau? I've not done that since your mother was a girl.
  • And Sybil laughed? Good. She hasn't laughed much lately. Thank you, dear.
  • Edith sent you to haggle? Half? She always starts at half.
  • Two-thirds, then, for her nerve. Tell her I enjoyed it, and that she owes me a proper hour next week.
  • Edith had you haggle with Isabeau? Two-thirds? Ha! My sister will be insufferable.
  • Tell her I'll hear all about it at supper. Tell her... tell her I have plenty to listen to and not much to say this week.

docs.title: Lemon Balm Dye
docs.text:
Edith wants to dye the Magician's robe a pale green no merchant sells, from lemon balm off the downs.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Edith Level 29 After Haggling by Proxy

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Gather 12 Lemon Balm Flower

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,150 EXP
  • 580 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Edith
Dialogue
  • The Magician's robe. Rosamund wants a green nobody's seen. Isabeau doesn't sell it. Nobody does.
  • Lemon balm off the downs, boiled long, gives the palest green you ever saw. My mother did it once.
  • Gather 12 Lemon Balm Flowers on the downs for me.
  • Fresh as you can, dear. Wilted balm goes grey.
  • Then she'll have to settle for an ordinary green. She won't.
  • Twelve sprigs of lemon balm, dear. Fresh.
  • That's the smell. That's the colour already. Look at your hands.
  • Rosamund will look like spring. Thank you, dear. Mind the pins on the way out.

docs.title: Edith pins that do not bend
Pins That Do Not Bend
docs.text:
Edith's market pins bend in heavy cloth. The stingers of the wild bees on the downs, she says, make finer pins than any smith.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Edith Level 21 Leads to Haggling by Proxy

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Bee Stinger (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,690 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Edith
Dialogue
  • Mmf. Pin. These market pins bend in anything heavier than linen, and the Balrog play is all heavy cloth.
  • The shepherds' wives on the downs use bee stingers. Fine, hard, never bend. I've a mind to try.
  • Bring me 15 Bee Stingers from the Wild Bees on Downs Edge.
  • Mind your sleeves out there, dear. Bees catch.
  • Never mind. I'll make do. I always make do.
  • Fifteen stingers, dear. Long ones.
  • Oh, these are lovely. Look how they go through felt.
  • Here, dear. And thank you. Nothing's thrown away in this attic, and nothing's wasted either.

docs.title: Bounty: The Hedge Lanes
docs.text:
Lieutenant Edric posts a standing bounty on the Hedge Lanes outside the Tree Gate: defeat 30 of its slimes, pigs or orange mushrooms. Selsior pays it every time.

Town Selsior Category Repeatable Given by Edric Level 5

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Hedge Lanes monsters (Slime, Pig, Orange Mushroom) in The Hedge Lanes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 100 EXP
  • 250 mesos
  • Red Potion x3
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +50 standing with Edric
Dialogue
  • The patrol can't ride every lane every day, Player. The Guard pays a bounty: 30 of the slimes, pigs and mushrooms on The Hedge Lanes, outside the Tree Gate. Any time you like.
  • Good. Farm carts use those lanes. Keep them clear.
  • Fair enough. The slimes aren't going anywhere. Unfortunately.
  • Thirty from the The Hedge Lanes, Player. Slimes, pigs, mushrooms, all count.
  • Thirty! The carters will thank you. Well, they won't, but they'd mean to. Here's the Guard's bounty.

docs.title: Bounty: The Rootlands
docs.text:
Edric's standing bounty on the Rootlands at the World Tree's foot: defeat 30 of its stumps, dark stumps or axe stumps. Selsior pays it every time.

Town Selsior Category Repeatable Given by Edric Level 15

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Rootlands monsters (Stump, Dark Stump, Axe Stump) in The Rootlands

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 960 EXP
  • 300 mesos
  • Orange Potion x5
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +50 standing with Edric
Dialogue
  • Where the road ends, at the Tree's foot, the The Rootlands. The stumps there walk into the road like they own it. 30 of them, Player, and the Guard pays every time.
  • Watch the axe stumps. I've a joke about them, but it's not sharp enough yet.
  • Fair. The roots aren't going anywhere. Neither are the stumps, sadly.
  • Thirty from the The Rootlands, Player.
  • The road to the Tree is clear again, for a while. Here's the bounty.

docs.title: Bounty: The Waystone Meadows
docs.text:
Edric's standing bounty on the Waystone Meadows: defeat 30 of its ribbon pigs, green mushrooms or horny mushrooms. Selsior pays it every time.

Town Selsior Category Repeatable Given by Edric Level 10

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Waystone Meadows monsters (Ribbon Pig, Green Mushroom, Horny Mushroom) in The Waystone Meadows

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 420 EXP
  • 250 mesos
  • Red Potion x5
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +50 standing with Edric
Dialogue
  • Further up the World Tree Road, the The Waystone Meadows. The shepherd's hut up there sends word the mushrooms are in the lane again. 30 of them, pigs included, and the Guard pays.
  • Mind the horny ones. They've got opinions, and the opinions are pointy.
  • Another day. The meadows will keep. That's the trouble.
  • Thirty from the The Waystone Meadows, Player.
  • The shepherd will sleep tonight. Here. The Guard's bounty, and my thanks with it.

docs.title: Old Cairn
docs.text:
Something as tall as a house has risen out of the First Cut's face. Ask Edric to take you to the First Cut and defeat Old Cairn, the Ancient of the Quarries.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Edric Level 68 After The Face Is Moving

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Old Cairn, the Ancient of the Quarries

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 129,000 EXP
  • 8,000 mesos
  • Elixir x10
  • Scroll for Topwear for DEF 60% x1
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Edric
Dialogue
  • The quarrymen call it Old Cairn. They named it before anyone had seen it whole, which tells you how long they've been afraid of it.
  • Defeat Old Cairn, the Ancient of the Quarries in the First Cut, Player. Ask me when you're ready, and I'll take you to it. I'll be at the mouth with the patrol, for what that's worth.
  • Right. Why did the golem cross the quarry? ...I've nothing. Go on.
  • Take your time. It's been in that stone longer than the city.
  • The First Cut, Player. Ask me and I'll take you there.
  • It's down. The face is still. The quarrymen came out to look at it, every one of them, without a word.
  • Constance is sending her notebooks to Bartholomew, every season of them. And Gervase came by: he's drawing the quarries again, with fewer dots. That's the best map I've seen in years.

docs.title: Queen of the Downs
docs.text:
Godwin found the great hive in a hollow of the chalk. Ask Edric to take you to the Hive Hollow and defeat Queen Amberwing.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Edric Level 28 After The Great Hive Leads to A Relic for the Stage

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Queen Amberwing

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,000 EXP
  • 1,500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x20
  • Scroll for Helmet for DEF 60% x1
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Edric
Dialogue
  • Godwin came to the Court with his arms stung to the elbow and a map drawn on a napkin. A hive in the chalk, he says, and a queen in it bigger than a calf.
  • Everything on the downs, the mean bees, the boars in the folds, it grows out of that hollow. I'd stake my horse on it.
  • Defeat Queen Amberwing in the Hive Hollow, Player. Tell me when you're ready and I'll take you to its mouth. Bring potions. Bring more than that.
  • Say the word and we ride. And Player: come back. That report I can't write.
  • No shame in waiting. The hive's waited this long.
  • The Hive Hollow, Player. Ask me and I'll take you there.
  • The queen's dead? You're sure? ...You're sure. Ha! Sit down before you fall down.
  • This goes to the palace tonight, the first report in a year I'll enjoy writing. And Gilbert sent word: his bees came back to the hives this morning. Calmer, he says. A little.

docs.title: Short a Rider
docs.text:
Edric's road patrol is a rider short. Ride out with Aylwin to Downs Edge, where the downs meet the World Tree Road, and clear 20 wild bees off the road verge. Then report to Aylwin.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Edric Level 20 Leads to Where the Horse Sweats, Boars on the Downs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 20 Wild Bee in Downs Edge
  2. Talk to Aylwin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,800 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Edric
Dialogue
  • Player. You'll do. The patrol is a rider short, and the road can't wait for me to find one.
  • Bees, of all things. The wild bees on the downs have turned mean, and they've come down to the verge where the downs meet the World Tree Road. A carter's horse bolted yesterday.
  • Ride out to Downs Edge with Aylwin and clear 20 Wild Bees off the verge. Then report to Aylwin; he'll know if the road is safe. Don't let him tell you the hat story.
  • Good. Why did the bee join the patrol? It wanted to buzz the road. ...I'll work on it.
  • Then I'll ride short. I've done it before. I don't like it.
  • Twenty bees on Downs Edge, Player, then report to Aylwin.
  • Aylwin says the verge is clear, and that you ride a road well. From him that's a poem.
  • It goes in the report. Bees on the downs, bolder than last year. Everything is bolder than last year.
  • Oh! You cleared the verge? Thank you, Player. My horse kept looking at the chalk banks the whole time, ears flat. I'll tell the Lieutenant the road's safe. Safe-ish.

docs.title: The Face Is Moving
docs.text:
The quarrymen say the face of the First Cut is moving. Edric wants eyes on it: go to the First Cut's mouth at the far end of the Deep Cut.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Edric Level 68 After Hold the Deep Cut Leads to Old Cairn

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the First Cut's mouth in The Deep Cut

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 97,000 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Edric
  • Unlocks boss.old_cairn
Dialogue
  • You held the Deep Cut. Constance told me, which means it was worse than she said. She never says anything is bad.
  • Now the quarrymen tell me the face of the First Cut is moving. Not cracking. Moving. The oldest stone in the kingdom, where the first keep came from.
  • Go to the mouth of the First Cut at the end of The Deep Cut, Player, and look. Just look. Then come and tell me I misheard.
  • No joke for this one. Go carefully.
  • Then I'll send the patrol, and I don't want to.
  • The First Cut's mouth, at the far end of the Deep Cut.
  • A face as tall as a house, and it turned to look at you. ...I didn't mishear.
  • Rest. Then come back to me. When you're ready, I'll take you to the First Cut, and we'll see what's standing up out of the stone.

docs.title: Bites for the Book
docs.text:
Edwina has stitched too many rat bites this season. She wants the drains below the lanes thinned, and the tails brought back so she can measure the bites against them.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Edwina Level 22 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to Notes on the Backs of Pages

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Drain Rat in The Old Drains
  • Bring 10 Drain Rat Tail (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,200 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Edwina
Dialogue
  • Sit down. No, you're not hurt. Good. I've stitched six rat bites this month, and two of them on children who should have known better and didn't.
  • Go under the grating and thin the Drain Rats: 30. Bring me 10 Drain Rat Tails. I want to measure the beasts against the bites. Somebody ought to.
  • Wash your hands when you come up. Before you touch anything of mine.
  • Then I'll go on stitching. I'm good at it.
  • Thirty drain rats and ten tails. You have (how many you carry).
  • (She lays a tail against a page in her fourth book and frowns.) Bigger than the bites, these. So the bites I've been stitching came from bigger still.
  • Hm. Well. You did as you were told, which is rare. Here. Wash your hands.

docs.title: Edwina notes on the backs of pages
Notes on the Backs of Pages
docs.text:
Edwina has kept notes on strange wounds on the backs of pages in her fourth book, and suspects Aldith keeps the same. She wants proof from the cisterns before she shows her oldest friend.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Edwina Level 25 After Bites for the Book, The Cistern Sluice

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 8 Black Rat Tail (taken)
  2. Talk to Aldith

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,670 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Edwina
Dialogue
  • I'll say this once. I've been writing down the wounds I can't name, on the backs of pages in my fourth book. I know Aldith does the same, down on the river. Fifty years, and neither of us has said a word.
  • I won't go to her with guesses. Bring me 8 Black Rat Tails from the The Cisterns, so I know what's down there. Then take my book to Aldith's bench and tell her to open hers.
  • Don't read it on the way. I'll know.
  • Then the pages stay closed. They've been closed a long time.
  • Eight black rat tails, then my book to Aldith on the Riverside.
  • She opened hers. (Edwina sits down, which she never does.) Same shapes, river and lanes. Fifty years, and it took a stranger with a book to get us to talk.
  • Well. You're not a stranger now. Here. And wash your hands.
  • Edwina's book? The fourth one? (She turns a page, then another, then reaches under her bench for a cheap book of her own.)
  • Same wounds. Same shapes. The old goat. Tell her I'll be at her door tomorrow with a teapot and my notes, and she'd better have the kettle on.

docs.title: Agna's Knots
docs.text:
Eilidh wants to tie a knot her grandmother will call better than "not bad". Look at Kestra's knots on the highest bridge, ask Agna what makes them good, and bring Eilidh 20 Fox Sinews for line.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Eilidh Level 28 After The Tide Slate

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the highest bridge in Goa Harbour
  2. Talk to Agna
  3. Bring 20 Fox Sinew (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,000 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Eilidh
Dialogue
  • Grandma has never said any knot of mine is better than "not bad". Not once. Not ever.
  • She says the only knots in Goa Harbour near as good as hers are on Kestra's bridges. "Shona's knots, near enough." So I need to know how Kestra ties them.
  • Go and look at the knots on the highest bridge on the Cliff Stairs. Then ask Grandma what makes them good. She'll tell you, she won't tell me. Then bring me 20 Fox Sinew from the Strand Foxes, it's the strongest line there is.
  • Look properly at the bridge. Which way the ends go. Kestra's knots never slip, everyone says so.
  • Then I'll tie it with old twine, and she'll say "not bad", and I'll scream.
  • The highest bridge, then Grandma, then 20 Fox Sinew. You have (how many you carry).
  • Twenty! And ends under, never over. Right. Watch me.
  • There. Grandma looked over my shoulder and said "not bad". But she said it slowly, Player. Slowly! That's practically a song. Here, Mum says I have to pay people.
  • Eilidh sent you to spy on Kestra's bridges, did she? Ha. Clever girl. Don't tell her I said so.
  • Tell her this and nothing more: Shona tucked her ends under, never over, and she tied with sinew, not that string Eilidh uses. Fox sinew, if you can get it. Off you go.

docs.title: The Tide Slate
docs.text:
Eilidh writes the cove's tides on her slate, but she wants to know how far the water goes out on the black rocks of the Strandwood. Go and see, and clear 40 Driftstumps there.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Eilidh Level 22 Leads to Agna's Knots

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach Strandwood Rocks
  2. Defeat 40 Driftstump

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,300 EXP
  • 900 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Eilidh
Dialogue
  • You go to the Strandwood, don't you? Everyone with a sword does.
  • I write every tide on my slate. Every evening. But the cove rocks only tell you about the cove. The black rocks out on the Strandwood go a long way out at low water, Dad says, and I've never been allowed to see them.
  • So you go. Go to Strandwood Rocks and look where the water stops. And the Driftstumps walk all over the low-water line, so clear 40 of them while you're there. Then tell me everything. Exactly.
  • Exactly, Player. Not "a bit further than here". Exactly.
  • Fine. I'll ask Arlo to ask someone. He'll get it wrong.
  • Have you been to Strandwood Rocks? And forty Driftstumps. You're slower than Ronan, and Ronan is slow.
  • Out past the third ledge of weed? At low water? That's much further than the cove. Much.
  • I'm writing it down tonight. No, you can't see where I keep my slate. Here, Mum's fish cakes. She doesn't count them, I checked.

docs.title: Elinor a partner who wont hold back
A Partner Who Won't Hold Back
docs.text:
A hooded recruit at the Knights' Court wants a sparring partner who will not hold back. Ask Rowena, and show her what you can do against a Disturbance-touched boar.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Elinor Level 26 After Boars on the Patrol Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Rowena
  2. Defeat 1 Elite Downs Boar

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60% x1
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Elinor
Dialogue
  • There is a hooded recruit at the Knights' Court who trains at dawn with Rowena. I hear.
  • The hooded one wants a sparring partner who will not hold back. Everyone holds back. It is maddening.
  • Would you ask Rowena whether you might be that partner? She will want to see what you can do first, I expect.
  • Go on, then! Before the drill bell.
  • Oh, everyone says that. Never mind.
  • Ask Rowena at the Knights' Court, and do whatever she says.
  • You did? The touched one? And Rowena said yes?
  • Then dawn, in the old yard. The hooded one will be there. Do not go easy, Player. Promise.
  • A partner for my dawn pupil? Hm. Anyone can swing at a practice post.
  • Bring down one of the Disturbance-touched boars on the The Thyme Banks, the big ones, and I will believe you will not hold back.

docs.title: Elinor boars on the patrol road
Boars on the Patrol Road
docs.text:
The boars of the Thyme Banks have been charging the road patrol's horses. Thin them out, then find Aylwin of the road patrol and see that he is whole.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Elinor Level 23 Leads to A Partner Who Won't Hold Back

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks
  2. Talk to Aylwin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,300 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Elinor
Dialogue
  • The road patrol rides past the The Thyme Banks. The boars there have been charging the horses. Someone told me that as if it were funny.
  • Thin out 30 Downs Boars there, would you? Then find Aylwin of the road patrol and... see that he is whole. Do not say I asked. Say nothing at all, actually.
  • Thank you. I mean it. For the horses.
  • Fine. I will go myself. I will. Probably not. Fine.
  • Thirty Downs Boars on the The Thyme Banks, then Aylwin. And not a word.
  • Every rider. Good. Good! Not that I was worried. I was asking for the horses.
  • Thirty boars off the Thyme Banks? The horses will thank you. So will I.
  • Tell... whoever asked, that the patrol is fine. All of it. Every rider.

docs.title: Thread for Stitches
docs.text:
The hunters keep bringing Elspeth fox bites. Bring her 20 Fox Sinew for stitching, and tell Torva to come and have her arm seen to.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Elspeth Level 26 Leads to The Lamp in the Window

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 20 Fox Sinew (taken)
  • Talk to Torva

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,800 EXP
  • 1,040 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Elspeth
Dialogue
  • Sit, sit, you're in the way of the door. Three hunters this week with fox bites, and Torva with a gash she says is a scratch.
  • I stitch with fox sinew. It's strong as fishing line and the body takes it kindly. The foxes give me the wounds, so it seems only fair they give me the thread.
  • Bring me 20 Fox Sinew from the Strand Foxes on Strandwood Rocks. And on your way, tell Torva to come and have that arm looked at. Today, not tomorrow.
  • And don't come back to me bitten. I'm out of patience before I'm out of thread.
  • Then go carefully, and come to me if you don't.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Fox Sinew. And has Torva been told? Today, I said.
  • A scratch. I told her it was a scratch. Tell her I'll come before dark. If I don't, she'll come and fetch me, and that's worse.
  • Twenty. Good clean sinew, too, you didn't hack at it.
  • And Torva came, scowling, and sat exactly where I told her to. She's the only one in Goa Harbour who does. Here, a few of my salves. Don't waste them on scratches.

docs.title: The Lamp in the Window
docs.text:
Elspeth's lamp burns every night, for Osric. Bring her 25 Sea Newt Hides for clean lamp oil, and look in on Osric on the way.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Elspeth Level 36 After Thread for Stitches

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 25 Sea Newt Hide (taken)
  • Talk to Osric

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,700 EXP
  • 1,440 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Tonic x5
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Elspeth
Dialogue
  • You'll have seen the lamp in my window. Everyone has. It burns all night, every night, and it eats oil the way a hunter eats stew.
  • Fish oil smokes and stinks. The old way is better: the fat from under a sea newt's hide, rendered clean. It burns slow and bright and doesn't blacken the glass.
  • Bring me 25 Sea Newt Hides from the Sea Newts on the Saltface. And on your way back, look in at Osric's hut. You needn't say anything. Just see that he's well.
  • The newts come up the cliff below the town. Mind their claws, and mind my stitches if you've had any.
  • Then I'll make do with fish oil for a while, and smell of the smokehouse.
  • (how many you carry) of 25 Sea Newt Hides so far. And have you looked in on Osric?
  • She sent you, I suppose. I see it, you know. The lamp, from my door, every night. Don't tell her that. Tell her the wick wants trimming.
  • The wick wants trimming, did he say? Well.
  • He used to say that when he was small, on nights he couldn't sleep and wanted me to sit up with him.
  • Here, for your trouble. Thank you, Player. The lamp will burn as long as I have oil, and now I have oil.

docs.title: Follow the Springs
docs.text:
The dying springs lead west and down. Go to the Red Ravine, look closely at three of the roots that run into the rock, and hunt 100 Stone Hulks.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Ennek Level 62 After The Old Walls Leads to The Rootdrinker

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Red Ravine
  2. Look at a root as thick as a pillar in The Red Ravine
  3. Look at a root split into the rock in The Red Ravine
  4. Look at the deepest root in The Red Ravine
  5. Defeat 100 Stone Hulk

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 181,000 EXP
  • 1,240 mesos
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ennek
Dialogue
  • My grandmother walked me through it with a stick in the dirt: the Greywater dry, then the old springs on the Dry Hills, failing toward the west. Water runs downhill, Player. Whatever is taking it is down and west of all of them.
  • Brakka came by and looked at the stick and the dirt, and said the only place it could be is under the The Red Ravine, where the rock is cracked deep enough. She wants to see it. I said nobody sees it until you do.
  • Go to The Red Ravine. Find anything going down into the rock that shouldn't be there, and look at it closely, three places if you can. The stone hulks there will not like you: 100 Stone Hulks.
  • Past the Deserted Ridge. Bring back what you see, not what you think. I'll do enough thinking for both of us.
  • All right. I'll keep carrying water skins. My shoulders are getting very strong.
  • Three of whatever goes down into the rock in The Red Ravine, and 100 Stone Hulks.
  • Roots? Thick as the pillars of the Great Hall, grey, going straight down into the rock? And all of them leaning the same way?
  • Brakka says nothing grows roots like that unless it's drinking from deep water. And the deep water is what feeds the springs. All of them, the Greywater too.
  • Then there's a tree down there under the Red Ravine, and it's drinking the highlands dry. I've never wanted to cut down a tree before. Take these, and rest, because we're going in.

docs.title: Sure Footing
docs.text:
Ennek teaches the Tolmach way of walking ledges to those who will follow him along the narrowest ledges of the South Path. Walk behind him, three ledges, and learn Sure Footing.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Ennek Level 20 After The Canyon Cairns

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the low ledge in The South Path
  2. Look at the switchback ledge in The South Path
  3. Look at the high ledge in The South Path

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,750 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • Skill: Sure Footing
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ennek
Dialogue
  • Remember the trick for ledges I promised you? Here it is. The Tolmach have walked these canyons with goats on their shoulders since before the town had a wall. We do not fall, mostly.
  • It is not something I can tell you across a counter. You have to walk it. Feet, knees, eyes, and whistling, which helps more than you would think.
  • Walk behind me along the three narrowest ledges of The South Path: the low ledge, the switchback ledge and the high ledge, in that order. Stop at each one and look down when I tell you to.
  • I will be just ahead. Do not watch me, watch where my feet go. And if you hear me stop whistling, stop walking.
  • Fair enough. Ledges are not going anywhere. That is rather the point of them.
  • The low ledge, the switchback ledge, then the high ledge on The South Path. Follow the whistling.
  • You looked down three times and you are still here. That is the whole lesson, really. Knees soft, weight forward, and never trust a stone you have not stood on.
  • Now it lives in your legs instead of mine.
  • That is Sure Footing. Open the skills window with K and you will find it there. The canyons will be a little kinder to you from now on.

docs.title: Tell Your Mother
docs.text:
Ennek has to tell Sennu that the Greywater is dry, before somebody else does. Go with him to her tent in the Tolmach Camps.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Ennek Completed with Sennu Level 50 After The Greywater Leads to The Old Springs

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,500 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ennek
Dialogue
  • My mother counts every head of the herd twice a night. If she hears about the Greywater from a trader at Corwell's counter, she'll never forgive me, and she'd be right.
  • Come with me to Sennu's tent. You saw the cleft with your own eyes. If I start whistling instead of talking, kick me.
  • She's in the camps at the low east end. I'll be a step behind you. Maybe two.
  • I'll find the words myself. Some day. Before the herds go out, anyway.
  • Sennu is in the Tolmach Camps, at the low east end of town. I'm right behind you.
  • Ennek, you only stand that straight when you've broken something. And you brought Player. Sit, both of you, and say it.
  • The Greywater. Dry since the start of summer, and you carried water so nobody would see. That is a herder's trick, and a foolish one, and I would have done the same.
  • I have been afraid of this day since I was a girl at my mother's fire. When the Greywater fails, the old springs fail with it, and the herds have nowhere left to go.
  • Thank you for standing with my son, Player. Now let me sit a while with this. Somebody must tell my mother, but not today.

docs.title: The Canyon Cairns
docs.text:
The Tolmach mark the canyon road with cairns, and Ennek wants three of them checked. Hunt 30 Dust Boggles while you are down there.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Ennek Level 15 Leads to Sure Footing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the upper cairn in The Canyon Road
  • Look at the middle cairn in The Canyon Road
  • Look at the lower cairn in The Canyon Road
  • Defeat 30 Dust Boggle in The Canyon Road

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,600 EXP
  • 300 mesos
  • Goat's Milk x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ennek
Dialogue
  • Morning, Player. You walk like someone who has done a few roads. Ever looked at the stone piles along the The Canyon Road? Those are ours. Tolmach cairns.
  • Every guide who passes adds a stone, and a cairn that is standing tells you the road is still the road. A knocked-down one tells you something else. The boggles have been knocking them down.
  • Check three cairns on The Canyon Road for me: the upper, the middle and the lower. Put a stone back if one is down. And clear 30 Dust Boggles while you are there.
  • Good. Look each cairn over closely. Add a stone of your own, too. You have walked the road; it is your road now.
  • No worries. They have stood for a hundred years, they will stand a few more days.
  • Three cairns on The Canyon Road, upper, middle and lower, and thirty Dust Boggles.
  • All three standing, with a new stone on each? Then the road is the road. My grandmother would have liked you.
  • Here, Goat's Milk from the camps. It does more for tired legs than any potion. Come and see me when you have a few more levels on you; I have a trick for ledges.

docs.title: The Greywater
docs.text:
Ennek has something to show you halfway down the South Path, at the Greywater Cleft. Go and look at the spring.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Ennek Level 50 After The Second Report Leads to Tell Your Mother, Withered Reach Bounty, Withered Reach Elites, A Withered Reach Epic

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the Greywater Cleft in The South Path

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 26,000 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ennek
Dialogue
  • Player. You walked the Far Slopes for the Old One and came back in one piece, so I'll trust you with something I've told nobody. Not my mother, not Ketta.
  • Halfway down The South Path there's a cleft in the rock we call the Greywater. Go and look at the spring there, and tell me I'm wrong about what you see. I'd go with you, but I've looked at it every trip this summer.
  • The cleft is on a small ledge halfway down The South Path, below the town gate. Damp stone, reeds. Or there were reeds.
  • Fair. It's been dry for weeks, it can be dry a few more days. Don't tell anyone I asked.
  • The Greywater Cleft, halfway down The South Path. Stand at the spring and look properly.
  • Dry. You saw it too, then. My grandmother says it ran through the driest year she ever knew, and it went dry at the start of this summer while I watched.
  • I've been carrying extra water skins up and down so the caravans don't notice. That works for a trader. It won't work for a herd.
  • Take these for your trouble. I know what comes next, and I don't like it.

docs.title: The Greywater Runs
docs.text:
Go and look at the Greywater Cleft again. Then tell Sennu, and take the news to Mabbu.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Ennek Completed with Mabbu Level 68 After The Rootdrinker Leads to The Verse

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the Greywater Cleft in The South Path
  2. Talk to Sennu

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 64,500 EXP
  • 1,360 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • Goat's Milk x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ennek
Dialogue
  • I went down this morning. I stood at the cleft for a long time. Then I came straight back up here, because I didn't trust my own eyes.
  • Go and look at the Greywater, Player. If you see what I saw, tell my mother first, and then go to my grandmother. She'll want it from you; she says I exaggerate.
  • Halfway down The South Path. The same cleft. Look at the stone.
  • Then I'll go and look again myself. And again. I might live there now.
  • The Greywater Cleft first, then Sennu, then Mabbu.
  • Wet stone and a thread of water? A thread is enough. A thread becomes a stream if nothing drinks it.
  • The herds can go back to the low springs by autumn, and the high pastures can rest. Go to my mother, Player. She has waited longer than any of us.
  • Sennu sent you running down here with a face like that? Then sit, and say it plainly.
  • Running. Thin, but running. The Greywater ran in the driest year of my girlhood, and it runs again in my old age.
  • Don't argue with me: I'm walking down to the cleft tomorrow, knees or no knees. I've been testing them on my morning walks, and they'll get me there. Lessa can scold me after.
  • Here, from my own stores, and a bowl of something hot before you go anywhere. The highlands owe you water, Player. I owe you dinner for the rest of my life.

docs.title: The Rootdrinker
docs.text:
In a hollow under the Red Ravine, a vast dead tree is drinking the highland springs dry. Ennek knows the way down: clear the Rootdrinker.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Ennek Level 66 After Follow the Springs Leads to The Greywater Runs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Rootdrinker

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 89,000 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • Elixir x3
  • +60 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ennek
Dialogue
  • I went down to the end of the ravine last night with a lamp. There's a hollow below it full of grey wood, and every root we found runs into it. In the middle stands a tree that should have died a hundred years ago and didn't.
  • The trackers have a name for it already: the Rootdrinker. It's deeply touched, Player, like the great beast on the Ash Mesa was. It won't just stand there and let you cut it.
  • I'll take you to the edge of the hollow. The fight is yours: I'm a guide, not a fighter, and I know which of us would come back. Kill it, and the water goes back where it belongs.
  • Talk to me when you're ready and I'll take you down. Bring every potion you own. When it drinks, it heals, so cut the roots that rise around it.
  • Good. Not good, but good. Take your time. The springs have waited this long.
  • The Rootdrinker, in the hollow under The Red Ravine. Talk to me when you're ready and I'll take you down.
  • You're back. You're back and it's down? I heard it from the ravine's edge, Player, like a whole forest falling at once.
  • I'm going to the Greywater at first light. Don't come yet. If it's still dry, I want to be alone for it.
  • Here, the best I have. Come and find me in a day or two, whatever the cleft says.

docs.title: Ermengarde a hide for the chronicles
A Hide for the Chronicles
docs.text:
The Aristocrat chronicles need new spines, and calf will not do this time. Ligator hide is tougher than anything Ermengarde can buy.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Ermengarde Level 32 Leads to Claw Glue

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 12 Reed Ligator Hide (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,050 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Ermengarde
Dialogue
  • The chronicles' spines are cracking, dear. All those armies and marches. Heavy reading.
  • Calf won't hold them. Ligator hide would. Tough as a librarian's opinion.
  • Bring me 12 Reed Ligator Hides from the Reed Ligators of The Reed Beds.
  • Thank you, dear. You'll be doing the chronicles a great service. A hide-ly important one.
  • Never mind. They've held this long. They're stubborn, like my brother.
  • Twelve hides from the The Reed Beds, dear. I've got the glue pot warm.
  • Oh, lovely. These will make spines to outlive us all.
  • Thank you, Player. That's one job I can finally put to bed. Bound to happen eventually.

docs.title: Claw Glue
docs.text:
Ermengarde boils lorang claws into the strongest glue in the Quarter. Then her brother Benedict must be told the new spines are on their way.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Ermengarde Level 38 After A Hide for the Chronicles

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 15 Bank Lorang Claw (taken)
  2. Talk to Benedict

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,930 EXP
  • 760 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Ermengarde
Dialogue
  • Old Master Quentin's best glue was boiled from claws. Smells dreadful. Holds forever.
  • The lorangs on the The Long Reach Banks have just the right sort. And then my brother should hear the new spines are coming, before he frets himself thin.
  • Bring 15 Bank Lorang Claws from The Long Reach Banks, then tell Benedict next door the chronicles will have new spines.
  • Tell him nicely. He's been searching again, I can hear it.
  • Then I'll use the ordinary glue. It's fine. It's just ordinary.
  • Fifteen claws, then my brother. Nicely.
  • Fifteen. Oh, the smell. Wonderful.
  • And he took it well? He sighed? That's well, for him. Thank you, dear. Stick around.
  • New spines for the chronicles? Ligator hide? She might have asked me. No, she did ask me. Twice. I said no twice.
  • Tell her thank you. Quietly. And tell her the gap on the shelf is still there. She knows which gap.

docs.title: A Touched Boar
docs.text:
A Disturbance-touched Wrack Boar has been goring the timber crews' ponies at the Strandwood Edge. Esk will split the pay: bring down the Elite and 30 of its herd.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Esk Level 22 After Dusk Ford Leads to Paid in Sinew

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 1 Elite Wrack Boar
  • Defeat 30 Wrack Boar

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,300 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • White Potion x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Esk
Dialogue
  • Player. The timber crews have work, and the pay is fair. I'd share it.
  • A boar on the Strandwood Edge has been goring their ponies. Bigger than the rest, wrong in the eyes. The kind the hunters call touched.
  • Bring down the touched Wrack Boar, an Elite, and 30 more of its herd, so the ponies can graze. Half the pay is yours.
  • The Strandwood Edge, off the Saltwood Road. Watch its feet before it charges. They always look at their feet.
  • Another time, then. The work will still be there. It usually is.
  • One touched Wrack Boar and thirty of the rest, on the Strandwood Edge.
  • Done. Cleanly, by the look of you.
  • Your half, to the copper. I counted it twice. I pay what I owe.

docs.title: Dusk Ford
docs.text:
Esk takes paid work on the merchant road. The carters' ford is crowded with Ligators and Jr. Neckis, and somebody has to clear it.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Esk Level 18 Leads to A Touched Boar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Ligator
  • Defeat 30 Jr. Necki

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,250 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +100 standing with Esk
Dialogue
  • The carters pay me to see them across Dusk Ford. I would rather they did not need me.
  • Ligators in the shallows, and the little snakes in the reeds. Clear them with me and I will split the fee.
  • Clear 30 Ligator and 30 Jr. Necki at Dusk Ford.
  • Cross by day. The ford looks best at dusk. That is not a reason to be there at dusk.
  • Another time, then.
  • The ford is on the merchant road, past the Seaward Woods.
  • Good work. Your half, and a little over. I pay my debts.

docs.title: Paid in Sinew
docs.text:
Esk owes Gwenna, who will not take her coin. Bring Esk 20 Fox Sinew, which Gwenna uses to whip her rope ends.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Esk Level 28 After A Touched Boar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Fox Sinew (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,700 EXP
  • 1,120 mesos
  • Return Scroll to Goa Harbour x3
  • Sea-Herb Salve x3
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Esk
Dialogue
  • I owe Gwenna. Not coin. She won't take coin from me for advice, and she gives me a great deal of advice.
  • She whips her rope ends with Fox Sinew. It holds where tar won't. The Strand Foxes on the Strandwood Rocks carry it, and she's running short.
  • Help me pay her. Bring me 20 Fox Sinew, and I'll take it to her myself. She'll tell me I've been foolish. I'll agree.
  • The Strandwood Rocks, past the Edge, down at the water. The foxes run in packs at dusk. Don't be there at dusk.
  • Then I'll go alone. Gwenna will tell me that's foolish too.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Fox Sinew. The foxes are on the Strandwood Rocks.
  • Twenty. Good, clean lengths.
  • Gwenna will call it a fair start. That's how she says thank you. Here. It's what I'd pay anyone for the work, and a little more, because it's you.

docs.title: A Point for Mariota
docs.text:
Mariota bet Everard he could not name the lorang's weak side. He knows it. He would rather she thought someone else did.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Everard Level 37 After Field Practice

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Bank Lorang in The Long Reach Banks
  2. Talk to Mariota

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,040 EXP
  • 740 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Everard
Dialogue
  • Mariota bet me I couldn't tell her where a lorang is weak. I can, as it happens. Underneath, when it rears.
  • But if I tell her, she'll know I know things. She keeps count, you see.
  • Find out for yourself on The Long Reach Banks: 40 Bank Lorangs. Then tell Mariota. It was your idea. Obviously.
  • If she asks whether I helped, yawn. It's very convincing.
  • Then I'll lose the bet. Losing is restful too.
  • Forty lorangs on The Long Reach Banks, then Mariota. Your idea.
  • She didn't believe you? She said "Everard told you"? How?
  • ...She's getting close. Don't tell her I said that. Here, for your trouble.
  • Underneath, when it rears? That's right. That's exactly right.
  • And you found it yourself. Of course you did. Tell Everard I'm adding a mark to my list. He'll know which list.

docs.title: Field Practice
docs.text:
Everard owes Morwen a day of field practice. He would much rather someone else did the field and he did the practice of telling her about it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Everard Level 31 Leads to A Point for Mariota

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Reed Ligator in The Reed Beds
  2. Talk to Morwen

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,280 EXP
  • 620 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Everard
Dialogue
