  • Morwen wants a report of field practice. Forty ligators in the The Reed Beds. Do you know how muddy the reed beds are?
  • Here's my idea. You do the forty. You tell her I was there in spirit. Everybody wins.
  • Defeat 40 Reed Ligators in The Reed Beds, then tell Morwen the practice is done.
  • Tell her the mud was terrible. That part's true, I'm told.
  • Fair. I'll go myself. Tomorrow. Or the day after.
  • Forty in the The Reed Beds, then Morwen. In spirit, remember.
  • She said what? "Tell him the real practice is the one he's avoiding." She would.
  • Well. Thank you anyway. Here, I had these. I'm told they're useful.
  • Everard sent you. Of course he did.
  • Tell him the reed beds are done, thank you. And tell him the real practice is the one he is avoiding. He will know what I mean.

docs.title: The Pane Ondine Hasn't Noticed
docs.text:
Faelan broke a pane on the outer path. He needs to replace it before Ondine notices it is out.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Faelan Level 23 After Past the Last Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 10 Shimmer Gel (taken)
  • Bring 10 Firefly Gel (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,877 EXP
  • 506 mesos
  • +100 standing with Faelan
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Player. Emergency. I broke a pane on the outer path. Small. Very small. Ondine hasn't noticed. Yet.
  • I can make a new one tonight, but I need gel from the lake slimes for the glow. Quickly. Before she does her rounds.
  • Bring 10 Shimmer Gel and 10 Firefly Gel from the Shimmerwater slimes.
  • You're saving my life. Well. My apprenticeship.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Gel! Quickly!
  • Done. In. Lit. She walked right past it.
  • ...She stopped. She looked at it. She said 'hm, better than the old one.' I may faint.

docs.title: A Colour Like Dusk
docs.text:
Faelan needs glimmerwing dust for coloured glass. It is a secret. From Linnet especially.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Faelan Level 12

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Glimmerwing Dust (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 428 EXP
  • 264 mesos
  • +60 standing with Faelan
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Player! Come here. Closer. Is Linnet anywhere about? No? Good.
  • I need a colour. A very particular colour. The dust off a glimmerwing's wings, in the right glass, goes the exact blue of dusk. For a lantern. For someone. Who mends homes.
  • Bring me 15 Glimmerwing Dust from the glimmerwings of the Bloomwood. And not a word to Linnet!
  • You're a true friend. The Bloomwood is out along the royal road, south and west of town.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Any dust yet? Shh! She's coming! ...No, false alarm.
  • Look at it shine. That's the one. That's the colour.
  • If this works, I'll owe you forever. If it doesn't, I'll owe you anyway.

docs.title: Faelan's First Lantern
docs.text:
The old wing has had no light in living memory. Faelan wants to make the lantern that goes in.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Faelan Level 22 After The Shelf List Before the Shelf List Leads to Corisande's Key

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Glimmerwing Dust (taken)
  2. Bring 10 Firefly Gel (taken)
  3. Talk to Ondine

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,672 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • +150 standing with Faelan
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +80 standing with Ondine
Dialogue
  • The old wing? Nobody's had a light in there for... ever? Then you'll need a lantern. A good one. Let me make it. Please.
  • I need glimmerwing dust for the glass and firefly gel for the glow. And then Ondine has to say it's good enough to leave the workshop. She's never said that. About any of mine.
  • Bring 10 Glimmerwing Dust and 10 Firefly Gel, then show the lantern to Ondine.
  • This is it. This is the one. I can feel it.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Dust and gel, then Ondine.
  • She said yes! She said 'hm, it'll do' and then she turned away and I think she was smiling!
  • My first lantern out of the workshop. Take it into the old wing. Bring it back. Or don't. Keep it.
  • Faelan made this? Hm.
  • Ondine turns the lantern in the light for a long time. 'It'll do,' she says, and turns away rather quickly.

docs.title: A Boar-Spear Head
docs.text:
Hatch is planning a hunt at the Wallow, and Ferro will forge the boar-spear head for it. Ferro wants the hog's own tusks for the crossbar that stops a charging boar: bring 30 Hog Tusks.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Ferro Level 45 After The Rare Root Leads to The Hunt at the Wallow

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Ironhide Hog Tusk (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 63,080 EXP
  • 6,750 mesos
  • +70 standing with Ferro
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Hatch came in. Second time in sixteen years Hatch has asked me for a spear. First time, I mended one. This time, I forge one. A boar spear, for whatever lives at the bottom of that marsh.
  • A boar spear has a crossbar below the blade, so the boar cannot run up the shaft at you. Iron lugs bend on a beast that size. Ironhide tusk does not. I will set tusk into iron. Most of them will crack in the quench. I need plenty.
  • 30 Ironhide Hog Tusks, from the Ironhide Hogs on the Tusk Path and in the bottoms. I will have the head ready by the time Hatch has the plan ready.
  • Big ones, if you can. Hatch's knees will not go with this spear. Somebody else's arms will. Make it worth carrying.
  • Then Hatch waits. Hatch is bad at waiting. You will hear about it.
  • (how many you carry) of 30 Ironhide Hog Tusks. Ironhide hogs, Tusk Path and the Reedwater Bottoms.
  • (Ferro works three nights with the forge roaring. Nineteen tusks crack in the quench. Eleven hold. The last two become the crossbar.)
  • There. Leaf blade, tusk lugs, socket wide enough for Hatch's old ash shaft. Heavier than it looks. It should be.
  • Its name is Hold Fast. Take it to Hatch, and tell Hatch the trade was still a good idea. Do not tell Hatch I said so.

docs.title: Names on the Tang
docs.text:
Ferro has a throwing knife back from the Gate Walk to mend, and a question nobody has ever asked out loud. Go and see Shade, the road guide who carries Ferro's knives.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Ferro Level 35

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Shade

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,610 EXP
  • 2,100 mesos
  • +70 standing with Ferro
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Shade's knives. Six of them, the best I make. Shade never misses and never brags, and never brings one back. Until now. (Ferro holds up a knife with a chipped edge.) Left on my bench with a note: Please mend, do not replace.
  • Mend. Not replace. Nobody says that about a throwing knife. It is cheaper to forge a new one, and Shade knows it. So why?
  • Go ask Shade, at the Gate Walk, why this one is to be mended. Do not say I sent you. ...Fine, say I sent you. Shade will know anyway.
  • Shade waits by the gate most evenings for travellers coming in off the road. Quiet. You will not see Shade until Shade wants you to.
  • Fine. I will mend it and not ask. Not asking is a thing I am very good at.
  • Shade. Gate Walk. Why mend, not replace.
  • Ferro wants to know why? (Shade turns one of the knives over, and shows you the tang under the grip. Two words scratched very small.) Mind the Step. Ferro names them. All of them. I found the names years ago, cleaning them.
  • You do not throw away something that has a name. Tell Ferro that. Do not tell Ferro I know the other five as well. ...Or do. Ferro will pretend not to care.
  • Shade read them. All six. Years ago. (Ferro sets the chipped knife very carefully on the anvil and looks at it for a long while.)
  • Hm. Well. Mind the Step gets a new edge, then, and keeps its name. Go on, Player. I am busy. (Ferro is not busy, and is smiling at the anvil.)

docs.title: The Iron Grate
docs.text:
A tunnel in the Deep Roads runs out under the hills to an open mouth: a way into the city that no gate guards. Ferro will forge an iron grate for the Watch to set across it, but needs red clay for the forge: bring 15 Clods of Red Earth.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Ferro Level 24 After The Deep Roads Leads to The Warm Quarry

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Clod of Red Earth (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,470 EXP
  • 2,060 mesos
  • +60 standing with Ferro
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Brindle was here. Stood where you stand, plain as a nail: a tunnel out of Low Grad comes up in the hills, open as a barn door. Anyone can walk in. Anything can. Brindle wants a grate across it before the week is out.
  • Big job. Bars as thick as your wrist, a frame bolted into old Aristocrat stone. I need to build a bigger hearth for it, and a big hearth needs good red clay to line it, or it cracks the first night.
  • 15 Clod of Red Earths. The dark stumps on the Western Descent carry the stuff about in their roots. Bring it and I start forging that night.
  • The Western Descent, up Stonefang Pass past the seeps. Dark stumps. Red earth. Do not bring me brown, I will know.
  • Then I will dig it myself and the grate will be late. Brindle will stand in my doorway saying nothing. I hate that.
  • (how many you carry) of 15 Clod of Red Earths. The dark stumps on the Western Descent.
  • Good red. Proper red. Ochre would weep. (Ferro is already kneading it into the new hearth.) Come back tomorrow. No: come back the day after. Iron does not hurry.
  • (Two days later the grate stands in the yard, black and heavy, every bar straight. Six of the Watch carry it out on poles, Brindle in front, and by nightfall it is set across the tunnel mouth in the hills.)
  • Its name is Shut Door. Scratched on the top bar, inside, where only the dark will read it. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Brown Chalk
docs.text:
Figgy has every colour of chalk except a good brown. Ochre says bog-lurcher mud dries to a fine brown: bring Figgy 10 Mud Clumps from the Seepwater Foothills.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Figgy Level 20 Leads to The Rain Rule

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Mud Clump (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,670 EXP
  • 890 mesos
  • +50 standing with Figgy
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I have red and yellow and blue and green and a pink that Jinx says looks like ham. I don't have brown. You can't draw a horse without brown. You can't draw a door. You can't draw a dog that rolled in something.
  • Mum says the bog-lurchers up the pass are made of mud, nearly, and the mud dries into a good brown if you wait. I don't like waiting. But I'll wait for brown.
  • Get me 10 Mud Clumps from the Bog-Lurchers. Please. That's me saying please. I don't say it much.
  • Up Stonefang Pass, the boggy bit, the Seepwater Foothills. Mum says. Bring them here and I'll put them in the sun.
  • Fine. I'll draw the horse purple. It'll be a weird horse. That's your fault.
  • (how many you carry) of 10 Mud Clumps! Bog-lurchers! Up the pass!
  • Ewww. They're perfect. (Figgy lines them up on the warm side of the bench to dry, and checks them every few minutes for two days. Then she rubs one on a flagstone.) BROWN!
  • A horse! A door! A dog that rolled in something! You can step on the dog for free. Once. Because you got the brown.

docs.title: The Rain Rule
docs.text:
Someone told Figgy that a drawing washed away by rain is a drawing ruined, not finished. Figgy wants the matter judged properly, by Nana Gristle, who judges everything.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Figgy Level 28 After Brown Chalk

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Nana Gristle

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,870 EXP
  • 1,680 mesos
  • +60 standing with Figgy
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • A man from a cart said my drawings get ruined when it rains. RUINED. He said it like it was sad. It's not ruined, it's finished. That's the rain rule. Everyone knows the rain rule.
  • But he was a grown-up and he said it very sure. So it has to be judged. Nana Gristle judges everything on the square. She's judged my drawings since I was little. Littler.
  • Ask Nana Gristle if the rain rule is right. On her bench. She'll say. If she says I'm wrong... she won't say I'm wrong.
  • Sunny side of the square. She's always there till the lanterns come on. Ask properly. Use the word 'rule'.
  • Fine. It's still the rule. Rules don't need judging. (Figgy frowns.) They do a bit.
  • Ask Nana Gristle! On her bench! About the rain rule!
  • Ruined? Pfah. Some cart-driver from who-knows-where told our Figgy her pictures are ruined by rain? Sit down, I'll tell you about rain. When I was a girl, half the roofs in this city leaked like baskets, and we chalked on the floors indoors, and the drips finished every one of them.
  • A picture you keep, you keep for yourself. A picture the rain takes down the gutter goes everywhere. Under every door on the square. Into the Night Market. Out the drains to the meadows. That's not ruined. That's shared.
  • Tell her the rule stands. Judged and upheld by Nana Gristle. And give her this honey cake, and tell her it's for a good day, because it is one.
  • UPHELD? Nana said upheld? That's the best word. And a honey cake? (Figgy takes one enormous bite.) Shared. Not ruined. Shared. I'm going to tell the cart man. I'm going to tell everybody.
  • You can step on any drawing you like today. Free. One step. Because it's a good day. Nana said.

docs.title: Barley Sugar for the Watch
docs.text:
Finch wants to thank Brisa for not telling Garrow about the outer pier, and Barnaby keeps barley sugar in his coat.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Finch Level 25 After Finch Wants to See One

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Barnaby

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,677 EXP
  • 550 mesos
  • +40 standing with Finch
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Brisa caught me on the outer pier twice. She said she'd tell Garrow. She never did.
  • I want to give her something. Barnaby always has barley sugar in his coat pocket. He saves it for me every voyage.
  • Ask Barnaby on the docks for a bit of barley sugar for Brisa. Don't say it's for Brisa. Say it's for me. It IS for me. To give to Brisa.
  • Don't tell Brisa it's from me. Tell her it's from me secretly.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Barnaby on the docks for barley sugar.
  • You got it! Barnaby gave you the BIG pieces. He likes you.
  • I'll leave it on her watch post. She'll know. She knows everything.
  • Barley sugar for young Finch? Ha! I'd give that boy the coat off my back. Here, take the big pieces.
  • He's the only one in this harbour who never laughed about the eyes. You tell him Barnaby says hello.

docs.title: Finch Wants to See One
docs.text:
Finch has heard every sailor's story about the deep water, and he wants to see a sea creature with his own eyes. A snapjaw tooth would do for proof.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Finch Level 21 Leads to Barley Sugar for the Watch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 15 Snapjaw
  • Bring 1 Snapjaw Tooth (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,202 EXP
  • 462 mesos
  • +40 standing with Finch
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Everybody's seen one but me. Barnaby saw eyes as big as cartwheels. Seraphine saw something she won't talk about. Kit saw a shell bigger than a door. I'm always running messages when the good stuff happens.
  • Brisa won't let me go up the Old Cut. She catches me every time. Nobody's faster than Brisa.
  • So YOU go. Up the Cut to the First Locks. There are snapjaws there. Fight 15 Snapjaws and bring me a Snapjaw Tooth. Then I'll have seen one. Sort of.
  • Pick a big tooth. A REALLY big one.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fifteen snapjaws at the First Locks, and a snapjaw tooth for Finch.
  • WHOA. Look at the size of it. That's not a fish tooth. That's a monster tooth.
  • I'm going to show Barnaby. He'll believe me. He's the only one who always believes me.

docs.title: Saving for a Bow
docs.text:
Fionn is saving for a bow and needs fox sinew for its string. Go out to the last stump on the Forest Shore, defeat 50 Strand Foxes on the Strandwood Rocks and bring him 12 Fox Sinews. Not a word to Hamish.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Fionn Level 26 After Fionn's Shortcuts

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the last stump in Goa Harbour
  2. Defeat 50 Strand Fox in Strandwood Rocks
  3. Bring 12 Fox Sinew (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,800 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Brodie's Smoked Fish x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Fionn
Dialogue
  • Can you keep a secret? A proper one? Uncle Hamish cannot, so I need someone who can.
  • I am saving for a bow. Coppers in a tin, in a place. If I can shoot, Torva will have to take me into the trees. But a bow wants a string, and a good string is fox sinew, and coppers do not buy much of that.
  • So. Go out to the last stump on the Forest Shore. That is where the fox tracks start. I know because I just know. Then take the Strandwood track off the Saltwood Road and follow them to Strandwood Rocks, bring down 50 Strand Foxes, and bring me 12 Fox Sinew. And not a word to Uncle Hamish.
  • The last stump first. Look for the clear prints in the mud, there are always good ones there. Funny, that. And not a word!
  • Fine. I will get it myself. No, I will not. I am not allowed. Forget I said anything.
  • The last stump, then the Strand Foxes on Strandwood Rocks, then (how many you carry) of 12 Fox Sinew. And you have not told Uncle Hamish? Good.
  • Sinew! Real fox sinew! That is a bowstring, that is. Three, maybe.
  • It goes in the tin with the coppers. When there is a stave too, I will have a bow, and then we will see. Here. Bethoc gave me these for a message. I am too excited to eat.

docs.title: Fionn's Shortcuts
docs.text:
Fionn will show you the quickest ways round the Cliff Stairs: the high landing, then the foot of the stairs, then the head of the Long Stair.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Fionn Level 20 Leads to Saving for a Bow

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the high landing in Goa Harbour
  2. Reach the foot of the stairs in Goa Harbour
  3. Reach the head of the Long Stair in Goa Harbour

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 900 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • White Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +100 standing with Fionn
Dialogue
  • Everyone takes the Long Stair. Everyone is slow. I know every shortcut on these cliffs, and for you, no charge. This once.
  • Try and keep up. First the high landing, by the goat path if you have the fingers for it. Then all the way down to the foot of the stairs, two landings at a time. Then back up to the head of the Long Stair. I will be waiting. I will be bored.
  • Go on, then! I will be there before you. I am always there before you.
  • Suit yourself. The stairs are very nice. Very long. Very nice.
  • The high landing, the foot of the stairs, then the head of the Long Stair. In that order. You are not lost, are you?
  • There you are! I have been here ages. Well, a bit. You are not bad, for someone who uses stairs.
  • I am not paying you a copper, they are for the tin. But Uncle Hamish gave me these for running a message, and you look like you need them more. Do not tell Gorm about the goat path.

docs.title: Follow Her Home
docs.text:
Ranger Hale has noticed Meg ranging past the far end of the Deepwood. He asks you to follow her quietly, past Breezy Hollow to the old road beyond, and make sure she comes home.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Hale Completed with Meg Level 50 After The Bluecap Mother Leads to A Dare

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach The Keep Road

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 30,000 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • The Bluecap Hollow is quiet, Player, and I have you to thank for it. But Meg has been going out past Breezy Hollow, further than the Deepwood goes, and she comes back with her mouth shut. Meg does not come back with her mouth shut.
  • She has not told me where she goes. I have been waiting for her to, and I can wait a while longer. What I will not do is let her go alone into something I have not seen.
  • Follow her, quietly. Past Breezy Hollow, along whatever road she takes beyond it. Do not stop her and do not let her see you. Just make sure she comes home.
  • Good. She leaves at first light, by the far end of Breezy Hollow. Keep well back: she has sharper ears than she lets on.
  • Then I will go myself, and she will hear me coming a mile off. Think it over.
  • Meg's road starts at the far end of Breezy Hollow, Player. Keep well back and see where it goes.
  • Oh, it's you. You know I heard you three times? Once on the Hollow path, once by the old wall, and once when you tripped over a root at the top. I waved. You did not wave back.
  • Hale sent you, didn't he. Of course he did. Fine. So now you have seen the road, the old keep at the end of it and the clearing in front of it. That is where I felt the ground shake this spring.
  • I was going to go back in there on my own. But since you followed me all that way, you might as well be useful. Talk to me again when you have caught your breath.

docs.title: A Ballad for Cecily
docs.text:
Fulke has written the ballad of the singing bank down for his pupil Cecily: the true verses first, then the good ones. Carry it to her at the Gilded Stage.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Fulke Level 26 After Pegs for the Lute

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Cecily

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • Scroll for Topwear for DEF 60% x1
  • +25 standing with Selsior
  • +130 standing with Fulke
Dialogue
  • New pegs, a new song, and a pupil who will be better than me one day. Do not tell her I said that. I have told everyone else.
  • I have written the ballad of the singing bank down for Cecily: the true verses first, then the good ones. She must decide for herself which she sings.
  • Take this Ballad of the Singing Bank to Cecily at the Gilded Stage on Theatre Row. And tell me what she thinks of it. Honestly. Watch her face, not her manners.
  • Thank you, Player. She is shy off the stage. Be gentle.
  • Another day. The song will keep.
  • Cecily, on Theatre Row. The ballad sheet.
  • She sang the true verses first, and then she asked whether the shepherd's bank was really there? Ha! Then she is learning the right thing.
  • Here, Player. For carrying the song further than I could today.
  • From Fulke? The true verses first, and then... oh, the good ones. He always writes the good ones in a different ink. ... Tell him I like it. Tell him I am going to sing it at the Stage, between the acts.

docs.title: Fulke a song from the downs
A Song from the Downs
docs.text:
A shepherd at the gate sang Fulke a song about a white bank on the downs where the bees sing all day. Is it a real place? Find the singing bank on Downs Edge.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Fulke Level 21 Leads to Pegs for the Lute

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the singing bank in Downs Edge
  • Defeat 25 Wild Bee

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,000 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Fulke
Dialogue
  • A shepherd at the gate this morning sang me a song, Player. A white bank on the downs where the bees sing all day, and the shepherds walk the long way round.
  • Every word of it sounded true. Which in my trade means very little. I should like to know if the place is real before I sing it to anyone who pays.
  • Go out to Downs Edge and find the singing bank. If the bees there sing as loud as the song says, quiet 25 Wild Bees for the shepherds.
  • Splendid! Bring me back the true verse. I will write the good ones myself.
  • Then I shall sing it as a guess. My eyebrows will tell on me.
  • The singing bank, out on Downs Edge. And twenty-five bees.
  • Real! A real white bank, and the bees real, and meaner than the song. Then the song is true. Mostly.
  • I shall sing it tonight and my eyebrows will stay exactly where they are. Here, Player, the singer's share.

docs.title: Pegs for the Lute
docs.text:
Fulke's old lute keeps slipping out of tune. He wants new pegs carved from Downs Boar tusk, which never swells in the damp.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Fulke Level 24 After A Song from the Downs Leads to A Ballad for Cecily

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Boar Tusk (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,700 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +110 standing with Fulke
Dialogue
  • Hear that? That string was in tune when I started the verse. This lute has more songs in it than I have years, but its pegs are older than both.
  • Tusk pegs, Player. Boar tusk never swells in the damp. The boars rooting up the folds on the downs have tusks to spare.
  • Bring me 10 Boar Tusks from the Downs Boars on the downs. The The Thyme Banks are thick with them.
  • Thank you! I shall write a verse about you. A true one, even.
  • Then I shall tune between every verse, and the crowd will think it is part of the act.
  • (how many you carry) of 10 Boar Tusks. The The Thyme Banks are thick with boars.
  • Look at these. White as the chalk. They will hold a note through a whole summer of rain.
  • Your verse is coming, Player. It is mostly true already.

docs.title: A Week Without Galen
docs.text:
Aurel loves his brother. Aurel would also love one week of lessons without Galen dropping by.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Aurel Level 21 After Past the Last Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Galen
  • Defeat 40 Creature of Shimmerwaters (Firefly Slime, Shimmer Slime, Water Sprite, Forest Sprite)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,202 EXP
  • 462 mesos
  • +120 standing with Aurel
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Galen
Dialogue
  • I love Galen. I do. But he comes to my classroom every day 'just to check'. The students call him Aurel's other teacher.
  • Could you... gently... suggest a week away? And could you clear the lake paths? Galen's been talking about going out there to 'see the monsters' for the students.
  • Talk to Galen, gently, and clear 40 creatures from the Shimmerwater paths so he has no reason to go.
  • Gently! He's very sensitive. He'll pretend he isn't.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Galen, gently.
  • He agreed? A whole week? He said I'm 'clearly ready'? He said that?
  • Oh. Oh no. Now I'm nervous. Good nervous.
  • Too often? Me? I just... I worry. He's my little brother.
  • ...A week. He's clearly ready. He's been ready for ages. I just like watching him teach. Don't tell him that part.

docs.title: A Second Pier
docs.text:
Garrow wants a second pier, and the council always says next year. He asks you to sound out the Harbour Master and Marisol.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Garrow Level 35 After Sea Legs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Quenna
  2. Talk to Marisol

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,920 EXP
  • 770 mesos
  • +40 standing with Garrow
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • A second pier. I've raised it at every meeting I'm not invited to. I stood outside the hall a whole meeting once with a drawing.
  • Ask the Harbour Master and Marisol what they'd say if it came to a vote. Marisol counts the votes before anyone raises a hand.
  • Ask Marisol second. She'll want to know what Quenna said.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask the Harbour Master and Marisol what they think of a second pier.
  • 'Next year, with the money from the Cut.' Both of them. The same words.
  • That's the nearest to yes I've had in sixteen years. I'm framing the drawing.
  • Garrow's pier. He's right, you know. He's always been right. It costs a fortune.
  • Tell him: next year, with the money from the Cut, if the Cut stays open. Don't tell him I smiled.
  • What did Quenna say? Next year, with the money from the Cut? Then that's what I'll say too.
  • Darling, I counted it already. Seven votes for, if the Cut pays. Tell him to keep the drawing clean.

docs.title: Carts on the Hill
docs.text:
The bluff wildcats of Baysight Hill leap onto the cargo carts coming down to the docks. Garrow wants them gone.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Garrow Level 14 Leads to Sea Legs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 35 Bluff Wildcat in Baysight Hill

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 671 EXP
  • 308 mesos
  • +40 standing with Garrow
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You came in over Baysight Hill? Then you've seen them. Wildcats. Sitting on every ledge like they own the bluff.
  • And when a cart comes down the hill, they jump on it. Into the cargo. I had a crate of Marisol's saffron opened like a parcel last week. Do you know what saffron costs, Player?
  • Clear 35 Bluff Wildcats off Baysight Hill. Then my carts can come down that hill without me holding my breath.
  • Good. I'll time the next cart. If it comes down without a cat on it, you'll know you did it right.
  • Another time, then.
  • Thirty-five wildcats on Baysight Hill. Every cat you leave is a crate I can't count.
  • Two carts down this morning and not a whisker on either. Two! I timed them. Fastest unloading this month.
  • Here's your pay, and here's my thanks, which is rarer. Now move, there's a coaster waiting.

docs.title: Sea Legs
docs.text:
Garrow teaches sea legs to anyone who works his docks: keep your footing on a moving deck, and get up fast when you go down.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Garrow Level 20 After Carts on the Hill Leads to A Second Pier

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the Heron's deck in The Docks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,908 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Skill: Sea Legs
  • +40 standing with Garrow
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You've done me two good turns on that hill. So here's one back: sea legs. Every dockhand I've ever kept learned them in a week. The rest I sent to Bryony's for an easier life.
  • A deck moves. A gangplank moves. A crate swinging off a crane moves, and so do you when it catches you. You stand loose, knees soft, weight low, and when you go down you're up again before anyone sees.
  • Go and stand on the Heron's deck at the Docks while she rides the swell, and don't grab the rail. Then come back and tell me you've got it.
  • Knees soft. Weight low. Don't grab the rail.
  • Another time, then.
  • Stand on the Heron's deck at the Docks without grabbing the rail.
  • There. You stood that deck like a bosun. I watched from the dock office.
  • That's sea legs. You'll keep your feet where other people lose theirs, and when something does knock you down you'll be up before it can do it twice.

docs.title: An Impossible Dot
docs.text:
A report puts golems on the Terraced Cuts, far ahead of the line on Gervase's map. It should be impossible. Confirm it.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Gervase Level 55 After The Quarry Village, Blank on the Map Leads to The Mason's Mark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Terraced Cuts
  2. Defeat 40 Quarry Golem in The Terraced Cuts

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 81,520 EXP
  • 1,650 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Gervase
Dialogue
  • Look at the second sheet. The marks come in along the roads, a line, a front. And then this one. Here. The quarries. Far ahead of the line.
  • It should be impossible. Things do not jump. A dot ahead of the line is a mistake, or it is the most important dot on the wall.
  • Go to The Terraced Cuts and see for yourself. If there are golems, bring down 40 Quarry Golems and count how many more there were.
  • Count! Everything. I want numbers, not shudders.
  • Then I'll pace. I'm good at pacing.
  • The Terraced Cuts. Forty golems, and a count of the rest.
  • Forty, and more standing. Then the dot is real.
  • So it does not spread like a stain. It wakes in places. I don't like that at all, Player. I don't like it, and I'm drawing it anyway.

docs.title: Blank on the Map
docs.text:
The downs are blank on Gervase's monster map. Are they quiet, or only unwatched? Walk to the Chalk Hives and mark them.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Gervase Level 25 After Comb for the Shepherds Leads to The Great Hive, An Impossible Dot

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach The Chalk Hives
  • Look at the western hive bank in The Chalk Hives
  • Look at the eastern hive bank in The Chalk Hives

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,040 EXP
  • 750 mesos
  • Orange Potion x20
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Gervase
Dialogue
  • Look at this. The downs. Blank! Not a dot. Either nothing has happened there in twenty years, or nobody has looked.
  • Gilbert says his bees have gone wild to the chalk. The shepherds say the same. Nobody has sent me a single report.
  • Go to The Chalk Hives and look at the western hive bank and the eastern hive bank. Tell me exactly what is there.
  • Exactly, mind! Not "lots of bees". How many, and where.
  • Then it stays blank. I hate it. I'll live.
  • The Chalk Hives, both banks. Exactly what is there.
  • Hives cut into the chalk, both banks, and bees by the hundred. Unwatched, then. Not quiet.
  • There. Dots. I hate them, and I'd hate a blank more. Thank you, Player. Someone should find out where they all come from.

docs.title: Gideon a bell he does not know
A Bell He Does Not Know
docs.text:
From his perch Gideon knows every bell in Selsior, but lately a new one clanks from the north. He thinks it is the shepherd's hut on the Waystone Meadows. Find out, and see why it rings.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Gideon Level 10 After Word for Clement Leads to Down the Ladder

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the shepherd's hut in The Waystone Meadows
  • Defeat 30 Ribbon Pig

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 480 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Gideon
Dialogue
  • Listen. No, listen. There. Clank, clank, from the north, when the wind is right. I know every bell in this city, Player, and that is not one of them.
  • Up the World Tree Road, past the hedges, there is a shepherd's hut on the The Waystone Meadows. A hut has a bell for the flock. I would bet my old tabard on it.
  • Go to the shepherd's hut on the The Waystone Meadows and see what the shepherd rings it for. If it is what I think, take care of it: 30 Ribbon Pigs should do.
  • Ha! A herald's errand. Come back and tell me what you heard.
  • Another time. The bell will keep clanking, I expect.
  • The hut on the The Waystone Meadows, and whatever is bothering the flock. Thirty pigs, I would guess.
  • Pigs among the flock, ringing her out every hour! Ha! I knew it was a shepherd's bell. Sixty years of ears, Player.
  • Quieter now, too. I shall miss it a little. A new bell is a rare thing at my age.

docs.title: Down the Ladder
docs.text:
Once a month Gideon climbs down to sit with Aldous at the Royal Vault when it closes. His knees are complaining. Tell Aldous he is coming, so the old keeper keeps the bench warm.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Gideon Level 14 After A Bell He Does Not Know

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Aldous

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 450 EXP
  • 280 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Gideon
Dialogue
  • It is the end of the month, Player, and at the end of the month I go down this ladder and walk to the palace to sit with Aldous when the vault closes. He does not climb ladders. Counts twice and smiles once, that man.
  • My knees have opinions about it this month. I shall go anyway. But I would like him to know I am coming slowly, so he does not count the vault a third time waiting.
  • Go to the Palace and tell Aldous that Gideon is on his way. Slowly. With a story.
  • Ha! Tell him the story is about the harvest fair of the year the cart fell in the river. He will know.
  • Then I shall shout it from the window. He will not hear it from the vault. Ha!
  • The Royal Vault, under the palace. Aldous. Tell him I am coming.
  • He smiled? Once? Ha! That is his whole allowance for the day. He must be pleased.
  • Thank you, Player. Forty years on the steps, and the best part of it was the friends who stood at the bottom.
  • Gideon is coming down? Slowly, with a story. Yes, that is Gideon. I shall count the vault once more and then wait on the bench. Thank you for telling me, Player.

docs.title: Word for Clement
docs.text:
Gideon heard Clement rehearse to the pigeons and thinks it was splendid. He is far too proud to climb down and say so. Tell Clement for him.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Gideon Level 6 Leads to Post the Notice, A Bell He Does Not Know

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Clement

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 45 EXP
  • 120 mesos
  • Red Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Gideon
Dialogue
  • Ha! Player, you have young knees. Did you hear the herald this morning? On the roofs, rehearsing to the pigeons? I did. Every word.
  • It was splendid. Go down and tell Clement so. Not from me, mind! Just... tell him an old man in a window was heard to say it was splendid.
  • Off you go. Mind the third rung on the way down. And the eighth.
  • No? Ha! Then I shall shout it from the window, and the whole plaza can hear.
  • He will be by the palace steps, looking nervous. Go on.
  • He blushed? Ha! Good. Blushing is the best sign there is. I blushed for twenty years on those steps.
  • Here, take these for your trouble. And come back up. I have more stories, and the pigeons have heard them all.
  • An old man in a window said it was splendid? ... He climbed down his whole ladder in his voice to say that. Thank you, Player. Tell him... no. I will tell him myself, on Thursday.

docs.title: Gilbert a swarm on the bell
A Swarm on the Great Bell
docs.text:
One of Gilbert's swarms has left the roof and settled on the Great Bell in the Royal Plaza. Thin the angry hives at the Chalk Hives that keep calling them out, look at the swarm, and tell Baldwin, who lights the plaza lamps, to keep his flame away from it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Gilbert Level 28 After Stingers for the Hives

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Chalk Hive Bee in The Chalk Hives
  2. Reach the Great Bell in Royal Plaza
  3. Talk to Baldwin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,800 EXP
  • 560 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Gilbert
Dialogue
  • Oh dear. Oh dear, hmm. A swarm left my roof this morning and settled, of all places, on the Great Bell. The guards are not amused.
  • I can coax them down, but not while the hives in the chalk keep stirring them. Clear 40 Chalk Hive Bees at the The Chalk Hives, go and look at my swarm on the bell, and then ask Baldwin to keep his lamp-flame away from it tonight. Smoke will only madden them.
  • Thank you, thank you. I'll fetch my basket and my calmest hum.
  • Hmm. Then I'll stand under the bell and hope.
  • Forty bees at the Chalk Hives, a look at the Great Bell, then Baldwin.
  • They came down into my basket at dusk, quiet as you like. Baldwin lit the far side of the plaza first, bless him.
  • Hmm. Thank you, Player. Here, and a candle of my best wax, in spirit if not in your bag.
  • Gilbert's bees on the bell? I saw them. Didn't like the look of the moths round them either.
  • Tell him I'll light the far side of the plaza first tonight and leave the bell in the dark till they're down. He undercharges me for oil. I owe him that and more.

docs.title: Comb for the Shepherds
docs.text:
Gilbert sent a frame of comb to the shepherds' hives on the downs and asked how their bees fare. The hives stand empty: the bees have gone wild into the chalk. Bring him pieces of their wild comb.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Gilbert Level 23 After Where the Horse Sweats Leads to Blank on the Map, Stingers for the Hives

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Wild Comb (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,910 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Gilbert
Dialogue
  • Hmm. Player, could you... I sent a frame of comb out to the shepherds' hives on the downs, to ask after their bees. The shepherd sent it back with one line: the hives are empty.
  • Empty. Not dead. Gone. Gone wild into the chalk banks, I think, with the Wild Bees. Bring me 10 pieces of Wild Comb from them. I need to see what they are building out there.
  • Out the Tree Gate and east onto the downs. Move slowly near them. Hum, if you can. It sometimes helps. Not lately, but sometimes.
  • Of course. Hmm. Another time.
  • Ten pieces of wild comb, Player. You have (how many you carry).
  • (He holds a piece to the light and stops humming.) Look at the cells. Deep, crooked, built in a hurry. Bees build like that before a long winter. Or a war.
  • Whatever has my rooftop on edge has the downs on edge too, only worse. Thank you, Player. I'll pass this on to anyone who will listen.

docs.title: Stingers for the Hives
docs.text:
Gilbert wants to compare the stingers of the wild bees on the downs with those of his own hives, to see whether they are the same bees at heart.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Gilbert Level 25 After Comb for the Shepherds Leads to A Swarm on the Great Bell

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Bee Stinger (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,690 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Gilbert
Dialogue
  • Hmm. I've been stung more this year than in the ten before it, so I've had plenty of my own bees' stingers to look at. Plenty.
  • I want to lay theirs beside mine: the wild ones on the downs. Bring me 15 Bee Stingers. Gently, if you can. Hmm. Well. As gently as one can.
  • Downs Edge and the Thyme Banks are thick with them. Mind your neck.
  • Hmm. Yes. I'd not want to be stung for my curiosity either.
  • Fifteen wild bee stingers. You have (how many you carry) so far.
  • Longer than my bees', and barbed further down. The same bees, I think, only angrier, as if they'd grown into their temper.
  • My bees aren't turning into something else, then. They're answering something. Hmm. That's both better and worse. Take this, with thanks.

docs.title: A Calm Garden
docs.text:
Old Gerold planted lemon balm round the hives to keep the bees kind. Gather lemon balm on the Downs and thin the wild bees of the Thyme Banks.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Godwin Level 29 After The Great Hive

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Gather 12 Lemon Balm Flower
  • Defeat 30 Wild Bee in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,400 EXP
  • 580 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Godwin
Dialogue
  • My old master Gerold planted lemon balm round the hives. 'Bees remember a kind smell,' he used to say.
  • Gather 12 Lemon Balm Flowers on the Downs for the rose walk, and thin the Wild Bees on The Thyme Banks, 30 of them. Perhaps the rest will remember their manners.
  • Pick the leaves young. Old balm is all stalk and opinion.
  • Another day, then. The balm will keep growing.
  • Twelve lemon balm, and the bees of The Thyme Banks. Gently, gently.
  • There. Smell that? ...Mm.
  • Only one sting this morning. One! A rose remembers the hand that pruned it, Player, and so will I.

docs.title: Godwin a cutting from the roots
A Cutting from the Roots
docs.text:
Godwin wants something green from the World Tree's own ground for his kingdom border. Look over the Tree's outermost root in the Rootlands, then thin out the Dark Stumps there.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Godwin Level 15

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the Tree's outermost root in The Rootlands
  2. Defeat 20 Dark Stump

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,250 EXP
  • 300 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Godwin
Dialogue
  • Ah... a visitor who walks the World Tree Road, by the look of the boots. Sit, if you like. I have a bed below the terrace, the kingdom border: a flower from every town.
  • But nothing in it grows from the Tree's own ground. A cutting from where the roots break the turf... that would please an old man.
  • Go to the Tree's outermost root in The Rootlands and look it over for anything green (press Up there). Then thin out 20 Dark Stumps; they guard that ground jealously.
  • Slowly, now. A cutting taken in a hurry sulks for a year.
  • Weeds come to those who wait. So do cuttings.
  • The outermost root of the Tree, in The Rootlands. Then the Dark Stumps. No hurry. Well. Some hurry.
  • Root-moss, with a little white star of a flower in it. In fifty-eight summers I have never seen its like.
  • It shall go at the head of the border, above all the towns. The Tree was here before any of them, after all. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: The Great Hive
docs.text:
Godwin has been stung four times since spring. Follow the Chalk Hive bees to where they all fly: the great hive at the Hive Hollow's mouth.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Godwin Level 27 After Blank on the Map Leads to Queen of the Downs, A Calm Garden

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Chalk Hive Bee
  2. Reach the Hive Hollow's mouth in The Chalk Hives

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,600 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Orange Potion x20
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Godwin
  • Unlocks boss.queen_amberwing
Dialogue
  • Four stings since spring, Player. Once on the eyelid. In fifty-eight summers the rose walk never stung me once.
  • Gervase has marked the The Chalk Hives on his map, I hear. Bees fly home. Somewhere out there is the hive our palace bees learned their temper from.
  • Go through the Chalk Hive Bees, 30 of them, and see where they all fly. The great hive. I only want to know where it is.
  • Take care. A bee stings once; a hive stings all summer.
  • I understand. I would not walk into a hive either, with my knees.
  • Follow the Chalk Hive Bees. They all fly the same way, toward the Hive Hollow.
  • A hollow in the chalk, walled with old comb, and something humming in it bigger than a calf? ...Well. That explains the temper.
  • Tell Edric; this is no work for a gardener's smoke-pot. And thank you. At last I have an answer for young Alaric.

docs.title: Below the Anvil
docs.text:
Gorm promised Iska a new stair to the far cove before the race. His crews will not work the lowest landings after dark.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Gorm Level 40 After The Wake Leads to The Chewed Ropes, The Last Flights, The Hardest Step

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Clear Below the Anvil
  2. Talk to Ulric

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 16,000 EXP
  • 1,600 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Gorm
Dialogue
  • The Anvil cracked in the spring frost. The flight below it has to be recut, and my crews will not stay past dark down there.
  • One night. Stand guard on the Saltface below the Anvil while we work, and I will have that flight cut by dawn. Then take a stone to Ulric for me. He will know what it is.
  • Guard Gorm's crew through a night's work below the Anvil, then show Ulric the scratched stone.
  • Stone does not wait for courage. Neither do I.
  • Then the stair stays half cut.
  • One night below the Anvil. Then Ulric.
  • The flight is cut. Sharper on the seaward side, the way I like them now.
  • And Ulric said claws. From below. I did not need him to say it. I needed somebody to.
  • Let me see. Hm. Four cuts, deep, side by side. Not a pick. Not a chisel.
  • Claws. And they came from below, see how the lip is pushed up? Something climbed. Tell Gorm I said so. He will pretend he did not know.

docs.title: The Far Cove Stair
docs.text:
Gorm is behind on the far cove stair. Clear 60 Shore Crabs off the Saltface below it, then ask Hamish to haul Gorm's cut stone up in his lift.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Gorm Level 34 Leads to The Last Flights

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 60 Shore Crab in The Saltface
  2. Talk to Hamish

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,000 EXP
  • 1,400 mesos
  • Steamed Crab x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Gorm
Dialogue
  • The stair I promised Iska, down to the far cove. It is going badly. Do not repeat that. The crabs have come up onto the face below it, and my crew will not set stone with claws round their ankles.
  • Clear 60 Shore Crabs off The Saltface. Then there is the cut stone on the quay. It wants hauling to the clifftop, and there is only one thing on these cliffs that hauls. Go and ask Hamish for his basket. For me. Once.
  • The Saltface is down the steep way off the Gullwalk. And when you see Hamish, say it is only this once. Say it twice if you have to.
  • Fine. I will carry the stone up myself, block by block. It will be good for me. That is what I will tell myself.
  • Sixty Shore Crabs on The Saltface first. Then Hamish. Only this once, mind.
  • Gorm wants my lift? Gorm? For his stone? Say that again, slowly, so I can remember it for the rest of my life.
  • Of course he can have it. Tell him the basket says hello. Tell him a lift would have had his whole stair down by now. No, tell him I said it gently. He will not believe you, but tell him.
  • You told him only this once? And what did he say? No. Do not tell me. I can see it on your face.
  • The crabs are off the face, at least, and the stone goes up tomorrow. Here, for your trouble. If anyone asks, I carried every block.

docs.title: The Last Flights
docs.text:
The far cove stair's last flights run down past the Wrack Ledges. Thin the Saltgulls there and the Sea Newts on the Saltface, then take Gorm's word to Kestra about a handrope.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Gorm Level 44 After The Far Cove Stair, Below the Anvil

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 50 Saltgull in The Wrack Ledges
  2. Defeat 30 Sea Newt in The Saltface
  3. Talk to Kestra

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 26,500 EXP
  • 1,800 mesos
  • Saltface Helm x1
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Gorm
Dialogue
  • The Anvil is cut, or near enough, and Ulric is pleased. He shows it by saying nothing. Now the last flights, down past the ledges toward the cove.
  • The gulls off the Wrack Ledges dive at my riggers as if we owed them money. And the newts come up the face at dusk. Every dusk.
  • Thin the Saltgulls on The Wrack Ledges, 50 of them, and 30 Sea Newts on The Saltface. Then go to Kestra and tell her I want a handrope down the last flights. And tell her to wear a line while she strings it.
  • Gulls, then newts, then Kestra. She will not wear the line. Tell her anyway. I like it said.
  • Then I will string the handrope myself. Badly. Kestra will laugh for a month.
  • Fifty Saltgulls on The Wrack Ledges, thirty Sea Newts on The Saltface, then Kestra. And the line. Mention the line.
  • A handrope down the last flights? Finally. I have had the rope spliced a week, waiting for him to ask.
  • A line? Tell him I will wear one the day he rides the lift. He will know what that means. The rope will be up by tomorrow night.
  • The day I ride the lift. Hmph. Then she will never wear one, and I will shout at her for the rest of my life.
  • The gulls are quieter, the face is clear at dusk, and the handrope goes up tomorrow. Three flights left. Take this. Stone falls on the Saltface, and I would like your head to stay the shape it is.

docs.title: The Cistern Count
docs.text:
Gorra keeps the stone cisterns that water the terraces, and it is time for her count. Check the four cisterns on the west terraces for her.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Gorra Level 21 Leads to The Founders' Trickle

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the Founders' Cistern in Midbarium
  • Look at the upper west cistern in Midbarium
  • Look at the middle cistern in Midbarium
  • Look at the lower cistern in Midbarium

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,000 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Goat's Milk x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Gorra
Dialogue
  • Water, Player. Everyone thinks about it when there is none. I think about it every day, so they do not have to. It is my count day, and I am short a pair of legs.
  • Four cisterns on the west terraces. Lid off, look in, measure the line on the stone, lid on. I scratch the numbers on the wall of my cistern house. Old Marn did it before me, and I have not missed a count in eighteen years.
  • Check the four cisterns on the west terraces: the Founders' Cistern on the top terrace, then the upper, middle and lower ones. Look each one over and read me the line.
  • Good. The line is the dark mark on the stone. Do not lean in. People lean in.
  • Then I count alone and it takes till dark. Fine. It usually does.
  • The Founders' Cistern, then the upper, middle and lower cisterns on the west terraces.
  • Upper, middle, lower. Good, good, a finger down. That is the summer. And the Founders'?
  • Lower than last count. A finger's depth more than the others. Hm. That is what I thought you would say. No, it is nothing. Old stone. I will look at it myself.
  • Here, milk from Yarrek's goats. We share the terrace water with his family, and they share this with me. Do not mention the Founders' to Dorrek. He worries, and then he builds things.

docs.title: The Founders' Trickle
docs.text:
Gorra can hear water running somewhere under the Founders' Cistern. Follow the trickle down the terraces and bring her 20 Swollen Wood to seal the leak.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Gorra Level 60 After The Cistern Count

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the foot of the Founders' Cistern in Midbarium
  • Look at the seep behind the old wall in Midbarium
  • Bring 20 Swollen Wood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 73,000 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Gorra
Dialogue
  • The Founders' Cistern loses a finger's depth every few nights. I've counted it on the wall of my cistern house all summer, and I've not told Dorrek how much it frightens me. Don't you either.
  • Put your ear to the stone at night and you can hear it: a trickle, somewhere deep in the rock. Water doesn't go nowhere. It goes somewhere, and I want to know where.
  • Follow it for me. Start at the foot of the Founders' Cistern, listen, then find where it comes out lower down. And bring me 20 Swollen Wood off the grey stumps of the Reach: that wood drinks and swells, and a wet crack packed with it seals tighter than mortar.
  • The Founders' Cistern is the oldest on the upper terrace, at the west end. Mind the lip. It's slippery when it's leaking, which is always.
  • Fine. I'll keep counting. Counting is what I'm good at.
  • The foot of the Founders' Cistern, the seep below it, and (how many you carry) of 20 Swollen Wood.
  • A seep behind the old wall below, wet stone and moss? That's where it's going: straight down through the rock and out above the Kragvar Quarter.
  • And twenty pieces of the grey wood, good. I'll pack the crack from below where the water comes out and from above where it goes in, and then I'll count again. If it holds a week, I'll tell Dorrek. If it holds a month, I'll tell him I was worried.
  • Take these, and thank you. You've given this town back a finger of water every few nights, and up here that's worth more than coin.

docs.title: The Grand Swordmaster's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Swordmaster of level 120 to the top of the sword's road. Prove it once more in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 400 of its monsters.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Rhys Level 120 Job Swordmaster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 400 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 180,000 EXP
  • Advance to Grand Swordmaster

Placeholder

A stand-in until the higher fields exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the region of level 120 when that is built (WORLD M5).

Dialogue
  • Player. Level one hundred and twenty. I have trained a great many Swordmasters in this yard, and few come back to ask for more.
  • The Grand Swordmaster is not a stronger Swordmaster. He is one who no longer waits for the enemy's blow to begin his own, and who can turn it aside while doing so.
  • One last trial, in the place where you began it: defeat 400 of the Greenwood Clearing's Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps without once letting your rhythm break.
  • Then go. Four hundred is a lot of cuts, so make each one lead into the next.
  • The last step is the longest. Come back when you are ready for it.
  • Four hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player, on the royal road outside the city. Do not let the rhythm break.
  • Four hundred. I watched your cuts from the first to the last, and I could not find the seam between them.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Grand Swordmaster.
  • Blade Tempest, Perfect Counter and Crescent Divide are yours now. Chain them into the Swordmaster's cuts, or fight each by itself: the sword has no wrong way. Use them well.

docs.title: Wood the Sea Gave Back
docs.text:
Gunna wants sound driftwood, the part of a Driftstump the sea has not rotted, from the Strandwood, past where the crews cut. Bring her 25 pieces.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Gunna Level 30 Leads to Gunna's Question

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Sound Driftwood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,700 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +25 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Gunna
Dialogue
  • You go out along the Strandwood, beyond the crews' edge. What do you think I need from there?
  • No? Wood. But not any wood. Wood the forest grew and the sea took and gave back again, and that did not rot in between. The Driftstumps carry a piece of it, deep inside.
  • Bring me 25 Sound Driftwood. Grey, dense, sound right through. Why that wood and no other? Ask me again when you bring it.
  • Twenty-five. Not twenty-four. Does that seem strange to you?
  • Another time, then. The wood has waited this long.
  • (how many you carry) pieces. I asked for twenty-five. Did you think I would not count?
  • Good. Feel the weight of it. What does that tell you?
  • I said I would tell you why this wood. I find I would rather you kept the question. It will do you more good than the answer. Here, for your trouble.

docs.title: Gunna's Question
docs.text:
Gunna wants you to ask Dunmor and then Tarran how they know a lantern is failing, and to bring her 20 Saltgull Feathers for her finest brushes.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Gunna Level 48 After Wood the Sea Gave Back

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Dunmor
  2. Talk to Tarran
  3. Bring 20 Saltgull Feather (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,500 EXP
  • 1,900 mesos
  • Elixir x2
  • +35 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Gunna
Dialogue
  • I have a question for you to carry. Not to answer. To carry.
  • Go to Dunmor, who lights the quay. Ask him how he knows a lantern is failing before anyone else can see it. Then ask Tarran the same thing.
  • And the long feathers of the Saltgulls on The Wrack Ledges make the finest brush there is. Bring me 20 Saltgull Feathers. Why does the finest brush matter for a light? You may carry that question too.
  • Dunmor first. Then Tarran. The order matters. Does it? We shall see.
  • Questions keep. That is the best thing about them.
  • Dunmor, then Tarran, then the feathers. You have (how many you carry) of 20.
  • Dunmor looks. Tarran takes it apart. Two answers, and both of them true.
  • Which of them would you teach, if you had one pupil and one craft and no book? Do not answer. I was asking myself.
  • The feathers are good. Long and straight. Here, for your carrying. And Player, if you ever find an answer to my question, bring it to me before you bring it to him.
  • Gunna asked that? How I know?
  • I don't know how I know. I light them every dusk and put them out every dawn, twenty-two years now. You get to know a thing you look at every day. That's all. Tell her that's all.
  • How do I know a lantern's failing? Easy. It goes out.
  • No, wait, that's a terrible answer. Tell her I'd take it apart and find out. Is that the right answer? Tell her that one.

docs.title: Gytha a stain she cannot place
A Stain She Cannot Place
docs.text:
Gytha has found a stain on the linen of houses near the gratings that she cannot scrub out or name. She wants samples of whatever lives in the cisterns to compare.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Gytha Level 26 After The Cistern Sluice Leads to Where He Goes at Dawn

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Cistern Bubble (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,780 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Gytha
Dialogue
  • I know every stain in the old quarters, Player. Wine, grass, ink, blood, lies. This one I don't know. Grey, slick, smells of old stone, and it comes back after the wash.
  • It's only on linen from the houses by the gratings. Something down in the The Cisterns leaves it, I'd bet my coppers. Bring me 10 Cistern Bubbles and I'll know my enemy.
  • Down the grating in Steps Lane, then the cisterns. Don't drip on my sheets when you come back.
  • Then I'll keep scrubbing and swearing.
  • Ten cistern bubbles, Player. You've got (how many you carry).
  • (She rubs one between finger and thumb, sniffs it, and nods grimly.) That's it. That's my stain. Coming up through the gratings with the damp.
  • Lye and a cold rinse, then. Now I know what I'm fighting, I'll win. Here, for your trouble.

docs.title: Gytha where he goes at dawn
Where He Goes at Dawn
docs.text:
The old broom handle is missing from the corner of Gytha's yard, and Hodge comes home at breakfast with roof moss on his knees. She asks you to ask her parents what they know, then clear the drains below the lanes he runs.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Gytha Level 28 After A Stain She Cannot Place

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Winifred
  2. Talk to Simkin
  3. Defeat 30 Drain rats (Drain Rat, Black Drain Rat)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,730 EXP
  • 560 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Gytha
Dialogue
  • The old broom handle's gone from my yard. Nobody steals a broom handle. And Hodge comes to breakfast with moss on his knees and a look like butter wouldn't melt.
  • My mother sees everything and says nothing, and my father reads feet. Ask them both what my son does at dawn. Then, since you're going below anyway, clear 30 drain rats under the lanes he runs. I want those lanes safe, roof or no roof.
  • Mother's on her step, Father's at his bench. They'll talk to you. They won't talk to me.
  • Then I'll go on not knowing. I'm good at that.
  • Winifred, then Simkin, then thirty rats under the lanes.
  • So. Recruit's heels, says Father. A boy on the ridge every dawn with something long over his shoulder, says Mother. And neither of them told me.
  • (She is quiet for a long moment.) I'll get up early tomorrow, then. Before the coppers. I'll see it for myself before I decide anything. Thank you, Player. Truly.
  • Ah. She sent you, did she? Then the story's reached that part.
  • I sleep very little, dearie. Most dawns a small figure crosses the ridge opposite my window with something long over its shoulder. Tell her that. Tell her I waited to see how it would go.
  • What does the boy do at dawn? I don't know. I know his feet.
  • Tile grit, roof moss, and heels worn like a recruit's from planting the back foot. I stitch them twice. Tell her that, and tell her I'm sorry I didn't say.

docs.title: A Flower from the Bloomwood
docs.text:
There is a flower in a corner of the Bloomwood that Halcy can no longer safely reach.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Halcy Level 14

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the corner of the Bloomwood in The Bloomwood, South

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 671 EXP
  • 308 mesos
  • Glade-Flower Garland x1
  • +60 standing with Halcy
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • There's a flower I used to gather, in a corner of the Bloomwood, out where the woods thin toward the plain.
  • I can't go there safely any more. Would you fetch one? Only one.
  • Pick the flower in the corner of the Bloomwood, on the high ledge of its southern stretch (examine it).
  • Thank you, Player.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The Bloomwood's southern stretch. The high ledge.
  • Oh. Yes. That's the one.
  • Here. I wove you a garland. No, take it. It's yours.

docs.title: A Newcomer Who Is Struggling
docs.text:
Halcy helps newer arrivals find their way. One is struggling, and Halcy thinks Niv could help.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Halcy Level 30 After Standing Quietly, Past the Last Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Niv
  • Defeat 50 Creature of Shimmerwaters (Firefly Slime, Shimmer Slime, Water Sprite, Forest Sprite)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,292 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • +150 standing with Halcy
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +80 standing with Niv
Dialogue
  • Someone new has come to the glade. Shy. Overwhelmed by the crowds. I know someone who understands that.
  • Ask Niv to stand with them a while? And keep the lake paths clear: they walk there in the evenings to be alone.
  • Ask Niv to keep the newcomer company, and clear 50 creatures from the Shimmerwater paths.
  • Thank you, Player.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Niv, and the lake paths.
  • Niv stood with them for an hour. Neither of them said a word.
  • They came to market this morning. Just for a minute. That's a start.
  • ...Someone shy? New?
  • ...I'll stand with them. Quiet standing is the best kind.

docs.title: The Edge Line
docs.text:
Haldor's crews cut only at the forest edge now. Stand at the last stump to see where the line is, then clear 50 monsters from Strandwood Edge.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Haldor Level 22 Leads to Word for Tamsin

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the last stump in Goa Harbour
  2. Defeat 50 monsters in Strandwood Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,300 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • Brodie's Smoked Fish x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Haldor
Dialogue
  • You'll have heard we've pulled the crews back. Twice this year. I'll not send a cutter where I can't hear him shout, and that's the end of it.
  • So we cut the edge, and the edge is crowded. Boars in the weed, stumps that walk. A cutter can't swing true for watching his back.
  • Go and stand at the last stump, at the far end of this shore, and listen. That's as far as we cut now. Then clear 50 monsters from Strandwood Edge, where the crews are working.
  • The Strandwood track leaves the Saltwood Road. Mind the crews out there. If one of them shouts, go to the shout.
  • Aye. The trees will wait. They're good at it.
  • The last stump first, so you know where the line is. Then 50 of whatever's on Strandwood Edge.
  • Merrin says you went through the boars like a felling wedge. She says it the way she says most things, as if she'd have done it faster.
  • Here. For the crews' sake as much as mine. They'll sleep better with the edge thinned, and so will I.

docs.title: The Timber Carts
docs.text:
Haldor's timber carts use the Saltwood Road. Walking stumps and grave-grey mushrooms have taken to standing in it.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Haldor Level 16

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Dark Stump
  • Defeat 25 Zombie Mushroom

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 900 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +100 standing with Haldor
Dialogue
  • Every cart that goes up the Saltwood Road to the downs comes back with a story now. A stump in the ruts that was not there yesterday. Mushrooms that grin.
  • I thank every tree before it falls. I do not thank the ones that walk.
  • Clear 30 Dark Stump and 25 Zombie Mushroom on Saltwood Road.
  • Go carefully. The road is sunk deep under the pines and the light goes early.
  • Aye. The carts will wait.
  • The road runs from Gull Heath up under the pines.
  • The carters say the ruts are their own again. I will tell the crews.

docs.title: Word for Tamsin
docs.text:
Haldor will not send a crew into the deep forest for Tamsin's keel. Bring him 25 Sound Driftwood to send her instead, and tell Tamsin why.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Haldor Level 30 After The Edge Line

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 25 Sound Driftwood (taken)
  • Talk to Tamsin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,600 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x5
  • Return Scroll to Goa Harbour x2
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Haldor
Dialogue
  • Tamsin was at the raft landing again this morning. Same words as last time: deep-forest timber, for the Gap Runner's keel. She thinks I've gone soft.
  • I'll not send a crew in for a keel. But I'd not have her think I don't care whether she wins. The soundest wood on this shore is the heart of a Driftstump: grey, dense, and the sea has seasoned it already.
  • Bring me 25 Sound Driftwood. It goes round on the next raft. And go to Tamsin at the quay yard: tell her it's coming, and tell her why the crews stay at the edge. She'll listen to you longer than she listens to me.
  • The Driftstumps are on Strandwood Edge and Strandwood Rocks. Tamsin's yard is on the Inlet Quay. She'll be under a hull, most likely, or shouting at one.
  • Aye. I'd not want to carry that message either.
  • (how many you carry) of 25 Sound Driftwood so far. And a word with Tamsin at the quay yard, if you've not had it yet.
  • Driftwood. He's sending me driftwood, for pins and trenails. It'll be sound, he has never sent me a bad stick in his life, and that's what makes it so maddening. Tell him I heard why. Tell him I still want my tree.
  • She still wants her tree. Aye, she will. She'll want it on the morning of the race and the morning after.
  • This goes round on the slack. Thank you, Player. I'd sooner she was angry with me than sorry for a cutter.

docs.title: Hale's Boarwood Bounty
docs.text:
Ranger Hale pays a bounty for keeping the Boarwood's herd back from the farms: defeat 40 boars in the Boarwood. He will pay it again, any time.

Town Kaldemor Category Repeatable Given by Hale Level 28 After Stilebrook Farm

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Boarwood boars (Hedge Boar, Rooting Piglet, Tusker)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,500 EXP
  • 1,500 mesos

The first time you complete it instead: 5,000 EXP, 2,500 mesos, +30 standing with Kaldemor

Dialogue
  • The Boarwood fills up again as fast as you empty it, Player. Every night there are fresh tracks at the stile.
  • I have been thinking about Gnarltusk since you came back from that yard. Those boars did not choose to come up to our farms. Nothing that size leaves good woods for a hedge and a turnip field. They ran from something deeper in.
  • I do not know what yet. But I mean to find out, and I expect I will need you when I do. Meanwhile the herd still needs thinning.
  • Same terms as the meadow: 40 boars of the Boarwood, any size, and I pay it again whenever you bring me another forty. The first time is a little more.
  • Good. Hedge Boars, piglets or Tuskers, they all count. The tracker keeps the tally.
  • Another time. The boars will not be going anywhere.
  • Forty of the Boarwood's boars, Player. Any size counts.
  • Forty. Elsie will have her cows back on the far pasture yet.
  • Here is your bounty. Come back whenever the tracks at the stile get fresh again.

docs.title: Hale's Bounty
docs.text:
Ranger Hale pays a bounty for thinning out the meadow: defeat 30 of the field's monsters. He will pay it again, any time.

Town Kaldemor Category Repeatable Given by Hale Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Field monsters (Snail, Blue Snail, Red Snail)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 100 EXP
  • 200 mesos

The first time you complete it instead: 150 EXP, 300 mesos, +30 standing with Kaldemor

Dialogue
  • The meadow is never empty for long, Player. If you have the stomach, I pay a bounty: 30 monsters of the field, snails of any colour, and I pay it again whenever you bring me another thirty. The first time is a little more.
  • Good. The field is east of the town square. Count them as you go: the tracker does it for you.
  • Another time, then. The snails will wait.
  • Thirty of the field's monsters, Player. Snails of any colour count.
  • Thirty! The meadow can breathe again.
  • Here is your bounty. Come back for another round whenever the snails get bold.

docs.title: Back on the Bridge
docs.text:
Hallek is ready to go back to work on the far canyon bridge, if the gnawers are fewer. Hunt 60 Cliff Gnawers at the Far Anchor.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Hallek Level 40 After What Hallek Did Not See

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Cliff Gnawer in The Far Anchor

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 16,500 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • Climber's Gloves x1
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Hallek
Dialogue
  • Vosk says I can go back out on the far bridge. The leg is healed. Lessa says so, and she does not say things she does not mean. I am the one who is not sure.
  • Here is what I want. Go out to The Far Anchor before me and clear 60 Cliff Gnawers from under the anchor ledge. Then I go back out and hang under those planks again, and I do not look down.
  • Thank you. I will be sharpening my chisels and pretending I am not waiting.
  • Then I keep cutting stone in the quarter. It does not bite.
  • Sixty Cliff Gnawers at The Far Anchor, under the anchor ledge.
  • You cleared them? Then I go out tomorrow. Before I think about it too long.
  • Take these gloves. Climber's gloves, padded for rope. I had them made for my first day back, and I find I do not need new gloves. I need to go. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: What Hallek Did Not See
docs.text:
Hallek, the mason bitten on the far canyon bridge this spring, will tell what bit him, or what little there was to see. Take the account to Lessa.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Hallek Completed with Lessa Level 31 After The Boys' Lookout Leads to What Bites, Back on the Bridge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,800 EXP
  • 620 mesos
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Hallek
Dialogue
  • You have been out to the far bridge, they say. Then you have seen the frayed ropes. I was the one hanging under the planks this spring, splicing on the far side, when it bit me.
  • I never saw it. I felt teeth in the back of my leg, deep, and I heard claws on the rock under me, a lot of claws, scrabbling away down the cliff. When I looked there was nothing but dust falling.
  • The leg went hot and swelled for a week. Lessa cleaned it with something bitter and grey. She has asked me a dozen times what it was, and I have no answer. Will you take her what I told you? You saw the ropes. Maybe between us it makes sense.
  • Tell her the teeth were small and many, not one big bite. She asked that, and I did not think of it until now.
  • Fair. It is not much of a story anyway. A bite in the dark.
  • Take what I told you to Lessa at the Brenna House. Small teeth, many of them, and claws going down the cliff.
  • Hallek finally remembered something? Small teeth, many of them, climbing down sheer rock. And you saw the ropes chewed on the side away from town. That is something to go on.
  • I have treated more bites this year than in my first ten years together, and every one of them festers the same way. I am tired of cleaning wounds without knowing what made them.

docs.title: Wolves in the Copses
docs.text:
The carters coming down the royal road say the scrub wolves are bold in the Chalk Downs' copses. Halloran wants them thinned.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Halloran Level 12

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Scrub Wolf in The Chalk Downs

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 428 EXP
  • 264 mesos
  • +40 standing with Halloran
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You know the royal road west, over the Chalk Downs? The carters bring half our flour down it. And the holm-oak copses up there have filled with scrub wolves this year.
  • They don't attack the carts, not yet. They follow them. A carter told me he had six at his wheels all the way to the hill. I'd like that not to become seven.
  • Clear 30 Scrub Wolfs out of the copses on the Chalk Downs, Player. The Watch can't leave the waterfront, and I'd rather it was someone who knows the road.
  • Thank you. Take a mug of something hot when you come back. I'll have one waiting.
  • Another time, then.
  • Thirty scrub wolves, on the Chalk Downs past Baysight Hill. Watch the copses.
  • That's the carters' road made safe for a while, and I didn't have to send a single watchman off the waterfront.
  • Here. The Watch pays its debts. And the carters will be buying you drinks at the Salt and Bread, if Delphine lets them.

docs.title: Everyone Who Writes Things Down
docs.text:
Halloran has finally decided to ask for the notes. Half the harbour writes down what it sees, and nobody has put the pages together.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Halloran Level 53 After Under the Pier Leads to Keeping the Light

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Brisa
  2. Talk to Delphine
  3. Talk to Clemence
  4. Talk to Ottilie

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 49,323 EXP
  • 1,590 mesos
  • +60 standing with Halloran
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • I've been a fool. I've a watchwoman who keeps a list of every strange thing the sailors tell her. My own sister keeps a ledger of tales behind the bar, I'd bet. Clemence writes down every wound. Ottilie counts every boat.
  • And not one of us has put our pages on the same table. Go and ask them, Player. Brisa, Delphine, Clemence, Ottilie. Tell them I asked. Tell them I'm sorry I didn't ask sooner.
  • Tell them I asked. That matters.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Brisa, Delphine, Clemence and Ottilie for their notes, for Halloran.
  • Sixty-four entries in Brisa's list. Thirty years of tales in Delphine's ledger. Round welts in Clemence's book, the size of the marks on my pilings. And Ottilie's boats, half what they were ten summers ago.
  • It's all one thing. Out past the headland, and coming closer. Ysolde's been watching that water for forty years. I'll ask her next. Will you go?
  • Captain asked for my list? Finally. Sixty-four entries. Date and teller for every one.
  • I'm coming when he reads it. I'm not missing that. Tell him I said so.
  • My brother asked? Halloran? Well. He drinks at the end of my bar every night for twenty years and never asked me anything but 'same again'.
  • Here's my second book. Teller, ship, date, place. Tell him I knew the pier watch was more than a precaution.
  • My casebook. I've shown it to no one, dear. But if Halloran is asking...
