  • This page. A deckhand, a row of round welts on the forearm, the size of a coin, each with a ring of fine scratches. Tell him to look at it next to his pilings.
  • My small-boat tally. I wasn't sure who to tell. Ten summers ago a fair week saw forty boats past the headland. Last summer, twenty-two. This spring, fewer.
  • Tell the Captain the figures are correct. I checked them against Hobart's chalk twice.

docs.title: The Outer Pier
docs.text:
Halloran has stood the outer pier's night watch himself since spring. He asks you to stand it with him, and on the boards, at last, he tells someone what he found.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Halloran Level 51 Leads to Under the Pier

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Outer Pier by Night

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 44,002 EXP
  • 1,530 mesos
  • +60 standing with Halloran
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You've done this harbour a lot of good, Player. The crabs, the sawbills, the night run. I've a favour to ask, and a thing to tell, and I've told it to one person only.
  • This spring, one morning at low tide, I found the Watch's launch hanging from her mooring line. The line pulled taut, straight down. Into the water. And fresh grooves in the pilings below the waterline. By the time help came the line was slack.
  • Quenna knows. Nobody else. I've stood the night watch on the outer pier most nights since. Stand it with me tonight. Ask me when you're ready, and we'll go.
  • Bring something warm. And don't tell Jowan.
  • Another time, then.
  • Stand the night watch on the outer pier with Halloran (ask him when you're ready).
  • Shadows climbing the pilings where that pale light fell. You saw them too. I'm not mad, then.
  • I'm glad it was you. Delphine would have made a speech, and Jowan would have stood at the end of the pier with his chest out. Thank you.

docs.title: Under the Pier
docs.text:
Halloran wants someone to look at the outer pier's pilings at the lowest tide. He has looked from above for months.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Halloran Level 52 After The Outer Pier Leads to Everyone Who Writes Things Down

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Under the Outer Pier

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 46,612 EXP
  • 1,560 mesos
  • +60 standing with Halloran
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The tide goes out further than usual tonight. Low enough to climb down among the outer pier's pilings and look at them close.
  • I've looked from above for months. I want someone to look properly. At the far end, where the line went down. Ask me when you're ready.
  • Look at the ones at the far end.
  • Another time, then.
  • Climb down under the outer pier at the lowest tide (ask Halloran when you're ready).
  • Rows of round marks, each one ringed with fine scratches. The size of a coin, some of them bigger.
  • Like something with... no. I won't guess. But I'll stop pretending it's nothing. Come and see me tomorrow. I've been a fool to keep this to myself.

docs.title: A Fair Copy
docs.text:
Halvard's ledger lacks the tides for the last month. Copy them from the Tide Book at Ailsa's desk, then bring the copy to Halvard.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Halvard Level 58 After The Count

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Ailsa
  2. Deliver 1 Copied Tide Marks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 24,000 EXP
  • 1,160 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x5
  • Return Scroll to Goa Harbour x3
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Halvard
Dialogue
  • Player, a favour, if you have the hands for it. Mine are full. Eleven ships due tomorrow, and the First Warden wants the list by first light.
  • Every ship in my ledger has its tide beside it: the hour through the gap and the height on the quay steps. For this last month I have the ships and not the tides. They are all in the Tide Book, at Ailsa's desk. Someone only has to copy them across.
  • Would you sit with Ailsa and copy this month's tides fair, then bring the copy to me? Neatly, please. I will check every line.
  • Ailsa will read them out faster than you can write. Ask her to slow down. She won't, but ask.
  • Yes, yes, I'll do it by candlelight. It is only my eyes.
  • The tides for this last month, from the Tide Book at Ailsa's desk, copied fair. Then the copy to me.
  • Halvard sent you to copy? He could have walked twelve steps. Sit. Pen. The first of the month: high water at the quay steps an hour before noon, run moderate, wind westerly. The second... keep up. ...There. Every day of it. Take it to him before he comes in here to straighten my stack.
  • Let me see. Hm. Hm. Yes.
  • Your hand slopes. Ailsa read too fast, didn't she. No, it is good, Player, it is perfectly good. I shall only rule a line under it.
  • There. Every ship with its tide, and the ledger straight. Take these, with my thanks.

docs.title: The Count
docs.text:
Halvard has counted every ship Varro ever took through the gap, and cannot decide whether to tell him. Ask Iska, then go back to Halvard.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Halvard Level 50 Leads to A Fair Copy

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Iska

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 13,000 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Halvard
Dialogue
  • Oh. Player. Would you close the door? Not all the way, it sticks. There.
  • Some time ago Varro said he had taken more ships through the gap than anyone could count, my ledgers included. So I counted. Fifteen years in my hand, and forty more in the clerks' before me. I have the number.
  • I have not told him. I do not know whether a man wants to hear a thing like that. You see the difficulty.
  • Would you ask Iska? Not the number, please, that stays in the ledger. Only whether I should tell him. She knows him better than anyone.
  • She is at the table, I expect, or on her way out of the door. Catch her on her way out. That is when she answers fastest.
  • No, of course. It is very safe in the ledger.
  • Only whether I should tell him. Not the number. Iska is about the house somewhere.
  • Halvard counted Varro's ships? Of course he did. ...No. Tell him to keep it. Varro said nobody could count them because he did not want them counted. A number like that is for keeping, not for handing to a man. Halvard keeps things well.
  • Keep it. Yes. I thought she might say that.
  • It is a good number, Player. I shall underline it once, very neatly, and never look at it again. Here, for your trouble.

docs.title: A New Rim
docs.text:
The cart's oldest wheel has new spokes, but its rim is split, and Hambone cannot bear to replace it. Ask Ferro whether an iron band could hold the old wood together.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Hambone Level 42 After Seasoned Wood

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ferro

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,190 EXP
  • 2,520 mesos
  • +60 standing with Hambone
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • All right. All right! The wheel is cracked. The left rear, the oldest one. There, I said it, and the sky did not fall, though I half expected it to.
  • The spokes are new now, from your wood. But the rim is split, and a rim is a rim: replace it and the wheel is a new wheel. Fenwick fitted that rim. Fenwick said it came off Juna's own cart, or near enough.
  • Ferro works odd metals. Ask Ferro whether a thin iron band could go round the old rim and hold it, so the old wood stays and the cart still rolls. I cannot ask. I would cry at the anvil, and Ferro is very gruff about crying.
  • Tell Ferro it is for Juna's cart. No, tell Ferro it is for the troupe. No... tell Ferro whichever will work.
  • Then I bind it in wire again, and hope, and hum.
  • Ask Ferro on Workshops Row about an iron band for the old rim, Player.
  • A band round an old rim, so the wood stays. Hm. (Ferro turns a scrap of iron over and over, not looking at you.) That is not a weapon.
  • Good. Tell Hambone to bring the wheel. The band gets a name on the inside, small, where nobody looks. And tell Hambone the old wood stays. That is the whole point of a band.
  • The old wood stays. (Hambone sits down on the tailboard.) The old wood stays, with an iron band round it and a name inside. Ferro said that?
  • Then the cart rolls on Walkout Day on Juna's rim, or near enough, and nobody will ever know but us and Ferro and Dina and Thimble and Sprout. Which is half the troupe. Which is fine. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Seasoned Wood
docs.text:
Hambone wants seasoned wood, the kind that does not warp on a wet Walkout Day, and swears it is for the shed and not for any wheel. The barkbacks of the Bristlewood carry heartwood under their moss.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Hambone Level 34 Leads to The Cart Must Roll, A New Rim

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Mossy Bark (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 36,660 EXP
  • 5,100 mesos
  • +50 standing with Hambone
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Ah, mind the wheel, mind the wheel. No, that one is fine. That one is... fine. (Hambone stands in front of the left rear wheel and polishes it a little too hard.)
  • Seasoned wood, that is what a cart wants. Never green. Green wood warps on a wet Walkout Day, and the grandee rolls into the crowd before his line. Good seasoned wood does not come up the roads any more.
  • The barkbacks in the Bristlewood, now, those are old stumps that walk, and the wood under the moss has been seasoning longer than I have. Bring me 30 Mossy Bark with the heartwood still on. Not for any wheel. Just for the shed. In general.
  • In general, mind. Not for a wheel. Why would it be for a wheel?
  • No, no, quite right. Nothing needs fixing. Nothing at all.
  • 30 Mossy Bark, Player. For the shed. You have (how many you carry).
  • Lovely. Dry inside, and heavy, and it rings when you knock it. Listen. (Hambone knocks on it and hums a bar of the play's opening song.)
  • This will make spokes. For... for the shed. Thank you, Player. You did not see me wipe my eyes. Sawdust.

docs.title: Hamish a brush for the rope
A Brush for the Rope
docs.text:
Hamish's oiling brush has gone bald. Bring him 15 Weedy Bristles from the Wrack Boars and 10 pieces of Sound Driftwood from the Driftstumps of the Strandwood.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Hamish Level 22 Leads to The Second Lift

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 15 Weedy Bristle (taken)
  • Bring 10 Sound Driftwood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,300 EXP
  • 900 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Hamish
Dialogue
  • My oiling brush has gone bald, Player. Fifteen years of rope will do that. And a rope that is not oiled is a rope that frays, and a rope that frays... well. Let us not.
  • Wrack boar bristle holds oil better than anything. Bring me 15 Weedy Bristle from the Wrack Boars, and 10 Sound Driftwood from the Driftstumps, for a handle that will not rot. They are out in the Strandwood.
  • Lovely. The Strandwood track leaves the Saltwood Road. And if you see Fionn anywhere near the forest, send him home. Not that he would go near it. He knows better.
  • No? The rope and I will muddle on. It is very patient. I am less so.
  • (how many you carry) of 15 Weedy Bristle and (how many you carry) of 10 Sound Driftwood. The rope is waiting, and it is not getting any oilier.
  • Look at these! Good stiff bristle, and driftwood that rings when you knock it. I will have a brush bound by supper.
  • Here, for your trouble. And ride the lift any time. I will tell you everything about everyone. It is the least I can do.

docs.title: The Second Lift
docs.text:
Hamish dreams of a second lift down to the far cove. Bring him 15 Fox Sinews for his counterweight lashings, and take his drawing of the second lift to Gorm.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Hamish Level 30 After A Brush for the Rope

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 15 Fox Sinew (taken)
  • Talk to Gorm

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,500 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Fur-Lined Cloak x1
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Hamish
Dialogue
  • Can I show you something? Do not laugh. It is the second lift. Down the cliff to the far cove. I have drawn it a dozen times on the backs of cargo lists, and this is the best of them.
  • Gorm promised Iska a stair to that cove before the race, and he is behind. A lift would have been finished by now. I have said so. Loudly. Often.
  • Two things. My counterweight baskets want new lashings, so bring me 15 Fox Sinew from the Strand Foxes of the Strandwood. And take this drawing to Gorm. Let him have a proper look. Then come and tell me what he said. All of it.
  • Here is the drawing. Hold it by the edges, it is my best one. And stand well back when he unrolls it.
  • Fair. Nobody wants to be standing next to Gorm when he sees that. I will keep it a while longer.
  • (how many you carry) of 15 Fox Sinew for the lashings, and my drawing to Gorm. Has he thrown anything yet?
  • What is this? Hamish's basket again? Give it here.
  • Hm. Hm. No. He has the anchor in the wrong rock. That shelf will spit a bolt out in one winter. A yard over, here, where the grain runs down.
  • There. Take it back to him. And tell him it is still lazy. A correct lazy, now.
  • He wrote on it? Let me see. A yard over, where the grain runs down. And a correct lazy! Ha! He is right about the rock. He is always right about the rock.
  • I will pin it over the windlass. Someday, Player. Here, take this, for the wind on the clifftop. And the lashings will hold for years.

docs.title: Chalk on the Board
docs.text:
A story on Hamon's road board says the dew pond at Downs Edge is overrun. Before he leaves it up, he wants it checked: go to the dew pond and clear 30 monsters on Downs Edge.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hamon Level 21 Leads to The Unsigned Story

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the dew pond in Downs Edge
  • Defeat 30 monsters in Downs Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,500 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Hamon
Dialogue
  • Player! Come here, look at this. My board. Every line's a road story, chalked up by whoever told it.
  • This one: 'Downs Edge, the dew pond: bees thick as smoke, don't water a horse there.' Shepherds water there. If it's true, it stays. If not, I rub it out.
  • Go and look at the dew pond at Downs Edge, and clear 30 of what you find there. Then I'll know what to write.
  • Off you go. Supper will be on when you're back.
  • Then it stays up, true or not. I hate that.
  • The dew pond at Downs Edge, then thirty there.
  • True, then. And now less true, thanks to you. I'll chalk it: 'cleared by Player, this week'.
  • Sit. Eat. You've earned the corner by the fire.

docs.title: The Unsigned Story
docs.text:
Someone chalked a story on Hamon's board that nobody admits to: 'Thyme Banks, past the white stone: the bees fly at night.' Find the white stone, clear 30 wild bees on the Thyme Banks, and ask Merrick whether it was his.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hamon Level 24 After Chalk on the Board

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the white stone in The Thyme Banks
  2. Defeat 30 Wild Bee in The Thyme Banks
  3. Talk to Merrick

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,200 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Hamon
Dialogue
  • Look. Overnight, under the ford news: 'Thyme Banks, past the white stone: the bees fly at night.' Nobody's admitted to it.
  • I know every hand that writes on that board. I don't know this one.
  • Find the white stone on the The Thyme Banks, clear 30 Wild Bees there, and see if it's true. Then ask Merrick. If anyone wrote it, it's him.
  • Bring me a name. I collect them.
  • It'll keep. They always keep. That's the trouble.
  • The white stone on the Thyme Banks, thirty bees, then Merrick.
  • Bees around the stone after dark, and Merrick swears it's not his chalk. So it's true, and nobody wrote it.
  • I'll leave it up. Somebody wanted it read. I'd still like to say their name some day.
  • Mine? Ha! My chalk's yellow, and I sign everything I write, so I can charge for it later. Not mine. But if it's true, I want it on my bill.

docs.title: Harbour master quenna the council hears it
The Council Hears It
docs.text:
The harbour council wants to thank you, loudly, as Quenna promised. Each of them wants a word.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Quenna Level 70 After The Deep Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Corwin
  2. Talk to Annis
  3. Talk to Marisol
  4. Talk to Dunstan

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 77,511 EXP
  • 1,540 mesos
  • +40 standing with Quenna
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The council sat late last night. They want to thank you. Separately. Because if I let them do it together it will take until the race.
  • Go round them: Corwin, Annis, Marisol, Dunstan. Then come back to me and I'll ring the bell.
  • Corwin will be brief. Marisol won't.
  • Another time, then.
  • Hear the council's thanks: Corwin, Annis, Marisol and Dunstan.
  • Every one of them? Even Dunstan? He thanked you? Out loud?
  • Then it's official. Bain Harbour owes you, Player. The harbour council of captains, shipwrights and merchants, and me at the end of the table with my bell.
  • Thank you. The Heron sails deep water again next week. That is the thanks.
  • And I won't grumble about the harpooner at council. For a month.
  • Forty-four years and I never asked anyone for help on the water. You helped anyway.
  • Here. A pinch of my salt. Throw it over your shoulder next time you go anywhere that matters.
  • Darling, the cargoes are already coming in on time. Three ships this week, all early. I've counted.
  • The merchants of Merchant Street thank you, and so do I, and so does Cordelia, who has opinions about your coat.
  • Hmph.
  • ...Thank you. There. Don't make me say it twice.

docs.title: Harbour master quenna the deep lantern
The Deep Lantern
docs.text:
The Harbour Master takes it to the council. The thing in the sea-hole has a name now, and the harbour asks you to put it down.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Quenna Level 68 After To See It Once Leads to In Ink, Not in the Margin, The Council Hears It

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Halloran
  2. Clear The Deep Lantern

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 103,429 EXP
  • 2,040 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +60 standing with Quenna
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Tristram stood in my hall this morning and told the council, in that voice of his, what he saw at the Rim. Nobody laughed. Not even Corwin.
  • The Deep Lantern, Ysolde calls it. It's what pulled Halloran's launch down, what brushed the Saltlark, what Barnaby saw, what Seraphine saw. And it's under my headland.
  • The council voted. All of them. Talk to Halloran; the Watch will see you to the wood. Then go down to the Lantern Deep and put the Deep Lantern down. The felling stone at the Rim marks the way down.
  • Come back. That's not a request, that's the council's vote.
  • Another time, then.
  • Talk to Halloran, then defeat the Deep Lantern in the Lantern Deep.
  • It's done. The lights are gone from the sea-hole. Ysolde says the water past the headland is dark tonight, the way it should be.
  • I'm not fool enough to call the sea healed. But this harbour can sleep tonight, and it's you we have to thank. The council will want to say so. Loudly.
  • The council voted. I heard. The Watch will see you as far as the Rim, and no further, because you won't need us.
  • Go carefully. I'll keep a mug of something hot. For when you're back. Not if.

docs.title: Boggle Dust
docs.text:
Harra pays in cheese for Boggle Dust, which the Tolmach rub into hides against moth. Collect 25.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Harra Level 14 Leads to Cheese for the Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Boggle Dust (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,650 EXP
  • 280 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Harra
Dialogue
  • Here, taste that. No, all of it. That is a three-month cheese, and you will not find better between here and the sea. Now that your mouth is full, listen.
  • The Dust Boggles on the canyon roads are a pest, but the dust they leave behind is worth something to me. Rubbed into a hide, it keeps the moth off all winter.
  • Bring me 25 Boggle Dust and I will pay you in cheese, which is better than coin and lasts longer in a pack.
  • Good! The boggles are on the The Canyon Road and the The South Path. Pick up what they drop with Z.
  • Suit yourself. The cheese offer stands, and it only gets better with age.
  • Twenty-five Boggle Dust, Player. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Look at that, fine and red and dry. My hides will thank you, and so will the lowland buyers, though they will never know it.
  • Ten wheels of Goat Cheese for the road. Eat one when you are tired, and one when you are not.

docs.title: Cheese for the Road
docs.text:
Harra is sending a wheel of her best cheese to Corwell, who will pretend it is too dear. Take it to him, and hunt 30 Ridge Stumps on the South Path on the way.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Harra Completed with Corwell Level 16 After Boggle Dust Leads to The Hard Bargain

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Ridge Stump in The South Path
  • Deliver 1 Harra's Cheese Wheel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,750 EXP
  • 320 mesos
  • Travel Ration x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Harra
Dialogue
  • Corwell wants a wheel of my best for his trading-post table, and he wants it for half what it is worth. I will send it anyway. He will argue, I will argue, and then we will have tea. That is how it goes.
  • But do not walk straight across the square with it. Ennek's caravan drivers say the Ridge Stumps on the The South Path have come right down to the switchbacks.
  • Clear 30 Ridge Stumps on The South Path, then take this Harra's Cheese Wheel to Corwell. Tell him the price is the price.
  • Here is the wheel. Do not sit on it. The The South Path is out of the south gate, and Corwell is at the Trading Post counter.
  • Then it waits in my cool box, and Corwell waits too. Good for him.
  • Thirty Ridge Stumps on The South Path, then the Harra's Cheese Wheel to Corwell.
  • Harra's three-month wheel? She sent it with you? Ah, and she says the price is the price. Of course she does.
  • Do not tell her, Player, but it is worth every coin, and I would pay double. The stumps on the switchbacks too? Then my drivers owe you as well.
  • Here are some Travel Rations from the back. Harra packs them; I only sell them. Do not tell her I said that either.

docs.title: The Hard Bargain
docs.text:
Fewer lowland traders make the climb every year, and Harra means to make the ones who come pay well. Bring her 20 Wild Boar Teeth, which the lowlanders prize.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Harra Level 30 After Cheese for the Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Wild Boar Tooth (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,600 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • Travel Ration x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Harra
Dialogue
  • Taste this first. Six-month, from the high pasture grass. You did that, they tell me, you and the old woman's legs. Now, business.
  • Fewer traders come up every year. The ones who do come want something they cannot get on the plain. Wool, they have. Cheese, they have, though not this good. Boar tusks, polished, they do not have, and they will pay through the nose.
  • Bring me 20 Wild Boar Tooth. The Wild Boars across the far canyon bridge carry the best of them.
  • Good. Pick the big curved ones. Corwell will say he can get them cheaper. Corwell is lying.
  • Suit yourself. The traders will get wool and like it.
  • Twenty Wild Boar Tooth, you have (how many you carry). The boars are across the far canyon bridge.
  • Look at the curve on that one. A lowland trader will hang it over his door and tell his neighbours he hunted it himself.
  • Corwell offered me half what I will get for these. I told him the price is the price. He laughed so hard he spilled the tea.
  • Cheese and rations, from the camps to you. A hard bargain is still a fair one, Player, when both sides walk away fed.

docs.title: A Quiet Word
docs.text:
Hask wants to know what the families would say about the patrols, if he asked them in council. Have a quiet word with Zirra, Ulm and Odda.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Hask Level 35 After The First Report

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Zirra
  • Talk to Ulm
  • Talk to Odda

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,400 EXP
  • 700 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • Goat Cheese x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Hask
Dialogue
  • If I stand up in council and say the patrols are too thin, every chieftain will nod, and every one will say their own family is managing. Then nothing changes.
  • I would rather know first what they would say if no one were listening. You belong to none of the families, Player, so they may say it to you. Have a quiet word with my sister Zirra, with Ulm by the fire, and with Odda. Then tell me.
  • Quietly. If it sounds like a council, they will answer like one.
  • That is fair. It was a lot to ask.
  • A quiet word with Zirra, Ulm and Odda about the patrols.
  • Zirra said ask her later. Ulm said the fire does not care who feeds it. Odda said it should be asked over food. Hm.
  • None of them said no, Player. In this town that is closer to yes than you would think. Thank you. I will remember who answered and how.
  • My brother sent you to ask about the patrols. He thinks I will not see through that. I raised him; I see through everything he does.
  • Tell him to ask me again later, when I have something to say that I can stand to say. He will understand. Or he will not, and I will have to explain, which I would hate.
  • Sit if you want. The fire does not mind. The patrols? I hear everything said in this hall, and everything not said too.
  • Every family brings wood for this fire and nobody asks whose wood burns brightest. The patrols should be the same. Tell Hask that. He knows already. He sits up with me after councils.
  • A quiet word? From Hask, through you. That is like him: he never asks for anything in the open.
  • The families will say it, but not in a council hall with their chieftains watching. Over food, maybe. Over a long night, certainly. Tell him that, and tell him the Brenna will host it whenever he likes.

docs.title: The First Report
docs.text:
You have walked the High Ridges from the North Ridge to Howling Peak. Tell the Old One the truth about them.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Hask Level 29 After The High Pasture Leads to The Second Stick, A Quiet Word, Far Slopes Bounty, Far Slopes Elites

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,100 EXP
  • 580 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • Town Return Scroll x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Hask
Dialogue
  • You are back from the ridges. Sit. The council will tell me tomorrow that the ridges are held, and it will be true. Now tell me the rest of it.
  • Tell me what the patrols are, Player. Not what they should be.
  • Go on.
  • Then come back when you are ready to tell it. I will wait.
  • The Old One is waiting for your report.
  • The ridges are held, you say. The stumps are cut back, Old Gnarl is down, the herds are on the high pasture. And they are held because you walked them. Skarra has too few hands. Tavi walks the worst stretch alone because nobody else will. Sennu and Tavi only spoke through you.
  • That is what I feared, and nobody has said it at the fire. Thank you for saying it to me. Not yet to the council. The families are not ready to hear it, and a truth said too early is only an insult.
  • Keep walking, Player. The far slopes are beyond the bridge, and I think the truth out there is harder. Take these for the road.

docs.title: The Gathering
docs.text:
Hask has called the four families to the Great Hall. Hear Thrun's drum and Ahvi's verse, then sit in council and tell the Old One the truth he asked you for.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Hask Level 69 After The Verse

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Thrun
  2. Talk to Ahvi
  3. Talk to Hask

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 67,500 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • Elixir x2
  • One of: Rootwood Greatsword, Rootwood Axe, Heartwood Shield, Rootwood Helm
  • +100 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Hask
Dialogue
  • Player. When the four families sit together in this hall, it is to choose somebody or to feast. Tonight I have called them for neither. Thrun is already warming his hands.
  • When we began, I asked you to walk the patrols and tell me the truth, because you belong to none of the families and owe none of them a kind word. You have walked the ridges, the slopes and the Reach since then. I have not yet heard that truth in council.
  • Tonight you will say it where all four can hear. First the drum, then the song, then the council. Go to Thrun; when he beats, the families will come.
  • Thrun first, then Ahvi, then come and sit by me. Ulm has built the fire high. He says it is the first time I have ever asked him to.
  • The families can wait one more night. They have waited all summer.
  • The drum, then the verse, then the council: Thrun, Ahvi, and then me.
  • Ha! There you are! The hide you brought home off the Ash Mesa, Player, and listen: it doesn't mutter, it sings. Stand back a step. It's loud.
  • There. That beat goes down every terrace and out to the camps and along the rim. Kragvar, Tolmach, Uskari, Brenna, they'll all be in the hall before the fire needs another log. Go on, Ahvi's waiting.
  • Sit with me while the hall fills. I will sing the long song from the beginning, every chieftain and every Old One, and Neffa will sit at my side, listening for her turn.
  • And at the end of the oldest part, I will sing the verse I kept to myself all summer: goats that bit, cats that hunted people, birds that would not settle, in a season before the Burning.
  • It says nothing more, and I will not make it say more. What the families do with it is theirs. Go and sit by the Old One; he will want you near when it ends.
  • The song is done and the hall is quiet, which in Midbarium means everyone is about to talk at once. Before they do, Player: the truth. What did you find?
  • You say the patrols could not hold the ridges, nor the bridge, nor the Reach, and that each was held only because one more pair of hands walked it. You say every family has carried its share alone and called it pride.
  • Dorrek is standing. Sennu is standing. Tavi has not sat down at all. Good. For the first time in my years as Old One, the families are saying aloud how thin the patrols are, and nobody is ashamed to say it.
  • Then here is the council's word, and I close it: from tonight the watch is shared. Kragvar on the bridges and the stairs, Tolmach on the pasture paths, Brenna in the camps, Uskari wherever the rest of us cannot go. We were already one town, Player. Tonight we learned to ask each other for help.
  • The hall is emptying slowly. Nobody wants to go home, which I have never seen before. Ulm says the fire burned brighter tonight than any night he remembers.
  • I asked you for the truth because you owed no family a kind word. You told it kindly anyway. That is rarer.
  • Take these, from all four families, and know that every fire in Midbarium is yours to sit at. Wherever the road takes you next, you go as one of the people who held the highlands.

docs.title: The Second Report
docs.text:
The far bridge is held and the herds are safe from the raider, for now. Report to Hask.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Hask Level 49 After The New Hide Leads to The Greywater

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,700 EXP
  • 980 mesos
  • Highland Salve x20
  • Rimwort Tonic x20
  • Elixir x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Hask
Dialogue
  • I heard the drum. The whole mountain heard the drum. Sit by me, Player, and tell me about the far slopes. Plainly, the way you told me about the ridges.
  • Take your time. The council is not until the new moon.
  • Later, then. I will be here.
  • Sit when you are ready, Player, and tell me about the far slopes.
  • The bridge holds because a Kragvar bridge-master sat up a night with his apprentice and a stranger to his family. The rimwort came home because a Brenna healer asked. The raider is dead because an Uskari boy would not let it go, and his mother let him go at last.
  • And you are telling me the patrols could not have done it alone. I know. The Uskari are stretched to a thread, and every family has carried a piece of this without saying so in council.
  • One day soon they will have to say it to each other's faces, not to you and not to me. Until then, take these. You have earned more than I can pay.

docs.title: Walk the Patrols
docs.text:
The Old One asks you, who belong to none of the four families, to walk the trail watch's patrols and tell him the truth about them. Go to Skarra on the Uskari Rim.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Hask Completed with Skarra Level 20 Leads to Red Dots

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,050 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Hask
Dialogue
  • Sit with me a moment, Player. I have listened to you being talked about at the fire. The roads, the cairns, the stumps on the ridge. You walk where you are asked and you come back.
  • Every council, the four families tell me the trails are held. Tavi says the patrols are doubled. Sennu says the herds are safe close to town. Dorrek says nothing, which is his way of agreeing. And every season the marks come closer.
  • I was the Uskari's chieftain once. I know how a family says all is well because the others are listening. You belong to none of the four. Nobody will be ashamed in front of you.
  • Walk the patrols for me. All of them, as far as they go, for as long as it takes. And when you have, come and tell me the truth about them, not what the council would like to hear. Start with Skarra on the Uskari Rim.
  • Thank you. Skarra will not like a stranger to the watch at her elbow, but she will like it less that I asked. Go gently with her.
  • I understand. It is a long walk I am asking for. The fire will be here when you are ready.
  • Skarra is on the Uskari Rim, on the east edge of town. Tell her I sent you.
  • The Old One sent you. To walk my patrols. Of course he did.
  • Tavi came by this morning and said you would be coming, and that I was to show you what I show nobody. I argued. Tavi won. Tavi always wins.
  • Fine. Come back when you are ready, and I will show you the map. Do not touch it.

docs.title: Hatch's Bounty: the Bristlewood
docs.text:
Hatch collects a bounty from the caravans for every beast cleared from the Bristlewood and passes it on to whoever does the work: defeat 60 bristle boars, barkbacks, ironhide hogs or reed-lurkers. Every round raises Urbanograd's regard for you, and Hatch will pay it again, any time.

Town Urbanograd Category Repeatable Given by Hatch Level 30

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Bristlewood monsters (Bristle Boar, Barkback, Ironhide Hog, Reed-Lurker)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 27,200 EXP
  • 3,600 mesos
  • +40 standing with Hatch
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The caravan masters pay me to keep the Bristlewood thin. I take the money and my knees take the day off, and somebody younger does the walking. 60 beasts of the Bristlewood: boar, barkbacks, hogs, the things in the reeds. You bring the count, I pass the purse on.
  • Good. Through the far end of the Outworks into the trees. Walk downwind of the boar. Don't argue, just do it.
  • Suit yourself. The caravans will keep paying. The woods will keep filling.
  • Sixty from the Bristlewood. Boar, barkbacks, hogs and reed-lurkers all count.
  • Sixty. You smell like a wallow. That is how I know you were really there.
  • Here's the caravans' money. The Table hears about it too; I make sure. Come back when the trees fill up again.

docs.title: Hackleback
docs.text:
Go down into the Wallow at the heart of the Reedwater Bottoms and bring down Hackleback, the deeply touched boar that drives the lesser ones onto the road. Hatch will show you the way in.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Hatch Level 47 After The Hunt at the Wallow Leads to The Fourth Version, When to Run

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Hackleback

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 40,470 EXP
  • 1,410 mesos
  • +80 standing with Hatch
  • +60 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Last thing. Charges come straight: step aside, then strike. Never the other way round. When it stamps, get off the ground. When it calls the boar, kill the boar, then the beast. Don't be brave. Be right.
  • Go to The Wallow and bring down Hackleback. Ask me for the way down when you're ready.
  • Good. Ask me when you want to go down. My nose says it's lying up in the mud right now. My nose is never wrong.
  • Good. A hunter who isn't ready knows it. That's the first thing I ever taught Shade.
  • Hackleback, in The Wallow. Ask me for the way down.
  • You're back. You're covered in mud to the eyebrows and you stink like the bottom of the world and you're back. Sit. No. Sit. I'm pouring.
  • Thirty years I've wanted to know what took my wagon. I'll never know that. But I know this one, now. It's in the notes, in your words. Somebody will read them when I'm gone, and they'll know what to look for.
  • Someone worth teaching. I said I was looking for one. I wasn't sure there'd be one before my knees finished me.
  • Go and see Tick. He'll want the story, and for once he should get the true one. Go on. I'm going to finish this cup and not cry in it.

docs.title: Reading Tracks
docs.text:
Hatch is too old to hunt alone and wants someone worth teaching. His first test: at Bristlewood Edge, among the tracks of half a dozen beasts, follow only the bristle boars and bring down 30 of them.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Hatch Level 30 Leads to A New Route

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Bristle Boar in Bristlewood Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 17,140 EXP
  • 1,800 mesos
  • +50 standing with Hatch
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • You. Stop. Let me look at you. Hm. You stand like someone who has been hit and got up again. That is a start. Most people who want to learn from me want stories. I tell stories after the second cup. Before that, I teach.
  • Out at Bristlewood Edge, where the trees start, the ground is all tracks. Barkbacks drag, stumps shuffle, boar dig in with the front feet and leave a split print, deep at the toe. Any fool can hit the first thing that moves. A hunter hits the right thing.
  • Go to the Edge. Follow the boar prints and nothing else, and bring down 30 Bristle Boars. Leave the rest alone. I will know if you didn't. My nose will.
  • Through the Outworks, out the far east end, into the trees. Split print, deep at the toe. Go.
  • Then you are not ready. No shame in it. Most aren't.
  • 30 Bristle Boars at Bristlewood Edge. Split print. Deep at the toe. Nothing else.
  • Come here. Let me smell your boots. Boar, boar, boar. A little barkback, but you walked through them, you didn't fight them. Good.
  • Here is something for your trouble. Those boar used to stay deep in the wood. Now they come right to the Edge, and they don't run from a man the way they did. I don't know why. I write it down. I never used to write anything down.
  • You'll do, for a start. Shade has been asking for someone to scout a new route. Go and see Shade. Tell Shade I sent you, and that I said you're slow.

docs.title: Hatch the hunt at the wallow
The Hunt at the Wallow
docs.text:
Hatch has a plan, a boar-spear from Ferro and a name for the beast: Hackleback. He cannot go himself. Make sure Torvi keeps Zip back from the Wallow, hear Zip out, then come back to Hatch for the way in.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Hatch Level 46 After A Boar-Spear Head Leads to Hackleback

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Torvi Brask
  2. Talk to Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,250 EXP
  • 5,520 mesos
  • +60 standing with Hatch
  • +30 standing with Urbanograd
  • Unlocks boss.hackleback
Dialogue
  • Sit. This is the second cup, so you get the long version. Thirty years ago a thing in a ravine took my wagon and my horses and I came home on foot. I didn't know what it was. I still don't. I bought a spear the next week.
  • The beast in the Bottoms, I've given it a name: Hackleback, for the bristles. It lies up in the Wallow, a mud hollow at the heart of the Reedwater. It charges straight, sweeps with the tusks, and when it's hurt it calls the lesser boar. When it's badly hurt its hide goes hard as a cart-tyre. Hit it before then, and hit it often.
  • I'd go. I want you to know I'd go. But my knees would get me halfway down the bank and leave me there, and then you'd have two things to carry. So I plan, and you hunt. That's the deal.
  • Two things first. Tell Torvi Brask that Zip does not come to the Wallow. Then go and tell Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway yourself, so she hears it from the one who's going. Then come back, and I'll show you the way in.
  • Torvi's on the training ground inside the gate, most likely. Zip will be wherever Torvi told her not to be.
  • Good. Better to say no here than halfway down the bank.
  • Torvi Brask first, then Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway. Then back to me, and I'll show you the way to the Wallow.
  • Hatch says Zip stays home. Ha. Hatch is right. I was going to say it myself, but it is better coming from three of us; she argues with one at a time.
  • Here is what I will tell her, and what I want you to tell her too. My grandmother Hulda said a fighter who never runs gets one bad day. That beast is a bad day. Knowing when to run is not the coward's part. It is the part that lets you come back.
  • I will keep her on the training ground until you are back. If I have to sit on her. Go and tell her. Gently. Then not gently.
  • No. No no no. You are going after my monster? The one from my bank? Without me? It is my story! I was there first! I fell off a bank for it!
  • ...Torvi says I am not ready. Torvi says when to run is the whole lesson. I hate the whole lesson. I can do footwork. I can do guard. I just cannot make my feet go backwards when everything in me says forwards.
  • Fine. FINE. I will stay. But you have to come back and tell me every single thing. The size of it. The noise. Everything. And if you do not come back I will be furious with you forever.
  • Torvi's sitting on her, more or less. Good. Then everything's ready but you. Ferro's spear-head is on the shaft; Ferro named it, I expect, and won't tell me what.
  • When you're ready, ask me, and I'll show you the way down to the Wallow. I'll be here. I'll be sitting in this chair the whole time, hating it.

docs.title: The Lost Notes
docs.text:
When his knees gave out, Hatch left his last camp in the Bristlewood in a hurry, and his notebook with it. The barkbacks have been through the camp since. Go to Hatch's Camp and find his notes.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Hatch Level 36 After A New Route Leads to Zip's Bank

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach Hatch's Camp
  2. Bring 1 Hatch's Notes (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,970 EXP
  • 2,640 mesos
  • +60 standing with Hatch
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Tracks crossing the path. Big as a cartwheel. Going down to the wet ground. Hm. Shade told me. I knew. I didn't want to know.
  • Last autumn I had a camp out past the The Tusk Path. Sat there a month, watching, writing. Then one morning my knees said no, and I walked out on a stick and left half my kit behind. My notebook too. Everything I saw out there is in it.
  • The Barkbacks will have been through the camp by now. They take things. Paper, cloth, anything soft. Tuck it into the moss on their backs, for all I know.
  • Go to Hatch's Camp and bring back Hatch's Notes. If it isn't in the camp, one of the Barkbacks round it has it.
  • Past the Tusk Path, a hollow under an old oak, a fire-ring of black stones. Don't sit in my chair. It's not for sitting. It's for falling off.
  • Then it rots in the moss. Thirty years of looking, rotting in the moss. Fine.
  • Hatch's Camp, and my Hatch's Notes. A Barkback has it, if the camp doesn't.
  • That's it. That's my hand. Wet, and something's chewed the corner, but it's all there. Look. Look at this page.
  • "Day nineteen. One boar. Not a herd: one. Tracks deep as my forearm. Bristles on a thornbush like nails. It went through the Reedwater Bottoms like a wagon through wheat." I wrote that, and then I went home, and I told myself I'd been drinking.
  • One huge boar. It's the one that drives the lesser ones out of the trees onto the road. It's why the caravans get hit. I don't know what made it like that. I've stopped pretending I can guess.
  • Torvi Brask saw tracks like these at the top of a stream bank, last spring. The day Zip broke her arm. Go and talk to Torvi. Tell Torvi I said it's the same beast. I'd bet my knees on it, and they're worth less every day.

docs.title: Hawise a colour nobody has seen
A Colour Nobody Has Seen
docs.text:
For Isabeau's festival of colours Hawise wants to try fern fibre from the Long Reach, mordanted with crushed lorang claw. Then Isabeau must see the cloth.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hawise Level 36 After Reed-Root Dye Leads to The Vat That Changed

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 10 Fern Fibre
  2. Bring 10 Bank Lorang Claw (taken)
  3. Talk to Isabeau

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,790 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Hawise
Dialogue
  • New idea! The ferns on the Long Reach banks, and crushed claw from the lorangs to fix it. Shell makes colours sing, I'm sure of it. Nearly sure.
  • Gather me 10 Fern Fibre on the Long Reach, and bring 10 Bank Lorang Claws. Then take the cloth to Isabeau. She smells wool and sees colour like nobody alive. I can't bear to watch her look.
  • Go, go! I'll have the vat hot when you're back.
  • Then I'll stand here stained to the elbows and dream. Fine.
  • Ten fern fibres, ten lorang claws, then the cloth to Isabeau.
  • She said what? Not yet, but warmer? WARMER! That's the nicest thing Isabeau's ever said about anything!
  • Thank you, Player! I'm close. I can feel it in my elbows. Here!
  • Hawise's cloth. (She holds it to the window, then to her nose.) Fern and shell. Clever girl.
  • Not the colour, not yet. But warmer. Much warmer. Tell her that, exactly that, and tell her the festival will wait for her.

docs.title: Reed-Root Dye
docs.text:
Hawise thinks the thick roots the ligators tear up in the Reed Beds might dye a colour she has never made. Bring her twelve.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hawise Level 33 Leads to A Colour Nobody Has Seen

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 12 Reed Root (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,750 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Hawise
Dialogue
  • Ooh! You've come at the right time! I was at the The Reed Beds on Monday, and the ligators had torn up the reeds, and the roots, Player, the roots were the colour of a bruise going green!
  • Bring me 12 Reed Roots. The Reed Ligators tear them up with their snouts. Twelve! It might be the one. It might be the colour!
  • Hurry! No, don't hurry, the ligators bite. Hurry carefully!
  • Oh. All right. I'll make another brown. I'm very good at brown.
  • Twelve reed roots! You have (how many you carry).
  • (She boils one, dips a scrap, lifts it out, and stares.) It's... grey-green. It's grey-green with a sulk in it.
  • Not the colour. But close to something! Thank you, Player. Number eight. I'm calling it River Mood.

docs.title: The Vat That Changed
docs.text:
One of Hawise's vats turned overnight to a colour she did not put in it and nobody on the bank can name. She wants the crocos that came up the bank that night driven back, and Hereward told before he hears it from someone else.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hawise Level 44 After A Colour Nobody Has Seen

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Undercut Croco Hide (taken)
  2. Talk to Hereward

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,200 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Hawise
Dialogue
  • Player. Come and look. Don't touch. This was madder on Friday. Rust red. This morning it's... I don't have a word. I always have a word.
  • There were croc tracks in the mud by the vat. Big ones, from the The Undercut. Bring me 10 Undercut Croco Hides, so I know they're driven back. Then tell Hereward before he hears it from the bank. He worries in silence. It's the loudest thing he does.
  • I'm going to sit and look at it. I'm not going to touch it. Probably.
  • Then I'll lid it and not look at it. For a day.
  • Ten croco hides, then tell Hereward.
  • Hereward came up the bank, looked at the vat a long while, and said, 'Leave it.' That's all. Leave it. So I'm leaving it.
  • I still don't know what turned it. Maybe I'm not meant to yet. Thank you, Player. Here.
  • A vat changed colour by itself. (He weighs it.) And croc tracks.
  • Tell her to leave it. Lid it, and leave it. Tell her I'll walk up after the stones stop. (A pause.) Tell her I said thank you for telling me first.

docs.title: Straps Through the Landing
docs.text:
Helewise's order of leather and shield straps came upriver to the Quarry Landing and sits there. Go to the landing and bring back 20 quarry rubble from the Spoil Heaps, which Vessa will take off the strap price.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Helewise Level 52 Leads to Whetstones for the Yard

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach The Quarry Landing
  • Bring 20 Quarry Rubble (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,000 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Helewise
Dialogue
  • Leather. Saddle leather and shield straps, bought cheap upriver, and it's been sitting at the The Quarry Landing for a week because no carter will go past the spoil heaps.
  • The bargemen will load it if someone shows them the landing's safe. And while you're there: Vessa lines her quench trough with quarry rubble, and she'll take a good piece off the straps for it.
  • Go to the The Quarry Landing, then bring me 20 Quarry Rubble off the golems on the The Spoil Heaps. The leather comes home, and Vessa gets her rubble. Housekeeping.
  • Every piece counts. I'll be counting them.
  • Then the leather rots on the wharf, and I write it off. I hate writing things off.
  • The Quarry Landing, and twenty pieces of quarry rubble.
  • Twenty. Good weight, too. The barge came down this morning with every bale.
  • Vessa will call me a bandit. I'll call it a fair price. We'll both be right.

docs.title: Whetstones for the Yard
docs.text:
The practice yard is wearing through whetstones. Bring Helewise 25 quarry stone from the Terraced Cuts, then tell Bertrand the new whetstones are coming.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Helewise Level 55 After Straps Through the Landing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 25 Quarry Stone (taken)
  2. Talk to Bertrand

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 30,000 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • Scroll for Shield for DEF 60% x1
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Helewise
Dialogue
  • Whetstones. The biggest intake the Guard has ever had, every one of them blunting a blade a day, and the market wants a fortune for a stone.
  • The golems on the terraces are made of the best grit in the kingdom. I see no reason to pay for it.
  • Bring me 25 Quarry Stone from the The Terraced Cuts. Then tell my husband, Bertrand, the new stones are coming, so he stops shouting about it.
  • Good stone, mind. Not chips.
  • Then the recruits sharpen on the cobbles. Bertrand will love that.
  • Twenty-five quarry stone, then tell Bertrand.
  • Twenty-five, and Bertrand is happy, which means the whole Court heard about it.
  • Thank you, Player. The numbers still won't come right this year. But this column does.
  • WHETSTONES? Real ones? From golems? HA! Tell my wife she's a marvel! No, don't, she'll put it in the ledger.

docs.title: Oak for the Wheel
docs.text:
Hereward needs the clangs off the Long Reach Banks so oak timbers can be floated down past them, and their claws for the wheel's iron straps, as the old millwrights did.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hereward Level 38 Leads to Something in the Race

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Bank Clang in The Long Reach Banks
  • Bring 10 Bank Clang Claw (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 19,010 EXP
  • 760 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Hereward
Dialogue
  • (He weighs his words.) There is oak upstream. Good oak, cut, waiting. It can float down past the Reach. It will not, while the Bank Clangs climb onto everything that floats.
  • Clear 40 of them on the The Long Reach Banks. And bring me 10 Bank Clang Claws. The old millwrights set clang claw under the iron straps. It grips the wet wood. My father swore by it.
  • Thank you. Mind the race on your way out. It's quicker than it looks.
  • (He nods slowly.) The oak will wait. The wheel may not.
  • Forty clangs and ten claws. You have (how many you carry).
  • (He turns a claw over in his floury hand.) Good. The oak comes down on Lucan's next barge.
  • That is more than I could do alone. (He weighs the next words a long time.) Thank you. Here.

docs.title: Something in the Race
docs.text:
Something in the mill race at night was strong enough to stop the wheel for the space of a breath. Hereward wants the crocos of the Undercut thinned, and Hawise told: he will not have her working the bank at night.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hereward Level 42 After Oak for the Wheel

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Undercut Croco in The Undercut
  2. Talk to Hawise

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,660 EXP
  • 840 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Hereward
Dialogue
  • Last night the wheel stopped. For one breath. Then it went on. Nothing in the race at dawn. Nothing in the grate.
  • The Undercut Crocos come downriver from the The Undercut. Thin them: 30. Then tell my wife, Hawise, not to drain the vats after dark. She will listen to you. She does not listen to me.
  • (He claps your shoulder and leaves it white.)
  • (He nods.) Then I'll sit up with the wheel tonight.
  • Thirty crocos on the Undercut, then a word with Hawise.
  • The wheel turned all night. I sat up and listened anyway.
  • Hawise said she'd drain at noon. She said it to you, not to me, but she said it. (Something like a smile under the flour.) Thank you.
  • Hereward sent you to tell me not to drain after dark? He could have told me himself! He'd rather weigh a word for a week.
  • Tell him yes. Noon only, from now. And tell him... no. I'll tell him. There's a jar under the dye shed he doesn't know about, and it's nearly full. That's all I'll say.

docs.title: Bitter Water
docs.text:
The churned soil smells bitter. Bring Hesper water from Shimmerwater so she can find out why.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Hesper Level 22 After Past the Last Lantern Leads to A Cleansing Draught

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 10 Lake Dew (taken)
  • Defeat 40 Shimmer Slime in Shimmerwater, the Second Path

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,672 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • +60 standing with Hesper
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Smell that soil from Merrow's beds. Go on. Bitter. Garden soil shouldn't be bitter.
  • The slimes came up from the lake. I want the lake's water. Bring me some and I'll tell you what's in it.
  • Bring me 10 Lake Dew from the water sprites at Shimmerwater, and clear 40 Shimmer Slimes from the second path while you're there.
  • Off you go. Don't drink any.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • (how many you carry) of 10. Keep at it.
  • Poison. Not much, yet. Something's seeping into that lake from somewhere.
  • The slimes aren't raiding the gardens. They're fleeing the water. I'm adding Shimmerwater to the back of my seed book.

docs.title: A Cleansing Draught
docs.text:
Hesper means to cleanse the slimes' poison with a draught of lake reed from the third Shimmerwater path.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Hesper Level 24 After Bitter Water Leads to Something Grey at the Lakehead

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 12 Lake Reed (taken)
  • Defeat 50 Sprite of Shimmerwaters (Water Sprite, Forest Sprite) in Shimmerwater, the Third Path

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,742 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • Mintleaf Salve x10
  • +60 standing with Hesper
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • If the lake is souring, its creatures will sicken, and sick creatures go savage. I can't cure a lake. But I can make a draught for the hurt ones who come to me.
  • Lake reed. It grows on the third path, where the sprites are thickest. They carry it about. Don't ask me why. Sprites.
  • Bring me 12 Lake Reed from the sprites on the third Shimmerwater path, and thin 50 sprites there.
  • Mind the sprites. They spit.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • (how many you carry) of 12 reeds.
  • Good reed. Good and green.
  • Celandine will make it up tonight. Take these salves. You've earned the first of them.

docs.title: Herbs from the Glimmer Path
docs.text:
The Glimmer Path is too dangerous now for Hesper's gardeners. Gather marjoram there for her.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Hesper Level 10

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Gather 6 Marjoram Flower

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 251 EXP
  • 220 mesos
  • Mintleaf Salve x4
  • +60 standing with Hesper
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • My gardeners used to gather marjoram along the Glimmer Path. Not any more. Not with the slimes on it.
  • You've got legs and a sword. That's two more than my gardeners want to risk.
  • Gather 6 Marjoram Flower from the marjoram along the Glimmer Path. Gather from a patch.
  • Good. Pick from the patches that look healthiest, and leave some.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Not done yet? The marjoram won't pick itself.
  • Good, good. You left some. I can tell.
  • Take these salves. You'll want them, out there.

docs.title: The Back of the Seed Book
docs.text:
More hurt travellers, with wounds that should not have come from the animals that made them. Hesper is ready to show her list to the seal scholars.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Hesper Completed with Caelum Level 40 After The Lost Season Leads to Three Kinds, Sharpened

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Hesper's List

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 21,418 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Mintleaf Salve x10
  • +100 standing with Hesper
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Another one off the northern path this morning. A Lupin bite. A Lupin, Player. Lupins don't bite like that. Not the Lupins I know.
  • I've kept a list for years. Every hurt traveller: what, where, how bad. I've never shown it to anyone at the Heart Tree. They've enough reading.
  • Take Hesper's List to Caelum in the Old Records. Don't let him spill ink on it.
  • Go on, before I change my mind.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Caelum. The Old Records, up the Heart Tree.
  • Is this... Hesper's? She kept this? For years? Every attack, where, when, what?
  • This is exactly what I've been missing. Exactly. Why did nobody tell me she had this?

docs.title: The Aristocrat Lock
docs.text:
The Open Table has agreed to open the iron door under the Great Hall, but nobody has ever opened its Aristocrat lock. Ask Leland, the old well-digger who watches the door, to show you the lock, and bring Hex the description.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Hex Level 20 After The Table Argues Leads to The Undercroft, The Returned Box

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Leland

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 870 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • +60 standing with Hex
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
  • Sets lowgrad.open
Dialogue
  • So the Table argued all night and decided to open the iron door behind the kitchens. I heard Bastian from here. Now they want a lock opened that the Walkers themselves gave up on a hundred years ago. And who do they send for? Riddle me that.
  • Me, of course. But I do not walk to a lock blind. A lock is a question; I want to hear it asked first. What shape, what studs, what wear on the metal, where the old hands touched it most.
  • Go to the Great Hall, Player. By the iron door there is an old well-digger called Leland who has been staring at it for longer than is healthy. Have him show you the lock, every inch, and come back and tell me.
  • Look at it the way you would look at a face. The scratches are the expression. Go.
  • No? Then it stays a door with nothing behind it, which is the most boring sort. Come back when curiosity bites.
  • Leland, by the iron door in the Great Hall, behind the kitchens. I want the lock described to the last scratch.
  • Hex sent you, did Hex? Good. Come here, bring the lamp. See: no keyhole. Seven iron studs in a ring, like a crown, and a plate in the middle shaped like a key, set into the door and not meant to come out.
  • The third stud and the fifth are worn bright. The others are dull. And the key plate has a scratch round it, as if it was turned, once, against the way you would think. I have dug wells under this city for sixty years and I never saw a lock that looked so pleased with itself.
  • Tell Hex all that. And tell Hex I have rope and lamps ready, for when it opens. If it opens.
  • Seven studs in a crown, a key that is not a key, the third and fifth worn bright, a scratch turned against the sun. Oh, that is lovely. That is an Aristocrat joke. They built a lock that tells you its answer and dares you to believe it.
  • (Hex is out of the door before you finish, tool roll under one arm. You follow to the Great Hall. Third stud, fifth stud, the key plate turned backward against the sun, a hard knock with the heel of the hand. Something deep in the iron goes clunk. The door breathes out cold air and dust.)
  • Ha! A hundred years! I could kiss it. I will not, it is filthy. Leland, somebody has to keep this door now, and the Table will name nobody else: you have stared at it longer than anyone alive. Keeper of the Low Door. It suits you.
  • Thank you, Player. A riddle for the road: what has been waiting a hundred years behind a door? Whatever it is, Leland will show you. Go and see before it gets bored.

docs.title: The Returned Box
docs.text:
Hex cannot remember the trick of an old walnut puzzle box that came back unopened. Something rattles inside. Hex thinks a good ear might hear the sequence: take the box to Drum.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Hex Level 32 After The Aristocrat Lock

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Drum

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,770 EXP
  • 1,920 mesos
  • +70 standing with Hex
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Confession, Player, since you have earned one. I opened a door the Walkers could not, and I cannot open a box I made with my own hands. The walnut one. It rattles. Every time I shake it, it rattles a little differently.
  • When I was young I made locks to music. Sequences like little tunes. I think the trick is a rhythm, and I have lost it. I have a good eye. I do not have the ear.
  • Take it to Drum on Lantern Square. Drum hears rhythm in buckets and kettles; perhaps Drum will hear one in a rattle. Do not let Drum hit it with a mallet. Probably.
  • Shake it gently by Drum's ear. Then do whatever Drum says, which will not be much.
  • Then it goes back on the shelf, rattling at me. We are used to each other.
  • Drum, on Lantern Square. Let the box rattle by Drum's ear.
  • (Drum stops playing, takes the box, and shakes it slowly by one ear. Then again. Then turns it over and shakes it the other way.) Tk. Tk-tk. Tktk. ... Tk.
  • (Drum taps the box: one face, then the opposite face twice, quick, then the top, then a pause long enough to count four, then the bottom.) That. Rattle says it. Wait on the four.
  • (Drum hands the box back and picks the mallets up again.) Tell Hex. Wait on the four.
  • Wait on the four? One face, the opposite twice, the top, wait on the four, the bottom... (click) ... Oh. Oh, of course. The rest. I always forgot the rest.
  • (The box falls open in four petals. Inside is a small carved wooden owl, and a folded note in a young, pleased hand: This box was too clever for its buyer.)
  • I wrote that. Twenty-eight years ago I sold a box with an insult hidden in it, to a stranger, and then forgot the trick myself. Riddle me this, Player: who was the buyer? Me, all along. Thank Drum for me.

docs.title: The Stamp
docs.text:
Hobart has four iron-bound crates in the back of the oldest warehouse that nobody has ever claimed, and a stamp burned into their lids that nobody can name.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Hobart Level 20 Leads to Every Plank of Her

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Kenwyn

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,775 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • +60 standing with Hobart
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Eh? Speak up. On the right. That's it. You've a sharp eye, they tell me. Come and look at this.
  • Four crates. Iron-bound, back of the oldest warehouse, older than me, older than the chalk on that post. Never claimed. Never opened. On every lid, the same stamp burned in: a three-masted ship inside a ring of rope.
  • Nobody on the docks knows it. Not Garrow, not the captains. But old Kenwyn, at the top of the salvagers' steps past the rope walk, has handled more old timber than anyone alive. Ask him.
  • On the right side, when you come back. And don't touch the crates.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Kenwyn, at the top of the salvagers' steps on the Waterfront, about the stamp on Hobart's crates.
  • The Saltgrace? The old wreck in the Bellcaves? Her stamp, on my crates?
  • Then those crates came off her, or went to her, a very long time ago. Chalk says four. Ledger says four. Nobody ever said where from. Go and see Kenwyn again; he'll want to show you.
  • A ship in a ring of rope? Burned in deep, the rope with a twist to it? I know that mark like my own hand.
  • That's the Saltgrace's mark. It's burned into her mainmast's foot and half her beams. She was a great trader in the harbour's first days, and she lies in the Bellcaves now. Tell Hobart. Then come back to me.

docs.title: Heavier Than a Broom
docs.text:
Hodge wants to know how a real fight goes, not a drill. Clear the pigs on the Hedge Lanes and tell Mab how it went, so she can tell it with cartwheels.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hodge Level 7 Leads to What I Saw From the Ridge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Pig in The Hedge Lanes
  2. Talk to Mab

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 100 EXP
  • 140 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Hodge
Dialogue
  • Psst. You fight real things, don't you? With a real sword? Is it heavy? Heavier than a... than a stick?
  • Go and fight 30 Pigs on the The Hedge Lanes and then tell Mab how it went, every bit. She'll tell it to the crowd at the Bell with cartwheels. Then I'll know too.
  • Out the Tree Gate. Pigs are easy. Probably. Tell Mab everything!
  • Aw. All right. Maybe tomorrow?
  • Thirty pigs on the Hedge Lanes, then Mab, by the Great Bell.
  • Mab did the whole thing with cartwheels. The pig charging, you dodging, everything. Three cartwheels for the last one!
  • So it IS heavier than a broom. I knew it. Here, I saved these. Don't tell Mum where I got them.
  • Hodge sent you? Thirty pigs! Tell it again, slower. Where did you stand? Which way did they run?
  • Right. Pig, pig, sword, cartwheel, pig. I've got it. The crowd's going to love it. Tell Hodge I'm doing it at noon.

docs.title: Hodge what i saw from the ridge
What I Saw From the Ridge
docs.text:
From the highest ridge of the old quarters Hodge has seen, every dawn, flocks of birds lift off the Waystone Meadows all at once, as if something startled them. Go and look, then tell Wat, who will know a shortcut back.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hodge Level 11 After Heavier Than a Broom

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach where the birds lift in The Waystone Meadows
  2. Defeat 30 Ribbon Pig in The Waystone Meadows
  3. Talk to Wat

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 300 EXP
  • 220 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Hodge
Dialogue
  • You can't see it from the street. Only from up high. Every dawn, out past the Tree Gate, all the birds on the The Waystone Meadows go up at once. Whoosh. Like something scared them.
  • Go and stand where they lift, and clear the Ribbon Pigs there: 30. Then tell Wat. Wat finds out everything, and he'll know the fastest way back.
  • Look for the willows by the river line. That's where they go up.
  • Fine. I'll go and look myself. Later. Probably.
  • Where the birds lift on the Waystone Meadows, thirty ribbon pigs, then Wat.
  • Pigs. Just a big herd of ribbon pigs, rooting about at dawn. They scare the birds up. That's all?
  • Huh. Good. I mean, I wanted a monster. But good. Wat says you're all right. That means you are. Here.
  • The birds Hodge sees? Ribbon pigs, was it? Ha. He'll be disappointed. He wanted a dragon.
  • Tell him I know a way back through the cart yards that beats the main road by a mile. And tell him you're all right. He'll want to hear it from me.

docs.title: Stern, Then Smiling
docs.text:
A traveller Hollis welcomed claimed he had come straight in off the Royal Road, but there was black bark dust on his boots. Bring 10 dark stump bark to compare, then tell Brann.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hollis Level 17 After The End of the Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Dark Stump Bark (taken)
  2. Talk to Brann

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,500 EXP
  • 340 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Hollis
Dialogue
  • I started stern, like the Sergeant says, then I smiled, like I always do. He said he'd come straight in off the Royal Road.
  • But his boots were black to the ankle with bark dust. That's not Royal Road dust. I think he lied to me.
  • Bring me 10 Dark Stump Bark from the The Rootlands, so I can be sure it matches. Then tell Brann. I'd rather he heard it from you than saw it on my face.
  • Thanks. I'm going to practise frowning while you're gone.
  • Maybe I'm wrong. I'd like to be wrong.
  • Ten dark stump bark, then the Sergeant.
  • It matches. Same black, same smell. He came from the Rootlands and said otherwise.
  • Still, I'd smile at him again. Is that a flaw? The Sergeant says it is. Mostly.
  • Bark from the Rootlands on a man who said the Royal Road? Hm. Hollis noticed. Good lad. That's why I never tell him to stop smiling. Travellers tell him things.

docs.title: Hollis the end of the road
The End of the Road
docs.text:
Hollis can't leave his post, and he has always wanted to know what is at the far end of a road. Walk the World Tree Road to the Rootlands, where it ends at the Tree's foot, and clear 30 of the monsters there.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hollis Level 14 Leads to Stern, Then Smiling

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach where the road ends in The Rootlands
  • Defeat 30 monsters in The Rootlands

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,300 EXP
  • 280 mesos
  • Orange Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Hollis
Dialogue
  • Can I ask you something odd? I stand here twelve hours looking down roads. I've never walked one to its end. Not once.
  • The World Tree Road ends at the Tree's foot, in the The Rootlands. Would you go and stand where the road ends, clear 30 of whatever's there, and tell me what it looked like? Properly. The light and everything.
  • Thank you! Look at everything. I mean it.
  • That's all right. The road will still be there. I hope.
  • Where the road ends, in the Rootlands. Then thirty there. Then tell me everything!
  • Roots like walls, and the Tree filling the whole sky? ...I knew it. I knew it would be like that.
  • One day I'll walk it myself. Till then, you walked it for me. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Home Again
docs.text:
Button is home. Dottie wants to tell her grandmother everything at last, and asks you to come with her. Then Rufus's cat and Molly's pedlar need telling too.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Dottie Level 45 After The Woodcutters' Hut Leads to Houses That Will Not Listen

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Elsie
  2. Talk to Rufus
  3. Talk to Molly

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 40,000 EXP
  • 6,000 mesos
  • +80 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player! He is back! Button is back! A man with a great many words brought him down the lane this morning with a cat on his shoulder, and Button walked straight to me as if he had been out for the afternoon.
  • Forty. Forty out loud and forty under my breath. And now I have to tell Gran. I never told her, you see. I said forty every night and it was a lie, and she must have known.
  • Will you come with me? Just to stand there. And then the cat is Rufus's, the pedlar said, and the pedlar is Molly's, so somebody ought to tell them. Will you?
  • Gran is in the farmhouse. Go on ahead and I will catch you up. I just need to count them once more.
  • Oh. That is all right. I will do it on my own. I will. Tomorrow.
  • First Gran, then Rufus, then Molly, Player. I have not lost my nerve. Very nearly, but not quite.
  • Dottie told me. All of it. The bramble, the tracks, the forty. She cried, and then I cried, and then the lamb ate my apron string.
  • I knew, Player. I knew a week ago. I was waiting for her to tell me. Now she has, and I can stop pretending not to see her walk to the woods every evening. Thank you for standing with her.
  • Mistress Whiskers! Back? She is back? Three weeks, and she comes home riding on a pedlar like a queen on a cart. Of course she does.
  • I shall have to cross her off my notices. No. I shall add a notice. HEAR YE: THE CAT IS HOME. Mildred will leave room at the bottom.
  • He walked in an hour ago, complained about the stairs, and fell asleep in the chair by the fire before he got to them. I took off his boots. There is a lamb's hair on everything.
  • There. I have crossed him off. Look, a nice straight line. That is the best line on the whole list.
  • Gran says I did right to tell her, and that next time I am to tell her on the first day, not the ninth. And Button is to sleep in the cheese room until he learns the woods are not for lambs.
  • Thank you, Player. Winnie gave me a tuft of his wool this morning, all wrapped up. She says she found it. I do not know how she found it. Here, take this.

docs.title: Houses That Will Not Listen
docs.text:
Since spring the mushroom houses nearest the woods have leaned away from the trees, and Bertie cannot hear them. Bring him a Paleveil cap from Breezy Hollow.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Bertie Level 46 After Home Again Leads to Where the King Came From

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Paleveil Cap

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 42,000 EXP
  • 7,000 mesos
  • +50 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Fifty years I have shaped these houses, Player, and they have always told me what they want. A bit more light here, a bit less rain there. You put your hand on the stem and you know.
  • This spring the ones by the woods went crooked. All leaning the same way, away from the trees. I put my hand on them and there is nothing. Like talking to a man with his back to you.
  • Rufus says the caps out in Breezy Hollow have gone pale. Bring me one, would you? A Paleveil Cap, off a Paleveil Cap. I want to hold it up to the houses and see what they do.
  • Just the one. Carry it gently. I would rather it did not get inside the town more than it has to.
  • Another time, then. They will keep leaning.
  • One Paleveil Cap from Breezy Hollow, Player. Just one.
  • Hold it up. There, by the yellow house. Do you see? It leans away from it. Like a dog from a stranger. That is the thing they lean from. The damp of it, the pale.
  • And Daisy's paint on these same houses cracks every morning. She thought it was her mixing. It is not her mixing. It is this damp, coming up from under, from the woods.
  • Now I know what they are telling me, I can listen. Thank you, Player. I shall put this cap somewhere far from my houses, and tell Daisy it is not her fault.

docs.title: A Still Evening
docs.text:
Hugh asks something he has never asked anyone: wait with Baldwin until the dais lamps are lit, then stand by the Great Bell and listen.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hugh Level 9 After Polish for the Dais

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Baldwin
  2. Look at the Great Bell's dais in Royal Plaza

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 140 EXP
  • 180 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • Scroll for Helmet for DEF 60% x1
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Hugh
Dialogue
  • Player. You brought the bubbles; you can be trusted with a small thing. It will be a still evening tonight. No wind at all.
  • Find my brother Baldwin when he lights the lamps. When the last lamp around the dais has caught, stand by the Great Bell a moment. Just stand. And listen.
  • Talk to Baldwin, then stand by the Great Bell's dais and press Up. Then come and tell me what you heard. Honestly.
  • Honestly, mind. Whatever it is.
  • Another evening, then. There will be other still ones.
  • Baldwin first, when the lamps are lit. Then the dais. Then tell me.
  • Well? ... You are not sure. No. Neither am I, some evenings. The lute, the crowd, one's own blood in one's ears.
  • It rings for a crowning and for no one else. That is the whole of my duty. ... Thank you for standing there, Player. Take this. And not a word to the dancer.
  • Hugh sent you to stand by the Bell? ... He has gone quiet on still evenings for a while now. I have never asked him why. There, the last lamp is lit. Go on, then.

docs.title: Polish for the Dais
docs.text:
Hugh polishes the Great Bell's dais every morning, and his polish is running out. The old Warden swore by a polish thickened with slime bubbles. Bring him some.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Hugh Level 7 Leads to A Still Evening

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Slime Bubble (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 80 EXP
  • 140 mesos
  • Red Potion x8
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Hugh
Dialogue
  • The tin is nearly empty, Player. Thirty years I have polished this dais every morning, and the old Warden before me swore by one thing for the stone: polish thickened with Slime Bubbles.
  • Do not laugh. It works. The Slimes on the The Hedge Lanes have plenty.
