  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You brought down the Bootbreaker, so you get a say. Bree wants its claw for her stall. I want it over the bar at the Salt and Bread, where every sailor who laughs at a crab can see it.
  • Delphine says yes, if it doesn't drip. Bree says she'll have the second one. Bring me a Bootbreaker's Claw. It drops when the thing goes down.
  • Clean it first. Delphine meant the dripping.
  • Another time, then.
  • A Bootbreaker's claw for over the bar. You have (how many you carry).
  • There. Over the bar, just above Halloran's stool. He looked up at it and didn't say a word, which from Halloran is a speech.
  • Thank you, Player. Next time someone tells me crabs are nothing to fear, I'll point.

docs.title: The Bootbreaker
docs.text:
The great crab moulting in the Pinch is where the bootcrabs come from. Keziah asks you to put it down.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Keziah Level 28 After Kit on the Lock Gate Leads to A Claw Over the Bar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Bootbreaker

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,467 EXP
  • 840 mesos
  • Elixir x3
  • +60 standing with Keziah
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Kit saw it. A shell bigger than his grandfather's workbench, moving in the Pinch. So that's where the bootcrabs come from. It moults in the lock, and its young go down the Cut to the sea.
  • Tristram calls it the Bootbreaker. Bree calls it something about Hesketh that I won't repeat.
  • Go up to the Pinch and put the Bootbreaker down. The old lock post at the end of the towpath will let you down into the lock. Watch the floor: when it slams, the stones crack.
  • Count the exits. Then don't need them.
  • Another time, then.
  • Defeat the Bootbreaker in the Pinch Lock. The lock post on the Pinch's towpath lets you down.
  • You did it. The Bootbreaker. Tristram owes me a drink; he said it would take three of us.
  • The bootcrabs will thin out now there's nothing moulting in the Pinch. For a while. Bree's going to want that claw.

docs.title: Fourteen Knots
docs.text:
Kit can tie fourteen knots, but he has forgotten the name of the last one Wilmot taught him. He sends you to ask.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Kit Level 20 Leads to The Shell in the Pinch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Wilmot

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,908 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • +40 standing with Kit
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • I know fourteen knots. FOURTEEN. Grandad taught me most of them and Mr Wilmot taught me the last ones.
  • But I forgot what the last one's called. It goes over, under, round twice, and then you pull and it holds forever. Nobody else knows it.
  • Ask Mr Wilmot what it's called! He's at the rope walk on the Waterfront. Then come back and tell me. I'll practise while you're gone.
  • Over, under, round twice... over, under...
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Wilmot at the rope walk what Kit's last knot is called.
  • A rolling hitch! That's it! Over, under, round twice, pull. Rolling hitch.
  • Now I know fourteen knots AND all their names. That's better than most sailors. Probably.
  • Kit's knot? Over, under, round twice and it holds forever? Ha. That's a rolling hitch, that is. Holds on a wet spar when nothing else will.
  • Tell him he ties it better than I did at his age. Don't tell him I said 'better'. Tell him 'nearly as well'.

docs.title: Kit the shell in the pinch
The Shell in the Pinch
docs.text:
Kit wants proof that what he saw in the Pinch was real. He asks you to look at the cast shell he saw by the lock wall.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Kit Level 27 After Kit on the Lock Gate, Fourteen Knots

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the great cast shell in The Pinch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,612 EXP
  • 594 mesos
  • +40 standing with Kit
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Everyone thinks I made it up. The shell in the Pinch. Even Poppy, and she believes in everything.
  • I saw it, by the lock wall, on the high bank on the left. A shell bigger than a door. Empty. Something MOVED out of it.
  • Go and look at the great cast shell in the Pinch, and come back and tell everyone it's real. Please?
  • Tell Poppy first. She'll be so annoyed.
  • Another time, then.
  • Look at the great cast shell on the high bank in the Pinch.
  • It's real. You saw it. It's REAL.
  • Poppy says she believed me all along. She did not. I'm going to draw it. Bigger than she can.

docs.title: Kite Laid Up
docs.text:
Kite has twisted an ankle and cannot run. An urgent message from the gate has to reach Perch's loft on the Crooked Tower before dusk, over the Rooftops.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Kite Completed with Perch Level 53 After What Waits at Dusk Leads to The Newest Lens

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Urgent Message

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,410 EXP
  • 3,180 mesos
  • +60 standing with Kite
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Do not laugh. I came down off the Wobbler wrong, and the Wobbler does not even wobble, that is the insulting part. Twisted ankle. Ivo says a week. A week! I have never been still for a week in my life.
  • And this came in from the gate an hour ago for Perch's loft. It has to go out with a bird before dusk, and the streets will take too long tonight, the market is setting up.
  • Take the Urgent Message over the Rooftops to Perch, up on the Crooked Tower. Please. I do not say please. You know it is bad when I say please.
  • Go by the roofs, not the stairs. You know the way. Tell Perch I am fine. Tell Perch I am bored.
  • Then I will hop. On one foot. Over the Fiddler's Crossing. You will hear about it.
  • The Urgent Message goes to Perch on the Crooked Tower, before dusk. Please do not make me hop.
  • From the gate, and in a hurry. Kite's knot on the string, too, but not Kite's feet. Ah. The ankle. Ivo told me this morning.
  • Thank you, Player. It goes out with Greyfeather's daughter before the light turns. She will fly this route at this hour. Whether she would fly it an hour later, I do not know any more. That is the trouble, these days.

docs.title: Rooftop Dash
docs.text:
Kite teaches Rooftop Dash only to legs that have done the roofs: touch the ridge, the gutter run and the chimney stack on the Rooftops, in that order, then come back.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Kite Level 20 Leads to The Crooked Tower Run

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the ridge in Urbanograd
  2. Reach the gutter run in Urbanograd
  3. Reach the chimney stack in Urbanograd

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,080 EXP
  • 3,600 mesos
  • Skill: Rooftop Dash
  • +60 standing with Kite
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • You there, Player, yes, you, the one looking up. Everybody looks up at the Rooftops and hardly anybody comes up. Well, you came up. That counts for something. Not much. Something.
  • I can teach you Rooftop Dash, the run my grandmother taught me: low, quick, feet barely touching. But I only teach legs that have done the roofs. Touch the ridge, then the gutter run, then the chimney stack, in that order, no stairs, and come back. I will be timing. I am always timing.
  • Go! Ridge, gutter, chimney. If the slates sing under you, you are doing it right. If they crack, you are doing it wrong, and Vane will want a word.
  • Ground-walker, then. Fine. Somebody has to use the stairs. They were built for somebody.
  • Ridge, gutter, chimney, Player, in that order. You can talk while you run, you know. I do.
  • Not bad! Not record-not-bad, I hold the record, but not bad. You land heavy on your left foot. Everybody does at first. My grandmother said I landed like a sack of cabbages.
  • Here: lean in, push off the back foot, and let the roof carry you. That is Rooftop Dash. Open your skills with K and put it on a key. Then come and try to catch me. You will not, but come and try.

docs.title: The Crooked Tower Run
docs.text:
Kite dreams of a run from the top of the Crooked Tower to the fortress gate without touching a stair. Run the line first, while Kite times it from outside.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Kite Level 26 After Rooftop Dash

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the top of the Crooked Tower in Urbanograd
  2. Reach the fortress gate in Urbanograd

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 3,120 mesos
  • +60 standing with Kite
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I have a run nobody has ever made. From the top of the Crooked Tower, where Perch's loft is, all the way down to the fortress gate, and not one stair. Not one! Cobble says it cannot be done in any boots he ever made, and he has made all of them.
  • I need somebody to run the line first, so I can watch from outside where it goes wrong. Climb to the top of the tower, then run for the gate. I will turn the sand-glass the moment you start. Will you?
  • Up the tower first. Say hello to the pigeons. Do not say hello to the cat, he takes it as an invitation.
  • Fine, fine. I will run it blind one day and tell you about it. At length.
  • Top of the Crooked Tower, then the gate, Player. No stairs. I have had the glass ready for an hour.
  • There! Did you see where you had to drop off the Long Lean? That gap, right there, that is where the line breaks. I knew it was there. I just needed somebody else's legs to prove it.
  • Not a record. Nobody gets a record on a line that does not exist yet. But your name goes on the back of Cobble's door under mine, as the first to run it. Smaller letters. Much smaller.

docs.title: Owls for the Watch
docs.text:
Knox wants to carve an owl for every post on the gate, and the best carving wood is the moss-cured bark of the Bristlewood's barkbacks. Bring him 10 pieces of Mossy Bark.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Knox Level 30

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Mossy Bark (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,220 EXP
  • 1,500 mesos
  • +60 standing with Knox
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I have carved Dagny so many owls she has run out of shelf. So I thought: one for every post on the gate. Something to sit with whoever has the watch.
  • Pine splits. Oak is too hard on the knife. But the bark off a Barkback out in the Bristlewood, the moss cures it, and it cuts like cheese and holds like iron.
  • Bring me 10 Mossy Bark? I would go myself, but somebody has to know every face that comes up the road.
  • Good. Out through the Outworks, past the far end, and into the trees. The Barkbacks are the stumps that move.
  • No hurry. The posts have stood without owls for a hundred years.
  • 10 Mossy Bark from the Barkbacks. You carry (how many you carry).
  • Feel that. Soft as cheese under the knife, and see the grain. This one wants to be a barn owl. This one is already a little owl; I only have to find it.
  • One for each post, and one for you, when it is done. Do not tell Dagny hers has bigger eyes. She will say I am making fun. I am not.

docs.title: The Highland Traveler
docs.text:
The old button-seller from the highlands walks down Stonefang Pass every season, and he has not come. Knox asks you to walk the Western Descent and clear the dark stumps from the switchbacks.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Knox Level 18 After The Late Egg Cart

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach Western Descent
  2. Defeat 20 Dark Stump

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,130 EXP
  • 1,800 mesos
  • +50 standing with Knox
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • You found the egg woman. Now I have another face missing. The old button-seller comes down Stonefang Pass with a sack of horn buttons the first week of every season. It is the second week.
  • He is slow on the switchbacks of the Western Descent, and the Dark Stumps there have taken to standing in the road. They look like old trees until they do not.
  • Walk the Descent for me. Clear 20 Dark Stumps off the path, and look for a grey beard and a big sack while you are there.
  • Out of the gate, then northeast through the Seepwater Foothills and up. Mind the boardwalks; they are rotten.
  • I understand. He is a stubborn old man. He may yet walk in on his own.
  • The Western Descent, past the foothills. 20 Dark Stumps, and a grey beard if you see one.
  • He came in an hour ago, walking like his knees were made of glass. Said the stumps had him penned on a ledge for two nights and then all at once the path was clear.
  • He gave me a button for whoever cleared it. I told him I would pass on his thanks instead; the button is for my coat. Thank you, Player. That is two faces back.

docs.title: The Late Egg Cart
docs.text:
Knox knows every regular on the Walkers' Road, and the egg woman's cart is two days late. Clear the stack rats round the Halfway Stone so she can come through.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Knox Level 14 Leads to The Highland Traveler

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Stack Rat in The Halfway Stone

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,440 EXP
  • 840 mesos
  • +40 standing with Knox
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The egg woman brings eggs up the Walkers' Road every fourth morning. Ten years, and she has been late once, the week of the floods. This is the second day she has not come.
  • A carter came through yesterday and said the The Halfway Stone is crawling with Stack Rats. They get in under the stone piles and run at the wheels. A pony will not go past that.
  • I cannot leave the gate. Would you walk down to the Halfway Stone and thin out 30 Stack Rats? Then her pony might be persuaded.
  • Thank you. Out through the gate to the Gate Meadows, then east along the road. You will know the Halfway Stone: tall, grey, and a crane leaning over it.
  • No matter. I will keep an eye on the road. I always do.
  • Thirty Stack Rats at the The Halfway Stone. She drives a brown pony with one white sock. If you see her, tell her Knox asked.
  • There she is, look, coming up past the meadows. Brown pony, white sock. I could hear her complaining from here, which means she is well.
  • I will tell her who cleared the way. She will try to pay you in eggs. Let her; she will not take no.

docs.title: A Word with Iska
docs.text:
Kor wants a seat in the race crew and will not ask for it. He would like someone to put in a word with Iska.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Kor Level 36 After Before Slack

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Iska

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,000 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • Sea-Mittens x1
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Kor
Dialogue
  • Can I ask you something? Not a favour. Well. A small favour, shaped like a question.
  • Iska picks the race crew soon. I'm not going to ask her. You don't ask the First Warden for a seat. You work where she can see you. I've been working where she can see me for about a year.
  • But if you happened to be at the Wardens' House. And she happened to mention the crew. You could say Kor reads a cross-sea faster than anyone on the quay. Which is true. Ask Corrie, she's written it down.
  • Would you put in a word with Iska? Just a word. Not a speech. She hates speeches.
  • Thanks, Player. Don't tell Jory. Don't tell anyone. Mostly don't tell Jory.
  • No, you're right. I'd rather she picked me for the rowing than for the asking.
  • Just a word with Iska, at the Wardens' House. Not a speech.
  • Kor sent you. No, don't tell me he didn't. He has been working where I can see him for a year. ...Tell him I have noticed. Tell him nothing else, because there is nothing else yet. The crew is chosen when it is chosen.
  • She's noticed? She said noticed? ...That's good. That's good, isn't it? Noticed is good.
  • Nothing else yet. Right. Yet is good too. I'm going to row round the inlet till I'm too tired to think about it.
  • Here, take these. Morag knitted me two pairs and I've only got the two hands. Keep the oar in the water, Player.

docs.title: Before Slack
docs.text:
Kor went through the gap before slack and had to put in on the Undercliff, where the Shore Crabs went for his boat. Clear 50 of them from the Undercliff.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Kor Level 30 Leads to A Word with Iska

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Shore Crab in The Undercliff

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,700 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Kor
Dialogue
  • Player! Have you got a minute? Have you got an afternoon? Better.
  • Last week I took a timber ship in a little before slack. A little. The run pushed my pilot boat onto the Undercliff and I had to put in on the boulders, and the Shore Crabs came at the boat like I owed them money.
  • Now, Nessa would say: wait for slack, Kor. And I would say: the tide likes me. So what I need is somewhere to put in for the days it likes me a bit less.
  • Clear 50 Shore Crabs off the Undercliff, would you? And don't tell Nessa why. Tell her you like crabs.
  • Down the steep way off the Gullwalk, then along the cliff foot. Go at low water. The beach drowns at high.
  • Fair. I'll just have to be lucky. I'm good at that.
  • Fifty Shore Crabs on the Undercliff. Low water's best. Not a word to Nessa.
  • Fifty! The beach is mine again. Well, the tide's. But it likes me.
  • Here, a share of my pilot's fee. Corrie wrote down that I went before slack, by the way. She has a page for it. She has a page for everything.

docs.title: The Boys' Lookout
docs.text:
Korrin and Kesh have a lookout above the terraces nobody knows about. Look out from it, then go and look at the far canyon bridge up close on the Broken Ground.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Korrin Level 30 After The Second Stick Leads to What Hallek Did Not See

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the boys' lookout in Midbarium
  2. Look at the near end of the far canyon bridge in The Broken Ground

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,700 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Korrin
Dialogue
  • The lookout is up on the little ledge above my mother's terraces, just over my head. Climb up and look east. On a clear evening you can see the far bridge, small as a thread.
  • Then go and look at the bridge up close, from the near end on The Broken Ground. You are allowed out there. We are not. Tell me what you see, and do not tell my father where we watch from.
  • Mind the wall at the lookout. We built it ourselves, so do not lean on it.
  • All right. But you swore on stone, so you still cannot tell anyone.
  • The lookout first, on the ledge just above the terraces. Then the near end of the far bridge, on The Broken Ground.
  • You saw it? The ropes on the far side, the frayed ones? That is where it was moving. I knew we did not dream it.
  • You will tell somebody, I know. Somebody should. Just say you saw it yourself from the bridge. That is even true now. Thank you for keeping the lookout, Player. Kesh and I will put a notch on a stick for you.

docs.title: The Tallest Ledge
docs.text:
Korrin swears the trail watch's scouts climb to the very top ledge of the North Ridge. Climb there and tell him what you can see.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Korrin Level 20

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the tallest ledge in The North Ridge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,750 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Korrin
Dialogue
  • Psst. You. You go out on the The North Ridge, right? Bekk says the scouts climb all the way up to the top ledge, the highest one, where you can see the woods and the whole sky.
  • I am going to be a scout. Everyone in my family laughs. But I cannot go up there yet, because my mother counts me like she counts water.
  • Will you climb to the tallest ledge on The North Ridge for me? The very top. And then come back and tell me everything you saw. Everything.
  • Yes! Climb like Bekk. He never looks at his feet. Well, he does. But fast.
  • Fine. I will ask Kesh. Kesh is scared of heights. That is why I asked you.
  • The very top ledge of The North Ridge! Then tell me everything.
  • You were up there? What did you see? The woods? Were they green? Could you see the Uskari Rim from up there? Could you see me?
  • When I am a scout I will go up there every day. Twice. Do not tell my grandfather. He says Kragvar climb scaffolds, not ridges.
  • Here. My mother gave me these for when I scrape my knees, but you need them more. I have good knees.

docs.title: Before the Still Pool
docs.text:
Lachlan has something to tell you before the last chamber.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Lachlan Level 24 After The A Mark Leads to The Inkmother

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach The Still Pool

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,800 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Lachlan
  • Unlocks boss.inkmother
Dialogue
  • Before we go to the last chamber. I have to tell you something. I have never turned back from anywhere in my life. Except once.
  • In the deepest cave I ever reached, I heard water moving. At slack. When it should have been still. I turned round. The Still Pool is past there.
  • Reach the Still Pool, the Sounding Caves' last chamber.
  • I will be right behind you. Mostly.
  • I understand. I did not want to either.
  • The Still Pool. Past the Long Echo.
  • You saw it. The pool breathes. In and out. That is the moving water.
  • Something lives in there. And I want my map finished more than I want to be safe. That is a bad thing to know about yourself.

docs.title: Ronan at the Mouth
docs.text:
Lachlan's rope is gone from the coves, and so is Ronan.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Lachlan Level 20 After The First True Map Leads to The A Mark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Mouths
  2. Talk to Ronan

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 870 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Lachlan
Dialogue
  • My rope is gone. The long one. And Sorcha cannot find Ronan.
  • He has been at me for months to take him to the caves. Go, quick, to the Mouths. I will look along the coves.
  • Go into the Sounding Caves' Mouths and find Ronan, then make sure he gets home.
  • Go! I will look along the coves.
  • Then I will go myself.
  • The Mouths. Find him.
  • Home safe, and sulking. I will give him his rope back when he is my height.
  • You went in. What is it like, past the mouth? No, do not tell me. Show me.
  • I only wanted to see! I was coming back. I was.
  • ...Do not tell Mum I went right in. I will go home. Can I keep the rope? No. All right.

docs.title: The A Mark
docs.text:
Deep in the Long Echo there is a tide mark scratched beside a letter. Lachlan wants to know who made it.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Lachlan Level 22 After Ronan at the Mouth Leads to Before the Still Pool

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Deliver 1 Gwenna's Old Map
  • Look at the tide mark by the A in The Long Echo

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,400 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Lachlan
Dialogue
  • Gwenna's map shows a passage she called the Long Echo, under the cliffs. Surges come down it. Time them.
  • Her map has a mark on it there. A tide mark, scratched in the rock. Find it for me.
  • Give Lachlan Gwenna's old map, then find the tide mark in the Long Echo (press Up there).
  • Time the surges. Hide in the alcoves.
  • Later, then.
  • The Long Echo. The tide mark.
  • An A. Beside the mark. And the mark is where the water was, the day he made it.
  • My grandfather Alasdair went a little way into the caves when he was young. He came out fast and never said why. This is where he turned back.
  • ...Give me a minute.

docs.title: The First True Map
docs.text:
Lachlan wants to make the first true map of the sea caves under the cliffs. Gwenna has old maps, and she has always said no.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Lachlan Level 20 Leads to Ronan at the Mouth

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Gwenna

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 870 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • Gwenna's Old Map x1
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Lachlan
Dialogue
  • A few dozen yards in. That is all anyone knows of the Sounding Caves, and it is all on my map. Nobody has ever mapped them properly.
  • Gwenna has old maps. She went in, years ago. She keeps saying no. Maybe she will say yes to you.
  • Ask Gwenna for her old maps of the caves.
  • Be nice to her. I have tried being charming. It does not work.
  • Ah well. She will say no to you too, probably.
  • Gwenna, at the Lantern Market.
  • She gave it to you? She gave it to you! And a lecture, I suppose.
  • We go in at low water, from the Fishers' Coves. Talk to me when you are ready and I will take you to the Mouths.
  • My old maps. Lachlan sent you. Of course he did.
  • Here. It is wrong in three places and it stops where I stopped. Read the lecture folded inside. All of it. Then read it again.

docs.title: The Inkmother
docs.text:
Something vast breathes in the Still Pool. Lachlan's map ends there.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Lachlan Level 25 After Before the Still Pool

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Inkmother

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,000 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Sounding Charm x1
  • +50 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Lachlan
Dialogue
  • An octopus. A vast one. Its breathing through the narrow ways is the moving water. That is all it ever was.
  • When you are ready, ask me to take you to the Still Pool, and we will finish the map.
  • Defeat the Inkmother in the Still Pool. Ask Lachlan to take you there.
  • Watch its arms. And the ink. Mostly the ink.
  • It is not going anywhere.
  • Ask me to take you to the Still Pool when you are ready.
  • The map is finished. The first true map of the Sounding Caves. I have written your name beside mine.
  • Take this. I found it on the pool's edge. It rings when you hold it near the water. I am sure of it.

docs.title: A Word from Rafe
docs.text:
Lambert does not know how a street juggler gets invited to perform for the queen. His old teacher Rafe might. Ask him on Theatre Row.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lambert Level 18 After Wood for New Clubs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Rafe

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,000 EXP
  • 360 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +110 standing with Lambert
Dialogue
  • New clubs, a routine to the last catch, and still no invitation. Clement was kind and promised nothing. I keep thinking: Rafe would know. Rafe always knows.
  • The trouble is he will not say it to me. He will say it with a puppet, and I will understand it a week later.
  • Would you go to Rafe's puppet booth on Theatre Row and ask him how a juggler gets to the palace steps? Maybe he will say it plainly to you.
  • Thank you! Watch his hands, not his face. That is where he keeps his answers.
  • Another time. I have nine clubs to keep in the air anyway.
  • Rafe's puppet booth, Theatre Row.
  • The puppet bowed to the crowd first, and then to the queen? ... Oh. Oh, I see. Play for the people until the palace hears about it.
  • That is it, Player. That is exactly what he showed me when I was ten, and I forgot it. Thank you.
  • Rafe says nothing. He lifts a little wooden juggler, makes it bow low to the children in front of the booth, then turns it, and makes it bow again, higher, toward the palace. Then he hands you the puppet's hat for Lambert.

docs.title: Wood for New Clubs
docs.text:
Lambert's juggling clubs are cracked. For the queen's festival he wants new ones turned from Dark Stump bark, which is light and hard as horn.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lambert Level 16 Leads to A Word from Rafe

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 12 Dark Stump Bark (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 800 EXP
  • 320 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +90 standing with Lambert
Dialogue
  • Look at this club, Player. See that crack? Another week and it goes into the crowd on its own, and not in the funny way.
  • If I am juggling for the queen, I want new clubs. Dark Stump Bark from the The Rootlands: light as a feather, hard as horn. A turner in the old quarters will make them up.
  • Bring me 12 Dark Stump Barks from the Dark Stumps at the The Rootlands, where the road meets the Tree.
  • Ha! You will be in the routine. Third catch from the end. I will point at you.
  • Fine, fine. I shall juggle carefully. Very carefully. The crowd will hate it.
  • (how many you carry) of 12 Dark Stump Barks so far. Up at the The Rootlands.
  • Feel that. Feel the weight of that. These will be the best clubs on Veligor.
  • Emmeline says I am to thank you properly, so: thank you properly, Player. And this, too.

docs.title: Lavinia a relic for the stage
A Relic for the Stage
docs.text:
Lavinia wants a real wonder on her stage, no questions asked: a piece of the amber comb from the great hive's queen.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lavinia Level 30 After An Ending by Friday, Queen of the Downs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 1 Amber Comb (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,580 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Scroll for Helmet for DEF 60% x1
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Lavinia
Dialogue
  • They say the great hive on the downs had a queen as big as a calf. They say her comb was amber.
  • A piece of that, darling, on my stage, in the fourth act. The gallery will gasp. I want the gallery to gasp.
  • Bring me a piece of Amber Comb from Queen Amberwing's hollow. No questions asked.
  • And not a word to Edith about where it came from. She will want to cut it up for buttons.
  • No? The gallery will not gasp, then. It will merely applaud.
  • A piece of Amber Comb, darling. The gallery is waiting.
  • Oh. Oh, look at it in the light.
  • The fourth act has its wonder. Now if only it had a fifth. Thank you, Player. You may call me Lavinia. Once.

docs.title: An Ending by Friday
docs.text:
Lavinia needs to know when the fifth act is coming, and she needs Tibb to carry the answer back to her slowly enough that she can bear it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lavinia Level 26 After Real Tusks for the Warrior Leads to A Relic for the Stage

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Crispin
  2. Talk to Tibb

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Lavinia
Dialogue
  • I have bet the savings, darling. And a loan on the building. And my name. I would like a fifth act by Friday.
  • Crispin will not answer me. He will answer anyone else.
  • Ask Crispin when the ending will be ready, then give his answer to Tibb. Tibb will bring it to me. He knows how.
  • Tibb softens things. I pretend not to notice. It is our arrangement.
  • Then I shall ask Crispin myself, and he will start a sentence.
  • Crispin, then Tibb. Then Friday, darling.
  • Tibb says Crispin says "soon". Tibb took four minutes to say it. That means "not Friday".
  • Well. I have waited fifty-seven years for this house. I can wait one more week. Thank you, darling.
  • Friday? She said Friday? I have... the fourth act is... I have five endings, Player, which is the problem.
  • Tell her soon. Tell her it will be worth it. Tell her, no, wait, write this down: tell her soon.
  • Crispin said "soon"? Right. I'll take it up to her. Slowly.
  • Leave it with me. By the time I get to her office it'll sound like a promise.

docs.title: Lavinia real tusks for the warrior
Real Tusks for the Warrior
docs.text:
Lavinia wants real boar tusks on the Savage warrior's costume in the Balrog War play. The gallery can tell painted wood from the real thing.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lavinia Level 22 Leads to An Ending by Friday

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 12 Boar Tusk (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,930 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Lavinia
Dialogue
  • Painted wood, darling. The gallery can always tell. And the gallery is where the money sits.
  • The Savage warrior will wear real tusks. Real ones, from the downs, where the boars have come up from the woods.
  • Bring me 12 Boar Tusks from the Downs Boars on The Thyme Banks.
  • Splendid. Do not haggle with the boars; I never do.
  • No? Then wood it is. And the gallery will know.
  • Twelve tusks, darling. Twelve. I counted the costume.
  • Look at them. Yellowed, terrible, magnificent. Edith will grumble about sewing them on.
  • Here, take this. And a ticket. No, not a ticket. A ticket costs money.

docs.title: Low Grad Rounds
docs.text:
The Warm Quarry does not stay quiet. Every so often Leland hears stone moving down there again. Go down, put the Warmstone Colossus down once more, and come back up. He will ask again, any time.

Town Urbanograd Category Repeatable Given by Leland Level 20 After The Warm Quarry

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Warmstone Colossus

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,560 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • +30 standing with Urbanograd

The first time you complete it instead: +40 standing with Leland, +30 standing with Urbanograd

Dialogue
  • I put my ear to the floor of the kitchen passage every night. Old habit. Most nights there is only water. Some nights there is stone moving, deep, slow, like something getting up.
  • When I hear it, somebody has to go down and put it back down. The Warmstone Colossus, once more. I will mark it on the map each time, and the city will know whom to thank.
  • Ask me and I will open the way. Same as before: potions, and mind the glowing floor.
  • Then I will keep listening. It is slow. It takes its time getting up.
  • The Warmstone Colossus, in the Warm Quarry. Ask me to open the way.
  • Quiet again. I heard it go still from up here, a long settling, like a house at night.
  • Another mark on the map. The Table hears about every one of them, Player; Rook reads my chalk tallies out. Come back when the stone moves again.

docs.title: The Floodwells
docs.text:
Below the Undercroft lie the Floodwells, the fortress's old cisterns, flooded halls crossed by narrow walkways. Leland needs them crossed and the floodwell eels thinned before he can chalk the way on.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Leland Level 22 After The Undercroft Leads to The Deep Roads

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Floodwell Eel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,000 EXP
  • 1,760 mesos
  • +60 standing with Leland
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The water at the bottom of the Undercroft stair: I know it. I dug a well down to it, forty years ago, from a yard off Workshops Row, and drew it up for years. Sweet, cold water. I never knew there was a hall around it.
  • The fortress kept its water down there once: great flooded halls, with walkways laid over the dark. The Floodwells, I am calling them on my map. The walkways are still there, most of them. So are the eels. Long, quick things, and they do not like lamps.
  • Cross the Floodwells and thin the Floodwell Eels: 40 of them. Keep to the walkways; I will not be able to haul you out of that water, my arms are old and you are not light.
  • Ask me to take you down. The Undercroft first, then the stair, then the water. Watch for ripples that move against the current.
  • The eels will keep. Eels always keep. Come back when you want to get wet.
  • Forty floodwell eels in the Floodwells. Keep to the walkways, and keep your lamp off the water.
  • Across and back. I have chalked the walkways, every one: there are more than I guessed, and one of them ends right under the shaft of my old well. I could see a coin of daylight up there. I nearly waved.
  • Past the far side the halls narrow into tunnels, long and straight, running out under the hills. Sally roads, from when the fortress was a fortress. Brindle will want to hear about those. They may run all the way to that wanderer's tunnel mouth.
  • Go and tell Brindle at the gate, Player. The Watch should walk those tunnels before I chalk them. Some roads are a keeper's business, and some are a captain's.

docs.title: The Undercroft
docs.text:
The iron door under the Great Hall is open, and Leland is its keeper. Go down into the Undercroft, the old keep's buried halls, and clear the dust drifters and creeping slimes that have had the place to themselves for a hundred years.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Leland Level 20 After The Aristocrat Lock Leads to The Floodwells, The Well Winch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Dust Drifter in Low Grad: the Undercroft
  • Defeat 30 Creeping Slime in Low Grad: the Undercroft

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,300 EXP
  • 2,400 mesos
  • +50 standing with Leland
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Keeper of the Low Door. That is what the Table called me this morning. I have been called a good many things down a well, and none of them so grand. I think they only chose me because I was the one standing nearest.
  • Fifty years I dug wells under this city. I have heard what is under the streets through a hand's width of stone: water moving, old rooms settling, things that echo where nothing should. Now the door is open, and I have put my lamp through it. The first level is the Undercroft: the old keep's halls, storerooms, dust up to your ankles.
  • And it is not empty. Dust that drifts against the draught, and slimes that creep along the shelves like they own them. They will have to learn otherwise before I can map past the first stair.
  • Go down and clear it: 30 Dust Drifters and 30 Creeping Slimes in Low Grad: the Undercroft. I will hold the rope and chalk the map as you go. When you are ready, ask me to take you down.
  • Good. Ask me and I will take you down. Mind the third step, it is not a step. And keep your lamp low; the dust likes to rise toward it.
  • No shame in it. I waited fifty years on the near side of that door. I can wait a few more days.
  • Thirty dust drifters and thirty creeping slimes, in the Undercroft. Ask me to take you down when you are ready. I will be here. I am always here now.
  • You are back, and grey to the eyebrows with hundred-year-old dust. I could hear you through the floor. I chalked the Undercroft while you worked: storerooms, a long hall, a stair that goes down and down.
  • Crates with the Aristocrats' marks on them, still nailed shut. Shelves fallen like dominoes. And at the bottom of that stair, water. A great deal of water. I could hear it from the top.
  • Rest. Eat some of Mags's stew; she has been sending bowls through the kitchen door all day out of curiosity. The water can wait one night. It has waited longer.

docs.title: The Warm Quarry
docs.text:
With Ferro's grate across the tunnel mouth, the only way left is down: the Warm Quarry, where the Aristocrats cut Old Grad's dark stone. Something huge stands in it. Defeat the Warmstone Colossus and bring Leland back a chip of the stone.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Leland Level 25 After The Iron Grate Leads to Low Grad Rounds, A Chip of Warm Stone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Clear The Warmstone Colossus
  • Bring 1 Chip of Warm Stone

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,270 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +80 standing with Leland
  • +30 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The grate is in. Ferro's iron, the Watch's padlock, and Brindle standing in front of it with arms folded until I chalked it on the map. The road in from the hills is shut. Good. That leaves the one road that goes down.
  • Under the Deep Roads the tunnels open into a quarry. This is where they cut the dark stone the whole fortress is built of. And the stone down there is warm. Not hot. Warm, like a hearth the morning after. I put my hand flat on it and kept it there a long time.
  • I did not go further. There is something standing in the quarry's heart, made of the same stone, and it moved when my lamp touched it. I am an old well-digger, not a fool. I came back up and chalked a large question mark.
  • Go down to the Warm Quarry and put the Warmstone Colossus down. Then bring me back a chip of the stone, a small one, so I can hold it up here in the light. When you are ready, ask me and I will open the way to it.
  • Take potions. Take more than that. The floor glows before it burns, I saw that much. Ask me when you are ready to face it.
  • Wise. It has stood there a long time. It will be standing there tomorrow.
  • The Warmstone Colossus, in the Warm Quarry, and a chip of its stone. Ask me to open the way when you are ready. Mind the glowing floor.
  • You came back up. I stood at that door the whole time with my hand on the rope, and I am not ashamed to say it shook. The rope, I mean. Let me see the chip.
  • Still warm. All the way up from the quarry, through the cold water, and still warm. I have dug in every kind of stone this city sits on, and none of it does that. I do not know why it does. I am not going to pretend I do.
  • Keep it. Somebody up here will want to look at it with better eyes than mine. Tinsel on Workshops Row has been trying to make glass glow for years; a stone that keeps its own warmth might interest a person like that.
  • Low Grad is mapped, top to bottom. Not understood. Mapped. The door stays open, and I stay by it. Whenever you want to go down again, Player, ask.

docs.title: Survey the Quarry Road
docs.text:
The waves are real, and Leofric wants the quarry road surveyed again by someone who can defend themselves. Walk the Deep Cut and clear the road through it.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Leofric Level 65 After The Waves, The Quiet Stretch Leads to Two Maps Agree, Hold the Deep Cut

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Deep Cut
  2. Defeat 60 monsters in The Deep Cut

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 146,000 EXP
  • 1,300 mesos
  • Elixir x10
  • Scroll for Helmet for DEF 60% x1
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Leofric
Dialogue
  • Gervase came round with his dates and a stack of notebooks. Waves, they say. I put my ruler on the map, and they are right.
  • I surveyed the quarry road myself, twenty-odd years ago. I would walk it again, but my wife says a consort with a measuring chain is not a defended position.
  • So I need it walked by someone who can defend themselves. Go to the The Deep Cut and clear the road through it: 60 of whatever stands up there.
  • Note where they come from. The direction matters more than the number.
  • No, no, quite right. Come back when you are ready; the road is not going anywhere. That is rather the trouble.
  • The The Deep Cut, 60 of them. Note the direction, if you can.
  • The marks run up the cuts toward the oldest face. Toward the First Cut. A line, Player. I said it was a line.
  • I will show the queen tonight. Thank you. You walked the road I could not.

docs.title: The Quiet Stretch
docs.text:
Not one report from the quarry road in six weeks, and that worries Leofric more than any red mark. Walk it from the Quarry Landing to the Spoil Heaps.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Leofric Level 51 Leads to Survey the Quarry Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Quarry Landing
  2. Defeat 40 Rubble Golem in The Spoil Heaps

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 47,000 EXP
  • 1,020 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Leofric
Dialogue
  • Look here, Player. The quarry road, above the The Quarry Landing. Not one red mark in six weeks.
  • Anyone else would be glad. I am a surveyor. A road with no reports is a road nobody is walking.
  • Walk it for me: up past the The Quarry Landing to the The Spoil Heaps, and if you find what I think you will find, thin out 40 Rubble Golems.
  • Count as you go. A surveyor's habit; it calms the nerves.
  • Of course. The map will wait. Maps are good at waiting.
  • The The Quarry Landing, then the The Spoil Heaps. Count as you go.
  • Golems. On the quarry road, and nobody walking it to say so.
  • Forty red marks on one day. My hand is not steady enough tonight. Thank you, Player; a quiet road is worse than a loud one.

docs.title: Two Maps Agree
docs.text:
Leofric wants his last marks fresh before he compares maps with his old colleague Gervase. Thin the Cut Golems of the Deep Cut, then take his copy to Gervase.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Leofric Level 66 After Survey the Quarry Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Cut Golem
  2. Talk to Gervase

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 89,600 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • Elixir x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Leofric
Dialogue
  • Gervase and I have not compared maps face to face in a year. He keeps his, I keep mine, and Peterkin runs between.
  • Thin out the Cut Golems in the The Deep Cut, 40 of them, so my last marks are fresh. Then take my copy to Gervase in the Scholars' Quarter. Tell him I said he was right. He will enjoy that.
  • Mind the copy, it is still... no, it is dry. Probably.
  • Another time. We have waited a year; we can wait a week.
  • Forty Cut Golems, then my copy to Gervase.
  • He said that? Ha. Seven years on the road together and we still hope the same things.
  • From Leofric? He says I was right? Write that down somewhere.
  • ...They agree. Every mark. Tell him I hoped they would not, either.

docs.title: A Venom Gland
docs.text:
Lessa has been cleaning drake bites from the watch's canyon trail and guessing at each one. Bring her 5 Drake Venom Glands from the Frost Drakes of the Chill Caves.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Lessa Level 24 After Back into the Dark Leads to Hollowmaw

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 5 Drake Venom Gland (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,700 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Lessa
Dialogue
  • Ketta came by holding out her arm for a scratch that wasn't there, and then told me about the cave. I have cleaned four drake bites from the canyon trail this summer, Player, and I have been guessing at every one.
  • I don't guess if I can help it. Bring me 5 Drake Venom Glands from the Frost Drakes in the Chill Caves, and I'll learn what their bite carries. Wrap them. And wipe your boots before you come in.
  • The glands sit under the jaw. Don't press them with a bare hand, and don't bring them anywhere near my kitchen.
  • Then I'll keep guessing, and I hate guessing.
  • (how many you carry) of 5 Drake Venom Glands, from the Frost Drakes of the Chill Caves. And your boots.
  • Five, and wrapped, and your boots are nearly clean. Let me look.
  • Cold. Their venom is cold, not foul like the gnawers' bites: it numbs, then it slows the blood. Rimwort is the wrong thing entirely. A warm draught and a firm wrap is the right one.
  • I'd have been treating it wrong all summer. Take these, they're the right thing for a drake bite now. Mud on the mat, though. I noticed.

docs.title: More Bites
docs.text:
Lessa is setting more bones than ever, and her splints keep cracking. Bring her 20 Iron Boar Armor plates from the Hot Rocks to bind them.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Lessa Level 44 After Grey and Bitter

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Iron Boar Armour (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 26,500 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • Bonesetter's Draught x10
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Lessa
Dialogue
  • Do not stand on that rug with those boots. Thank you. Now: more hunters on the slopes means more people falling off them, and more people charged by boars, and my wooden splints crack before the bones knit.
  • The Iron Boars on The Hot Rocks carry plates of hide hard as iron. Cut thin, they make splints that do not crack. Bring me 20 Iron Boar Armour.
  • And wipe your feet when you come back. I am not asking.
  • Then I keep splinting with wood and swearing at it.
  • Twenty Iron Boar Armour from The Hot Rocks. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Good, thick plates. These will hold a leg straight through anything.
  • Here, my own draught, for when you are the one who falls. You will be, sooner or later. Everyone is. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Grey and Bitter
docs.text:
Lessa's rimwort is nearly gone, and the Uskari have not brought any home since the hunts stopped. Gather 15 Rimwort on the Far Slopes and take it to Odda to dry.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Lessa Completed with Odda Level 35 After Fresh Cable Leads to A Message for the Old One, More Bites

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Rimwort (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,000 EXP
  • 700 mesos
  • Rimwort Tonic x10
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Lessa
Dialogue
  • Every bite you have seen this year, I cleaned with Rimwort. It is grey and bitter and it grows only on the far slopes, past the canyons. The Uskari used to bring it home from their hunts, but Skarra has not sent hunters out there since spring.
  • I have a handful left. I count the leaves now. Bring 15 Rimwort from The Far Anchor and the slopes beyond, and take it to my mother, Odda. She dries it the old way, better than I do, though I will deny I said that.
  • Take it to my mother, not to me. If it comes to me first I will use it fresh and waste half.
  • Then I keep counting leaves. Come back if the bites start coming faster.
  • Fifteen Rimwort for Odda. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Rimwort, and fresh. Lessa sent you to me, did she? She will have said I dry it better, and then said she would deny it. She is her father's daughter.
  • I learned to hang it in the shade, stems up, from an old herb woman of the Fairy Forest when I was an envoy there. A week, and it will keep through winter. The Brenna House thanks you, Player, and so will every bitten mason on the bridge.

docs.title: What Bites
docs.text:
Lessa wants to know the beast behind the bites she treats. Hunt 30 Cliff Gnawers at the Far Anchor and bring her 10 Gnawed Rope Ends so she can match the teeth.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Lessa Level 32 After What Hallek Did Not See Leads to The Night Watch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Cliff Gnawer in The Far Anchor
  • Bring 10 Gnawed Rope End (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,400 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Lessa
Dialogue
  • Something lives under the far end of the bridge, on the ledge where the ropes are anchored. Something small, toothy and climbing. The Uskari call the creatures there Cliff Gnawers and never think twice about them.
  • I want to think twice. Go to The Far Anchor, thin out 30 Cliff Gnawers, and bring me 10 Gnawed Rope Ends. Rope keeps the shape of a bite better than a leg does, and I can lay the marks beside Hallek's scar.
  • Do not let them bite you. And if they do, come here first, not after supper.
  • Then I keep cleaning bites without knowing whose they are. I am good at that by now.
  • Thirty Cliff Gnawers at The Far Anchor, and ten Gnawed Rope Ends. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Give them here. Look: two long front teeth, then the little ones behind, in a crescent. It is the same crescent I have on Hallek's leg, drawn in my book.
  • So it is the gnawers, and the bites fester because they nest in old rope and filth. Tell Vosk. He has been splicing those ropes twice this season and he still does not know what chews them.

docs.title: Hold the Lantern
docs.text:
Lettice needs someone to hold the lantern at the mouth of a deep tunnel while she goes in, and to deal with the rats that come out at it. Nip won't go first.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Lettice Level 22 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to Mice in the Flies, A Basket for Lettice, The Cistern Sluice

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Drain rats (Drain Rat, Black Drain Rat)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,440 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Lettice
Dialogue
  • Right. Here's a thing I've never said: I need a hand. There's a deep tunnel off the old channels, and Nip won't go in first. Nip goes in first everywhere.
  • Hold the lantern at the mouth while I go in, and deal with whatever comes out at it. Rats, I hope. 30 of them, Drain Rats or the black ones. Never go anywhere you can't back out of. That's why I need you at the mouth.
  • Down the Steps Lane grating. Nip, heel. Good boy. Brave boy. Mostly.
  • Fair enough! It's double for the deep tunnels for a reason.
  • Thirty drain rats, black or brown, at the tunnel mouth.
  • We came out! Both of us, and Nip. He went in second, which is a first.
  • They weren't hunting, Player. They were running past us, up toward the light. The deep rats are moving up. Here, and thank you. Truly.

docs.title: Mice in the Flies
docs.text:
Tibb says the theatre's mice have fled the under-stage for the flies, as high as they can get. Lettice wants the stirges under that end of the old quarters cleared, and to know which cellar wall is nearest the drains.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lettice Level 24 After Hold the Lantern Leads to Where Nip Won't Go

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Drain Stirge
  2. Talk to Tibb

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,410 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Lettice
Dialogue
  • Tibb brought me mice again. Two hundred and some on my cellar door now, the menace. But he said a thing that stopped me laughing.
  • The theatre's mice have all gone up into the flies, as high as they can get. Clear 30 Drain Stirges in the drains under that end, then ask Tibb which cellar wall is nearest the old drains. He'll know. He knows every rope and wall in that place.
  • Nip says hurry. Nip doesn't say anything, but he looks it.
  • I'll go and ask him myself, then. With a basket. For his mice.
  • Thirty stirges in the drains, then ask Tibb at the theatre about the cellar wall.
  • The east wall. The one that's damp all year. (She chalks a mark on her door, not for a mouse.)
  • Thank you, Player. I'll set traps along that wall tonight. Double rate. For the theatre, Lavinia can afford it. Ha!
  • Lettice wants to know which cellar wall? The east one. Damp all year, and the mice won't go near it. Haven't for weeks.
  • Tell her... tell her I've another basket for her. Not mice. Well. Mostly not mice.

docs.title: Where Nip Won't Go
docs.text:
Nip stopped dead at the edge of the buried street and would not go on. Lettice wants the black rat packs there cleared and Ida told exactly where the dog stopped.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lettice Level 28 After Mice in the Flies, The Buried Street

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Black Drain Rat in The Buried Street
  2. Talk to Ida

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,950 EXP
  • 560 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Lettice
Dialogue
  • It happened. The day I was afraid of. Nip stopped at the edge of that The Buried Street and wouldn't go another step. Sat down. Whined.
  • I'm not going without him. So you go. Clear 40 Black Drain Rats down there, then tell Ida exactly where Nip stopped: at the first claw-cut wall. She'll want it on the map.
  • Thank you. Nip thanks you. He's licking my boot, which is how he says it.
  • Then nobody goes. That's the rule, and it's a good rule.
  • Forty black drain rats on the Buried Street, then tell Ida where Nip stopped.
  • Ida marked it on her father's map, a little cross with a dog beside it. Ha! I'm keeping that map one day.
  • Nip's fine. He's eating. I'm fine. Thank you, Player, for going where we wouldn't. Here.
  • At the first claw-cut wall? That's where the new tunnels begin. The dog knew before we did.
  • (She draws a small cross on the map, and after a moment, a small dog beside it.) Tell Lettice she was right not to go on. Tell her Nip's the best scout under the city.

docs.title: Something for Aspen to Point At
docs.text:
Aspen must not notice the sleeping homes, or everyone will know by supper. Linnet has a plan.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Linnet Level 52 After The Homes That Will Not Wake Leads to Soil and Root-Water

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Aspen

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 46,612 EXP
  • 1,560 mesos
  • +60 standing with Linnet
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +80 standing with Aspen
Dialogue
  • Master Oriel told me. Don't worry, I won't tell anyone. But Aspen will notice, and Aspen tells everyone by supper.
  • So I've left a mend slightly unfinished on the high bridge. Aspen loves an unfinished mend. Go and sit with him at the Dewdrop and mention it. He'll talk about it for a week.
  • Sit with Aspen at the Dewdrop and mention the bridge.
  • Thank you. I feel terrible. It's a very small unfinished mend.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Aspen. The Dewdrop. The bridge.
  • He's told six people about my bridge already. Nobody's said a word about the homes.
  • I'll finish the mend tomorrow. Very slowly.
  • The high bridge? Unfinished? Linnet's work? Never! Well, I'll have to go and look. In my day, a mend was finished before supper.
  • Sit, sit. Have I told you about the bridge Oriel built in the year of the long rain? You'll love this.

docs.title: Water for a Secret
docs.text:
Linnet wants clear water and soil from a Bloomwood glade for her secret seedling home.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Linnet Level 13

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at a glade spring in The Bloomwood
  • Defeat 20 Glimmerwing in The Bloomwood

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 540 EXP
  • 286 mesos
  • +60 standing with Linnet
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • I need a favour, Player, and it needs to stay a secret. Master Oriel can't hear of it.
  • I've started growing a home. From a seedling. It needs water from a spring that's never run near the town, and the soil from beside it. There's a glade spring in the Bloomwood.
  • Fill a flask at the glade spring in the Bloomwood (examine it), and clear the Glimmerwings from around it while you're there.
  • Thank you. Gently with the soil. It's alive.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The glade spring is on the upper ledge of the Bloomwood, west of the road.
  • It's perfect. Cold and clear. She'll love it.
  • Not a word to Oriel. I'll tell him myself. Eventually. When she's tall.

docs.title: The High Bridge
docs.text:
A storm cracked a high branch-bridge. Linnet wants it mended before nightfall, with deadfall wood the forest can spare.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Linnet Level 28 After Past the Last Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Gather 2 Tree Branch
  • Look at the cracked high bridge in Fairy Forest

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,134 EXP
  • 616 mesos
  • +100 standing with Linnet
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Last night's wind cracked the high bridge by the lantern-makers. Before nightfall I want it whole.
  • I need a length of fallen wood. Fallen, mind. And a steady pair of hands on the bridge while I coax it.
  • Gather 2 Tree Branches from a fallen log (gather from one), then help mend the cracked high bridge (examine it).
  • Fallen wood only. Thank you.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The wood, then the bridge.
  • There. She'll hold. Feel her? Steady.
  • Thank you. Oriel will say I did it too fast. He'll be wrong.

docs.title: A Quarter of an Hour
docs.text:
Liri needs to sit still through Sorrel's listening lesson for a quarter of an hour. She would rather fight a monster.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Liri Level 12

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Road monsters (Slime, Bubbling)
  2. Talk to Sorrel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 428 EXP
  • 264 mesos
  • +120 standing with Liri
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Sorrel says if I sit still for a quarter of an hour I can learn something exciting. A quarter of an hour! That's forever!
  • I've got an idea. If you go and fight thirty slimes and tell me every single bit, I'll be too tired from listening to fidget. Then tell Sorrel I'm ready.
  • Defeat 30 slimes or bubblings on the Eastern Forest Road, then tell Sorrel Liri is ready.
  • Every bit! Every single bit!
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Thirty slimes, then Sorrel.
  • I sat still! A whole quarter of an hour! I heard a bird! A whole bird!
  • Sorrel said 'good'. Just 'good'. It's the best word.
  • ...Liri is ready?
  • Sorrel nods once. Later, Liri sits still for a quarter of an hour, and hears a bird.

docs.title: A Drawing of a Real Monster
docs.text:
Since the last lantern, Liri wants a proper drawing of a real monster for her wall. Juniper draws them.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Liri Level 26 After A Safer Way to See

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Sprite of Shimmerwaters (Water Sprite, Forest Sprite)
  • Talk to Juniper

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,127 EXP
  • 572 mesos
  • +150 standing with Liri
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Juniper
Dialogue
  • I saw a firefly slime from the last lantern. It was the best thing ever. Now I want a drawing of a sprite for my wall.
  • Juniper draws monsters. Real ones. If you help her catch one to draw, maybe she'll give me a copy.
  • Help Juniper by keeping 30 sprites busy at Shimmerwater, then ask Juniper for a copy for Liri.
  • Ask for a scary one!
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The sprites, then Juniper.
  • It's PERFECT. It's got teeth! Do sprites have teeth? Juniper says they do now!
  • It's going right over my bed. Mum says no. It's going over my bed.
  • A copy for Liri? Of course. Here: a forest sprite, life size. I added the teeth. They do have them now.
  • Tell her to look at it, not touch the real thing. Ever.

docs.title: The South Shore Verse
docs.text:
Lorcan needs a verse for the race shanty's stretch along the south shore. He sends you to walk the Long Sands and tell him what it is like.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Lorcan Level 18 Leads to Two Endings

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the foot of the western cliffs in The Long Sands
  • Defeat 25 Grey Tom

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,400 EXP
  • 396 mesos
  • +40 standing with Lorcan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • My friend! You walk the roads, I walk the bar. Between us we make one complete sailor.
  • The race goes round the south shore, past the Long Sands, and I have no verse for it. I have never been. I have a terrible sense of direction and an excellent sense of the bar.
  • Walk the Long Sands to the foot of the cliffs at the west end and look at it for me. And if the grey toms trouble you, trouble 25 of them back. Then tell me everything.
  • Notice the light! Poets need light. And the smell. Never mind the smell.
  • Another time, then.
  • The foot of the western cliffs, on the Long Sands. And twenty-five grey toms.
  • Pale sand for a mile, the cliffs rising grey, and the toms yowling at the surf. Oh, that's lovely. 'Where the cliffs fall back to the sand and the grey toms sing to the sea...'
  • Delphine! Put a drink for my friend on my tab. No, the other tab.

docs.title: The Long Way Home
docs.text:
Lorcan has heard that Wilmot has found the last verse of 'The Long Way Home', and he wants it sung at the Salt and Bread by the man who remembers the tune.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Lorcan Level 22 After The Last Verse

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Wilmot

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,524 EXP
  • 484 mesos
  • +40 standing with Lorcan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Player! The rope walk's been humming all day. Wilmot's found the last verse of 'The Long Way Home'! My father played that one. I never knew how it ended.
  • I could learn it. I will learn it. But it ought to be sung first by the man who's waited sixty years for it. Go and ask Wilmot to come to the Salt and Bread tonight and sing it. I'll play. Quietly. For once.
  • Tell him I'll play. Quietly. He'll laugh, but tell him.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Wilmot to come and sing 'The Long Way Home' at the Salt and Bread tonight.
  • He's coming? Wilmot? Singing? In front of people?
  • Then tonight the whole inn learns how it ends. Delphine, a table by the fire. For Wilmot. And put his drinks on my tab. The long one.
  • Sing it? At the inn? I haven't sung in front of anyone since Tamar... well.
  • Tell Lorcan yes. Tell him to tune that fiddle, and if he plays louder than me I'm walking out.

docs.title: Two Endings
docs.text:
Delphine told Lorcan to write two endings to his race shanty. He has written the winning one five times and the losing one never.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Lorcan Level 36 After The South Shore Verse

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Delphine

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,782 EXP
  • 792 mesos
  • +40 standing with Lorcan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Delphine says I must write two endings to the race shanty, or my tab grows a second column. A winning ending and a losing one.
  • I have written the winning one five times. The losing one is bad luck. Annis agrees with me! Would you ask Delphine if one and a half endings would do?
  • Be charming. On my behalf. Somebody should.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Delphine at the Salt and Bread about the shanty's endings.
  • 'Write the losing one and burn it, then you'll have written it.' She's a genius. A terrible, wonderful genius.
  • I'll write it tonight and burn it before the ink dries. Here, a drink on my tab. The long one.
  • One and a half endings? Tell him to write the losing one and burn it. Then he'll have written it, and the luck can't find it.
  • And tell him the tab doesn't burn.

docs.title: Lowen a bag for the heron
A Bag for the Heron
docs.text:
Lowen sails on the Heron soon, and his gran sewed him a kit bag after calling him a fool to the whole market. He is too embarrassed to fetch it.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Lowen Level 31 Leads to Stars on the Night Watch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Wenna

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,932 EXP
  • 682 mesos
  • +40 standing with Lowen
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Gran sewed me a kit bag. Double seams. After she called me a fool in front of the whole fish market.
  • I can't go and get it. She'll say something. In front of everyone. Could you get it from Gran? On the market steps? Please?
  • She won't bite. Probably.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fetch Lowen's kit bag from Wenna at the Fish Market.
  • Double seams! Look at it! It'll outlast the Heron.
  • Did she say anything? No, don't tell me. Yes, tell me. No. Thanks, Player.
  • For the fool? Here. Double seams. If it splits I'll know he's been carrying rocks in it.
  • Tell him... tell him his grandfather had one just like it. That's all.

docs.title: Lowen stars on the night watch
Stars on the Night Watch
docs.text:
Caspian promised to teach Lowen the night sky from the Heron's deck. Lowen wants the star chart Caspian keeps in Maren's old lesson book.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Lowen Level 38 After A Bag for the Heron

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Caspian
  2. Talk to Maren

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,651 EXP
  • 836 mesos
  • +40 standing with Lowen
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Caspian's going to teach me the stars on night watch. But he says I have to know the summer ones first, from Miss Maren's old lesson book. He won't tell me which page.
  • Ask Caspian which page, then ask Miss Maren if I can borrow the book. She likes you.
  • Ask nicely. She marks spelling.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Caspian which page, then ask Maren for her lesson book.
  • Page forty! The summer triangle and the Old Bain's Hook. I knew some of these already. Not the names.
  • When I'm navigator... I mean, when I'm a deckhand who knows the stars. Thanks.
  • Which page? Forty. The summer sky. It's in Miss Maren's old lesson book, the brown one. Obviously I know it by heart.
  • Tell him if he learns those by the next watch I'll show him the storm stars. No. Not storms. The other ones. The calm ones.
  • Page forty! Caspian remembers. Well, of course he does; he was the only child who ever learned all of it.
  • Tell Lowen he may borrow it if it comes back without salt water on it. And tell him his spelling of 'Kittiwake' was wrong in his last letter to me.

docs.title: Lucan a barge that must sail
A Barge That Must Sail
docs.text:
Lucan has a barge of grain that must sail tonight, whatever the river is doing, and not enough hands. Ride with it past the Long Reach Banks and clear what climbs aboard.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Lucan Level 36 After Torn Nets Leads to Seasoned Timber, Stone From the Landing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Long Reach Banks monsters in The Long Reach Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,700 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Lucan
Dialogue
  • Player! Just the face! I've a barge of grain for Hereward's mill, and it sails tonight or half the city's bread is late. Two hands short. Two!
  • Ride with her past the The Long Reach Banks. Clangs, lorangs, ligators: they climb aboard at the bends. Put 50 of them back in the river. Two to one you'll love it!
  • HO! Stand at the bow and look fierce. That's half of it.
  • Ha! Can't blame you. I'll find someone. Somewhere. Probably.
  • Fifty of anything on the Long Reach Banks.
  • The grain's in, dry, and Hereward nodded at me! He never nods at me!
  • You've the makings of a bargehand, Player, and that's the highest praise on the river. Here's your pay, and a bit over. Don't tell the others.

docs.title: Stone From the Landing
docs.text:
The builders want stone from the quarry landing, and Lucan's crews won't go past the Reach without someone at the bow. Meet the barge at the stone wharf, clear the banks on the way, and tell Bennet the barge came home dry.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Lucan Level 40 After A Barge That Must Sail

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the stone wharf in The Quarry Landing
  2. Defeat 40 Bank Clang in The Long Reach Banks
  3. Talk to Bennet

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,670 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Lucan
Dialogue
  • Stone! Half of Selsior's walls came down this river on my decks, and the builders want more. But the crews won't run past the Reach without a fighter at the bow. Can't say I blame them.
  • Meet my barge at the stone wharf on the The Quarry Landing, clear 40 Bank Clangs on the way down, and then tell Bennet she came home dry. He bet me she'd spring a seam. Ha!
  • HO! I'll see you at the wharf. Bring an appetite.
  • Another day! The stone's been there since the first keep. It'll wait.
  • The stone wharf at the Quarry Landing, forty clangs, then tell Bennet.
  • Bennet says the bet's off because his joinery doesn't spring seams, so it was never a fair bet. HA! He owes me something. Possibly a goat.
  • Good run, Player. Here's your share. And a little extra, for listening to me sing the whole way down.
  • Came home dry, did she? Of course she did. I built her.
  • Tell Lucan the bet was never fair, because my joinery doesn't spring seams. He'll say it adds to the wager. Everything adds to the wager.

docs.title: A Safer Way to See
docs.text:
Liri means to sneak past the last lanterns to see a monster. Lumi wants a safer way, so nobody has to tell on anybody.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Lumi Level 22 After Past the Last Lantern Leads to A Drawing of a Real Monster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Seren
  2. Reach the last lantern at dusk in Fairy Forest
  3. Talk to Tansy

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,524 EXP
  • 484 mesos
  • +100 standing with Lumi
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +80 standing with Liri
  • +60 standing with Tansy
Dialogue
  • Can I ask you a question? It's a big one.
  • If your best friend was going to do something dangerous, and she told only you, and you promised, would you tell her mum? Liri's going to sneak out past the lanterns to see a monster. I don't want to tell. I don't want her hurt either.
  • Find a safer way. Ask Seren if Liri may watch from the last lantern at dusk, take her there, then tell Tansy.
  • Yes! A safe way! Why didn't I think of that? I'll go and tell Liri. I won't tell Tansy. You will.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Seren first, then the lantern, then Tansy.
  • Liri says she saw a firefly slime at the edge of the trees, glowing. She says it was the best thing she ever saw.
  • Nobody had to tell on anybody. That's the best answer to a question I ever had.
  • Liri wants to see a monster? From the last lantern, at dusk, with you beside her? ...Yes. That I'll allow. She stays behind the light.
  • Better she sees one from here than finds one out there.
  • She what? With Seren's leave? And you stood beside her the whole time?
  • ...Well. I suspected something. Better this than whatever she was planning. Thank you, love. Truly.

docs.title: Questions for Grown-Ups
docs.text:
Lumi has questions that grown-ups won't answer. Lumi wants you to ask them instead.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Lumi Level 13

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Sefa
  • Talk to Aspen
  • Defeat 30 Road monsters (Slime, Bubbling, Glimmerwing, Crowned Glimmerwing)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 540 EXP
  • 286 mesos
  • +120 standing with Lumi
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • I have three questions. Grown-ups won't answer them. Why do slimes bounce? Why does Aspen tell the same story every day? Why does Sefa never say which stories are Sefa's?
  • Go and find out. You can fight slimes for the first one. That's research.
  • Research the first question (30 monsters on the roads), then ask Aspen and Sefa.
  • Write it all down! Or remember it! Remembering is fine!
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Slimes, Aspen, Sefa.
  • Slimes bounce because they're happy? You made that up. I love it.
  • And Aspen tells it every day so he doesn't forget. And Sefa says a story belongs to whoever's listening. That's three answers. That's the most I've ever had.
  • Why do I tell the same story every day? So I don't forget it, child. Every telling, I remember a little more.
  • Which stories are mine? A story belongs to whoever's listening. Tell Lumi that.
  • Sefa smiles. That is all you will get.

docs.title: The Beacon Ruins
docs.text:
Lux wonders whether the old Aristocrat beacons on the downs could carry a light again. Clear the downs howlers from the Beacon Line so Lux can look.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Lux Level 57 After The Lower Beacon Leads to The All-Hours Route

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Downs Howler in Beacon Line

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 121,560 EXP
  • 5,700 mesos
  • +70 standing with Lux
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Starling came down from the roof talking about the beacon towers on the downs. A whole line of them along the crest, built to pass a fire from one to the next. I have not slept properly since.
  • Lanterns on the walls, I understand. A light on every hill between here and the middle of the island would be something else. Pigeons that refuse a route might not refuse a lit one. Or they might. I would like to look.
  • The howlers have the Beacon Line. Clear 50 Downs Howlers from Beacon Line and I will come up behind you with a lamp and a tape and have a proper look at the old stones.
  • I will pack the long tape and a spare wick. I will try not to climb anything until you say so.
  • Fair. It is a long way to go for a hope. The beacons have waited a few hundred years; a few more nights will not hurt them.
  • 50 Downs Howlers on Beacon Line. I am ready when the ruins are.
  • I climbed three of them while you kept watch. The fire baskets are rusted through. The stairs end in air. One tower leans worse than the Crooked Tower, and the Crooked Tower is famous for it.
  • They cannot carry a light. Not now, and not with what this city has in timber and iron, which Vane will tell you is nothing to spare.
  • Yet. Write that down somewhere, Player. They cannot carry a light yet. A keeper is allowed one stubborn word.

docs.title: The Smashers
docs.text:
Lux wants to know what breaks the outer lanterns. Follow the smashers into the Outworks, thin out the lampbats and find where they roost: the cellars under the outer towers.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Lux Level 22 After Morning Prints Leads to New Panes

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Lampbat
  2. Reach The Outworks: Tower Cellars

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,150 EXP
  • 3,080 mesos
  • +60 standing with Lux
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Brindle's slate says the eyes in the dark and my broken lanterns are two different things. I believe the slate. Dagny's prints were all low to the ground, and my lanterns hang twice as high as a man.
  • Something flies, then. Only the outward side of the walls, never two nights in a row. I watched three nights and saw nothing. On the fourth one went.
  • Go out into the Outworks at dusk, Player, where the lights are. Thin out the 40 Lampbats that swarm them, and follow the rest home. I want to know where they roost.
  • The side path into the Outworks leaves the Gate Meadows. Watch which way they fly when the lanterns are lit. My guess is down, under the old outer towers.
  • I understand. I will sit up again tonight. Perhaps the fifth night is the lucky one.
  • 40 Lampbats in the Outworks, and then their roost. Follow them down into The Outworks: Tower Cellars.
  • The cellars under the outer towers. Hundreds of them, hanging in the dark, and wing marks on the stones wider than a market awning. That is not a lampbat. That is something they follow.
  • So: something big, every second night, and the swarm with it. That is why the lanterns are never smashed two nights running. I feel better and worse at once.
  • Better, mostly. Half the outer frames have no glass left, and I cannot light an empty frame. Tinsel will have to hear about this. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: The Twelfth Keeper
docs.text:
Lux, the twelfth Keeper of the Lanterns, sends you along the evening round: to Perch's loft on the Crooked Tower, and to Tinsel's furnace about amber glass.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Lux Level 20

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Perch
  2. Talk to Tinsel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,390 EXP
  • 2,400 mesos
  • +50 standing with Lux
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Every keeper walks the same round. Eleven of them did it before me, and I do it now, and I still learn something on it most nights. You live in the kingdom, Player, but have you ever seen this city from the lantern side?
