  • Walk two stops of it for me tonight. Tell Perch at the loft that the round is late, so the tea will wait. Then ask Tinsel for amber panes for the fog side. Tinsel will argue. Let it happen.
  • The loft is on the Crooked Tower, the tallest and leanest roof in the city. Tinsel's furnace is on Workshops Row. You will smell it before you see it.
  • Another night, then. The round is not going anywhere. That is rather the point of it.
  • Perch first, up on the Crooked Tower, then Tinsel's furnace on Workshops Row. Amber panes, for the fog side.
  • Late, is it? Then the kettle goes back on the coals. Lux always comes up the last stair very quietly, so the birds do not startle. I have watched every keeper's light come on from this roof since I was twenty.
  • Lionel Callow used to whistle on the way up. Lux never does. Tell Lux the tea will keep, and so will I.
  • Amber for the fog side. Lux says amber carries furthest in fog. Look. Hold this one up to the window with me. See how it goes gold at the edges?
  • It depends on the fog. Thin river fog, yes, amber. Thick wall fog, I would say rose. But Lux climbs up there, and I only melt sand. Tell Lux the amber will be ready by dusk tomorrow.
  • Tea waiting and amber by tomorrow, and Tinsel argued. Good. Then you have walked a piece of the round. Come with me a moment, to the lamp store at the foot of the first tower.
  • This beam. Eleven names, scratched in by whoever held the ladder. The first ones are nearly worn smooth. Lionel Callow's is the last. Mine is under it, crooked, because my hand was shaking.
  • Nobody walks the round alone, Player. The loft, the furnace, the beam. Now you know why I never mind the climb.

docs.title: The Lost Verse
docs.text:
One of the old songs about the Balrog War has a hole in it. Lyra wants the missing verse.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Lyra Level 16 Leads to A Song Nobody Asks For

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Aspen
  • Talk to Sefa
  • Defeat 40 Road monsters (Slime, Bubbling, Glimmerwing, Crowned Glimmerwing)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 992 EXP
  • 352 mesos
  • +120 standing with Lyra
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • 'The Seal-Song of the Grove.' The third verse is gone. Grandfather only remembers the tune, and he hums it wrong.
  • Someone old must know it. Grandfather's friends, maybe. Or Sefa, who knows every story and admits to none of them.
  • Ask Aspen and Sefa about the third verse, and clear 40 monsters off the roads so I can sing on them again.
  • Every song is worth finishing.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Grandfather, then Sefa.
  • 'And the grove stood still, and the grove stood true.' That's it! That's the line!
  • Sefa swore it wasn't one of Sefa's. Sefa always swears that.
  • The third verse? Hm hm hmm... no. I only know the tune. Ask Sefa. Sefa knows everything and admits nothing.
  • The third verse? Hmm. 'And the grove stood still, and the grove stood true.'
  • Is it mine? Ah. That would be telling.

docs.title: A Song Nobody Asks For
docs.text:
There is one old song nobody has requested in years. Lyra wants to sing it for someone who asks.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Lyra Level 33 After The Lost Verse, The Swarming Shore

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the bridge by the Dewdrop at dusk in Fairy Forest
  • Defeat 60 Creature of the High Shore or the Oaks (Evil Eye, Curse Eye, Cold Eye, Sharpened Lupin, Gloomfur Lupin, Surgeon Eye)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,337 EXP
  • 726 mesos
  • +150 standing with Lyra
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • There's a song nobody asks for. 'The Long Watch.' It's slow and it's sad and it's about the guardians who stayed behind.
  • Come to the bridge at dusk and ask me for it. And clear the shore, so the watch can come in and hear it.
  • Clear 60 creatures from the High Shore or the Hollow Oak, then come to the bridge by the Dewdrop at dusk.
  • Ask me properly. It's a proper song.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The bridge, at dusk.
  • You asked. Nobody's asked in years.
  • Half the Lantern Paths stopped to listen. Thorne cried. He says he didn't. He did.

docs.title: Tell Hodge
docs.text:
Mab wants her friend Hodge to know someone stood on top of the great waystone. Hodge runs the rooftops of the old quarters and thinks nothing is higher.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Mab Level 12 After The Great Waystone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Hodge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 310 EXP
  • 240 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Mab
Dialogue
  • Now you have to tell Hodge. He runs on the rooftops in the old quarters and he thinks nothing is higher than a roof. Ha!
  • Go to the Old Quarter and tell Hodge about the waystone. Make it sound really high.
  • Make it sound higher than it was, even. That's what Fulke does.
  • He'll find out anyway. I'm going to tell everyone.
  • Hodge! In the Old Quarter!
  • He said he'd climb the clock tower to beat it? He won't. ... He might.
  • Thanks, Player. You're nearly as good as a real performer.
  • The great waystone? You could see the palace? ... Huh. That's high. That's nearly as high as the bell tower roof. Tell Mab I'm not impressed. Tell her I'm a bit impressed.

docs.title: The Great Waystone
docs.text:
Mab heard that from the top of the great waystone on the Waystone Meadows you can see the palace. She is not allowed past the gate. You are.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Mab Level 10 Leads to Tell Hodge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the top of the great waystone in The Waystone Meadows
  • Defeat 20 Green Mushroom

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 440 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +90 standing with Mab
Dialogue
  • Psst. Player. Lambert says there is a waystone on the The Waystone Meadows so tall that from the top you can see the palace. I want to stand on it. I am not allowed past the gate.
  • So you stand on it. And then I will know it can be done, and when I am famous I will do it with a cartwheel.
  • Climb to the top of the great waystone on the The Waystone Meadows. And the Green Mushrooms there are in the way, Lambert says, so do 20 of them. For me.
  • Yes! Don't fall. Or fall in a good way, with a bow.
  • Scaredy. ... Fine. Later.
  • The great waystone, on the The Waystone Meadows. And twenty mushrooms!
  • You could see the palace? The whole palace? From all the way out there?
  • Then it can be done. I knew it! Here, Father says I have to give you these, for being nice to me.

docs.title: The High Pasture
docs.text:
The ridge pasture can be used again, and Mabbu wants to see it with her own eyes, though she has not climbed that far since her knees gave out. Walk her up slowly to the high pasture on the Long Ridge.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Sennu Completed with Mabbu Level 28 After Old Gnarl Leads to The First Report, The Herds Go Out

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Mabbu
  2. Reach the high pasture in The Long Ridge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,650 EXP
  • 560 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • Bonesetter's Draught x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Sennu
Dialogue
  • The herds went up at the new moon, with the watch on the switchbacks. Tavi was there before us. Neither of us said anything. It was the best morning I have had in a year.
  • Now my mother. She has been walking further every morning, and she thinks I do not see. Her knees gave out five years ago on a climb above the terraces, and she has kept the home camp ever since. She wants to see the high pasture again. She has not said so. She has said everything else.
  • Take her up, Player. Go to Mabbu at the home camp, and walk her up to the high pasture on The Long Ridge. Slowly. She will tell you to hurry. Do not.
  • Thank you. Two of our herders will carry her down after, whether she likes it or not.
  • Then she will try it alone one morning, and that frightens me more than stumps.
  • Go to Mabbu at the home camp, then walk her slowly up to the high pasture on The Long Ridge.
  • Sennu sent you, did she? To carry me up the ridge like a sack of wool? I will walk, thank you. You may walk beside me. And do not look at my knees, look at the path.
  • You took me up. All the way. I have not seen grass like that since before my knees went, and the herd on it, and the wind.
  • I told you to hurry eleven times and you did not listen once. Good. A herder who hurries on a ridge loses goats, and you would have lost an old woman.
  • Here, cheese, and the bonesetter's draught Lessa makes me take. I will not be needing so much of it, I think. Go and tell the Old One what you have seen; he will want to hear it from someone who does not count goats.

docs.title: The Old Springs
docs.text:
Mabbu remembers every spring that ran in the driest year. Check three old springs on the Dry Hills and hunt 80 Swollen Stumps there.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Mabbu Level 52 After Tell Your Mother Leads to A Shimmering Night

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the spring under the split rock in The Dry Hills
  2. Look at the spring in the white hollow in The Dry Hills
  3. Look at the spring at the foot of the long bank in The Dry Hills
  4. Defeat 80 Swollen Stump in The Dry Hills

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 86,000 EXP
  • 1,040 mesos
  • Rimwort Tonic x5
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Mabbu
Dialogue
  • So. My grandson told my daughter, and my daughter told me last of all, as if I were a cracked pot. The Greywater is dry. Sit down, eat something, and listen, because I am the only one left who remembers.
  • In the driest year of my girlhood we took the herds west, past the far slopes, onto hills nobody goes to now. Three springs ran there: one under a split rock, one in a hollow of white stone, and one at the foot of a long bank, the westernmost. They kept us alive.
  • Go to The Dry Hills and find them. Nobody has checked them in years, and the trees out there have gone grey and walk about, so thin them while you look: 80 Swollen Stumps. And eat before you go.
  • The Dry Hills lie past the far end of The Hot Rocks. The split rock, the white hollow, the long bank, east to west. Take some cheese.
  • Hmph. My knees would do it if they could. Come back when yours are willing.
  • Three springs on The Dry Hills, east to west: the split rock, the white hollow, the long bank. And thin the grey trees while you're there.
  • Well? Don't soften it for me. I'm old, not made of clay.
  • A trickle at the split rock, mud in the white hollow, and the long bank dry as a bone. Failing from the west, one by one, the way a fire eats a fence. That is not a dry year. Something is taking them.
  • Here, salve and tonic, Lessa makes too much of it anyway. And come and eat with me when you're back from wherever this takes you.

docs.title: Mabyn nicks on the boat hook
The Nicks on the Boat-Hook
docs.text:
Mabyn wants to know whether Jowan and Quenna still remember the stories of Old Bain's boat-hook.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Mabyn Level 20 Leads to Old Bain's Goat

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Jowan
  • Talk to Quenna

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,908 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • +40 standing with Mabyn
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Do you know, love, I taught every child who sat on that step the stories of the nicks? Jowan knew them all by seven. Quenna knew them before she could tie a reef knot.
  • I wonder if they still remember. Busy people forget the old stories.
  • Ask Jowan about the deepest nick, and the Harbour Master about the long one. Then come and tell me. If they forgot, I'll have words.
  • The deepest and the long one. Off you go.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Jowan about the deepest nick and the Harbour Master about the long one.
  • The capsized boat and the stern ring. And the fishing line in the fog. They remembered!
  • Oh, I'm pleased. Here, love, have a sweet bun. I bring one for Ottilie every morning; she can share.
  • The deepest nick? That's where Old Bain rowed into a winter storm and hauled a capsized boat home by its stern ring. Mabyn told me on the hall step a hundred times.
  • Don't tell her I said a hundred. Tell her I said 'often'.
  • The long nick? A fishing line in the fog, nearly took Old Bain overboard. She cut it with her teeth. Or her knife. Mabyn changes it.
  • Tell her I remember every word. And tell her the council can wait for her stories any day.

docs.title: Old Bain's Goat
docs.text:
Mabyn has never decided whether Old Bain's goat is true. Thaddeus claims his grandfather knew someone who knew.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Mabyn Level 38 After The Nicks on the Boat-Hook

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Thaddeus

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,651 EXP
  • 836 mesos
  • +40 standing with Mabyn
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Old Bain sailed round Veligor with her cousins and a goat. I've told that story fifty years and never decided about the goat.
  • Thaddeus says his grandfather knew someone who knew. Go and ask Thaddeus, love. He'll tell you more than you asked. Just bring back the goat part.
  • Only the goat part. He'll try to tell you about the race.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Thaddeus on the Waterfront about Old Bain's goat.
  • The goat was called Pepper and ate the mainsheet off Goa? Oh, that's lovely. It can't possibly be true.
  • I'm keeping it. Every word. Here, love, a sweet bun. Ottilie won't miss one.
  • Old Bain's goat? Of course it's true. My grandfather knew a man whose grandmother knew. The goat was called Pepper.
  • Ate the mainsheet off a Goa boat in the first race ever sailed. That's why the race began, you know. Now, about the race thirty-three years ago...

docs.title: Mags a stove that does not smoke
A Stove That Does Not Smoke
docs.text:
The Great Hall's kitchen chimney is as old as the fortress and fills the hall with smoke on cold nights. Carry Mags's challenge to Margo 'Sparks' Venn, ask Bastian about a bellows to help the draught, and bring the ironhide hog tusks Margo needs for her grate.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Mags Level 44 After Rooftop Greens

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Margo 'Sparks' Venn
  2. Talk to Bastian 'Bellows' Krell
  3. Bring 10 Ironhide Hog Tusk (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 31,020 EXP
  • 7,480 mesos
  • +80 standing with Mags
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Smell that? That is my chimney. It is as old as the fortress and it draws like a sulking child. Every cold night the whole hall goes grey, and the Table argues through it, coughing, and blames the Caller.
  • Twenty-two years I have shouted 'somebody invent a stove that does not smoke' in the direction of Workshops Row. Today I am sending somebody to shout it in the right door.
  • Go to Margo 'Sparks' Venn, the workshop with the smoke stains round the door, and tell her my kitchen is her next invention. Then ask my husband about a bellows; it is his trade, when he is not talking. Bring whatever Margo asks for.
  • Margo's is the door that has been blown off twice. Bastian is in the hall, or in his shop, or halfway between the two telling someone about a bridge.
  • Then I will keep shouting at the Row. One day the Row will shout back.
  • Margo, Bastian, and whatever Margo wants. You have (how many you carry) of 10 Ironhide Hog Tusks, if tusks are what she wanted. With Margo, who knows.
  • A stove that does not smoke? For Mags? Oh, yes. Yes! Listen. One: the smoke is not the fire's fault, it is the chimney's, the old flue is too wide and too cold. Two: so you warm the flue and squeeze the draught. Three: so you need a spark grate!
  • Let me explain it another way. A grate of tusk-and-iron bars, here, that throws a little spark when the fire settles, so it never sulks. No, a third way: it is a fire that keeps itself awake. Ironhide hog tusk takes heat without cracking; nothing else I have does.
  • Ten Ironhide Hog Tusks from the Ironhide Hogs on the Tusk Path. And a bellows to push the draught up the flue. Bastian makes the best on the Row. Do not tell him I said 'best'.
  • A bellows for the kitchen flue? For Mags? For MAGS? Player, I have been waiting seventeen years for her to ask me for a bellows. I have a speech ready. I will spare you it. Most of it.
  • A small one, a quiet one, if I can make a quiet one, I have never tried. Fixed under the grate, worked by a foot pedal so she can stir and pump at once. She will say it is too loud. It will not be. It will be a little loud.
  • Tell her it will be ready before the next Table night. And tell her I said yes before she finished asking. She likes that, though she will not say so.
  • A spark grate. A pedal bellows. My husband, quiet. I will believe two of those when I see them. Give me the tusks; I will walk them to Margo myself and stand over her until she starts.
  • If it works, the Table will argue in clear air for the first time in a hundred years. They will be able to see each other's faces. That may make it worse. We will find out.
  • Thank you, Player. You will always eat first in this kitchen. Grandmother would have said the same, only louder.

docs.title: Rooftop Greens
docs.text:
More of the great pot's greens come from the rooftop gardens every season. Go up to Old Parsnip's tubs near the Crooked Tower and ask what he can spare Mags this week.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Mags Level 26 After Tentacle Stew Leads to A Stove That Does Not Smoke

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Old Parsnip

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,500 EXP
  • 1,560 mesos
  • +50 standing with Mags
  • +20 standing with Old Parsnip
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Half the green in my pot grows on a roof now. Old Parsnip's cabbages, his leeks, his beans in the old bathtub. Twenty years ago I would have laughed. Now I would be lost without him.
  • Go up and ask Old Parsnip what he can spare me this week. Be polite to him, and be polite to the cabbages. He says they listen. I say who am I to argue with a man who grows leeks in a bathtub.
  • His garden is across three roofs near the Crooked Tower. If a big grey cat is asleep in a trough of catmint, you are there.
  • Then I will send Bastian. He will come back with no greens and a long opinion about leeks.
  • Old Parsnip, by the Crooked Tower. Greens. And mind your feet up there; I have fed enough people with sprained ankles this year.
  • Mags sent you? Good. Hear that, you lot? Mags's pot. Best place a cabbage can go. They like to be useful, cabbages. Same as anybody.
  • Tell her: the leeks are ready, the beans next week, and the cabbages by the old bathtub in three days, if the weather holds. Pounce slept on the open slates this morning, so it will. I will send it all down by Rivet's lift.
  • And tell her people are coming up for seed every week now. More than ever. I give it gladly. Every tub on a roof is one more mouth that does not need a cart.
  • Leeks now, beans next week, cabbages in three days. Down Rivet's lift. That old man is worth more to this city than half the Table, and do not tell Bastian I said so, he will want to debate it.
  • Thank you, Player. Sit, there is bread. Wash your hands first. I saw that cat.

docs.title: Tentacle Stew
docs.text:
Fewer farm carts reach the city, and Mags's great pot, never emptied since her grandmother's day, needs feeding. Bring her pool octopus tentacles from the Halfway Stone for the stew.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Mags Level 20 Leads to Rooftop Greens

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Octopus Tentacle (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,090 EXP
  • 2,670 mesos
  • +50 standing with Mags
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • You. Did you wash your bowl last night? You did. I saw. Good. Then you may stand in my kitchen, and you may hear about my problem, which is this pot.
  • My grandmother never let it go empty and neither will I. But the farm carts are late, the meat carts are later, and the Table eats like it argues: all night. The octopi down by the Halfway Stone are good meat if you stew them long enough, and I stew everything long enough.
  • 30 Octopus Tentacles, from the Pool Octopuses in the drainage pools on the Walkers' Road. Bring them and you eat first tonight, before the Table.
  • Out the gate and east to the The Halfway Stone. Off with you. And do not bring them through the hall, bring them round the back. Bastian faints at tentacles. He says he does not.
  • Hm. Then it is barley again. The Table will complain, loudly, and I will tell them whose fault it is.
  • (how many you carry) of 30 Octopus Tentacles. Not enough for the pot. The pot is very big. Have you seen it? You have. Go on.
  • Look at those. Fat as my thumb. In they go, and by midnight they will be tender enough to cut with a stern look. Grandmother would have called that a good haul.
  • Come by on a Table night and there will be a bowl with your name on it. Not really, I do not write on bowls. But you know what I mean. And wash it after.

docs.title: A Schoolhouse, One Day
docs.text:
Maren brings the children's work to every council meeting and asks for a schoolhouse. This year she has a lesson about the Old Cut to show them.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Maren Level 60 After The Shelf of Beach Finds

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Quenna

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 49,014 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • +40 standing with Maren
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The council meets tomorrow. Every year I bring the children's work and ask for a schoolhouse. Every year they defer it.
  • This year the children have done a whole lesson on the Old Cut: bootcrabs, sawbills, Poppy's chart. Would you give it to the Harbour Master? Ahead of the meeting. So she reads it before Corwin talks about costs.
  • Before Corwin. That's the important part.
  • Another time, then.
  • Give the children's lesson on the Old Cut to the Harbour Master.
  • She read it? All of it? And said 'put it on the agenda first'?
  • First! Not last, not 'any other business'. First. I shan't hope too much. I shall hope exactly the right amount.
  • Maren's children did this? A lesson on the Old Cut? With Poppy's chart? Look at the spelling. Better than the council's.
  • Tell her I'm putting it on the agenda first. Not last. First. Corwin can talk about costs after.

docs.title: A Lesson from the Cut
docs.text:
Maren would like to know what has come up the Old Cut before she makes a lesson of it.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Maren Level 22

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 5 Snapjaw Tooth (taken)
  • Bring 5 Glass Jelly Stinger (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,524 EXP
  • 484 mesos
  • +40 standing with Maren
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The children have heard there are creatures in the Old Cut. Kit came to lessons with a story about a shell bigger than a door. Finch has three.
  • I won't teach them stories. I'll teach them what's true. For that I need to see the things myself.
  • Bring me 5 Snapjaw Tooths and 5 Glass Jelly Stingers from the Cut. I'll label them properly and we'll have a real lesson.
  • Mind the stingers. I'd like them in the jar, not in you.
  • Another time, then.
  • Five snapjaw teeth and five glass jelly stingers. You have (how many you carry) teeth and (how many you carry) stingers.
  • Snapjaw tooth: long, curved back, set for gripping, not chewing. Glass jelly stinger: a barb ringed with tiny hooks. Labelled.
  • Tomorrow's lesson writes itself. Thank you, Player. That's the first time this year I've known what something on the shelf was.

docs.title: The Shelf of Beach Finds
docs.text:
Maren's grooved driftwood matches the sawbills' bites. She lends you a hand lens and asks for one whole sawbill bill so she can label her shelf at last.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Maren Level 35 After Long Straight Tears Leads to What Tears the Nets, A Schoolhouse, One Day

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Sawbill
  • Bring 1 Whole Sawbill Bill (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,429 EXP
  • 1,050 mesos
  • +60 standing with Maren
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Tegan says sawbills. Then the grooved driftwood on my shelf is a sawbill's bite, and I can label it at last. But I won't label it from a scale.
  • Here, take my hand lens. Most bills break when they die. Find me a Whole Sawbill Bill, unbroken, from a grown Sawbill. Thirty of them should give you one, if you're careful.
  • A whole one. Teeth and all.
  • Another time, then.
  • Thirty sawbills on the Salt Reach or the Sea Locks, and one whole sawbill bill.
  • There. Put it next to the driftwood. Look through the lens: the teeth are set in a line, and every one hooked backwards. The grooves match tooth for tooth.
  • Labelled. 'Driftwood, bitten by a sawbill.' I have waited three years to write that card. The children will love it, and none of them will be frightened, because now it has a name.

docs.title: Spark Powder
docs.text:
Margo's spark lamp needs a powder that flashes bright and burns clean. Ground ironhide tusk, she has decided, is the answer: bring her 15 Hog Tusks.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Margo 'Sparks' Venn Level 38 Leads to The Spark Lamp

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Ironhide Hog Tusk (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 25,230 EXP
  • 2,850 mesos
  • +50 standing with Margo 'Sparks' Venn
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Problem! The spark lamp sparks. But the sparks are small, orange and sad. Way one to say it: the powder's wrong. Way two: the powder's very wrong. Way three: it smells like burnt toast and frightens nobody.
  • Then I struck a flint against an ironhide tusk Hatch had on a string and nearly lost a finger to the spark. White! Hot! Wonderful! Grind the tusk fine and the powder throws white sparks a yard long.
  • I need 15 Ironhide Hog Tusks, Player. The Ironhide Hogs on the Tusk Path have them. On the hog, attached. Sorry. That's the hard part.
  • Wonderful! Bring them back whole, I like to grind them myself. Bolt likes it less. He sneezes.
  • No? That's fine. I'll keep trying toast powder. Maybe the monsters are afraid of breakfast.
  • (how many you carry) of 15 Ironhide Hog Tusks! Ironhide hogs, Tusk Path. Whole ones, please.
  • Look at them! Bolt, get the mortar. No, the big mortar. No, put the goggles on first. (A great deal of grinding, sneezing and one small, very white flash later...)
  • White sparks a yard long! The lamp's ready. Now all it needs is a real monster and someone brave. I know just the someone.

docs.title: The Spark Lamp
docs.text:
The spark lamp is ready for real boar. Go with Zip: she takes the lamp, you thin the bristle boars and ironhide hogs while she tests it, and then she brings it back to Margo, as she promised.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Margo 'Sparks' Venn Level 40 After Zip's Bank, Spark Powder Leads to The Rare Root

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway
  2. Defeat 30 Bristle Boar
  3. Defeat 20 Ironhide Hog
  4. Talk to Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 51,550 EXP
  • 8,800 mesos
  • +80 standing with Margo 'Sparks' Venn
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Torvi came back from Zip's Bank with the tracks measured. Big. Too big. Hatch says the beast that made them drives the lesser boar out of the trees and onto the road. So! If the lesser boar can be frightened back off the road, the caravans have a chance.
  • The lamp, explained three ways. One: wind it, point it, the boar runs. Two: wind it, point it, the boar runs, and you are not trampled. Three: if the boar does not run, you run. Zip has volunteered. Zip has also promised, on her grandmother's tubs, to bring it back.
  • Go with her, Player. Find Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway at the Gate Walk and give her the lamp. Then out to the Bristlewood: 30 Bristle Boars and 20 Ironhide Hogs, while she tries it on the rest. And bring her back. And the lamp.
  • Here. Wound, loaded, safety catch on. The safety catch is the little copper toad. Do not let her name it. She will name it.
  • Fair. Very fair. It might explode. It won't! But it might. I'll keep polishing it.
  • Zip first, at the Gate Walk. Then 30 Bristle Boars and 20 Ironhide Hogs in the Bristlewood. Then Zip, and the lamp, back to me. Both whole, please.
  • Is that it? Is that the lamp? Oh, it's beautiful, it's got a little copper toad on it! I'm calling it Sparky. No, Sir Flash. No, Sparky.
  • Torvi says I hang back and point, and if it doesn't work, I run first and you run second. I said heroes don't run. Torvi laughed like a rockslide. Fine. I'll run. Let's go find some boar!
  • Did you SEE that? FWASH! And the whole lot of them turned tail into the hazels squealing! Well, most of them. The big hog just looked annoyed. But it left! Annoyed counts!
  • Here. The lamp. I promised Margo. Grandmother always said a promise is a tub you carry all the way home. Tell Margo Sparky was very brave.
  • It's back! It's whole! It's slightly singed, which means it was used! And they ran? Ordinary boar, hogs too, ran from it? Bolt! BOLT! They RAN!
  • ...Sparky. She named it. Of course she named it. Well, Sparky has earned a spot on the wall where the door used to be.
  • Thank you, Player. It won't stop whatever made those tracks, Hatch is sure of that. But it'll keep the little ones off the road, and that's something. That's a real something.

docs.title: A Word with Papa
docs.text:
Marigold wants someone to ask her father, once more, about a child's part in the Balrog War play, and then to tell her mother she was very well behaved about it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Marigold Level 26 After Wings for a Bat

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Crispin
  2. Talk to Rosamund

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Marigold
Dialogue
  • The bat was a triumph. Tibb fell off a ladder. Well, nearly.
  • Now. I need someone to ask Papa about the part. Not me. If I ask he says "we'll see".
  • Ask Crispin whether there is a part for me yet. Then tell Rosamund I didn't sulk. Whatever he says.
  • Be persuasive. Use a pause. Like this... (a long pause) ...see?
  • Then I'll ask him. And he'll say "we'll see". And we won't.
  • Papa, then Mama. And I did not sulk.
  • "We'll see, but this time I mean it"? He has never said "I mean it" before.
  • That is practically a playbill. Thank you, Player. You may have my second-best sweet.
  • Is there a part for her yet? Not... not yet. But the truce scene needs a messenger, and the messenger could be... we'll see.
  • No, tell her: we'll see, but this time I mean it. She'll know the difference. She always does.
  • She didn't sulk? My daughter? Then she's learning the hardest part of the craft.
  • Tell her I'm proud of her. And tell her the bat was magnificent, and that if she goes near those drains herself I shall faint, for real.

docs.title: Wings for a Bat
docs.text:
Marigold means to prove she deserves a part by arriving at rehearsal as the most terrifying bat ever seen on a stage. She is forbidden to go into the drains. You are not.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Marigold Level 23 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to A Word with Papa

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Stirge Wing (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,600 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Marigold
Dialogue
  • I am going to prove I deserve a part. I shall arrive at rehearsal as a bat. The most terrifying bat ever seen.
  • The wings must be real. Stirge wings, from the drains. I am forbidden to go into the drains. You, I notice, are not.
  • Bring me 10 Stirge Wings from the Drain Stirges in The Old Drains. Do not tell Mama.
  • Excellent. You have been cast. Small part. Very important.
  • Fine. I'll be a moth. A moth is nobody's idea of terrifying.
  • Ten wings, Player. Real ones. Hush.
  • Oh, they're horrible. They're perfect.
  • Here, payment. I'm told this is what grown-ups give each other. Now: exit, and say nothing. That's the hardest part.

docs.title: Mariota a weak side for tobe
A Weak Side for Tobe
docs.text:
Tobe asked his sister whether golems have a weak side. Mariota would rather he heard it from someone who has fought them.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Mariota Level 59 After The Adventurer's Notes

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Quarry Golem in The Terraced Cuts
  2. Talk to Tobe

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 46,830 EXP
  • 1,180 mesos
  • Scroll for Topwear for DEF 60% x1
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Mariota
Dialogue
  • My brother Tobe asked me whether a golem has a weak side. He read it somewhere. Of course he read it somewhere.
  • I don't want him to learn from a book whether a book was right. Not about this.
  • Fight 40 Quarry Golems on The Terraced Cuts, then tell Tobe at the Knights' Court what you learned. Honestly.
  • And don't tell him I asked. Tell him you were passing.
  • Fine. He'll find out the hard way. That's how he finds everything out.
  • Forty on The Terraced Cuts, then Tobe. You were passing.
  • He listened? He actually listened? Well. He's never listened to me.
  • Thank you. Don't tell him I said thank you either.
  • You were passing? Mariota sent you. She always sends someone.
  • Low on the left, after it swings. Right. I'll practise that. Tell her the third cut's coming along. Don't tell her it isn't.

docs.title: Count Them for Me
docs.text:
Mariota wants a count from the Spoil Heaps, for a date she can set beside Theobald's night book of the same weeks.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Mariota Level 50 Leads to The Adventurer's Notes

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Rubble Golem in The Spoil Heaps
  2. Talk to Theobald

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,320 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • White Potion x5
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Mariota
Dialogue
  • Evidence. I need a date and a number from somewhere the stone has started standing up. The The Spoil Heaps.
  • Theobald keeps a night book of the same weeks. Sky down there, ground up here. Side by side.
  • Bring down 40 Rubble Golems on The Spoil Heaps, then give Theobald the count and today's date. He'll write it in.
  • Dates, Player. A number with no date is just a rumour.
  • Fine. I'll find someone with a sword and a notebook. Eventually.
  • Forty on The Spoil Heaps, then Theobald. With the date.
  • He wrote it in? Good. Look at that, next to his night. Nothing, yet. Which is also data.
  • Three things I'm fairly sure of. This makes the third one surer. Thank you.
  • A count, for Mariota? Forty, and the date. There, in the margin.
  • She has stopped telling me things, you know. I write down what she sends me anyway. Tell her that.

docs.title: The Adventurer's Notes
docs.text:
An adventurer at the Crooked Lantern keeps notes on every monster she fights. Mariota wants them very badly. Broker a meeting.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Mariota Level 57 After Count Them for Me, The Mason's Mark Leads to A Weak Side for Tobe, A Golem Core

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Constance
  2. Talk to Mariota

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 57,440 EXP
  • 1,710 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Mariota
Dialogue
  • There is an adventurer at the Crooked Lantern who writes down every monster she fights. Every one! Dates, places, what it did.
  • Do you know what that is? It is evidence. Years of it. And she has never once shown it to the Academy.
  • Go to Constance at the Crooked Lantern and ask if she'll lend me a book of her notes. Then come back to me.
  • Be polite. Be more polite than me. That shouldn't be hard.
  • Then I'll ask her myself, and probably argue, and she'll say no.
  • Constance, at the Crooked Lantern. One book. Ask nicely.
  • One season's book. She trusts us with one season. That is more than I would have done.
  • Here, take this. And don't look at me like that: I'm not going to tell you what I think yet. I'm going to check first.
  • A student of Morwen's school wants my notes? She wants them very badly, I take it.
  • One season's book. Not more. Tell her to bring it back with the corners straight.
  • She said yes? She said yes! Give it here. No, don't, give it here carefully.
  • Look at these dates. Look at them. I need a map. I need Gervase's map.

docs.title: A Barge in the Locks
docs.text:
A barge of Marisol's spices is stuck at the First Locks, its crates scattered by bootcrabs. She wants them back.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Marisol Level 22 Leads to Cargo by the Sea Gates

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Bootcrab in The First Locks
  • Bring 6 Spice Crate (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,524 EXP
  • 484 mesos
  • +40 standing with Marisol
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Darling, a disaster. My barge, bringing pepper in from the north quays, tried to come round by the Old Cut to save a day. The lock jammed. The crew ran.
  • And the crabs got into the crates. Bootcrabs, Bree calls them. They've dragged my pepper all over the towpath.
  • Clear 40 Bootcrabs at the First Locks and bring back 6 Spice Crates. I'll pay what pepper's worth, which is more than you think.
  • Mind the crates. Mind the pepper. Mind yourself, in that order.
  • Another time, then.
  • Forty bootcrabs at the First Locks, and six of Marisol's spice crates. You have (how many you carry) crates.
  • Six crates! A little nibbled, a little damp. Still pepper.
  • You've saved me a very difficult conversation with Cordelia. Here. And come by the shop; I'll make you something with that pepper.

docs.title: Marisol cargo by the sea gates
Cargo by the Sea Gates
docs.text:
Marisol's captains want to try the Old Cut again, now it runs salt to the sea. She wants the Salt Reach cleared first.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Marisol Level 34 After A Barge in the Locks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 monsters in The Salt Reach

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,106 EXP
  • 748 mesos
  • +40 standing with Marisol
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Darling, the captains have a notion: if the Old Cut runs salt to the sea now, a small boat could come in through it and skip the long way round the headland. Two days saved.
  • Not with sawbills on the towpath. Clear 50 of whatever's on the Salt Reach, and I'll send a barge through to see.
  • Two days saved is a fortune, sweetheart.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fifty of anything on the Salt Reach, for Marisol's barge.
  • The barge came through! Slowly, and with Tully poling, but it came through.
  • Here. And not a word to Cordelia about how nervous I was.

docs.title: A Theory for Margery
docs.text:
Maud has a new theory about what Dame Orsa did for the crown. Tell Margery, her oldest friend. Then ask Dame Orsa straight out, since Maud never has.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Maud Level 15 After Mushrooms for the Pie

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Margery
  2. Talk to Dame Orsa

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 600 EXP
  • 300 mesos
  • Red Potion x15
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +110 standing with Maud
Dialogue
  • Player, come close. Twenty-two years I have dusted that house and found nothing. No medal, no letter, no portrait. That is suspicious in itself.
  • My new theory: she sank a pirate ship. Single-handed. With a rope from her own stock. Tell Margery, she collects them.
  • Tell Margery my theory. Then go and ask Dame Orsa straight out what she did for the crown. I never have. Twenty-two years, and I never once simply asked.
  • Watch her face when you ask. Her face, not her hands. Her hands will be selling you rope.
  • Coward. ... I mean, quite right.
  • Margery first, then ask Dame Orsa. Watch her face.
  • She said what? "Long ago, dear, for service to the crown," and then she sold you rope? ... Of course she did.
  • Well. That proves nothing. Which is exactly what a pirate-sinker would want. Thank you, Player. I shall keep looking.
  • Pirates again? That is the fourth pirate theory this year. Tell Maud it is my favourite so far. Tell her I said so last month, too.
  • What did I do for the crown, dear? Long ago, for service to the crown. ... Now, have you rope? A good length of rope never hurt anyone. Well. Hardly anyone.

docs.title: Mushrooms for the Pie
docs.text:
For the first time in years Maud's dawn list has something no stall has: the mushroom pickers will not go out to the Waystone Meadows. Clear the Horny Mushrooms so they will.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Maud Level 14 Leads to A Theory for Margery

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Horny Mushroom

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 700 EXP
  • 280 mesos
  • Red Potion x15
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +90 standing with Maud
Dialogue
  • Mind the baskets, Player! And look at this list. Mushrooms. Mushrooms, for Dame Orsa's pie. Not one stall has them. Twenty-two years, and that has never happened.
  • The pickers say the Horny Mushrooms on the The Waystone Meadows have turned mean and butt anyone who bends down. Well, I am not having it.
  • Thin out 30 Horny Mushrooms on the The Waystone Meadows, so the pickers will go out again. I shall be at Margery's stall when you are done.
  • Good. Quick about it, the pie is Thursday.
  • Then Dame Orsa has no pie, and I shall tell her whose fault it is. Kindly.
  • Thirty of the horned ones, on the The Waystone Meadows. The pie is Thursday!
  • The pickers are out again? Good! A market should run out at noon, not at dawn.
  • Here, for your trouble. And mind the baskets on your way.

docs.title: Meg's Count
docs.text:
Meg is keeping count in the Inner Ward, and she wants your number in her book next to hers. Defeat 150 of the Inner Ward's Wallcreeper Caps and Crowncaps.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Meg Level 66 After The Inner Ward Leads to What Drove It Out

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 150 Inner Ward monsters (Wallcreeper Cap, Crowncap)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150,000 EXP
  • 9,000 mesos
  • Spore Draught x10
  • +45 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • One thousand, six hundred and three. That is my count. Snails, boars, Bluecaps, Capguards, all of it. It went up by forty just now. Do not ask how.
  • I have started a new page, just for the Inner Ward. One column for me, one for you. Whoever gets to a hundred and fifty first gets supper bought at the Sleepy Snail. Mott says he will keep the tally honest. Mott is very bad at keeping things honest.
  • 150 of the Inner Ward's Wallcreeper Caps and Crowncaps. Your column. Go on, I have already started. That is not cheating, that is a head start.
  • Ha! Catch me if you can, Player.
  • Then I win by default. You can still buy supper.
  • A hundred and fifty in the Inner Ward, Player. Your column is looking very empty from here.
  • A hundred and fifty. You got there first. I counted. Then I counted again and added a few to mine, and you still got there first.
  • Do you know what? I do not mind. Last spring I ran all the way home from that clearing. This summer I have been inside the walls every day, and I have not run once. That is a better count than any of them.
  • Supper is on me, then. Take these too, Bram made too many and I hate the taste. Now go and tell Hale the ward is quiet. He will pretend he already knew.

docs.title: An Envoy Overdue
docs.text:
An envoy is nine days late, coming by the river because the road was worse. Clear the crabs from the Long Reach towpath and ask Petronella when the last letter was written.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Melisende Level 33 Leads to The Quarrel over Carts

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Long Reach Banks
  2. Defeat 40 Bank Lorang
  3. Talk to Petronella

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,800 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Melisende
Dialogue
  • An envoy's room has been ready for nine days: windows open, sea salt on the bread. The envoy has not come.
  • The bargemen of the Long Reach say the towpath is crawling with crabs as big as cartwheels. Envoys do not care for crabs.
  • Go along the The Long Reach Banks and clear the towpath: 40 Bank Lorangs. Then ask Petronella when the envoy's last letter was written; she copies them all.
  • Thank you. Calmly, now. Nothing is lost by arriving composed.
  • Of course. I shall keep the bread warm a little longer.
  • The The Long Reach Banks, forty Bank Lorangs, then Petronella.
  • Eleven days, by the river, because the road was worse.
  • Then the towpath you cleared is the one they will walk. Thank you, Player. I shall have the bread warmed.
  • The envoy's last letter? Eleven days ago, sealed in a hurry. The seal was cracked, naturally. They all are now.
  • Tell Melisende it said 'by the river; the road is worse'. The river was meant to be the safe way.

docs.title: The Quarrel over Carts
docs.text:
Two envoys have quarrelled all week over who pays the guards on the river carts. Clear the Long Reach Banks, then take the news to the queen for her one sentence.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Melisende Level 38 After An Envoy Overdue

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 50 monsters in The Long Reach Banks
  2. Talk to Aveline

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 23,000 EXP
  • 760 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +25 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Melisende
Dialogue
  • Two envoys have quarrelled at my table all week over who should pay the guards on the river carts. A year ago they quarrelled over the price of wool.
  • I would rather they had nothing to guard against. Failing that, a little less.
  • Clear the The Long Reach Banks: 50 of whatever walks the towpath. Then go to the queen and tell her the banks are clear; she will want one sentence to end this with.
  • Thank you. Tell Her Majesty the facts, and let her find the sentence.
  • Then they will quarrel another week. They enjoy it more than they admit.
  • Fifty on the The Long Reach Banks, then the queen.
  • 'The crown pays the first month, and the towns the rest.' Of course. Nobody else thought to say it.
  • Thank you, Player. Tonight I can seat them side by side.
  • The banks are clear? Then there is less to pay for, and less to quarrel over.
  • Tell Melisende: 'The crown pays the first month, and the towns the rest.' One sentence. She will know how to serve it.

docs.title: A Stone Run
docs.text:
Merrick is hiring guards at twice his rate for a stone run up to the quarries, and won't say what he's carrying. Clear the road: 30 monsters on the Spoil Heaps and 30 on the Terraced Cuts.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Merrick Level 54 Leads to The Empty Wagon

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 monsters in The Spoil Heaps
  • Defeat 30 monsters in The Terraced Cuts

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 40,000 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Merrick
Dialogue
  • You! Yes, you, the one looking at the trees. Good. That's the right thing to look at.
  • A run up to the quarries. Twice my rate. Don't ask what's in the wagons, because I won't tell you, and I'll think less of you for asking.
  • My wagons go up the The Spoil Heaps and on to the The Terraced Cuts. Clear 30 of whatever's walking on each, and the road's mine for a day. Twice the rate. I said that already. It's still true.
  • Ha! Knew it by the way you stand. Go on, then.
  • Then I'll find someone else, and pay them twice the rate instead of you.
  • Thirty on the Spoil Heaps, thirty on the Terraced Cuts. My wagons are greased and waiting.
  • Road's clear, wagons are rolling, and nobody's asked me what's in them. Perfect.
  • Twice the rate, as promised. Merrick delivers on the day he says.

docs.title: The Empty Wagon
docs.text:
One of Merrick's wagons came back from the terraces with its driver and oxen safe and its cargo gone. Find the wagon bed on the Terraced Cuts, clear 40 quarry golems around it, then tell Edric.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Merrick Level 57 After A Stone Run

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the empty wagon bed in The Terraced Cuts
  2. Defeat 40 Quarry Golem in The Terraced Cuts
  3. Talk to Edric

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,000 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • White Potion x25
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Merrick
Dialogue
  • Driver's safe. Oxen safe. Cargo gone. He can't say what took it. He tried four times and went white every time.
  • Never lost a driver, and I'm not starting now. But I want to know what's walking off with my loads.
  • The wagon bed's still up on the The Terraced Cuts; we cut the oxen loose and ran. Look it over, clear the 40 Quarry Golems around it, then tell Edric. He'll want it in a report.
  • Look at the stone, not the wagon. The wagon's just wood.
  • Then it stays up there, and I price the terraces at three times. Nobody will pay it.
  • The wagon bed, forty golems, then Edric.
  • Gravel and dust in the wagon bed, you say, and the golems standing round it like they'd been there forever.
  • Edric's put it in a report, and I've put it on the bill. Here. You earned the rate, and a bit.
  • Merrick's wagon? ...Gravel where the cargo was. Right. It goes in tonight's report. Tell him he still owes me for the stones he threw at the horses.

docs.title: Merrin a crew of her own
A Crew of Her Own
docs.text:
Merrin wants a crew to lead. Clear 50 Wrack Boars round her cutting, then ask Haldor about it, straight.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Merrin Level 25 After Merrin's Tally Leads to Rules This Time

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 50 Wrack Boar
  2. Talk to Haldor

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,300 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x3
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Merrin
Dialogue
  • I've asked Haldor for a crew of my own three times. He says I'll get one. That's all I need to hear, really, so why hasn't it happened yet?
  • I think he needs to see I can keep a cutting safe. The boars come up out of the weed every time a tree goes down. If my pair cut the cleanest edge on the shore, he can't say no.
  • Clear 50 Wrack Boars from Strandwood Edge, round the stumps my pair is working. Then go and ask Haldor about my crew. Ask him straight. He answers people straight, when they're not me.
  • I'll be swinging. You'll hear me.
  • Then I'll ask him a fourth time. Fourth time's the one, everybody knows that.
  • Fifty Wrack Boars from round my stumps, then Haldor. Straight, mind. No hedging for my sake.
  • Did she send you? Aye, she would. Tell her what I've told her: she'll get a crew, and she's not ready yet. Both halves, Player. She keeps dropping the second one. And tell her the edge she kept today was clean. That's true as well.
  • Well? What did he say?
  • That I'll get one! I knew it. He always says that.
  • A second half? There's always a second half with Haldor. I'll hear it once I've got the crew. Here, for the boars.

docs.title: Rules This Time
docs.text:
Merrin will race Kenna again, with rules this time. Carry the challenge to Kenna, then clear 60 monsters off Strandwood Rocks.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Merrin Level 29 After A Crew of Her Own

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Kenna
  2. Defeat 60 monsters in Strandwood Rocks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,800 EXP
  • 1,160 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x5
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Merrin
Dialogue
  • Kenna was at the edge again today, watching my crew work and telling the other hunters I cheated in a race when we were nine. Ten years. She's still on about it.
  • Raft landing to the end of the point and back, at low tide. She was ahead at the turn. I came back over the rocks because it was shorter. Nobody made any rules. That's the first line of my tally, and it's staying there.
  • But fine. If she wants it run again, we'll run it again, with rules this time. Any rules she likes. I'll still win.
  • Go and tell Kenna that. Then clear 60 monsters off Strandwood Rocks, because nobody is racing over that weed with foxes in it. Not even me.
  • Say it just like I said it. Any rules she likes. Make sure she hears the bit about me winning.
  • Suit yourself. She'll be on about it for another ten years, then.
  • Kenna first, at the edge with the hunters. Then 60 of whatever is out on Strandwood Rocks.
  • A rematch? With rules? She said any rules? Then tell her: the sand both ways, nobody touches the rocks, and Bethoc holds the line. And tell her I'll not slip this time.
  • The sand both ways. Of course she would.
  • Fine. Sand. I'll still win. But not this month: Haldor needs me at the edge and Torva needs her on watch. We'll pick a day.
  • Here, for clearing the rocks. And Player? If she asks, I never said she was fast at the turn. I didn't say that.

docs.title: Merrin's Tally
docs.text:
Merrin keeps a tally of who has felled the most, and the edge-wood is slow. She has decided a Driftstump counts: bring down 45 of them.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Merrin Level 21 Leads to A Crew of Her Own

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 45 Driftstump

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,000 EXP
  • 840 mesos
  • Brodie's Smoked Fish x5
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Merrin
Dialogue
  • See my axe handle? Every notch is a tree. I'm third on the tally. Third. Since we pulled back to the edge nobody notches much, and the two above me are sitting on their lead.
  • So here's my thinking. A Driftstump is a tree, isn't it? It's got bark. It's got roots, nearly. It walks, which is cheating, but I didn't make the rules.
  • Bring down 45 Driftstumps on Strandwood Edge and I'll notch every one. Haldor will say they don't count. Haldor isn't keeping the tally.
  • Count them out loud. I'll know if you skip one.
  • Fine. I'll fell them myself, one swing at a time. Takes longer, that's all.
  • Forty-five Driftstumps, on Strandwood Edge where they crowd the stumps we left. Then come and watch me notch.
  • Forty-five? Hold still while I notch. One, two, three...
  • There. Haldor looked at my handle and said walking trees don't count, and then he laughed, which means they half count. Half is still up the tally, Player.

docs.title: The Beds Stay Whole
docs.text:
The seedling beds have stayed whole. Merrow wants to walk out to the last lantern himself, for the first time in years.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Merrow Level 29 After The Blightstone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the last lantern in Fairy Forest

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,281 EXP
  • 870 mesos
  • Shimmerwater Earrings x1
  • +150 standing with Merrow
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Two nights, and not a bed touched. Not one. Ailo's barely had to replant.
  • I've been thinking. The watch out there keeps us safe and I've never so much as said thank you. Celandine made them a basket of salves. I'm going to take it to them. Myself. Out to the last lantern.
  • Walk with me to the last lantern at the Forest Edge?
  • Right. Right. Here we go. Don't walk too fast.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The last lantern. Down the western path. I'm... I'm right behind you.
  • ...There. That wasn't so bad. Seren took the basket and said thank you, just like that.
  • I walked out to the Edge, Player. Me. Take these. Celandine says they suit you, and I say whatever she says.

docs.title: The Night Diggers
docs.text:
Merrow's seedling beds keep being dug up in the night. Find out what is doing it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Merrow Level 20 Leads to Sitting Up with Ailo, Rest for the Scholars

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ailo

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,387 EXP
  • 300 mesos
  • +15 standing with Merrow
  • +10 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Look at that. Look at it. My seedling beds, all churned up again. Third night this week.
  • Every morning I find them dug through, and every morning Ailo and I replant. Something's coming in from the Edge at night. I won't go out there, Player. I'm not brave about the Edge.
  • Will you find out what it is? Ask Ailo. Ailo's up before anyone.
  • Thank you. Ailo's just down the bed, by the far row.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Ailo's by the far row. Ailo sees more than Ailo says.
  • Ailo will sit up with you tonight? Good. Then we'll know.
  • ...The diggers?
  • They come after the lanterns dim. Sit with me tonight. You'll see.

docs.title: The Gap at Dawn
docs.text:
Mhairi's first verse is the gap at dawn, but she plays too late to ever see one. Look at the gap from the head of the Long Stair, then ask Bethoc what she remembers of the race send-offs.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Mhairi Level 22 Leads to The Saltface Verse

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the head of the Long Stair in Goa Harbour
  2. Talk to Bethoc

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,150 EXP
  • 450 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x2
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Mhairi
Dialogue
  • Here's a thing nobody knows. My verse about the gap at dawn? I've never seen the gap at dawn. I play till the inn shuts and sleep till noon.
  • Go up to the head of the Long Stair, early as you can stand it, and look at the gap. Then ask Bethoc what she remembers of the race send-offs at first light. She's seen every one since she was a girl.
  • Look at the colour of it. I need the colour.
  • Fine. I'll make it up. I always have.
  • The head of the Long Stair, then Bethoc. Colour, Player. I need the colour.
  • Grey, then pink. And Malcolm's pot! Oh, that's going in.
  • That's the first verse finished properly. Well, finished till Jory hears it and wants his made longer again. Here, Bethoc says I'm to feed you.
  • The send-offs? I've seen every one since I could see over the bar.
  • The gap goes grey first, then pink along the forest cliff, and the whole quay goes quiet just before the boat slips out. Then my father would bang a pot. Tell her about the pot. She'll want the pot in it.

docs.title: The Saltface Verse
docs.text:
Mhairi wants a verse for the boat going out under the Saltface, with the cliff's own noise in it. Clear 60 monsters on the Saltface, then ask Cormac how the old songs sang the cliff.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Mhairi Level 34 After The Gap at Dawn

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 60 Saltface monsters in The Saltface
  2. Talk to Cormac

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,400 EXP
  • 1,400 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x3
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Mhairi
Dialogue
  • The Gap Runner goes out right under the Saltface, under the big cliff, and I haven't got a verse for it. I want the cliff in it. The noise of it.
  • The watch say you can't hear yourself on the Saltface for the crabs clacking and the newts croaking. I want to hear it. Through you.
  • Clear 60 monsters on The Saltface, and listen while you do it. Then ask Cormac how the old camp songs sang the cliff. I won't ask him for a verse, mind. Just that. Just the cliff.
  • Listen properly. With your ears, not your sword.
  • Then the cliff will have to wait. It's waited long enough.
  • Sixty on The Saltface, then Cormac. Only about the cliff!
  • Slow, low on the string, like the sea leaning on it. Oh, that's him all over.
  • I'll play it slow. Once. Then fast, and he'll laugh. Here, Player, and thank you. I'll play the cliff verse twice at the send-off, and you'll know whose ears it came through.
  • She asked? She asked what the old songs did with the cliff? Mhairi asked me?
  • Tell her they sang it slow, low on the string, like the sea leaning on it. Slow, mind! She'll play it fast anyway. And tell her... no. Just tell her slow.

docs.title: Ribbons for Dusk
docs.text:
Mirabel wants ribbons for her ankles that flutter when she turns. The Ribbon Pigs of the Waystone Meadows wear the best ones.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Mirabel Level 11 Leads to The Far Side of the Bell

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 12 Pig's Ribbon (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 250 EXP
  • 220 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +90 standing with Mirabel
Dialogue
  • Oh, Player, I have had the loveliest idea. Ribbons, at my ankles, so every turn leaves a little colour in the air behind it.
  • The pigs on the The Waystone Meadows wear such pretty ones. I am sure they would not mind. Well. They would mind. But you are braver than I am.
  • Would you bring me 12 Pig's Ribbons from the Ribbon Pigs? There is no hurry. There is never any hurry.
  • Lovely. I shall practise without them until then.
  • Of course. Another day. Dusk comes every evening.
  • You have (how many you carry) of 12 Pig's Ribbons. The pigs are on the The Waystone Meadows.
  • Oh, look at the colours! Pink and gold and that one is almost blue.
  • Come at dusk and watch me turn in them. Fulke will play something fluttery. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Mirabel the far side of the bell
The Far Side of the Bell
docs.text:
Mirabel wants a second pair of ears: stand on the far side of the Great Bell at dusk, when the wind is kind, then ask Fulke whether he heard anything over his own lute.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Mirabel Level 13 After Ribbons for Dusk

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the far side of the Bell in Royal Plaza
  2. Talk to Fulke

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 380 EXP
  • 260 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +110 standing with Mirabel
Dialogue
  • There is a breeze coming, Player. Soft, from the west. On evenings like this the Bell sings, I know it does.
  • Hugh says the wind makes a great many noises. So I need another pair of ears, on the other side of the Bell from me. And then Fulke's, if he can hear anything over himself.
  • Stand on the far side of the Bell and press Up, and listen. Then ask Fulke what he heard. Then come and tell me.
  • Thank you. Do not listen too hard. It is shy.
  • Another breeze will come. They always do.
  • The far side of the Bell, then Fulke.
  • Fulke says he heard a note and his eyebrows did not go up? Then it is true. Or Fulke believes it, which is nearly the same.
  • You are not sure what you heard. That is all right, Player. Neither am I. That is the nicest part.
  • Did I hear it? I heard a note, Player, under the lute, faint and sweet. Or I heard my own lute remembering. Watch my eyebrows. ... They stayed put, did they not? Tell her that.

docs.title: The Gullwalk
docs.text:
Moira would rather be out on the coast than on the stairs. She wants the Gullwalk clear of the kestrels and crabs that crowd its path.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Moira Level 18

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Kestrel
  • Defeat 20 Lorang

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,250 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +100 standing with Moira
Dialogue
  • Do you know the Gullwalk? The path south along the clifftop, with the sea right under your boots. It is the best walk on the whole coast.
  • Or it was, before the kestrels started stooping at people. And the crabs climb up from somewhere. Ruan will not spare me for it.
  • Clear 30 Kestrel and 20 Lorang on The Gullwalk, off the town's south end.
  • Tell me what it looks like now. Everything.
  • Oh. Fine. The stairs it is, again.
  • The Gullwalk starts at the south end of the quay.
  • You walked the whole of it? I am so jealous I could spit. Thank you, really.

docs.title: The Unlit Stretches
docs.text:
Moira has noticed the climbers keep to the stretches no lantern reaches. She knows where they gather.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Moira Level 33 After Lanterns to the Landings Leads to The Wake

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Sea Newt in The Saltface

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,100 EXP
  • 1,300 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Moira
Dialogue
  • I told Ruan. They do not come up where the lanterns are. They come up the dark stretches, always, every time.
  • There is a run of ledge on the Saltface, between the two old rope-way stumps, that nothing lights. They gather there before they climb.
  • Clear 50 Sea Newt on The Saltface, where they gather in the unlit stretches.
  • I wish I could come. I really do.
  • Then they will keep coming up in the dark.
  • The unlit ledges on the Saltface, between the rope-way stumps.
  • Fifty! They will think twice about the dark stretches now. I am telling Ruan you agreed with me.

docs.title: Moira's Wager
docs.text:
Moira wants to prove to Torva that she can hunt. Defeat 60 Sea Newts, race her from the foot of the stairs to the head of the Long Stair, then carry her case to Torva on the Forest Shore.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Moira Level 36

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 60 Sea Newt
  2. Reach the foot of the stairs in Goa Harbour
  3. Reach the head of the Long Stair in Goa Harbour
  4. Talk to Torva

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,000 EXP
  • 1,500 mesos
  • Gap Inn Stew x10
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Moira
Dialogue
  • Torva will not take me out with the hunters. She says the stairs need me more. So I will show her I can hunt. The Sea Newts that climb the Saltface. Sixty of them. Then she has to listen.
  • And here is the wager. Bring down 60 Sea Newts, then meet me at the foot of the stairs and race me to the head of the Long Stair. Lose, and you carry my case to Torva on the Forest Shore. I do not intend to lose.
  • Newts first. The Saltface is down the steep way off the Gullwalk. Then the foot of the stairs, and try to keep up.
  • Scared of a few stairs? I will ask Kestra. She would win, though. Do not tell her I said that.
  • Sea Newts, then the foot of the stairs, then the race to the head of the Long Stair, then Torva. I will be faster than you either way.
  • Moira sent you. With a wager, I would guess, and you lost it.
  • Sixty newts. That is good work, and she knows it. She rang the bar three winters ago when nobody else was near it. That is why the stairs need her more than I do.
  • Tell her that. She will think I am being kind. I am not. Ask anyone.
  • Well? What did she say? The stairs need me. Of course they do. She is being kind.
  • Sixty newts, though. And you nearly had me on the last flight. Nearly. Here, the stew is on me. Tomorrow we go again.

docs.title: Morwen a place he must try
A Place He Must Try
docs.text:
Morwen means to take her class onto the Long Reach Banks, where a mage must try. Clear the banks, then tell Everard he is coming.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Morwen Level 41 After Books for Constance

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Bank Clang in The Long Reach Banks
  2. Talk to Everard

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 18,440 EXP
  • 820 mesos
  • Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60% x1
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Morwen
Dialogue
  • Everard passes everything I set him without trying. So I will take him somewhere trying is the only way through.
  • The The Long Reach Banks, for a practical. But not while the clangs hold the bank. I want my students afraid of the right things.
  • Clear 40 Bank Clangs from The Long Reach Banks, then tell Everard he is coming on the practical.
  • And watch his face when you tell him. I want to know.
  • Then the practical waits. So does he.
  • Forty clangs on The Long Reach Banks, then Everard. Watch his face.
  • He said that? And he looked like that? Good. He is frightened. That means he knows.
  • I am not trying to make him great, Player. I am trying to make him ready. There is a difference, and he has not seen it yet.
  • A practical? On the The Long Reach Banks? With her watching?
  • ...Tell her I'll come. Tell her I'll probably sleep through it. She won't believe the second part, will she.

docs.title: Books for Constance
docs.text:
Morwen has set some books aside for her former student Constance, who now takes to the road. Tell her, without making it sound warm.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Morwen Level 35 After Gloves for the Practical Leads to A Place He Must Try

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Constance

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,230 EXP
  • 700 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Morwen
Dialogue
  • Constance studied under me for five years. The most careful student I ever had. She left in her final year to take up the road.
  • She comes back to borrow books. I have set three aside for her. She will want them before the next season out.
  • Go to the Crooked Lantern and tell Constance the books are ready. Do not tell her I am glad to see her.
  • She is clever. She will understand perfectly what I did not say.
  • Then she can find out from the shelf. As usual.
  • Constance, at the Crooked Lantern. The books are ready. That is all.
  • She laughed? Of course she laughed.
  • Well. The books are there. That is what matters. Here, take this for your trouble.
  • Morwen set books aside for me? She never says so. She sends someone else to say so.
  • Tell her I will come for them before the next season out. And tell her nothing else; she will understand it all.

docs.title: Gloves for the Practical
docs.text:
Morwen's young mages burn their fingers in practical lessons. Ligator hide from the Reed Beds makes gloves that do not scorch.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Morwen Level 30 Leads to Books for Constance

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Reed Ligator Hide (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,060 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Morwen
Dialogue
  • My first-years burn their fingers every practical. Every one. They wave their hands about instead of being patient, and the spell bites.
  • Ligator hide does not scorch. The The Reed Beds are full of ligators this year.
  • Bring me 15 Reed Ligator Hides from the Reed Ligators of The Reed Beds.
  • Good. Be patient with them. They are, after all, only doing what they are made to do.
  • Then my students will keep burning their fingers. It teaches them something, I suppose.
  • Fifteen hides, Player. Not fourteen and a good story.
  • Fifteen. Clean cuts, too. You were patient.
  • Every glove will have a name stitched in it, so they cannot lose them. They will lose them anyway. Thank you.

docs.title: A Letter for Ossie
docs.text:
Morwenna sails on the Saltlark tomorrow and wants a letter to reach Ossie at the lighthouse path.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Morwenna Level 35 Leads to At the Wheel

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ossie

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,920 EXP
  • 770 mesos
  • +40 standing with Morwenna
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • We sail on the morning tide. Ossie's up at the lighthouse with his gran and I won't have time to climb all hundred and seventeen stairs.
  • Take him this? It's only a letter. A song, really. My dad sang it at the oars. Ossie likes the part about the gulls.
  • Tell him I'll be home before the full moon.
  • Another time, then.
  • Take Morwenna's letter to Ossie at the lighthouse path.
  • He read it? He read it twice and wrote it in his logbook? That's my boy.
  • Thank you, love. I miss home the moment we cast off. It helps knowing he's got the song.
  • A letter from Mum? Thank you. It's the oar song. The gull part's my favourite.
  • I'll write it in my logbook. Under 'songs'. I started a page for songs. Tell her I'll keep the light company.

docs.title: At the Wheel
docs.text:
Morwenna had the Saltlark's wheel the night the keel was brushed. She has not told her mother or her son. Now she wants to.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Morwenna Level 62 After A Letter for Ossie, Where the Keel Was Brushed

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ysolde

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 54,031 EXP
  • 1,364 mesos
  • +40 standing with Morwenna
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • I had the wheel that night. When it brushed the keel. I felt it through the spokes, all the way from bow to stern.
  • I never told Mum. Or Ossie. Annis knows and never pressed me. Now it's gone, I want them to know. Will you go up with me? Just stand there. Talk to my mother first, so she's sitting down.
  • Make sure she's sitting down.
  • Another time, then.
  • Go to Ysolde with Morwenna, so she can tell her mother.
  • She took my hand and said 'I know, love, I saw your face when you came in that morning.' She KNEW.
  • Ossie wants to hear it as a story. I'll tell it at the oars, like Dad did. Thank you.
  • Morwenna wants to tell me something? Sit me down, then. My knees will thank you.
  • ...I knew, love. I saw her face that morning. I've waited a year for her to say it. Send her up.

docs.title: Counting Names
docs.text:
The reed-lurkers of the Reedwater Bottoms have stopped the carts on the far road. Moth has an idea that breaks the old rule of the hat: save the best corners for outside traders. Clear the reed-lurkers, then take the idea to Rook as a question for the Table.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Moth Level 48 After Empty Corners

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Reed-Lurker
  2. Talk to Rook

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 53,710 EXP
  • 6,720 mesos
  • +80 standing with Moth
  • +20 standing with Rook
  • +30 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I have been thinking. At night, which is when I think. What if the hat kept the two best corners back, every night, for anybody who came in from outside? Brave enough to walk the roads, first pick of the market. It would bring them.
  • It would also break a rule older than anyone in this market. First name, first pick, nobody owns the best corner. Old Bramble would come back from the dead to scold me. So it is not mine to decide. It is a question, and questions go to the Table.
  • But a question about roads is no good while the roads are shut. The carts from the far side of the Bristlewood come along the bottoms, and the Reed-Lurkers pull them into the reeds.
  • Clear 40 Reed-Lurkers from the Reedwater Bottoms. Then take my idea to Rook, in the Great Hall. As a question, mind. Not a decision. I will not have the hat thinking I went behind its back.
  • The bottoms are past the Tusk Path, where the stream goes black and slow. And Rook is easiest to catch before a Table night, when Mags is feeding everyone and nobody is talking yet.
  • Probably wise. Ideas made at three in the morning should be slept on. I will sleep on it until noon. Then I will think it again.
  • Forty reed-lurkers first, then Rook. A question, not a decision. The hat is listening.
  • From Moth? Keep two corners back for outside traders, every night? Hm. That would break the hat. The hat is older than the Table's oldest book, and twice as stubborn.
  • But it is a good question, and Moth was right to send it as one. The quiet ones will want a say: the stall-holders whose names would come out second. I will put it to the Table at the next gathering, as Moth's question, in Moth's words.
  • Tell Moth it will be argued properly. Which means slowly. Which means Bastian will argue both sides. But it will be heard, and that is the whole point of the Table.
  • Argued properly. Slowly. Both sides by Bastian. Good. That is exactly what should happen to an idea I had at three in the morning.
  • And the road is clearer: a spice cart came in last night, the first in months. The whole market smelled of cloves. I drew the cart's name fourth. Fourth! Got a middling corner and sold out anyway.
  • Maybe the Table will say yes, maybe no. Either way the hat stays honest. Thank you, Player. Come by after dark. It is always after dark here.

docs.title: Empty Corners
docs.text:
Moth's hat of names grows thinner every night: the salt sellers, wool carters and spice peddlers are not getting through. The bristle boars on the Tusk Path drive the traders off the road. Thin them.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Moth Level 34 Leads to Counting Names

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Bristle Boar in The Tusk Path

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 22,850 EXP
  • 3,400 mesos
  • +60 standing with Moth
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Evening. It is evening, is it not? Good. Anything earlier I refuse to discuss. This is the hat. Every name in it is a stall, and every evening I draw them out, first name, first pick, the way the first traders did. Lately I count the names first. That never used to be necessary.
  • No salt seller in a month. The wool carters, twice since spring. The spice peddler who smelled of cloves from three stalls away: gone. Shade brings a few in, but even Shade says the boar have taken the Tusk Path, and a cart that meets a boar turns round.
  • Corners stand empty for nights now, and the market feeds half the city through the winter. Clear the road for them: 50 Bristle Boars on The Tusk Path. I would go myself, but it would mean being awake at a reasonable hour.
  • Through the Outworks, into the Bristlewood, up to the hill path with the tracks too big for comfort. Come back after dark. I will be here. I am always here after dark.
  • Fair. Into the hat goes another empty fold of paper, then. I will draw it out and pretend it is a trader.
  • Fifty bristle boars on the Tusk Path. I counted the hat again tonight. Same number as last night, minus one.
  • Two names in the hat tonight that were not there last week. A wool carter, still white with fright, and a woman with a barrow of pepper who says the Tusk Path was 'almost pleasant'. Almost. From a pepper seller, that is a hymn.
  • I put them in the hat with everybody else. No special corner; the hat would never forgive me. But I did smile when I drew them. Do not tell anyone. I have a reputation.

docs.title: Roofs to Avoid
docs.text:
Nana Gristle warned Kite about the rotten gutter on the north end of the long roof over the Night Market. Kite jumped it anyway, and something happened. Nana wants Kite to admit she was right.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Nana Gristle Level 21 Leads to The Basket

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Kite

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 800 EXP
  • 1,260 mesos
  • +50 standing with Nana Gristle
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • That Kite. Fastest legs in the city and the deafest ears. I said, the long roof over the Night Market, the north end, the gutter's rotten. I said it a dozen times. I said it slowly.
  • Well, last night a whole length of gutter came down in the Night Market and nearly landed in Ladle's cider. And who was seen running away across the slates, very fast and very guilty?
  • Go up and find Kite on the Rooftops, and ask, very politely, which end of the long roof the gutter came off. I want to hear Kite say it. Through you will do.
  • And don't let Kite run off mid-sentence. Kite does that. Stand in front of the ladder.
