  • Pfah. I'll wait. I've been right for seventy-nine years. I can be right for a few more days.
  • Kite. The Rooftops. Which end did the gutter come off? Make Kite say it.
  • Nana sent you, didn't she. I knew it. I KNEW it. (Kite jogs on the spot, not quite meeting your eyes.) Fine. FINE. It was the north end. The gutter. The rotten one. It went right out from under my back foot.
  • Tell Nana she was right. Tell her I said it. Tell her I'm not happy about it. And tell her... tell her thanks. She's always right about the roofs. It's so annoying.
  • The north end. Out from under the back foot. Ha! And 'she's always right about the roofs'? Did Kite say 'always'? Say it again. Slowly.
  • Lovely. That'll keep me warm all winter. Here, sit, have the cake side today. You earned it, Player. And go and tell Ladle to move her cider.

docs.title: The Basket
docs.text:
Nana Gristle has remembered something about her mother's basket on the Long Walk: a ribbon. She wants Ozzie Lantry, the Walkers' historian, to write it into his history properly.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Nana Gristle Level 32 After Roofs to Avoid

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ozzie Lantry

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,770 EXP
  • 1,920 mesos
  • +70 standing with Nana Gristle
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I was sitting here this morning in the sun, and it came back to me clear as a bell. The basket. My mother's basket, on the Long Walk. It had a ribbon on the handle. Blue. My grandmother tied it there so she'd know it in a crowd.
  • Ozzie Lantry has written my mother's story down I don't know how many times. Not once with the ribbon. Well, it has to go in. It's a fact. It's an important fact.
  • Go to Ozzie Lantry in the Great Hall and tell him: a blue ribbon on the handle, so Marguerite could find the basket in the crowd. Make him write it down while you watch.
  • He'll be in his corner of the Great Hall looking for his spectacles. They'll be on his head. Tell him that too.
  • Pfah. Then I'll tell him myself, and he'll get that look, and I'll have to be cross. Save us both the trouble, another day.
  • Ozzie, the Great Hall. A blue ribbon on the handle. Make him write it down.
  • A blue ribbon on the handle? (Ozzie pats three pockets for his spectacles, then finds them on his head.) Hm. Hmm. You know, I have written Posy's story down eleven times now, and every telling Nana adds something lovely. The year before last it was a song Marguerite hummed. Last year a dog followed them out of the gates.
  • I don't think it's untrue, exactly. I think a story that's been carried for a hundred years grows a little, the way a child does. Nobody alive can say there was no ribbon. And it's a very good ribbon.
  • There. (He writes, carefully.) 'A blue ribbon tied on the handle, so that Marguerite might find it in the crowd. As told by her granddaughter.' Tell Nana it's in. Tell her I underlined 'blue'.
  • He wrote it? With 'blue' underlined? Good. Good. (Nana's mouth goes very firm, the way it does just before she cries, and then she does, a little, and blows her nose very loudly.)
  • It's a true ribbon. I'm nearly sure. Don't you look at me like Ozzie does. Here. Honey cake. Go on.

docs.title: Neffa a name in the song
A Name in the Song
docs.text:
Deep in the oldest part of the long song is a chieftain who held the western edge 'behind a wall of faces'. Bring Neffa a Carved War Mask Shard from the War Camp Ruins and tell her what it was.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Neffa Level 60 After The Long Song

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Carved War Mask Shard

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 30,500 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Neffa
Dialogue
  • I sing Varra's verse without stumbling now. Ahvi says so, and Ahvi doesn't say things. So I've started on the oldest part, from the Age of Division, and there's a line I can sing and can't understand.
  • A chieftain who held the western edge behind a wall of faces. Ahvi says it must be the old camp out past the Weathered Rocks, but she has never been, and she says a song-keeper shouldn't guess. Faces. Whose faces?
  • You've been out there. Bring me something from that camp, Player: a Carved War Mask Shard, if the masks there are what I think. Then tell me what it was.
  • The masks in The War Camp Ruins move about, Bekk says. I don't need a whole one. Just a piece.
  • That's all right. I'll sing it without understanding. Ahvi says I have to learn to do that too.
  • A Carved War Mask Shard from The War Camp Ruins. Just a piece.
  • Wood. Old wood, painted red and black, carved with a mouth like a shout. It isn't anybody's face at all. It's a mask somebody carved to look like one.
  • The old camp's own war masks, you said, made for it in the old wars. So anyone looking up at that camp saw a wall of faces. It isn't a riddle. It's just what they saw.
  • I'm going to sing it to Ahvi tonight and see if she notices that I understand it now. She will. She always does. This is for you, from my own savings, which are mostly salve.

docs.title: The Long Song
docs.text:
Neffa always stumbles on the same verse of the long song: Old One Varra's. Ask Ahvi, Thrun and Odda what Varra was like, and bring their answers back to Neffa.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Neffa Level 50 Leads to A Name in the Song

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Ahvi
  • Talk to Thrun
  • Talk to Odda

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,500 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Neffa
Dialogue
  • I can sing three-quarters of the long song of the Old Ones without a slip. I have counted every restart under my bed. There are hundreds.
  • I always stumble in the same place: Varra's verse. Ahvi's sister, the Old One before Hask. I was four when she died, and I remember her hands and nothing else, and the words won't stay when I don't know who they're about.
  • Will you ask about her for me? Ahvi, Thrun and my grandmother Odda. I can't ask them myself. They would know why, and they would look at me sadly.
  • Ask them what she was like. Not what she did; the song says what she did. What she was like.
  • That's all right. I'll keep restarting. I'm good at restarting.
  • Ahvi, Thrun and Odda. What was Varra like?
  • Neffa sent you, and did not come herself. That is very like her, and very like Varra too.
  • My sister was eleven years older than me and never once let me win at anything. She laughed when she was angry, which frightened chieftains, and she said exactly what she meant, which frightened them more. Tell Neffa that.
  • Varra? I drummed her choosing! Thirty-one years ago, and my arms ached for a week.
  • She used to tap the beat on her knee while I drummed, always a little ahead of me, to hurry me up. Tell the girl her verse should go a little fast. Varra would want it fast.
  • Varra was Old One for twenty-five years, and for most of my years as chieftain. She used to say a council should end with everyone a little unhappy, so that nobody was unhappy alone.
  • She died in her sleep, with her boots by the door, as tidy as she was in everything. Tell Neffa that Varra would have been proud of every one of those restarts.
  • She never let Ahvi win. She laughed when she was angry. She tapped ahead of the drum. She was tidy.
  • I think I can hear her now, in the words. They're about somebody.
  • I'm going to sing it tonight, fast, the way Thrun said. Thank you, Player. This is from Mother's shelf. She won't mind; she says you're good for us.

docs.title: The Ledge She Was Reaching For
docs.text:
Nerissa stopped diving after something moved below the shelf at the reef's edge. She asks for a pearl from the ledge she was reaching for, and then she will tell.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Nerissa Level 65 After Checking the Marks Leads to To See It Once

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 1 Ledge Pearl (taken)
  2. Talk to Tristram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 90,442 EXP
  • 1,950 mesos
  • +60 standing with Nerissa
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Saw the marks on Ambrose's chart. Under the headland.
  • Last dive, late spring. Reef's edge, outside the sea gates. A ledge with an oyster bed. Big pearls. Reaching for one. Something moved below the shelf, in the dark. Big. Saw it a moment. Came up.
  • Haven't been down since. Bring me a Ledge Pearl from that ledge: the pale sawbills nest on the gate stones above it at the Gullet. Then come with me. I want to tell Tristram. You there.
  • Breathe first.
  • Another time, then.
  • Bring a pearl from the ledge at the Gullet's sea gates, then be there when Nerissa tells Tristram.
  • That's the pearl. That's the ledge.
  • Told him. He went quiet, then put his hand on my shoulder. Didn't pick up the harpoon. That's why I didn't tell him before. Thought he'd go down to look. He won't. He wants to see it, not kill it. Different.
  • ...Nerissa told me. What she saw below the shelf.
  • I won't go down after it. I want to see it once. From somewhere it can't reach. That's all.

docs.title: The Sea End
docs.text:
Nerissa's reef lies just outside the broken sea gates. She teaches you how the tide runs in through them, and asks for oysters from the old gate stones.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Nerissa Level 39 After What Tears the Nets Leads to The Night Run

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Gate Oyster (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 19,872 EXP
  • 1,170 mesos
  • +60 standing with Nerissa
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Cobb saw them. Good.
  • My reef's outside the sea gates. Tide runs in through the broken ones. Fast. Two rules: tell someone on shore. Breathe before you go down.
  • Not diving. Not now. But the old gate stones on the Sea Locks grow oysters. Good ones. Bring me 15 Gate Oysters. The spitting sawbills nest on the stones. Mind them.
  • Told Wenna you're going. That's rule one.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fifteen gate oysters from the old stones on the Sea Locks. You have (how many you carry).
  • Good oysters. Big ones.
  • You breathe right. Watched you come back. Maybe later I'll tell you about the reef's edge. Not today.

docs.title: One at a Time
docs.text:
Nessa takes quay children out in the pilot boats at slack, one at a time, and wants an honest second opinion. Ask Kor which child he would put on an oar, then see that child.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Nessa Level 30 Leads to Under the Saltface

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Kor
  2. Talk to Arlo

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,900 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Nessa
Dialogue
  • Too few young pilots. You've heard me say it, the whole quay has. The table nods and does nothing, so I've stopped waiting for the table.
  • I take quay children out in a pilot boat at slack water. One at a time. Don't look at me like that. I've not asked anyone, and I'm not going to.
  • I want a second opinion, and I'll not get an honest one at the table. Ask Kor which of the quay children he'd put on an oar. Then go and see whoever he names, and come back and tell me.
  • Kor will be on the quay, whistling. Follow the whistling.
  • Fine. I'll pick them myself. I usually do.
  • Kor first: who would he put on an oar? Then the one he names.
  • Who'd I put on an oar? Arlo. Obviously. He's on the quay before I am, and I'm on it early, and he asks why about everything. Don't tell Nessa I said obviously. She'll say nothing's obvious.
  • An oar? In a pilot boat? Yes! ...But Nessa should ask Eilidh too. She reads the water quicker than me. I'm more careful. Don't tell her I said quicker.
  • Arlo. Of course it's Arlo. Iska's boy, in my boat, without a word to the table.
  • And he named Eilidh before himself. Did you hear that? Nine years old and he names a rival before himself. That's a pilot. Two, then. One at a time.
  • Take these, and keep it quiet at the Gap Inn. I'll buy the round, as usual.

docs.title: Out at Slack
docs.text:
Nessa wants you in a pilot boat with her at slack water. Clear 50 Saltgulls from the Wrack Ledges first, then meet her at the lowest quay steps.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Nessa Level 46 After Under the Saltface

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 50 Saltgull in The Wrack Ledges
  2. Reach the lowest quay steps in Goa Harbour

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 30,000 EXP
  • 1,840 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • Gap Inn Stew x5
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Nessa
Dialogue
  • Right. You've cleared the rocks for my children. Now I want you in the boat.
  • I've a case to make at the table, and the table only listens to a thing that's been done. When I say a child can learn the gap at slack, I want to say who else has rowed it with me.
  • One thing first. The Saltgulls off the Wrack Ledges have taken to diving at small boats in the gap. I'll take a child past a gull. Not past fifty.
  • Clear 50 Saltgulls from the Wrack Ledges, then meet me at the lowest quay steps. I'll have the boat.
  • Ledges first, then the steps. Don't be late for slack. Slack doesn't wait, whatever Kor says.
  • Scared of a little water? Fine. The offer's open. So's the boat.
  • Fifty Saltgulls on the Wrack Ledges, then the lowest quay steps. I'll be in the boat.
  • There. Back on dry stone. You felt it, out in the gap, the moment the run let go? That's slack. The whole gap holds its breath, and for a few minutes a child can row it.
  • You pulled a fair oar. Not as fair as mine. Better than Kor's first time, which I will be telling him tonight.
  • I'll take it to the table now: a child can learn the gap at slack, with a warden in the stern, and I've proved it twice and you once. They'll argue. I'll argue back. Then I'll buy the round.
  • Take these, and dry off. You've earned the wet. Round's on me tonight, as always.

docs.title: Under the Saltface
docs.text:
Nessa rows her young pilots along under the Saltface, and the Sea Newts lie out on the rocks there watching. Clear 60 of them from the Saltface.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Nessa Level 38 After One at a Time Leads to Out at Slack

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Sea Newt in The Saltface

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,500 EXP
  • 1,520 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x5
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Nessa
Dialogue
  • When I take a child out, we go along under the Saltface, on the town side of the gap. The water's kindest there at slack, and if anything goes wrong, the rocks are close.
  • Lately the Sea Newts lie out on those rocks and watch the boat go by. I'll not have a child at the oars rowing past something that's deciding whether she's supper.
  • Go down the Saltface and clear 60 Sea Newts off the cliff. The table can argue about it afterwards. I'll have won by then.
  • The steep way down leaves the Gullwalk. Mind the ones on the walls, they climb.
  • Then I'll row further out. I won't like it, and I'll say so.
  • Sixty Sea Newts on the Saltface. Mind the walls.
  • Sixty? Ha. I told Kor you'd manage fifty, so I win that one too.
  • Here, for your trouble. Tomorrow at slack the rocks will be empty, and the only thing watching my boat will be Ysmay from her window.

docs.title: Oriel Lingers
docs.text:
Oriel seems worried and lingers in the oldest homes. Niv wants to know why, so Niv can help.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Niv Level 50 After Not Wrong Yet Leads to The Homes That Will Not Wake, The Gloaming Watch, The Deeply Touched

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Oriel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,746 EXP
  • 750 mesos
  • +100 standing with Niv
  • +10 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • ...Oriel stays late in the old homes. Later every day.
  • He touches the walls and listens. He doesn't say anything. Find out why? So I can help.
  • Ask Oriel, gently, what is wrong.
  • ...Thank you.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • ...Oriel. By the oldest homes.
  • ...Thin sap. Cold rooms.
  • ...I'll sit with him. Niv says it quietly, and then stands a little closer to you than before.
  • Niv sent you? Hm. That child notices too much.
  • ...All right. Not here. Come and see me properly. There's something I've told nobody.

docs.title: Standing Quietly
docs.text:
Niv stands at the edge of the glade every day. Niv would like company, if it is quiet company.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Niv Level 18 Leads to A Newcomer Who Is Struggling

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the edge of the glade in Children's Glade
  • Defeat 30 Road monsters (Slime, Bubbling, Glimmerwing, Crowned Glimmerwing)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,400 EXP
  • 396 mesos
  • +200 standing with Niv
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • ...Market day tomorrow. Crowds.
  • ...Today, could you stand with me? At the edge. Not talking. And keep the roads quiet, so the carts come and go fast.
  • Stand with Niv at the edge of the glade (examine it), and clear 30 monsters off the roads for market day.
  • ...Thank you.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • ...The edge of the glade.
  • ...
  • Niv says nothing at all, for a long time. It is, you understand, a great compliment.

docs.title: Not Wrong Yet
docs.text:
With Hesper's list, Juniper's notebooks and the lost season, Caelum has built his thirty-second theory. It needs checking. He needs sleep.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Caelum Level 49 After Old Grizzlemane Leads to Oriel Lingers

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Tansy
  2. Deliver 1 Honey Cake for Caelum

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 39,078 EXP
  • 1,470 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +150 standing with Caelum
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Thirty-two. Theory thirty-two. With Hesper's list and Juniper's lost season it... it doesn't fall apart. I keep pushing it and it doesn't fall apart.
  • I've started a new drawer for it. 'Not wrong yet.' I won't say what it shows until I've checked it twice. Three times. I've been awake since... what day is it?
  • Somebody should make him sleep. Ask Tansy at the Dewdrop for something that will.
  • ...I'm fine. I'm fine. Is there cake?
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Tansy. Cake. Sleep. In that order.
  • Honey cake. Warm. Oh, that's... that's not fair.
  • Caelum eats the cake, sits down on a pile of notes, says 'two hours, then I'll check it again', and is asleep before he finishes the sentence.
  • Caelum? Hasn't slept? Hasn't eaten either, I'll bet. That boy.
  • Here. My warmest honey cake. Get it into him and he'll be asleep in a minute. It works on Liri every time.

docs.title: Notices for the Lanes
docs.text:
Rufus's notices are not reaching the farms along the Cider Lanes, because folk have stopped walking in to hear them. Carry them out to the farm gate above the lanes and clear 30 orchard pigs.

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Rufus Level 9

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Orchard Pig
  • Reach the farm gate above the lanes in The Cider Lanes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,100 EXP
  • 700 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Hear ye, hear ye, and nobody hears. The orchard folk along the Cider Lanes have stopped walking in for the notices, Player, because the pigs out there have got bold. Would you carry this week's out to the farm gate above the lanes, and clear 30 orchard pigs while you are at it?
  • Splendid. The lanes start at the far east end of Kaldemor Field. The farm gate is up on the high path, above the hedges. Read the notices aloud if you like. I always do.
  • Then I shall read them to the square again, and the square shall pretend to listen.
  • Thirty orchard pigs and the farm gate above the lanes, Player. The notices will not post themselves.
  • Delivered! And the lanes cleared besides. I may read the next ones a little louder, out of sheer joy.
  • Here is your fee. Hear ye, hear ye: Player did a good day's work.

docs.title: A Wall for Figgy
docs.text:
Ochre has secretly found a wall for Figgy: the low wall under the Fiddler's Crossing, right below one of Splash's bridges. Carry one pointed remark to Splash and bring one back, then tell Figgy the wall is hers.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Ochre Level 30 After Good Red

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Splash
  2. Talk to Figgy

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,580 EXP
  • 3,600 mesos
  • +70 standing with Ochre
  • +30 standing with Figgy
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Secret. Can you keep one? Figgy wants a wall of her own more than anything. She saves her coppers for it in a jar under her bed. And I've found one. The low wall under the Fiddler's Crossing, round the back of the square. Nobody's touched it in years.
  • The trouble is the bridge above it. Splash has painted the underneath of that bridge. A heron, upside down. So the wall's sort of... in Splash's sky. I'm not asking permission. Splash doesn't believe in permission. But it would be rude not to say.
  • Go up to Splash on the Rooftops and say, from me: the wall under the Fiddler's Crossing is spoken for, and a painter who never signs anything can hardly object to a painter who signs everything in chalk. Then bring back whatever Splash says. Then tell Figgy.
  • Say it exactly like that. Don't soften it. Splash would be insulted if you softened it.
  • Fair enough. I'll find another way. I always find another way. It usually involves a ladder and a lot of muttering.
  • Splash first, up on the Rooftops: the remark, exactly. Then Figgy: the wall is hers.
  • (Splash listens to the whole remark without blinking, grinning wider at every word.) 'Signs everything in chalk.' Ha. Ochre's been practising that one. Fine. Here's one back.
  • Tell Ochre: good wall. Mind the drips, my heron's directly above, and herons drip. And tell Ochre that whoever repaints a cartoon line for line every spring has no business calling anyone else unsigned. ...Tell the kid it's a good wall. That part's not a remark.
  • A WALL? Mine? A whole one? Under the Fiddler's Crossing? With Splash's heron on top? (Figgy is jumping.) That's the best wall in the whole city. Splash's things are the best things. Don't tell Mum I said that.
  • Looking is free and stepping is one copper. Same rules. And it's not finished till it rains. Tell Mum thank you. No, I'll tell. I'll tell loud.
  • Splash said mind the drips? And 'no business calling anyone unsigned'? (Ochre goes rather red, the good red.) Well. Well! That's... fair, actually. Annoyingly fair.
  • And 'tell the kid it's a good wall'. Splash said that? Not as a remark? (Ochre is quiet for a moment, holding a dripping brush and not noticing.)
  • I heard Figgy from three streets away. Thank you, Player. Maybe one day Splash and I will actually talk. Not today. Today there's a small person with a lot of chalk and a wall.

docs.title: Good Red
docs.text:
Ochre needs good red for the Walkers' oldest pictures, and good red is made from a red earth dug outside the walls. The dark stumps of the Western Descent carry it in their roots: bring Ochre 25 Clods of Red Earth.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Ochre Level 19 Leads to A Wall for Figgy

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Clod of Red Earth (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,630 EXP
  • 2,710 mesos
  • +50 standing with Ochre
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Look at this, Player. The guild master's nose. In the Walkers' cartoon. It's gone pink. Pink! The Walkers did not paint a pink nose. They painted a furious red one, and I'm out of furious red.
  • Good red comes from a red earth outside the walls, ground and mixed with linseed. The carts used to bring it every spring. Not this spring. The dark stumps up on the Western Descent drag clods of the stuff about in their roots.
  • Would you bring me 25 Clod of Red Earths from the Dark Stumps? Enough for the nose, the cart wheels and the lantern's flame. The wall will thank you. I'll thank you louder.
  • Wonderful! Stonefang Pass, past the boggy foothills, up onto the red ledges. You'll know the earth when you see it. It's the colour of a good argument.
  • Oh, that's all right. The nose can be pink a little longer. (To the wall:) Sorry, old friend.
  • (how many you carry) of 25 Clod of Red Earths. Dark stumps, the Western Descent.
  • (Ochre crumbles a clod between two fingers, sniffs it, and beams.) Oh, that's the stuff. That's the Walkers' red. I'd know it anywhere. I've been mixing it since I was twelve, grinding colours for Rosalba.
  • The nose will be furious again by tonight. And there's enough over to start the first sheet of the Gate Walk. Just the first. Thank you, Player. (To the wall:) See? I told you.

docs.title: Letters to the East
docs.text:
Odda writes to an old friend in Fairy Forest each spring, and the letters go east along the Northern Woodland Trail. Hunt 40 Edge Lizards in the Edgewood so they get there.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Odda Level 17 Leads to Spring Letters

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Edge Lizard in The Edgewood

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,200 EXP
  • 340 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Odda
Dialogue
  • Come in, sit by me a moment. When I was young I walked to the forests as an envoy, as the Brenna did in the old days, and I made a friend there I have never lost. I write to her every spring.
  • The letters go east along the old trail, with whoever is walking. But the walkers tell me the Edge Lizards have crowded into the The Edgewood, where the red rock meets the first trees, and my last letter came back still sealed.
  • Would you clear the way for this year's letters? 40 Edge Lizards in The Edgewood. Then I will trust the trail with them again.
  • Thank you, Player. The The Edgewood is past the The North Ridge, where you first see green. It is a lovely walk, when nothing bites.
  • Of course. A letter that waits a little only has more to say.
  • Forty Edge Lizards in The Edgewood, Player. The trail leaves from the north gate.
  • The walkers say the trail is quiet as a song between verses. Then my letters will reach her this year. She will be cross that the last one was late; she always is.
  • Take these, with my thanks. When the next letter is sealed, I may ask you again.

docs.title: Spring Letters
docs.text:
Odda's letter to her old friend in Fairy Forest is sealed. Take it to Corwell for the next caravan east.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Odda Completed with Corwell Level 30 After Letters to the East

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Odda's Spring Letter

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,400 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • Town Return Scroll x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Odda
Dialogue
  • My letter for the forest is sealed at last. It took me most of the spring. When you are old, you have more to say and less hurry to say it.
  • Corwell sends a caravan east along the woodland trail before the summer is out. He keeps a pouch for my letters, and he has never once lost one. He tells me so every year.
  • Would you take this Odda's Spring Letter to Corwell at the Trading Post, for the next caravan east?
  • Thank you, Player. Mind the seal. My friend reads the seal before the letter, to see if I was cross when I wrote it.
  • Of course. It can sit on my table a little longer. It will not mind.
  • The Odda's Spring Letter to Corwell at the Trading Post.
  • Odda's spring letter? Into the pouch it goes, with the caravan east at the end of the month. I have never lost one, you know. Not in twenty years.
  • Tell her it will be the first thing on the mule and the first thing off.
  • Here, a few things from the shelves, for the walk back. Odda will ask you if the seal was straight. Say yes.

docs.title: The Verse
docs.text:
Ahvi has waited all summer for Odda's word on whether to sing her old verse at a gathering. Hear Odda out, then take her answer to Ahvi.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Odda Completed with Ahvi Level 68 After The Greywater Runs Leads to The Gathering

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 39,000 EXP
  • 1,360 mesos
  • Highland Salve x5
  • Rimwort Tonic x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Odda
Dialogue
  • Ahvi asked me in spring whether to sing the old verse at the next gathering, and I have not answered her. A chieftain who frightens four families for nothing does more harm than any beast.
  • But look at what is in front of me. Lessa's bites. Yarrek's goats. Vosk's gnawed ropes. The springs, and the tree that drank them. And Imre's dates, each a little before the worst nights of the year.
  • You have seen more of it than any of us, Player. I don't need you to tell me what it means; nobody can. I only need you to take my answer to Ahvi: tell her to sing it.
  • Tell her plainly. She will ask whether I am sure, and you may say I am as sure as I have ever been of anything I did not understand.
  • Then I will sit with it another night. I am good at sitting. It is the deciding that is hard.
  • Ahvi is here in the Brenna House. Tell her Odda says to sing it.
  • Odda said that? Sing it? After a whole summer of not yet?
  • Then I will sing it as it was taught to me, no more and no less: that the beasts grew wild in a season before the Burning. The verse does not say why, and I will not add a word to it.
  • Thank you, Player. Neffa will be pleased. She has been listening through the wall all summer and thinks I don't know.

docs.title: Lights on the Hem
docs.text:
Carters from Kaldemor say the Forest's Hem is crawling with bubblings. Thin them out so the travelling lights get through.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Ondine Level 8

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 25 Bubbling in The Forest's Hem

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 131 EXP
  • 176 mesos
  • Travelling Light x2
  • +60 standing with Ondine
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Vesper sells my small lights to the Kaldemor carters, and the carters say the Forest's Hem is crawling. Bubblings, all over the road, bouncing into the carts.
  • I can't have my lanterns arriving in pieces, Player. And I can't send Faelan. He'd come back with fewer fingers and more glass.
  • Clear 25 Bubblings off the Forest's Hem, where the farmland gives way to the trees.
  • Down the lower path from the Forest Edge, then on along the Glimmer Path to the Hem. Mind the carts.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • You've cleared some of them, I hope. The carters will tell me if you haven't.
  • The carters came in this morning without a single cracked pane. Vesper sold out by noon.
  • Take two travelling lights. Don't tell her they were free.

docs.title: The Farthest Lantern
docs.text:
The western outer lanterns keep dimming. Ondine needs one replaced too far out for the workshop to reach safely.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Ondine Level 59 After What the Wind Says Leads to Spring-Glow

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 80 Forest Glimmerfox in The Deepening, V
  • Look at the farthest lantern's post in The Deepening, V

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 67,821 EXP
  • 1,770 mesos
  • +60 standing with Ondine
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • My western lanterns keep dimming. All of them, all at once. Lanterns don't do that.
  • There's a post at the far end of the Deepening with one of mine on it. The workshop can't reach it safely any more. You can.
  • Clear 80 Forest Glimmerfoxes from the last stretch of the Deepening and hang the new lantern on the farthest lantern's post (examine it).
  • It's my brightest. Don't drop it.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The farthest post, end of the Deepening.
  • It's lit? Good. Good. And the old one was dim? Of course it was.
  • Something out there is drinking the light. I need a stronger oil.

docs.title: Spring-Glow
docs.text:
Ondine wants spring-glow from the Twilit Wood's springs for a stronger glow-oil.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Ondine Level 61 After The Farthest Lantern Leads to Nineteen Years of Lanterns

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 20 Spring-Glow (taken)
  • Defeat 100 Creature of the Twilit Woods (Night Glimmerfox, Blue Spring Sprite, Deep Spring Sprite)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 74,882 EXP
  • 1,830 mesos
  • Glow-Oil x5
  • +60 standing with Ondine
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • The springs of the Twilit Wood glow in the dark, and the sprites that live in them carry the glow about. Spring-glow. My grandmother made oil with it, once.
  • Twenty measures and I'll have an oil that won't dim.
  • Bring 20 Spring-Glow from the spring sprites of the Twilit Wood.
  • Mind the cold. The sprites freeze what they touch.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • (how many you carry) of 20.
  • Look at it shine. Grandmother's recipe, my hands.
  • Here, the first of the batch. The rest goes on the western path tonight.

docs.title: Nineteen Years of Lanterns
docs.text:
Ondine has written down how bright she made the outer lanterns every autumn for nineteen years. It is time the Eldest read it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Ondine Level 63 After Spring-Glow Leads to The Watch Goes Out

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Calyra
  2. Talk to Thessaly

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 82,418 EXP
  • 1,890 mesos
  • +150 standing with Ondine
  • +80 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +100 standing with Seren
Dialogue
  • Nineteen years, Player. Every autumn I made the outer lanterns brighter, and every autumn I wrote down how bright. I never showed anyone.
  • Take my book to the Eldest. She should see how far the dark has come.
  • Take Ondine's book to Calyra in the Heart Tree's chamber, then hear what Thessaly says.
  • Mind the pages. Some of them are older than Faelan.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Calyra first. Then Thessaly will have something to say. She always does.
  • They kept it? The promise? Seren has her guards?
  • ...Nineteen years I've been writing in that book. I think I can stop making the lanterns brighter now. I think I can just make them good.
  • Ondine's book. Every autumn, brighter. Nineteen years.
  • Calyra reads for a long time without speaking. Then she closes the book. 'Thessaly. The ledger, please.'
  • The oldest unkept line in my ledger: 'The Council will consider the Warden's request for more guards.' Nineteen years ago. Considered, and considered, and considered.
  • Thessaly reads it aloud, once, very precisely. Then she takes up her pen and, for the first time anyone can remember, draws a line through one of her oldest entries. 'Kept,' she says. 'Seren has her guards.'

docs.title: Following the Root
docs.text:
Oriel comes out himself, for the first time in years, to follow the root to where it is being strangled.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Oriel Level 66 After The Watch Goes Out Leads to The Knotbriar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 120 Creature of the Twilit Woods (Night Glimmerfox, Blue Spring Sprite, Deep Spring Sprite)
  • Reach the Spring-Root Tree in The Twilit Wood, III

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 94,642 EXP
  • 1,980 mesos
  • +150 standing with Oriel
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
  • Unlocks boss.knotbriar
Dialogue
  • I haven't been past the Forest Edge in eleven years. Linnet says that's too long. Linnet is right, and I'll never tell her.
  • The root runs west, under the Twilit Wood, to a spring. I want to see it with my own eyes.
  • Clear the way through the Twilit Wood (120 creatures) and bring Oriel to the Spring-Root Tree at the far end.
  • Slowly. My knees are older than these brambles.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The far end of the Twilit Wood. The tree by the spring.
  • There. You see it? Round the root, under the water. Bramble. Knotted thick as a house, tightening.
  • The Knotbriar. That's what's strangling my homes. The tree will let you down to the spring now.

docs.title: Further Out
docs.text:
Something further out is choking the root. Oriel wants the Deepening cleared enough to follow it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Oriel Level 55 After Soil and Root-Water Leads to What the Wind Says

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 150 Creature of the Deepenings (Gloaming Wisp, Thorny Bramble, Forest Howlet, Night Howlet, Forest Glimmerfox)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 55,056 EXP
  • 1,650 mesos
  • +60 standing with Oriel
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Cold soil, thin water. The root's being strangled somewhere past the Deepening, and I can't follow it with every bramble in the wood snapping at my ankles.
  • Thin them out for me. Then we'll see.
  • Clear 150 creatures from the Deepening.
  • Mind the brambles. They bleed you.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • One hundred and fifty. I'm counting the roots, you count the brambles.
  • Better. I could hear the wood again, out there. Mostly.
  • Sorrel will want to know. He's been hearing something too.

docs.title: The Homes That Will Not Wake
docs.text:
A handful of the very oldest homes woke late this spring, with thin sap and cold rooms. Help Oriel examine one without alarming the family inside.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Oriel Level 51 After Oriel Lingers Leads to Something for Aspen to Point At, Old Friends

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the oldest home's root-wall in Fairy Forest

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 44,002 EXP
  • 1,530 mesos
  • +60 standing with Oriel
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • You'll keep this to yourself. The oldest homes, the ones the first Magicians shaped, woke late this spring. A handful of them. Thin sap. Cold rooms.
  • I need to look at one properly, and I can't have the family inside thinking their home is sick. You'll knock and talk about the weather. I'll put a hand on the root-wall.
  • Put your hand on the oldest home's root-wall beside me (examine it) while the family is distracted.
  • Talk about the weather. Loudly. Linnet says I have no gift for small talk.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The root-wall. Quietly.
  • Feel that? Slow. Like a heart that's tired.
  • It's not the home. The home is fine. It's what feeds it. Something's wrong with the root.

docs.title: Soil and Root-Water
docs.text:
Oriel needs soil and root-water from where the forest's great roots break the surface in the Deepening.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Oriel Level 53 After Something for Aspen to Point At Leads to Further Out

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 12 Root Soil (taken)
  • Bring 12 Root-Water (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 49,323 EXP
  • 1,590 mesos
  • +60 standing with Oriel
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • The great roots come up out of the ground west of the Hollow Oak, in the Deepening. The forest believes they run all the way to the World Tree's.
  • Bring me soil from beside them and the water that pools in their hollows. The wisps and the brambles out there are thick round the roots. They'll be carrying both.
  • Bring 12 Root Soil from the wisps and 12 Root-Water from the brambles of the Deepening.
  • Gently. It's alive, that soil.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • (how many you carry) soil, (how many you carry) water.
  • Cold. Both of them, cold. And the water's thin.
  • Something further out is taking from the root.

docs.title: A Trick for Siora
docs.text:
Orla thinks Siora is far too serious about her fizzling spells. A gentle trick might help.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Orla Level 24 After The Trick That Works, Past the Last Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 6 Firefly Gel (taken)
  • Talk to Siora

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,260 EXP
  • 528 mesos
  • +120 standing with Orla
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Siora
Dialogue
  • Siora practises and practises and fizzles and fizzles and then looks so sad. My rules say never frighten anyone. They don't say never cheer anyone up.
  • Firefly gel glows. If her practice wand glowed just a little the next time she tried... she'd think it worked. And then it might actually work. Belief is half of it.
  • Bring 6 Firefly Gel for Orla's trick, then go and watch Siora practise.
  • Gently. Always gently.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Gel, then Siora.
  • It glowed, and she gasped, and then she tried again and it glowed by itself! A little! Really!
  • I didn't do the second glow. That one was all Siora. Best trick ever.
  • Look! It glowed! I did it! ...I did it?
  • Siora tries again. This time, faintly, it glows by itself.

docs.title: The Trick That Works
docs.text:
Orla has decided Thorne needs to laugh more. Help plan the trick that finally works.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Orla Level 21 After Past the Last Lantern Leads to Catching the Trickster, A Trick for Siora

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Thorne
  2. Look at Thorne's helmet in Fairy Forest

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,202 EXP
  • 462 mesos
  • +100 standing with Orla
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Thorne
Dialogue
  • Shh! I need an accomplice. A good one. You look good.
  • Thorne needs to laugh more. I've moved his boots a little to the left every night for a month and he just gets crosser. My rules are strict: never take, never break, never frighten, never make anyone look foolish in front of others. So. A trick that makes him laugh. Alone.
  • Distract Thorne with a chat, then turn Thorne's helmet by the last lantern around so the plume faces backward (examine it). Just that. Trust me.
  • Hee hee. This is going to be perfect.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Thorne first. Then the helmet.
  • He put it on backwards! He looked in the lantern glass and he laughed! Properly! All on his own!
  • Best trick ever. Thank you, accomplice.
  • Oh, hello! Talking to me? Nobody talks to me on watch. What about? Monsters? Spears? Monsters with spears?
  • ...You're just being friendly? Huh. That's nice. That's actually nice.

docs.title: A Key Missing
docs.text:
For the first time in thirty-four years a key is missing from Osbert's ring: the old cistern key, by the cellar drain. Clear the black rats of the Cisterns and search the silt.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Osbert Level 25 After Scratching in the Cellars Leads to Three Sealed Notes

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Cisterns
  2. Defeat 30 Black Drain Rat in The Cisterns
  3. Look at a glint in the silt in The Cisterns

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,700 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Osbert
Dialogue
  • For thirty-four years every key on this ring has been where it ought to be. This morning, one was not.
  • The old cistern key. It hangs by the cellar drain, and the cellar drain, as you know, is now a highway for rats.
  • I believe it went down the drain, with help. Go to the The Cisterns, clear 30 Black Drain Rats and look in the silt for anything that glints.
  • You will not mention this to anyone. A steward who loses a key is a steward who is asked questions.
  • Then I shall carry a ring with a gap in it. It will feel like a missing tooth.
  • The The Cisterns. Thirty Black Drain Rats, then the silt.
  • ...The cistern key. With tooth marks.
  • Back on the ring. I do not thank people often, Player, so pay attention: thank you.

docs.title: Scratching in the Cellars
docs.text:
Rats are coming up from the old drains into the palace cellars. Deal with them in the Old Drains, then tell Cuthbert his stores are safe.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Osbert Level 22 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to A Key Missing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Drain Rat in The Old Drains
  2. Talk to Cuthbert

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,700 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Osbert
Dialogue
  • The cellar book says nothing about rats. The cellar, I regret to say, does.
  • Something is driving them up out of the old drains and into my larders. I will not have it.
  • Go down by the grating in Steps Lane and see to 30 Drain Rats in the The Old Drains. Then tell Cuthbert his stores are safe, before he starts shouting at the rats instead of the pots.
  • Thank you. Wipe your boots when you come back. Thoroughly.
  • Very well. I shall count the flour sacks again. Twice.
  • Thirty Drain Rats, then Cuthbert. And the boots.
  • Cuthbert said nothing polite? Then he is pleased. The cellar book will say 'rats: none'. I prefer that kind of entry. Thank you.
  • Thirty of them? HA! That is thirty fewer thieves in my flour!
  • Tell Osbert thank you. No, tell him nothing; he worries when I am polite.

docs.title: Three Sealed Notes
docs.text:
Osbert has three sealed notes for Agnes, Peterkin and Cuthbert, in that order. Carry them, do not hurry, and do not read them.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Osbert Level 27 After A Key Missing

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Agnes
  2. Talk to Peterkin
  3. Talk to Cuthbert

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,400 EXP
  • 540 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Osbert
Dialogue
  • I have three notes to deliver: to Agnes, Peterkin and Cuthbert, in that order. Sealed.
  • Carry them, would you? Do not hurry, and do not lose them. And, naturally, do not read them.
  • Agnes first. She will be somewhere in the upper halls, hearing things.
  • Then I shall give them to Peterkin, who will run, and drop one.
  • Agnes, then Peterkin, then Cuthbert. Seals unbroken.
  • Three notes delivered, three seals unbroken. I looked.
  • There was nothing to read, of course; it was not the notes I was testing. Do come back, Player. I may have more errands for someone who does not peek.
  • A note from Osbert? For me? ...Oh. It is blank.
  • Both sides! He is testing you. You did not peek, did you? I would have.
  • Is it urgent? Shall I run it somewhere? ...It is blank!
  • He did that to me too, when I was new. I did not peek either. Nearly.
  • A note from His Stewardship? Blank! HA! The old fox.
  • He gave me one of these thirty years ago. I read it. Do not tell him.

docs.title: Across After Dark
docs.text:
For the first time anyone can remember, Osmund asks someone to cross with him after dark. Clear the crocos from the Undercut, then stand above the Heron Pool where the deep water runs.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Osmund Level 43 After Seasoned Timber Leads to The Boy and the Deep, The Truth for Lucan

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Undercut Croco in The Undercut
  2. Reach above the Heron Pool in The Undercut

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 24,850 EXP
  • 860 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Osmund
Dialogue
  • (The old ferryman looks at you for a long time. Then, very quietly:) Cross with me. Tonight. After dark.
  • (He nods upriver.) First, the The Undercut. 40 Undercut Crocos. Then stand above the Heron Pool. Deep water. Watch it. Then come.
  • (A nod. That one means: thank you.)
  • (A nod. That one means: another night.)
  • (He holds up four fingers, then points upriver, then at the deep water.)
  • (At dusk he poles you out. In the deep channel, the ferry lifts a hand's breadth under you, slowly, and settles.)
  • End of last summer. Same. Then a wake, against the current. Nothing at its head. Shadows since. (He looks at you.) Not there when I was young. Now you know. Now someone knows.

docs.title: Osmund the boy and the deep
The Boy and the Deep
docs.text:
Osmund fears the day Robin decides he is old enough to find out what is in the deep channel. He asks you to put down one of the great crocos of the Undercut, and to tell Robin what you saw.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Osmund Level 45 After Across After Dark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 1 Elite Undercut Croco
  2. Talk to Robin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,170 EXP
  • 900 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Osmund
Dialogue
  • (Osmund watches Robin on the mud below the landing. Then he turns to you.) Boy's brave. Too brave.
  • (He points upriver.) Big one. Touched. On the The Undercut. Elite Undercut Croco. Kill it. Then tell Robin. Tell him true.
  • (A long nod.)
  • (A short nod. Another time.)
  • (He points upriver, then at Robin, then at you.)
  • (Robin is sitting on the step beside Osmund, closer than usual. Osmund's hand rests on his shoulder.)
  • Told him true. Good. (He pulls a knot in the mooring rope tight, then nods at you, the longest nod you have seen him give.)
  • Grandad sent you? You killed a croc as big as that? Bigger than the ferry?
  • (He is quiet for a bit.) I won't go to the deep end. I promise. Not alone, and not ever after dark. Tell Grandad. Actually, I'll tell him myself.

docs.title: Knock Twice
docs.text:
Osric keeps the old woodsmen's sayings. Put down 40 Driftstumps near the crews, then knock twice on the last stump on the Forest Shore.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Osric Level 26 Leads to The Black Marks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Driftstump
  2. Look at the last stump in Goa Harbour

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,800 EXP
  • 1,040 mesos
  • Salted Fish x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Osric
Dialogue
  • You knock on a stump before you sit on it. Twice. Every woodsman on this shore did, once. Now only I do, and the young ones laugh.
  • They don't laugh at the Driftstumps, mind. A stump that gets up and walks, and they still sit down without knocking.
  • Put down 40 Driftstumps on Strandwood Edge, near where the crews rest. Then go to the last stump on this shore and knock on it. Twice. Humour me.
  • And don't whistle out there. Not under the big trees. I'm not asking.
  • Suit yourself. The sayings don't need you to believe them.
  • Forty Driftstumps on Strandwood Edge. Then knock on the last stump. Twice, not once.
  • Twice? Good.
  • Never whistle under the big trees. Never sleep with your back to the deep wood. Be out of the forest before the sun is. Those are the ones that matter.
  • My father laughed at them. I never did. Here, take this, and keep the sayings. They cost nothing.

docs.title: The Black Marks
docs.text:
Osric wants a black line marked along the forest edge that no cutter goes past. Bring him 25 Slater Plates for the tar, and tell Haldor what the marks are for.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Osric Level 40 After Knock Twice

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 25 Slater Plate (taken)
  • Talk to Haldor

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,000 EXP
  • 1,600 mesos
  • Elixir x3
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Osric
Dialogue
  • I mark the trees now. Which ones the crews cut, along the edge. I've marked trees one way or another for thirty years.
  • I want another line marked. Not trees to cut. Trees no one goes past. A black mark at the height of a man's eye, all along the edge, so a cutter knows where the edge stops without asking me.
  • Chalk washes off. Paint flakes. But the slaters on the Wrack Ledges eat tarred rope, and their backs come away black with it. Boiled down, that holds on bark through a winter.
  • Bring me 25 Slater Plates from the Sea Slaters on the Wrack Ledges. Then tell Haldor what I'm marking, and that it's for all of them. He'll know who I mean.
  • I'll boil it down in daylight and mark in daylight. Don't bring them to me after dark. I'll not open the door.
  • Then I'll find another way. There's always another way, it's only slower.
  • (how many you carry) of 25 Slater Plates. The slaters keep to the Wrack Ledges and the Undercliff. And a word with Haldor.
  • A black line along the edge, and no one past it. Aye. Osric's right, and he's never once asked me for anything in twelve years. Tell him I'll walk the line with the crews myself, every one of them. Merrin first.
  • He'll walk them along it? Merrin first? Good.
  • She looks at the deep trees the way I used to. A mark won't stop her, maybe. But it'll make her stop and look at it, and that's a breath of time. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Birds for Miss Maren
docs.text:
Ossie wants Maren to see the bird page of his logbook. He is shy about it.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Ossie Level 58 After The Blue Logbook

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Maren

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 44,318 EXP
  • 1,276 mesos
  • +40 standing with Ossie
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • My logbook has a page of birds. With drawings. Miss Maren gave me the book.
  • Could you show her the bird page? I'd show her myself but she'll mark the spelling.
  • Don't let her mark 'cormorant'. I know it's wrong.
  • Another time, then.
  • Show Ossie's bird page to Maren on Merchant Street.
  • She liked it? She said 'a keeper's eye'? A KEEPER'S eye.
  • She can mark 'cormorant' then. I don't mind.
  • Oh, look at these. The gulls, the terns, a skua over the headland. He's drawn the wing shapes exactly.
  • Tell him he has a keeper's eye. And that 'cormorant' has two r's. I'll only say it once.

docs.title: The Blue Logbook
docs.text:
Ossie has something in his blue logbook he has told no one about. He wants you to check his dates against his gran's log.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Ossie Level 56 After Keeping the Light Leads to The Locked Chart, Birds for Miss Maren

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ysolde

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 58,082 EXP
  • 1,680 mesos
  • +60 standing with Ossie
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Can I show you something? Only you. And then maybe Gran.
  • This spring, one night I couldn't sleep, I was at the top of the tower alone. I saw a pale light moving under the water, far out past the headland. I wrote it down. Date, time, weather.
  • I didn't tell anyone. Gran says don't repeat things. Could you ask Gran if she ever saw it too? On the same night?
  • Only you. And Gran.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Ysolde whether she saw a light on the night in Ossie's logbook.
  • The same night? The SAME night? Gran saw it too?
  • Then it's real and I'm a real keeper. I wrote it down properly. Like a keeper does. Gran's going to put my logbook next to hers.
  • The boy logged it? Show me the date. ...That's in my margin too. The same night. The same hour, near enough.
  • He told no one. Of course he didn't. He's mine. Tell him a keeper writes it down and then tells the keeper. Tell him he did both.

docs.title: Figures for the Vault
docs.text:
Ottilie compares her ledgers with Hobart's chalk tallies every season. She asks you to carry the comparison down to the warehouses.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Ottilie Level 31 Leads to The Dues Ledger

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Hobart

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,932 EXP
  • 682 mesos
  • +40 standing with Ottilie
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Every season I compare the hall's ledger with Hobart's chalk on the warehouse door post. When they agree, I sleep very well.
  • My knees won't take the dock steps today. Would you take this page of figures down to Hobart? Speak on his right side. He hears better there. Mostly.
  • His right side. He pretends otherwise.
  • Another time, then.
  • Take Ottilie's figures to Hobart at the Docks.
  • He agrees? To the crate?
  • Oh, that is a good day. Have a sweet. Have two. You filled in nothing incorrectly at all.
  • Eh? Ottilie's figures? Give 'em here. On the right. That's it.
  • Ledger says forty-one. Chalk says forty-one. Tell her the chalk agrees with her, for once. She'll be unbearable.

docs.title: The Dues Ledger
docs.text:
Corwin and Annis argue about harbour dues at every council meeting. Ottilie asks you to fetch both captains' figures so the ledger can settle it.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Ottilie Level 42 After Figures for the Vault

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Corwin
  • Talk to Annis

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 17,013 EXP
  • 924 mesos
  • +40 standing with Ottilie
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The council has spent three meetings on whether the Heron pays more dues than the Saltlark. The Heron does. By two coppers a ton. I have the ledger.
  • But nobody believes a ledger until both captains have said their own number out loud. Ask Captain Corwin and Captain Annis what they think they pay. Then I'll show them both the page.
  • Write down exactly what they say. Exactly.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Captain Corwin and Captain Annis on the docks what dues they pay.
  • Corwin says he pays more. Annis says she pays more. They are both right, by two coppers a ton, in opposite directions, because Annis counts her salt barrel.
  • I'll write that in the minutes. They will both be furious. It will be the shortest council meeting this year.
  • My dues? Four silver and two coppers a ton, and every copper of it a waste. Write that down.
  • And tell Ottilie the Saltlark loads first more often than it should.
  • What I pay? Four silver and four coppers a ton, counting the salt. The salt counts.
  • Tell Ottilie that Corwin casts off under new moons and pays less for the privilege.

docs.title: Marguerite's Bobbins
docs.text:
Nana Gristle said the bobbins packed around her mother on the Long Walk were blue, and Ozzie Lantry has never heard that before. Ask Nana about the lace bobbins again, and bring Ozzie boar bristle to bind his swelling notes.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Ozzie Lantry Level 33 After The First Winter

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Nana Gristle
  2. Bring 15 Boar Bristle (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,220 EXP
  • 4,180 mesos
  • +70 standing with Ozzie Lantry
  • +20 standing with Nana Gristle
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Blue. I keep coming back to blue. I have written Nana's mother's story down twenty-three times, and in twenty-two of them the bobbins had no colour at all. Now they are blue. Either she has remembered something, or she has improved something.
  • Marguerite made lace, you know. A Walker, and a fine one, and no Selsior guild would have her. If her bobbins were blue, perhaps they were painted for her, perhaps someone in the city still has one. A history is mostly small things like that.
  • Ask Nana Gristle about the bobbins again, kindly. And while you are out past the Outworks: my notes have burst their strings. Bring me 15 Boar Bristle from the Bristle Boars and I will twist a cord that never frays.
  • Bristle cord: my grandfather tied his song sheets with it. They are still tied. Do not ask Nana whether she made it up, mind. Ask about the bobbins and let her talk.
  • Ah, well. The notes will sit in a heap, and the bobbins will stay blue, or not blue. I can wait. I am very good at waiting. I am bad at everything else.
  • Nana and the bobbins, and (how many you carry) of 15 Boar Bristle so far. My notes are currently held together by a stern look.
  • The bobbins? Ozzie has gone and wondered about them, has he? Good. About time somebody did. My grandmother's bobbins were what kept my mother in that basket all the way from Selsior. Little turned wooden things, a whole bag of them.
  • Were they blue? Well. Mother said they were the colour of the sky on the day they walked. And I have always thought that day must have been blue. So yes. Blue. And if Ozzie writes a question mark next to it, I shall know.
  • Tell him that's the honest truth, and tell him to come and sit with me himself one evening instead of sending young people. We'll go to Saucer's. He can pay.
  • The colour of the sky on the day they walked. Oh. Oh, that is better than blue. That is much better than blue. That is true in a way that blue never was.
  • I shall write it down exactly as she said it, and no question mark. And I shall bind it with this bristle, which is excellent bristle; you have pulled it from boars that did not want to give it, I can tell.
  • And I am to go to Saucer's with Nana, and pay. I suppose that is history too. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: The First Winter
docs.text:
Ozzie Lantry's history of Urbanograd has a hole in its middle: not one account of the Walkers' first winter. Ask the city's keepers of old things, Nana Gristle, Hambone and Thimble, whether they ever heard a word of it.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Ozzie Lantry Level 21 Leads to Marguerite's Bobbins

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Nana Gristle
  2. Talk to Hambone
  3. Talk to Thimble

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,400 EXP
  • 3,780 mesos
  • +50 standing with Ozzie Lantry
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Ah, hello, hello. Mind the box. And that one. Have you seen my spectacles? The reading ones. No, wait, I am wearing them. Then where are the distance ones? Never mind. You look like someone who asks questions. Good. I have one.
  • Eighteen years I have been writing Urbanograd's first hundred. I have the Walk, I have the spring after, I have the first lanterns. And of the first winter I have nothing. Not a letter, not a line. As if the whole city held its breath for a season and wrote none of it down.
  • I have asked everyone, of course. But I am an old man, and old men ask the same way every time. Ask for me: Nana Gristle on her bench, Hambone at the theatre cart, and Thimble with her costume chests. Somebody's grandmother might have said something once.
  • Nana is in Lantern Square, Hambone and Thimble in the Old Barracks Yard. If you find so much as a recipe from that winter, come back running. Well, walking. I would hate you to fall.
  • Of course, of course. It has kept a hundred years. It will keep another week. Probably. I say that every week.
  • Nana Gristle, Hambone, Thimble. Anything at all about the first winter. A word. A rumour of a word.
  • The first winter? Ozzie sent you. Of course he did. Sit, then. My mother, Posy, was a baby of a few months on the Long Walk, carried out of Selsior in a laundry basket, with her grandmother Marguerite's lace bobbins packed round her to keep her from rolling.
  • That is the most important fact in this city, and you may tell anyone who argues. The bobbins were blue, did I say that? They were blue.
  • The winter, though? I was not born, dear, and Mother was a baby. A baby remembers milk and a basket. Tell Ozzie I said that, and tell him the bobbins were blue.
  • The first winter? Can't help you there, I'm afraid. I can tell you about these three planks, mind. Dark ones, in the middle of the stage. Fenwick Corliss told me they came off Juna's own cart, and Fenwick kept this cart before me.
  • Is it true? I couldn't swear to it. Ozzie's looked for a letter either way for years and found nothing. But I polish them every Walkout Day and I hum her songs while I do it, and they've never let anybody fall through.
  • Winter, though, no. Nothing about any winter was handed down with the cart. Just the planks, and the songs, and the wheels. Tell him I'm sorry. I am, too. I'd love to know.
  • Mm? Hold still, I am not talking to you, I am talking to this hem. The first winter? Ozzie asks me every year. Every year I tell him: I keep cloth, not stories.
  • I have a scrap of every Juna jacket I ever made, sewn in my coat lining, here. Thirty years of green. The oldest jacket of all, the very first one, I have never found. Not in any chest, not in any attic. If it ever turns up, it may have a letter in its pocket. They usually do. But it has not.
  • So no. Nothing. Tell him to eat something; he looks thin. And tell him he owes me a button.
  • Blue bobbins. Three planks. A lost green jacket. And not one word of the winter. No, no, do not look like that; it is exactly what I expected. It is still useful. Every 'nothing' is a door I can stop knocking on.
  • Though the bobbins being blue is new. She has never once said blue. I shall write it down, with a small question mark, the way I write down everything Nana adds.
  • Thank you, Player. If you are ever in an old attic, and you see paper, think of me. Then think of my spectacles, and tell me where they are.

docs.title: Seed from Kaldemor
docs.text:
Old Parsnip's oldest vegetable varieties came from Kaldemor's farms long ago, and his seed drawers are running empty. Rue grew up on a farm out that way.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Old Parsnip Level 28 After Earth for the Tubs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Rue

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,870 EXP
  • 1,680 mesos
  • +50 standing with Old Parsnip
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • My old varieties, the yellow beet, the long white radish, the wrinkled pea that tastes of honey, came up the road from Kaldemor's farms a long time ago. I have kept them going by saving seed. But every year a few more drawers come up empty.
  • Young Rue, the girl who plays Juna, grew up on a farm out Kaldemor way. Ask whether her people could send fresh seed of the old kinds when the carts run. I would ask her myself, but she goes all quiet when anybody looks at her.
  • She rehearses up here sometimes, to the cat. Or try the theatre yard. Follow the sound of somebody being very brave at a wall.
  • Then the drawers make do. Drawers are patient. I am less so, at my age.
  • Ask Rue about seed from Kaldemor's farms, Player.
  • The honey pea? We grow that! My mother calls it the wrinkled pea; she says it looks like my grandad. (Rue laughs, then remembers you are listening, and goes quiet.)
  • I will write home tonight. The cider cart goes next week, if the road is open. Tell Old Parsnip I will ask for the yellow beet too. It turns the soup pink.
  • The yellow beet too? Did you hear that, drawers? Help is coming. Slowly, by cart, the way help always comes.
  • You are a good seed, Player. That is the highest thing I say about anybody. Do not tell the beans.

docs.title: Parsnip red earth for the tubs
Earth for the Tubs
docs.text:
Every handful of soil on the Rooftops was carried up the stairs, and more people want seed than ever. Old Parsnip needs the black mud of the bog-lurchers to fill new tubs.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Old Parsnip Level 19 Leads to Seed from Kaldemor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Mud Clump (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,340 EXP
  • 1,690 mesos
  • +40 standing with Old Parsnip
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Shh. Not you, I was talking to the beans. They are sulking. They want deeper soil, and I cannot blame them.
  • Everything up here was carried up the stairs, every handful. And now more folk come asking for seed each week, which means more tubs, which means more earth, and the carts bring less of everything.
  • The bog-lurchers in the Seepwater Foothills are made of the best black mud you ever smelled. Mixed with old straw, it sets a tub right. Bring me 20 Mud Clumps, and the beans will stop sulking.
  • The foothills are up Stonefang Pass, past the Gate Meadows. Wet boots. Bring a spare pair.
  • No hurry. Seeds teach you that. Seeds and beans.
  • 20 Mud Clumps from the bog-lurchers, Player. You have (how many you carry).
  • Ohh, smell that. That is good mud. That is mud with opinions.
  • There you are, beans, a deep bed. No more sulking. Thank you, Player. Come back in a month and I will give you a carrot that makes you weep.

docs.title: Bite Herbs
docs.text:
The lampbats' bites go bad if they are not cleaned, and Patch's jar of bite-cleaning herb is empty. It grows only in the Outworks' ditches, where the ditch rats drag it into their nests. Bring her 15 sprigs.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Patch Level 24 After New Panes Leads to The Rhythm Outside

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Bite Herb (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,000 EXP
  • 2,400 mesos
  • +50 standing with Patch
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • You have been in the Outworks. I can tell; you have that grey ditch mud on your boots and a scratch on your neck you have not noticed. Sit. Hold still.
  • Every lantern Lux hangs out there now, somebody goes out to hang it, and somebody comes back bitten. Lampbat bites go green in two days if you do not clean them. I clean them with a bitter little herb, and my jar is empty.
  • It grows in the wet bottoms of the old ditches, under the walls. My mother used to send me for it. The Ditch Rats line their nests with it now, the clever things. It keeps the fleas off.
  • Bring me 15 Bite Herbs. Turn out the Ditch Rats' nests and you will find it. Narrow leaves, smells like pepper when you crush it.
  • Good. And there, your neck is done. It will sting. That means it is working. Off you go.
  • Then I will make do with salt water and swearing. It has worked before. Barely.
  • Fifteen Bite Herbs from the Ditch Rats' nests in the Outworks. You carry (how many you carry). Narrow leaves, peppery.
  • Peppery. Yes. Fresh, and not too much rat on it. This will clean every bite that comes through the gate this month, and the lamp-hangers will stop looking at me like I am the dangerous one.
  • Thank you, Player. Go and see Drum; I hear Drum has some notion about noise and lanterns. Here, a sweet first. Everybody gets one.

docs.title: Meadow Herbs
docs.text:
Patch's jars are emptying and Brindle will not let her into the fields alone. Thin out the verge adders in the Gate Meadows and bring back 10 bundles of the herbs they nest in.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Patch Level 16

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 20 Verge Adder
  • Bring 10 Meadow Herb (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,470 EXP
  • 1,550 mesos
  • +40 standing with Patch
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Sit down, you are in the way of the light. No, I do not need to look at you, you are not bleeding. I need your legs. Mine are sixty-eight years old and Brindle has forbidden them the fields.
  • Yarrow, feverfew, a bit of plantain: the hedge herbs. They grow thick along the verges of the Gate Meadows, and the Verge Adders have taken to coiling up in them. Lie down in a patch of yarrow and you wake up bitten. Which then comes back to me.
  • Clear 20 Verge Adders out of the verges and bring me 10 Meadow Herbs. You will find the herbs in their nests. Yarrow has feathery leaves. Hemlock has purple spots on the stem. If it has spots, leave it.
  • Good. And if one bites you, walk back here; do not run, it pumps the poison. I will scold you and fix it, in that order.
  • Then go and stand somewhere else. I have work.
  • Twenty Verge Adders, ten Meadow Herbs. You carry (how many you carry). No spots on the stems.
  • Let me see. Yarrow. Yarrow. Plantain, good. Feverfew, a little crushed, it will do. No hemlock. Hm. Somebody taught you something.
  • That is a week of bites cleaned, maybe two. Here, a boiled sweet. Do not look at me like that, everybody gets one. Now go, I need the table.

docs.title: The Rare Root
docs.text:
Patch's best fever root grows only in the Silent Cutting, the wooded road Shade no longer walks. The barkbacks there grub it up and carry it in the moss on their backs. Bring her 5 Silent Roots.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Patch Level 43 After The Spark Lamp Leads to A Boar-Spear Head

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 5 Silent Root (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,280 EXP
  • 2,150 mesos
  • +60 standing with Patch
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • If there is going to be a hunt, there are going to be fevers after. There always are. Tusk wounds go hot by the second night. I have one root that pulls a fever down, and I have none of it.
  • It grows in the The Silent Cutting, where the birds stopped singing. Shade will not take travelers through there any more, and Shade is not a nervous person. I used to dig it there with my mother, and the birds were so loud you could not hear yourself.
  • The Barkbacks dig it up and pack it into the moss on their backs. Do not ask me why. Ask the barkbacks. Then hit them, and take it.
  • Bring me 5 Silent Roots from the Barkbacks in the Silent Cutting. Pale, knotted, smells of earth and cloves. And come back. That part is not optional.
  • Good. Take a sweet for the road. No, two. It is quiet in there; you will want something to crunch.
  • Then I pray nobody comes back from that hunt with a fever. I do not pray. I will start.
  • Five Silent Roots, from the Barkbacks in the The Silent Cutting. You carry (how many you carry). Cloves and earth.
  • Oh. Oh, look at these. Fat as thumbs. Nobody has brought me silent root in four years. I could weep. I will not; I have patients.
  • Was it as quiet as they say? No, do not tell me. I want to remember it with the birds in it.
  • Thank you, Player. You have the hands for this, you know, and the head. If you ever get tired of hitting things, I will teach you yarrow from hemlock properly. Now get out, I have roots to dry.

docs.title: Across the Crest
docs.text:
The great feathers come from the Crest. Climb across it toward the Highbeacon and bring down three of the Disturbance-touched duskhawks that guard the way.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Perch Level 63 After The All-Hours Route Leads to The Highbeacon

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Crest
  2. Defeat 3 Elite Disturbance-touched duskhawks (Duskhawk)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 84,520 EXP
  • 7,560 mesos
  • +60 standing with Perch
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The feathers come from the crest. The herders on the Ram Hills say a shadow goes over the highest tower there, morning and evening, and the duskhawks under it are not like other duskhawks.
  • Climb across The Crest toward the Highbeacon and see how close a person can get. The worst of the duskhawks there are Disturbance-touched. Bring down 3 of the touched ones, and tell me what the air is like up there.
  • Starling watches from the crest, some nights. If you meet Starling up there, make sure Starling has eaten something.
  • Nobody has to climb toward a thing that frightens pigeons. I would not ask twice.
  • Across The Crest, Player, and 3 touched Duskhawks. Mind the wind on the high ground.
  • The hawks went for you as if you were standing in their doorway. Then you were close. Closer than any of my birds would go.
  • So it nests on the Highbeacon. The tallest tower of the old line, and the one my birds will not fly past at any hour. I think I must see Starling about this.

docs.title: Stormcrest
docs.text:
Stormcrest sleeps at noon on the Highbeacon, and the routes over its tower have been dead for years. Go up and face it.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Perch Level 66 After The Highbeacon Leads to Dates and Lists

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Stormcrest

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 110,910 EXP
  • 1,980 mesos
  • Elixir x10
  • +80 standing with Perch
  • +50 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Stormcrest sleeps at noon on the Highbeacon. The routes over its tower have been dead for as long as Greyfeather has been grey.
  • I will not ask you to go. I will only say that if Stormcrest were gone, some of my birds might fly east again at any hour, and the carts would not be the only road. Will you go up the Highbeacon and face it?
  • Speak to me when you are ready, and I will tell you the wind. Take more potions than you think you need. Then take a few more.
  • Good. I mean it: good. Nobody should go up there lightly.
  • Stormcrest, on the Highbeacon. Ask me for the way when you are ready, Player.
  • You are back. You are back, and your hair is full of feathers, and I have never been so glad to see feathers on anybody.
  • This morning I opened the loft at dawn and Greyfeather's daughter went east. East, over the crest, without circling once. I stood there like an old fool and watched until she was gone.
  • Take these, for the bruises. I have more thanks than I have words, Player. The birds will say the rest, in time.

docs.title: The All-Hours Route
docs.text:
A few routes Perch's birds refuse at every hour, and all of them cross the Ram Hills. Clear the rams and howlers along the route and bring back the great feathers the rams carry in their fleece.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Perch Level 60 After The Beacon Ruins Leads to Across the Crest

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Millstone Ram in Ram Hills
  • Defeat 30 Downs Howler in Ram Hills
  • Bring 3 Great Grey Feather (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 226,860 EXP
  • 10,200 mesos
  • +60 standing with Perch
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The dusk routes I understand now, a little. It is the others that trouble me. A few roads the birds will not take at any hour: noon, midnight, a clear blue morning. All of them pass over the Ram Hills, toward the tallest tower on the crest.
  • Lux came back from the Beacon Line saying the old towers stand bare and dark. Bare and dark is not what my birds are afraid of.
  • Walk the all-hours route across the Ram Hills. Clear 40 Millstone Rams and 30 Downs Howlers from the way, and bring me 3 Great Grey Feathers. The herders say the rams pick them up in their fleece and wear them about without noticing.
  • Keep your eyes on the ground for the feathers and on the sky for whatever dropped them. Both at once. I know. Pigeon keepers learn to.
  • Then the list stays as it is, a while longer.
  • 40 Millstone Rams and 30 Downs Howlers on the Ram Hills, and 3 Great Grey Feathers. You have (how many you carry).
  • Let me see. Oh. Oh, look at the size of it. A feather as long as my arm, and a quill like a pipe stem. No hawk wore this.
  • Whatever it is lives on the crest, and my birds can feel it from the loft. I would rather know than guess, Player. I am too old to guess. Keep these out of the cat's reach while I think.

docs.title: The Highbeacon
docs.text:
Perch wants to know when the thing on the Highbeacon leaves its tower and when it sleeps. Ask Starling to watch it through the telescope.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Perch Level 65 After Across the Crest Leads to Stormcrest

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Starling

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 28,260 EXP
  • 3,900 mesos
  • +70 standing with Perch
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
  • Unlocks boss.stormcrest
Dialogue
  • I have kept my list and Starling has kept the dates, and between us we have watched that tower for two years without knowing what we were watching. Now we know what lives in it, at least.
  • Go up to Starling's roof, Player, and ask Starling to turn the telescope on the Highbeacon. I want to know when the thing on the tower leaves it, and when it comes home. Then come back to me.
  • Starling sleeps through the afternoons, in the hammock between the chimneys. Wake Starling gently. Or loudly. Gently does not usually work.
  • Another day. The tower is not going anywhere. That is rather the problem.
  • Starling's roof, Player, below the Crooked Tower. Ask about the Highbeacon.
