  • Perch sent you? About the tower? Oh, I have watched that tower. Here, look, the third eyepiece. No, the third, the one with the scratch. It leaves at first light and at dusk, every day, and it comes home with the wind behind it.
  • Something with wings wider than a street, Player. It sits on the beacon cup like a lid. Tell Perch: at noon it sleeps. If anybody goes, go at noon.
  • At noon. Of course. Even the worst of them must sleep. Thank you, Player. And thank Starling, if Starling remembers being asked.
  • The herders call it Stormcrest. If you mean to go up the Highbeacon, tell me, and I will tell you which way the wind is. That much I can do. I cannot make my birds brave. I can only stop asking them to be.

docs.title: The Refused Message
docs.text:
Perch's pigeons refuse to carry a message east over the downs. Walk it over the Lower Downs and release a young pigeon on the far side, past where the birds turn back.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Perch Level 50 Leads to What Waits at Dusk

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the far side of the Lower Downs in Lower Downs

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,970 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • +60 standing with Perch
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Sit, if you like. Mind the cat. I have kept this loft fifty-one years, Player, and for most of them a bird went where it was asked. Then, a few years ago, old Greyfeather would not take the road east at dusk. Then others would not. I keep a list.
  • This message must go east, over the downs. Three birds I have tried. Each one went up, circled the tower once, and came back to the loft as if I had asked it to fly into a wall.
  • So we will cheat a little. Carry Perch's Message and a young bird in a basket over the Lower Downs, past where they turn back, and let her go on the far side. From there she knows her way, I think. Will you walk it for me?
  • Out through the Bristlewood's far end and up onto the downs. Open the basket where the ground starts to fall away east. Speak to her first. Not much. Just so she knows your voice.
  • Of course. The message has waited three days. It can wait a fourth. The birds do not hurry for anyone, and I have learned not to either.
  • The far side of the Lower Downs, Player. Open the basket there, not before. Before, she would only turn round and come home to me.
  • She went? East, and did not circle back? Good. Good. Then it is the ground nearer the city they will not cross, not the whole road.
  • I will write that beside the route. Another line on the list. I do not know what the list means, Player. I only know it grows.

docs.title: What Waits at Dusk
docs.text:
The routes Perch's birds refuse at dusk they will fly at noon. Something hunts along them when the light goes: thin the duskhawks of the downs.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Perch Level 51 After The Refused Message Leads to Kite Laid Up

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Duskhawk

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 97,940 EXP
  • 5,100 mesos
  • +60 standing with Perch
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • The routes they refuse at dusk, they will take at noon. Same road, same wind, same bird. It is the hour that matters to them, not the place.
  • Something waits along the dusk routes. If it is what I think, it has wings, and it hunts when the light goes. Go out on the downs and thin them for me: 50 Duskhawks.
  • Watch the sky when the shadows get long. A pigeon sees them before you will. Look where a pigeon would look.
  • Another evening, then. There is always another evening. For now.
  • 50 Duskhawks on the downs, Player. They come out as the light goes.
  • Duskhawks. Of course. I should have guessed from how the birds hold their wings when they come in late: tucked tight, every one of them, as if the air bit.
  • Fifty fewer is a kindness to every bird I own. It will not empty the sky, I know. But tonight I may send one out a little later than I dared yesterday.

docs.title: How the Line Held
docs.text:
Percival wants to know how it feels to stand against a charge, for the play's Savage warrior. He would go himself, but there is a matinee.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Percival Level 23 Leads to What She Would Need

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 35 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,810 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Percival
Dialogue
  • The front line held the Balrog at the Tree for days. Days! I want to stand as they stood.
  • I need to know what a charge feels like. From the front. I would go myself, naturally, but there is a matinee.
  • Stand against the charge of 35 Downs Boars on The Thyme Banks, then tell me how you held your ground.
  • And how you stood. Feet. Shoulders. Every detail.
  • Quite right. It is not for everyone. It is barely for me.
  • Thirty-five boars on The Thyme Banks. Notice your feet.
  • Low? Wide? You did not swirl anything? Fascinating.
  • I swirl too much. I see it now. Thank you, Player. That was more useful than any book.

docs.title: What She Would Need
docs.text:
For the first time in ten years, Percival wants to ask Rosamund what she would need from him to make the Last Stand work. He cannot ask her himself.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Percival Level 27 After How the Line Held

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Rosamund

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,370 EXP
  • 540 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Percival
Dialogue
  • I have been thinking. A dangerous pastime. The Last Stand needs the Magician and the warrior both.
  • I want to ask Rosamund what she would need from me to make it work. I have rehearsed it eleven times. I cannot say it to her face.
  • Ask Rosamund for me: what would she need from me, to make the Last Stand work? Exactly that.
  • Not through Tibb. Tibb edits.
  • No. Of course. I shall rehearse it a twelfth time.
  • Ask her, Player. Exactly my words.
  • Stop swirling the cloak in her scene? I can do that. I can... try to do that.
  • And she said the Last Stand needs me? She said that? You are certain? Do not tell her I asked twice.
  • He asked what I would need? Percival? Asked?
  • Tell him to stop swirling that cloak in my scene. And... tell him the Last Stand needs him. Don't tell him I said the second part.

docs.title: Ballast for the Model
docs.text:
Peregrine wants to tow his half-model again in the rock pools, properly weighted this time. Ironback claws are heavy and even.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Peregrine Level 23 Leads to Faster Through the Cut

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Ironback Claw (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,877 EXP
  • 506 mesos
  • +40 standing with Peregrine
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • I want to test the model again. Properly. Last time Kit stood on it, which isn't a fair test.
  • I need ballast, all the same weight. Ironback claws! They're heavy and they're all nearly the same. I weighed one Keziah brought back.
  • Bring me 10 Ironback Claws from the Timber Ponds? For science. And for winning the race. Mostly science.
  • Same size if you can! Science!
  • Another time, then.
  • Ten ironback claws. You have (how many you carry).
  • Ten. Weighed. Matched. Nearly matched. Close enough.
  • We towed it twice in the pools this morning. It won both times. Kit didn't stand on it once. I'll show Master Dunstan. When he lifts the rag.

docs.title: Faster Through the Cut
docs.text:
Peregrine wants to tow his half-model in real current. The Salt Reach runs straight and strong.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Peregrine Level 38 After Ballast for the Model

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at a straight run of the Salt Reach in The Salt Reach
  2. Bring 6 Sawbill Scale (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,651 EXP
  • 836 mesos
  • +40 standing with Peregrine
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The rock pools are too still. I need current! Real current! The Salt Reach runs straight and fast now the sea gates are broken.
  • Find me a straight run of the Salt Reach to tow it in, and bring 6 Sawbill Scales. I want to fair the model's bottom with them. They're smoother than sandpaper. Probably.
  • Straight and fast. And six scales!
  • Another time, then.
  • Find a straight run on the Salt Reach and bring six sawbill scales.
  • Towed it down the straight run with Kit holding the line. It flew. It FLEW.
  • I'm leaving it on Master Dunstan's bench, under the rag. With a scale on top. So he knows.

docs.title: Clear the Stretch
docs.text:
Perrin rides the World Tree Road to the Tree's foot, and the Ribbon Pigs of the Waystone Meadows keep scattering his horse. Clear 25 of them, then ride on to the Rootlands.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Perrin Level 12 Leads to Courier's Stride

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 25 Ribbon Pig
  • Reach The Rootlands

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 600 EXP
  • 240 mesos
  • Red Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Perrin
Dialogue
  • Player! You have legs, I see. Good. I have a letter for the World Tree and a stretch of road I would rather not gallop through twice.
  • The The Waystone Meadows. The Ribbon Pigs have gone bold, and they run straight under a horse. Mine has opinions about that. So do my blisters.
  • Clear 25 Ribbon Pigs off the The Waystone Meadows, then go on up to The Rootlands and tell me the road is open. Quickly, if you can manage it.
  • Go, go! The meadows are past the The Hedge Lanes, north out of the Tree Gate.
  • Fine. I will take the long way. Again. Not that anyone counts.
  • Twenty-five pigs, then the The Rootlands. The letter is not getting any younger, Player.
  • Done? Already? Hm. You are quicker than you look. Not quicker than me, naturally.
  • The whole stretch, open to the Tree's foot. That is my next letter delivered by noon. Here, take these, and keep your legs warm.

docs.title: Courier's Stride
docs.text:
Perrin, the Royal Courier, will teach his burst of speed to anyone who can run his old test: the palace steps, the great gate and back to him in the plaza.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Perrin Level 20 After Clear the Stretch Leads to The Long Way

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the palace steps in Palace
  2. Reach the great gate in Selsior Gate
  3. Talk to Perrin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,800 EXP
  • Skill: Courier's Stride
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Perrin
Dialogue
  • You cleared my stretch of the road like you had somewhere to be. I like that, Player. Couriers have a trick for the last mile: a burst of speed, short and sharp, saved for when it counts.
  • I teach it the way I learned it. Touch the palace steps, run to the great gate, and come back to me here. No dawdling at the pie stall.
  • Off you go! The palace first, then the gate, then me.
  • Legs tired? Fair. The road will still be long tomorrow.
  • Palace steps, the great gate, then back here. The count is in your tracker.
  • There you are, and barely puffing! You run like a courier already, Player.
  • Come here and I will show you the trick properly.
  • Weight on the front foot, breathe out, and go. Not for long: a burst, then let it rest before the next.
  • That is Courier's Stride. Use it well, and if you ever carry a letter for me, use it twice.

docs.title: The Long Way
docs.text:
Perrin wants the Dark Stumps on the Rootlands thinned so he can ride the short way to the Tree. Then tell his cousin Tilda he took it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Perrin Level 20 After Courier's Stride

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Dark Stump on the Rootlandss (Dark Stump) in The Rootlands
  2. Talk to Tilda

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,000 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +25 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Perrin
Dialogue
  • You kept up with me. Nobody keeps up with me. So you can do me a favour, Player, a courier's favour.
  • Up at the The Rootlands, the Dark Stumps have taken to standing in the road and pretending to be roots. I go round. Everyone thinks I go round because I like the view.
  • Thin 30 Dark Stumps on the The Rootlands, so I can ride the short way. Then go to the gate stand and tell my cousin Tilda that I took it. The short way. She will want to hear it from someone she believes.
  • Thirty stumps, then Tilda. In that order. She checks my boots, you know.
  • Not today? Fine. The long way is very scenic.
  • Thirty Dark Stumps on the The Rootlands, then my cousin at the gate stand. Off you go.
  • She laughed? She always laughs. But she believed you. I can tell, because she has not come round to inspect my boots.
  • The short way to the Tree, Player. I will think of you every time I take it. Briefly. I will be going quite fast.
  • Perrin took the short way through the Rootlands? Did he now. Then why are his boots this muddy? ... Oh, very well. Tell him I believe it. This once.

docs.title: A Courier's Knot
docs.text:
Real couriers tie their bundles in a courier's knot. Bring Peterkin ribbons from the Ribbon Pigs, then show Osbert the knot.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Peterkin Level 11 After As Far as a Courier Rides

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Pig's Ribbon (taken)
  2. Talk to Osbert

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 450 EXP
  • 220 mesos
  • Red Potion x15
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Peterkin
Dialogue
  • Real couriers tie their bundles with ribbon, in a courier's knot, so nobody can open them without it showing. I asked one.
  • Could you get me 10 Pig's Ribbons from the Ribbon Pigs in the The Waystone Meadows? Then show Osbert the knot. If he says yes, I can use it on palace messages!
  • Thank you! I am practising the knot on my bootlaces.
  • Oh. I will use string, then. String is not the same.
  • Ten Pig's Ribbons, then Osbert!
  • It will DO? He said it will do? That is practically praise! Thank you, Player!
  • A courier's knot. On palace messages.
  • Hm. It shows if it is opened. It is neat. It is not regulation. ...Tell the boy it will do.

docs.title: Peterkin as far as a courier rides
As Far as a Courier Rides
docs.text:
Peterkin wants to know how far a royal courier gets before the first bell. Run to the far end of the Hedge Lanes for him, chasing off pigs on the way.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Peterkin Level 6 Leads to A Courier's Knot

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the far end of the Hedge Lanes in The Hedge Lanes
  • Defeat 30 Pig

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • 120 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Peterkin
Dialogue
  • Royal couriers ride the World Tree Road every week! I want to know how far they get by the time the first bell rings.
  • Run out to the far end of the The Hedge Lanes for me, and chase off 30 Pigs on the way; they get under the horses. Then come back and tell me how long it took!
  • Go! Go go go! I am counting!
  • Oh. All right. I will count anyway.
  • The far end of the The Hedge Lanes, and thirty Pigs!
  • That long? A courier on a horse would be twice as fast. Three times! I am going to be so fast one day.

docs.title: Petronella a witness for the history
A Witness for the History
docs.text:
Petronella's secret history needs a witness, not a letter. See the old towpath bend on the Long Reach Banks, deal with the crabs, and tell Melisende what you saw.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Petronella Level 35 After Ink for the Palace Books

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the old towpath bend in The Long Reach Banks
  2. Defeat 40 Bank Lorang
  3. Talk to Melisende

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 16,800 EXP
  • 700 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Petronella
Dialogue
  • May I confide in you? Melisende knows already. I am writing a history. From the letters. Of these years.
  • But a letter says 'monsters on the towpath'. A history must say what they were, how many, and what the bank looked like.
  • Go to the old towpath bend on the The Long Reach Banks, see it with your own eyes, deal with 40 Bank Lorangs and tell Melisende what you saw. She will tell me at supper, and I will set it down exactly.
  • Precision, please. Adjectives are welcome; exaggeration is not.
  • Of course. History is patient. Historians, less so.
  • The towpath bend, forty Bank Lorangs, then Melisende.
  • 'Cartwheel.' A splendid word. Chapter four has its witness, Player. You may find yourself in a footnote.
  • Petronella sent you? Then she has told you. She does not tell many.
  • Crabs as big as cartwheels at the towpath bend, forty of them. I shall tell her word for word. She will want the word 'cartwheel'.

docs.title: Petronella ink for the palace books
Ink for the Palace Books
docs.text:
The ink barge is held up below the Long Reach by 'lizards'. Clear the Reed Beds for the bargemen and ask Benedict for a bottle of his ink in the meantime.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Petronella Level 31 Leads to A Witness for the History

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Reed Ligator in The Reed Beds
  2. Talk to Benedict

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,200 EXP
  • 620 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Petronella
Dialogue
  • A calamity of modest proportions: the ink barge is a fortnight late, held up on the Long Reach by, and I quote, 'lizards'.
  • I have ink for one more week of decrees. The decrees are indifferent to my predicament.
  • Clear the The Reed Beds for the bargemen, 30 Reed Ligators, and meanwhile ask Benedict in the Scholars' Quarter for a bottle of his north-room ink. He will grumble. Permit him.
  • Splendid. Do wipe your hands before you touch the bottle.
  • Then I shall write very small.
  • The The Reed Beds, thirty Reed Ligators, then Benedict.
  • The 'g' leaned. It did. He is insufferable and correct. Thank you, Player; the decrees shall go out on time.
  • Petronella needs ink? Petronella has never run out of anything in her life.
  • Here. And tell her the 'g' on her last page leaned. Only slightly. She will know which one.

docs.title: One More Round
docs.text:
Pim wants a sparring partner after drill. He thinks watching someone fight for real would help more: clear 25 monsters of the Hedge Lanes while he takes notes.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Pim Level 5 Leads to Too Early for Patrol

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 25 Hedge Lanes monsters (Slime, Pig, Orange Mushroom) in The Hedge Lanes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 120 EXP
  • 100 mesos
  • Red Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Pim
Dialogue
  • Recruit Pim, reporting! Player, could I ask a favour? Sergeant Bertrand says I learn more by watching than by swinging. He said it very loudly.
  • Would you go out to the The Hedge Lanes and fight 25 of the slimes, pigs and mushrooms? I'll watch from the hedge and take notes! I have a pencil and everything.
  • Hooray! Er. I mean: understood!
  • That's all right! I'll ask again tomorrow. And the day after.
  • Twenty-five from the Hedge Lanes! I'm watching! From the hedge!
  • I wrote down everything! You step in before you strike. Every time! Nobody told me that. Well, Tobe did. But you showed me.
  • One hole closed tonight, Captain! Thank you, Player!

docs.title: Too Early for Patrol
docs.text:
Pim volunteered for a meadow patrol nobody wanted, and Bertrand said no. Clear 30 monsters on the Waystone Meadows in his place, then tell Bertrand the road is clean.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Pim Level 10 After One More Round

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 monsters in The Waystone Meadows
  2. Talk to Bertrand

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 500 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Pim
Dialogue
  • I volunteered for the meadow patrol! Nobody else wanted it. Sergeant Bertrand said NO so loudly the horses complained.
  • He's right, I know he's right. But the shepherd up at the waystones really does need it done.
  • Could you clear 30 monsters on the The Waystone Meadows for me? Then tell Sergeant Bertrand the road's clean. Maybe he'll see I volunteer for good reasons.
  • Thank you! I'll do extra drills while you're gone. Double extra.
  • Oh. All right. I'll just volunteer again tomorrow, then.
  • Thirty on the meadows, then tell the Sergeant!
  • He said I'm not ready for patrol. But he said it quietly! He never says anything quietly! That means something, doesn't it?
  • Pim sent you, did he? HA! That boy volunteers for everything. The meadows are clear? ...Good. Tell him he's still not going. Tell him I'm proud he asked. Tell him QUIETLY.

docs.title: A New Comedy
docs.text:
Pip is writing a new comedy she will show nobody, and she needs something only Ozzie Lantry has, or rather does not have: the story of Juna's first winter.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Pip Marrow Level 45 After The Third Play

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ozzie Lantry

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,590 EXP
  • 2,700 mesos
  • +60 standing with Pip Marrow
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I am writing something new. No, you cannot see it. No, I will not tell you the title. The notebook stays in my coat and the coat stays on me.
  • But I need something from Ozzie. Or something Ozzie does not have, which is the strange part. He told me once that nobody has a word written about the city's first winter. Not a letter, not a song. A hundred years of stories and a hole in the middle.
  • Ask Ozzie Lantry about that winter. About Juna, in that winter. Whatever he knows, and whatever he does not. Especially what he does not.
  • He will wander off into some other story. Let him. The good parts are always three stories in.
  • Fine. I will invent it all. That is what writers do. It is also what liars do. Ask Hambone.
  • Ask Ozzie Lantry about Juna's first winter, Player. The hole in the middle.
  • Juna's first winter? Ah. Ah, now. Nobody has that, I am afraid. I have looked for eighteen years. The Table's books begin in the spring after. Before that, nothing. Too cold to write, perhaps. Or burned for warmth. Or hidden.
  • We know she was here, and we know she stayed, and we know the play was on its cart again by summer. Everything between is snow. Tell Pip: if she ever finds a single line, she must show me first. I will cry, probably. I will find my spectacles first.
  • Nothing. A whole winter of nothing, and Juna somewhere inside it, keeping warm and staying.
  • Do you know what you can do with nothing, Player? Anything. Do not look at me like that, I said nothing about the title. Go on. Go away. I have to write.

docs.title: The Third Play
docs.text:
Pip Marrow has a finished play in a drawer that she thinks is only good. Ask Dina, in general and without saying whose it is, whether a play that is only good belongs on a cart.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Pip Marrow Level 27 Leads to A New Comedy

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Dina Finch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,680 EXP
  • 1,620 mesos
  • +50 standing with Pip Marrow
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • If you are about to say 'Ah, a Marrow', please do not. Everybody says it. I am Pip. Just Pip.
  • I have written three plays. Burned two. The third is in a drawer, finished. It is not bad. That is the problem. It is not bad, and Juna's was brilliant, and nobody remembers the not-bad ones.
  • Ask Dina Finch, for me. Not about my play. Just, in general: whether a play that is only good should ever go on a cart. Do not say it is mine. She will know anyway, but do not say it.
  • And if she gives a note, do not write it down. If I see it written down I will have to burn it, and I am running out of drawers.
  • Wise. Very wise. Nobody should get between a writer and her drawer.
  • Ask Dina Finch about plays that are only good, Player. In general. Very general.
  • In general? A play that is only good. (Dina looks at you for a long, theatrical moment.) Tell Pip that Juna's play was only good too, the first time. It was the crowd that made it great. The crowd, a cart, and a guild that hauled it away.
  • And tell Pip that when it is ready, she will not have to ask. She will take it out of the drawer and hand it to me herself. Until then it is safe where it is.
  • She knew it was mine. Of course she did. She knew before you opened your mouth.
  • Only good, the first time... Fine. It stays in the drawer. But I will stop thinking of the drawer as a grave and start thinking of it as a wing. A very small backstage wing. Thanks, Player.

docs.title: Play with Saffi
docs.text:
Saffi has heard the whistle parts Piper wrote for her street tunes, and now Piper cannot go near Lantern Square. Ask Saffi whether Piper may play with her, once.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Piper Level 40 After The Walker Songs, The Thin Whistler

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Saffi

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,350 EXP
  • 2,400 mesos
  • +60 standing with Piper
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • She heard them. Saffi heard the second parts, the whistle parts I wrote for all nine of her street tunes. Now she knows that the thin person with the tin whistle who never plays it is me.
  • I have carried them round for months. I know every one by heart. But now she knows, and I cannot go near Lantern Square without my hands going cold.
  • Would you ask Saffi... whether she would mind... if I played with her. Once. Just the Night Market tune. If she says no, do not tell me how she said it.
  • She is usually on the iron knee of Ferro's fiddler. If she is playing fast, wait. If she is playing very fast, wait longer.
  • No, you are right. Better she never sees how cold my hands get.
  • Ask Saffi in Lantern Square whether Piper may play with her, Player.
  • Piper? The whistle? FINALLY. (Saffi laughs before anybody else can.) I have played the Night Market tune nineteen times this week waiting for that whistle to come in.
  • Tell Piper: tonight, when Drum starts. And tell Piper I play it fast. I mean fast. If the whistle keeps up, it stays.
  • Tonight? When Drum starts? Fast? (Piper takes out the tin whistle, looks at it as if it might run away, and holds it up, ready.)
  • I can keep up. I wrote the parts keeping up; I have been playing them at her speed in my head for a year. Thank you, Player. If I faint, catch the whistle first.

docs.title: The Walker Songs
docs.text:
Piper keeps the Walker songs Ozzie Lantry once sang, all but the third verse of the fiddler's song. Ask Ozzie for it.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Piper Level 33 Leads to Play with Saffi

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ozzie Lantry

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,030 EXP
  • 1,980 mesos
  • +50 standing with Piper
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Oh, hello, sorry, I was humming. I am always humming. This one is new; I fell in love with it on the way here from the Night Market. It will be gone by Thursday.
  • Ozzie sang me the Walker songs his grandfather taught him, years ago. I have them all written out, tied up with a ribbon. All but one verse: the fiddler's song, the third verse. Ozzie got to it, started crying, and told a story about a goat instead.
  • Would you ask Ozzie Lantry for the third verse? I cannot ask again. Last time he cried, and I cried, and then the goat story was so long that we both missed supper.
  • If he starts on the goat, just nod. It ends eventually. I think.
  • That is all right. Some songs are better with a hole in them. The hole hums.
  • The third verse of the fiddler's song, from Ozzie Lantry, Player.
  • The third verse? Oh. Oh, dear. Yes. My grandfather always sang that one last. Selsior's theatres had turned his songs away, you see, so he played them on the road out instead.
  • Write this down, I cannot say it twice: 'They would not let us play inside, so we played it on the way.' That is the whole verse. One line, sung three times, slower each time. Tell Piper not to change it.
  • 'They would not let us play inside, so we played it on the way.' (Piper hums it, then hums it again, slower.)
  • Oh, that is going in the play. Unchanged. Not one note. Well, maybe one, on the third time round. No. Not one. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Drawing the Old Cut
docs.text:
Poppy wants to draw the Old Cut as a chart, the way Ambrose would. She asks you to look at two places she cannot reach.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Poppy Level 21 Leads to Drawing the Outer Cut

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Look at the first lock's gates in The First Locks
  • Look at the timber ponds from the high bank in The Timber Ponds

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,202 EXP
  • 462 mesos
  • +40 standing with Poppy
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Mr Ambrose says a chart is only as good as the person who looked. I want to draw the Old Cut, from above, like a gull. But I'm not allowed up it.
  • Could you look for me? At the first lock's gates in the First Locks, and at the Timber Ponds from the high bank. Tell me how many gates, which way the water goes, where the logs are.
  • I'll draw it very small, so it fits. Like Mr Ambrose.
  • Count the gates! And look which way the water goes.
  • Another time, then.
  • Look at the first lock's gates, and at the Timber Ponds from the high bank.
  • Two gates at the first lock, the water going down towards the town, and the logs all in a raft on the far pond. Got it.
  • There. It's not very good yet. But it's true. Mr Ambrose says true comes first.

docs.title: Drawing the Outer Cut
docs.text:
Poppy's chart of the Old Cut stops at the Pinch. She asks you to look at the sea half for her.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Poppy Level 35 After Drawing the Old Cut Leads to The New Marks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the Salt Reach's middle bank in The Salt Reach
  2. Look at the broken sea gates in The Gullet

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,920 EXP
  • 770 mesos
  • +40 standing with Poppy
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • My chart of the Old Cut stops at the Pinch. Mr Ambrose says a chart that stops in the middle is a promise you didn't keep.
  • Could you look at the Salt Reach's middle bank and at the broken sea gates in the Gullet? Tell me how wide, which way the water runs, and what's broken.
  • Which way the water runs! That's the important bit.
  • Another time, then.
  • Look at the Salt Reach's middle bank and the broken sea gates in the Gullet.
  • The water runs in at the gates and out at the Pinch, and the gates hang off their hinges on the sea side. Got it.
  • Now the chart goes all the way to the sea. Mr Ambrose says I can show it to him. He's never asked to see one before.

docs.title: The New Marks
docs.text:
Poppy has drawn every new mark Ambrose put on the chart as you reported them. She wants him to see her copy.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Poppy Level 64 After Drawing the Outer Cut, Checking the Marks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ambrose

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 59,378 EXP
  • 1,408 mesos
  • +40 standing with Poppy
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • I drew every new mark while you told Mr Ambrose about the light. On my own copy. Very small.
  • Could you show him? He's never asked to see my work. He's always busy. Show Mr Ambrose.
  • Very small. Like he showed me.
  • Another time, then.
  • Show Poppy's copy of the new marks to Ambrose.
  • He said 'better than mine at your age'? Mr Ambrose said that?
  • I'm going to be a chartmaker. I haven't told Mum yet. I'll tell her now. No. Tomorrow.
  • Poppy's copy? Let me see. The marks, the sea-hole, the Rim... the bearings are right. The lettering is better than mine.
  • Tell her: better than mine at her age. Tell her exactly that.

docs.title: Forty Lights
docs.text:
Prism wants to paint the Long Walk in lights over Lantern Square on Walkout Day, but forty lights are the most Prism has ever held, and the square's lanterns drown them out. Ask Lux whether the lanterns can be dimmed for the show.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Prism Level 24 Leads to The Long Walk in Lights

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Lux

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,190 EXP
  • 1,440 mesos
  • +40 standing with Prism
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Oh, hello, hello! Where have you come from? Was it far? Did you see anything shining? Look, look, watch this: a heron! Isn't it? It only lasts a few breaths. That is the trouble.
  • For Walkout Day I want to paint the whole Long Walk over Lantern Square: the line of people with their bundles, the cart, the first lanterns going up. Hundreds of lights. I have managed forty, once, for about as long as it takes to sneeze, and then I had to sit down.
  • And even forty is nothing against the square's lanterns. They are so bright! Which is lovely. But my lights vanish in them like fireflies in the sun.
  • Would you ask Lux if the square's lanterns could be dimmed, just for the show? Lux keeps them. I am a little afraid to ask; Lux loves them so much. Will you? Will you really?
  • Thank you! Lux is in Lantern Square, or up a tower. Ask what Lux thinks. Ask about the amber ones too. No, just the dimming. No, both!
  • Oh, that is all right! I will practise more. Forty-one. Forty-two. One day.
  • Did you ask Lux? About dimming the lanterns? What did Lux say? Oh, you have not gone yet. That is all right!
  • Prism sent you. Of course. Prism asks me more questions in an evening than I answer in a year, and somehow saved this one for someone else.
  • Dim the square's lanterns? For the length of a light show, on Walkout Day, once the play is done? Yes. I will do it from the first tower; there is a shutter on each one, and I know which to close.
  • Tell Prism I promised. And tell Prism the lanterns will not mind. They have been bright for a hundred years. They can spare a few breaths for something lovely.
  • Lux said yes? Lux PROMISED? Oh! Oh, I have to sit down. Not because of the lights. Because of the yes.
  • Now there is no excuse. Now it is only me and the size of it. Hundreds of lights. I can do forty. That is... a lot of practising. Good! Good. Where do I start?
  • Thank you, thank you! Here, a little heron, just for you. Watch it go. There. It was yours.

docs.title: Prism the long walk in lights
The Long Walk in Lights
docs.text:
Prism cannot hold hundreds of lights alone, but lights can rest on something: a frame of woven reeds, the way the forest weavers hang lanterns on the branch-bridges. Bring Prism 20 Reed Bundles from the Reedwater Bottoms.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Prism Level 44 After Forty Lights

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Reed Bundle (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 39,570 EXP
  • 3,910 mesos
  • +60 standing with Prism
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I have been thinking. Mostly at night. Do you know what my family does, back in the forest? Baskets! And the branch-bridges at home have little frames woven along them for the lanterns to sit in.
  • What if my lights did not have to float on nothing? What if each one had somewhere to rest, a thread of a frame across the whole square, too thin to see in the dark? Then I would only have to light them, not hold them up. I tried it with string. String burns. Reeds do not!
  • Could you bring me 20 Reed Bundles? The good long ones grow in the Reedwater Bottoms, where the Reed-Lurkers are. The lurkers sit on them, I am told. Rudely.
  • Thank you! I will start weaving the corners now, with what I have. My grandmother would laugh to see me. Baskets after all!
  • That is all right! The Bottoms are a long way. I will keep practising with string. And buckets of water.
  • Twenty Reed Bundles from the Reedwater Bottoms. You carry (how many you carry). The long straight ones are best!
  • Look at them! So long, so straight. I can split these into threads as fine as hair. Watch: one light, resting on one reed. It is not tired. I am not tired!
  • Forty became a hundred and twelve last night, with the frame in the corners only. Lux came down from the tower to look and said nothing for a long time. Lux says nothing when something is good.
  • On Walkout Day, after the play, stand in the middle of the square and look up. That is all. Just look up. Thank you, Player!

docs.title: Grit for the Furnace
docs.text:
Prudence's furnace lining cracked in the last experiment. Golem rubble is the only grit that holds that heat.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Prudence Level 52 Leads to Powdered Golem Stone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Quarry Rubble (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 29,940 EXP
  • 1,040 mesos
  • White Potion x5
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Prudence
Dialogue
  • My furnace lining cracked. Not an explosion. A controlled event that exceeded the lining.
  • Ordinary sand melts. The rubble the golems shed holds its shape in my fire. I tested it. Twice.
  • Bring me 25 Quarry Rubble from the Rubble Golems of The Spoil Heaps. Stay behind the chalk line when you hand it over.
  • Exact, please. Twenty-five is not "about twenty".
  • Then I will brew in a cracked furnace, and the neighbours will write a third letter.
  • Twenty-five Quarry Rubble. Not near enough to twenty-five. Twenty-five.
  • Twenty-five. Counted. Good.
  • The neighbours will be relieved to know the furnace is safer. I will tell them. At length.

docs.title: Powdered Golem Stone
docs.text:
Prudence needs a reagent found only where monsters have moved in: powdered golem stone, for the potion that heals in a moment.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Prudence Level 60 After Grit for the Furnace, A Golem Core Leads to Ore for a First Sword, The Jar That Glows

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Quarry Stone (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 111,620 EXP
  • 1,800 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Prudence
Dialogue
  • The moment potion. Three years. And the one thing every old account of it agrees on is a stone ground fine that had stood up and walked.
  • That may be a story. I am not paid to believe stories. I am paid to test them.
  • Bring me 30 Quarry Stones from the Quarry Golems of The Terraced Cuts. I will grind them myself.
  • Wrap them dry. Wet stone grinds wrong.
  • Then I wait. I have waited three years. I can do arithmetic.
  • Thirty Quarry Stones from The Terraced Cuts. Dry.
  • Thirty. Dry. You listen; I like that.
  • If this does nothing, it has told me something. If it does something, Mirel will have to buy it from me. Either way, thank you.

docs.title: The Jar That Glows
docs.text:
One jar of Prudence's powdered golem stone has started to glow on its own. She wants darker stone to compare, and her rival Mirel to see it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Prudence Level 64 After Powdered Golem Stone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Dark Quarry Stone (taken)
  2. Talk to Mirel

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 39,830 EXP
  • 1,280 mesos
  • Scroll for Shield for DEF 60% x1
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Prudence
Dialogue
  • That jar. The third one on the left. It started glowing on Tuesday. Nobody touched it. I checked; I would have touched it.
  • I need the darker stone from deeper down, to see if it does the same. And I want a witness. A hostile one.
  • Bring 10 Dark Quarry Stones from The Deep Cut, then show the jar to Mirel in the Crown Market. If he admits it glows, it glows.
  • Do not let him keep it. Do not let him sell it.
  • Then it will go on glowing without a witness. I shall write everything down.
  • Ten Dark Quarry Stones, then Mirel. Bring the jar back.
  • He admitted it glows. Mirel. Admitted something. Write down the date.
  • I do not know why it glows, Player. Nobody does. But it is in a jar with my label on it, and that is a start.
  • She sent you with a jar? Let me... oh. That is glowing. That is certainly glowing.
  • Tell her I said so. Tell her it is not near enough to anything I know. She'll enjoy that more than she should.

docs.title: Quietly, for Dottie
docs.text:
Winnie knows Dottie's lamb Button is missing, though Dottie has told no one. Follow the large, round, damp tracks from the bramble at the woods' edge into Windflower Glade, defeat 40 Windflower Caps and find a tuft of speckled wool. Dottie must not learn Winnie sent you.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Winnie Level 34 After Shiny Things Leads to Roots from Below

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach Windflower Glade
  2. Defeat 40 Windflower Cap
  3. Deliver 1 Tuft of Speckled Wool

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 22,000 EXP
  • 4,500 mesos
  • Elixir x2
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Come in, Player, and shut the door, would you? This is not for the lane. I walked up to the hill pasture with buns for Dottie. I counted the lambs while she ate. Eight. There should be nine.
  • It is Button, the speckled one with the bent ear. She promised me his first clip. She has not said a word to anyone, poor thing, and every evening she walks toward the woods and comes back with nothing.
  • I walked up twice more and watched her from the hill. She goes as far as a bramble at the woods' edge, where the pasture ends, and stands there, and turns back. If there is anything to find, it starts at that bramble.
  • Go and look for me. Start at the bramble, and if there is a trail, follow it into the woods, into Windflower Glade if that is where they go. Clear the Windflower Caps out of the way, 40 of them, and bring me anything of his you find. And Player: Dottie must not know I sent you. She will tell when she is ready.
  • Look at the ground by the bramble first. If something went in, it left a mark. And not a word to Dottie.
  • No, of course. It is a lot to ask. Forget I said anything, would you? Especially to Dottie.
  • From the bramble at the woods' edge into Windflower Glade, Player. 40 Windflower Caps, and anything of Button's. Quietly.
  • Oh. Oh, that is his wool. Speckled, see, and that little kink in it. I would know it anywhere. I have been saving a peg for it.
  • So he went in on his own four legs, and something with big round feet went in beside him. And the wool was clean. Not torn. He was walking, Player, not dragged.
  • That is more than I hoped. I will keep this tuft safe until Dottie has her lamb back. Here, take this, and thank you. And remember, not a word.

docs.title: Reading Slowly
docs.text:
Every Walkout Day Quint reads the Open Charter before the play, and every year Dina Finch says he reads too slowly. Ask Dina how she times the cart's first entrance to his reading, and bring her answer back to Quint.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Quint Level 22 Leads to The Cedar Case

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Dina Finch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 920 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • +50 standing with Quint
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Thirteen years I have opened Dina Finch's play by reading the Charter, and thirteen years she has told me I read too slowly. I do. On purpose. A ruling that let a whole city exist should not be gabbled like a grocery list.
  • But I have never asked her how she does it: the cart comes round the corner the very moment I roll the scroll shut, every year, to the breath. I would ask her myself, but she would give me a note on my posture.
  • Go to the The Old Barracks Yard and ask Dina Finch how she times her first entrance to my reading. Do not tell her I asked. She will know anyway, but do not tell her.
  • The Old Barracks Yard. She will be the one directing, or eating breakfast and directing. It is the same voice.
  • Quite right. Some mysteries keep a festival going. I shall go on reading slowly and wondering.
  • Dina, at the Old Barracks Yard. How does she time the cart to my last word? I have a theory involving a small boy and a mirror.
  • Quint sent you. No, do not deny it, you have the look of a person carrying a question for an old man. How do I time it? Darling, I do not time it to the words. Nobody could. He changes his pace every year.
  • I time it to the crowd. When Quint starts, the square goes quiet. Halfway through, it goes quieter. And just before the end there is a moment when nobody in the whole square breathes. That is my cue. The cart moves on the silence, not the scroll.
  • Tell him he still reads too slowly. Tell him that if he ever reads faster, I shall have him replaced by Bastian. That should hold him another thirteen years.
  • On the silence. Not the scroll. Well. Well, well. I have spent thirteen years trying to read so that the cart would be on time, and it was the crowd keeping time all along.
  • That is the Charter, you know, in a nutshell. Nobody keeps it alone. The whole square holds its breath together, and then the play begins.
  • And she threatened me with Bastian? Ha! I shall read slower. Thank you, Player. Come and stand at the front this Walkout Day.

docs.title: The Cedar Case
docs.text:
The lining of the cedar case that keeps the hall's copy of the Open Charter is cracking, and damp is the scroll's worst enemy. Quint wants dry, springy moss-bark from the barkbacks of the Bristlewood to reline it.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Quint Level 36 After Reading Slowly

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Mossy Bark (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 24,440 EXP
  • 3,600 mesos
  • +70 standing with Quint
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Every morning I dust the case. Every week I check the scroll for damp. And this week, for the first time in twenty-six years, I found a crack in the case's lining, the length of my little finger.
  • Do not laugh. Well, laugh a little, I am an old bookbinder fussing over a crack. But a crack lets in damp, and damp lets in mould, and mould does not care what a ruling meant to anyone. The old binders lined their best cases with moss-bark: it drinks the damp and gives it back slowly.
  • The Barkbacks of the Bristlewood carry the best of it, thick and springy. Bring me 20 Mossy Bark and I will reline the case myself. Nobody else touches it. Not even you, I am afraid, though you may watch.
  • The barkbacks root along Bristlewood Edge and in The Silent Cutting. Pick the pieces with the moss still on; the moss is the point.
  • I will put a cloth over the crack and check it twice a day instead of once. It will make me insufferable. More insufferable.
  • You carry (how many you carry) of 20 Mossy Bark. The crack has not grown. I measure it with a thread every morning.
  • Oh, that is good bark. Smell it: green and dry together. Mercy Oakes would have approved, and she approved of almost nothing, including me.
  • The scroll will sleep dry for another hundred years, if I have anything to say about it, and while I am alive I do. Thank you, Player. That was a Charter's worth of help.

docs.title: The Empty Box
docs.text:
Rafe's Balrog puppet is gone from its box. Teeth marks on the lid. The rats of the drains have been coming up into the Row's cellars.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Rafe Level 22 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to The Fox's Letter

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 25 Drain Rat in The Old Drains
  • Bring 1 Rafe's Balrog Puppet (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,520 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Rafe
Dialogue
  • Fox says: the Balrog is gone! Out of its box! In the night!
  • (Rafe, quietly, showing the lid.) Teeth. Small ones. The rats come up from the drains now, under the Row.
  • Fox says: go into The Old Drains, see off 25 Drain Rats, and bring back the Rafe's Balrog Puppet! Rafe will hold the door.
  • Fox says: be careful! It is very frightening. It's only cat-sized, but still.
  • Fox says: oh. Well. The children will be relieved. Rafe will not.
  • Fox says: the Balrog! In the drains! Bring it back!
  • (Rafe takes the puppet in both hands, and smooths its hinge.) ...Thank you.
  • Fox says: back in the box it goes! And the children will scream at the end, and then laugh. That's how it should be.

docs.title: The Fox's Letter
docs.text:
Rafe has written something he cannot say aloud to his old pupil Lambert. He has written it in the voice of the fox.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Rafe Level 25 After The Empty Box

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Lambert

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,690 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Rafe
Dialogue
  • (Rafe holds out a folded paper. The fox nods at it.) Fox says: a letter. For Lambert. From me. Not from Rafe. Rafe could never.
  • Fox says: it's about the first apple. And about the lesson. And about how proud... no, that's in the letter.
  • Fox says: take it to Lambert in the plaza. Don't read it! Well. Don't read it aloud.
  • Fox says: thank you! (Rafe looks at his shoes, very pleased.)
  • Fox says: oh. Another day. Rafe will keep it on the nail with me.
  • Fox says: Lambert, in the plaza. The letter.
  • (Rafe listens to what Lambert said, and does not speak for a long moment.)
  • Fox says: he said that? About Rafe? (The fox covers its eyes with a paw. Rafe is smiling.)
  • A letter from Rafe's fox? He never... he's never said a word about it. Twelve years.
  • Tell the fox I said thank you. Tell Rafe every trick I have is his. And tell him the apples are early this year.

docs.title: The Cost of Guards
docs.text:
Prices from the far towns are up, and Reynold has checked: it is not greed but the cost of guards on the roads. The wool and honey carts from the downs pass Downs Edge. Clear it.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Reynold Level 21 Leads to The Honey Cart

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Monster on Downs Edges in Downs Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,600 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Reynold
Dialogue
  • Quickly, please, Player. I have been through the ledger three times. Prices from the downs are up a fifth. I checked every scale twice, and every stall is honest.
  • It is the guards. The carters pay guards to cross Downs Edge, and the guards cost money, and the money comes out of my market. I cannot fine a bee.
  • Clear 40 of whatever is on Downs Edge: bees, boars, I do not mind which. Fewer guards, fairer prices.
  • Good. Fair weight for fair work.
  • Then the carters keep paying and the market keeps paying. I shall write it in the ledger.
  • Forty on Downs Edge. Any kind.
  • The carters came in this morning without a guard between them. I watched the prices. Down a tenth already.
  • Here, Player. Weighed and counted. I checked it.

docs.title: The Honey Cart
docs.text:
The honey cart from the downs is stuck behind boars rooting up the Thyme Banks road. Clear them, then have Wat tell the stalls the honey is coming.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Reynold Level 24 After The Cost of Guards Leads to Wat Is Late

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Downs Boar on the Thyme Bankss (Downs Boar) in The Thyme Banks
  2. Talk to Wat

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,500 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +25 standing with Selsior
  • +110 standing with Reynold
Dialogue
  • Three stalls are short of honey and four are quarrelling about it. The honey cart from the downs has not come in two days.
  • The carter sent word: the Downs Boars have rooted up the road across the The Thyme Banks and stand in it.
  • Clear 30 Downs Boars on the The Thyme Banks. Then find Wat and have him tell the stalls the cart is coming, before they come to me.
  • Thank you. Wat will be somewhere he should not be, quickly.
  • Then I shall settle four quarrels about honey. Again.
  • Thirty boars on the The Thyme Banks, then Wat.
  • The honey cart is in, the stalls have stopped quarrelling, and Wat told all of them before I reached the first. Good.
  • Here, Player. And thank you. I have not had a quiet morning in a week.
  • Honey cart's coming? Right! Every stall in the market, before the warden gets to the first one. Watch me. ... Gone already, see? I took the courtyard with two doors.

docs.title: Wat Is Late
docs.text:
Wat has not come back from an errand, and Reynold is worried. Find Wat, then help with what kept him: Chalk Hive bees swarming the sheepfold road.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Reynold Level 27 After The Honey Cart

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Wat
  2. Defeat 30 Chalk Hive Bee

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,000 EXP
  • 540 mesos
  • Orange Potion x20
  • Scroll for Shield for DEF 60% x1
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +140 standing with Reynold
Dialogue
  • Player. Wat went to the far end of the market at noon with a message. It takes him four minutes. I have timed him. It has been two hours.
  • It is probably nothing. He is probably showing a carter a shortcut. I would like you to find him anyway.
  • Find Wat and see what kept him. Then whatever it is, help with it.
  • Thank you. ... It is probably nothing.
  • No, quite right. He will turn up. He always does. I shall check the weights.
  • Find Wat. Then deal with whatever kept him.
  • Bees. Swarming the sheepfold road, and the carters afraid to move, and the boy ran out to tell them where the shortcut is. Of course he did.
  • He is honest, Player. He is also eleven. ... Thank you for finding him. Here. I checked it twice.
  • Is the warden cross? He's not cross. He's worried, that's worse. ... The honey carters are stuck at the edge of the downs. The Chalk Hive Bees are swarming the sheepfold road. I ran out to show them the way round.
  • There's thirty bees if there's one. Out by the The Chalk Hives. You do that, and I'll tell the warden I'm all right. Before he hears it from anyone else.

docs.title: Good Rope
docs.text:
Good rope from outside is getting scarce, and Rivet's lift runs on rope. Twisted adder skin makes a strong cord: bring Rivet 25 Adder Skins.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Rivet Level 21 Leads to The Well Winch

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Adder Skin (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,600 EXP
  • 2,330 mesos
  • +50 standing with Rivet
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • After last winter's jam I replaced the whole counterweight line. Good hemp, from the carts. Now the carts don't come and the rope-makers are sending me rope I wouldn't hang washing on.
  • Old trick from the porters: twist dried adder skin in with the hemp. Supple, doesn't rot, doesn't stretch. Only problem is the adders want to keep their skins.
  • 25 Adder Skins. The Verge Adders in the Gate Meadows, right outside the gate. Easy. Well. Easy for someone with a sword.
  • Whole skins. No holes. I'll know.
  • Fine. I'll keep checking the line twice a day. Three times. Fine.
  • (how many you carry) of 25 Adder Skins. Verge adders, Gate Meadows.
  • Good skins. Supple. (Rivet twists two together with the hemp, hauls on it, then hangs off it with both hands.) Doesn't give. That's a line.
  • That'll hold the platform and two porters and Scrap, who thinks I don't know. Thanks, Player. Good work. That's high praise. Don't spend it all at once.

docs.title: The Well Winch
docs.text:
Leland's old well shaft drops straight into Low Grad, and Rivet wants to rig a rope winch down it. Bring 15 more Adder Skins for the line, and ask Leland where the shaft can take the bolts.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Rivet Level 23 After Good Rope, The Undercroft

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 15 Adder Skin (taken)
  2. Talk to Leland

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,210 EXP
  • 2,910 mesos
  • +60 standing with Rivet
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Heard you've been down under the Great Hall. Ropes everywhere, they say, and Leland lowering people on them by hand like buckets. That's fine for one trip. It's daft for a hundred.
  • Leland's got an old well shaft he dug years back that broke into the Undercroft, and now the Table's had the cap taken off, it drops straight down there. Put a winch at the top, a counterweight, a proper line. Second lift. Sort of. Goes the wrong way. Still counts.
  • I need 15 more Adder Skins for the line, and I need Leland to tell me where the shaft's stone will take bolts. Leland knows that shaft better than his own hands.
  • Adders, Gate Meadows. Leland, by the iron door in the Great Hall. Ask about the top of the shaft, and the first ledge down.
  • Fine. They can keep going down on Leland's arms. Leland's arms are old.
  • (how many you carry) of 15 Adder Skins, and ask Leland where the old well shaft will take bolts.
  • A winch, down my old shaft? Ha. I dug that shaft forty years ago looking for water, and my pick went straight through a vaulted roof into black air. The Table had it capped the same week and told me to forget it. Now the cap is off, and it is a second way down, if someone rigs a rope and a winch worth trusting.
  • Tell Rivet: the top course is soft brick, no good. Three arm-lengths down there is a ring of fortress stone. That will take any bolt you like. And the first ledge is a long way down, so tell Rivet to make the line long and the jokes short.
  • Fortress stone three arm-lengths down. Perfect. Same stone as my counterweight. It likes being useful.
  • (It takes Rivet two days, Leland's chalk marks and a great deal of muttering. Then a winch stands over the old well shaft, an adder-skin line running down into the dark, and a little platform that sinks slow on its own.)
  • Works. Of course it works. Thanks, Player. If the Table ever lets me talk, I'm telling them about this one first.

docs.title: A Present for Mum
docs.text:
Robin wants to give his mother something for her nets: the banks cleared of the claws that cut them, so she can fish deeper again. He asks you to tell her it was his idea.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Robin Level 34 After Low Water Finds Leads to Grandad's Nods

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Bank Lorang in The Long Reach Banks
  2. Talk to Agatha

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,330 EXP
  • 680 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Robin
Dialogue
  • Mum's nets keep coming up cut. She mends them every night, and she pretends she's not tired. I want to give her a present.
  • Clear 30 Bank Lorangs on the The Long Reach Banks, they're the ones with the claws. Then tell Agatha it's a present. From me. You did the fighting, but it was my idea!
  • Thank you! Don't tell her before it's done, it's a surprise!
  • All right. I'll think of another present. A shiny one.
  • Thirty lorangs on the Long Reach Banks, then tell Mum it's from me.
  • Mum laughed so loud they heard it on the far bank. Then she hugged me so hard I got mud in my ear.
  • Best present ever. Here, this is for you. I found it. It's not a crown, but it's close.
  • A present? From Robin? (She laughs, loud enough to carry across the river.)
  • That boy. Tell him it's the best present I ever had. And tell him he's still not going to the deep end.

docs.title: Grandad's Nods
docs.text:
Robin knows every one of Osmund's nods but one: the nod he gave the badge. Robin wants the clangs cleared off the far bank where Osmund ties up, and asks you to ask his grandfather what else that nod meant.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Robin Level 38 After A Present for Mum

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Bank Clang in The Long Reach Banks
  2. Talk to Osmund

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,670 EXP
  • 760 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Robin
Dialogue
  • I know all Grandad's nods. Get in. Sit down. You're welcome. Mind the edge. All of them. Except one.
  • When I showed him the badge he nodded and I said it meant put it somewhere safe. But maybe it meant more. Clear 40 Bank Clangs off the far bank where he ties up, and then ask Osmund. He might tell you. He likes you.
  • Thank you! Watch his eyebrows. That's where the real answer is.
  • That's all right. I'll ask him myself. One day.
  • Forty clangs on the Long Reach Banks, then ask Grandad about the nod.
  • He said 'Safe. That's all.' And he winked? Grandad never winks!
  • Then it's still a secret. Good. I like it better that way. Here, for being brave enough to ask him.
  • (You ask about the badge. Osmund looks at the river for a long time.)
  • Safe. That's all. (And then, for the first time you have seen, he winks.)

docs.title: Low Water Finds
docs.text:
The ligators of the Reed Beds churn the mud, and the mud gives things up. Robin wants the reed beds cleared so he can hunt at low water there, and his best find shown to Jasper.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Robin Level 31 After A Night Without Lanterns Leads to A Present for Mum

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Reed Ligator in The Reed Beds
  2. Talk to Jasper

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,060 EXP
  • 620 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Robin
Dialogue
  • Psst. The The Reed Beds! When the ligators thrash about, the mud turns over, and things come up. Old things! I saw a buckle shine from the bank. I'm not allowed that far.
  • Clear 30 Reed Ligators so the bank's safe, and take this buckle I found to Jasper in the Crown Market. He'll tell you its story. Then come and tell me!
  • Go on! Look for anything shiny on the way. Shiny is good.
  • Aw. Mum would say no anyway.
  • Thirty ligators in the Reed Beds, then show the buckle to Jasper.
  • Jasper said it's from a harness, from the old king's reign, and he'll give me four coppers! Four!
  • That's practically a crown. Here, you get some too. Finders share. That's the rule. It's my rule.
  • Robin's buckle! Let me see. Brass, a little silver, a harness from the old king's reign. Lovely. Four coppers, tell him, and a story with it.
  • And tell him the offer on his badge still stands. He'll say no. He always says no. Good lad.

docs.title: The Cart-Sized Boar
docs.text:
Roland's old story of a boar the size of a cart happened on the downs. He wants to know if the place is still there, and if the boars there still grow that big: bring him a tusk or five.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Roland Level 24 Leads to The Dew Pond

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 1 Elite Downs Boar
  • Bring 5 Boar Tusk (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,290 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Roland
Dialogue
  • Sit. You've heard the boar story? The size of a cart, that boar. The size of a house, by the end of the evening. Ha!
  • It was out on the downs, past the Thyme Banks. Go and see if they still grow them big. Find me one of the touched ones, an Elite Downs Boar, and bring back 5 Boar Tusks. I want to hold one.
  • Out the Tree Gate, east to the downs. And Player: don't charge it head on. I did. Look at my leg.
  • Ha. Wise. Wiser than I was.
  • One of the big ones, and five tusks. You have (how many you carry).
  • (He weighs a tusk in his palm a long while.) Bigger than mine was. Much bigger. And you say there are more like it?
  • In my day that boar was the worst thing on the downs, and it was one boar. Well. Here's for your trouble. And that tusk goes on my shelf, story and all.

docs.title: The Dew Pond
docs.text:
Roland's best summer was spent camped by a dew pond on the downs. He wants to know if it is still there, the bees around it cleared, and Joan told that he asked, though he would never tell her himself.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Roland Level 26 After The Cart-Sized Boar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the dew pond in The Thyme Banks
  2. Defeat 30 Wild Bee in The Thyme Banks
  3. Talk to Joan

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Roland
Dialogue
  • One more, then I'll let you go. There was a dew pond up on the Thyme Banks, high on the slope. I camped by it one summer with nothing to do but mend boots and watch hawks. Best summer of my life.
  • Go and see if it's still there. Clear the Wild Bees off it, 30 of them, so a man could sit. Then tell Joan I asked. She'll know why.
  • High on the slope, mind. Ha. My knees could tell you how high.
  • Fair enough. It's been there forty years. It'll keep.
  • The dew pond on the Thyme Banks, thirty bees, then tell Joan.
  • Still there. Still full. (He clears his throat, twice.) Good.
  • Joan says she might close the Lantern one day in summer and drive me up in a cart. Me! In a cart! Ha. Well. Here.
  • He asked about the dew pond? (She puts down the cloth.) That's where he was the summer I was born. Mother told me. He never did.
  • Tell him... no. I'll tell him. Maybe I'll hire a cart one day and take him up there. Don't tell him I said so.

docs.title: Shells and Sea-Glass
docs.text:
Ronan wants a Wrack Boar tusk for his box, and the sea-glass his grandmother Agna has been saving for him. Bring him 10 tusks and the sea-glass.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Ronan Level 24 After The Magpie's Box

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 10 Wrack Boar Tusk (taken)
  2. Talk to Agna
  3. Deliver 1 Agna's Sea-Glass

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,450 EXP
  • 900 mesos
  • Fish Cake x5
  • White Potion x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Ronan
Dialogue
  • My box needs a tusk. A real one, green with weed, from the boars on the Strandwood shore. Lachlan has one on a string.
  • And Grandma's been saving sea-glass out of the nets for me, but she's cross lately and keeps forgetting to give it to me. She's cross about the nets. Not about me.
  • Bring me 10 Wrack Boar Tusks, so I can pick the best one. And ask Grandma for my sea-glass. Say please. She likes please.
  • Grandma's on her crate by the nets. She's always on her crate.
  • All right. I'll ask her myself. She'll say "what's the magic word, magpie".
  • Tusks, and Grandma's sea-glass. You've got (how many you carry) tusks.
  • The sea-glass! It's green like a wave. Grandma always finds the best ones.
  • And this tusk is the biggest. I'm keeping all ten, actually. You can have these instead.
  • The magpie sent you, did he? Ha. He's got a nerve, that one.
  • Here. Green as a wave, and it's been sitting in my apron pocket a month waiting for him. Tell him I didn't forget. I was busy.

docs.title: The Magpie's Box
docs.text:
Ronan wants the feathers of the birds that hang level with the Gullwalk, for his treasure box. Bring him 15 Kestrel Feathers.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Ronan Level 20 Leads to Shells and Sea-Glass

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Kestrel Feather (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,750 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • Fish Cake x5
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Ronan
Dialogue
  • You've been on the Gullwalk? Where the birds hang in the air level with the path, and don't even flap?
  • I want their feathers. For my box. Mum won't let me go up there. Could you bring me 15 Kestrel Feathers from the Kestrels? The stripy ones. Not the dull ones. Well, the dull ones too.
  • The Gullwalk is off the south of the town. Don't tell Eilidh. She'll say they're dirty.
  • Oh. That's all right. I'll find one on the shingle. Probably. Someday.
  • (how many you carry) feathers! You need 15. Stripy ones are best.
  • Fifteen! Look at that one, it's got a white tip. That's the king feather.
  • They're going in my box, at the side, so they don't get squashed. You can have these. Grandma says paying people is polite.

docs.title: Letters to the Queen
docs.text:
Rook's fortnightly letter to Queen Aveline is late. Take it by way of Nana Gristle's bench, who always has something to add, to Perch's loft on the Crooked Tower, then tell Rook it has flown.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Rook Level 22 Leads to The Quiet Ones

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Nana Gristle
  2. Talk to Perch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,840 EXP
  • 2,640 mesos
  • +50 standing with Rook
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Nine years I have written to Queen Aveline every fortnight, and this one is three days late. The Table ran long. The Table always runs long. The queen will notice, and she will say so, in writing, at length.
  • Would you carry it to Perch's loft, on top of the Crooked Tower? And on the way, stop at Nana Gristle's bench in Lantern Square. She likes to hear the letter is going. She also likes to send me a message. I cannot stop either.
  • Thank you. Nana is on the sunny side of the square, Perch is as high as the city goes. Whatever Nana says about me, it is probably true.
  • Then I will run it up myself, after the Table, after supper, after I find the stairs. Another day late. She will love that.
  • Nana's bench, then Perch's loft at the top of the Crooked Tower. The letter is the one with the candle-wax seal; I am a chandler, I cannot help it.
  • A letter to the queen, is it? Good. Tell her the honey cakes at Saucer's are the best in the kingdom; she ought to know. And tell Rook something from me, since Rook never listens when I say it.
  • Rook skips supper on Table nights. Rook talks so softly the back benches have to guess. And Rook lets Bastian go on until the candles gutter, and Rook makes the candles, so there is no excuse.
  • Off you go. Mind the third roof past the bakery on the way up, it has been soft since I was a girl, whatever Kite says.
  • Rook's letter. The birds know that seal; they like it, I think. The wax smells of honey. Hold still, this one is particular about strangers.
  • The birds still fly the road to the capital gladly, at any hour. Not every road is like that, these days. There. Off she goes, over the Gate Walk and east.
  • Tell Rook the letter has flown. And that Pounce sends regards. He does not, but somebody should.
  • Flown? Good. She will have it before her breakfast, and her answer will tell me off for it by mine. I look forward to that more than is decent.
  • And Nana's message? Supper, softness and Bastian. Yes. All three, every time. She is right about all three, which is why I take the long way round her bench.
  • Thank you, Player. If the queen's answer has a good part, I will read it at the next Table, and I will say who carried the letter.

docs.title: The Quiet Ones
docs.text:
The carters and small traders who used to sit quietly at the back of the Open Table are out on the Walkers' Road, waiting on caravans the boars keep stopping. Thin the bristle boars and ironhide hogs of the Bristlewood so they can come home and be heard.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Rook Level 40 After Letters to the Queen

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Bristle Boar
  • Defeat 20 Ironhide Hog

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 35,100 EXP
  • 4,800 mesos
  • +70 standing with Rook
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • My job, mostly, is the back benches. The quiet ones: the carters, the egg-sellers, the woman who mends sacks. They never speak first, so the Caller has to notice when they have something to say.
  • Lately the back benches are empty. Their caravans are late or turned back, so they sit out by the Halfway Stone waiting for them, or ride out to meet them. The boar in the Bristlewood have taken to the road, and the hogs behind them.
  • I cannot rule on boars, more is the pity. But you can thin them. 40 Bristle Boars and 20 Ironhide Hogs, and maybe the quiet ones get home in time to sit at a Table again.
  • The Bristlewood is past the Outworks' far end, east along the road. Hatch at the gate knows those woods better than anybody, if you want advice with your boar.
  • No, it is a long way for a Caller's worry. I will keep their seats warm.
  • Forty bristle boars and twenty ironhide hogs, Player. The back benches are still empty. I counted.
  • Two carts came in yesterday that had been sitting at the Halfway Stone for a week. And last night the sack-mender stood up at the Table for the first time in a year.
  • She said the sacks are fine, thank you, and sat down again. Best speech of the season. Inkpot underlined it.
  • That is your doing, Player. The Table will never know it, so I am telling you instead.

docs.title: The Table Argues
docs.text:
A tunnel under the walls is a way into the city no gate guards, and the only door to it is the locked iron door under the Great Hall. Rook puts the question to the Open Table: hear Bastian and Quint, then come back for the Table's answer.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Rook Level 20 After A Way In Leads to The Aristocrat Lock

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Bastian 'Bellows' Krell
  2. Talk to Quint

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,730 EXP
  • 2,400 mesos
  • +60 standing with Rook
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
  • Sets lowgrad.agreed
Dialogue
  • So. A wanderer walks into a tunnel in the hills and comes out under our walls, and Brindle says nobody at the gate would ever know. Brindle is right, which is the worst thing Brindle can be.
  • Behind the kitchens of this hall there is an iron door the Walkers found locked and never opened. A hundred years nobody has wanted to. Now I think somebody has to, and that is not mine to decide. It is the Table's.
  • The Table sits tonight. Hear out Bastian 'Bellows' Krell, who will speak first and longest, then Quint, who will speak last and best. Then come back and I will tell you what we agreed, if we agree anything before breakfast.
  • Good. Take a bench near the stew. Bastian is the one already standing up; Quint is by the cedar case behind my chair.
  • Fair enough. The door has kept a hundred years; it can keep one more night. The Table cannot, mind you, but that is my problem.
  • Bastian, then Quint, Player. Bastian is easy to find: follow the noise. Quint is easy to find too: follow the silence after it.
  • Player! Sit, sit! Tonight I argue that the door must be opened. Who knows what creeps up that tunnel while we sit here eating stew? We look, we know, we sleep! Applause, thank you.
  • And now I argue that the door must stay shut! A hundred years it has kept the dark on the far side! Who are we to pull the bolt? A door, friends, is a promise made of iron! Applause again. I am very good tonight.
  • Inkpot tells me I have won both arguments, which leaves the Table exactly where it began. Go and hear Quint. When Quint speaks, I stop. It is the only time I do.
  • Ah. You have heard Bastian win twice. Let an old man be serious for a moment, then; it happens once a year and this is it.
  • The Charter let the Walkers live as they chose, so long as they kept the kingdom's peace and laws. A road under our walls that nobody watches is not peace. It is a promise we are not keeping, to every traveller who comes through our gate believing it is the only way in.
  • So: open it, look, and keep it, the way we keep the gate. That is what I will tell the Table. Go back to Rook. And if Bastian stands up again, sit on him.
  • Dawn, Player. Bastian argued both sides and won both, Quint said his piece, Mags fed everyone twice, and Inkpot has it all down, heckles included. The Table has agreed: the iron door will be opened.
  • Agreed in one night. Nobody can remember the last time that happened. Dimity is checking the shelves to be sure.
  • Now somebody has to open it. Nobody has a key. Hex, on Workshops Row, has never met a lock that was not a conversation. And old Leland, the well-digger who has stood by that door all week, will want to be there.

docs.title: Roots from Below
docs.text:
Something strips the roots of Clem's orchard trees nearest the woods, deep underground and only at night. Sit up with him in the orchard, then collect 20 Pale Threads from Bluecaps in the Bluecap Groves.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Clem Level 36 After Quietly, for Dottie Leads to The Late Pedlar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Clem
  2. Bring 20 Pale Thread (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 26,000 EXP
  • 5,000 mesos
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • I lost another young tree, Player. That makes two. Bark fine, leaves fine, and then one morning it leans over and you can pull it up with one hand. The roots underneath are stripped clean, like someone peeled them.
  • No silver trail, so it is not snails. No holes, so it is not moles. It happens at night and it happens on the rows nearest the woods. My mother's rows.
  • Will you sit up with me tonight? Two pairs of ears are better than one. Come and talk to me when you are ready, and we will watch the rows together.
  • Bring something warm. The orchard gets cold after dark.
  • No, that is fair. It is a strange thing to ask. I will sit up on my own again.
  • If you are watching with me, talk to me when you are ready. And if we have watched already: 20 Pale Threads from the Bluecaps in The Bluecap Groves.
  • There. Do you hear it? Not a dig. A sort of creak, under the ground, like a rope pulled tight. And look, the grass is moving, in a line, from the woods to the tree.
  • It is coming from the Bluecap Groves. The great blue caps grow so thick there, and they trail long pale threads under the ground. Wilf told me once they reach farther than you would think.
  • Bring me 20 Pale Threads from the Bluecaps, Player. If they match what I dig out of my roots, I will know what I am fighting.
  • Look at that. Same thread. Same pale colour, same way it clings. It is the Bluecaps, all right, or what they put out under the ground.
  • I can cut a trench along the rows and line it with ash to keep them back for now. It will not stop whatever is making them grow like this, but it buys my trees a summer. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: A Note from Percival
docs.text:
A note in Percival's hand says Rosamund is too old for the Magician. Rosamund wants to know if he really wrote it before she starts their worst quarrel yet.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Rosamund Level 26 After Rosemary for the Magician

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Percival

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Rosamund
Dialogue
  • Read this. "Too old for the Magician. Let a girl play it." In what looks very like his hand. Left on my mirror.
  • I could scream. I could faint. I could do both, in that order, in front of the whole company. But first I want to be sure.
  • Show the note to Percival and ask him, straight, whether he wrote it. Watch his face; he cannot act with his face when he is surprised.
  • Bring me his face, darling. Exactly as it was.
  • Then I'll ask him myself. On stage. At the matinee.
  • Percival, the note, his face. Go.
  • He went white? And then furious, on my behalf? Then he did not write it.
  • Someone wanted us at each other's throats. Someone will be disappointed. Thank you, darling. I will not forget it.
  • Let me see that. "Too old"? I would never. That is not even my hand; I loop my y's.
