Walk with Sorrel to the outer lanterns at dawn and tell him honestly what you hear. Then follow it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Sorrel Level 57 After Further Out Leads to The Farthest Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the western outer lantern at dawn in Fairy Forest
  • Defeat 120 Howlets (Forest Howlet, Night Howlet)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 61,217 EXP
  • 1,710 mesos
  • +120 standing with Sorrel
  • +25 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • ...Walk with me.
  • The outer lanterns. At dawn. Then tell me what you hear. Honestly.
  • Stand at the western outer lantern at dawn with Sorrel, then follow the sound into the Deepening and quiet 120 howlets.
  • ...Listen first.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • ...Listen.
  • ...A creak. Far off. Like a rope pulled tight.
  • Yes. That. It's loudest at the western lanterns, facing the Deepening. The howlets were only answering it.

docs.title: A Red That Lasts
docs.text:
Whoever paints the heron under the Fiddler's Crossing has run out of red, Splash says, and only raw red earth from outside the walls lasts. The dark stumps of the Western Descent carry it in their roots.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Splash Level 24 Leads to Seen from the Gate Walk

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Clod of Red Earth (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,780 EXP
  • 2,060 mesos
  • +40 standing with Splash
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Did you see the heron? Under the Fiddler's Crossing, in the rain barrel? No? Good. I mean, I did not paint it, nobody knows who painted it, but you should go and look.
  • Whoever painted it, and I am only guessing, ran out of red. Red is the hard one. Sign-shop red goes brown in a week. Brick dust is better. Raw red earth from outside the walls is best.
  • The Dark Stumps on the Western Descent are full of it, red clods right in their roots. Bring 15 Clod of Red Earth, and do not mention where they went. Especially not to anybody with paint on their elbows.
  • Western Descent, up Stonefang Pass. The stumps do not like being dug at. Neither would I.
  • Fine, fine. Brown herons it is. Very modern.
  • 15 Clod of Red Earth, Player. You have (how many you carry). Quietly.
  • Oh, that is a red. That is a red that could start a fight.
  • You never saw this. I never saw you. But go and look under the Long Lean in about three nights. Just look. Do not tell anybody you looked.

docs.title: Splash seen from the gate walk
Seen from the Gate Walk
docs.text:
Splash wants to paint one picture travelers can see from the Gate Walk, and has decided that Kite gets to know what it is first. Carry the folded note to Kite, unread.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Splash Level 36 After A Red That Lasts

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Kite

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,920 EXP
  • 2,160 mesos
  • +60 standing with Splash
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Here is the thing. Everything I... everything anybody paints up here, you have to climb to see. Chimney backs, bridge bellies. Rooftop folk get it. Nobody coming in through the gate ever will.
  • I want one picture you can see from the Gate Walk. So travelers come in, look up, and know they have arrived. I know exactly what it is. I have known for a year. I have told nobody. Not even Kite.
  • I have decided Kite gets to know first. It is in a note, folded three times, sealed with a thumbprint of blue. Take it to Kite. Do not read it. I will know. I will not actually know, but I will feel it.
  • Kite will be running somewhere. Stand still on a roof long enough and Kite comes past.
  • Maybe I keep it another year. Secrets get better with age. Like cheese. Like Nana Gristle.
  • The note goes to Kite, Player. Unread. Thumbprint intact.
  • From Splash? Give it here. (Kite reads it, reads it again, and grins so wide it looks painful.)
  • Not telling. Not you, not anybody, not Cobble even if he takes my boots away. Tell Splash yes. Tell Splash I will carry the pots. Tell Splash it is the best idea anybody has ever had, including all of mine.
  • Kite said yes? And the best idea? Including Kite's own? Kite has never said that. Kite thinks Kite invented running.
  • Right. Now I need a wall nobody owns, a night with no moon, and a great deal of paint. You will know it when you see it, Player. Everybody coming in will.

docs.title: Spores for Two
docs.text:
Wilf supplies Rosa and Bram both, and they both want more. Bring him 20 Wild Spores from the patches of the Deepwood. He will take more, any time.

Town Kaldemor Category Repeatable Given by Wilf Level 30 After Too Bold

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 20 Wild Spore

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,000 EXP
  • 2,500 mesos

The first time you complete it instead: 14,000 EXP, 3,500 mesos, +20 standing with Kaldemor

Dialogue
  • Rosa wants spores for her bread and Bram wants them for his tinctures, and both want them yesterday. Rosa pays on the nail, Bram argues about every bag. Bring me 20 Wild Spores and I will split them between the two, and pay you whenever you bring me another twenty.
  • The patches on the The Humming Trail are the best. A few grow farther in, if you are passing.
  • Then they can argue with each other instead of with me. They are good at it.
  • 20 Wild Spores, Player. Rosa is waiting. So is Bram, loudly.
  • Twenty, and good ones. Ten for Rosa, ten for Bram, and not one word to either about who got the bigger ones.
  • Here is your share. Come back whenever your basket is full.

docs.title: A Hat My Size
docs.text:
Sprout wants to play the grandee one day, mostly for the hat. Ask Thimble whether she could make one his size.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Sprout Level 23 Leads to The Grandee's Fall

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Thimble

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,050 EXP
  • 1,380 mesos
  • +40 standing with Sprout
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Hey! Hey, are you in the play? You should be in the play. I am the urchin. I cheer for Juna. I steal the whole first scene, Dina says, and she says it like it is a bad thing, but it is not.
  • One day I am going to be the grandee. Not for the falling. Well, a bit for the falling. For the HAT. It is purple and tall and it has feathers, and Thimble keeps it locked up with the key on her spectacles.
  • Ask Thimble if she could make one my size. A little one. Just to try. She says no to me, but she might say yes to you. You look very serious.
  • Do not say it is for me. Say it is for a very small grandee. Who is not me.
  • Aww. Okay. I will just wear a bucket.
  • Ask Thimble about a hat my size! Please, Player! Please!
  • A hat his size. (Thimble's pins stop moving. For a moment she looks at a packet on her table, and then very firmly does not look at it.) Mf. No.
  • Tell him the grandee's hat is earned, not asked for. Tell him to grow. Tell him to learn his lines, all of them, which he already has. Tell him... no. Just tell him: not yet.
  • Not yet? She said NOT YET?
  • Not yet is not no! Not yet is nearly! Dad says not yet means 'yes, later' in grown-up. Thank you, Player! I am going to grow SO much.

docs.title: The Grandee's Fall
docs.text:
Sprout once did the grandee's fall off the Great Hall's table and landed on his elbow. Ask Dex how to do it properly, loudly, while Sprout listens from behind the curtain.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Sprout Level 31 After A Hat My Size

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Dex

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,520 EXP
  • 1,860 mesos
  • +50 standing with Sprout
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I did the grandee's fall once. Off the big table in the Great Hall, in the middle of a debate. Everybody laughed. Then Mags made me wash every bowl in the kitchen.
  • But I did it wrong. I landed on my elbow. Dad lands like a pillow. Every time. Fifteen years and not one bruise, he says.
  • Ask Dex how to do the fall properly. He will not teach me himself, he says I am too little. But he loves explaining things. If you ask, he will explain for an hour, and I will listen from behind the curtain.
  • Ask him loud. I will be behind the blue curtain. Do not look at the blue curtain.
  • Okay. I will practise on Hambone's sacks. They are soft. Mostly.
  • Ask Dex about the grandee's fall, Player! I am behind the curtain! Do not look!
  • The fall? Ah, the fall! The secret is that you are already falling before you trip. You go loose, loose as a sack of washing. The crowd sees a man fall. The man knows he is only lying down, very quickly. (Dex glances, not at all secretly, at the blue curtain.)
  • And you never, ever land on the elbow. Shoulder, hip, roll. Say it louder, Player, so the curtain can hear. SHOULDER. HIP. ROLL.
  • SHOULDER, HIP, ROLL! I heard! He said it so the curtain could hear! He knew I was there!
  • Dad always knows. I am going to practise on the sacks, and then on the cart, and then on the Great Hall table again, and this time Mags will not even notice. Thank you, Player!

docs.title: A Flicker Night
docs.text:
The new lens is in, and Starling thinks tonight is a flicker night. Borrow Perch's list of refused routes and watch the eastern horizon from Starling's roof.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Starling Level 55 After The Newest Lens Leads to The Lower Beacon

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Perch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 17,210 EXP
  • 3,300 mesos
  • +60 standing with Starling
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player! The lens, Tinsel's new lens, it is in, and it is perfect. There is a tiny bubble at the very edge that makes the moon wear a hat, but it is perfect. And tonight, I think, tonight is a flicker night.
  • I can feel it. No, I cannot feel it, that is nonsense. I have been counting the gaps between them, and tonight is due. Roughly. Possibly.
  • Before it gets dark, go up to Perch and borrow the route list. Perch and I put my dates beside the refusals, and I want both on the roof tonight. Then come back and watch with me.
  • Ask Perch for the copy in the blue ribbon, not the one the cat sat on.
  • Oh. Well, the sky will still be up there. It is very reliable that way.
  • The route list from Perch, Player, then back to my roof. It will be dark soon. Up here it is always dark soon.
  • Starling wants the list again. Of course. Here, the one in the blue ribbon. Every route the birds refused, with the date and the hour.
  • Some of Starling's dates sit right on top of mine, Player. Some do not. We have sat up there with both lists and a pot of tea and not been one bit wiser. Tell Starling I will come up once the birds are in.
  • Good, put it there, under the teapot, so it does not blow away. Now: look. Not through the telescope yet. Just look. East, toward the middle of the island, low, where the land meets the sky.
  • Wait... wait... There. Did you see it? The horizon, wavering, like the air over Ladle's grill. A few breaths, and gone. That is a flicker. I have watched them for two years, and they never look like more than that.
  • Perch's list says the birds refused the dusk route east the night before last, and tonight. But not last week, when I had a flicker too. So: some match, and some do not. That is all I know. That is all anybody knows.
  • Stay a while, if you like. There is tea, and the Fiddle is coming up over the Great Hall. I call the stars by the Walkers' names. It seems right, on a roof they patched.

docs.title: Dates and Lists
docs.text:
Starling's flicker dates and Perch's list of refused routes go to Rook, who writes to Queen Aveline every fortnight. Perhaps somebody in Selsior knows what they mean.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Starling Completed with Rook Level 67 After Stormcrest

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Deliver 1 Starling's Dates
  • Deliver 1 Perch's List

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 61,860 EXP
  • 8,040 mesos
  • +70 standing with Starling
  • +30 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Perch's birds fly east again, some of them. And still I see the flicker some nights, and still neither of us knows what it is. I have stared at the same two lists so long I can see them with my eyes shut.
  • So Perch and I agreed, for once, over a whole pot of tea. Take Starling's Dates and Perch's List to Rook at the Great Hall. Rook writes to the Queen every fortnight. Perhaps somebody in Selsior knows what we do not.
  • Tell Rook not to read them aloud at the Table. They are not funny. Well, the bit where the cat sat on the list is funny. Rook may read that bit.
  • Mm. One more year of watching, then. I am good at watching.
  • My dates and Perch's list, to Rook at the Great Hall, Player.
  • Starling's dates and Perch's list. I wondered when those two would stop squinting at each other's papers and send them somewhere.
  • Into the next letter to Queen Aveline, then. The capital writes back to me about all sorts; it can write back about this too, if anybody at court knows what it means.
  • I will not pretend an answer will come quickly, Player. Letters are slow and courts are slower. But it goes in the next one, with a line saying the city is grateful to the people who carried it.

docs.title: The Lower Beacon
docs.text:
Starling has only ever seen the flicker from the Rooftops. Go to the Beacon Line, watch again from one of the lower beacons, and thin the duskhawks while you wait.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Starling Level 57 After A Flicker Night Leads to The Beacon Ruins

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach Beacon Line
  2. Defeat 40 Duskhawk

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 97,480 EXP
  • 7,980 mesos
  • +60 standing with Starling
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I have been thinking. Every flicker I have seen, I saw from the Rooftops. Never once from below them. So either the flicker is very far away and needs height to be seen, or it is shy of the street. I prefer the first.
  • Go out to the Beacon Line and watch from one of the lower beacons. If it is far, you will see it just as I do. And thin the Duskhawks while you wait, 40 of them. Perch says they make watching unpleasant.
  • Look east, low, as the light goes. And look up now and then. Perch was very firm about looking up.
  • The beacons have waited a few hundred years. They can wait for you.
  • The Beacon Line, Player, and 40 Duskhawks. Watch east from a lower beacon.
  • You saw it too? From down there? Then it is far. Far beyond the downs, further east than they even reach. Not shy at all. Just a long way off.
  • And the duskhawks hunted late, you say, that same evening? Later than Perch has ever seen them. Hm. Hm! So on flicker nights the hawks are restless. That is why some of my dates match the refusals and some do not: the birds are not refusing my flicker. They are refusing the hawks.
  • It does not tell us what the flicker is. Nothing tells us that. But it is one thing we know that we did not, and I will write it in the margin in very small letters, so it does not get ideas.

docs.title: The Walker Stars
docs.text:
Starling's old star chart has the Walkers' names for the stars, but one name has faded away. Ozzie Lantry knows the Walkers' songs; perhaps one of them knows the stars.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Starling Level 35

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ozzie Lantry

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,610 EXP
  • 2,100 mesos
  • +50 standing with Starling
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • My parents left me a star chart from the city's first years, with the Walkers' names for the stars: the Cart, the Fiddle, the Open Door. Lovely names. But in the north the ink has gone, right where a name should be.
  • Ozzie Lantry collects the Walkers' songs and letters. If any of them sang about the stars, Ozzie will know. Will you ask for me? I would go, but the Great Hall is downstairs, and I mostly do not do downstairs.
  • It is the little crooked one, seven stars, just above the Fiddle's neck. Tell Ozzie that. Ozzie will know what I mean. Or say a great deal about something else first, and then know.
  • The gap will keep. Gaps are patient.
  • Ask Ozzie Lantry at the Great Hall about the crooked seven stars above the Fiddle, Player.
  • Seven stars above the Fiddle? Now where are my spectacles... no, not those, those are for reading... Ah. My grandfather sang about those. A fiddler, you see. He would point up from the roof and say: there is the fiddle, and there, just above, is the...
  • ...the Lost Bow! Because the fiddle never could keep track of it. Ha! He laughed every single time. Tell Starling: the Lost Bow. And tell Starling to come down and have supper some evening, will you?
  • The Lost Bow. Oh, that is perfect. Of course the fiddle lost its bow. Everybody in this city loses everything.
  • There, inked in. The chart is one gap smaller: a hundred-year-old gap, filled by a fiddler's joke. I think the Walkers would have liked that best of all.

docs.title: Stilebrook Farm
docs.text:
The herd's wallow is the yard of Stilebrook Farm, an old farm in the deep Boarwood that has stood empty since long before anyone alive. Hale wants to know what keeps the herd there. Reach the farm's old gate.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Hale Level 28 After Thinning the Herd Leads to Hale's Boarwood Bounty, Too Bold

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach Stilebrook Farm's gate in The Deep Boarwood

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,000 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • +50 standing with Kaldemor
  • Unlocks boss.gnarltusk
Dialogue
  • There is an old farm in the deep Boarwood, Player. Stilebrook. Nobody alive remembers anyone living there. Its fields went back to the woods a long time ago.
  • The tracks all lead there. The herd has made the yard its wallow, and something in it keeps them close. Something big. Elsie says she can hear it on still nights, grunting like a mill wheel.
  • Go to the farm's old gate, in The Deep Boarwood, and look over it. Do not climb it. Just look, and come back and tell me what you saw.
  • The gate is past the first stretch of the deep wood, by the fence the boars have not knocked down yet. Look, and come straight back.
  • Fair enough. It has waited this long.
  • Stilebrook Farm's gate, Player, in The Deep Boarwood. Look over it and come back.
  • As tall as a cart? Tusks like ploughshares? And the whole herd lying round it in the mud like it owns the place.
  • Then that is the one that leads them. Gnarltusk, the farm folk will be calling it by supper time, if I know Wilbur. While it holds that yard, the herd will keep pushing up to the stile.
  • When you are ready, ask me and I will take you through the gate to Stilebrook Farm. Watch it lower its head: that is the charge coming. And remember, no scroll will get you out of there.

docs.title: Strength of a Warrior
docs.text:
Tobin says a warrior is measured by more than errands. Reach level 5 and use Power Strike five times. He will teach you Warrior's Resolve.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Tobin Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach level 5
  • Use Power Strike 5 times

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 200 EXP
  • Bronze Helmet x1
  • Skill: Warrior's Resolve
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player, I have watched you grow these past days. Snails, shells, errands: not bad for a newcomer. But a warrior is measured by more than errands.
  • Put your points to work. Reach level 5, and learn the Power Strike: open the skill window with K, spend a skill point on it, and use it 5 times on whatever gets in your way.
  • Skill points go into your skills in the K window, and ability points into your stats in the S window. Come back when you have done both, Player.
  • Strength can wait a little. Come back when you feel ready.
  • Level 5 and five Power Strikes, Player. Press K if you have not spent your skill points yet; the strike sits on Shift until you move it.
  • Level 5, and a Power Strike that makes the snails think twice! I knew you had it in you.
  • Take this Bronze Helmet. Keep your head covered and your chin down, and it will serve you well. And take something I cannot wrap: Warrior's Resolve, a battle cry that hardens you for three minutes. It is on the Beginner tab of the skills window; drag it onto a key, or press F1.

docs.title: Swithin a line under a name
A Line Under a Name
docs.text:
A wool buyer Swithin wrote going out to the downs a year ago never came back through the gate. Find the milestone at Downs Edge she would have passed, clear 30 wild bees there, and tell Brann what you found.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Swithin Level 23 Leads to The Margin Guess

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the old milestone in Downs Edge
  2. Defeat 30 Wild Bee in Downs Edge
  3. Talk to Brann

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,000 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Swithin
Dialogue
  • A moment, Player. Do not lean on the desk. I have told only the Sergeant this.
  • A wool buyer, written going out a year ago: 'to the downs folds, back by the month's end.' Green cloak. In the margin I wrote, 'will marry a shepherd.' She never came back in.
  • Travellers mark the old milestone at Downs Edge; they scratch their initials. Look for hers, clear 30 Wild Bees so you can, then tell Brann.
  • Initials, a date, anything. I can work with very little.
  • Then the line stays open. I am used to it. I do not like it.
  • The old milestone at Downs Edge, thirty bees, then the Sergeant.
  • Her initials, and 'gone on with the flocks'. Gone on. Not lost.
  • I shall draw half a line under her name. Half is a great deal more than nothing. Thank you.
  • Swithin's wool buyer? Initials on the milestone and 'gone on with the flocks'. ...Good. Tell him to stop fretting. He won't. Neither will I.

docs.title: The Margin Guess
docs.text:
Last month Swithin wrote in a margin that a stranger with a fine spear was 'hunting a great boar, and will come back hurt'. He did. The boar is still on the Thyme Banks. Defeat it, an Elite downs boar, and 30 more of its herd.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Swithin Level 26 After A Line Under a Name

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 1 Elite Downs Boar
  • Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • Scroll for Helmet for DEF 60% x1
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Swithin
Dialogue
  • My margins are a harmless amusement. Usually. Last month I wrote, of a stranger with a fine spear: 'hunting a great boar; will come back hurt.'
  • He came back hurt. I put the cross in the column myself. I did not enjoy being right.
  • The boar is still on the The Thyme Banks, he says, larger than the rest. Defeat that Elite Downs Boar, and 30 of its herd, so that my margin has a better ending.
  • I shall write you a very good margin.
  • Of course. I shall leave the ending blank. For now.
  • The great boar on the Thyme Banks, and thirty of its herd.
  • The great boar is down. I have written it in: 'and then a hero came'.
  • Do not read it. It is a margin. Margins are private.

docs.title: The Sword Saint's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Grand Swordmaster of level 160 beyond the Guard's ranks, to the Sword Saint. Prove your edge in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 600 of its monsters.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Rhys Level 160 Job Grand Swordmaster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 600 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 600,000 EXP
  • Advance to Sword Saint

Placeholder

A stand-in until the fields past level 120 exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the far fields when they are built.

Dialogue
  • Player. Level one hundred and sixty. I have no rank left to give you, and I am told there is one beyond all of them.
  • The old Guard called it the Sword Saint: one for whom the sword is no longer carried but followed, who cuts the sky open and lets a thousand blades answer.
  • I can only set you the old test: defeat 600 of the Greenwood Clearing's Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps, and show me that the road has nothing left to teach you.
  • Then go. Six hundred, and each cut leading into the next.
  • Few ask twice. Come back when the sword calls you.
  • Six hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player, on the royal road outside the city.
  • Six hundred. I stopped counting the cuts at two hundred and began to watch your blade instead; it no longer seemed to hold you.
  • Kneel, Player, one last time. By the old authority of the Guard, I name you a Sword Saint.
  • Heavenly Severance and Infinite Blade Dance are yours now. Chain them into the cuts you know, as the sword wills. Use them well.

docs.title: The Swordmaster's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Swordsman of level 70 into the Swordmaster's way. Prove it with a long hunt in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 200 of its monsters.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Rhys Level 70 Job Swordsman

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 200 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 40,000 EXP
  • Advance to Swordmaster

Placeholder

A stand-in until the higher fields exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the region of level 70 when that is built (WORLD M5).

Dialogue
  • Player. Level seventy, and still the same steady arm. The Guard has a name for those who get this far: Swordmaster.
  • A Swordmaster does not end a cut. He lets it run into the next, and the next after it. That cannot be taught on a practice dummy, only in a long fight that does not let up.
  • Go back to the Greenwood Clearing, on the royal road outside the city, and defeat 200 of its Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps. They are the toughest creatures the Guard can set you against today. Cut them down one after another, and do not stop between cuts.
  • Good. It is a long hunt, so bring potions and patience. Come back when the count is full.
  • A long road needs a steady start. Come back when you are ready.
  • Two hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player. The clearing is on the royal road, outside the city. Keep cutting.
  • Two hundred, and your guard never dropped. That is the rhythm I was looking for.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Swordmaster.
  • Four new cuts are yours: Flash Cutter, Blade Cyclone, Thousand Cuts and Rising Blade. Press one while another is still finishing, and it takes over at once. Use them well.

docs.title: The Swordsman's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Warrior of level 30 into the Swordsman's way. Prove it on the Selsior Downs: defeat 30 of the Downs Boars of the Thyme Banks or the Chalk Hive Bees of the Chalk Hives and bring back 5 trial seals.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Rhys Level 30 Job Warrior

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Downs monsters (Downs Boar, Chalk Hive Bee)
  • Deliver 5 Guard's Trial Seal

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,000 EXP
  • Advance to Swordsman
Dialogue
  • Player. Level thirty, and a steady arm. I have been waiting to say this: you are ready for the Guard's trial.
  • A Swordsman does not swing harder. He swings truer. That is learned where the fight is real, not on a practice dummy.
  • Go out to the Selsior Downs, off the Hedge Lanes north of the Tree Gate. Defeat 30 of the Downs Boars of the Thyme Banks and the Chalk Hive Bees of the Chalk Hives, and bring me 5 Guard's Trial Seals. The Guard stamps a seal on a leaf, and those creatures carry them off while you are on trial.
  • Good. Mind the Axe Stumps: they hit harder than they look. Keep your potions close, and come back when it is done.
  • A sword that is not ready is worse than no sword. Come back when you are.
  • Thirty of the Downs' boars and hive bees and five trial seals, Player. The Downs are off the Hedge Lanes, north through the Tree Gate.
  • Five seals, and the clearing quieter for it. I watched for a steady arm, and here it is.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Swordsman.
  • Your cuts will come quicker and truer from now on: the Swordsman's attacks are yours. Use them well.

docs.title: Sybil a thread by a certain date
A Thread by a Certain Date
docs.text:
Sybil needs river fern fibre for a royal garment, ready by a date she will not name. Gather it on the Long Reach and take it to her sister Edith to spin.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Sybil Level 33 Leads to Boots That Wear Through

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 15 Fern Fibre
  2. Talk to Edith

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,000 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Sybil
Dialogue
  • I need thread. Not any thread: river fern fibre, which spins finer than silk and takes a dye like a dream.
  • For a royal garment. To be ready by a certain date. Which date is none of your business.
  • Gather me 15 Fern Fibres on the Long Reach, then take them to my sister Edith on Theatre Row. She has the only wheel in Selsior fine enough.
  • Clean hands when you pick it. Fibre remembers.
  • Then I shall use silk, and it will look like silk, and I shall know.
  • Fifteen Fern Fibres, then Edith on Theatre Row.
  • Edith talks too much. Thank you, Player. The date stands, whatever it is.
  • Fern fibre, from Sybil? For a royal garment, and she would not say which?
  • Then it is for someone she is proud of. She goes quiet about exactly one person. Tell her I will spin it by the week's end.

docs.title: Boots That Wear Through
docs.text:
A certain pair of riding boots wears through in a month. Bring Sybil hide from the Undercut's crocos for soles that will last.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Sybil Level 44 After A Thread by a Certain Date

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Undercut Croco Hide (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,000 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Sybil
Dialogue
  • Riding boots should last a year. A certain pair lasts a month. The soles wear through as if someone walked round and round a yard.
  • Croc hide from The Undercut makes the toughest soles there are. Bring me 10 Undercut Croco Hides and I will resole them to last. Ask me nothing about the yard.
  • Good. And not a word about boots to anyone. Particularly at breakfast.
  • Then I shall patch them again. Patches show.
  • Ten Undercut Croco Hides from The Undercut.
  • Good hide. These will last a season of... riding. Thank you, Player. And mend that hem; I cannot bear to look at it.

docs.title: A Pot for Haldor
docs.text:
Tamsin and Haldor have had their argument about the deep forest again. Take Haldor a crock of her best pine tar. It is not an apology. It is tar.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Tamsin Completed with Haldor Level 40 After Sound Grain Leads to Ballast

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Tamsin's Pine Tar

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,700 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Tamsin
Dialogue
  • Haldor and I had the argument again. The whole quay heard it. Jory can do both sides now, word for word.
  • He's not wrong. He'll not send a cutter where he can't hear him shout, and I'd not either, if I'm honest. Which I'm not, while he's standing in front of me.
  • So. This is my good pine tar, the batch Fergus taught me. It keeps a raft's lashings sound round the point. It's not an apology. It's tar.
  • Take it to Haldor on the Forest Shore. Don't say sorry. Say it's tar.
  • He'll be at the raft landing, if he's not out at the edge. And if he asks whether I've given up on the deep timber, say no.
  • Fine. The argument keeps. It's kept for years.
  • The tar to Haldor, on the Forest Shore. It's tar, not sorry.
  • Tamsin's tar. The good batch. I can smell old Fergus in it.
  • Tell her thank you. Tell her I'll send her the first sound tree from the edge that's fit for a keel, and that I'll not send a cutter past the edge for it. She'll know both halves of that.
  • Here. For carrying it, and for carrying it all this way without spilling a word of whatever she said about me.

docs.title: Ballast
docs.text:
The Gap Runner sits wrong in the water, and Tamsin wants to trim her with Wrackstone. Clear 40 Wrackgolems on the Skerries and bring her 15 Wrackstone.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Tamsin Level 58 After A Pot for Haldor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Wrackgolem in The Skerries
  2. Bring 15 Wrackstone (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60,000 EXP
  • 2,320 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Tamsin
Dialogue
  • She sits wrong. The Gap Runner. Half a hand down at the stern with the crew aboard, and I can feel it through the tiller like a stone in a boot.
  • It's the ballast. Iron sits all in one place. Beach stone's too light. The Wrackgolems on the Skerries are stone and weed grown into one, and that stone's as dense as anything I've weighed. I want to trim her with it, a lump at a time, till she sits true.
  • Clear 40 Wrackgolems off the Skerries and bring me 15 Wrackstone. I'll weigh every one.
  • The Skerries lie off the foot of the Forest Jaw, past the Wrack Ledges, at the cliff foot. Bring them dry if you can. You can't. Bring them anyway.
  • Then she sits wrong another week, and I'll hate every day of it.
  • Forty Wrackgolems, and (how many you carry) of 15 Wrackstone. The Skerries, off the Jaw.
  • Fifteen. Heavy. Good. Jory! Scales!
  • I'll lay them in tonight, a lump at a time. She'll sit true by the end of the week, or I'll have the keel out again. Again.
  • Will it win the race? Nobody knows that till the line, Player. But she'll be the best boat I can make, and Fergus never asked more than that. Here.

docs.title: Sound Grain
docs.text:
Tamsin blames the Gap Runner's losses on her timber. Bring her 20 Sound Driftwood from the Driftstumps of the Strandwood so she can read the grain.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Tamsin Level 26 Leads to A Pot for Haldor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Sound Driftwood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,750 EXP
  • 1,040 mesos
  • Fish Cake x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Tamsin
Dialogue
  • You. Hold this. No, the other end. Good. Now listen.
  • The Gap Runner's lost five summers to Bain, two of them by a single length. I've changed the mast, the keel, the line and the sails. It's not the crew and it's not Iska. It's the timber.
  • The good boat timber's in the deep forest, and Haldor won't send his crews in. Fine. Then I want to know what else there is. The Driftstumps in the Strandwood are old timber that walks. Most of it's rot. The heart of some isn't.
  • Bring me 20 Sound Driftwood. I'll split them and read the grain. If even one is close, I'll know.
  • Strandwood Edge or the Rocks, the stumps walk about on both. Bring the grey bits, not the soft bits. You'll know.
  • Then stand clear of the slip. I've work.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Sound Driftwood. The grey, dense bits.
  • Let me see. Split this one. And this. Hm.
  • Close-grained, but short. Good for a thole pin, no good for a keel. I knew it. I knew it, and I had to see it.
  • Here. It's not your fault the woods grow what they grow. Fergus would have said I wasted your afternoon. Fergus would have done the same.

docs.title: The Cistern Sluice
docs.text:
Below the Old Drains lie the cisterns of the first city, flooded and silted. Tancred still has the sluice keys: go down to the Cisterns and turn the sluice wheel to drain them.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Tancred Level 25 After Hold the Lantern Leads to Notes on the Backs of Pages, A Stain She Cannot Place, The Buried Street

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Cisterns
  2. Look at the sluice wheel in The Cisterns

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,000 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Tancred
Dialogue
  • Lettice says the rats are running up. Ida says the scratching's under the cisterns now. Then the cisterns have to come down, Player, and the sluice is the way.
  • Thirty years I turned that wheel. My knees won't do the ladders now. Here's the key. Go down to the The Cisterns, find the sluice wheel at the far end, and turn it. Press up on it, the way you'd open a door. She'll groan. Let her.
  • The water'll go down slow. Mind the slimes in it. They don't drain.
  • No shame in it. That water's cold.
  • Down to the Cisterns, and turn the sluice wheel at the far end.
  • Hear that? The whole quarter's pipes just sighed. She turned for you.
  • And with the water down, there's something on the cistern floor I never saw in thirty years: an old street, going on under the wall. Go and tell Ida. Here, and keep the key. I won't be needing it.

docs.title: Cakes for the Heart Tree
docs.text:
A scholar has not left the Heart Tree in three days. Tansy is sending cakes, whether they like it or not.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Tansy Level 19

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Caelum
  • Defeat 30 Road monsters (Slime, Bubbling, Glimmerwing, Crowned Glimmerwing)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,641 EXP
  • 418 mesos
  • Honey Cake x5
  • +100 standing with Tansy
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Three days! Not one of those scholars has come down for a cake in three days. That's not study, that's starving.
  • Take a basket up to Caelum. And clear the roads on the way back, the carters with my flour come tomorrow.
  • Take Tansy's basket to Caelum in the Old Records, and clear 30 monsters off the roads for the flour carts.
  • Make him eat one in front of you.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Caelum. Watch him eat.
  • He ate two? Good boy.
  • Here, some for you too. You've the look of someone who skips meals.
  • Cakes? For me? I don't have time to... oh, they're warm.
  • Caelum eats one standing up, then a second sitting down, then looks slightly embarrassed.

docs.title: Dew from a Far Grove
docs.text:
The near leaves have run dry, and Tansy's dew tea needs dew. Bring her Glimmer Dew from the slimes of the Glimmer Path.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Tansy Level 11

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 12 Glimmer Dew (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 332 EXP
  • 242 mesos
  • Dew Tea x6
  • +60 standing with Tansy
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • The near leaves have run dry, Player! Dry! In this forest! I've been brewing dew tea since before Liri was born and I've never seen it.
  • The slimes on the Glimmer Path soak up the morning dew, the greedy things. Squeeze one and it all comes out.
  • Bring me 12 Glimmer Dew from the Slimes on the Glimmer Path, and the first pot is yours.
  • Wonderful! The Glimmer Path is just past the Forest Edge, under the first outer lanterns.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • (how many you carry) of 12 so far? Keep at it, love.
  • Oh, it's lovely and clear. Smell that.
  • Here, some of the first pot, bottled for the road. Don't drink it all at once.

docs.title: The Blue Flame
docs.text:
Tarran thinks the salt in dried weed once made his lantern burn blue. Bring him 20 Weedy Bristles from the Wrack Boars so he can try again.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Tarran Level 26 Leads to The Market Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Weedy Bristle (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,750 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • White Potion x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Tarran
Dialogue
  • Can you keep a secret? Not a big one. A lantern-sized one.
  • I had a lantern burn blue once. Blue, Player! I've been trying for a year to do it again. I think it was the wick. I'd twisted it with a bit of boar bristle that had dried weed in it, the salty kind, from the shore.
  • Bring me 20 Weedy Bristle from the Wrack Boars on the Strandwood. And don't tell Gunna. I'm not hiding it. I just want it to work first.
  • Twenty! The weediest ones you can find.
  • Oh. No, that's fine. I'll keep trying with candle-ends.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Weedy Bristle. Weedy as you can.
  • Right. Twist it in. Light it. Watch.
  • Yellow. Of course it's yellow. Perfectly good, steady, ordinary yellow.
  • Gunna walked past just now, said "what a nice yellow" and kept walking. She knew. She always knows. Thanks, Player. One day it'll burn blue again, and you'll be the first to see it.

docs.title: The Market Lantern
docs.text:
Tarran has hung his brightest lantern over the Lantern Market square. Go and look at it for him, then bring him 20 Shore Crab Claws to toughen the next one's glass.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Tarran Level 36 After The Blue Flame

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the Lantern Market square in Goa Harbour
  2. Bring 20 Shore Crab Claw (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,700 EXP
  • 1,400 mesos
  • Elixir x1
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Tarran
Dialogue
  • I've hung my brightest lantern over the Lantern Market square. The last bright one lit the whole market for half a night, then cracked its own glass.
  • Go and stand in the square and look at it for me, would you? I can't watch, I'll jinx it. It's the heat that cracks the glass, I'm sure of it. The old glassmakers on the quay put ground shell in the melt to toughen it, and crab shell is the thickest there is.
  • So: the Lantern Market square first. Then bring me 20 Shore Crab Claws from the Shore Crabs on The Undercliff. For the next one. There's always a next one.
  • Don't look straight at it. Well, do. Just not for long.
  • Fair enough. Glass is dull. Until it cracks.
  • The square, then (how many you carry) of 20 Shore Crab Claws. The thick ones.
  • Don't tell me. It cracked. Was it bright first, though? It was bright first?
  • Brilliant, then dark. Half and half, like always.
  • With crab shell in the glass the next one will hold. I'm nearly sure. Here, Player. You're the only one who hasn't laughed. Well, you and Kestra.

docs.title: Dates and Dots
docs.text:
Imre left a book of dates with Tavi, and Tavi laid it beside Skarra's hide map. Carry Imre's book to Ahvi in the Brenna House.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Tavi Completed with Ahvi Level 54 After A Shimmering Night Leads to Hold the Old Camp

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Imre's Book of Dates

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 19,500 EXP
  • 1,080 mesos
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Tavi
Dialogue
  • Imre came up to the rim at dawn with a book under one arm and no breakfast. Skarra's map does not leave her tent, so I took the book to the map instead. Look at this with me.
  • Here: the night the ropes were gnawed. Here: the night the goats ran. Here: the raids on the pastures, both of them. Every one comes a day or two after one of Imre's shimmering nights.
  • I can't explain it, and I don't like what I can't explain. Take Imre's Book of Dates to Ahvi at the Brenna House; Imre will meet you there. If the songs remember anything like this, Ahvi will know.
  • Keep it dry and keep it closed. Imre would sooner lose a hand than that book.
  • Then I'll keep it under my bedroll and stare at it every night. That should help.
  • Imre's Book of Dates goes to Ahvi, in the Brenna House on the middle terraces.
  • Imre's book, and Imre close behind you, out of breath. Put it here, by the lamp. Let me read the dates against the map's, slowly.
  • The songs have no shimmering stars, Player. But they have one verse, very old, about a season when the beasts grew wild, before the Burning. I have sung it to myself every night this summer.
  • I do not know what this means, and I will not pretend to. But I will keep these dates beside my verse. Thank you for carrying the book so gently.

docs.title: Let Ketta Lead
docs.text:
Ketta has decided to tell Tavi about the cave herself. Go with her to Tavi.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Ketta Completed with Tavi Level 21 After Earn Her Trust Leads to Back into the Dark

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,200 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ketta
Dialogue
  • I've been thinking about it all night. If drakes are breeding under the watch's own trail, Tavi has to know. And Tavi should hear it from me, not from you, not from Skarra.
  • Come with me? You don't have to say anything. I just need somebody standing next to me so I can't turn around halfway.
  • Tavi's on the rim as always, staring at the trail like it owes money. Let's go.
  • No, you're right, I should do it alone. I'll do it tomorrow. Probably.
  • Tavi is on the Uskari Rim. I'm right behind you. Don't let me turn around.
  • Ketta. And Player. Ketta, you have the face of someone about to say something carried too long. I know that face. I've worn it.
  • Drakes breeding below the trail, and a great one in the dark. Thank you for telling me. That took more than any patrol I've ever sent you on.
  • Here is what we'll do. Nobody goes into that cave until Ketta says so, and when we do, Ketta leads. You know it better than any of us, Ketta, even if you only saw it running.
  • Player, stay close to her. She will decide when. And when she does, you go down together.

docs.title: Old Gnarl
docs.text:
The oldest of the ridge trees, Old Gnarl, has rooted on Howling Peak, and the stumps of the ridges grow thick around it. Tavi will take you up. End it.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Tavi Level 28 After The Worst Stretch Leads to The High Pasture, Twisted Wood

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Old Gnarl

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,000 EXP
  • 560 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • One of: Gnarlwood Axe, Gnarlwood Greatsword, Ridgewalker Boots
  • +60 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Tavi
  • Unlocks boss.old_gnarl
Dialogue
  • Every stump you have cut on the ridges grew from somewhere. Uskari hunters have known the oldest tree up there all their lives: a great split stump on Howling Peak, older than the town. They called it Old Gnarl and left it alone, because it left them alone.
  • It does not leave anyone alone now. It has walked. It roots where it pleases, and the dead wood around it gets up and follows. While Old Gnarl stands, the patrols cannot hold the ridges, however many spears Tavi sends.
  • End it. There is no path up to Howling Peak; I will take you up the Uskari way when you are ready. Defeat Old Gnarl and the ridges can be held.
  • Talk to me when you want to go up, and I will open the way. When it is half dead it will call up pale stumps and roots from the ground. Watch the ground. And come back.
  • No shame in that. Old Gnarl has waited a hundred years. It can wait for you to be ready.
  • Old Gnarl on Howling Peak. Talk to me when you want to go up.
  • It is down? The old split stump, down?
  • My grandmother told me the hunters used to touch it for luck on the way out. Tavi will tell Skarra to rub the red off the ridges. Some of them, anyway.
  • Take one of these, made from the ridges' hardest wood, and the elixirs. You have earned the ridges, Player. Sennu will want to hear it from you.

docs.title: Withered Reach Bounty
docs.text:
Tavi pays a bounty for every hundred monsters of the Withered Reach, and will pay it again any time.

Town Midbarium Category Repeatable Given by Tavi Level 51 After The Greywater

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 100 Monster of the Withered Reachs (Swollen Stump, Raider Boar, Swollen Dark Stump, War Mask, Bone Hound, Swollen Axe Stump, Stone Hulk)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 80,000 EXP
  • 1,020 mesos
  • +20 standing with Midbarium

The first time you complete it instead: 80,000 EXP, 2,000 mesos, Elixir x2, +15 standing with Midbarium, +30 standing with Tavi

Dialogue
  • The Reach is past where the watch can walk in a day, and everything out there is worse than it was last season. I can't send scouts I don't have. I can pay.
  • A bounty: 100 monsters of the Withered Reach, stumps, boars, masks, hounds or hulks, and I pay every time you bring me another hundred.
  • Count them as you go. And don't let me catch you resting at the Old War Camp before the hundredth.
  • Then the Reach keeps its monsters a while longer. They won't thank you.
  • A hundred monsters of the Withered Reach, any kind. Then come back to the rim.
  • A hundred. Skarra will want to move her dots back a finger's width.
  • Here's your bounty. The Reach will fill up again; it always does. Come back when it has.

docs.title: Withered Reach Elites
docs.text:
Tavi pays for every Elite of the Withered Reach brought down: the stirred ones, bigger and meaner than their kind.

Town Midbarium Category Repeatable Given by Tavi Level 52 After The Greywater

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Elite Elite of the Withered Reach (Swollen Stump, Raider Boar, Swollen Dark Stump, War Mask, Bone Hound, Swollen Axe Stump, Stone Hulk)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,500 EXP
  • 1,040 mesos
  • +20 standing with Midbarium

The first time you complete it instead: 14,500 EXP, 2,000 mesos, White Potion x10, +15 standing with Midbarium, +30 standing with Tavi

Dialogue
  • Some of what walks the Reach is worse than the rest: bigger, faster, and harder to put down. The watch calls them the stirred ones. My scouts are told to walk around them.
  • You don't have to walk around them. Bring one down, an Elite of the Withered Reach, and I'll pay for it, every time.
  • You'll know one when you see it. Everything near it goes quiet.
  • Sensible. Unlike me.
  • One Elite of the Withered Reach. Then come back to the rim.
  • One of the stirred ones, down. Good. That's one less my scouts have to walk around.
  • Your pay. There'll be another out there by the time you're back. There always is.

docs.title: A Withered Reach Epic
docs.text:
Now and then the Reach throws up something far worse than an Elite. Tavi pays well for every Epic brought down.

Town Midbarium Category Repeatable Given by Tavi Level 55 After The Greywater

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Epic Epic of the Withered Reach (Swollen Stump, Raider Boar, Swollen Dark Stump, War Mask, Bone Hound, Swollen Axe Stump, Stone Hulk)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,500 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • +20 standing with Midbarium

The first time you complete it instead: 34,500 EXP, 2,500 mesos, Elixir x2, +15 standing with Midbarium, +30 standing with Tavi

Dialogue
  • Twice this season a scout has come back from the Reach white as chalk, talking about a hulk the size of a hall door that the stones themselves seemed to shake for. The deeply touched ones, the worst of them.
  • If you meet one, and you're still standing afterwards, I'll pay for it: an Epic of the Withered Reach. I'll pay for every one, and I'll pay well.
  • Don't go looking for it tired. It'll find you either way.
  • Good. I'd rather you came home.
  • One Epic of the Withered Reach. Then come back to the rim, in one piece.
  • You brought one down? A deeply touched one, and you're standing here? I'd have bet against that, and I hate losing bets.
  • Your pay, and well earned. I'll tell the scouts. It'll do them good to know it can be done.

docs.title: The Worst Stretch
docs.text:
Tavi walks the worst stretch of the patrols personally: out along the Broken Ground to the far canyon bridge. Walk it together, look at the bridge, and hunt 60 Dark Axe Stumps on the way.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Tavi Level 25 After Three Goats' Tracks Leads to Old Gnarl

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 60 Dark Axe Stump in The Broken Ground
  2. Look at the far canyon bridge in The Broken Ground

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,750 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x20
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Tavi
Dialogue
  • Ready? Good. Talking about a trail is half as useful as walking it, and walking it with someone who keeps up is twice as useful. Let us see if you keep up.
  • The The Broken Ground is the far end of the ridges. Cracked rock, dead wood swinging axes, and at the end of it the far canyon bridge, the only way to the far slopes. Tavi walks it every week. Nobody else wants to.
  • Walk it with me. 60 Dark Axe Stumps on The Broken Ground, and at the end, look at the far canyon bridge with me. Look it over at the near end. Then we race back.
  • Do not wait for me. If I fall behind, which I will not, keep going.
  • Tomorrow, then. The stretch is not going to walk itself. Well, the stumps on it are.
  • Sixty Dark Axe Stumps on The Broken Ground, then the near end of the far canyon bridge.
  • You beat me back. Do not say anything.
  • That is the stretch. Tavi doubled the patrols on it, and it is still the worst. And the bridge: you saw the new lashings at the near anchor, and Vosk's splices. Something gnaws those ropes at night. Vosk does not know what, and Vosk knows rope better than anyone alive.
  • Potions and salve, and the right to say you walked the worst stretch with the chieftain of the Uskari. Do not say it to Skarra; Skarra will want to race you too.

docs.title: Boots for the Road
docs.text:
The hill road eats Teague's boots. Bring him 15 Ligator Skins from Dusk Ford for a new pair before his summer trip.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Teague Level 20 After The Carters' Road Leads to Brave Company

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Ligator Skin (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,750 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • Salted Fish x5
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Teague
Dialogue
  • See these boots? Two years on the hill road and they're more hole than boot. The hill eats boots, Player. It's famous for it.
  • The cobbler on the market says ligator hide is the toughest there is. Bring me 15 Ligator Skins from the Ligators at Dusk Ford, on the Western Merchant Road, and I'll have boots that outlast me.
  • Go by daylight, mind. It's a long road back.
  • No? I'll stuff them with straw. Done it before. There's a story in that, too.
  • (how many you carry) of 15 Ligator Skins. Dusk Ford, on the Western Merchant Road.
  • Look at that hide! From a ligator as long as my cart, was it? It was. I'll say it was.
  • New boots before the shearing. Morag will say I look thin in them, but my feet will be dry. Here, for your trouble.

docs.title: Brave Company
docs.text:
Teague wants company that has stood in the rocks at dusk and not run. Defeat 60 Strand Foxes, then carry his question to Esk on the Inlet Quay once more.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Teague Level 26 After Boots for the Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 60 Strand Fox
  2. Talk to Esk

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,600 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • Salted Fish x10
  • +25 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Teague
Dialogue
  • I need brave company for the next trip, after the shearing. Half the adventurers at the inn laughed and said they'd come if I paid them in stories.
  • I'd pay them anyway. But I want someone who has stood in the rocks at dusk and not run. The Strand Foxes on the Strandwood come out of the rocks in packs at dusk. That'll do for a start.
  • Defeat 60 Strand Foxes. Then go and ask Esk on the Inlet Quay again, for me. She hasn't said yes and she hasn't said no. Best answer I've ever had.
  • The foxes favour the black rocks. And be gentle with Esk. She's thinking. I can tell.
  • Fair. Nobody wants to be brave on an empty stomach.
  • Sixty foxes, then Esk on the Inlet Quay. She's thinking. I'm sure she's thinking.
  • "Still thinking." Ha! That's a better answer than last time. Last time she just looked at me.
  • And you, sixty foxes. You'll do, Player. Here, salted fish and potions, the drover's way: you never know how long the road is. Ask me some night about the time I ate nothing but salted fish for a month. It's a different month every time.
  • Teague sent you. Again.
  • Tell him I heard him. Tell him I'm still thinking. It's a fair question, and I don't give fair questions quick answers.

docs.title: The Carters' Road
docs.text:
Teague brings his wool down the Western Merchant Road. Crabs walk the Seaward Woods and Lupins pelt the carts.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Teague Level 16 Leads to Boots for the Road

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Lorang
  • Defeat 30 Lupin

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 900 EXP
  • 640 mesos
  • Fish Cake x5
  • +15 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +100 standing with Teague
Dialogue
  • Crabs, Player. In a wood. A mile from the sea. I have told that at the Gap Inn and nobody believed me, so I have stopped telling it, and now they are bigger.
  • And the Lupins. A Lupin will throw anything. I lost a whole cheese to one.
  • Clear 30 Lorang and 30 Lupin in Seaward Woods, inland from Gull Heath.
  • Mind the bananas. I am not joking.
  • No shame in it. I have walked past them a hundred times myself.
  • The Seaward Woods start right off Gull Heath, on the merchant road.
  • You did it? Then the next load goes down with a song. Here, for your trouble.

docs.title: Tegan a tooth for a needle
A Tooth for a Needle
docs.text:
Tegan says a sailmaker could make something of a tooth the size of the Ripsaw's. Bring her its saw.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Tegan Level 48 After Long Straight Tears

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 The Ripsaw's Saw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 25,273 EXP
  • 1,056 mesos
  • Sawtooth Cutlass x1
  • +40 standing with Tegan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The Ripsaw's saw. If you bring it to me, I'll show you what a sailmaker does with a tooth that size.
  • Not a needle. I'm joking about the needle. Bring me the The Ripsaw's Saw.
  • It drops when the thing goes down. Bring it whole.
  • Another time, then.
  • The Ripsaw's saw, for Tegan. You have (how many you carry).
  • Look at that. Every tooth hooked. That's what's been in my sails all these years.
  • I took three teeth for my bench, as fids for splicing. The rest Merriwether set along a cutlass edge for you. Don't tell Dunstan I let Merriwether into the loft.

docs.title: Bolt Rope and Gnawed Canvas
docs.text:
Tegan needs bolt rope from Wilmot, and the snapjaws have been gnawing the canvas stored by the Old Cut's water doors.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Tegan Level 20

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Wilmot
  • Defeat 30 Snapjaw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,908 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • +40 standing with Tegan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Player. Two things, and I only have time to say them once.
  • One: I need bolt rope from Wilmot, the heavy kind, for storm canvas. Tell him Tegan's paying full price, he'll know what that means.
  • Two: the canvas we keep in the warehouses by the Old Cut's water doors has been chewed. Snapjaws. Clear 30 of them. Then come back.
  • Full price. Tell him exactly that.
  • Another time, then.
  • Get the bolt rope from Wilmot, and clear thirty snapjaws from the Old Cut.
  • Wilmot's rope. Good. And no new tooth marks in the canvas this week.
  • Doubled seams and heavy bolt rope. That's what every captain wants now. Thank you.
  • Full price, she said? Then Tegan wants the good rope. The heavy bolt rope, laid tight. For storm canvas, I'd guess.
  • Here. Tell her it's the best I've laid this year. She'll check every inch anyway.

docs.title: Long Straight Tears
docs.text:
The sails that come back from deep water carry the same long straight tear as Cobb's net. Tegan wants proof of what makes it, from the sea half of the Old Cut.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Tegan Level 32 After A Strip of Net Leads to The Shelf of Beach Finds, A Tooth for a Needle

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Sawbill Fry in The Salt Reach
  • Bring 15 Sawbill Scale (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,073 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • +60 standing with Tegan
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Wenna's net, my sails, Maren's driftwood. One thing. And I'll wager it's come in through the Old Cut since the sea gates broke.
  • Past the Pinch the Cut runs salt all the way to the sea. The Salt Reach. The fishermen say there are fish there now that haul themselves out on the towpath on stubby fins. Long, narrow, with a bill like a plank.
  • Go down to the Salt Reach. Bring back 15 Sawbill Scales and clear 40 Sawbill Fry while you're there. If it's them, I'll know by the teeth.
  • And mind your own canvas. You've only got the one.
  • Another time, then.
  • Forty sawbill fry on the Salt Reach, and fifteen sawbill scales. You have (how many you carry).
  • Sawbills. Young ones. Look at the scale, look at the line it grew along. And the fry already have the teeth.
  • That's what tears my sails. They leap across the decks at night. Thirty years I've sewn sails and I never had a name for it. Now I do.

docs.title: The Old Race
docs.text:
Thaddeus lost the summer race by a boat's length thirty-three years ago. He wants to know whether Annis still says she would have won.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Thaddeus Level 40 After Tiller Work

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Annis

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,725 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • +40 standing with Thaddeus
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Thirty-three years. I had the helm, I led the whole way round Veligor, and in the last mile the wind dropped on me and held for Goa.
  • Annis says she'd have won. Go and ask Annis whether she still says it. I want to hear it. I like hearing it. Don't tell her that.
  • Ask her exactly. 'Would you have won?'
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Captain Annis on the docks whether she would have won the old race.
  • She said I'd have lost by two? By two!
  • Ha! She hasn't changed in thirty-three years. Neither have I. Best sailor in this harbour, that woman. Don't you dare tell her I said that.
  • Would I have won? Of course I would. He'd have lost by two boat lengths if I'd held the helm, and he knows it.
  • Tell him the wind didn't drop. He let the sheet go. Tell him I said that, exactly.

docs.title: Tiller Work
docs.text:
Thaddeus has advice for young Lowen's tiller work, and Lowen goes the long way round his bench. Carry the advice.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Thaddeus Level 33 Leads to The Old Race

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Lowen

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,337 EXP
  • 726 mesos
  • +40 standing with Thaddeus
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • That boy Lowen. Good hands, terrible tiller. He pushes when he should ease. And he goes the long way round my bench.
  • Tell him from me: ease her up before the gust, not after. And don't say it came from me. Say it came from a sailor. I am a sailor.
  • Ease her up before the gust. Remember it.
  • Another time, then.
  • Tell Lowen at the Docks what Thaddeus says about the tiller.
  • He said 'thanks'? He said 'thanks'. Ha!
  • Thirty years at sea and the finest compliment I've had this summer is a boy saying 'thanks' to a message. Sit down. I'll tell you about the race.
  • Ease her up before the gust, not after? That's... oh. That's why I keep losing way off the pier end.
  • That's from Thaddeus, isn't it. Tell him... tell him thanks. Don't tell him I said it.

docs.title: The Blightstone
docs.text:
Defeat the Blightstone at the Lakehead so the lake can heal.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Seren Level 28 After Something Grey at the Lakehead Leads to The Beds Stay Whole, The Swarming Shore

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Blightstone

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,467 EXP
  • 840 mesos
  • Elixir x3
  • +60 standing with Seren
  • +50 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • The Blightstone. That's what Hesper calls it. A golem of mossy stone and rotten wood, squatting on the lake's spring and souring it.
  • Put it down, Player. Then the slimes can go home to clean water and Merrow can sleep.
  • Defeat the Blightstone at the Lakehead. The old listening tree at the end of the third path will let you up.
  • Watch its slam. Where it lands, the ground sours.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The Blightstone. At the Lakehead.
  • It's done? The guards say the lake glows a little brighter tonight.
  • Go and tell Merrow. He'll want to hear it from you.

docs.title: The Bluecap Mother
docs.text:
The Bluecaps, the pale threads, the leaning houses: Hale thinks they all come from one place in the Deepwood. Reach the mouth of the Bluecap Hollow, at the foot of Breezy Hollow, and come back.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Hale Level 48 After Where the King Came From Leads to Follow Her Home

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the mouth of the Bluecap Hollow in Breezy Hollow

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60,000 EXP
  • 9,000 mesos
  • +60 standing with Kaldemor
  • Unlocks boss.bluecap_mother
Dialogue
  • Garrick came to me, Player. He told me about the line. For once I did not just nod. Sit down. I have been putting things side by side.
  • Clem's roots stripped from below. Bertie's houses leaning. The Bluecaps thicker every week, the pale ones round the hut, the Shrooms all crowding the same way. And the boars running out of the Deepwood ahead of all of it.
  • Wilf says there is a hollow at the foot of Breezy Hollow where the blue light is brightest. He would not go near it. He says something there is the mother of all the Bluecaps, and she has grown.
  • Go and look at the mouth of that hollow. Only look. If it is what Wilf thinks, I will take you in myself, when you are ready.
  • The foot of Breezy Hollow, past the hut, where the ground goes down. Look, and come straight back.
  • Then rest. She is not going anywhere. That is rather the trouble.
  • The mouth of the Bluecap Hollow, Player, at the foot of Breezy Hollow. Look, and come back to me.
  • A blue mushroom the size of a house. Wilf was right, then. She has fed on every Shroom that crowded toward the far side, and her brood has spread through the whole Deepwood.
  • Whenever you are ready, ask me, and I will take you to the Bluecap Hollow. Watch the red marks: they show where her threads will come up and where she will land. And no scroll will get you out of there.

docs.title: The Cart That Never Came
docs.text:
A harvest cart left Kaldemor for Bain Harbour along the Verdant Coast Road and never arrived. Walk the road and look for it in the Greenmarsh, then tell Percy, who built it, what you found.

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Tobin Level 10

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the tipped cart in the reeds in The Greenmarsh
  2. Talk to Percy

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,200 EXP
  • 900 mesos
  • White Potion x5
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • A harvest cart went out to Bain Harbour along the coast road, Player, and Bain says it never came. Two good drivers and a full load. Would you walk the Verdant Coast Road and see if you can find it? Start at the Cider Lanes, past Kaldemor Field.
  • Thank you. Look carefully in the Greenmarsh. The causeway is narrow, and a cart that slipped would end up in the reeds. If you find it, show Percy. He built it, and he will want to know.
  • I understand. I will ask Hale to send someone when he can.
  • The Greenmarsh, Player, on the coast road past the Cider Lanes. Then Percy, in the workshops.
  • Tipped in the reeds, load all over the marsh? Hm. And the wheels, did you see the wheels? Not a gouge on them. The Royal Road carts come back scored like a butcher's block, and this one has not a mark. I do not like what I cannot explain, Player. Tell the mayor I said so.
  • Tipped over in the Greenmarsh, and no sign of the drivers. And Percy found nothing on the wheels. I will not pretend I know what that means.
  • Thank you for looking, Player. Bain will hear what we know, and the coast road will have riders on it again.

docs.title: The Clock Stopped
docs.text:
The clock tower in the park has stopped. Old Ewan thinks a Shroom took its gear: hunt 20 Shrooms, then bring the gear back.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Ewan Level 4 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 20 Shroom
  2. Deliver 1 Clock Gear

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 400 EXP
  • Old Pocket Watch x1
  • +50 standing with Kaldemor
  • Sets kaldemor.clock_running
Dialogue
  • Ah, a visitor! Mind the dust. I am Ewan, keeper of this clock these forty years, and this morning it stopped.
  • The works are not broken. A gear is missing: the great gear, and I would swear a Shroom from the woods dragged it off in the night. They take anything shiny.
  • Thin out 20 Shrooms in the woods, past the hills west of the town square, and bring me my Clock Gear. One of them will have it, I am sure.
  • Thank you, Player. When the Shrooms are fewer, the gear will turn up: bring it straight here. The whole town will thank you when the bell rings again.
  • I understand, it is a long walk. The clock will be here. Not ticking, but here.
  • Twenty Shrooms first, then the gear. The woods are west of the town square, past the hills.
  • My gear! Oh, look at it, not a scratch. Give me a moment...
  • There. Do you hear that? Tick, tick, tick. Kaldemor has its time back.
  • Please take my old pocket watch. It never stopped once in forty years, and I hope it brings you luck.

docs.title: The Cloud That Didn't Move
docs.text:
Nell has shown you a page of her tally book: a grey cloud over the woods that did not move. Bring her 20 Spore Puff wisps from Stonecap Keep so she can see what it was made of.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Nell Level 52 After A Dare Leads to Up the Walls Condition Friend standing with Kaldemor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 20 Spore Puff Wisp

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 50,000 EXP
  • 3,500 mesos
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
  • +60 standing with Nell
Dialogue
  • Shh. I am counting. Twenty-one, twenty-two. There. You can talk now, Player. Actually, no, I will talk. Everyone says you are good at finding things out. I have something. But it is a secret.
  • On three evenings this summer there was a low grey cloud over the woods past the hills. It did not move with the others. It just sat there, and in the morning it was gone. I drew it as a snail, like all of them. I have not shown anybody this page. Look.
  • Meg says there are floaty grey mushrooms past the woods that puff out clouds. If you could catch 20 Spore Puff Wisps from the Spore Puffs, I could see if my cloud was made of them. Will you? And you must not tell Mayor Tobin. He will only try to guess my total again.
  • Good. Catch them in jars, they drift off otherwise. And come back before the light goes, that is when I count the evening ones.
  • That is all right. The page will keep. I will just keep counting.
  • Twenty Spore Puff Wisps, Player. From the Spore Puffs on the Keep Road and the walls. They float, so look up.
  • They do not move! Look, I tipped the jar and the wisp just stayed in the air, like my cloud did. So my cloud was all of these, thousands of them, hanging over the old keep.
  • I am going to write that next to the snail I drew. Not the number. The number is mine. But I will write what it was.
  • Thank you, Player. You are the second person who has seen that page. The first was my grandpa, and he had his glasses off.

docs.title: The Inner Ward
docs.text:
Hale wants the way through the Inner Ward of Stonecap Keep cleared before anyone goes further. Defeat 100 Wallcreeper Caps and Crowncaps, and 3 of them that are Disturbance-touched.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Hale Level 63 After The Old Wall's Marks Leads to Meg's Count

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 100 Wallcreeper Cap or Crowncaps (Wallcreeper Cap, Crowncap)
  • Defeat 3 Elite Disturbance-touched Wallcreeper Cap or Crowncaps (Wallcreeper Cap, Crowncap)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 130,000 EXP
  • 8,000 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +45 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Garrick came down off his ledge. Wilf came in from his hollow. Nell showed me a page of her book, though she made me promise not to look at the number. Everyone in Kaldemor has a piece of what is in that keep, Player, and you carried most of them home.
  • Past the walls is the inner ward, and past that a tower. The mushrooms in there are bigger, and some of them carry the same wrongness we have been seeing in the fields this year. Disturbance-touched. I want the ward cleared before anyone goes near the tower.
  • Defeat 100 of the Wallcreeper Caps and Crowncaps in the Inner Ward, and 3 of them that are Disturbance-touched. Keep your potions close and your feet moving.
  • Good. Watch the walls in there. The Wallcreepers cling to the stones, and they slow your legs when they catch you.
  • Then nobody goes past the walls until someone does. Come back when you are ready.
  • A hundred Wallcreeper Caps and Crowncaps in the Inner Ward, Player, and three of the touched ones among them.
  • A hundred, and three of the touched ones. I would have liked to see it. I would have liked even more not to have needed it.
  • There is a tower at the far end of that ward. The roots in the ward's stones all lean toward it, like grass in a wind. Whatever we are looking for is in there.
  • Rest a while, Player. And talk to Meg. She has been at the ward too, I hear, and she will want to tell you about it. She will want to tell everybody about it.

docs.title: The Keep Bounty
docs.text:
Ranger Hale pays a bounty for keeping Stonecap Keep in hand: defeat 80 monsters on the Battlements or in the Inner Ward. He will pay it again, any time.

Town Kaldemor Category Repeatable Given by Hale Level 55 After Up the Walls

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 80 Battlements or Inner Ward monsters (Spore Puff, Hoarder Shroom, Wallcreeper Cap, Crowncap)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60,000 EXP
  • 6,000 mesos

The first time you complete it instead: 90,000 EXP, 9,000 mesos, +40 standing with Kaldemor

Dialogue
  • The Keep fills up again as fast as you clear it, Player. I pay a bounty for keeping it in hand: 80 monsters on the Battlements or in the Inner Ward, Spore Puffs, Hoarder Shrooms, Wallcreeper Caps or Crowncaps. I pay again whenever you bring me another eighty. The first time is a little more.
  • Good. The walls are past the Keep Road. Count them as you go: the tracker does it for you.
  • Another time, then. The walls will wait.
  • Eighty from the Battlements or the Inner Ward, Player. Any of the four kinds count.
  • Eighty. The walls can breathe again, for a day or two.
  • Here is your bounty. Come back for another round whenever the walls fill up.

docs.title: The Knotbriar
docs.text:
A vast, deeply touched bramble is knotted round the forest's oldest root at the Hidden Spring. Cut it free.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Oriel Level 68 After Following the Root Leads to The Sap Rises

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Knotbriar

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 103,429 EXP
  • 2,040 mesos
  • Elixir x8
  • +200 standing with Oriel
  • +100 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Cut it free, Player. Every coil you cut is a home that wakes.
  • I'll be at the tree, listening. I'll know when it's done.
  • Defeat the Knotbriar at the Hidden Spring. The Spring-Root Tree at the end of the Twilit Wood will let you down.
  • Mind the whips. Mind the coils. Mind yourself.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The Knotbriar. The Hidden Spring.
  • I felt it go. Through the ground. Like a breath let out.
  • Go home ahead of me. I want to walk back slowly and listen to it.

docs.title: The Late Pedlar
docs.text:
A travelling pedlar who stops at the Sleepy Snail every summer is three weeks late, and Molly fears the Deepwood. Search the Bluecap Groves for him: defeat 60 Bluecaps and find any sign of him.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Molly Level 38 After Roots from Below Leads to Bites That Will Not Close

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 60 Bluecap
  • Deliver 1 Mott's Pack Strap

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 32,000 EXP
  • 6,000 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player, a moment. I keep a list in my apron. Travellers who promised to stop on the way back. Most I cross off by midsummer. This one I cannot.
  • Mott. Tinware and ribbons. Every summer, the same room, the same complaint about the stairs. He is three weeks late, and he is never late. He always cuts through the woods to save a day.
  • The travellers who do come in talk about the Bluecap Groves, deep in the woods, thick with blue caps. If he went that way, will you look for him? Thin out the Bluecaps, 60 of them, and bring me any sign of him at all.
  • A small round man with a pack twice his size. If he dropped anything, it will be tin, or it will be ribbon. Thank you, Player.
  • No, no. I am sure he is only late. I am sure.
  • 60 Bluecaps in the Bluecap Groves, Player, and any sign of Mott. Tin, ribbon, anything.
  • That is his strap. That buckle is one of his own, I have bought three like it. Where was it?
  • Torn off and dragged along. Not cut. Something wanted what was in the pack, not the man. So he may have dropped it and run. Mott can run, when he has to. He just complains about it.
  • I am not crossing him off. Not yet. Here, take this, and keep your eyes open past the Groves.

docs.title: Old Wall Iron
docs.text:
Gareth has seen the iron coming out of Stonecap Keep's walls. Bring him 30 pieces of Old Wall Iron from the Crowncaps of the Inner Ward, and he will forge the next tier of equipment from it.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Gareth Level 58 After Brass and Tin Leads to A Draught for the Dust

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Old Wall Iron (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 90,000 EXP
  • 6,000 mesos
  • One of: Wall Iron Helm, Wall Iron Shield
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • You are holding that sword wrong. No. Better. A little. You have been in the old keep past the woods. I can tell from the dust on your boots. That is not woods dust. That is mortar.
  • Somebody brought me a bar of iron from there last week. Old iron, from the walls. The big mushrooms in the inner ward have their roots in the stones and they pull it loose. It is better iron than I have had in years. Older than Kaldemor, and it has never been asked to do anything but hold a wall up.
  • Bring me 30 pieces of Old Wall Iron off the Crowncaps in the Inner Ward, and I will make you something worth wearing up there. Copper forgives. Iron remembers. This iron remembers a great deal.
  • Thirty. Not twenty-nine. I know how many it takes.
  • Then I will wait for someone else to bring it. I am good at waiting. So is iron.
  • Thirty pieces of Old Wall Iron, from the Crowncaps of the Inner Ward.
  • Thirty. Look at the grain in that. Whoever forged this knew their work, and they did it a very long time ago. I will not waste a single piece.
