  • It took me three nights. I did not tell Hilda I was working late, so she will have noticed. Here. Old wall iron, new shape. The next tier, for the next walls you climb.
  • Hold it properly. And come back when it is notched. I would rather mend it than make you another.

docs.title: The Old Wall's Marks
docs.text:
Lottie has heard there are masons' marks on the stones of Stonecap Keep. Copy the marks on the keep's gate and on the west and east towers of the Battlements for her notebook.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Lottie Level 61 After A Draught for the Dust Leads to The Inner Ward

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the keep's gate in The Keep Road
  • Reach the west tower in The Battlements
  • Reach the east tower in The Battlements

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 80,000 EXP
  • 5,000 mesos
  • +35 standing with Kaldemor
  • +50 standing with Lottie
Dialogue
  • Player! Have you seen my spectacles? Oh. On my head. Thank you. Now: Garrick tells me the old keep past the woods is built of cut stone, and that some of the stones have marks on them. Little marks, scratched in, all alike.
  • Those will be masons' marks. In the old days every mason had a sign of their own, and they cut it into the stones they dressed, so they would be paid for their work. The history books say the Aristocrats built forts out past the hills in the Age of Division. If those marks are theirs, I can read them.
  • Would you copy the marks for me? There should be some on the keep's gate, at the end of the Keep Road, and on the west tower and the east tower, up on the Battlements' high walk. Just a rubbing on paper will do.
  • Wonderful. Here is paper and a stub of charcoal. Rub gently, old stone flakes. And mind the mushrooms, I am told they stand in rows.
  • Another time, then. The stones have waited a long while. They can wait a little more.
  • The gate at the end of the The Keep Road, and the west and east towers on the Battlements' high walk, Player. A rubbing of each.
  • Oh, these are lovely. Look: a little key, a wheel with three spokes, and a pair of crossed hammers. Plain as a signpost. That is a mason's way of saying I cut this, pay me for it.
  • The wheel turns up in the old Aristocrat ledgers I read in Selsior. Masons who built walls for whoever paid best, a very long time ago. Nothing mysterious about them at all. I find that rather comforting.
  • I am putting them in the back of my green notebook, with your name beside them. When the children ask who built the old keep, I can tell them: three masons, and here are their signs.

docs.title: The Sap Rises
docs.text:
After the Knotbriar, the sap rises in the oldest homes, late but green. See who else felt it.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Oriel Level 69 After The Knotbriar

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Sorrel
  • Talk to Niv

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 108,019 EXP
  • 2,070 mesos
  • Heartroot Earrings x1
  • +200 standing with Oriel
  • +100 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Late, but green. Every one of the old homes. I put my hand on the root-wall this morning and it pushed back. Like a heart again.
  • The coldest room of the oldest home is still colder than I remember. I'm not done listening. But go and see Sorrel. And Niv. They'll want to tell you themselves.
  • Visit Sorrel and Niv.
  • Go on. I'll be here.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Sorrel at the school. Niv in the glade.
  • They told you, then. Good.
  • Here. Two drops of sap from the great root, hardened. The forest doesn't give these lightly, and neither do I.
  • ...The note in the wind is gone.
  • Sorrel is quiet for a long time. Whether the woods are still listening back, he does not say.
  • ...Oriel's working late again. But differently.
  • ...I'll go and sit with him. Niv smiles, very slightly, and goes.

docs.title: The Snail King
docs.text:
Ranger Hale has heard something huge in a hollow beyond the woods. Walk to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge past the hills, and tell him what you find.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Hale Level 12 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach Kaldemor Woods

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 300 EXP
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
  • Unlocks boss.snail_king
Dialogue
  • You are not the newcomer who carried shells for the mayor any more, Player. So I will tell you what I have not told the others: something huge has settled in a hollow past Kaldemor Woods. The snails do not stray that way now, and the ground shakes at night.
  • I need someone to walk out to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge beyond the hills, and tell me whether the road to it is clear. If it is, I can show you the way to the hollow myself. Will you go?
  • Good. The woods are west of the town, past the hills. Bring potions, Player: whatever sleeps out there is no snail of the meadow.
  • Wise to be sure of yourself. Come back when you are.
  • Kaldemor Woods, Player: west of the town, past the hills. Walk to it and come back to tell me it is clear.
  • You made it there and back, and you are in one piece. Then it is as I thought: the old giant snail Mano has taken the hollow, and it has called itself a king.
  • Whenever you are ready, ask me and I will take you to the Snail King's hollow. Mind the red marks on the ground: they show where it will land. And remember: no scroll will get you out of there.

docs.title: The Stretch at Dusk
docs.text:
Pell will not drive the cab past the Crossing after dark any more. Clear the Crossing so the evening run can go again: defeat 40 of its monsters.

Town Kaldemor Category Side Given by Pell Level 8

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Monster on the Crossings in The Crossing

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 900 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • You know the evening run to the capital, Player? I stopped doing it. Something ran at the cab on the Crossing a few weeks back, right out of the dark, and the horse has not forgiven me for driving on. Thin out the Crossing, 40 monsters, and I will try the dusk run again.
  • The Crossing is the hilltop past Kaldemor Woods, west of the Hills. Pigs, stumps, the lot. Do not ask me what ran at us. I did not get a good look, and I am not guessing.
  • Fair enough. The cab will keep to daylight a while longer.
  • Forty on the Crossing, Player. The hilltop with the gazebo, where the farm lanes meet the road.
  • Forty! The hilltop will be quiet for a while, then. I will take the dusk run tomorrow and see if the horse agrees.
  • Here, for your trouble. And no, I still did not see what it was. Big. Low. Fast. That is all you get.

docs.title: Old Grizzlemane
docs.text:
The ape in the Hollow Oak's crown drives everything below it down and out. And it has Juniper's notebook.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Juniper Level 46 After Before Dark Leads to Not Wrong Yet

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 80 Creature of the Hollow Oaks (Sharpened Lupin, Gloomfur Lupin, Surgeon Eye)
  2. Clear Old Grizzlemane
  3. Bring 1 Juniper's Notebook (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 32,402 EXP
  • 1,380 mesos
  • +150 standing with Juniper
  • +50 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • I've named it. Old Grizzlemane. It's been up there since before the spring, tearing the crown apart and driving everything below it down the oak and out onto the shore.
  • That's your sharpening, Kestrel's swarm, Seren's snapped spears. All of it running from one angry ape. And it has my notebook.
  • Clear the way up (80 creatures), then face Old Grizzlemane in the Torn Crown (the broken bough at the top of the Heights will show you the way) and bring back Juniper's Notebook.
  • Mind the branches. It throws them.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Old Grizzlemane. The Torn Crown. My notebook.
  • My notebook! A whole season! Look, the pages are... chewed. Mostly fine. Mostly.
  • Grizzlemane's gone. The oak will grow a new crown. Oaks are patient. Thank you, Player. Truly.

docs.title: The Wager
docs.text:
Percy and Gareth have a wager on what has been gouging the wheels on the Royal Road. Bring Percy 15 Curved Tusks from the Boarwood's boars, and let Gareth look at one first.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Percy Level 23 After What the Ledger Says Leads to The Woodcutter's Sign

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 15 Curved Tusk (taken)
  2. Talk to Gareth

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,000 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • Elixir x2
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player. Look at this felloe. Curved gouges, as if something closed on the rim and pulled. Half the wheels off the Royal Road come in like it this year, and one iron tyre bent inward. Pell's cab came in with two spokes cracked through.
  • Gareth and I have a wager on what does it. I will not tell you my guess, and he will not tell you his. But you have been in those woods past the stile. You have seen what lives there now.
  • Bring me 15 Curved Tusks from the boars. Enough to lay against every gouge in my yard. And show one to Gareth before you come back, so he cannot say I cheated.
  • The big ones carry the best tusks, I expect. Everything with a curve on it breaks in the end, but let us see what fits.
  • Well. The wheels will go on breaking whether we know why or not.
  • Fifteen Curved Tusks, Player, and show one to Gareth at the forge before you bring them here.
  • A tusk? Let me see it. Hm. Hooked, and worn sharp at the tip from rooting. Heavier than it looks.
  • Lay that against one of Percy's gouges and it will sit in it like a key in a lock. Now I know what a blade must cut, Player. I have been forging for the wrong thing all spring.
  • Tell Percy I have won. No, I will not tell you what I guessed. He would only argue.
  • Fifteen. Let me lay one here. And here. Fits every gouge in the yard. Boars, closing on the rims and pulling, and Pell's cab too, I should think. Not that Pell will say.
  • Gareth says he has won? He has not. I have. And no, Player, I will not tell you what I guessed either. A wager is a private thing.
  • Here. For your boots and your trouble. I will put the tusks on the shelf by the barrow wheel, where they can remind me who won.

docs.title: The Woodcutters' Hut
docs.text:
Past the Bluecap Groves stands the old woodcutters' hut in Breezy Hollow, and Molly thinks Mott could have taken shelter there. Reach the hut, defeat 50 Paleveil Caps around it so whoever is inside can walk out, then talk to Mott.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Molly Level 44 After Bites That Will Not Close Leads to Home Again

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach the old woodcutters' hut in Breezy Hollow
  2. Defeat 50 Paleveil Cap
  3. Talk to Mott

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 48,000 EXP
  • 8,000 mesos
  • Elixir x3
  • +60 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player, Orin was in last night, and I asked him. Past the Groves there is a quiet bit of the woods, Breezy Hollow, with an old woodcutters' hut. His father's crew built it. Four walls and a stove.
  • If Mott ran from whatever took his pack, that hut is where a sensible man would go. And Mott is sensible, under all the talking.
  • Go to the hut. If he is there, clear whatever is keeping him in, so he can walk out. Rufus says the caps out there have gone pale as milk. Will you go?
  • Through the Bluecap Groves and on. The hut is up on the high ground in Breezy Hollow. Tell him his room is aired.
  • No. No, it is a long way. I will wait a little longer.
  • The woodcutters' hut in Breezy Hollow, Player. Find it, clear the 50 Paleveil Caps around it, and talk to Mott if he is there.
  • Player! You knocked. A Paleveil Cap does not knock. I knew it was a person before I opened the door, and then I opened it a crack, and then I opened it a bit more.
  • Three weeks in that hut. The Shrooms took my pack, all the tin, every ribbon but the one I was wearing, and the pale ones came round the hut like a fence. And I was not alone, look: a lamb with a bent ear wandered in the first week, and a cat came after him as if she owned the place.
  • The lamb is speckled. Very forgiving. The cat is called, I believe, Mistress Whiskers, because she told me so, by not answering to anything else.
  • Now the caps are cleared, the three of us can walk out. I will bring them home, and then Molly's, the stairs, the room. Tell her I am coming. Tell her I am coming slowly.
  • He is coming? With a lamb and a cat? Of course he is. Of course he is coming with a lamb and a cat. Only Mott.
  • I am crossing nothing off until he is through that door, but I am airing the room. Thank you, Player. Truly. Here.

docs.title: The Woodcutter's Sign
docs.text:
Forty years ago Orin cut his sign into a great old oak in the woods, the finest tree he left standing. Find it in the deep Boarwood and come back to tell him whether it still stands.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Orin Level 24 After The Wager Leads to Thinning the Herd

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: 1. Reach Orin's oak in The Deep Boarwood

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,000 EXP
  • 2,000 mesos
  • Hunter's Bento x5
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • They tell me the old woods past the stile are all churned to mud now, Player. Boars. Forty winters I felled trees in there, and never saw so much as a piglet.
  • Forty years ago I cut my sign into a great old oak in the deep part of those woods. The finest tree I ever left standing. My father would have had it down for the timber. I could not do it.
  • My back will not take me there now. Would you go and see if my oak still stands? You will know it: the biggest tree in the deep Boarwood, with my sign cut into the bark about as high as my shoulder.
  • Go through the Boarwood and on into the deeper part. Mind the big boars. And do not tell Wren where you are going: she will say I sent you to fetch my youth.
  • No matter. It has stood forty years without me looking at it.
  • The great oak in The Deep Boarwood, Player. The biggest tree there, with my sign cut into the bark.
  • It stands? Mud all round it, you say, and the bark scored low where the boars rub, but it stands. And my sign is still on it.
  • Ha! Forty years. That tree will see me out, and Hob too, I should think. Wren, did you hear? My oak still stands.
  • She did not hear. Never mind. Take these, Player. Wren packs them for me and I never eat them all.

docs.title: A Dark Ridge
docs.text:
Theobald wants a ridge on the downs with no city lamps, for his students and his glass. The bees will have to go first.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Theobald Level 21 Leads to Jasper's Lens

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 25 Wild Bee in Downs Edge
  2. Reach the high ridge in Downs Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,220 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Theobald
Dialogue
  • The city has too many lamps. Lovely for walking home. Terrible for stars.
  • On the downs there is a ridge. No lamps, wide sky. I would take my students up, but there are bees, and my students are mostly good at tea.
  • Clear 25 Wild Bees on Downs Edge, then stand on the high ridge and tell me how much sky there is.
  • Look up while you are there. Everyone forgets to look up.
  • Of course, of course. Some other night. There are a great many nights.
  • Downs Edge. Bees first, then the ridge. Look up!
  • All of it? Horizon to horizon? Oh, that is very good news.
  • Here. And thank you. Did you look up? Good. Then it was worth it.

docs.title: Jasper's Lens
docs.text:
Jasper the curio dealer has saved Theobald a lens. Fetch it, and try it from the highest point on the downs.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Theobald Level 25 After A Dark Ridge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Jasper
  2. Reach the top of the hive banks in The Chalk Hives

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,690 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Theobald
Dialogue
  • Jasper has a lens for me. He says it is ground glass from Urbanograd, and he says it every time, and he is right about a third of the time.
  • I would go myself, but it is daylight. I do not do well in daylight.
  • Fetch the lens from Jasper at the Crown Market, then hold it up from the top of the hive banks on The Chalk Hives. Tell me if the far ridge comes clear.
  • Hold it by the rim. Never by the glass. Never.
  • Mm. Jasper will keep it. He always does.
  • Jasper first, then the top of The Chalk Hives.
  • The far ridge came clear? Every stone? Then it is a good one. Oh, Jasper.
  • It goes in the telescope, third from the end. The stars are about to come a little nearer, Player.
  • For Theobald? Of course, of course. Ground glass, Urbanograd, I'd swear to it. Mostly.
  • Tell him to try it from somewhere high, and tell him I'll want an hour of talk about it next week. He'll know.

docs.title: A Discrepancy
docs.text:
Thessaly's ledger and Ilwen's minutes disagree about one promise. Thessaly does not tolerate disagreement in records.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Thessaly Level 18 Leads to The Promise to the Gardens

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Talk to Ilwen
  • Talk to Briony

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,400 EXP
  • 396 mesos
  • +100 standing with Thessaly
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • My ledger says the Council promised the Herb Gardens a new well on the twelfth of spring. Ilwen's minutes say the thirteenth. One of us is wrong. It is not me.
  • Find out why.
  • Ask Ilwen about his minutes, and Briony, who proposed the well.
  • Precisely, please.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Ilwen, then Briony.
  • Briony proposed it at midnight, between the twelfth and the thirteenth. Over tea. Of course she did.
  • Both dates are correct. I shall write a note in the margin. I dislike margins.
  • The thirteenth. Page forty-one. I wrote it down the morning after the meeting.
  • ...The meeting ran rather late, now that I think of it.
  • The well? I proposed it at the stroke of midnight, dear. Thessaly was so tired she wrote it down on the wrong side of it.
  • Don't tell her I said so. Well. Do.

docs.title: The Promise to the Gardens
docs.text:
The Council promised the Herb Gardens a new well, and Thessaly means to see it kept. The well needs stone, and the stone is on the roads.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Thessaly Level 24 After A Discrepancy, Past the Last Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Gather 6 Copper Ore
  • Defeat 50 Creature of Shimmerwaters (Firefly Slime, Shimmer Slime, Water Sprite, Forest Sprite)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,260 EXP
  • 528 mesos
  • +120 standing with Thessaly
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Hesper
Dialogue
  • The well for the Herb Gardens. Promised. Dated. Twice, apparently. Not yet kept.
  • The mason needs copper for the pump and the path to Shimmerwater cleared for the stone carts. I will not have a promise sit in my ledger unkept.
  • Mine 6 Copper Ore for the pump and clear 50 creatures from the Shimmerwater paths for the stone carts.
  • I will be counting.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Copper and the carts' road.
  • The well is dug. Hesper has already complained about where.
  • Thessaly draws a neat line through the entry. 'Kept,' she says, with deep satisfaction.

docs.title: Thimble feathers for a small hat
Feathers for a Small Hat
docs.text:
Thimble has secretly kept the grandee hat's trimmings in case a smaller hat is ever wanted. A small hat deserves better feathers: the duskhawks of the downs have the right ones. Tell nobody, especially Sprout.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Thimble Level 52 After The Oldest Jacket

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Duskhawk Feather (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 55,720 EXP
  • 4,620 mesos
  • +70 standing with Thimble
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Come here. Closer. Quieter. You have a trustworthy face, or at least a face that cannot sew, which is the same thing.
  • Sprout wants to play the grandee one day. For the hat. Every year he asks to touch it. And I have been keeping the trimmings from the big hat in a packet, all these years, in case a smaller one were ever wanted.
  • A hat that size wants better than trimmings. The Duskhawks on the downs have the right feathers: barred, long, a little wicked. Bring me 20 Duskhawk Feathers. And if you tell Sprout, or Dex, or anybody at all, I will hem you.
  • Not a word. I have pins, and a very long memory.
  • Mf. Forget I spoke. I never spoke. I was humming.
  • 20 Duskhawk Feathers, Player. Quietly. You have (how many you carry).
  • Oh, these are good. These are wicked feathers. The big hat will be jealous. (Thimble tucks them into the packet without another word, and her hands are not quite steady.)
  • It may be years before he is ready. It may be never. But the hat will be ready first. That is what costume makers are for. Now go away, Player, before I get sentimental, which I never do.

docs.title: The Oldest Jacket
docs.text:
Thimble keeps a scrap of every green Juna jacket she has sewn, but the very first jacket has never been found. Ask Ozzie Lantry whether any Walker paper mentions it.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Thimble Level 30 Leads to Feathers for a Small Hat

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ozzie Lantry

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,290 EXP
  • 1,800 mesos
  • +50 standing with Thimble
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Hold still. No, you are not being measured, I just like people to hold still. Mf. (Thimble talks round a mouthful of pins.) Juna wears a green jacket. Has done since the first play.
  • I have made a good many of them in thirty years, and I keep a scrap of every one sewn into my coat lining. Here, feel. But the oldest one, the very first, I have never found. Not a thread of it.
  • Ozzie Lantry has every scrap of paper the Walkers left. Ask Ozzie whether any of it mentions a green jacket: who made it, where it went. Do not tell Dina. She thinks I am sentimental. I am not. I am thorough.
  • And find his spectacles for him first, or you will be there until Walkout Day.
  • Fine. It has been lost a hundred years. It can stay lost a little longer, the wretch.
  • Ask Ozzie Lantry about the first green jacket, Player.
  • A green jacket? Juna's? Oh, now, there is a lovely question. Let me see, there is a diary here somewhere... no, that is a recipe... ah. (Ozzie reads for a long while, lips moving.)
  • Nothing, I am sorry. A great deal about the cart, and a quarrel over a goat, but not a word about the jacket. Tell Thimble I will keep looking; there is a box here I have not opened in years. Tell her not to get her hopes up, and then tell her I said it kindly.
  • Nothing. Of course nothing. It has been hiding from me for thirty years and it is very good at it.
  • Still. A box Ozzie has not opened. I am extremely patient. Mf. Hold still, Player, there is a thread on your sleeve. There. Thank you.

docs.title: Thinning the Herd
docs.text:
Hale's bounty now reaches past the woods. Defeat 60 Tuskers in the deep Boarwood and one Disturbance-touched monster, so the herd stops pushing up toward the farms.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Hale Level 26 After The Woodcutter's Sign Leads to Stilebrook Farm

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 60 Tusker
  • Defeat 1 Elite Disturbance-touched boar (Hedge Boar, Rooting Piglet, Tusker)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 12,000 EXP
  • 4,000 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Wilbur came to the gate this morning and made me say something back, Player. So here it is: my bounty used to stop at the meadow. Now it goes past the woods. Mildred has a column for it.
  • The big boars in the deep Boarwood, the Tuskers, are the ones shoving the herd up toward the farms. Defeat 60 Tuskers, and one of the strange ones too, the boars with the wrong light in them. Folk call them Disturbance-touched. Will you take it?
  • Good. The Tuskers keep to the deeper part, past the first wood. Bring potions. They hit like a loaded cart.
  • Then I will thin them myself, slowly. Come back if you change your mind.
  • Sixty Tuskers in The Deep Boarwood, Player, and one Disturbance-touched boar.
  • Sixty, and one of the touched ones. Elsie says her fence stood all last night. That is the first quiet night out there since spring.
  • Here is the bounty, and something from my own pocket. Do not tell Mildred: she will only write it down.

docs.title: A Rubbing for Bartholomew
docs.text:
Thomasin wants the golems kept off the old faces while the quarrymen look for more marks, and her rubbing shown to her mentor Bartholomew.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Thomasin Level 59 After The Mason's Mark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Quarry Golem in The Terraced Cuts
  2. Talk to Bartholomew

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 46,830 EXP
  • 1,180 mesos
  • Scroll for Helmet for DEF 60% x1
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Thomasin
Dialogue
  • The quarrymen think there may be more marks on the old faces. They will not look while the golems stand on them.
  • And I want the Master to see the rubbing. He will ask me a better question than I have.
  • Clear 40 Quarry Golems from The Terraced Cuts, then take the rubbing to Bartholomew.
  • Tell him I said nothing about what it means. He will like that.
  • Of course. The faces are dangerous. The Master is only dangerous in conversation.
  • Forty golems on The Terraced Cuts, then the Master.
  • What did he ask? "Who was the mason proud of the stone for?" Oh, that is annoying. That is a very good question.
  • Thank you, Player. I will be in the library for some time.
  • Thomasin's rubbing? Let me see. Hm. A mason who signed his stone.
  • Tell her my question: who was he proud of it for? Then tell her not to answer it before she has finished asking.

docs.title: Stone, Not Stories
docs.text:
Thomasin must lecture to the quarrymen's families, who want to know whether the golems are new. She wants real stone on the table, not a story.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Thomasin Level 51 Leads to The Mason's Mark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Quarry Rubble (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 23,950 EXP
  • 1,020 mesos
  • White Potion x5
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Thomasin
Dialogue
  • Another lecture: the quarrymen's families, this time. They want to know if the stone that stands up was always asleep, or something new.
  • Nobody knows. But I will not tell frightened people that with nothing in my hands.
  • Bring me 20 Quarry Rubble from the Rubble Golems of The Spoil Heaps. Real stone. They can hold it.
  • Thank you. A thing you can touch is worth ten things you were told.
  • Then I will lecture with empty hands, and they will fill them with stories.
  • Twenty pieces of Quarry Rubble, Player. From the golems, not the road.
  • That will do. Ordinary stone, by the look of it. Which is the interesting part.
  • They will ask me again whether the stone was asleep. I will say nobody knows, and put this in their hands.

docs.title: The Mason's Mark
docs.text:
The oldest face of the Terraced Cuts carries an Aristocrat mason's mark. Thomasin wants it copied exactly, as a rubbing, not described.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Thomasin Level 56 After Stone, Not Stories, An Impossible Dot Leads to The Adventurer's Notes, A Rubbing for Bartholomew

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the mason's mark in The Terraced Cuts

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 54,450 EXP
  • 1,680 mesos
  • Elixir x5
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Thomasin
Dialogue
  • Gervase says there are golems where his map says there should be none. And the quarrymen say the oldest face on The Terraced Cuts has a mark cut in it.
  • An Aristocrat mason's mark, they say. They also say it is a crown, a hand and a tree, depending on who is telling it.
  • Go to the mason's mark on The Terraced Cuts and take a rubbing. Paper and charcoal. Copied, not described.
  • Press hard and do not tidy anything. If a line is broken, I want it broken.
  • I understand. It has been on that face a very long time. It can wait a little longer.
  • A rubbing of the mason's mark on The Terraced Cuts. Not a drawing. Not a memory.
  • Let me see. No, hold it flat. Oh.
  • It is an Aristocrat mark, a mason's, the kind the old families cut on stone they were proud of. That much we can say. Who cut it, and why that face: nobody knows. Yet.

docs.title: Catching the Trickster
docs.text:
Thorne is going to catch whoever keeps moving his things. He wants help setting a trap, and something to do while he waits.

Town Fairy Forest Category Side Given by Thorne Level 22 After The Trick That Works Leads to The Watch Drill

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 40 Firefly Slime in Shimmerwater, the First Path
  2. Talk to Orla

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,524 EXP
  • 484 mesos
  • +60 standing with Thorne
  • +15 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +60 standing with Orla
Dialogue
  • Every night my boots move. Every night! A hand to the left. I'm going to catch them. I've a plan.
  • Step one: clear the slimes off the first path so I can hear anything sneaking. Step two: ask around the glade. Somebody knows something.
  • Clear 40 Firefly Slimes on the first Shimmerwater path, then ask around the Children's Glade, starting with Orla.
  • Ha! They won't know what hit them. Well. Nothing will hit them. I just want to know who.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Slimes first, then the glade.
  • Orla said it 'couldn't possibly say' and then giggled for a full minute? ...Hm.
  • Hm! You know, I don't think I mind. Whoever it is never takes anything. Keep the pay. I'm going to go and move Orla's things a hand to the right.
  • Who, me? Move Thorne's boots? I couldn't possibly say.
  • Orla's face does something complicated and then dissolves into giggles that go on for a full minute.

docs.title: The Watch Drill
docs.text:
Thorne runs a drill every night. It mostly involves him charging at things. He wants a partner.

Town Fairy Forest Category Repeatable Given by Thorne Level 20 After Catching the Trickster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 50 Creature past the lanternss (Firefly Slime, Shimmer Slime, Water Sprite, Forest Sprite, Evil Eye, Curse Eye, Cold Eye, Sharpened Lupin, Gloomfur Lupin, Surgeon Eye)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,041 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • +15 standing with Thorne
  • +20 standing with Fairy Forest

The first time you complete it instead: 2,081 EXP, 900 mesos, +15 standing with Thorne, +30 standing with Fairy Forest

Dialogue
  • The watch drill! Every night! You go out, I stay at the lantern, and you tell me everything you hit. It's the best drill.
  • Seren made up the 'I stay at the lantern' part.
  • Defeat 50 creatures at Shimmerwater, the High Shore or the Hollow Oak, and tell Thorne everything.
  • Everything! Every swing!
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Fifty. Tell me everything.
  • Fifty! And you hit them ALL? Here, the watch's drill pay. Same again?

docs.title: The New Hide
docs.text:
Vosk and Thrun will fit Grimhorn's hide to the great drum. Fetch Vosk to the hall, then come back to Thrun for the drum's first beat.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Thrun Level 48 After Grimhorn Leads to The Second Report

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Vosk

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 13,800 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • Drumhide Jerkin x1
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Thrun
Dialogue
  • The hide has soaked three days and it is ready. Now I need hands that know rope, and there is only one pair in Midbarium I trust with my drum. Go and fetch Vosk. Tell him it is time to keep his promise.
  • Hurry, but do not tell him to hurry. He ties slower when he is rushed, and better when he is not.
  • Ha. The hide will keep another day. Just about.
  • Fetch Vosk from the Kragvar Quarter. Then come back here.
  • There. The new hide is on, Vosk's lashings are tight, and the old hide is folded away, because you do not throw out a drum's skin. Stand there, Player. Right there, where you can feel it.
  • Listen.
  • That is a beat. That is the great drum of Midbarium, speaking again, and every family on this mountain heard it just now. They will come up the stairs asking who. I will tell them. I made you a jerkin from the trimmings; the Brenna cut it the drum's way. Wear it.
  • Time, is it? I have had the lashing cord cut and waxed for a week. Do not tell Thrun.
  • A great horned beast's hide. I did not think I would see one again. I will be up at the hall before you are. Go on, tell him I am coming, and tell him not to touch the lashings.

docs.title: The Split Drum
docs.text:
The great drum's hide has split and only a great horned beast's hide could replace it. Thrun asks only that Vosk check the drum's stand.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Thrun Completed with Vosk Level 37 After A Message for the Old One Leads to Wide Tracks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,400 EXP
  • 740 mesos
  • Goat's Milk x10
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Thrun
Dialogue
  • Player! Come and hear this. No, closer. Listen. Hear that? That is not a beat, that is a mutter. Forty-five years I have drummed for the families and my drum mutters at me.
  • The hide split across its face at the first feast this spring. I patched it, but a patch on a drum is a lie and everyone in the hall can hear it. The old hide came from a great horned plateau beast in my grandfather's time. Nobody has brought one home in years, and the few seen out there are wild.
  • I will not ask anyone to go and hunt one. I will not. But do me a small kindness: ask Vosk to come and look at the stand. Perhaps, just perhaps, it is the stand that mutters and not the hide.
  • Vosk is in the Kragvar Quarter, glaring at a rope. Tell him his old friend needs him.
  • Ha! Fair enough. The drum will mutter on, and so will I.
  • Ask Vosk to come and look at the drum's stand. He is in the Kragvar Quarter.
  • The stand? I rebuilt that stand when Thrun and I were young, and I check its lashings before every feast. It does not mutter. The stand is the soundest thing in the Great Hall.
  • It is the hide, and Thrun knows it. He just wants it to be anything else. He will not ask anyone to go after one of those beasts, and I will not either. But I promised him that if a hide ever comes, I will help him fit it. That promise stands.

docs.title: A Bounty Alone
docs.text:
Thurstan took a bounty on a Disturbance-touched golem on the Terraced Cuts, and for once Constance refused to come: she wants them watched, not killed. Help him finish it.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Thurstan Level 51 After Watch, Don't Kill Leads to The Quarry Village, The Rival at the Gate

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Elite Elite golem in The Terraced Cuts

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 41,230 EXP
  • 1,020 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Thurstan
Dialogue
  • Player! Perfect. I've a bounty on a touched golem up on the The Terraced Cuts. A big one. And Constance won't come. She says she's watching them now. Watching!
  • I'm not saying I can't do it alone. I'm saying it'd go faster with two. Find the Elite golem on the Terraced Cuts and put it down. I'll split the bounty. Mostly.
  • Great! Charge first, plan... you know the rest.
  • Fine. I'll do it myself. Probably. Eventually.
  • The Elite golem on the Terraced Cuts. One. A big one.
  • Down? Properly down? Ha! Wait till I tell the old man.
  • (He hesitates.) Don't tell Constance I said it'd go faster with two. Here, the bounty. Your half. Your bigger half.

docs.title: Thurstan the rival at the gate
The Rival at the Gate
docs.text:
Someone has been taking the quarry bounties off the gate board before Thurstan gets there. He wants to beat them to the Spoil Heaps, and asks Roland to judge who did more.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Thurstan Level 54 After A Bounty Alone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 50 Rubble Golem in The Spoil Heaps
  2. Talk to Roland

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 29,940 EXP
  • 1,080 mesos
  • White Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Thurstan
Dialogue
  • Three mornings running, the quarry bounties are gone off the gate board before I'm out of bed. Someone's out there taking my golems!
  • Well, not today. Go up to the The Spoil Heaps with me and clear 50 Rubble Golems before they can. Then tell the old man, Roland. He'll say who's the better adventurer. He'll say me. Probably.
  • Up early, then! Earlier than them, whoever they are.
  • Then I'll lose another morning to whoever it is. Grr.
  • Fifty rubble golems on the Spoil Heaps, then tell Roland.
  • The old man said what? That a good adventurer doesn't care who takes the bounty, only that the road gets cleared? (He scowls.) ...He's right. Don't tell him.
  • Here. Your share. And thanks, Player. I'll get up earlier tomorrow anyway.
  • Somebody's beating the boy to the board, is it? Good. Keeps him humble. Somebody has to.
  • Tell him a good adventurer cares that the road's cleared, not whose name's on the bounty. And tell him I'm proud of him. No. Don't tell him that last bit.

docs.title: A Basket for Lettice
docs.text:
Tibb has caught one more mouse, from the very top of the flies, for Lettice's count. He would like it delivered with a message he has not quite worked out.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Tibb Level 24 After The Wall Under the Stage, Hold the Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Lettice

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,370 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Tibb
Dialogue
  • Caught one. Top of the flies, above the fourth batten. Highest a mouse has ever been in this theatre.
  • It's for Lettice. For the count. I'd take it, but there's a rehearsal, and Rosamund and Percival are both in the building.
  • Take the basket to Lettice in the Old Quarter. And tell her... something. You'll think of something.
  • Not too much. Not too little. You know.
  • Then the mouse stays with me. We'll get on.
  • The basket, Lettice, something. Not too much.
  • She said that? She laughed, and then she said that?
  • ...Right. I'll be up in the flies. Thinking. Don't follow me.
  • Another one? From the top of the flies? He brings me mice like other men bring flowers.
  • Tell him that's the highest one yet, and that I'm counting. Tell him I'm counting more than mice. He can work that out.

docs.title: Tibb's Bounty: Under the Row
docs.text:
Tibb pays from his own pocket for every drain monster kept away from the Gilded Stage's cellar. Repeatable.

Town Selsior Category Repeatable Given by Tibb Level 24 After The Wall Under the Stage

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Drain monsters (Drain Rat, Drain Stirge, Black Drain Rat)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,200 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +30 standing with Tibb
Dialogue
  • Every one you put down there is one that isn't coming up through my cellar. I pay for that. Out of my own pocket.
  • Not much. But steady.
  • Clear 40 rats or stirges in the drains under the Row. Come back, get paid. Do it again if you like.
  • Good. Mind the square board on your way out.
  • Suit yourself. They'll still be there.
  • Forty, down below. I'll be counting.
  • Forty. Lovely. Here you go.
  • Same again whenever you like. The drains never run out of them, more's the pity.

docs.title: Tibb the wall under the stage
The Wall Under the Stage
docs.text:
The mice have fled the Gilded Stage's under-stage for the flies. Lettice asked which cellar wall is nearest the old drains. Tibb wants it looked at from the other side.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Tibb Level 21 After The Pushed-Up Grating Leads to A Basket for Lettice, Tibb's Bounty: Under the Row

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the wall under the Gilded Stage in The Old Drains
  2. Defeat 30 Drain Stirge in The Old Drains

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,210 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Tibb
Dialogue
  • No mice under the stage. All up in the flies, as high as they can get. Mice don't climb for fun.
  • Lettice asked which cellar wall's nearest the old drains. I told her. She stopped laughing. I don't like it when she stops laughing.
  • Go down into The Old Drains, find the wall under the Gilded Stage and look at it from that side. Clear 30 Drain Stirges while you're there.
  • Take a lantern. And don't tie anything to anything. Trust me.
  • Fine. I'll go. I'll hate it. You'll hear about it.
  • The Old Drains. The wall under the Stage, and the stirges.
  • Scratches on the drain side, low down, and the stirges thick as smoke. Right.
  • I'll move the props off the cellar floor. Here. And thanks. I mean it, which I don't usually.

docs.title: Beat the Record
docs.text:
Tick means to beat Kite's record from the Gate Walk to the Great Hall, running by the streets instead of the roofs. He wants to know what Kite says about that. Ask Kite.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Tick Level 22

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Kite

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 920 EXP
  • 1,320 mesos
  • +40 standing with Tick
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player! Salute! Do you know Kite? The rooftop runner? Kite has the record from the Gate Walk to the Great Hall, over the roofs. Cobble keeps it written on the back of his shop door.
  • I am going to beat it. By the streets! I know every stair and alley and the shortcut behind the Night Market where the fish smell is. Everybody says it is impossible. I write down their names, so I know who to tell when I do it.
  • Will you ask Kite what Kite thinks? Up on the Rooftops. I want to know before I start training properly. I want Kite to know I am coming.
  • Thank you! Kite is fast; you might have to wait for Kite to land. Ask exactly: can it be done by the streets?
  • That is all right. I will ask Kite myself. When I catch Kite. Which is the problem.
  • Ask Kite on the Rooftops: can the record be beaten by the streets?
  • By the streets? Ha! The streets go round things. The roofs go over them. I go over them faster than anyone alive, and I did it twice more since last summer, so the number on Cobble's door keeps getting smaller.
  • Tell Tick it is impossible. Tell Tick I said so, personally. And tell Tick I salute back. Not that I have ever seen Tick standing still long enough to salute.
  • Kite said impossible? Personally? Yes! YES! Hold on. Notebook. Back page. The list.
  • "People Who Say It Is Impossible." Da. Hatch, twice. Brindle, but kindly. Patch, but rudely. Dagny, then she said maybe. And now: Kite. In capitals. Underlined.
  • And Kite salutes back! That is going in the other book too. Thank you, Player. When I beat it, you will be the second to know. Kite first. That is only fair.

docs.title: Proof for the Notebook
docs.text:
A traveler told Tick about a ford whose water ran backwards for an evening, and the pool octopi at the Halfway Stone have been crawling out of their pools ever since. Tick wants proof, one way or the other: defeat 25 pool octopi and tell him what you saw.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Tick Level 15

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 25 Pool Octopus

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,450 EXP
  • 750 mesos
  • +40 standing with Tick
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player! Sir! I mean, hello! Can I read you something? It is from volume two. Page forty-one. A carter told it me and I wrote it down exactly.
  • "At the ford below the Halfway Stone the water ran backwards for a whole evening, uphill, and the octopi came out of the drainage pools and sat on the bank and watched it." That is what he said. Then he asked for his supper.
  • Da says it is nonsense. Hatch says he has never seen water run uphill, and he has seen everything. But the Pool Octopuses really are out of the pools now. Everyone says so.
  • Will you go and look? Defeat 25 Pool Octopuses at the The Halfway Stone and watch the water while you do it. Then I can write down what really happened. Proof!
  • Thank you! Watch everything! Which way the water goes, what the octopi do, if anything is odd. I will have the pencil ready.
  • Oh. All right. I will leave a space on the page. It will wait.
  • Twenty-five Pool Octopuses at the The Halfway Stone, and watch the water. Which way does it run? I need to know!
  • So the water ran downhill. The proper way. And the octopi were just octopi, only grumpier and further out of the pools than they should be. Hmm.
  • That does not prove it did not run backwards that evening. And it does not prove it did. I am writing it under the story: "Checked by Player. Water ran the right way. Octopi plenty, and cross."
  • That is how Hatch says you do it: you write down what you saw and not what you wanted. Thank you! I salute you. There.

docs.title: The Fourth Version
docs.text:
Zip's broken arm is in Tick's notebook three times, in three versions, each with a bigger monster. Now that the beast is down, Tick wants the true story: hear it from Zip and from Torvi, then bring it to him.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Tick Level 48 After Hackleback

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway
  2. Talk to Torvi Brask

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 22,980 EXP
  • 5,760 mesos
  • +60 standing with Tick
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player! You did it! Everybody says! Hatch said it and he never says anything before the second cup! I saluted you while you were gone. Three times. In case it helped.
  • Look. Volume three, pages eight, twenty and thirty-one. Zip's arm. In the first one it was a boar as big as a cart. In the second one, as big as a house. In the third, it breathed fire. I wrote them all down exactly, because you write down what people say.
  • But now there is a real one, and you saw it. So I want the true version. Hatch says that is the most important kind, and the rarest.
  • Will you ask Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway to tell it true, and then ask Torvi Brask, because Torvi was there too? Then come and tell me, and I will write it as version four.
  • Thank you! Zip first. Make her tell it slow. She goes fast when she gets to the tusks.
  • Oh. That is all right. I will keep a page empty. It is a very good page.
  • Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway first, then Torvi Brask. The true version. Slow at the tusks.
  • The true version. For Tick's book. Right. Fine. Ahem. Two days out, something big came out of the brush, and everyone reached for spears, and I ran at it. I did not have a plan. I had a borrowed sword and a lot of feelings.
  • I chased it over the stream and up a bank, and it was gone, and I ran right off the top and landed on a rock. That is it. That is the whole story. I did not even see it properly. I saw a back and a lot of bristles.
  • And you went and saw all of it, the whole beast, and you came back, because you knew when to do what. Huh. Tell Tick that is version four. Tell him I said the true one is better. It is not. But it is true.
  • Ha! Tick is writing it down true? Good. Then here is my part. I was on the wrong side of the stream. I splashed across too late. She was on the rock with her arm in two pieces, laughing and shouting about tusks.
  • And I laughed too, and said bravery was wasted on someone who could not fight. That was true. It is less true now. She learned. Not the running, yet. She stayed home from the Wallow, though, and that was the running, a little.
  • Tell Tick that. Tell him the beast was real, and the tracks were five hand-spans, and somebody went and finished it. That is a good story. It does not need fire.
  • Slower. Slower! I am writing! "The beast was real. She did not see it properly. Torvi was on the wrong side of the stream. She fell off the bank onto a rock. Torvi carried her home."
  • "Then, a year later, Player went into the Wallow and brought it down, and Zip stayed home, which Torvi says was the running, a little." Version four. The true one. It is shorter than the others. I like it best.
  • I am going to read it to Da tonight. And to Hatch, after the second cup, so he cannot pretend he is not listening. Thank you, Player! Salute!

docs.title: The Wanderer's Story
docs.text:
Tick's notebook holds the story of a frightened wanderer who sheltered in a tunnel mouth in the hills, followed it underground and came out running with a stone that would not cool. Tick thinks Brindle should hear it.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Tick Completed with Brindle Level 20 Leads to A Way In

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 870 EXP
  • +50 standing with Tick
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Player! Can I read you one? This one is not like the others. Volume three, page fifty-two. I did not know who to tell, and then I thought, you, because you go places.
  • "A wanderer came in at dusk with no pack and mud to the knees, and would not sit down. Said it had rained in the hills, and they sheltered in a tunnel mouth, an old stone one, cut square. And it went down, and on, and they followed it, because it was dry."
  • "It went under the hills for hours. It was warm. And then it came out somewhere under stone, under buildings, they could hear carts overhead. They picked up a stone off the floor and it was warm too, and it would not cool, and they ran all the way back."
  • They would not tell me their name. They sold the stone to Velvet at the Night Market the same night and left by the morning cart. Velvet still has it. She lets you hold it if you are buying something. It is still warm. I checked.
  • Carts overhead. Under buildings. Player, I think they came out under the city. I think there is a way in under the walls that does not go through the gate. And the gate is Da's job, and Brindle's.
  • Will you take the story to Brindle? Brindle listens to grown-ups more. You can say it is from my notebook. Actually, please say it is from my notebook.
  • Thank you! Brindle is by the slate. Tell it exactly. Warm tunnel, carts overhead, a stone that will not cool.
  • Oh. All right. Maybe it is nothing. It is probably nothing. I will keep it on page fifty-two.
  • Tell Brindle the wanderer's story! From my notebook. Warm tunnel, carts overhead.
  • Tick's notebook. Of course it is. Tell me again. Slowly. A square-cut tunnel mouth in the hills. Warm. Hours underground. Carts overhead. A stone that will not cool, which Velvet now sells.
  • Old Grad was an Aristocrat fortress. Fortresses had sally tunnels: ways out under the walls, for when the gate was shut. If one still runs, it is also a way in. And nobody guards it. Nobody even knew.
  • I have spent seventeen years watching one door, Player, and a ten-year-old with a pencil just told me there is another. Remind me to salute him.

docs.title: Lamp Oil
docs.text:
Tinder's fire-eating fuel smokes and stings. Lampbat wings are waxy with the oil of the lanterns they swarm; pressed, they give a clean-burning oil. Bring Tinder 20 Lampbat Wings.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Tinder Level 24 Leads to The Middle of the Square

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Lampbat Wing (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,690 EXP
  • 2,130 mesos
  • +50 standing with Tinder
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • (On stage voice:) Behold the dragon's breath! (Off stage voice, coughing:) The dragon has a cold. My fuel's gone bad. The oil-sellers are short, and what they've got smokes black and stings like nettles.
  • Lux told me something once: the lampbats that swarm the outer lanterns come away with their wings greasy from them. Press the wings and you get oil. Clean. Bright. Lux was not happy to tell me where it came from.
  • Bring me 20 Lampbat Wings, friend. The Lampbats are out in the Outworks, round the lights on the outer wall.
  • Out through the gate, then the side path off the Gate Meadows into the Outworks. Go at dusk, when the lights draw them.
  • Then the dragon keeps its cold. (Cough.) The show goes on.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Lampbat Wings. Lampbats, the Outworks, round the outer lights.
  • (Tinder presses the wings in a little screw-press, then sniffs the jar, then tips a drop on a wick, three times, of course.) Clear flame. No smoke. Oh, that's lovely.
  • Tonight the dragon breathes properly! Come and watch. From well back. Thank you, friend.

docs.title: Tinder the middle of the square
The Middle of the Square
docs.text:
Tinder wants to play one big show right in the middle of Lantern Square, the biggest in years. Ask Jinx to warm up the crowd and keep it back, and tell Ivo the first coins of the night are his.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Tinder Level 30 After Lamp Oil

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Jinx
  2. Talk to Ivo Sable

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,580 EXP
  • 3,600 mesos
  • +70 standing with Tinder
  • +20 standing with Ivo Sable
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I've had an idea, and it frightens me, which is how I know it's a good one. One show. The whole of Lantern Square. Not off to the side. Dead centre, under the first string of lanterns, on a good night when everyone's out.
  • The new oil burns clean enough for it now. But a crowd that size leans in. I need someone working the edge, keeping them back and laughing. And I need Ivo to know what's coming. He always gets the first coins of a good night. Always.
  • Ask Jinx to warm them up and hold the edge, friend. Then go to Ivo Sable under the green awning and tell him the first coins are his. I'd do it myself, but if I go round asking, I'll lose my nerve.
  • Jinx is wherever the noise is. Ivo's under the patched green awning on the edge of the square. Go on, before I check the bucket again.
  • (Visibly relieved and disappointed at once.) Another night, then. The side of the square is very nice. Very safe.
  • Jinx, to hold the crowd. Ivo, for the first coins. Then the middle of the square is mine.
  • Tinder wants ME to warm up the crowd? For the big one? In the MIDDLE? Yes! Yes yes yes. I'll juggle the bouncy ones round the edge, everyone will step back to catch them, nobody gets singed.
  • Tell Tinder I'll keep them back a whole arm's length. Two arms. Mine are long. And tell Tinder I won't touch the torches. I promise. I'll want to. I won't.
  • The middle of the square? Well, good for her. (Ivo puts down the bandage he is rolling.) Tinder's given me the first coins of every good night since she stayed here. I've never once asked her to. I keep them in a tin for the salve-money.
  • Tell her I'll be right here under the awning with the burn salve, the same as always, and I fully expect not to need it, the same as always. And tell her to breathe out slowly. That's the singer in me talking.
  • Jinx says yes. Ivo says breathe out slowly. (Tinder checks the bucket. Once. Twice. Stops before the third, and laughs.) All right. All right. Tonight.
  • (At dusk the first string of lanterns comes on and Tinder walks out into the very middle of Lantern Square. Jinx's green balls bounce round the edge, the crowd steps back laughing, Drum finds a beat, and Tinder breathes a long gold flame straight up toward the lanterns.)
  • (Afterwards, hands still shaking:) Did you see it? Dead centre. Thank you, friend. The first coins are already in Ivo's tin.

docs.title: Tinsel a chip of warm stone
A Chip of Warm Stone
docs.text:
Tinsel wants the chip of warm stone from the Warm Quarry for the glowing-glass experiments. Bring it to the furnace on Workshops Row.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Tinsel Level 25 After The Warm Quarry

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Chip of Warm Stone

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,670 EXP
  • 1,500 mesos
  • +70 standing with Tinsel
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Leland came up from under the Great Hall talking about a quarry where the stone is warm. Warm all the way down, with no fire anywhere. I have been thinking about nothing else since. Stone that holds heat. Glass is mostly stone, you know.
  • You brought a chip of it back, didn't you, Player? Would you let me have it? Only for a while. I will be careful with it. I am careful with everything, it takes me hours to do anything.
  • Bring the Chip of Warm Stone to the furnace whenever you like. I will clear a space on the sill.
  • No, of course. You carried it up. It is yours to keep warm.
  • The Chip of Warm Stone, from the Warm Quarry. There is a space waiting on the sill.
  • It is warm. Like a cup someone just put down. Let me hold it up to the window... no. Dark all the way through. No glow. I put it in the dark cupboard, in case. Nothing.
  • I ground a little dust from one edge into a melt. The glass came out grey and ordinary. So that is one more paperweight, and this little stone goes at the end of the row on the sill.
  • It is still warm, Player. The furnace is cold behind it and it is still warm. I do not know why, and I am not going to pretend I do. Thank you. Truly.

docs.title: New Panes
docs.text:
The outer lanterns have lost their glass. Carry a crate of Tinsel's new panes from the furnace through the crowded Night Market to Lux before the outer lanterns go dark.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Tinsel Completed with Lux Level 23 After The Smashers Leads to Bite Herbs

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Moth
  2. Deliver 1 Crate of Lantern Panes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,620 EXP
  • 2,760 mesos
  • +60 standing with Tinsel
  • +30 standing with Lux
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Lux came by with a sack of broken glass and a very quiet face. Half the outer frames, empty. I have been at the pipe since noon. Look: amber, all of it. Lux will want amber.
  • The trouble is the way. Lux is out on the walls, and the shortest road from here goes straight through the Night Market at the busiest hour. I carry glass slowly. Crowds do not.
  • Would you carry this crate to Lux, Player? Ask Moth to clear you a way through the stalls first. Moth knows every corner of that market by smell.
  • Both hands. Straw on top, so do not tip it. Find Moth in the Night Market, then go on to Lux. The outer lanterns go up at dusk.
  • Then I will carry it myself, slowly, and Lux will wait in the dark, patiently. We are both good at that.
  • Moth first, in the Night Market, to clear a way. Then the Crate of Lantern Panes to Lux. Keep it level.
  • Glass? Through here? At this hour? Tinsel has a sense of humour after all. Hold still, I need to think, and I think best with my nose. Fried dough to the left, cider straight on, Crow's tonics stinking up the right.
  • Right. Ladle, swing that ladle the other way. Remy, move the fish basket a foot. There: a gap the width of one crate. Go now, before the next draw fills it.
  • Amber. Of course it is amber. And not one cracked, after the Night Market at its busiest. Moth must have parted it like a curtain.
  • Hold the ladder, Player. We can have the whole outer string lit before the lampbats wake. Tell Tinsel I said thank you. No: I will tell Tinsel myself, in the morning, with tea.

docs.title: The Newest Lens
docs.text:
Kite is laid up, and Starling needs Tinsel's newest lens tonight. Carry it up through the crowded evening streets to Starling's roof.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Tinsel Completed with Starling Level 54 After Kite Laid Up Leads to A Flicker Night

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Deliver 1 Tinsel's Newest Lens

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 16,290 EXP
  • 3,240 mesos
  • +60 standing with Tinsel
  • +30 standing with Starling
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Starling's lenses are my flawed ones. The bubble-ridden ones, the ones with a wave in them. Starling never minds. But this one... this one came out of the mould clear all the way through. I held it to the sun for an hour.
  • Kite would usually run it up. Kite is laid up with that ankle and very cross about it. And Starling wants it tonight, because Starling says tonight the sky will be clear toward the middle of the island.
  • Carry the Tinsel's Newest Lens up to Starling, Player? The streets are thick at this hour. Hold it against your chest, not in a pocket. Pockets have keys in them.
  • Starling's roof is near the Crooked Tower, between two chimney stacks with a hammock strung across. If Starling is asleep, it is still afternoon somewhere. Wake Starling anyway.
  • Then it waits on the sill with the paperweights. It will be the only thing on the sill that is not a failure.
  • The Tinsel's Newest Lens, to Starling's roof by the Crooked Tower. Against your chest, not in a pocket.
  • Oh. Oh, look at that. Tinsel finally made a clear one and gave it to me instead of selling it to someone sensible. Hold the tube steady... there. There!
  • I can see the rings on the third bright one in the Fiddle. I have never seen them before. I have been looking at that star since I was a child, Player.
  • And the east, tonight. With this I will see the horizon properly, if it does... what it does. Stay a while. Two pairs of eyes are better than one on a night like this.

docs.title: A Seventh Account
docs.text:
Mariota heard of a seventh account of the Sword Saint on a bookseller's cart, overturned at the Waystone Meadows. Ask Mariota where, then clear 30 monsters from around the waystones so Tobe's book can be fetched.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Tobe Level 13 After The Third Cut, Slowly

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Mariota
  2. Defeat 30 monsters in The Waystone Meadows

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 700 EXP
  • 260 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Tobe
Dialogue
  • My sister sent a note. A seventh account of the Sword Saint, on a bookseller's cart! The cart turned over in the meadows, and the bookseller ran.
  • Would you ask Mariota exactly where, and then clear 30 monsters on the The Waystone Meadows so the bookseller can go back for his cart? I'd go, but... my arms.
  • Thank you! Mariota will tease you about me. Just nod.
  • That's fair. Six accounts is already a lot of disagreeing.
  • Ask Mariota, then thirty on the Waystone Meadows.
  • The bookseller brought it straight here. A seventh account, and it disagrees with all six others.
  • It's wonderful. I'm taking it to Aubrey. He'll pretend to be asleep.
  • You're Tobe's adventurer? He's told me all about you, at length. The cart's by the great waystone. If the book's ruined, don't tell him till he's eaten.

docs.title: The Third Cut, Slowly
docs.text:
Tobe asks to see the third cut done on something that moves. Defeat 30 orange mushrooms on the Hedge Lanes while he watches your feet, then tell Pim what he learned.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Tobe Level 8 Leads to A Seventh Account

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Orange Mushroom in The Hedge Lanes
  2. Talk to Pim

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 200 EXP
  • 160 mesos
  • Red Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Tobe
Dialogue
  • The books describe the third cut four different ways. I thought if I watched someone do it on something that moves, not a post, I might see which book is right.
  • Would you fight 30 Orange Mushrooms on the The Hedge Lanes? Slowly, if you can. I'll watch your back foot. Then tell Pim; he says he wants to know too.
  • Thank you. I'll count. Step, strike...
  • Of course. I'll keep reading. That's what I'm good at.
  • Thirty orange mushrooms on the Hedge Lanes, then Pim.
  • None of the books were right. Your back foot turns before the cut, not after. It isn't in any of them.
  • Avice said it in five words. You showed it in thirty mushrooms. I think I might actually get it now.
  • Tobe figured out the third cut? From watching you? Ha! I knew it would be watching! Watching is my whole strategy!

docs.title: Kaldemor's Pest Watch
docs.text:
Mayor Tobin pays the town's bounty on the hills: defeat 40 of Kaldemor Hills' monsters. Every round raises Kaldemor's regard for you, and he will pay it again, any time.

Town Kaldemor Category Repeatable Given by Tobin Level 7 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 40 Hills monsters (Pig, Orange Mushroom, Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • 250 mesos
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • The pigs are in the turnips again, Player, and the mushrooms are not far behind. The town pays a standing bounty: 40 monsters of Kaldemor Hills, pigs, mushrooms or stumps, and again whenever you bring me another forty. Kaldemor does not forget who keeps its fields.
  • Good. The hills are west of the square. Your tracker keeps the count.
  • Another day, then. The pigs will still be there.
  • Forty from the hills, Player. Pigs, mushrooms and stumps all count.
  • Forty! The farmers will sleep tonight.
  • Here is the town's bounty, with its thanks. Come back whenever the hills fill up again.

docs.title: Too Bold
docs.text:
Wilf the spore gatherer will not go back into the Deepwood alone: the Hoarder Shrooms on the Humming Trail have grown too bold. Gather 15 Wild Spores from the patches there and defeat 40 Hoarder Shrooms.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Wilf Level 30 After Stilebrook Farm Leads to Shiny Things, Spores for Two

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Gather 15 Wild Spore
  • Defeat 40 Hoarder Shroom

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15,000 EXP
  • 4,000 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player. You have been past the Boarwood, they say. Then you know the woods go on. Past the boars the trees close in and the ground goes soft: that is the Deepwood, and the best wild spores in the country grow on the The Humming Trail.
  • Twenty years I have picked that trail. This summer the Shrooms follow me in threes and fours. One knocked the basket clean off my arm. They used to scatter when you clapped. Now they stare.
  • Walk the trail with me. Well. Walk it for me. Pick 15 Wild Spores from the patches there, and thin out the 40 boldest Hoarder Shrooms while you are at it. And mind where you put your feet: half the trail is spore beds.
  • Through the Boarwood and out the far side, and you are on the The Humming Trail. The patches are low and pale, under the hollow trunks. Do not stamp on them.
  • Hmph. Then the Shrooms can have the spores, and Rosa can bake without them.
  • 15 Wild Spores and 40 Hoarder Shrooms, Player. The Humming Trail, past the Boarwood. You are treading on things. I can tell from here.
  • Fifteen spores, and not one squashed. Well. Only a little squashed. And the Shrooms are thinner on the trail, I can see it in your boots.
  • Keep the spores: you picked them. Here is something for the walking. I will go back in tomorrow, early, before they are awake.

docs.title: Bethoc's Board
docs.text:
Every morning Bethoc's sighting board says the same thing: the Strandwood. Torva wants the timber crews' edge cleared.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Torva Level 20 Leads to The Night Trap

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 40 Wrack Boar
  • Defeat 30 Driftstump

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,100 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Torva
Dialogue
  • I read Bethoc's board every morning before the gulls are up. Every morning it says the Strandwood.
  • Boars rooting the weed on the shore. Driftstumps where the crews left stumps last year. They used to keep to the deep wood. Now they are at the edge, and so are the crews.
  • Clear 40 Wrack Boar and 30 Driftstump on Strandwood Edge. The track leaves the Saltwood Road, out past Gull Heath.
  • Stay where the crews can see you. That is the rule out there.
  • Then I will go alone. I usually do.
  • The Strandwood track leaves the Saltwood Road, out past Gull Heath.
  • That will keep the crews cutting for a few days. A few.
  • Every year there are more of them, and closer. I want to know why. Caddoc might, before me. Go and see him.

docs.title: Old Brushtail
docs.text:
Old Brushtail's earth lies under the roots of a fallen pine at the end of the Strandwood. Torva will take you in.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Torva Completed with Caddoc Level 28 After The Cub Leads to Lanterns to the Landings

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Old Brushtail

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 9,350 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x3
  • +60 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Torva
Dialogue
  • It is grey all round the muzzle. Old. Disturbance-touched, Elspeth would say, by the look of what it has been doing.
  • When you are ready, tell me to take you to Brushtail's Earth and we will go in.
  • Defeat Old Brushtail in its earth under the fallen pine. Ask Torva to take you there.
  • Watch the dust. It goes where the dust goes.
  • When you are ready.
  • Ask me to take you to Brushtail's Earth when you are ready.
  • You did it. Kenna is already telling it at the Gap Inn, and it has grown a tail already.
  • Go and tell Caddoc. He will say his traps worked. Let him.

docs.title: The Gapclaw
docs.text:
The first climber, the one that scarred Torva's jaw, survived its fall. It leads the others from a hollow behind the Wrack Ledges.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Torva Completed with Ruan Level 48 After What Leads Them Leads to The Greystrand

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Gapclaw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 46,000 EXP
  • 1,900 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x5
  • +60 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Torva
Dialogue
  • I know that shape. I would know it in the dark. I did know it in the dark.
  • Three winters ago we drove it off the high landing and it went over the edge. It lived. It grew. Tell me when to take you to its hollow.
  • Defeat the Gapclaw in its hollow behind the Wrack Ledges. Ask Torva to take you there.
  • When it goes up the walls, watch the floor under it.
  • It has waited three winters. It can wait.
  • Ask me to take you to the Gapclaw's hollow when you are ready.
  • It is done. It is really done.
  • They will still climb. Fewer, and less boldly. They will not stop. Go and tell Ruan and Iska. I am going to sit down.

docs.title: Torvi's Bounty: the Downs
docs.text:
The caravans that cross the Beacon Downs pay Torvi to keep the high road open, and Torvi shares the purse: defeat 60 duskhawks, downs howlers or millstone rams. Every round raises Urbanograd's regard for you, and Torvi will pay it again, any time.

Town Urbanograd Category Repeatable Given by Torvi Brask Level 50

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Downs monsters (Duskhawk, Downs Howler, Millstone Ram)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 70,560 EXP
  • 6,000 mesos
  • +40 standing with Torvi Brask
  • +30 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Up on the Downs it is like home: wind, grass, and things that want to eat the goats. The caravans pay me to keep the high road, and I would rather share the money than the walking. 60 beasts of the Downs: hawks, howlers, rams. Every time.
  • Ha! Good. Through the far end of the Bristlewood and up onto the chalk. Watch the sky at dusk.
  • Fair. The Downs are a long walk. They will be there.
  • Sixty from the Downs. Duskhawks, downs howlers and millstone rams all count.
  • Sixty! The caravan masters will grumble about paying and smile about it later. That is how city people say thank you.
  • Here is your share, and the city's thanks along with it. Come back when the Downs get crowded again.

docs.title: The Wool Carts
docs.text:
The highland wool carters are late, stuck on the rotten boardwalks of the Seepwater Foothills where the bog-lurchers have come up out of the reeds. Torvi asks you to clear 30 of them.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Torvi Brask Level 17

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Bog-Lurcher in Seepwater Foothills

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,820 EXP
  • 1,020 mesos
  • +40 standing with Torvi Brask
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Ha! You. You have the look of someone who does not mind mud. Good. The wool carts are late. They bring word from my homestead, and cheese, and this season they bring neither.
  • The carters say the Bog-Lurchers have come up onto the boardwalks in the Seepwater Foothills. Big lumps of walking mud. A cart wheel goes through a plank, a lurcher sits on the cart, and that is the afternoon gone.
  • I would go, but I have a caravan to Selsior at dawn and a student who will follow me if I go anywhere. Clear 30 Bog-Lurchers off the boardwalks. I will buy the first cup when the cheese comes.
  • Northeast from the Gate Meadows, up the pass. Step on the planks with nails in them; the others are lying.
  • Ha. Fair. Nobody in this city likes mud. I have learned this.
  • Thirty Bog-Lurchers in the Seepwater Foothills. They are slow. You will be slow too, in that mud. Keep moving.
  • HA! The carts came in at noon, every one, wool to the rails, and the old carter shouting that the boardwalks were clear as a dance floor. I told him who to thank.
  • My mother sent cheese. It smells like a goat pen in summer. I am saving you a piece; in the highlands you share the good things. Eat it outside.

docs.title: The Touched Boar
docs.text:
Disturbance-touched bristle boars charge the caravans in the Bristlewood and do not turn aside for anything. Torvi asks you to put down 2 Elite bristle boars, and will ask again, any time.

Town Urbanograd Category Repeatable Given by Torvi Brask Level 35

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 2 Elite Bristle Boar

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,480 EXP
  • 1,400 mesos
  • +40 standing with Torvi Brask
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • A boar charges, you step aside, it runs on, it forgets you. Good boar. Then there are the touched ones: they turn, and turn again, and come back. Put down 2 Disturbance-touched Bristle Boars in the Bristlewood. When they come back, so do you.
  • Good. Do not stand in front of one to see what it does. Zip did that. You know how it ended.
  • Fair. Knowing when not to fight a boar is half of fighting boar.
  • Two touched Bristle Boars. Step aside, then strike. Not the other way round.
  • Two! HA! Hulda would have stood you a cup for that.
  • The caravans pay, I pass it on, and the city hears. Come back when the woods send more.

docs.title: Zip's Bank
docs.text:
Last spring Torvi saw tracks at the top of the stream bank where Zip fell, larger than any boar's. Go back to Zip's Bank at the edge of the Reedwater Bottoms, hunting reed-lurkers on the way, and measure them.

Town Urbanograd Category Story Given by Torvi Brask Level 40 After The Lost Notes Leads to The Spark Lamp

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Reed-Lurker
  2. Reach Zip's Bank in Reedwater Bottoms: Zip's Bank

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 48,430 EXP
  • 4,800 mesos
  • +60 standing with Torvi Brask
  • +25 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Hatch says it is the same beast? Ha. Hatch would. Hatch has been right more times than I have had breakfasts. Sit. I will tell you the true version. Zip tells better ones.
  • Two days out on the road to Kaldemor, something big and tusked came out of the brush. Zip ran at it. I was on the wrong side of the stream. She went up the bank after it and off the top onto a rock, and when I got there the beast was gone. Only tracks, at the top. Bigger than any boar's. I put my hand in one. My whole hand.
  • I laughed at her, on that rock. I told her bravery was wasted on someone who could not fight. Then I carried her home. I have wondered every day since what made those tracks.
  • The bank is at the edge of the The Reedwater Bottoms. The Reed-Lurkers sit thick in the reeds on the way down; clear 30 of them, then go to the top of Zip's Bank and measure what you find there. Hand-spans. Like a highlander.
  • Good. Do not tell Zip where you are going. She will follow you. She will follow you and fall off the same bank, to make the story symmetrical.
  • Fair. It has waited a year. A bank does not go anywhere.
  • Thirty Reed-Lurkers, then the top of Zip's Bank in the Reedwater Bottoms: Zip's Bank. Measure the tracks. Hand-spans.
  • Fresh tracks. Not a year old: this month. Five hand-spans across, and deep. So it is still there, still using the bank, still crossing to the wet ground. Hatch is right. Hatch is always right. It is very tiresome.
  • That beast is why the lesser boar run onto the road, and why caravans get hit, and why my student has a crooked arm when it rains. Somebody has to go down into the Bottoms and deal with it. Not yet. Hatch will want a plan, and Hatch's plans are good.
  • And Margo has a lamp that throws sparks, and Zip has promised to test it. Ha! Go and see Margo. If Zip is going near a boar, I want someone sensible with her.

docs.title: A Night Without Lanterns
docs.text:
Tristan asks someone steady to watch the Long Reach with him through a night, without a lantern. Clear the ligators from the Reed Beds and reach his hide.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Tristan Level 30 Leads to Teeth for Comparing, Low Water Finds

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Reed Ligator in The Reed Beds
  • Reach Tristan's hide in The Reed Beds

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,580 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Tristan
Dialogue
  • (Quietly.) Player. I need someone steady. Not brave. Steady. To watch the Long Reach with me through a night. No lantern.
  • The The Reed Beds are on the way. Clear 30 Reed Ligators so we're not disturbed, then come to my hide at the far end of the beds. Quietly.
  • Move slowly in the reeds. Read them as you go.
  • Understood. Not everyone can sit still in the dark.
  • Thirty ligators in the Reed Beds, then my hide at the far end.
  • (Dawn. He has not moved all night.) You saw the herons? None. You saw the reeds, pressed flat to the water? Cart-wide.
  • I won't say what I think it is. I'm not sure. But now someone besides my brother has seen it. Thank you.

docs.title: Longjaw
docs.text:
The great croc Longjaw followed Bennet's fast barge into the Heron Pool. Defeat it. Bennet's talk takes you to the pool.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Tristan Level 48 After The Fast Barge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear Longjaw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 45,950 EXP
  • 960 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • Elixir x5
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Tristan
Dialogue
  • It's in the Heron Pool. The thing that pressed the reeds flat, lifted Osmund's ferry, tore Agatha's nets and gripped Lucan's man. All one beast.
  • Ask Bennet to take you to the pool. Defeat Longjaw. I'll be on the bank.
  • Watch the water where it humps. That's where it comes up.
  • Then I'll keep watching. It's what I do.
  • Defeat Longjaw in the Heron Pool. Ask Bennet to take you there.
  • (He walks the bank of the Heron Pool and stops.) A heron. Just one. Standing in the shallows like it never left.
