  • Lucan's put a wager on it already: that the river runs quiet till winter. First wager he's made since. Thank you, Player. From the whole river.

docs.title: The Truth for Lucan
docs.text:
Tristan has kept what he saw on the Long Reach from Lucan. After Osmund's crossing, he knows it is time. Stand beside him while he tells Lucan, then help keep the Undercut clear for the barges.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Tristan Level 46 After Across After Dark Leads to The Fast Barge

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Lucan
  2. Defeat 50 Undercut Croco in The Undercut

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 30,380 EXP
  • 920 mesos
  • White Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Tristan
Dialogue
  • Osmund told you. The lift under the ferry, the wake against the current. Then it's the same thing, and it travels the whole river.
  • I have to tell Lucan. I'd like you beside me when I do. After, the barges need the The Undercut clear: 50 Undercut Crocos.
  • He'll shout. Let him.
  • Then I'll go alone. Tomorrow. Or the day after.
  • Stand with me while I tell Lucan, then fifty crocos on the Undercut.
  • Lucan hasn't made a wager since. Not one. The bargehands say he's ill.
  • He's not ill. He's listening. Thank you for standing there. And for the Undercut.
  • (Tristan speaks for a long time, for him. Lucan says nothing at all, which no one has ever seen.)
  • ...Something as long as a barge. Following my barges. (He lets out a breath.) No wager on that. Not a copper. Tell me what we do, Tristan, and we'll do it.

docs.title: To See It Once
docs.text:
Tristram wants to see the thing in the deep water once, with his own eyes, not to kill it. Go with him at night to the rim of the Lantern Deep.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Tristram Level 67 After The Ledge She Was Reaching For Leads to The Deep Lantern

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the rim of the Lantern Deep at night in The Rim
  2. Defeat 60 monsters in The Rim

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 98,971 EXP
  • 2,010 mesos
  • +60 standing with Tristram
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Go with me tonight. To the Rim, in the wood. The edge of the sea-hole.
  • I want to see it once. That's all. Keep the shades off while I look. Sixty should do.
  • Patience.
  • Another time, then.
  • Go with Tristram to the rim of the Lantern Deep at night, and hold off sixty of what comes.
  • It rose. Among its lights. Long as a ship. Its eyes.
  • I saw it. Once. That was enough. The Harbour Master should hear it from me. Tell her I'll come.

docs.title: A Touched Bootcrab
docs.text:
Tristram pays for every Disturbance-touched bootcrab put down in the Old Cut.

Town Bain Harbour Category Repeatable Given by Tristram Level 24

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Elite Bootcrab

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,778 EXP
  • 336 mesos
  • +20 standing with Bain Harbour

The first time you complete it instead: 2,668 EXP, 528 mesos, +30 standing with Tristram, +30 standing with Bain Harbour

Dialogue
  • Some of the bootcrabs aren't right. Bigger. A light in the shell. Touched, the old sailors say.
  • Put one down. A Disturbance-touched Bootcrab. I'll pay for every one.
  • Mm.
  • Another time, then.
  • A Disturbance-touched bootcrab in the Old Cut.
  • Good.
  • Again, when you see one.

docs.title: A Touched Sawbill
docs.text:
Tristram pays for every Disturbance-touched sawbill put down in the Outer Cut, and more for a deeply touched one.

Town Bain Harbour Category Repeatable Given by Tristram Level 38

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Elite Disturbance-touched sawbill (Sawbill, Spitting Sawbill, Pale Sawbill)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,901 EXP
  • 532 mesos
  • +20 standing with Bain Harbour

The first time you complete it instead: 10,351 EXP, 836 mesos, +30 standing with Tristram, +30 standing with Bain Harbour

Dialogue
  • Some of the sawbills carry a light along the flank. Touched.
  • Put one down. A Disturbance-touched sawbill. I'll pay.
  • Mm.
  • Another time, then.
  • A Disturbance-touched sawbill on the Outer Cut.
  • Good.
  • Again.

docs.title: A Touched Shade
docs.text:
Tristram pays for every Disturbance-touched creature put down in the Holm Wood.

Town Bain Harbour Category Repeatable Given by Tristram Level 57

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 1 Elite Disturbance-touched Holm Wood creature (Dusk Wolf, Whipshade, Hookshade, Glimshade)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 22,956 EXP
  • 798 mesos
  • +20 standing with Bain Harbour

The first time you complete it instead: 34,435 EXP, 1,254 mesos, +30 standing with Tristram, +30 standing with Bain Harbour

Dialogue
  • The wood's creatures carry its light. Some more than others. Touched.
  • Put one down. A Disturbance-touched creature of the Holm Wood. I'll pay.
  • Mm.
  • Another time, then.
  • A Disturbance-touched creature of the Holm Wood.
  • Good.
  • Again.

docs.title: Tully a boat of my own
Hooks for Merriwether
docs.text:
Merriwether pays well for good hooks, and wildcat claws make fine ones. Tully needs a little more for his boat.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Tully Level 15 After Pelts for the Tanner Leads to The Boat Under the Sailcloth

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Wildcat Claw (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 821 EXP
  • 330 mesos
  • +40 standing with Tully
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You know what Merriwether told me? Wildcat claws make the best fish hooks. Curved just right, and they don't rust.
  • He'll pay good coin for them. Better than the tanner. And I'm so close now, Player. A little more in the tin and I can ask Dunstan to put my name down for a boat.
  • Bring me 25 Wildcat Claws from Baysight Hill? I'll carry anything you like for a month.
  • You're a good friend. Don't tell Garrow I'm doing deals on his docks.
  • Another time, then.
  • Twenty-five wildcat claws. You've got (how many you carry).
  • Merriwether's going to be so pleased. And so am I.
  • That's it. That's the price of a boat in the tin, or near enough. Dunstan's too busy this summer. But next summer, Player. Next summer.

docs.title: Pelts for the Tanner
docs.text:
Tully knows a tanner who takes scrub wolf pelts as part-payment, and every coin goes towards his boat.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Tully Level 12 Leads to Hooks for Merriwether

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Scrub Wolf Pelt (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 428 EXP
  • 264 mesos
  • +40 standing with Tully
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • You hunting up on the downs? I've got a deal for you. Well. A deal for me, mostly.
  • There's a tanner out past Baysight who takes scrub wolf pelts instead of coin for his work, and I owe him for a sea chest. If I pay him in pelts, I keep the coin.
  • And the coin goes in the tin. For the boat. Bring me 20 Scrub Wolf Pelts? I'll split what I save with you. Fair's fair.
  • Brilliant. I'll be on the docks. Or near lunch. Probably near lunch.
  • Another time, then.
  • Twenty scrub wolf pelts. You've got (how many you carry).
  • Twenty! Look at that. That's my sea chest paid for and not a copper out of the tin.
  • Here's your half, like I said. Two thirds of a boat, me. Two thirds and a bit.

docs.title: The Boat Under the Sailcloth
docs.text:
Tully has looked at the narrow boat under a sailcloth on the beach below the Waterfront, and wants to know whose it is.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Tully Level 40 After Hooks for Merriwether

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Tristram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 14,725 EXP
  • 880 mesos
  • +40 standing with Tully
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • There's a boat on the beach below the Waterfront, under a sailcloth. Narrow. Old. Beautiful. Nobody touches it.
  • I want to know whose it is. Not to buy it. Just... someone should. Ask around for me? Start with Tristram. He looks at it sometimes.
  • I'd never buy someone's boat. Just looking.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Tristram on the docks whose boat lies under the sailcloth.
  • His father's? The Patience. And he hunted from her alone, all those years.
  • Then I'll not look at her like that again. A boat like that waits for someone. Good to know who.
  • The Patience. My father's. Then mine.
  • Tell him he can look. She likes being looked at. Just not sailed. Not yet.

docs.title: By the Fire
docs.text:
Ulm wants someone to sit up by the council fire with him tonight. What he says there, he will not say in council: carry it to Hask.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Ulm Completed with Hask Level 60 After Wood for the Fire

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 26,500 EXP
  • 1,200 mesos
  • Travel Ration x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ulm
Dialogue
  • Sit. No, closer, the fire won't bite you. The council's gone home and the Old One's gone to bed early for once. I've kept this fire forty years, and there's a thing I've wanted to say all summer to somebody who will carry it.
  • The Kragvar cut wood alone this year, because the watch has nobody to spare to walk with them. Vosk sends no young ones onto the bridge alone. Every family is carrying its trouble on its own back and calling it pride.
  • I'm the keeper of the fire; I don't speak in council, I keep it warm. You tell Hask. Tell him the Kragvar would walk the trail beside the Uskari tomorrow if they were asked, and that my son will never be the one to ask.
  • He'll be up before dawn. He always is, after a council. Go gently; he worries more than he shows.
  • Then the fire heard it, and that's something. It's heard worse.
  • Tell Hask what I said by the fire. The Kragvar would walk, if they were asked.
  • You sat up with Ulm. I can tell: you smell of his woodsmoke, and you have the look of someone carrying something heavy.
  • The Kragvar would walk, if they were asked, and Dorrek will never ask. In all the years I have sat with Ulm, he has never once said a word to me about the council.
  • Thank you, Player. I will keep this until I can use it, and then I will use it well. Take these, and go and sleep.

docs.title: Wood for the Fire
docs.text:
Ulm has kept the council fire for forty years and never let it burn low. Bring him 30 Dark Bark from the ridges, which burns slow and hot.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Ulm Level 21 Leads to By the Fire

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 30 Dark Bark (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,400 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • Travel Ration x5
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Ulm
Dialogue
  • Mind your feet. That is the council fire, and it has not gone out in forty years, not on my watch and not on any keeper's before me.
  • Brakka brings me wood, when she remembers. She has a stairway in her head and not much room left for an old man's woodpile. The pile is low. The fire does not know that yet, and I mean to keep it that way.
  • The dark stumps up on the ridges carry a bark that burns slow and hot all night. Bring me 30 Dark Bark.
  • Good. Hmph. Do not bring it wet.
  • Then I will burn the stool you would have sat on. Go on.
  • Thirty Dark Bark. You have (how many you carry). The fire is waiting.
  • Black, dry and split clean. That will see me through the next council, and the council always runs long.
  • Take these. And sit by the fire a moment before you go. It likes company. So do I, though you will not hear me say so twice.

docs.title: Edges for the Anvil
docs.text:
The Anvil blunts Ulric's chisels faster than he can sharpen them. Bring him 20 Newt Hides for a strop, and take his word to Gorm about his mallet grip.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Ulric Level 38 Leads to The Hardest Step

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Bring 20 Sea Newt Hide (taken)
  2. Talk to Gorm

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,500 EXP
  • 1,500 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Tonic x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Ulric
Dialogue
  • Ah. Player. The Anvil. That is what the crews call the rock where the far cove stair cracked. They are right. It eats an edge an hour.
  • A good strop brings an edge back. Newt hide makes the best. Tough, and a little oily. Bring me 20 Sea Newt Hide, from the Sea Newts of the Saltface. And on your way, tell Gorm his grip is wrong again. He will know.
  • No hurry. The stone has waited a long time. It can wait for you.
  • Another day, then. The Anvil is not going anywhere. Nor am I. Not yet.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Sea Newt Hide. Good. Slowly. And Gorm. Do not forget Gorm.
  • My grip? He said my grip? He watched me from his bench, then. Thirty-three years and he still watches me cut.
  • Tell him thank you. No. Tell him I know. He will hear the thank you in it. He always does.
  • Hide. And Gorm's answer. He said he knew? Yes. That is what he says when he means thank you.
  • Here. For your trouble. Come by the bench some evening. I sharpen the chisels in the last of the light. It is a good time to sit, and not say much.

docs.title: The Hardest Step
docs.text:
Ulric is cutting the last of the Anvil, where the far cove stair runs closest to the water. Keep the Wrack Ledges below him quiet through his long day's work: defeat 80 monsters there.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Ulric Level 48 After Edges for the Anvil, Below the Anvil

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 80 monsters in The Wrack Ledges

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,500 EXP
  • 1,900 mesos
  • Cliff-Runner Boots x1
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Ulric
Dialogue
  • The last of the Anvil is the worst of it. Low down, where the stair runs closest to the water. The crews will not stand there. I do not blame them.
  • I cut by daylight. Only daylight. But the day is long, and the ledges below are busy. Gulls. And worse.
  • Stand below me through the day, Player. Keep The Wrack Ledges quiet. 80 of whatever comes up, I would think. Then come to the bench and tell me it is done. I will know already. I will have heard.
  • Good. I start at first light. Slowly. You will hear the chisel. When you cannot hear it, come and look.
  • Then I will wait. I have waited on stone before. It is better at waiting than I am. Not by much.
  • The Wrack Ledges. Eighty, I think. Listen for the chisel.
  • Done. The hardest step on the far cove stair. I carved a seal into it, looking out at the cove. Seals like to watch the boats go out. So will the town.
  • Fionn says my animals are for luck. Gorm says they are for love. I let them both be right. If a carving has to be explained, it was carved badly.
  • These are for you. Old Struan gave me boots like them, once. They hold on a wet step. Use the steps, Player. All of them. Not only the shortcuts.

docs.title: Up the Walls
docs.text:
Garrick wants to know what can be seen from the top of Stonecap Keep. Climb to the highest point of the Battlements, the old lookout over the first wall.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Garrick Level 54 After The Cloud That Didn't Move Leads to Shiny Things, Found, The Keep Bounty

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the lookout on the Battlements in The Battlements

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 45,000 EXP
  • 3,500 mesos
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Fine view from up here. Fine view. But not fine enough, Player. From my ledge I saw the line of broken trees. From Breezy Hollow we saw where it began. There is one more place to stand, and it is taller than both.
  • That old keep past the Deepwood has walls, and walls have tops. On the first stretch of the Battlements there is a stair up to a lookout. Whoever built that place wanted to see a long way.
  • Climb to the lookout on the Battlements, the highest point of the walls, and look around. Then come back and tell me what you saw. Up is just a direction.
  • Bend your knees, look up, and let go. The stair is narrow, so take it one step at a time.
  • The walls will still be tall tomorrow.
  • The lookout on the first stretch of the The Battlements, Player. Climb the narrow stair to the top.
  • Well? You saw it, I can tell. The Keep under your feet, the Deepwood spread out below, the line of broken trees cutting through it, and the hollow at the far end where old Mano settled. All of it, in one look.
  • It is a chain. Something in that keep pushed the woods, and the woods pushed the boars, and the boars pushed the old snail out toward the meadow. Hale guessed some of it. Now we have seen it.
  • I like a view that explains itself. Here, for your trouble. Tell Hale I said the top of the wall is a fine place to think.

docs.title: Scrap and the Roads
docs.text:
Scrap has started asking about the roads, and Vane cannot test a road by jumping on it. Ask Shade at the Gate Walk what Scrap is really learning.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Vane Level 44 After Short of Timber

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Shade

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 7,100 EXP
  • 2,640 mesos
  • +60 standing with Vane
  • +20 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Scrap asked me last night how far it is to the Halfway Stone. Just like that, over supper. Nine years old, and asking about the road.
  • I build bridges so people can cross the gaps without falling. Every one of them, I have jumped on first. But I cannot jump on the road for her. I cannot test that.
  • Shade has taken Scrap under a wing, a little. Ask Shade, for me, what Scrap is really learning down by the gate. I do not want the polite answer.
  • Shade is on the Gate Walk, usually by the gate with travelers. Do not let Scrap see you go. She will follow you, and then deny it.
  • No. Maybe I do not want to know yet, either.
  • Ask Shade on the Gate Walk what Scrap is learning, Player.
  • Vane wants to know? Fair.
  • Scrap is learning to fall. From a low wall, into a roll, and up again. It is the first thing anybody should learn and the last thing anybody does. Tell Vane: she falls well now. Better than I did.
  • Learning to fall. (Vane is quiet for a long moment.) That is what I would have taught her. That is exactly what I would have taught her.
  • All right. All right. If she must go out one day, she will go out knowing how to land. I can live with that. I will have to. Thank you, Player.

docs.title: Short of Timber
docs.text:
Timber is scarce, so Vane binds the rooftop bridges with soaked bark instead. The Gutter Queen needs new strapping before the autumn winds: bring mossy bark from the Bristlewood's barkbacks.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Vane Level 34 Leads to Scrap and the Roads

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 25 Mossy Bark (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 30,550 EXP
  • 4,250 mesos
  • +50 standing with Vane
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Hold on. (Vane jumps twice on the plank, hard.) There. Good plank. This one is the Gutter Queen, Player, and she is old, and she wants new strapping before the autumn winds.
  • Timber does not come up the roads like it used to, and what does come goes to beams. So I bind the bridges with bark instead. Thick mossy bark from the Bristlewood, soaked and strapped tight, holds a plank like a fist.
  • The barkbacks in the Bristlewood wear the best of it. Bring me 25 Mossy Bark, and the Gutter Queen sees another winter.
  • The barkbacks are in the woods past the Outworks. They look like stumps until they do not.
  • Then I tie her up with rope and hope. Rope and hope. Not my favourite pair.
  • 25 Mossy Bark, Player. You have (how many you carry). Barkbacks, in the Bristlewood.
  • Good bark. Thick, and still damp under the moss. That will soak up fine.
  • Two hundred bridges, and most of them older than me. Every one I save is one less I have to build out of nothing. Come up and jump on the Gutter Queen in a week, Player. She will not mind.

docs.title: Where the Eddy Turned
docs.text:
Varro will go out to the Forest Jaw at slack water and show you where the eddy turned, and where it turns now.

Town Goa Harbour Category Story Given by Varro Level 62 After The Verse and the Page Leads to Under the Jaw

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach The Forest Jaw
  2. Defeat 60 Jaw Crab in The Forest Jaw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 59,000 EXP
  • 2,500 mesos
  • +40 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Varro
Dialogue
  • Ailsa sent you. Aye. I did not ask her. A man does not ask a question when he knows the answer will keep him up at night.
  • Meet me at the Forest Jaw at slack water. I will show you the eddy. The crabs there have grown as big as cartwheels. You keep them off my knees.
  • Go to The Forest Jaw with Varro at slack water and keep 60 Jaw Crab off him.
  • Slack water. Do not be late.
  • Aye.
  • The Forest Jaw. Slack water.
  • There. Where the weed lies flat. That is where the eddy turned when I was twenty. Now it turns there, by the forest cliff, and it comes late.
  • Fifty-six years I have read this water. Tell Iska. She will know what to do. She always did.

docs.title: The Lee Rocks
docs.text:
Jaw Crabs have taken the lee rocks under the Forest Jaw, where pilot boats lie out of the run. Varro wants 60 of them cleared.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Varro Level 56 After Three Mornings

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 Jaw Crab in The Forest Jaw

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 36,000 EXP
  • 2,240 mesos
  • Elixir x3
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Varro
Dialogue
  • There are rocks under the Jaw, on the inside, where a pilot boat can lie out of the run and wait on a turn. We call it the lee. Every pilot in this town has sat there wet through.
  • Maili and I sat there the first summer I had a boat. She brought bread and complained about the wind the whole tide. Best day I remember.
  • Kor tells me the crabs have taken the lee. Crabs as big as a cartwheel, on the rocks where a tired boat puts in. A boat that runs in there in a hurry will have her planks stove in.
  • Get out to the Forest Jaw and clear 60 Jaw Crabs off it. My knees will not take me there. Yours will.
  • Past the Wrack Ledges, at the cliff foot. It is a walk. Take bread.
  • Then the pilots will lie off and get wet. They have before.
  • Sixty Jaw Crabs on the Forest Jaw. Don't get pinched.
  • Clear? Aye.
  • That is the first time in five years I have sent anyone out to the Jaw who did not come back complaining. Take these. And when you sit on those rocks, sit on the flat one. That one was hers.

docs.title: Three Mornings
docs.text:
Arlo has not come to the quay at dawn for three mornings. Varro wants to know why, without asking. Find Arlo, then go back to Varro.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Varro Level 50 Leads to The Lee Rocks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Arlo

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 13,000 EXP
  • 1,000 mesos
  • Steamed Crab x5
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Varro
Dialogue
  • You. You know the First Warden's boy. Arlo.
  • He has stood on my quay at dawn most mornings this half year. Three mornings now he has not come. I am not asking why. I am asking you to find out why.
  • Go and find Arlo. Don't tell him I sent you. Then come back and tell me what he says.
  • He'll be somewhere he is not supposed to be. Start there.
  • Aye. It is nothing. Forget I spoke.
  • The boy. Arlo. Don't tell him I sent you.
  • Varro sent you? He didn't. He wouldn't. ...I got five noes. Five mornings, five noes. I said what the water was doing and he said no every time. Five noes means he's given up. I'm not going back till I know the answer.
  • Five noes. And he thinks that is me giving up on him.
  • No is a lesson, Player. I gave his mother a hundred of them. Tomorrow I will stand a yard to the left, where he sees me first. If he comes, he comes.
  • Take this, for your trouble. And if he asks, you were never here.

docs.title: New Lashings
docs.text:
Twice this season Vosk has found the far canyon bridge's ropes gnawed half through. He is doubling the lashings at the anchors and needs stakes: bring him 20 Giant Firewood.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Vosk Level 26

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 20 Giant Firewood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,000 EXP
  • 520 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • Highland Salve x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Vosk
Dialogue
  • Never trust a rope you did not tie. I say it to every apprentice. I have tied every rope on the far canyon bridge, and twice this season I have found them gnawed half through by morning.
  • Gnawed, mind. Not cut. Teeth. On the side away from town. I spliced both breaks and doubled the lashings, but a doubled lashing wants a new stake, and a stake wants wood that will not split.
  • The Dark Axe Stumps on the ridges drop logs as hard as anything that grows. Bring me 20 Giant Firewood for bridge stakes.
  • Good. Long, straight ones if you can choose. I can't make a bent log into a straight stake, whatever Brakka thinks.
  • Hm. Then the old stakes hold another week, and I sleep a little less. Nothing new there.
  • Twenty Giant Firewood. You have (how many you carry).
  • Twenty logs, and straight. I will cut the stakes tonight and drive them at dawn, with Brakka holding the mallet and complaining.
  • Whatever has teeth for my ropes, it will have to work twice as hard now. I would still like to know what it is. I would like that very much.
  • Salve and potions. Not much for a load like that, but a bridge-keeper is paid in bridges. Go and walk on it sometime. Carefully.

docs.title: The Night Watch
docs.text:
Vosk will keep watch on the far canyon bridge after dark, with Brakka and with you. Hold the anchors at the Far Anchor through the night.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Vosk Level 33 After What Bites Leads to Fresh Cable

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Clear The Night Watch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 11,400 EXP
  • 660 mesos
  • Highland Salve x10
  • Rimwort Tonic x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Vosk
Dialogue
  • Gnawers. Lessa sent word. Seventy years I have tied knots, and it is rats with ideas that undo them. Well. Now I know what to watch for.
  • They come at night, from under the anchor ledge, always on the side away from town. I will not send a young one out there alone, so tonight I go myself. Brakka insists on coming, and I have stopped arguing with her.
  • Come with us. We hold the anchors till they give up or we do. When you are ready, tell me, and we go out across the bridge together.
  • Talk to me when you are ready to go. Bring something for the dark, and something for bites.
  • Then Brakka and I go alone. I would rather not, but I would rather that than leave the ropes.
  • When you are ready to go out to The Far Anchor for the night, tell me. Brakka is waiting with the lanterns.
  • Dawn, and the ropes are still whole. Brakka has not stopped talking since we crossed back. I let her. She earned it.
  • I saw where they come from now: nests right under the anchor ledge, chewed out of old cable. The ropes we have will not last another month of that. I need fresh cable, and the Trading Post is the only place it comes from.

docs.title: Wat a better hand than mine
A Better Hand Than Mine
docs.text:
Badly tied purses all over the market are being emptied by someone very good, possibly better than Wat ever was. Wat wants the warden to hear it from him first, and his brother Kenric too.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Wat Level 25 After A Message Past the Gate

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Reynold
  2. Talk to Kenric

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,700 EXP
  • 500 mesos
  • Orange Potion x15
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +130 standing with Wat
Dialogue
  • Player. Something's wrong. Every badly tied purse I've spotted this week, I go back to tell the owner, and it's already empty. Clean. No cut strings.
  • Somebody's very good. Better than I was. And if anyone remembers my face from the old days, they'll think it's me.
  • Tell Reynold what I've seen. He has to hear it from my side first. And then tell Kenric. He'll worry. He has to hear it isn't me.
  • Thanks. I'll keep watching purses. Watching, mind.
  • Fine. I'll tell them myself. ... Tomorrow. Maybe.
  • The warden first, then Kenric.
  • The warden said he never thought it was me? Not even for a minute? ... And Kenric just nodded and went back to the anvil. That's how he says it.
  • Right. Then I'll find out who it is. Here, Player. You're all right.
  • Empty purses, no cut strings, and Wat came to me first. Good. Tell him I never once thought it was him. Tell him the ledger says so, which is more than I say.
  • Wat sent you to tell me it isn't him? ... I know it isn't him. I've known for two summers. Tell him... tell him supper's at the forge, same as always.

docs.title: Wat a message past the gate
A Message Past the Gate
docs.text:
Wat has a message from the warden for the shepherds' sheepfold on Downs Edge, and his shortcuts stop at the city gate. Carry it, and clear the bees around the fold.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Wat Level 20 Leads to A Better Hand Than Mine

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the sheepfold in Downs Edge
  • Defeat 25 Wild Bee

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,200 EXP
  • 400 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Wat
Dialogue
  • Player! Errand for the warden. Message for the shepherds at the sheepfold on Downs Edge: market stall's held for their wool till Friday.
  • Thing is, I know every shortcut in the city, and not one of them goes outside it. And the bees out there sting.
  • Take this Warden's Message to the sheepfold on Downs Edge. And if the Wild Bees are bad, do 25 of them, so the shepherds can get their wool in.
  • Nice one! Don't tell the warden I got help. ... Actually, do. He likes it when I'm sensible.
  • Fine. I'll find a shortcut. There's always a shortcut.
  • The sheepfold, out on Downs Edge. And bees.
  • They got it? And the bees are fewer? Then the wool's in Friday and the warden's happy, and when he's happy he nearly smiles.
  • Here. It's honest money. I checked. Twice. Like he does.

docs.title: Welcome Home
docs.text:
Lia says the mayor wants to meet you. Go and see Tobin.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Lia Completed with Tobin Level 1 Leads to Settling In

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15 EXP
  • +10 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • There you are, Player! Mayor Tobin has been asking for you all morning. Would you go and see him? He is just west of here.
  • Wonderful! Tobin is the mayor, standing in front of the treehouse. Just walk up to him and talk.
  • No rush. If you change your mind, I am right here.
  • Mayor Tobin is waiting for you, Player. He is just to the west.
  • Ah, Player, there you are! Lia found you, then. Good. I have been meaning to talk to you.
  • Take this as a welcome gift. Come and talk to me again when you are ready for more.

docs.title: A Strip of Net
docs.text:
Wenna has kept a strip of Cobb's torn net rolled in her basket, and shown it to nobody. She lets you carry it to someone who might know what made the tear.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Wenna Level 31 Leads to Long Straight Tears, Twine for the Saltlark

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Tegan
  2. Talk to Maren

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,082 EXP
  • 930 mesos
  • +60 standing with Wenna
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Sit. Not there. That's Kenver's step. There.
  • You've been up the Old Cut. Everyone's talking about the crabs. Crabs don't do this.
  • Look. A strip of my son's net. A long straight rent, longer than my arm. Clean, but the edges are pulled. Not cut. Pulled. I've mended nets on these steps since I was five and I never saw a fish do that.
  • I've shown it to no one. Take it to Tegan in the sail loft, she knows tears. And to Maren, she keeps those things on her shelf. Then bring it back to me.
  • Bring it back. It's Cobb's net.
  • Another time, then.
  • Show the strip of net to Tegan in the sail loft and to Maren on Merchant Street.
  • Well?
  • Tegan's sails, the same tear. Maren's driftwood, the same grooves. So it's one thing doing all of it. One thing out in the deep water.
  • Good. Now I know I'm not a mad old woman. Off you go, then. Tegan will want you.
  • Give it here. Hm. Long, straight, the edges pulled out as if teeth caught and dragged. I've seen this tear before.
  • In sails. The sails that come back from deep water. Tell Wenna I'll want to talk to you myself.
  • Oh. Oh, look at that. The grooves on my driftwood are the same: long, straight, and the fibres dragged, not cut.
  • Whatever does this has teeth set in a line. Like a saw. Tell Wenna thank you for showing me.

docs.title: Twine for the Saltlark
docs.text:
The Saltlark's nets need mending before she sails deep again, and Wenna needs twine from Wilmot's rope walk.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Wenna Level 50 After A Strip of Net

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Wilmot

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 28,526 EXP
  • 1,100 mesos
  • +40 standing with Wenna
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The Saltlark sails deep again soon. Her nets need mending first. Not a strand of twine left in my basket.
  • Go to Wilmot at the rope walk. Tell him Wenna wants the good twine, and she'll know if it isn't.
  • The good twine. Tell him I'll know.
  • Another time, then.
  • Get twine for Wenna from Wilmot at the rope walk.
  • The good twine. He sent the good twine.
  • Hmph. You'll do. Sit, if you like. Not on that step. That one's Kenver's.
  • Wenna wants the good twine? Then she gets the good twine. She'd know otherwise.
  • Tell her it's laid the old way, like Penrose laid it for her mother. She'll know what that means.

docs.title: What Drove It Out
docs.text:
Hale has wondered all year what drove old Mano out of the woods. The answer is at the top of Stonecap Keep. Reach the foot of the Crown Tower at the far end of the Inner Ward.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Hale Level 68 After Meg's Count Leads to Said Out Loud

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the foot of the Crown Tower in The Inner Ward

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 120,000 EXP
  • 10,000 mesos
  • +60 standing with Kaldemor
  • Unlocks boss.cap_king
Dialogue
  • This spring I stood at the gate after dark and heard something huge settle in a hollow past the woods. I found out what it was. What I never found out is why an old snail would leave a place it had lived in longer than I have been alive.
  • The boars pushed it. Something pushed the boars. Something pushed the Bluecaps, and the Shrooms, and the cloud Nell drew. Garrick saw the whole line from the wall. It ends at a tower at the far end of the Inner Ward.
  • Go to the foot of the Crown Tower, at the far end of the The Inner Ward, and look up. Then come and tell me what is at the top. I have waited the whole summer to hear it.
  • Do not go in. Just look, and come back. I will be at the gate.
  • It has waited this long. A day more will not hurt it, or us.
  • The foot of the Crown Tower, Player, at the far end of the Inner Ward. Look up, and come back.
  • A mushroom, grown up through the great hall and out of the top of the tower. Its roots in every stone. And on its head a crown made of everything the Shrooms carried off: thimbles, ladles, buttons, half a weathervane. A Cap King.
  • It rose this spring and its roots heaved the ground, the shudder Meg felt. Its spores hung over the woods. The Shrooms ran it everything that shone. The Bluecaps crowded in after the Shrooms, the boars ran from the Bluecaps, and old Mano ran from the boars. Everything ran from the same place.
  • Then we know. Whenever you are ready, ask me and I will open the way up the Crown Tower. Jump the red lines when its roots heave, and keep moving when the hoard comes down. And remember: no scroll will get you out of there.

docs.title: What the Ledger Says
docs.text:
Mildred's ledger shows the far farms by the woods losing more this year than in any five years before. Ask Elsie why her cows will not graze the far pasture, then defeat 40 Rooting Piglets and Hedge Boars in the Boarwood.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Mildred Level 21 After A Trail Too Broad Leads to The Wager

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Elsie
  2. Defeat 40 Rooting Piglet or Hedge Boars (Rooting Piglet, Hedge Boar)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 6,000 EXP
  • 2,500 mesos
  • Blue Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player. Sit, if you can find a chair under the papers. I have been adding up the far farms' losses. Geese, hens, pumpkins, young orchard trees. More this year than in any five years before it, and all of it on the farms nearest the woods.
  • A ledger can tell me how much. It cannot tell me why. Elsie told Hale her cows will not go near the far pasture. Would you ask her what she has seen, and then see to whatever is doing it? I would like a reason to write in the margin.
  • Thank you. Elsie is at the Last Stile more often than her farmhouse these days, keeping an eye on the woods. Mind her knees, and do not mention cheese unless you mean to stay a while.
  • Then I will keep adding. The numbers do not get smaller for being left alone.
  • Talk to Elsie about her cows, Player, then thin out what comes up from the Boarwood at night: piglets and boars both.
  • The far pasture? My cows will not go near it. I drove them up twice this spring and twice they came home alone, Bluebell first, with her ears back. Cows are not fools.
  • I sat up one night to see. Boars, Player. They come up out of the woods after dark, the little ones rooting and the big ones shoving, right up to my fence. Thin them out, and tell Mildred to write that down.
  • Boars, up to Elsie's fence by night. Well. That answers the geese and the pumpkins, and very likely the young trees.
  • I have written it in the margin: "Boars, out of the Boarwood. Seen to, in part, by Player." Please take this for your trouble.

docs.title: Where the King Came From
docs.text:
Garrick saw a line of broken treetops leading toward Mano's hollow from somewhere far past the hills. He wants to see where it begins. Climb with him to the top of Breezy Hollow and look out.

Town Kaldemor Category Story Given by Garrick Level 47 After Houses That Will Not Listen Leads to The Bluecap Mother

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the top of Breezy Hollow in Breezy Hollow

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 46,000 EXP
  • 7,000 mesos
  • +50 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player. This spring, from the lookout on the hills, I saw a line in the woods. Treetops pushed apart, some fallen, like something big had walked through them. It ran toward the hollow where the Snail King sat. I told Hale. He nodded.
  • I have been up every tall thing between here and the Boarwood since. I can see where the line ends. I cannot see where it starts. It starts somewhere in the Deepwood.
  • Breezy Hollow sits high, and its top looks south over the whole wood. Climb up with me. Stand at the top and look out, and tell me what you see.
  • I will meet you up there. Climb the ropes, not the caps. At the very top, look south.
  • The line will still be there. Lines are patient.
  • The top of Breezy Hollow, Player. Stand at the edge and look out.
  • You saw it too. The line starts there, at the Deepwood's southern edge, right where the boars used to keep. It does not start deeper. It starts at the edge.
  • So the old snail did not come from the Deepwood. It was pushed out of the woods at the edge, by something running out of the Deepwood. The boars. And the boars were running from something too.
  • I will tell Hale. He will nod. But this time I think he will mean something by it. Here, for the climb.

docs.title: Wilmot a child for the wheel
A Child for the Wheel
docs.text:
Wilmot needs a child to turn the rope walk's wheel for a day, and fewer children come every year.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Wilmot Level 20

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Finch

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,908 EXP
  • 440 mesos
  • +40 standing with Wilmot
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The rope walk needs a child at the wheel. A copper a day, steady turning, and a song if they like.
  • Fewer every year. Nobody young wants to walk backwards in a shed. I don't blame them.
  • Ask Finch on the docks if he'll turn the wheel for a day. He runs everywhere; perhaps he'd like to stand still for once.
  • Tell him there's a song in it. Children like a song.
  • Another time, then.
  • Ask Finch on the docks to turn the rope walk's wheel.
  • Finch says yes! A whole day. He wants two coppers. I said yes. Don't tell Garrow.
  • Perhaps he'll like it. Perhaps not. But it's a day of rope I'd not have had.
  • Turn the wheel at Mr Wilmot's? For a whole day? Standing still?
  • ...Two coppers. And he has to sing the song about the drowned bell. Deal.

docs.title: The Last Verse
docs.text:
Wilmot learned an old song of homecoming as a boy, all but its last verse. Kenwyn swears the whole song is carved into the Saltgrace's forecastle beam.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Wilmot Level 22 After Every Plank of Her Leads to The Long Way Home

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the carved forecastle beam in The Main Deck

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 2,524 EXP
  • 484 mesos
  • +40 standing with Wilmot
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • There's a song old Penrose used to sing on the rope walk. 'The Long Way Home.' A ship coming in after a year at sea, every headland named, the harbour lights at the end.
  • I've had every verse in my head for sixty years but the last. He died before I thought to ask it. Kenwyn says there's a song carved into the Saltgrace's forecastle beam, deep, by some sailor with a long night and a knife.
  • If it's ours, the last verse is there. Go and copy it for me, would you? The forecastle beam, up on the Main Deck's high ledge, at the bow.
  • Copy it exactly. Every word. Penrose would know if you didn't.
  • Another time, then.
  • Copy the song carved into the forecastle beam on the Saltgrace's Main Deck, for Wilmot.
  • Let me see. 'And the bell in the cliff rang us in from the grey, and the rope that we laid held the Saltgrace in Bain.' Ha! 'The rope that we laid.' A ropemaker's verse. Of course it was.
  • Sixty years. Thank you. I'm going to sing it to myself all afternoon. Badly.

docs.title: Winifred a story for the lane
A Story for the Lane
docs.text:
The children of the lane now ask whether the Balrog is coming back. Winifred wants a happy ending she can stand behind: a meadow that was safe for her as a girl, walked and made safe again.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Winifred Level 12 After The Fifth Tale

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 30 Green Mushroom in The Waystone Meadows
  2. Reach the shepherd's hut in The Waystone Meadows
  3. Talk to Hodge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 380 EXP
  • 240 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Winifred
Dialogue
  • The children used to ask if the Balrog was real, dearie. Now they ask if it's coming back. I don't know, and I won't pretend to.
  • But I can give them a true ending for tonight. When I was a girl we picnicked by the shepherd's hut on the The Waystone Meadows. Clear 30 Green Mushrooms there, sit by the hut a moment, then tell my grandson Hodge that it's safe. He'll tell the others. He always does, from a roof.
  • Thank you. Bring me back the colour of the sky over the hut, if you can.
  • Then I'll tell them a funny one, so they sleep.
  • Thirty green mushrooms, the shepherd's hut, then a word to Hodge.
  • Hodge had it all round the lanes before supper, and bigger than you told it, I expect. Good. That's how stories should travel.
  • The four peoples beat it once, together, and the kingdom they made is still here. Tonight I'll add: and the meadow is still green. Thank you, dearie.
  • The meadow by the shepherd's hut? Gran's picnic place? You cleared it?
  • Brilliant. I'll tell Mab and Wat. I'll tell everyone. From the ridge, so they all hear!

docs.title: The Fifth Tale
docs.text:
A traveller on Winifred's step told a fifth version of the Balrog's coming, one she has never heard, and said he had it from someone by the wayside well on the Hedge Lanes. She wants to know if the well is real.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Winifred Level 8 Leads to A Story for the Lane

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach the wayside well in The Hedge Lanes
  • Defeat 25 Orange Mushroom in The Hedge Lanes

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 110 EXP
  • 160 mesos
  • Red Potion x10
  • +10 standing with Selsior
  • +80 standing with Winifred
Dialogue
  • Sit, dearie. Last night a traveller on my step told me a fifth tale of the Balrog. Four peoples, four tales, sixty years, and then a fifth! I nearly fell off my stool.
  • He said he had it by the wayside well on the The Hedge Lanes, outside the Tree Gate. Go and see if there's a well, and whether anyone sits by it. Mind the Orange Mushrooms on the way: clear 25 for me. They used to be shy.
  • Off you go. Come back and tell it to me properly, with the good bits.
  • Another day, then. The tale will keep. Tales always do.
  • The well on the Hedge Lanes, and twenty-five orange mushrooms.
  • A well, a bucket, a stone with old marks scratched in it, and nobody at all? Oh, that's lovely. That's the best kind of answer.
  • Now the tale has a place, and no teller. I shall tell it on Thursday, by the well, in the rain. Thank you, dearie. Here, for your boots.

docs.title: A Present, Unlabelled
docs.text:
Wulfric wants to give Jocelyn something too good to label: a ledger-weight cut from the fine grey stone of the Terraced Cuts.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Wulfric Level 56 After The Quarry Village

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Quarry Stone (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 25,000 EXP
  • 1,120 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +15 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Wulfric
Dialogue
  • May I ask you something? It is... not about the vault.
  • Jocelyn labels everything. Everything. I want to give her something she will not label at once. Something too good to stick a label on.
  • Stone from the The Terraced Cuts, the fine grey my father cut. 15 pieces of Quarry Stone from the Quarry Golems. A mason I know will cut her a ledger-weight from the best one.
  • Please do not tell her. She will find out anyway. She always does.
  • That is all right. I will think of something else. Probably a label-holder. She would label it.
  • Fifteen pieces of Quarry Stone, from the The Terraced Cuts.
  • Oh, this is good stone. Father would have liked it.
  • If she labels it, I will keep the label. I keep all of them, in a tin. ...I have never told anyone that.

docs.title: Digging Behind the Vault
docs.text:
On still nights Wulfric hears scraping behind the vault's deepest corridor. Follow the claw-cut tunnels of the Buried Street to the wall nearest the vault.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Wulfric Level 30 After The Buried Street Leads to The Delver

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Look at the claw-cut wall in The Buried Street

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 8,600 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Orange Potion x20
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Wulfric
  • Unlocks boss.delver
Dialogue
  • On still nights I hear something in the deepest corridor of the vault. Not a door. I know every door by its echo.
  • Scraping. Like a spade, only slower. It comes from behind the wall, and lately it is closer.
  • Ida says the claw-cut tunnels run under the old street. Could you follow them in the The Buried Street and look at the wall nearest the vault? Press Up there. I cannot leave the doors.
  • Thank you. I... thank you. Be careful down there.
  • No, of course. It is only a noise. Probably.
  • The The Buried Street, past the end of the claw-cut tunnels. The wall nearest the vault.
  • A burrow. Just behind the wall. As big as a cart, you say.
  • Then it is not the vault I must guard, it is the burrow. Tell Ida; she will know what to do. And please, do not tell Jocelyn how close it is. Not yet.

docs.title: The Quarry Village
docs.text:
Wulfric's home village is in the quarries upstream, and the stone there has started to stand up. Clear the golems around the Spoil Heaps so the people still there can sleep.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Wulfric Level 53 After A Bounty Alone Leads to An Impossible Dot, A Present, Unlabelled

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 60 monsters in The Spoil Heaps

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 84,800 EXP
  • 1,060 mesos
  • White Potion x30
  • +40 standing with Selsior
  • +150 standing with Wulfric
Dialogue
  • I grew up upstream, in a quarry village. My father could lift a block two men could not. My mother sang while she split slate.
  • A carter told Jocelyn the village is half empty now. The stone has been... standing up. And I cannot leave the vault doors.
  • Would you look in on it for me, Player? Clear the golems around the The Spoil Heaps, 60 of them, so the people still there can sleep.
  • If you see a house with a slate roof split very thin, that was my mother's work. ...Sorry. Go on.
  • No, no. It is a long way. I understand.
  • The The Spoil Heaps, above the The Quarry Landing. Sixty of them.
  • Half the doors shut, but smoke from the rest? Good. That is good.
  • Thank you. No, really. Thank you. I... yes. Thank you.

docs.title: The Gap in the Numbering
docs.text:
Wynne found a gap in the numbering of one old seal record: leaves removed long ago, cleanly and skilfully. She wants help searching the oldest shelf lists.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Wynne Level 20 Leads to The Shelf List Before the Shelf List

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ilwen

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,387 EXP
  • 300 mesos
  • +100 standing with Wynne
  • +10 standing with Fairy Forest
Dialogue
  • Can I tell you something? I haven't told anyone. Not even Grandmother.
  • This spring, copying one of the old seal records, I found a gap in the leaf numbers. Several leaves, gone. Not torn. Cut, cleanly, a very long time ago, by someone who knew what they were doing. I want to know where they went.
  • Ask Ilwen for the oldest shelf list he has. He'll know which one.
  • Thank you. Don't tell Caelum. He'd make a theory of it.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • Ilwen. The oldest shelf list.
  • He found it? Of course he found it. Page and shelf.
  • Let's read it together.
  • The oldest shelf list? Not the one in use. The one before it. Second shelf of the third case, behind the guest lists, page one.
  • Ilwen fetches it without asking why, which, for Ilwen, is a great kindness.

docs.title: Whom to Tell
docs.text:
The fragments' leaf numbers fall inside Wynne's gap. She has decided, at last, whom to tell.

Town Fairy Forest Category Story Given by Wynne Level 25 After The Rootbound Wing Leads to Quiet Shelves

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Deliver 5 Torn Leaf Fragment
  2. Talk to Isaura

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,348 EXP
  • 750 mesos
  • +200 standing with Wynne
  • +80 standing with Fairy Forest
  • +150 standing with Isaura
Dialogue
  • Let me see them. The stitching holes... the numbers... Player, these are from the gap. These are the cut leaves. Some of them. Parts of some of them.
  • I'm going to tell Grandmother. Now. Today. Will you come with me?
  • Give Wynne the 5 Torn Leaf Fragments, then go with her to Isaura.
  • ...Thank you for coming.
  • Another time, then. I'll still be here.
  • The fragments, then Grandmother.
  • She said thank you. Just that. Then she took them to the Eldest.
  • I don't know what they say. I don't think anyone does yet. But they're not lost any more.
  • Wynne. And you. What is...
  • Isaura reads the fragments in silence, for a long time. Then she says, very quietly, 'Thank you.' That night she takes them to Calyra herself. Nothing more is said.

docs.title: Wystan the horse that came back alone
The Horse That Came Back Alone
docs.text:
A patrol horse came back to the stables at night with an empty saddle. Its rider walked home safe, but the horse will not go near the road. Find where it bolted on the Thyme Banks and clear 30 downs boars there.

Town Selsior Category Side Given by Wystan Level 24 After Where the Horse Sweats

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the broken tether in The Thyme Banks
  2. Defeat 30 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,600 EXP
  • 480 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Selsior
  • +120 standing with Wystan
Dialogue
  • Came in at midnight. Empty saddle. Not a scratch on her. I near stopped breathing until the rider walked in after, muddy and sorry.
  • Rider's fine. The mare isn't. Won't go out of the yard. I've sat with her two nights.
  • Go to the The Thyme Banks. Find where she broke her tether, high on the bank. Then clear the 30 Downs Boars nearest it. I want that bank quiet when I walk her back out.
  • Mind the bank. It's steep, and boars don't care.
  • Then she stays in. A horse that won't take the road is no patrol horse. Hmph.
  • The broken tether, high on the Thyme Banks. Then thirty boars.
  • Tusk marks on the tether post, and you say the bank's quiet now. Good.
  • I'll walk her out tomorrow. Slowly. She'll decide. She always does.

docs.title: Where the Horse Sweats
docs.text:
Wystan wants to know what the patrol horses smell out there. Ride the road past Downs Edge and note where a horse starts to sweat, then hunt 25 downs boars on the Thyme Banks, where the smell leads.

Town Selsior Category Story Given by Wystan Level 21 After Short a Rider Leads to Comb for the Shepherds, The Horse That Came Back Alone

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Reach Downs Edge
  2. Defeat 25 Downs Boar in The Thyme Banks

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,200 EXP
  • 420 mesos
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +30 standing with Selsior
  • +100 standing with Wystan
Dialogue
  • You. You rode with my grandson. He says you sit a horse like a sack of turnips, but a brave sack. Hmph.
  • Horses come back from the road wild-eyed. I want to know where it starts. Not a guess. The place.
  • Take a patrol horse out past Downs Edge. Watch its neck. Where it sweats, that's where. Then follow your nose to the The Thyme Banks and thin the Downs Boars there. 25. I've a feeling.
  • And bring the horse back. If you lose the horse, don't bother coming back yourself.
  • Hmph. The horses will keep telling me. I just can't understand them.
  • Downs Edge, then the Thyme Banks. Twenty-five boars. Is the horse fed? Did you check?
  • Sweating at Downs Edge, where the road passes the downs. And boars on the thyme, rooting up the folds like they own them.
  • So that's it. Boar musk and something under it. Something the horses know and we don't. Good work. Don't tell anyone I said that.

docs.title: The Wild Goats
docs.text:
Yarrek's three wild goats still bite and will not eat from his hand. Bring him 15 Rimwort to try on them.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Yarrek Level 40 After Three Goats' Tracks

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Rimwort (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20,000 EXP
  • 800 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • Goat's Milk x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Yarrek
Dialogue
  • My three are still apart in their pen. Ash, Stubborn and Little Moss. They butt the fence and bite, and they will not eat from my hand. I sit with them every evening. It does not help yet.
  • My mother used to give a fretful goat a bitter herb from the far slopes, grey, chewed small. And Lessa says Rimwort cleans their bites. Would you bring me 15 Rimwort? I would like to try, at least.
  • Thank you. I will tell them you are coming. They do not listen, but I tell them.
  • That is all right. They are not going anywhere.
  • Fifteen Rimwort for the goats. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Grey and bitter, like she said. Let me try Little Moss first. She was always the gentle one.
  • She ate it. From my hand. She looked at me for a long time first, but she ate it. The other two, not yet. One out of three is a start, Player. Take some cheese. Take milk. Take more than that.

docs.title: Three Goats' Tracks
docs.text:
Last month three of Yarrek's goats strayed down a gully below the Long Ridge and came home wild. Follow their old tracks and hunt 40 Axe Stumps in what they ran from.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Yarrek Level 23 After A Word for Tavi Leads to The Worst Stretch, The Wild Goats

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Look at the tracks at the gully floor in The Long Ridge
  2. Look at the tracks among the trees in The Long Ridge
  3. Look at where the tracks run in The Long Ridge
  4. Defeat 40 Axe Stump in The Long Ridge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,450 EXP
  • 460 mesos
  • Goat Cheese x10
  • Highland Salve x5
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Yarrek
Dialogue
  • The herds will go up to the ridge soon. Good. But I keep thinking of my three. Burr, Ash and Little Horn. They slipped away one night last month and came back two days later, up from the valley, on their own.
  • They will not eat from my hand now. They butt the fence. I sit by their pen every evening. I followed their tracks as far as I dared, down a gully under the The Long Ridge. The tracks were running. Running from something among trees that were not where trees should be.
  • Will you follow them further than I did? Three places along the tracks below The Long Ridge: the gully floor, the trees, and where they ran. And whatever is down there, 40 Axe Stumps of it.
  • Thank you. Kesh will want to come with you. He will say he knows the way. Let him walk you to the trailhead and then send him home to his mother, please. Gently.
  • That is all right. They are home, at least. That is more than some herders can say.
  • The gully floor, the trees and where the tracks run, below The Long Ridge. And forty Axe Stumps.
  • Stumps with axes in them, walking in a ring around the gully. And the tracks going round and round inside it until they broke out up the slope.
  • So that is what they ran from. Two days of it. No wonder they do not trust a hand now. I will sing to them tonight, the way my mother taught me. It may help.
  • Cheese, and a little salve. And thank you for sending Kesh home. He told me you let him carry your pack to the trailhead. He has not stopped talking about it.

docs.title: A Sharp Note
docs.text:
Ysmay has written a sharp note about a pilot who swung wide in the gap. Take it to Varro on the Inlet Quay, then tell Arlo what Varro said.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Ysmay Level 32 Leads to Quills and Advice

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Talk to Varro
  2. Talk to Arlo

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 3,500 EXP
  • 650 mesos
  • Sea-Herb Salve x10
  • +20 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +150 standing with Ysmay
Dialogue
  • Did you see that? The timber ship this morning. The pilot swung wide past the point where the old eddy sat, then hauled her back late, with the whole inlet watching. I was watching, anyway.
  • I have written it down. Take this note to Varro at the end of the Inlet Quay. He will know who had that tiller, and he will see they hear it. Then find Arlo and tell him what Varro said. He keeps the book.
  • Do not read it on the way. It is not for you. Well, read it if you like. It is very good.
  • Then I will shout it out of the window. They will hear me at the gap. They usually do.
  • My note to Varro, on the quay. Then Arlo. It is not a long walk. It is all downhill.
  • Ysmay's hand. I would know it in the dark. Hm.
  • Aye. Tell her I will see to it. Tell her nothing else.
  • Grandmother sent you? What did Varro say? Exactly, please. Every word.
  • Aye. Then they agree. They nearly always agree. I will write it under this morning. But why did he not argue? He always argues. Grandmother will want to know that too.
  • Aye, he said? And nothing else? Hm.
  • Well. That is Varro. Thank you, Player. Take these, and take your time going down. The stairs are steeper than the pilots are careful.

docs.title: Quills and Advice
docs.text:
Ysmay wants Saltgull quills for Arlo, who wears his pens to stubs writing down what she says. Bring her 20 Saltgull Feathers, and take her written advice to Iska at the Wardens' House.

Town Goa Harbour Category Side Given by Ysmay Level 44 After A Sharp Note

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 20 Saltgull Feather (taken)
  • Talk to Iska

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 26,500 EXP
  • 1,800 mesos
  • Pilot's Oilskin x1
  • +30 standing with Goa Harbour
  • +200 standing with Ysmay
Dialogue
  • Arlo wears his pens to stubs writing down what I say. That is how you know it is worth writing. He needs quills. Good stiff ones.
  • And while you are about it. My daughter takes the Gap Runner out before the race. She will want advice. She will not ask for it, so I have written it out.
  • Bring me 20 Saltgull Feathers from the Saltgulls on The Wrack Ledges, for the quills. And take this to Iska at the Wardens' House. It is advice. Only advice. Do not tell her anything else I have said about her.
  • Good. Saltgulls have the best quills and the worst tempers. And mind: advice. Nothing else.
  • Then the boy can write with a stick. And Iska can manage without me. She usually does. Very well, too. Do not tell her I said that.
  • (how many you carry) of 20 Saltgull Feathers, and my advice to Iska. You are dawdling. I can see the Wardens' House from here.
  • From my mother. Of course. Twelve points. Number seven is about the way I stand at the tiller.
  • She tells the whole town she is proud of me. The fishers, the pilots, everyone who rides the lift. Never me. Me she gives advice.
  • Tell her I read every point. Tell her I will take number seven. She will know what that means.
  • She will take number seven? She will take number seven. Good. It was the best one.
  • And these will make Arlo quills for the whole summer. Sit a moment, Player.
  • This was mine. Forty years in the pilot boats. Iska has her own, and it is wasted on a hook. Wear it, keep it dry, and stand straight if you ever take a tiller.

docs.title: In Ink, Not in the Margin
docs.text:
With the Deep Lantern gone, Ysolde writes the lights into the lighthouse log properly. She wants you there.

Town Bain Harbour Category Side Given by Ysolde Level 69 After The Deep Lantern, Keeping the Light

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Ossie

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 74,263 EXP
  • 1,518 mesos
  • +40 standing with Ysolde
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • The lights are gone. Three summers I marked them in the margin, with my little sign.
  • Tonight I'm writing them into the log properly. In ink. Every night I saw them, and the night they stopped. Fetch Ossie. A keeper's entry wants a witness.
  • Ossie first. He'll want his pen.
  • Another time, then.
  • Fetch Ossie to witness Ysolde's entry in the lighthouse log.
  • There. In ink. 'Pale lights past the headland, these dates. Seen by the keeper and by the keeper's grandson. Gone this night.'
  • Forty years and that's the best entry in the book. Go on, you've earned a look at my opinions of the captains. Ossie, show them page nine.
  • A witness? For Gran's log? I'm coming. I'm bringing my pen. And my logbook, so they match.
  • Tell Gran I'll sign it in my neatest. Miss Maren says my neatest is very neat.

docs.title: Keeping the Light
docs.text:
Ysolde's knees will not manage the hundred and seventeen stairs tonight. She asks you to keep the light, and to watch the water past the headland from the Holm Wood's cliff edge.

Town Bain Harbour Category Story Given by Ysolde Level 55 After Everyone Who Writes Things Down Leads to The Blue Logbook, In Ink, Not in the Margin

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 50 Dusk Wolf in The Timber Path
  2. Look at the lighthouse's view over the Drop in The Cliff Edge

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 55,056 EXP
  • 1,650 mesos
  • +60 standing with Ysolde
  • +25 standing with Bain Harbour
Dialogue
  • Halloran came to me. Forty years I've watched that water, and he's the first to ask what I've seen.
  • My knees won't climb tonight. You keep the light. The lighthouse path runs out through the Timber Path, and the dusk wolves are bold on it after dark. Clear 50 of them, then go out to the Cliff Edge where you can see the water past the headland from up high, the way the lamp sees it.
  • And watch. Just watch. Then come back and tell me what you saw.
  • Watch the water. Don't blink.
  • Another time, then.
  • Clear fifty dusk wolves on the Timber Path, then watch from the Cliff Edge's view over the Drop.
  • Pale lights. Under the water, out past the headland. Moving. You saw them.
  • Three summers I've seen them, about a dozen nights. I marked them only in the margin of the log, with a little sign of my own. I never told a soul. Not even Clemence. Here. Look at my margins.

docs.title: What Bravery Costs
docs.text:
Zip has heard that Torvi once said bravery was wasted on her, and she wants to know if Torvi still thinks so. She will not ask herself. Ask Torvi for her.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway Level 26

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Torvi Brask

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 1,500 EXP
  • 1,560 mesos
  • +40 standing with Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway
  • +10 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • Can I ask you something? Not a dare. A real thing. When I was lying on that rock with my arm the wrong shape, Torvi laughed and said bravery was wasted on someone who could not fight.
  • I have been training every morning for a year. Footwork. Guard. I can do a hundred blocks without dropping the sword. I want to know if Torvi still thinks it. But if I ask, Torvi will laugh, and I will do something stupid to prove a point.
  • Will you ask Torvi Brask for me? Just ask if it is still wasted. And do not say I asked. Say you were wondering. Everybody wonders about me.
  • Thank you! Torvi is on the training ground, or wherever the loudest laugh is. Same place, usually.
  • No, fair. It is a silly question. I will just do another hundred blocks.
  • Ask Torvi Brask if bravery is still wasted on me. You were wondering. Not me. You.
  • Ha! She sent you. Do not look like that; nobody wonders about that by accident. Sit. I will tell you, and you can carry it back.
  • It is not wasted now. She can fight. Not well, but honestly, which is the part you cannot teach. What she cannot do yet is run. Bravery that cannot run is not bravery, it is a bill. Someone pays it. Last time it was her arm.
  • Tell her that. And tell her the hundred blocks were good. I watched. I always watch. Do not tell her that part.
  • Not wasted? Torvi said not wasted? Ha! HA! I knew it. I mean, I hoped it. Same thing.
  • Bravery that cannot run is a bill. Hm. That is annoyingly good. I am going to put it on my wall. In large letters. And then argue with it every morning.
  • Thank you, Player. When they write the song about me, there will be a verse about you. A short one. But a verse.

docs.title: When to Run
docs.text:
Zip stayed home from the Wallow, and it was the hardest thing she has ever done. Now she wants Torvi to tell her whether that counts as learning to run. Carry the question.

Town Urbanograd Category Side Given by Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway Level 50 After Hackleback

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Torvi Brask

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 10,370 EXP
  • 3,000 mesos
  • +60 standing with Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway
  • +15 standing with Urbanograd
Dialogue
  • I stayed home. You went to the Wallow and I stayed on the training ground with Torvi more or less sitting on me, and I did not climb the wall, and I did not follow you, and it was the worst afternoon of my whole life.
  • Torvi always says knowing when to run is the whole lesson. Well, I did not run, exactly. I did not go. Is that the same? Does it count? I need to know if it counts, or I am going to go and fight something just to feel normal.
  • Ask Torvi Brask. Properly. Does staying home count as running? And come straight back. I will be right here, not doing anything stupid. Probably.
  • Go! Quickly. Before I think of a dare.
  • Fine. I will ask myself. Torvi will laugh. It is fine. It is all fine.
  • Ask Torvi Brask if staying home counts. Please. I am being very good while I wait.
  • Does it count? Ha! She stood at the wall the whole afternoon, gripping the sword, looking at the gate. Every part of her wanted to go. She did not go. Of course it counts.
  • Running is not the feet. It is deciding the fight is not yours today, and walking away from it with your head up. Hulda walked away from more fights than she ever told stories about, and came back to every one of them when it was hers. That is the lesson. The second day.
  • Tell her she has learned it. Tell her I said so, which I do not say. And tell her tomorrow morning we start on the second day.
  • It counts. It COUNTS. Torvi said so, and Torvi does not say things like that. Torvi says things like "again" and "slower" and "ha".
  • The second day. I like that. You walk away, and you come back when it is yours. That is not ordinary at all, is it? That is a whole verse.
  • Thank you, Player. For the Wallow, and for asking. One day I am going to walk through that gate with a crowd waiting. And I am going to walk back out of it, too, when I have to.

docs.title: A Message for the Old One
docs.text:
Zirra has a message for Hask that she would rather die than deliver herself. Carry it to him, and hunt 60 Scarred Boars on the way.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Zirra Completed with Hask Level 36 After Grey and Bitter Leads to The Split Drum

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Deliver 1 Zirra's Message
  • Defeat 60 Scarred Boar

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 25,500 EXP
  • 720 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • Blue Potion x20
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Zirra
Dialogue
  • Hold your arm out. No, like this. Hm. You hold a weapon like someone who has been bitten and learned from it. Good. I need an errand run by someone who does not ask questions.
  • This goes to my brother. The Old One. It is folded and it stays folded. I would carry it myself, but I would rather walk off the rim than stand in front of him and say it out loud.
  • Take your time getting there. The Scarred Boars on the slopes have been trampling the young trees I take staves from: kill 60 of them first, and then give him the Zirra's Message. I would pay you in arrows, but you do not shoot.
  • Folded. It stays folded. If he asks how I looked, say I looked busy.
  • Then it stays in my apron. It has been in there a week already.
  • Sixty Scarred Boars, then my message to Hask in the Great Hall. Still folded.
  • From Zirra? She lives a hundred steps from me. Let me see.
  • The canyon valleys where her best staves grow are red on Skarra's map, and her wood is the lowest it has been in her life. By winter the Trail Watch will be short of bows. She did not want to ask me for anything. She raised me, and she still cannot ask me for anything.
  • Thank you, Player. I will find her the wood, and I will not tell her you saw me smile. Take these; my sister would want you paid, even if she would never say so.

docs.title: New Staves
docs.text:
Zirra needs new bow staves, and the canyon valleys are closed to her. Bring her 10 Sound Staves cut from the Swollen Stumps of the Dry Hills.

Town Midbarium Category Story Given by Zirra Level 56 After Hold the Old Camp Leads to The Old Walls

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 10 Sound Stave (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 34,500 EXP
  • 1,120 mesos
  • White Potion x20
  • +40 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Zirra
Dialogue
  • My best staves came from the twisted trees low in the canyon valleys. Those valleys are red on Skarra's map now, and my rack is emptier than it has been since I was a girl. Don't look at me like that. I'm not asking for pity, I'm asking for wood.
  • There's a stand of sound twisted trees at the edge of The Dry Hills. I went out yesterday, cut three staves, and complained the whole way home. I won't cut more, or there'll be no stand left to seed the hill.
  • The grey stumps that crowd it were that stand's cousins once, and a few still carry a straight, sound limb under all the swelling. Fell them and cut me the good wood: 10 Sound Staves. Most of them will be rot. Keep looking.
  • Bring them to me on the rim when you have ten. And hold them by the ends, not the middle. The middle is where the bow lives.
  • Fine. I'll make bows out of tent poles. Hask will love that.
  • (how many you carry) of 10 Sound Staves, from the Swollen Stumps on The Dry Hills. Most are rot. Keep looking.
  • Let me see. This one twists, this one has a knot like a fist, this one... this one is good. Most of them are good. Who taught you to choose wood?
  • Nobody? Then you have the eye for it, which is worse, because now I'll keep sending you. Don't tell Hask I said anything kind.
  • Take these. And when you're out on the Reach, watch for sound twisted wood. I'll pay for every piece.

docs.title: Twisted Wood
docs.text:
Zirra's best staves come from twisted trees, and her stock is at its lowest in a lifetime. Bring her the Gnarlwood that Old Gnarl drops.

Town Midbarium Category Side Given by Zirra Level 30 After Old Gnarl

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 1 Gnarlwood (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 5,700 EXP
  • 600 mesos
  • Orange Potion x20
  • Blue Potion x10
  • +20 standing with Midbarium
  • +30 standing with Zirra
Dialogue
  • You are holding that sword like you are afraid it will run off. Never mind. I am not asking you to hold a bow. I am asking you to fetch wood.
  • My best staves come from twisted trees low in the canyon valleys. Those valleys are red on Skarra's map now, every one of them, and my rack has never been this bare. The best twisted wood there ever was is up on Howling Peak, walking about. Was walking about. I hear you stopped it.
  • Old Gnarl's heartwood is called gnarlwood, and it bends like nothing else. Bring me a piece of Gnarlwood. If you already have one, all the better.
  • Good. Do not let it dry in the sun on the way. I will know.
  • Then I make bows of whatever is left, and they shoot like whatever is left.
  • A piece of Gnarlwood, from Old Gnarl on Howling Peak.
  • Hm. Let me see. Close grain, twisted twice, no checks. It will want a year to season, and it will make the finest stave on this rim when it does.
  • Do not look so pleased. It was the tree that did the growing.
  • Here, potions. My brother would tell you that is a thank-you. He would be right, but do not tell him I said so.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Runs are staged challenges entered through an NPC.

Run Stages The Bright Morrow's Night Run 1 The Outer Pier by Night 1 Under the Outer Pier 1 Caddoc's Night Trap 1 Below the Anvil 1 Kaldemor Gauntlet 3 The Night Watch 1

docs.title: Caddoc's Night Trap
docs.text: Sit up through the night beside Caddoc's biggest cage trap on the Strandwood Rocks, while the creatures come out of the trees. Potions work; scrolls do not.

docs.title: 1. The Long Night
docs.text:
Map: Caddoc's Trap, at Night

  • Keep watch until dawn

Wave 1: 2 Wrack Boar, 1 Strand Fox

docs.title: Rewards (Normal)
docs.text:
First clear: 3,000 EXP, Gap Inn Stew x2, +30 standing with Goa Harbour

Every clear: 750 EXP, 800 mesos, Salted Fish x3

docs.title: The Night Watch
docs.text:
Keep watch with Vosk and Brakka at the far anchor of the canyon bridge through the night, and find out what gnaws the ropes. Hold until dawn. Potions work out there; scrolls do not.

Dying ends the run.

docs.title: 1. The Far Anchor at Night
docs.text:
Map: The Far Anchor at Night

  • Hold the anchor until dawn

Wave 1: 3 Cliff Gnawer

Wave 2: 1 Wild Boar

docs.title: Rewards (Normal)
docs.text:
First clear: 12,000 EXP, Highland Salve x5, +60 standing with Midbarium

Every clear: 4,000 EXP, 2,500 mesos, Goat Cheese x5

docs.title: Below the Anvil
docs.text: Stand guard on the Saltface below the Anvil through a night's work, while Gorm's crew recuts the cracked flight. Potions work; scrolls do not.

docs.title: 1. The Night's Work
docs.text:
Map: Below the Anvil, at Night

  • Guard the crew until dawn

Wave 1: 2 Sea Newt, 1 Shore Crab

docs.title: Kaldemor Gauntlet
docs.text:

Dying ends the run.

Wave 1: 3 Pig, 3 Orange Mushroom

docs.text: Sail the Bright Morrow's night run past the headland in Keziah's place. The sawbills leap across the deck in the dark; keep them off the mainsail until the run is done. Potions work; scrolls do not.
